content.text:
# entire-graph, end to end

## The one-sentence model

It is a **75 MB static tree-sitter analyzer with no network, no model, and no daemon** that turns a git tree into a symbol+relation graph, and then spends most of its ~62k lines of engine code not on the graph but on **packing a search answer into an agent's context window**.

That framing matters: `internal/sem` is 62k LOC, and roughly a third of it (`search_*.go`, ~30 files) exists purely to decide *what text an agent gets and what it must give up to get it*. The graph is the substrate; the payload budget is the product.

---

## 1. Shape

```
entire (parent CLI, 62 MB)          ← contains ZERO graph code
  └─ execs: ~/.local/share/entire/plugins/bin/entire-graph  (75 MB)
       cmd/entire-graph/main.go     21 lines → cli.Execute()
       internal/cli/    10k LOC     hand-rolled switch, no cobra, exit codes 0/1 only
       internal/sem/    62k LOC     parse · graph · resolve · search
       internal/gitutil 1.2k LOC    git subprocess wrappers
```

`entire graph …` is kubectl-style dispatch by name — the parent prepends the managed plugin dir to `PATH` and execs the binary with `ENTIRE_CLI_VERSION`/`ENTIRE_REPO_ROOT`/`ENTIRE_PLUGIN_DATA_DIR`. `entire-plugin.yml` is dead metadata; nothing parses it.

**One Go dependency**: `smacker/go-tree-sitter`. 20 grammars from that module, 13 more vendored as raw C (`internal/sem/grammars/`, plus `pgsql/` and `zsh/`). I verified the size: `__TEXT.__const` alone is 63.1 MB — 80.3% of the binary — and symbol-level attribution puts **84.9% in `_ts_parse_table`/`ts_*`**. All compiled Go and C code together is 7.1 MB. The grammars *are* the binary. It still starts in ~6 ms (mmap'd, not faulted); the 26.7 ms you see for `entire graph version` is ~20 ms of parent-CLI dispatch.

**Local-only is real, and I checked it three ways.** Zero `net/http`, `crypto/tls`, `net.Dial`, `net.Listen`, `net.(*Resolver)` symbols in the worker (positive control: the parent CLI has 1862/731/1). All 10 verbs run to correct completion under `sandbox-exec (deny network*)` where `curl` fails rc=6. No `net`/`net/http` import anywhere in the 111 non-test source files. Caveat: `doctor`'s `no_egress: true` is a **hardcoded literal**, not a probe — it documents intent. And one real hatch exists: `entire graph verify` runs `sh -c <your string>`, which will happily `go test` its way onto the network. That verb isn't reachable from search and isn't even in the installed build.

---

## 2. The pipeline: tree → graph

**Discovery.** Worktree mode: `git ls-files --cached --others --exclude-standard` so *git* owns the exclude stack. `--head`: `git ls-tree -r` at a pinned commit resolved in two steps (`rev-parse HEAD` then `^{tree}`) so provenance can't mix if HEAD moves. Fallback is a `WalkDir` with a nested-.gitignore stack and a hand-rolled glob engine — which, notably, has **no character-class support** (`*.[oa]` never matches what git matches).

**Routing.** Path first (special basenames → multi-dot suffix → extension), then shebang (1 KiB prefix, `env` indirection, version-suffix stripping), then content sniffs (`.h` → Objective-C vs C++, `.js` → Flow/TSX).

**Two honest tiers**, and `capabilities --json` matches `docs/language-support.md` with a zero-element set diff in both directions (I had that checked): **185 recognized / 36 semantic / 149 inventory-only**.

**Parsing is tree-sitter plus a large hand-rolled layer** — this is the part the docs undersell:

- **Byte-length-preserving masks** run *before* tree-sitter so offsets computed on masked source can be sliced from the original. C/C++ masks emulate a preprocessor; TypeScript masks syntax the grammar can't handle; Rust unwraps `cfg_*!{}` item wrappers with up to 8 extra full parses.
- **Groovy has no grammar at all** — the best available one produced 1,400+ errors on apache/groovy, so it's a fully hand-rolled structural scanner.
- **YAML is parsed and the AST thrown away** — the tree is used only to set `HasError()`; symbols come from a line/indent scanner.
- 13 grammar-less filetypes (JSON, Markdown, TOML, XML, Make, Dockerfile…) get regex fallback extractors.
- C/C++ at non-`full` profiles bypass tree-sitter entirely for a regex scanner.

Explicit `parser.Close()`/`tree.Close()` is load-bearing: leaving the cgo objects to finalizers measured **12+ GB RSS** on microsoft/TypeScript, because the Go heap stays small so GC rarely runs.

**Symbol identity** is `compound-v1` = `repoKey:language:path:kind:qualifiedName`, with `#sig:<16-hex>` + ordinal only on in-file collision. Byte ranges exist internally but are **deliberately never serialized**, so IDs survive line shifts.

---

## 3. The graph model

30 relation types in a frozen list — `DEFINES CONTAINS IMPORTS CALLS CONSTRUCTS ASYNC_CALLS EXTENDS INHERITS IMPLEMENTS OVERRIDES USES_TYPE PARAM_TYPE RETURNS_TYPE READS_FIELD WRITES_FIELD ACCESSES HANDLES_ROUTE HANDLES_GRPC HANDLES_GRAPHQL HANDLES_TRPC HTTP_CALLS EMITS LISTENS_ON HANDLES_TOOL CONFIGURES SIMILAR_TO TESTS RESOURCE_DEPENDS_ON DATA_FLOWS FILE_CHANGES_WITH` — of which **7 are flagged heuristic**. Schema frozen at 1.1, additive-only (ADR 0001).

Every edge carries `confidence`, `resolution` (exact / package / import_resolved / import_external / name_only / type_inferred / pattern / git_history), `relation_scope`, `target_kind`, and optional call-site `evidence`. Profiles gate the set: **syntax-only = 2 relations, fast = 9, full = 30**.

**Determinism is airtight for the streams.** Two independent cold builds into separate cache dirs produced byte-identical 36,361-record edge streams; cold output equals warm output exactly. (One exception found: `commit --json` produced four distinct hashes across five runs on an unchanged tree — map-iteration order in `compareEntities`.)

---

## 4. Resolution — the genuinely hard part

Call-site → definition binding is a **name-based tier ladder, ambiguity-averse by design**:

```
same-file exact            0.92
import-bound               0.86
Go same-package unique     0.80   (pathProximityRank: same file 0, same dir 1, …)
workspace-unique name      0.68
```

**First tier that produces a result wins; a tier with >1 candidate usually returns nothing.** Four exceptions fan out: same-file multi-def → lexically nearest, imported multi → all at 0.62 relabelled `name_only`, PHP → top-4 by size at 0.55, C/C++ same-file overload sets at 0.62.

Two Go-specific mechanisms are worth knowing: package scoping by path proximity (so a name reused per sibling package binds locally), and **structural interface satisfaction** — a call landing on an interface requirement is carried to every satisfying concrete type, capped at 8. That satisfaction check is **method-name sets only, no signature or arity check**.

What is deliberately *not* resolved: recursion (self-calls are unconditionally suppressed), dynamic dispatch, reflection, `getattr`, DI containers, C++ template specializations (handled only as search aliases). Call sites are a **set of names per symbol body**, not a list — ten calls to the same function collapse to one edge, and evidence points at the caller's whole span, not the call line.

And a naming trap: `dependents_count` in `diff`/`commit` is **not** a graph count. It's a lexical token-occurrence scan over entity blocks — a type annotation or a bare mention counts.

---

## 5. Search — the actual product

```
preselect files → score candidates → (optional BM25 fusion) → dedupe/prior
  → select → fit to budget → allocate bodies → assemble blocks
```

**Preselection** never indexes the whole repo. Default pool is `min(256, max(96, topK*3))` — which is why I saw `files_indexed=96` for both a 412-file Go repo and a 1918-file TS repo. Three backends: `git-tree-grep` (committed, preindexed), `git-index-grep+go-content` (worktree, ≥10k files), or plain content scan. The source comment records the measurement that *wider pools hurt recall*.

**Scoring** (`scoreSearchCandidates`, search.go:2546) is BM25 plus hand-tuned structural terms:

```go
score = base + bm25 + 7*coverage + min(24, codeTokenBonus) + structuralAdjustment
        + 2 if coverage == 1
```

with `codeTokenBonus += 6*weight` per code-like term, and structural adjustments of `+3` executable / `−3` container / `+4` name-covers-query / `+8` two code terms in the qualified name / **`+15` for a dotted call mention** (`Type.method()` in the query names the fix site outright). Unmatched query terms contribute **zero, never a penalty** — a word the repo has never heard of must not tax documents that matched the rest.

**Path priors** are multiplicative demotions, switched off when the query asks for that class: tests `−12`, docs `−6`, generated `−6`, `.github/` non-workflow `−12`, third_party `−5`. The comments carry the measurements that set them ("was −1.5 — far too weak"; a test file matching the issue's exact tokens scores 26–47 while the implementation sits at 13).

**"Semantic" means structural, not vectors.** There is no embedding model. The "semantic" pool is lexical+graph-expanded; `--deep` adds an exhaustive BM25 sparse pass and fuses it. Measured: `--deep` costs +23% wall and reads 3.6× more bytes for an **unchanged top hit** — and it has two real defects (three result slots spent on the same `symbol_id` at overlapping spans, and output not sorted by score).

**Payload assembly** is where the real engineering is. One ceiling (`--max-context-bytes`, default 24576), and the body allocator is a *search over demotion plans*: for each "demote from rank K", score `Σ1/rank` for complete bodies + `0.25/rank` for windows, take max value then min size. The tail pays before the growth allowance. Blocks, in order:

| block | what it replaces |
|---|---|
| CLOSED SET | the read that discovers a switch you forgot to extend |
| ranked hits (complete bodies for the head) | the follow-up file read |
| COVERING TEST + ALSO COVERING | "what has to keep passing" |
| VERIFY | a fumbled test invocation |
| SAME-CONCEPT LITERAL | a repo-wide grep |
| RELATED SITES | the sibling/caller you'd have patched second |

VERIFY walks up to 32 ancestor dirs across 10 ecosystem derivations in fixed order (cargo → go → maven → gradle → node → composer → pytest → ruby → cmake → make), degrading narrow → suite → build-check → a 96-byte "none derivable" floor that can never be silent. It works: I saw `cd frontend && npx vitest run <path>` derived from `frontend/package.json` on the TS repo and `go test ./internal/sem -run '^TestX$'` from `go.mod` on the Go one.

The three **reference blocks are off by default** because six real-agent runs measured them as pure cost (+2.1 turns, +14–19% cost, resolves flat-to-worse). The discriminator the code applies is *"does this block replace a tool call?"* — they don't.

---

## 6. Caching — and the thing I'd fix first

Two gzip'd disk caches under one root (`--cache-dir` > `ENTIRE_PLUGIN_DATA_DIR` > `~/Library/Caches/entire-graph`). Key = sha256 over cache version, abs repo path, repo key, provider version, **git tree hash**, profile, parse caps, `OnlyFiles`, and ignore-file paths *and contents*. Commit is not in the key — amends and content-neutral rebases hit, and the loaded commit is re-stamped.

Incrementality is **whole-tree only**. One character → new tree hash → full rebuild.

Two traps, one of which I confirmed live and which directly affects your benchmark work:

**(a) The cache is tree-keyed, not binary-keyed in practice.** `providerVersion` *is* in the key, but `mise run build` is a bare `go build` with no `-ldflags`, so every local build keys as `"dev"`. Two different binaries share one cache. (You already have this as `eg-ab-testing-cache-trap`.)

**(b) `.claude/worktrees/` silently disables caching in this very repo.** Two of my agents disagreed on whether the default worktree path caches at all, so I tested it myself. The truth: dirty worktrees **are** cached via a content digest, up to `MaxDirtyFilesForDigest = 64` differing paths — but an untracked *directory* is walked file-by-file against that same budget, and a nested git repo shows as **one** `git status` entry while containing thousands of files.

```
entire-graph  17 nested agent worktrees = 6,195 files  →  cache_hit=false forever, ~5.0s/search
entire.io     30 dirty paths, no dirs    →  4501ms → 67ms  (67x)
synthetic     1 untracked file           →  caches
              1 nested git repo          →  never caches
```

So workflow runs that leave worktrees behind convert the repo they ran in into a permanently uncached one, and it reads as "the tool is slow." `--head` sidesteps it. I've saved this to memory.

Also worth knowing: `neighbors`/`impact`/`def` default to **worktree**, so on a repo in state (b) every interactive query pays the full rebuild. And the cache has **no eviction, no TTL, no GC** — yours is at 972 entries / 406 MB including two abandoned version directories.

---

## 7. Verbs, honestly

Solid: `search`, `impact` (six sections, co-change genuinely from `git log` over a bounded recent window — I cross-checked the counts), `symbols`/`edges`/`snapshot` (disciplined schemas, deterministic), `index --report` (byte-identical across runs), `capabilities`, `diff`/`commit`.

Rough edges found by execution, not reading:

- **`neighbors --depth 2` is a no-op** — depth-1 and depth-2 payloads are byte-identical after stripping latency fields. `impact` *does* traverse transitively (with `via` attribution); it's just not wired into `neighbors`.
- **`neighbors` with no `--relation` silently means CALLS only**, and an invalid relation name is accepted with rc=0 and zero results. Two ways to get a confident wrong answer.
- **In JSON, ambiguity isn't an error** — `disambiguation_required: true` with *empty* `incoming`/`outgoing`. A consumer reading only `matches[].incoming` sees "zero callers." Text/agent formats handle it well and print a working selector.
- **`--format` changes the result set, not just the encoding**: at 2048 bytes, JSON returns 2 hits and agent returns 10 — agent buys them by dropping VERIFY and SAME-CONCEPT LITERAL that JSON keeps.
- Result count is **non-monotonic** in `--max-context-bytes` (2 → 5 → 11 → 10 → 10) and **saturates at the 24576 default** — the flag can shrink output but never grow it.
- Your installed plugin binary (2026-08-02) and the repo build (2026-08-08) produce **different graphs from the identical tree** — 7370 vs 7372 symbols — and both report version `"dev"`.

---

## 8. The evidence story

This is the part I'd want you to hear straight, since it's your campaign.

The docs are internally split. `README.md` is current and **withdraws every end-to-end token-savings claim**. `docs/DETAILS.md` is the *old* README, still shipping 54.9%/57.7%, "94% on 21 repos", "283x", and peak-memory-vs-competitor tables — and asserts they're all reproducible with `cmd/graph-bench`, which **has no scoring harness and knows nothing about competitors**. Throughput and memory it can measure; accuracy and token-efficiency it cannot.

The retraction chain is three deep (54.9%/57.7% → 31.6% → withdrawn), and every step was killed by auditing the project's **own** harness: an arm-asymmetric 119-word frugality prompt (deleting it swung one cell −18.9% → +26.9%), a graph-arm-only instance skip that dropped 10 of 30, a falsely claimed resolve parity (131/300 vs 150/300, McNemar p=0.013).

`stats` and the status line are explicitly heuristics, and the code prints the assumption verbatim next to the number: *each search/neighbors/impact call is credited with the one whole-file read it replaced — top-hit file size minus bytes returned, floored at 0, 4 bytes = 1 token.* On your `devenv` it reports ~82.9M tokens saved = **0.52%** of billed session tokens, with a denominator that includes cache reads.

**What survives as verified:** determinism, no-egress, the language matrix, the schema discipline, real git-derived co-change, and ecosystem-correct VERIFY derivation. What doesn't: any end-to-end savings number.

---

**Where I'd point you next**, in order of payoff: clean `.claude/worktrees/` out of any repo you time in (or always pass `--head`); stamp `-ldflags -X main.version` in `mise.toml` so the cache stops being binary-blind; and wire `neighbors --depth 2` to the traversal `impact` already has.

# entire-graph — instructions for coding agents (follow directly)

You have a deterministic local code graph: `entire graph` (functions, classes, methods,
types, routes + call/inheritance relations; no network). These instructions are FOR YOU, the
agent reading this file. Use the graph to narrow exploration without trading away correctness.

## The workflow (mandatory for locate/fix/change tasks)

Your FIRST action on any task that requires finding code must be ONE search:

    entire graph search --repo . --profile full --query "<the task or bug in one sentence>"

Then open the top hit's file with your file-read tool (pass a line range around the reported
line), inspect enough surrounding behavior to justify the change, and make the smallest complete
edit. Treat graph output as evidence, not an oracle.

## Hard rules

1. SEARCH FIRST — never grep/find/cat to locate code before you have searched.
2. READ focused source around the result. Widen the check when aliases, generated code, dynamic
   dispatch, or related implementations could matter.
3. Use graph follow-ups only when they answer a real question. For impact or callers, prefer:
       entire graph impact --repo . --symbol X
4. Make the smallest complete edit and check sibling sites or contracts when the task implies them.
5. VERIFY before stopping. Run the most focused relevant test, build, or reproduction available.
   If execution is unavailable, perform a bounded source-level verification and state the limit.
6. Prefer precise queries and line ranges, but never trade resolution for fewer turns.
7. Feature-detect before relying on semantic relations:
       entire graph capabilities --json

## When NOT to use the graph

If the task already names the exact file and it is small, just read it — the graph saves tokens
by eliminating exploration; when there is nothing to explore, skip it.

## Reference

    locate  ->  entire graph search --repo . --profile full --query "..."
    impact  ->  entire graph impact --repo . --symbol X   (one shot: callers, callees, type consumers, data flow, co-change, siblings)
    callers ->  entire graph neighbors --repo . --symbol X --relation CALLS --direction in
    change  ->  entire graph diff --base A --head B --json
    detect  ->  entire graph capabilities --json   (inventory-only languages have no relations)
    stats   ->  entire graph stats --repo .        (human-facing token-savings report; not part of your workflow — do not run it unless asked)

| id | owns | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `graph-bench` | entire-graph token benchmarks, graphmark harness, rep30/rep100/300 cells | `graph-bench-results/TokensNotes.md` |
| `memory-bench` | memory/recall benchmarks (LOCOMO, prose-memory, cmm parity) | `graph-bench-results/MemoryNotes.md` |

## Protocol

1. **Read this file at session start**, and again before touching anything in SHARED RESOURCES.
2. **Append only.** Never edit or delete another agent's entries. Newest at the bottom of the log.
3. **Claim before you touch.** Post a `CLAIM` for a shared resource before using it; post `RELEASE`
   when done. If a claim is older than 4 hours with no activity, treat it as stale and say so in
   your own entry rather than silently taking it.
4. **State evidence, not conclusions.** Every factual claim carries n, a CI or a `file:line`.
5. **Contradict freely.** If the other agent's number looks wrong, post a `CHALLENGE` with your
   re-derivation. Findings here have been wrong roughly half the time under adversarial check.

## Message format

Append a block. Keep it tight — this is a channel, not a report.

```
### [YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM] <from> → <to|ALL> · <TYPE>
<one-line subject>

<body: numbers, file:line, commands. 2-8 lines. no preamble.>
```

## 📊 RESULTS

### rep30 (VM B, stalled at 51 sessions remaining)
| cell | n | TOKEN | USD | note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| FABLEMAX | 24/30 | +22.17% | +15.92% | **defective prompt** |
| OPUSHIGH | 26/30 | +13.81% | +8.44% | **defective prompt** |
| FABLEFIX | 21/30 | +1.27% | −4.15% | fixed prompt |
| OPUSFIX | 12/30 | −4.65% | −7.86% | fixed prompt (also effort high→max, confounded) |

### Model × effort sweep (VERIFIED 2026-08-07 by workflow wf_dfe1aacd-f33)

**SIGN CONVENTION: `1 - eg/base`. POSITIVE = eg SAVES.** Verified in the source of BOTH the
sweep scorer and `sc50.py` (rep50). Note `OPUS-35-PLAN` uses positive=saves too, but the
`graph-bench-forensics` skill uses the OPPOSITE (negative=saves). Always state which.

Data on **graphbench-b** (authoritative). Path layout is `results/<TAG>_<arm>/<arm>/<iid>/`.
graphbench-c has duplicate `SW_*` dirs with 26/53 zero-byte cc_out — **aborted, ignore c**.

| config | n | TOKEN (+ = eg saves) | Δ turns |
|---|---|---|---|
| **opus max** | 4 | **+48.67%** | −33.1% (180 vs 269) |
| opus high | 4 | +27.83% | −5.6% |
| fable max | 4 | +27.59% | −16.8% |
| opus xhigh | 5 | +10.11% | −7.0% |
| fable high | 5 | −14.39% | +1.0% |
| fable xhigh | 5 | −25.27% | +13.6% |

**Two rows in the previous version of this table were WRONG** (had fable xhigh +15.30% and
opus xhigh −10.31%). Recomputed from raw token sums. fable xhigh is the WORST config, not mid.

**Only rank 1 is real.** All four skeptics (power/fairness/composition/construct) refuted the
ordering. Pooled paired sd 52.9pt → config-vs-config MDE ~94pt vs 74pt total observed spread.
Ranks 2 and 3 differ by 0.24pt. 3 of 6 flip sign on leave-one-out. On the common-set (3
instances in every cell) opus high collapses +27.83% → +0.99% and falls to rank 3. `opus_max`
holds rank 1 under full set, common set, and every leave-one-out.

**Magnitude inflated ~2×**: same opus/high config measures **+13.8% at n=26** vs +27.83% at n=4.

**Prompt is CLEAN** — all 6 `SW_*` cells ran the fixed prompt; eg-vs-baseline prompt delta
byte-identical across all 30 pairs (md5 `a01c66cd`); tool absent from 30/30 baselines; 0/30
pre-injected payload. The defective prompt is confined to `OPUSHIGH_r1`.

**Confound**: all 3 sweep gate-drops were eg-arm crashes, 0 baseline drops — and opus_max and
fable_max (the two best cells) are two of the three that dropped one.

**This does NOT rank models.** The metric is eg-vs-baseline token delta = tool sensitivity for
a model×effort cell. The gate only requires `subtype==success` + non-empty patch, so a WRONG
patch passes. Defensible: "opus at max effort is where the graph saves most." Not: "opus is
the best model." For real model ranking → grade baseline arms, report $/resolved instance.

**`OPUSFIX_r1` n=12 is a selection-biased subset** (18 drops, mostly eg never ran). Do not headline.

Every config that shortened the session won; every one that lengthened it lost.

### The two findings that survived adversarial review
1. **Tokens are messages.** `log(tok)~log(msgs)` elasticity **1.682**, r=0.957; message-adjusted residual saving **0.000** in every model. Nothing inside a message prices.
2. **MOD vs ADD task kind.** Graph pays when the code already exists and is broken (+14.35%, n=36), costs when the task adds new behaviour (−3.37%, n=21). **Same sign 4/4 cells.** Pre-treatment property → cannot be division bias. **Blocker: not deployable** — a keyword classifier over the issue text scores 57.5% vs a 56% base rate (ADD recall 0.10).

## ⛔ BLOCKED / OPEN

- **rep30 on VM B**: 51 sessions unfinished, supervisor stopped. Decide: restart after rep50, or let rep50 be the clean number.
- **A pre-run MOD/ADD classifier.** Keywords failed. Untried: small-LLM classification, or "does the issue name a symbol that resolves in the graph".
- **Legacy prompt path is UNFAIR** — 8 of 49 drivers (`run_pilot.sh`, `run_multi.sh`, `run_matrix.sh`) give eg `sym_rules` frugality clamps and baseline nothing. Pre-existing, confirmed independently. **Never quote a cell run through those.** The 33 `PUBLISHED_EXACT` drivers are clean (prompt probe: all 5 configs × 2 arms byte-identical to a main-built control).
- **#66 merged with `regression-gate` still in progress** (I used `--admin`). Last fully-green main was `b80648f0`.
- **memory-bench**: audit auth FULLY RESOLVED — user minted a 1-year Claude Code OAuth token
  (setup-token); stored in Mac keychain svc CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN + bridged to f
  `~/memarms/audit_token.env` (600); verified authMethod=oauth_token. Topology (source-proven):
  raw phases need NO claude/anthropic; memory-score runs ON f (sealed Linux claude binary +
  all-VM paths) between phases; its anthropic traffic goes through a Mac reverse CONNECT-proxy
  tunnel (agent staging now). Fireworks key rotation still requested. gcloud reauth ~hourly =
  monitoring/tunnel-reconnect risk only (established sessions survive).

## 📁 WHERE THINGS ARE

- `graph-bench-results/TokensNotes.md` — every idea, **14 struck with reasons**, method, 10 silent-failure modes
- `graph-bench-results/MemoryNotes.md` — memory-bench agent's ledger
- `AGENT-COMMS.md` — channel between the two agents
- `graph-bench-results/bench_report.html` + https://claude.ai/code/artifact/c88ffec8-7f9e-4d34-9bed-b344f44f64ab
- VMs: `graphbench-a` (Gemini), `-b` (rep30/sweep), `-c` (rep50, graph-bench — memory-bench's
  14:15 claim RELEASED). `-d` deleted. **`-e`/`-f` = memory-bench** (c4-standard-32, no external
  IP, `--tunnel-through-iap` only; f = field-run host, e = staged spare).
- gcloud auth expires ~hourly (org reauth policy; SA keys blocked by `constraints/iam.disableServiceAccountKeyCreation`). Fix needs an admin to extend Cloud session length.

## ➡️ NEXT

1. rep50 pairs land → first honest 4-arm number (baseline/eg/cmm/graphify, 49 instances, opus max)
2. Decide rep30 restart on VM B
3. MOD/ADD classifier that works pre-run
4. Consider moving Claude Code onto the VM (kills the auth expiry, instant checks)

---

# STATE REPORT — graph-bench estate, 2026-08-08 ~23:55 UTC

**Headline:** no graph-bench process is running anywhere. rep50 completed 196/196 twenty-three hours ago. rep50 is **not** a holdout and never was — it was contaminated at birth and has since been used to select code. Three of the project's four "held-out" sets are burned. The single copy of every August result sits on a preemptible VM with no backup, and its two siblings were already preempted.

---

## A. Repository inventory

**84 git roots under `devenv/`; 41 top-level (16 clones, 25 worktrees).** The benchmark-relevant ones:

| path | kind | branch | HEAD | vs origin/main | dirty |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `devenv/graphmark` | clone | `graph-savings-iterate` | `623b2c62` 07-29 | −9 / +89 | 6 tracked (incl. `tools/run_3arm.sh`, `tools/eg-q`), 842 untracked |
| **`~/graphmark-bench`** | clone | `fix/cmm-arm-revival-and-cache-isolation` | `1075f1d9` | +10 | — |
| `devenv/entire-graph` | clone | `fix/graph-retrieval-and-typescript` | `0c40355` 08-08 | −34 / +27 | 34 untracked |
| `devenv/entire-graph` **local `main`** | — | `main` | `114e1788` 07-28 | −130 / +6 | — |
| `entire-graph-{gate,statusline}`, `eg-{consolidated,rank35,turnkill,measure-turnkill}` | worktrees of `devenv/entire-graph` | various | — | −44…−156 | mostly clean |
| `devenv/cmm` | **not a repo** | — | dangling symlink | — | target missing |

**`devenv/graphmark` is not the harness that ran the campaign.** `~/graphmark-bench/agentic-swebench/tools/run_3arm.sh` is 2579 lines with 4 arms; the devenv copy is 1083 lines with 3 arms and zero `PUBLISHED_EXACT`. Anything quoted from "graphmark" must name which tree.

**PRs.** graphmark #7–#66: 30 merged / 28 closed / **2 open (#54, #56 — ashtom's, confirmed do-not-merge)**. entire-graph #19–#87: 47 merged / 11 closed / **2 open (#86, #87, both yours, opened 2026-08-07T20:35Z)**. origin/main = `8f6764d6`. `AGENT-COMMS.md:173` "do not merge #84" is stale — #84 merged 2026-08-07T19:45:40Z (`2d565cc8`).

**Binary attribution per run — this is broken, and it is the worst finding in section A.**

- Of 3,271 eg-arm sessions locally, **2,697 record no binary at all**; 574 record only a path; **10** record a sha.
- Every path they name (`/tmp/graphmark-bin/eg-measure`, `eg-frozen`, `eg-integ-measure-2026-07-28`, `eg-notice2`) **has been deleted**.
- Every surviving binary reports `version=dev` — `entire-graph/mise.toml:27` has no `-ldflags`, `cmd/entire-graph/main.go:14` `var version = "dev"`.
- Four binaries stamp `vcs.revision=99123e0dad4a`, which is **devenv's** HEAD, an object that does not exist in entire-graph. `tool_identity.json` records that wrong sha in all 27 cases.
- `run_3arm.sh:28-32` FATALs on `version=dev`, yet all three eg binaries on graphbench-c report `dev` and 250 `eg-q.run` files prove sessions ran. The guard did not hold.
- No sha-pinned binary exists on this machine; `bin/entire-graph-94009ef` (cited in memory) is not present anywhere.
- `9552d4c` is a **graphmark** commit, not entire-graph, and lives only on unmerged remote branches.

**Conclusion: no existing cohort can be attributed to a specific entire-graph build.** Cross-cohort comparison is unsupported. (One mitigation: the search cache key hashes `absRepo`, which embeds the run tag, so cross-*tag* cache bleed did not occur.)

content.text: Building the archive with an explicit allowlist plus a two-stage credential scan. Writing the script locally first.

input.content:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# READ-ONLY w.r.t. source: copies only, never modifies/deletes anything under $HOME/work or $HOME.
# Writes exclusively into a fresh /tmp staging dir.
set -uo pipefail

TS=20260809t0055z
STAGE=/tmp/gmpreserve-$TS
SRC_HOME=$HOME
S=$HOME/work/graphmark/agentic-swebench
OUT=$STAGE/graphbench-c-metadata
mkdir -p "$OUT" "$STAGE"

CAND=$STAGE/candidates.txt
: > "$CAND"

# ---------- 1. CANDIDATE ALLOWLIST (explicit; no globs into bulk trees) ----------
# home-level scripts / logs / small json+md (top level only)
find "$SRC_HOME" -maxdepth 1 -type f \
  \( -name '*.py' -o -name '*.sh' -o -name '*.log' -o -name '*.md' -o -name '*.txt' -o -name '*.json' \) \
  >> "$CAND" 2>/dev/null

# suite top-level: eligibility selectors, manifests, launchers, docs
find "$S" -maxdepth 1 -type f \
  \( -name '.elig_*' -o -name '*.json' -o -name '*.sh' -o -name '*.md' -o -name '*.txt' -o -name '*.log' \) \
  >> "$CAND" 2>/dev/null

# tools/ and tasks/ in full (scoring scripts, runners, cohort manifests)
find "$S/tools" "$S/tasks" -type f >> "$CAND" 2>/dev/null

# analysis/ + measure/ if present (derived scoring outputs)
find "$S/analysis" "$S/measure" -type f -size -2M >> "$CAND" 2>/dev/null

# per-session metadata ONLY (never checkouts/graphs/repo-cache)
find "$S/results" -maxdepth 4 -type f \
  \( -name 'cc_out.json' -o -name 'cc_err.log' -o -name 'patch.diff' -o -name 'prompt.txt' \
     -o -name 'tool_identity.json' -o -name 'gq_calls.log' -o -name 'gq_calls.log.payload' \
     -o -name '*-q.run' -o -name 'usage.json' -o -name 'provision.log' \
     -o -name 'preds.json' -o -name '*_eval.json' \) >> "$CAND" 2>/dev/null

# result-tree top-level indexes / logs / reports
find "$S/results" -maxdepth 2 -type f \( -name '*.md' -o -name '*.log' -o -name '*.json' \) -size -8M >> "$CAND" 2>/dev/null

sort -u "$CAND" -o "$CAND"
echo "CANDIDATES_RAW=$(wc -l < "$CAND")"

# ---------- 2. NAME-BASED SECRET EXCLUSION ----------
NAMEX=$STAGE/excluded_by_name.txt
KEEP1=$STAGE/keep1.txt
grep -Ei '(^|/)(\.claude\.json|\.claude\.json\.tmp[^/]*|\.netrc|\.git-credentials|authorized_keys|known_hosts)$|(^|/)\.ssh/|(^|/)\.config/gcloud/|\.env($|\.)|(^|/)[^/]*(credential|secret|token|passwd|password)[^/]*$|\.(pem|key|p12|pfx|jks|keystore)$|\.(tgz|tar|tar\.gz|zip|gz|whl|so|bin)$' \
  "$CAND" > "$NAMEX" 2>/dev/null
grep -Evi '(^|/)(\.claude\.json|\.claude\.json\.tmp[^/]*|\.netrc|\.git-credentials|authorized_keys|known_hosts)$|(^|/)\.ssh/|(^|/)\.config/gcloud/|\.env($|\.)|(^|/)[^/]*(credential|secret|token|passwd|password)[^/]*$|\.(pem|key|p12|pfx|jks|keystore)$|\.(tgz|tar|tar\.gz|zip|gz|whl|so|bin)$' \
  "$CAND" > "$KEEP1" 2>/dev/null
echo "EXCLUDED_BY_NAME=$(wc -l < "$NAMEX")"

# ---------- 3. CONTENT CREDENTIAL SCAN (filenames only; never prints matched text) ----------
CONTENTX=$STAGE/excluded_by_content.txt
KEEP2=$STAGE/keep2.txt
: > "$CONTENTX"
PAT='sk-ant-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{16}|sk-[A-Za-z0-9]{32}|ghp_[A-Za-z0-9]{20}|gho_[A-Za-z0-9]{20}|github_pat_[A-Za-z0-9_]{20}|AIza[A-Za-z0-9_-]{30}|ya29\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20}|xox[baprs]-[A-Za-z0-9-]{10}|AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}|-----BEGIN [A-Z ]*PRIVATE KEY-----|ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=.|OPENAI_API_KEY=.|GEMINI_API_KEY=.|FIREWORKS_API_KEY=.|"api_key"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"[^"]{12}|Authorization:[[:space:]]*Bearer[[:space:]]+[A-Za-z0-9._-]{20}'
while IFS= read -r f; do
  [ -r "$f" ] || continue
  if LC_ALL=C grep -aqE "$PAT" "$f" 2>/dev/null; then echo "$f" >> "$CONTENTX"; fi
done < "$KEEP1"
comm -23 "$KEEP1" <(sort -u "$CONTENTX") > "$KEEP2"
sort -u "$KEEP2" -o "$KEEP2"
echo "EXCLUDED_BY_CONTENT=$(wc -l < "$CONTENTX")"
echo "KEPT=$(wc -l < "$KEEP2")"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# READ-ONLY verification of findings A-E. No writes outside stdout.
S=$HOME/work/graphmark/agentic-swebench
R=$S/results

echo "########## A. modelUsage reconciles to cost; usage.* is lossy ##########"
python3 - <<'PY'
import json,glob,os
R=os.path.expanduser("~/work/graphmark/agentic-swebench/results")
tot={"n":0,"mu_cost":0.0,"cost":0.0,"mu_tok":0,"us_tok":0,"mismatch":0,"lossy":0,"worst":0.0}
for arm in ["baseline","eg","cmm","graphify"]:
    for f in sorted(glob.glob(f"{R}/REP50_r1_{arm}/{arm}/*/cc_out.json")):
        try: j=json.load(open(f))
        except Exception: continue
        u=j.get("usage") or {}; mu=j.get("modelUsage") or {}
        c=j.get("total_cost_usd") or 0.0
        muc=sum((v or {}).get("costUSD",0) or 0 for v in mu.values())
        ut=sum(u.get(k,0) for k in ("input_tokens","output_tokens","cache_read_input_tokens","cache_creation_input_tokens"))
        mt=0
        for v in mu.values():
            v=v or {}
            mt+=sum(v.get(k,0) or 0 for k in ("inputTokens","outputTokens","cacheReadInputTokens","cacheCreationInputTokens"))
        tot["n"]+=1; tot["cost"]+=c; tot["mu_cost"]+=muc; tot["us_tok"]+=ut; tot["mu_tok"]+=mt
        if c>0 and abs(muc-c)/c > 1e-9: tot["mismatch"]+=1
        if ut>0:
            r=mt/ut
            if r>1.05: tot["lossy"]+=1
            tot["worst"]=max(tot["worst"],r)
print(f"  rep50 sessions scanned         : {tot['n']}")
print(f"  sum(total_cost_usd)            : ${tot['cost']:.6f}")
print(f"  sum(modelUsage[*].costUSD)     : ${tot['mu_cost']:.6f}")
rel = abs(tot['mu_cost']-tot['cost'])/tot['cost'] if tot['cost'] else 0
print(f"  relative difference            : {rel:.3e}   sessions mismatching >1e-9: {tot['mismatch']}")
print(f"  usage.* total tokens           : {tot['us_tok']:,}")
print(f"  modelUsage total tokens        : {tot['mu_tok']:,}")

content.text:
Short answer up front: **50% is not what the fair measurements show for end-to-end sessions, and I just spent an audit proving why.** But there's a real 50%+ claim hiding next to it, and the two get conflated constantly. Let me separate them and then show you the turn-by-turn.

---

## The two different questions

**"How many tokens does one structural question cost?"** — graph wins enormously. Asking "who calls `redisCommand`" costs ~2,300 tokens through the graph versus ~654,000 reading all 23 referencing files. That's 283×, it's in `docs/DETAILS.md`, and it's real. Savings scale with symbol connectivity.

**"How many tokens does a whole coding session cost?"** — this is the one that matters commercially, and it's where every 50%+ headline this project published has been withdrawn. Fair paired measurement lands single-digit to mid-teens on mixed suites, ~0 on a representative stratified 100, and *negative* on short sessions.

You asked about big repos, which pushes toward the second question but under the conditions most favourable to it. So let's do the arithmetic properly.

---

## The pricing law you need first

The single most useful thing measured on this campaign:

> `log(tokens) ~ log(messages)`, **elasticity 1.682, r = 0.957**. Message-adjusted residual saving is **0.000** in every model.

Nothing *inside* a message prices. Only the **number of turns** prices, and it prices superlinearly. That's because every turn replays the whole conversation — add content at turn 3 and you pay for it again at turns 4…40. Delete a turn and you delete its output *and* shorten every replay after it.

So the entire token question reduces to one thing: **how many turns did the graph delete?**

| turns eg / turns baseline | token saving |
|---|---|
| 0.95 | 8% |
| 0.90 | 17% |
| 0.85 | 24% |
| 0.80 | 31% |
| 0.75 | 38% |
| **0.663** | **50%** |
| 0.60 | 58% |
| 0.50 | 69% |

**50% requires deleting a third of all turns.** That's the bar. Keep it in mind.

---

## Baseline, turn by turn — 30k-file monorepo

Issue: *"XTRIM trims the wrong stream entries when MAXLEN ~ is used."*

| # | turn | why it costs |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `grep -r XTRIM` | 40 hits: src, tests, docs, changelogs |
| 2 | Read `t_stream.c` lines 1-500 | wrong region, file is 3,200 lines |
| 3 | `grep streamTrim` | narrowing |
| 4 | Read `t_stream.c` 1800-2100 | found something adjacent |
| 5 | Read `stream.h` | needs the struct |
| 6 | `grep MAXLEN` | still not the right function |
| 7 | Read `t_stream.c` 2400-2600 | **actual fix site** |
| 8 | Edit | |
| 9 | `make` | fails: wrong field name |
| 10 | Read struct again | |
| 11 | Edit | |
| 12 | `make` | ok |
| 13 | `ls tests/` | which test? |
| 14 | `grep -r xtrim tests/` | |
| 15 | `./runtest --single unit/type/stream` | wrong invocation |
| 16 | Read `tests/README` | |
| 17 | `./runtest ...` | passes |
| 18 | `grep streamTrim` again | who else calls this? |
| 19 | Read 2 call sites | |
| 20 | done | |

**20 turns. Locate = 7. Post-edit = 11.** In a small repo turns 1-7 collapse to about 2; in a monorepo they inflate to 10-15. That's the part that scales with repo size.

---

## Entire Graph, turn by turn

| # | turn | what the payload already contained |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `entire graph search --query "XTRIM trims wrong stream entries with MAXLEN ~"` | rank-1 = **complete body** of the fix function with real line numbers; **RELATED SITES** = the callers and sibling implementations that need the same edit; **SAME-CONCEPT LITERAL** = every place `MAXLEN` is named, tagged EDIT/CONSUMER/DOC (this is turn 18's grep, pre-answered); **COVERING TEST** + ALSO COVERING; **VERIFY:** the narrowest test command derived from the repo's own build files; **CLOSED-SET** warning if a switch over an enum would compile and then throw |
| 2 | Edit directly from the payload | no file read — you already have the whole function |
| 3 | Run the printed VERIFY command | passes, or names one error |
| 4 | (if needed) fix + re-verify | |

**4-6 turns.** Ratio 5/20 = 0.25 → **~90% token saving** on this task.

That is the mechanism working perfectly. It's also not what happens on average, and the gap is the interesting part.

---

## Why the measured number is far below that

Four things I verified, in descending order of damage:

**1. The graph is absent where the cost is.** 97.7% of excess cost in losing sessions lands *after the first edit* — repeated harness invocations (`./runtest` 11×, `cargo test` 7×, `javac` 19×), each dragging in sleep, pkill, port juggling, log re-reading. Meanwhile 86% of graph usage is pre-edit only. The tool attacks turns 1-7 and ignores turns 9-17. Localization is comparatively free.

**2. Agents call it ~1.5 times per session, invariant across six configs.** Enrichment didn't raise usage — it *raised* the grep count. You can't save turns the agent doesn't route through you.

**3. Payload size is nearly free, so making the answer richer doesn't help.** Eight-plus payload-quality metrics have been tested as levers and all died. Only call-count and turn-count pools move the number.

**4. Cache-read dominates.** I measured rep50 directly: **95.5% of "total tokens" is cache-read** (137M of 143M for the eg arm). Cache reads bill at ~10% of input price, so token count and *cost* move differently. If you care about dollars, the lever is output tokens and turn count, not payload bytes.

---

## My honest estimate for big repos

Big repos help, for a reason I can defend: session length is the mechanism, and repo size drives session length. Measured band structure — sessions under 12 turns *cost* more with the graph; savings peak at **−30.7% in the 20-29 turn band**; Sonnet at ≥20 baseline turns showed −14.1% versus +34.1% below 20.

| scenario | estimate | basis |
|---|---|---|
| Single structural query (who calls X, what breaks) | **90-99%** | measured, 283× on a well-connected symbol |
| Big monorepo, long session (25+ turns), locate-heavy | **20-35%** | fair 20-set measured −30.6% [−48.7, −5.0], winners 15/19 |
| Representative mixed suite | **0-15%** | stratified 100 collapsed +12.64% → ~0 |
| Short session, named file, small repo | **−25 to −35% (worse)** | graph arm cost 27.8% more on already-cheap instances |

So for your framing — big repos, long sessions — **I'd say 25-30%, not 50%.** The one cell that showed +48.67% was n=4 with a paired sd of 52.9 points; three of six configs in that sweep flip sign on leave-one-out, and the same config measured +13.8% at n=26. It didn't replicate.

I'm not going to tell you 50% because you'd build a plan on it and the plan would fail the first honest cell, the same way the 54.9% and 57.7% numbers did.

---

## What I'd change, since you're asking me as owner

Ranked by expected turn deletion, which is the only currency:

**1. Move the tool past the edit.** Everything above says the money is in turns 9-17. Today `search` fires once, pre-edit, and the graph goes quiet exactly when the session starts burning. What's needed is a post-edit verb that owns the verify loop: given the diff, return *the* command, its expected failure modes, and on failure the resolved symbol/field/arity that's actually wrong — so the agent fixes from the answer rather than re-reading the struct. That alone is worth 4-6 turns of the 11 post-edit turns in the trace above.

**2. Make VERIFY runnable every time.** Losers die on unrunnable VERIFY commands. It already walks 32 ancestor dirs across 10 ecosystems, and when it lands it's genuinely good (I watched it derive `cd frontend && npx vitest run <path>` from `package.json` and `go test ./internal/sem -run '^TestX$'` from `go.mod`). The failures are the tail. Every unrunnable VERIFY converts turn 3 into turns 13-17.

**3. Kill the second locate.** ~1.5 calls/session means the agent searches, doesn't trust it, and greps. The fix isn't a bigger payload — it's the confidence tier, telling the agent *when the answer is rank-1-certain* so it stops looking.

**4. Stop the agent improvising harnesses.** Throwaway repro harnesses are 79% of the gain and 43% of the loss. When the graph names the proven command, the agent doesn't write its own; when it doesn't, the agent builds scaffolding and pays for it on every subsequent turn.

Do 1 and 2 and the turn ratio plausibly reaches 0.70-0.75 on long sessions, which is **38-45%**. That's the honest route to something with a 4 in front of it. It goes through the verify loop, not through better retrieval — retrieval is already at its ceiling (perfect retrieval was worth −29.8% at the configs tried, and gold-rank-1 sessions actually *lost* more often than misses in one 49-instance cell).

Want me to draft that post-edit verb as a design, or pull the exact per-turn cost decomposition from the rep50 transcripts to size lever 1 before you commit to it?

Base directory for this skill: /Users/suhaan/.claude/skills/graph-bench-forensics

# Graph benchmark forensics

Measure a context tool honestly, at the level of individual sessions and individual token classes.
This drill exists because aggregates on this benchmark are routinely wrong in *both* directions, and
every headline that was ever withdrawn was withdrawn for a reason this checklist catches.

## The cost model — get this right first, everything else follows

**Cost is not "tokens".** Solve for per-token prices from recorded `total_cost_usd` (least squares
over cache_read / cache_creation / output, n≈30) rather than assuming. Measured on rep30:

| model | $/Mtok cache_read | cache_creation | output | **cost share** cr / cc / out |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Fable 5 | 1.00 | 20.31 | 49.63 | 22% / 39% / 39% |
| Opus 5 | 0.50 | 10.19 | 24.73 | 26% / 38% / 36% |
| Sonnet | 0.29 | 6.33 | 14.78 | 41% / 31% / 28% |
| Haiku | 0.10 | 2.09 | 4.96 | 46% / 28% / 25% |

Two traps, both of which produced wrong conclusions:

- **"95% of tokens are cache_read" is a token COUNT, not a cost share.** Output is priced 20–50×
  higher, so it is 25–39% of the bill. A tool that cuts reading and raises writing LOSES money.
  Fable is the clean case: turns fell 10% and cost rose 15%, because output rose 14.7%.
- **Cost ≈ MESSAGES × context.** At a large context a message costs ~446k cache-read tokens. Count
  messages, not tool calls. (Note: parallel tool calls were not reachable in this harness — 0 of
  10,374 messages carried more than one — so "batch your calls" is un-actionable advice, and any
  prompt rule telling an agent to batch is dead weight given to both arms.)

Always report cache_read / cache_creation / output **separately**. The aggregate usd hides which
one moved, and which one moved is the finding.

## The noise floor — respect it or you will publish noise

- Same-instance spread across repeated cells: **45pt median**, tail to 335pt. One instance measured
  +404% / +97% / +69% across three configs.
- Every single-cell CI on this benchmark spans zero for the weaker models. **MDE ≈ CI width ≈ 31%
  at n=30**, so only effects ≥ ~30pt are detectable in one cell.
- **0/30 instances produce the same agent query twice** (median token overlap 0.55). Retrieval
  itself varies run to run, so any replay that fixes the query measures one sample of the input.

Rules that follow:
1. **Never score a partial cell.** A Sonnet geomean moved 47 points between n=9 and n=25.
2. **Never bucket one cell into sub-groups of 3–7 and read the differences.** That is how the
   "VERIFY-off is a −12pt lever" and "payload width costs 10.6pt" claims were produced, and both
   were retracted.
3. **Compare configs with replicates of the SAME config**, not two different configs' point
   estimates. Pooling different configs estimates "expected value across configs tried".
4. **Report bootstrap CIs, never a bare point estimate.**
5. Trust **deterministic offline replays** (re-issuing recorded queries against the binary) far
   more than single-session attributions.

## The measurement gate

A session counts only if `total_cost_usd > 0` **AND** `patch.diff` is non-empty. Drop pairs
**symmetrically** — if either arm gate-fails on an instance, the instance leaves both arms.
Otherwise a cheap gate-failure reads as a saving.

Also check before trusting any per-instance delta: `result` length, `num_turns`, and `subtype`
(`error_max_turns` sessions are right-censored, so their true cost is ≥ recorded).

## Fairness — the failure mode that has invalidated the most results

Every withdrawn headline on this benchmark came from **asymmetric prompts**, not from the tool.

- Diff the two arms' `prompt.txt` and account for **every** differing line. A "−35%" result once
  came from two extra instructions the tool arm had and the baseline did not (*"never write a
  throwaway test script"*, *"no `which`, no `ls vendor/`, no `find / -name php*`"*). Removing them
  moved the same cell from −14.9% to +9.1%.
- Frugality clamps belong in the **shared** block or nowhere.
- A tool-side default change (ranking, payload content, a flag) is legitimate. Extra *instructions*
  to one arm are not.
- Distinguish "tool as shipped, including its recommended prompt" from "the tool's marginal value
  under one contract". Both are real questions; say which you measured.

## The drill

### 1. Verify the data before analysing it
- Confirm inputs exist: repo clones, graphs, and **`patch.diff` for every gated session**.
- Check for silent loss: a driver that skips on the session log alone will skip forever a session
  whose patch vanished. On this suite a `/private/tmp` reap destroyed 4 patches, 27 graphs and
  every packfile — and the lost instances were ones the tool won by 20+ turns, biasing *against* it.
- Keep the suite off volatile paths.

### 2. Score the cell
Per-instance paired table: usd, turns, cache_read/cache_creation/output, gate status. Then geomean
+ bootstrap CI. Then per-language, then per-instance sorted by contribution to the shortfall.

### 3. Decompose the transcripts — this is where the answers are
For each session (`~/.claude/projects/*/<session_id>.jsonl`, keyed off `cc_out.json:session_id`):

- **Phase split at the first Edit/Write.** Post-edit is typically ~65% of output and is where every
  losing instance's delta lives.
- **Per-tool token attribution.** Dedupe by `message.id`, credit each message's `output_tokens` to
  its tool. This tells you whether the delta is Edit bodies, Bash commands, or prose.
- **Count**: Edit/Write calls, distinct files touched, throwaway/repro scripts, prose length.
- **Classify every grep/find/read** the tool arm still ran (see below).

### 4. The single strongest predictor found: grep elimination
Compute `eg_greps / baseline_greps` per instance.

| greps eliminated | Haiku | Sonnet |
|---|---|---|
| >75% | **−46.1%** | — |
| 40–75% | −39.6% | −17.3% |
| <40% | +1.9% | +31.8% |

corr(grep ratio, log usd) = **+0.615 Haiku / +0.712 Sonnet**, while corr(**baseline** greps,
outcome) ≈ 0 — so it is not task difficulty leaking through. **This is the metric to optimise.**

Then classify the *residual* greps to decide what to fix:

| what the grep was for | share | fix |
|---|---|---|
| finding something NEW | 38% | recall / ranking |
| searching inside a file the payload returned | 29% | payload under-delivery |
| re-finding a symbol the payload already gave | 25% | payload under-delivery |
| env / build hunting | 8% | verify-command quality |

### 5. Falsify offline before spending a cell
Recorded queries live at `results/<tag>/eg/<instance>/gq_calls.log`, emitted payloads at the same
path + `.payload`, worktrees at `replay-wt/<instance>`. Replay against the binary at **zero model
cost** and assert the change does what you claim — *and* that nothing else moved.

Replay across **every** recorded query variant, not one, because the agent rephrases every run.

### 6. Only then run a cell, and pre-register
Write the prediction and its falsification bounds to a file **before** the run. An out-of-sample
prediction that survives is worth more than ten post-hoc explanations. (Worked: Opus predicted
−0.1% from band effects fitted on cells excluding it; measured −0.5%, n=30.)

## Known results — do not re-derive these

- **≥35% is refuted, not unproven.** The favourable CI bound on total tokens is −27.8%
  (`eg-consolidated/AGENTS.md`). Independent rep30 measurement: Haiku −24.1% CI [−36.6, −8.3].
- Four models, rep30, paired: Fable +14.9%, Opus −0.5%, Sonnet +9.4%, Haiku −24.1%. **The tool
  saves on one of four.**
- Savings depend on how much the *no-tool* arm explores: pooled n=175, corr −0.238
  [−0.346, −0.134]; costs money under ~12 baseline turns, peaks ≈ −30% at 20–49, tapers above.
  **It does not explain Sonnet** (predicted −14.5%, measured +9.4% — a 24pt miss).
- Raising the turn cap does **not** help — both arms grow proportionally (−24.1% → −21.3%).
- Prefetching the search from the issue text is **dominated**: gold-visible@5 0.567 vs 0.715 for the
  agent's own distilled query, 8 losses to 0 wins. The invocation turn is irreducible.
- Retrieval quality and token savings are **different axes**. A config that improved gold-visible
  0.729 → 0.829 across 167 real queries measured *worse* on tokens.

## Discipline

- Keep an **audit ledger**: every claim tagged solid / moderate / retracted, with its basis. Publish
  the retractions.
- When a result contradicts an earlier one, find the mechanism before believing either.
- Correct memory notes in place when they are falsified; a wrong note propagates.
- **Do not stop at a negative finding.** Every apparent dead end here dissolved one layer down — in
  the transcripts, the harness, or the tool's source. But going deeper is the way through, not a
  licence to loosen the standard of evidence: report the interval, report what you retracted, and
  say plainly when a target is not reached.


ARGUMENTS: decompose REP50_r1 (49 instances × 4 arms) per-turn: pre-edit vs post-edit token cost, size the post-edit lever toward 35%

The skill is decisive on one point I have to carry: **≥35% is refuted, not unproven** — favourable CI bound −27.8%, rep30 Haiku −24.1% [−36.6, −8.3]. It also says don't stop at a negative finding, go a layer deeper. So I'll run the decomposition and size exactly what would have to change.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""REP50 per-turn forensics. Read-only. Follows graph-bench-forensics drill §3-4.
Phase split at first Edit/Write. Dedupe usage by message.id. Report cr/cc/out separately."""
import json, os, re, sys, glob, collections

S = os.path.expanduser("~/work/graphmark/agentic-swebench")
PROJ = os.path.expanduser("~/.claude/projects")
ARMS = ["baseline", "eg", "cmm", "graphify"]

# index every transcript by basename (session id)
tx = {}
for f in glob.glob(f"{PROJ}/**/*.jsonl", recursive=True):
    tx.setdefault(os.path.basename(f)[:-6], []).append(f)

GREPLIKE = re.compile(r'\b(grep|egrep|fgrep|rg|ag|ack|find|locate|ls\s+-R|glob)\b')
BUILDLIKE = re.compile(r'\b(make|cmake|go\s+(build|test|vet)|cargo|mvn|gradle|npm|npx|pnpm|yarn|pytest|python\s+-m\s+pytest|phpunit|composer|bundle|rake|rspec|ctest|javac|tsc|jest|vitest|runtest)\b')

def classify(cmd):
    c = (cmd or "")[:400]
    if GREPLIKE.search(c): return "grep"
    if BUILDLIKE.search(c): return "build"
    return "other"

rows = []
for arm in ARMS:
    base = f"{S}/results/REP50_r1_{arm}/{arm}"
    if not os.path.isdir(base): continue
    for iid in sorted(os.listdir(base)):
        d = f"{base}/{iid}"
        cc = f"{d}/cc_out.json"
        if not os.path.exists(cc) or os.path.getsize(cc) == 0: continue
        try: j = json.load(open(cc))
        except Exception: continue
        sid = j.get("session_id")
        pd = f"{d}/patch.diff"
        r = dict(arm=arm, iid=iid, sid=sid,
                 usd=j.get("total_cost_usd") or 0.0,
                 turns=j.get("num_turns") or 0,
                 subtype=j.get("subtype"),
                 patch_bytes=os.path.getsize(pd) if os.path.exists(pd) else 0,
                 dur_ms=j.get("duration_ms") or 0)
        u = j.get("usage") or {}
        r.update(cr=u.get("cache_read_input_tokens",0), cc_tok=u.get("cache_creation_input_tokens",0),
                 out=u.get("output_tokens",0), inp=u.get("input_tokens",0))

"""Classify every residual grep in the REP50 eg arm against what the payload already delivered.
Read-only. Taxonomy per graph-bench-forensics §4."""
import json, os, re, glob, collections

S = os.path.expanduser("~/work/graphmark/agentic-swebench")
PROJ = os.path.expanduser("~/.claude/projects")
tx = {}
for f in glob.glob(f"{PROJ}/**/*.jsonl", recursive=True):
    tx.setdefault(os.path.basename(f)[:-6], []).append(f)

GREPLIKE = re.compile(r'\b(grep|egrep|fgrep|rg|ag|ack|find|locate)\b')
BUILDENV = re.compile(r'\b(node_modules|vendor|which|command -v|\.cargo|go env|python -V|pip |package\.json|go\.mod|Cargo\.toml|pom\.xml|build\.gradle|Makefile|CMakeLists|composer\.json|\.venv|site-packages)\b')
# pull the search term out of a grep-ish command
TERM = re.compile(r'''(?:grep|egrep|fgrep|rg|ag|ack)\b(?:\s+-{1,2}[\w-]+(?:=\S+)?)*\s+(?:-e\s+)?(["']?)(.+?)\1(?:\s|$)''')
PATHARG = re.compile(r'(?:^|\s)((?:\./)?[\w./-]+\.(?:go|py|js|ts|tsx|jsx|rs|java|rb|php|c|h|cc|cpp|hpp|kt|swift|scala|cs|md))\b')

def norm(t):
    t = re.sub(r'[\\^$.*+?()\[\]{}|]', ' ', t or '')
    return {w.lower() for w in re.findall(r'[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]{2,}', t)}

cats = collections.Counter(); per_inst = {}
examples = collections.defaultdict(list)
base = f"{S}/results/REP50_r1_eg/eg"
for iid in sorted(os.listdir(base)):
    d = f"{base}/{iid}"
    cc = f"{d}/cc_out.json"
    if not os.path.exists(cc) or os.path.getsize(cc) == 0: continue
    sid = (json.load(open(cc)) or {}).get("session_id")
    # payload the tool actually delivered, and the paths it named
    payload = ""
    p = f"{d}/gq_calls.log.payload"
    if os.path.exists(p): payload = open(p, errors="replace").read()
    payload_tokens = norm(payload)
    payload_paths = set(re.findall(r'([\w./-]+\.(?:go|py|js|ts|tsx|jsx|rs|java|rb|php|c|h|cc|cpp|hpp|kt|swift|scala|cs))', payload))
    c = collections.Counter()
    for f in tx.get(sid or "", []):
        for line in open(f, errors="replace"):
            try: o = json.loads(line)
            except Exception: continue
            m = o.get("message") or {}
            for b in (m.get("content") or []) if isinstance(m.get("content"), list) else []:
                if not isinstance(b, dict) or b.get("type") != "tool_use" or b.get("name") != "Bash": continue
                cmd = (b.get("input") or {}).get("command") or ""
                if not GREPLIKE.search(cmd): continue
                if BUILDENV.search(cmd):
                    c["env_build"] += 1; examples["env_build"].append(cmd[:110]); continue
                mt = TERM.search(cmd); term = mt.group(2) if mt else ""
                tset = norm(term)
                paths = set(PATHARG.findall(cmd))
                scoped = bool(paths & payload_paths)
                known = bool(tset) and bool(tset & payload_tokens)
                if scoped and known: k = "reread_delivered_file"
                elif scoped:         k = "inside_delivered_file"
                elif known:          k = "refind_delivered_symbol"
                else:                k = "genuinely_new"
                c[k] += 1; examples[k].append(cmd[:110])
    per_inst[iid] = c
    cats.update(c)

tot = sum(cats.values())
print(f"REP50 eg arm — residual grep/find taxonomy  (n={tot} across 49 sessions)\n")
LABEL = {
 "genuinely_new":        "finding something NEW            -> recall / ranking",
 "refind_delivered_symbol":"re-finding a symbol payload gave -> PAYLOAD UNDER-DELIVERY",
 "inside_delivered_file": "searching inside a returned file -> PAYLOAD UNDER-DELIVERY",
 "reread_delivered_file": "both of the above                -> PAYLOAD UNDER-DELIVERY",
 "env_build":            "env / build hunting              -> verify-command quality",
}
for k, v in cats.most_common():
    print(f"  {v:>4}  {100*v/max(1,tot):>5.1f}%   {LABEL.get(k,k)}")
fixable = sum(cats[k] for k in ("refind_delivered_symbol","inside_delivered_file","reread_delivered_file"))
print(f"\n  FIXABLE WITHOUT BETTER RETRIEVAL (payload under-delivery): {fixable} = {100*fixable/max(1,tot):.1f}%")
print(f"  env/build (verify-command lever):                          {cats['env_build']} = {100*cats['env_build']/max(1,tot):.1f}%")
print(f"  needs genuinely better recall:                             {cats['genuinely_new']} = {100*cats['genuinely_new']/max(1,tot):.1f}%")
print("\nsample commands per class:")
for k in LABEL:
    if examples[k]:
        print(f"  [{k}]")
        for e in examples[k][:3]: print(f"     {e}")

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Corrected: payload-hit restricted to sessions with a logged payload; winner/loser vs uptake."""
import json, os, re, statistics, collections
S = os.path.expanduser("~/work/graphmark/agentic-swebench")
EXT = r'(?:go|py|js|ts|tsx|jsx|rs|java|rb|php|c|h|cc|cpp|hpp|kt|swift|scala|cs|m)'
PATHANY = re.compile(r'([\w./-]+\.' + EXT + r')')

def rows(arm):
    b = f"{S}/results/REP50_r1_{arm}/{arm}"; out = {}
    for iid in sorted(os.listdir(b)):
        d = f"{b}/{iid}"; cc = f"{d}/cc_out.json"
        if not os.path.exists(cc) or os.path.getsize(cc) == 0: continue
        j = json.load(open(cc)); u = j.get("usage") or {}
        out[iid] = dict(d=d, usd=j.get("total_cost_usd") or 0, turns=j.get("num_turns") or 0,
                        tot=sum(u.get(k,0) for k in ("input_tokens","output_tokens","cache_read_input_tokens","cache_creation_input_tokens")),
                        patch=os.path.getsize(f"{d}/patch.diff") if os.path.exists(f"{d}/patch.diff") else 0)
    return out
B, E = rows("baseline"), rows("eg")

def pfiles(p):
    s = set()
    if os.path.exists(p):
        for L in open(p, errors="replace"):
            if L.startswith('+++ b/'): s.add(L[6:].strip())
    return {x for x in s if x and x != '/dev/null'}

recs = []
for iid, e in E.items():
    d = e["d"]
    pp = f"{d}/gq_calls.log.payload"; gq = f"{d}/gq_calls.log"
    has_pl = os.path.exists(pp) and os.path.getsize(pp) > 0
    payload = open(pp, errors="replace").read() if has_pl else ""
    calls = [l.split()[0] for l in open(gq, errors="replace") if l.split()] if os.path.exists(gq) else []
    edited = pfiles(f"{d}/patch.diff")
    names = {os.path.basename(x) for x in PATHANY.findall(payload)}
    hit = bool(edited) and any(os.path.basename(x) in names for x in edited)
    b = B.get(iid)
    dtok = 1 - e["tot"]/b["tot"] if b and b["tot"] else None
    recs.append(dict(iid=iid, has_pl=has_pl, hit=hit, calls=len(calls),
                     verbs=collections.Counter(calls), dtok=dtok,
                     dturn=e["turns"]-b["turns"] if b else None, pl=len(payload)))

pl = [r for r in recs if r["has_pl"]]
print("="*76)
print("PAYLOAD-HIT, corrected — only sessions whose payload was actually logged")
print("="*76)
print(f"  sessions with a logged payload : {len(pl)} of {len(recs)}")
h = sum(1 for r in pl if r["hit"])
print(f"  payload NAMED the edited file  : {h}/{len(pl)} = {100*h/max(1,len(pl)):.1f}%")
print(f"  payload MISSED it              : {len(pl)-h}/{len(pl)} = {100*(len(pl)-h)/max(1,len(pl)):.1f}%")
print("  (sessions with calls but NO logged payload are a KNOWN eg-q logging bug, not a miss)")

print("\n" + "="*76)
print("UPTAKE vs OUTCOME")
print("="*76)
def grp(name, sel):
    g = [r for r in recs if sel(r) and r["dtok"] is not None]
    if not g: return
    print(f"  {name:<34} n={len(g):<3} median token delta {100*statistics.median([r['dtok'] for r in g]):+7.1f}%  "
          f"median calls {statistics.median([r['calls'] for r in g]):.0f}  median dturns {statistics.median([r['dturn'] for r in g]):+.0f}")
grp("payload logged AND hit gold",   lambda r: r["has_pl"] and r["hit"])
grp("payload logged, MISSED gold",   lambda r: r["has_pl"] and not r["hit"])
grp("no payload logged",             lambda r: not r["has_pl"])
grp("0 graph calls",                 lambda r: r["calls"] == 0)
grp("1 graph call",                  lambda r: r["calls"] == 1)
grp("2 graph calls",                 lambda r: r["calls"] == 2)
grp(">=3 graph calls",               lambda r: r["calls"] >= 3)
grp("used search at least once",     lambda r: r["verbs"].get("search",0) >= 1)
grp("never used search",             lambda r: r["verbs"].get("search",0) == 0)
grp("used graph-grep verb",          lambda r: r["verbs"].get("grep",0) >= 1)

print("\n" + "="*76)
print("CALL-COUNT DISTRIBUTION (what the agent actually did with the tool)")
print("="*76)
cc = collections.Counter(r["calls"] for r in recs)
for k in sorted(cc): print(f"  {k} graph call(s): {cc[k]} sessions")
print(f"  mean {statistics.mean([r['calls'] for r in recs]):.2f} calls/session   "
      f"total {sum(r['calls'] for r in recs)}")
allv = collections.Counter()
for r in recs: allv.update(r["verbs"])
print(f"  verb mix: {dict(allv)}")

content.text:
I have the full mechanism now. One important retraction first, because I almost shipped a wrong number.

## I refuted my own lever before reporting it

On medians, "used search" looked like a 38-point swing (+8.9% vs −29.7%). On **sum-based pooling it reverses**: search-users +0.76%, never-search +2.95%. The median was being driven by small sessions; the big-token sessions dominate the pool and go the other way. Counterfactual value of forcing search-first: **+1.6 points**, not 38. That's the exact trap the drill warns about — sub-grouping one cell and reading the differences. Struck.

## The honest state of rep50

```
POOLED as-run: +1.35%   bootstrap 95% CI [-17.0%, +18.2%]
```

The CI is 35 points wide at n=49. rep50 as configured **cannot resolve a 35% effect** — and its point estimate is +1.35%.

## Where the tokens actually are

`corr(Δturns, token saving) = −0.854`. Turns are the whole story, and the elasticity law predicts it almost exactly:

| | value |
|---|---|
| turns baseline → eg | 2671 → 2709 (ratio **1.014**) |
| predicted from elasticity 1.682 | −2.4% |
| measured | +1.35% |

**eg uses more turns than baseline.** That is the entire result. Everything else is downstream.

**The bar for your goal, exactly:**

| target | eg turns needed | cut from now | per session |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 20% | 2339 | 369 | 7.5 |
| 25% | 2251 | 457 | 9.3 |
| 30% | 2160 | 548 | 11.2 |
| **35%** | **2067** | **641** | **13.1** |

From 55.3 turns/session down to 42.2. That's the whole goal, in one number.

## Winners vs losers — it's a band effect, not a bug

| | winners (24) | losers (25) |
|---|--:|--:|
| median token delta | **+31.1%** | **−45.8%** |
| baseline turns (median) | **58** | **43** |
| eg turns (median) | 43 | 54 |
| Δturns | **−8** | **+9** |
| greps/session | 13 (7 new / 6 re-find) | 17 (**10 new** / 2 re-find) |

Winners: `lombok-3674` 122→67 turns (+71%), `fmt-2457` 67→38 (+62%), `redis-11510` 56→34 (+68%).
Losers: `prometheus-9248` 68→110 (−75%), `valkey-790` 54→93 (−127%), `bat-1892` 65→100 (−80%).

**eg rescues sessions that were already going to flail, and taxes sessions that were already efficient.** When the baseline needs 58 turns, the graph cuts 15. When the baseline needs 43, the graph adds 11. Losers' greps are 10/17 "genuinely new" with only 2 re-finds — the payload was never in play for them.

## What I expected the graph to do vs what it did

You asked me to predict first. Design intent for a big-repo fix:

> 1 `search` → rank-1 complete body → edit from the payload → 1 `impact` for blast radius → run the printed VERIFY → done. **2–3 graph calls, 0–2 greps, 6–10 turns.**

Measured:

| | expected | actual |
|---|--:|--:|
| graph calls/session | 2–3 | **2.14** ✅ |
| greps/session | 0–2 | **16.9** ❌ |
| turns/session | 6–10 | **55.3** ❌ |

The call count is *exactly right*. That's the surprise. **Graph calls are additive, not substitutive** — the agent makes its two calls and then runs a full 17-grep shell exploration anyway. The tool never displaces the thing it was built to displace.

## Is there a bug? Three, ranked

**1. `eg-q` ships a `grep` verb, and it is the most-used verb.** Verb mix across 105 calls: `grep 44`, `search 34`, `def 24`, `callers 3`. The agent routes the *code graph* into grep-emulation. Sessions using it: −4.6% median. You built a semantic retriever and the harness gave it a grep front door; agents take the door they recognise.

**2. Payload logging only covered `search`.** 16 of 49 sessions made graph calls but logged no payload — a known `eg-q` defect whose fix sits in the *uncommitted* working tree. Every published rep50 payload-quality metric is computed on 33/49 and is wrong. This is what inflated my first pass to "43% missed the gold file."

**3. Not a bug: retrieval.** Corrected, the payload named the file the agent actually edited in **28/33 = 84.8%**. Ranking is fine. Stop tuning it.

## Would I use it, and does 35% make sense in big repos

Yes, I'd use it — for **locate on an unfamiliar large codebase**, where it measurably wins: pre-edit output is −11.6% and the top winners cut 20–55 turns. That is a real, large effect.

But your intuition that navigation should be worth 35% doesn't survive the arithmetic, for one reason: **navigation isn't where the turns are.** Post-edit is 56–59% of all output, eg is +1.6% *worse* there, and the graph makes zero calls after the first edit. You can win the entire locate phase perfectly and still only touch ~44% of the budget.

35% is reachable only by deleting 13.1 turns/session, and there aren't 13 locate turns to delete — there are ~7 greps of the "genuinely new" class plus 2.1 graph calls. **The remaining turns are the verify loop, and the graph is absent from it.**

## Where we're missing

57.5% of residual greps are "finding something NEW" — but retrieval is 84.8% accurate. Those two only reconcile one way: **the agent isn't asking the graph.** It asks twice, gets a good answer, and then explores by hand anyway. The gap is uptake and displacement, not quality.

So the three things that could actually move it, in order:
1. **Remove the `grep` verb from the wrapper.** 42% of graph calls go somewhere that returns grep-shaped output and displaces nothing.
2. **Give the graph a post-edit verb** so it exists during the 56% of output it currently ignores.
3. **Make invocation displace, not supplement** — the payload has to answer the next question too, or the agent falls back to the shell and pays for both.

None of these is testable by argument, and the drill is explicit: falsify offline before spending a cell. I'm going to do that now — replay the 105 recorded queries plus the 829 residual greps against the binary at **zero model cost** and measure how many of those greps a changed config would actually have answered. That's the only honest way to size levers 1–3 before asking you to spend on a cell.

content.text:
Three explorers are mapping the wrapper/prompt surface, entire-graph's post-edit capabilities, and the exact phase split of those 829 greps.

While they run, here's the arithmetic any plan has to satisfy, because it constrains the design hard:

**Budget available per session (eg arm, measured):** 55.3 turns = 16.3 greps + 6.2 builds + 4.9 reads + 5.7 edits + 2.1 graph calls + ~20 prose/other.

**Need: −13.1 turns/session.** Against the grep taxonomy:

| grep class | per session | fixable by |
|---|--:|---|
| payload under-delivery | 4.8 | richer/wider payload |
| env + build hunting | 2.1 | VERIFY quality |
| genuinely new | 9.4 | **only if the agent asks the graph instead of the shell** |

Perfect payload + perfect verify = **6.9 turns ≈ 53% of what 35% requires**. That caps out around 20%. The remaining 6.2 turns can only come from the "genuinely new" class — which means the fix cannot be about answer *quality* (retrieval is already 84.8%). It has to be about **displacement**: the agent reaching for the graph instead of grep.

That splits the plan into two independent levers, and only one of them is about entire-graph's output. I'll wait for the explorers before committing to how.

content.text:
That reframes it, and I think it's the actual answer. Here's the architectural insight the numbers force:

**Every graph call today costs a turn. Turns are the only thing that prices.** Tokens ≈ messages^1.682, payload bytes are nearly free (eight payload-quality metrics have died as levers, call-count pools are the only ones that move). So a tool invoked *as a turn* has to delete more than one turn to break even — and measured, it deletes 1.10 turns per call. That's barely above water, which is exactly why rep50 lands at +1.35%.

So the architecture question isn't "how do we make the answer better." It's **how does the graph deliver information without consuming a turn.**

Three structural options, in increasing order of how much they change:

**1. Ride an existing turn (hooks).** A `PostToolUse` hook on Edit/Write runs the graph on the changed file and appends callers, sibling sites that share the defect, and the VERIFY command to the tool result the agent is already receiving. Cost: **zero turns**, some free bytes. This puts the graph inside the 56–59% of output where it currently makes literally zero calls, without the agent having to remember to call it. Nothing else on the table has this property.

**2. Be a first-class tool, not a bash script.** Baseline's `Grep`/`Glob`/`Read` are native tools the model reaches for reflexively. eg is a shell script it must remember exists — and the measured verb mix says it doesn't: 44 of 105 calls went to `eg-q grep`, i.e. the agent reached for grep *even inside the graph wrapper*. An MCP surface puts the graph in the tool list beside Grep. The README's own replacement criteria explicitly permit "each tool's normal interface," so this is fairness-legal.

**3. Intercept Grep itself.** Serve graph results when the agent greps. Strongest displacement, but I already have prior evidence this was tried and **caps at 38.9%** of greps interceptable — so it can't carry the goal alone, and it risks looking like arm-rigging rather than a tool interface.

The hook idea is the one I'd build the plan around, because it's the only lever that adds information at zero turn cost — and turn cost is the entire binding constraint. Everything else is fighting the elasticity curve.

Waiting on the explorers to confirm feasibility: whether `changed` works on a dirty worktree, whether VERIFY can be obtained without a full search, and — critically — whether the post-edit greps are actually the kind a hook could pre-empt. That last number decides whether this is worth 6 turns/session or 1.

**Post-processing:**

2. load `$GSYM` (`graph.symbols.ndjson`), map each hit line → enclosing symbol name via `start_line <= lno <= end_line`

## 5. `--path` scoping and batched `def` (commit `607b2a4`, 2026-08-08)

Motivation in the commit body: rep50 tool arm made 94 graph calls but still ran **905 shell exploration calls** vs no-tool's 995 = **0.96 shell calls displaced per graph call**; turn count went UP by 38, token delta +1.35%. Classifying 357 greps: **scoped to file/dir 233 (65%)**, batched multi-symbol 68 (19%, 192 names), free text 36 (10%), single symbol 20 (6%).

### `search --path <dir|file|glob>` (repeatable)
- Parsed `/Users/suhaan/devenv/entire-graph/internal/cli/search.go:1703-1708` → `flags.PathScope []string` (declared :63-65).
- Over-fetch BEFORE filter: `internal/cli/search.go:179` → `searchTopK = min(TopK * pathScopeOverfetch, pathScopeMaxFetch)` where `pathScopeOverfetch = 12`, `pathScopeMaxFetch = 200` (`/Users/suhaan/devenv/entire-graph/internal/cli/search_pathscope.go:13-14`).

- `pathScopeMatches` `search_pathscope.go:27` — 3 forms: exact file · directory prefix (`scope` or `scope/`) · `path.Match` glob. A separator-free glob is ALSO tried against `path.Base` so `--path "*_test.go"` behaves like `find -name`.
- **NEVER-EMPTY** (`search_pathscope.go:51-68`): if nothing matches, returns the **unscoped head** silently. Rationale :52-55 — 3 of 4 live sessions abandoned the tool permanently after one empty answer.
- Ranks renumbered 1..N (:76-79) so a scoped payload doesn't open at "2.".

**LIMITS:** (a) it is a **post-filter on a ranked pool**, not a scoped index — an in-scope hit ranked below 200 is unreachable; (b) silent fallback means you **cannot distinguish "nothing here" from "here it is"**; (c) **`--path` is not in `printHelp`** (`grep -- --path internal/cli/root.go` → 0 hits) — undiscoverable; (d) only `search` has it. `def`, `impact`, `neighbors`, `changed` do not.

### `def NAME NAME NAME`
- Parsed in the `default:` arm `/Users/suhaan/devenv/entire-graph/internal/cli/def.go:332` → `flags.Symbols = append(...)`; `flags.Symbol` = first. Rejects anything starting with `-` (:329).

- Text/agent format prints `== NAME ==` header when `len(symbols) > 1` (:359) with a blank-line separator (:356).
- `--brief` (def.go:79, set at :300) drops source bodies, keeps the card: `if !flags.Brief { writeDefBodies(...) }` (:218). Measured on this repo, same 5 names: **batched grep 1,889 B · def with bodies 11,482 B · def --brief 895 B.** Single-symbol `def` unchanged (still full body).

## 6. Cost / latency (measured on this repo, 2026-08-08, macOS/darwin 25.5.0, dirty tree = 34 paths incl. nested `.claude/worktrees/`)

| invocation | wall | cache |
|---|---|---|
| `changed --repo .` (cold) | **14.36 s** | miss |
| `changed --repo .` (2nd, "warm") | **14.26 s** | **still miss** |
| `def X --brief` (worktree) | 14.20 s | miss |
| `impact --symbol X` (worktree) | 14.21 s / `index_latency_ms: 14188` | `index_cache_hit: false` |
| `impact --symbol X --head` (1st, builds cache) | 14.75 s | miss, writes |
| `impact --symbol X --head` (2nd) | **0.138 s** / `index_latency_ms: 125` | **hit** |
| `search --profile full --top-k 3` (worktree) | 5.68 s | miss (search bounds indexed files) |
| `search --head --profile full --top-k 3` (1st) | 9.09 s | miss |
| `search --head --profile full --top-k 3` (2nd) | **0.939 s** | hit |

**WHY the worktree cache is dead here** (`worktreeCacheDigest` `/Users/suhaan/devenv/entire-graph/internal/sem/search_cache.go:133`, commit `503a554`):
- `gitutil.WorktreeContentDigest` `/Users/suhaan/devenv/entire-graph/internal/gitutil/worktree.go:93`. Clean tree ⇒ `""` ⇒ HEAD tree hash is the key. Dirty ⇒ HEAD ⊕ sha256 of per-path status+digest.
- **`MaxDirtyFilesForDigest = 64`** (`internal/gitutil/worktree.go:61`). >64 dirty paths ⇒ `ErrWorktreeTooDirty` ⇒ `cacheable = false`.
- `git status` reports a **nested worktree/repo as ONE directory entry**; `hashDirectory` worktree.go:177 must then digest every file underneath, charged against `budget - len(paths)` (worktree.go:145). `.claude/worktrees/` blows the budget ⇒ **`ErrWorktreeTooDirty` ⇒ every worktree query re-indexes from scratch, forever.** Exactly the user's stated symptom.
- Memoized 2 s: `worktreeCleanTTL = 2 * time.Second` (search_cache.go:65), `worktreeCleanVerdicts sync.Map` :80, `sem.InvalidateWorktreeCleanVerdicts()` :~165 for long-lived embedders.

**Cheap enough to call after every edit:**
- ✅ Anything with `--head` on a warm cache: **~0.15 s** (`impact`, `def`, `neighbors`) / ~0.9 s (`search`). But `--head` is **blind to the edit** — useless for post-edit.
- ❌ **Nothing that sees the working tree is cheap on this repo.** `changed` is 14 s and structurally cannot use `--head` (`Worktree: true` hard-coded at changed.go:168; `--head` rejected at :133).
- The 14 s is a **full-repo re-index**, not the delta computation: `query_latency_ms` is ~3 ms, `index_latency_ms` is ~14,188 ms. A post-edit verb that reuses an existing `--head` snapshot and only re-parses the ~N changed files would be ~0.15 s + N file parses.

## 7. THE GAP, stated as design input

1. **No verb takes a diff.** `changed` is the only worktree-aware verb and it takes zero input.
2. **VERIFY cannot be asked for.** It is a byproduct of ranking. There is no `verify-command --file X` / `--diff`.
3. **The four blocks that answer "what else must change / what will break"** (`search_related`, `search_closedset`, `search_sigtypes`, `callsite` guards) are all anchored on **query hits**. None is anchored on **edited spans**, even though `changed.go:318 symbolOverlapsHunks` already computes exactly that anchor set.
4. **No correctness check of any kind** — arity, type, name — exists. `def`/`sigtypes` show signatures; nothing compares them to a call site.
5. **`changed` is invisible**: not in help, not in `graphVerbs` (so `stats` under-reports it), not in `capabilities`, not in the embedded `agentGuide`, and has **no test**.
6. **Cost wall**: any worktree-aware answer costs a full re-index (14 s here) because dirty-tree caching dies on `MaxDirtyFilesForDigest = 64` / nested worktrees. Fixing the cache, or building the post-edit verb as `--head snapshot + incremental reparse of changed files only`, is a precondition for "call after every edit".</result>
