content.text:
Explorer 2 back. The decisive structural finding:

**Every block that answers "what else must change / what will break" already exists — they're just anchored to the wrong thing.**

| block | what it answers | anchored on |
|---|---|---|
| `search_related.go` (950 L) | what else must change | **query hits** |
| `search_closedset.go` (996 L) | what breaks silently at runtime | **query hits** |
| `search_sigtypes.go` (430 L) | the types in this signature | **query hits**, off by default |
| `callsite.go` (25 KB) | real call line + enclosing guards | **query hits** |

Meanwhile `changed.go:318 symbolOverlapsHunks` **already computes the edited-span anchor set** and throws it away on everything except caller counts. The post-edit capability is mostly a rewiring job, not new analysis.

Three hard blockers it also found:

1. **VERIFY cannot be asked for.** `buildSearchVerifyCommand` is unexported, takes `[]SearchResult`, and lives inside `SearchRepository`. There is no `verify-command --file X`. The `--path` hack misfires — scoping to `changed.go` emitted a VERIFY for `TestDoctorPrintsEntireEnvironment`.
2. **No correctness check of any kind exists** — no arity, no type, no name check. `def` and sigtypes *show* signatures; nothing compares them to a call site. That's precisely the class of error that makes a patch fail to build.
3. **The cost wall.** Every worktree-aware query costs **14.2 s, warm or cold** — `index_latency_ms ≈ 14,188` vs `query_latency_ms ≈ 3`. It's a full re-index, caused by the same `MaxDirtyFilesForDigest = 64` / nested-worktree bug I hit earlier. A verb called after every edit at 14 s is a non-starter; this has to be fixed first or built as `--head snapshot + incremental reparse of changed files only`.

Also: `changed` has **zero tests**, isn't in `--help`, isn't in `graphVerbs` (so `stats` can't even see it), and its top-20 on this repo was entirely `.md` sections because Markdown is an inventory language with `CONTAINS/DEFINES`.

Waiting on the last explorer — the pre/post-edit split of the 829 greps — which sizes whether this is worth 6 turns/session or 1.

# Plan — move Entire Graph toward 35% token savings on SWE-bench Multilingual

## Context

The goal is 35% token savings. The current honest measurement is **+1.35%** on REP50_r1
(49 instances × 4 arms, Opus max), bootstrap 95% CI **[−17.0%, +18.2%]**. This plan exists because
the forensics say the shortfall has one cause, and it is not retrieval quality.

**Why tokens move at all.** `log(tokens) ~ log(messages)`, elasticity **1.682**, r=0.957;
message-adjusted residual saving is 0.000. Turns are the only thing that prices. Measured on rep50:
`corr(Δturns, token saving) = −0.854`.

**What that costs us.** To hit 35% the eg arm must run **2067 turns** against baseline's 2671 —
**641 fewer than the 2709 it actually ran**, i.e. **13.1 turns/session** removed (55.3 → 42.2).

**Where the turns are** (49 sessions, corrected to exclude `entire graph *` invocations from the
shell counts — my first pass miscounted them and reported "zero grep elimination", which was wrong):

| | baseline | eg | |
|---|--:|--:|---|
| shell exploration, pre-edit | 725 | 683 | −5.8% ✅ |
| shell exploration, post-edit | 542 | **606** | **+11.8%** ❌ |
| build/test runs | 508 | 493 | −3.0% ✅ |
| edits | 397 | 414 | +4.3% |
| graph calls | 0 | 105 (**98 pre / 7 post**) | 93% pre-edit |

**Displacement ratio: −0.21 shell calls removed per graph call.** The tool wins the phase it is
present in and loses more in the phase it is absent from. The post-edit pool is **19.5 turns/session**
(12.4 shell + 7.1 build) and the graph makes **0.14 calls/session** there. It is the only pool large
enough to fund 13.1 turns.

**Retrieval is not the problem.** Payload named the file the agent actually edited in **28/33 = 84.8%**
of sessions that logged a payload. Stop tuning ranking.

**REP50 also measured a stale, misconfigured tool** — nine relevant commits landed after it ran
(`changed`, riders, `--path`, batched `def`, never-refuse, payload logging), it ran `EG_TOPK=5`
instead of 10, its `grep` verb ran raw `grep -rInE` across `node_modules/`, and **13 knobs
`run_REP50.sh` exported were silently dead** because `eg-q.run` hardcodes a fixed variable list.

---

## Design

One idea: **anchor the post-edit answer on the diff instead of on query hits.**

Every block that answers "what else must change / what will break" already exists and is wired to the
wrong anchor. `changed.go:318 symbolOverlapsHunks` already computes the edited-span anchor set and
discards it on everything except caller counts.

| existing block | answers | currently anchored on |
|---|---|---|
| `internal/sem/search_related.go` (950 L) | what else must change | query hits |
| `internal/sem/search_closedset.go` (996 L) | what breaks silently at runtime | query hits |
| `internal/cli/callsite.go` (25 KB) | real call line + enclosing guards | query hits |
| `internal/sem/search_verify.go` (1867 L) | the narrowest test command | query hits, **unexported** |

### A. entire-graph (`/Users/suhaan/devenv/entire-graph`)

1. **Make VERIFY askable.** `buildSearchVerifyCommand` (search_verify.go:199) is unexported and takes
   `[]SearchResult`. Extract a subject-based entry point taking `(repo, sourcePath, testPath)`;
   `SearchRepository` (search.go:1225) becomes one caller. Keep the four-tier ladder and the residual
   floor exactly as-is. Do **not** use the `--path` hack — verified to misfire (scoping to
   `changed.go` emitted a VERIFY for `TestDoctorPrintsEntireEnvironment`).

2. **New verb `entire graph postedit`.** Model on `internal/cli/changed.go`; reuse
   `gitutil.WorktreeChangedFiles` (worktree.go:277) and `symbolOverlapsHunks` (changed.go:318).
   Emits, budgeted, for the edited spans only:
   - callers of each changed definition (already in `changed`)
   - **related sites** — re-anchor `selectSearchRelatedSites` (search_related.go:345) on edited spans
   - **closed-set warning** — re-anchor `buildSearchClosedSet` (search_closedset.go:142) on edited spans
   - **VERIFY** for the edited file, from A.1
   - **arity/name check** (new, see A.3)

3. **Arity/name check — the one genuinely new analysis.** Nothing in the repo compares a signature to
   a call site; `def`/sigtypes only display. Build it from `callsite.go`'s existing raw material plus
   the symbol's signature: for each edited symbol whose parameter list changed, walk its resolved call
   sites and report arity mismatches and unresolved field/method names. This is the class of defect
   that makes a patch fail to build, which is what the post-edit loop is burning turns on.

4. **Fix the cost wall — precondition, not optional.** Every worktree-aware verb costs **14.2 s warm
   or cold** (`index_latency_ms ≈ 14,188` vs `query_latency_ms ≈ 3`); it is a full re-index, caused by
   `MaxDirtyFilesForDigest = 64` (gitutil/worktree.go:61) plus `hashDirectory` (worktree.go:177)
   walking nested worktrees. `postedit` must reuse a `--head` snapshot and incrementally reparse only
   the changed files. **Target < 1 s.** A verb called after every edit at 14 s is worse than useless.

5. **Housekeeping that changes measurement.** Add `changed`, `postedit`, `def`, `verify` to
   `graphVerbs` (internal/cli/stats.go:62) — today every call to them is invisible to `stats`. Add
   `changed`/`postedit` to `printHelp` and to the embedded `agentGuide` (internal/cli/agents.go).
   Filter inventory-only languages out of `changed`'s ranking (Markdown `section`/`code_fence` records
   currently fill the top-20). Write the tests `changed` has never had (zero today).

### B. Harness (`~/graphmark-bench/agentic-swebench` — the live copy, **not** `devenv/graphmark`)

6. **Un-break the knob surface.** `run_3arm.sh:457` hardcodes the variable list baked into
   `eg-q.run`; anything absent is dead for agent calls. Forward the 13 dead knobs. Restore
   `EG_TOPK=10`.
7. **Fix the `grep` verb.** It takes `rx="$*"`, so `eg-q grep -i wikidata` searched for the literal
   string `-i wikidata`. Apply the post-REP50 vendor/minified filter and the never-refuse
   grep→search fallback (`b5473b0b`), both already written.
8. **Deliver post-edit at zero turn cost.** A verb costs a turn; a rider costs none, and bytes are
   nearly free while turns price at elasticity 1.682. Wire `postedit` output as a `PostToolUse` rider
   on Edit/Write (`EG_CHANGED_RIDER` already exists in LIVE) and gate it — fire on the first edit per
   file, cap hard, never on a no-op edit.
9. **Port the fairness gate.** `_assert_prompt_symmetry` exists only in `devenv/graphmark`
   (run_3arm.sh:1002-1029). LIVE has no machine-checked prompt-symmetry gate. Port it before any cell.
   Prompt changes stay **capability description only** — the harness's own rule (`run_3arm.sh:1203`):
   the arm block says what the tool *is and returns*, never *when to use it*.

### C. Interface lever, measured separately (phase 2)

10. `EG_MCP=1` (run_3arm.sh:787) puts the graph in the model's native tool list beside `Grep`/`Read`.
    It is mutually exclusive with `--safe-mode`, which silently strips all MCP servers.
    **`--safe-mode` must be dropped for both arms or it is an arm confound** — and doing so makes the
    cell non-comparable to every prior cell, which is why it gets its own cell.

---

## Verification

**Gate 1 — offline replay, zero model cost (do this before spending anything).**
Per the forensics drill §5: replay the 105 recorded queries in `results/REP50_r1_eg/eg/*/gq_calls.log`
against the new binary, and reconstruct the 606 post-edit shell commands from the transcripts. Measure
what fraction `postedit` would actually have answered. **Proceed only if it answers ≥ 40%** — below
that the arithmetic cannot reach even 20% and the cells are wasted.

**Gate 2 — sealed pre-registration.**
Draw the holdout by set-difference against every burned selector: rep50 ∪ val30/h30 ∪ ho5/10/20 ∪
gate_5/10/20/30/60/300 ∪ prereg30/100 ∪ GEM300 ∪ fab82 ∪ SW_* ∪ G1/G2/G3. Freeze the id list, the
predicted effect and the falsification bounds to a file **before** the run, with sha256.

**Gate 3 — the cells.** Opus at effort `high`, `xhigh`, `max`. Gate a pair only if both arms have
`usd > 0` and a non-empty patch; drop symmetrically. Report cache_read / cache_creation / output
**separately**, geomean plus bootstrap CI, never a bare point estimate.

**Cost:** ~$307 per 49-instance 2-arm cell at Opus (rep50's 196 sessions cost $614). Three effort
levels ≈ **$920**; the phase-2 interface cell adds ~$307. Budget **~$1,200–1,900**.

**Power caveat:** at n=49 a single cell detects roughly a 25-point effect. The three effort levels can
each answer "does eg save at this effort", but **cannot reliably rank each other** — config-vs-config
MDE is ~94 points against ~74 points of observed spread. Do not read the ordering.

---

## Honest expected value, and the stop rule

Post-edit pool is 19.5 turns/session. Reaching 35% needs 13.1 — **67% of the entire post-edit phase
displaced**. Answering 40% of post-edit shell plus the env/build greps is ~7 turns/session, which the
elasticity curve prices at **≈20%**.

So: **15–25% is the realistic outcome of this plan; 35% requires near-total post-edit displacement and
is not something I can promise from the arithmetic.** The project's own drill records ≥35% as
*refuted, not unproven* — favourable CI bound −27.8%, independent rep30 Haiku −24.1% [−36.6, −8.3].

**Stop rule:** if Gate 1 shows `postedit` answering < 40% of post-edit shell calls, stop and report
rather than spending the cells. If the sealed cell lands below the pre-registered lower bound, the
result is published as a miss — no post-hoc subsetting, no matched-success filter, no re-drawing the
set.

print(f"\n  turns/session this represents          : {ans/49:.1f} of the 13.1 needed for 35%")
print("\nsamples:")

**This is the finding.** The pool is exactly the right size:

| post-edit, per session | baseline | eg |
|---|--:|--:|
| **improvised repro-harness calls** | **8.3** | **8.4** |
| real test-suite runs | 2.7 | 2.3 |
| sessions that improvise at all | 46/49 | **46/49** |

Agents build throwaway harnesses **3.6× more often than they run the real suite**, and eg doesn't reduce it *at all* — it's marginally worse. This matches the known mechanism: throwaway repro harnesses are 79% of the gain and 43% of the loss.

So the addressable post-edit pool is **8.4 improvised + 5.1 answerable-shell ≈ 13.5 turns/session** — against the **13.1 needed for 35%**. The lever isn't "answer greps," it's **stop the agent improvising a verification harness**, which is exactly what VERIFY exists for and is currently locked inside `search`, fires pre-edit, and gets ignored by 46/49 sessions.

That moves my honest estimate up: **21% if we halve the improvisation, ~32% if we mostly eliminate it.** 35% is now arithmetically in range rather than out of it.

# Plan — move Entire Graph toward 35% token savings on SWE-bench Multilingual

## Context

The goal is 35% token savings. The current honest measurement is **+1.35%** on REP50_r1
(49 instances × 4 arms, Opus max), bootstrap 95% CI **[−17.0%, +18.2%]**. This plan exists because
the forensics say the shortfall has one cause, and it is not retrieval quality.

**Why tokens move at all.** `log(tokens) ~ log(messages)`, elasticity **1.682**, r=0.957;
message-adjusted residual saving is 0.000. Turns are the only thing that prices. Measured on rep50:
`corr(Δturns, token saving) = −0.854`.

**What that costs us.** To hit 35% the eg arm must run **2067 turns** against baseline's 2671 —
**641 fewer than the 2709 it actually ran**, i.e. **13.1 turns/session** removed (55.3 → 42.2).

**Where the turns are** (49 sessions, corrected to exclude `entire graph *` invocations from the
shell counts — my first pass miscounted them and reported "zero grep elimination", which was wrong):

| | baseline | eg | |
|---|--:|--:|---|
| shell exploration, pre-edit | 725 | 683 | −5.8% ✅ |
| shell exploration, post-edit | 542 | **606** | **+11.8%** ❌ |
| build/test runs | 508 | 493 | −3.0% ✅ |
| edits | 397 | 414 | +4.3% |
| graph calls | 0 | 105 (**98 pre / 7 post**) | 93% pre-edit |

**Displacement ratio: −0.21 shell calls removed per graph call.** The tool wins the phase it is
present in and loses more in the phase it is absent from. The post-edit pool is **19.5 turns/session**
(12.4 shell + 7.1 build) and the graph makes **0.14 calls/session** there. It is the only pool large
enough to fund 13.1 turns.

**Retrieval is not the problem.** Payload named the file the agent actually edited in **28/33 = 84.8%**
of sessions that logged a payload. Stop tuning ranking.

**REP50 also measured a stale, misconfigured tool** — nine relevant commits landed after it ran
(`changed`, riders, `--path`, batched `def`, never-refuse, payload logging), it ran `EG_TOPK=5`
instead of 10, its `grep` verb ran raw `grep -rInE` across `node_modules/`, and **13 knobs
`run_REP50.sh` exported were silently dead** because `eg-q.run` hardcodes a fixed variable list.

---

## Design

One idea: **anchor the post-edit answer on the diff instead of on query hits.**

Every block that answers "what else must change / what will break" already exists and is wired to the
wrong anchor. `changed.go:318 symbolOverlapsHunks` already computes the edited-span anchor set and
discards it on everything except caller counts.

| existing block | answers | currently anchored on |
|---|---|---|
| `internal/sem/search_related.go` (950 L) | what else must change | query hits |
| `internal/sem/search_closedset.go` (996 L) | what breaks silently at runtime | query hits |
| `internal/cli/callsite.go` (25 KB) | real call line + enclosing guards | query hits |
| `internal/sem/search_verify.go` (1867 L) | the narrowest test command | query hits, **unexported** |

### A. entire-graph (`/Users/suhaan/devenv/entire-graph`)

1. **Make VERIFY askable.** `buildSearchVerifyCommand` (search_verify.go:199) is unexported and takes
   `[]SearchResult`. Extract a subject-based entry point taking `(repo, sourcePath, testPath)`;
   `SearchRepository` (search.go:1225) becomes one caller. Keep the four-tier ladder and the residual
   floor exactly as-is. Do **not** use the `--path` hack — verified to misfire (scoping to
   `changed.go` emitted a VERIFY for `TestDoctorPrintsEntireEnvironment`).

2. **New verb `entire graph postedit`.** Model on `internal/cli/changed.go`; reuse
   `gitutil.WorktreeChangedFiles` (worktree.go:277) and `symbolOverlapsHunks` (changed.go:318).
   Emits, budgeted, for the edited spans only:
   - callers of each changed definition (already in `changed`)
   - **related sites** — re-anchor `selectSearchRelatedSites` (search_related.go:345) on edited spans
   - **closed-set warning** — re-anchor `buildSearchClosedSet` (search_closedset.go:142) on edited spans
   - **VERIFY** for the edited file, from A.1
   - **arity/name check** (new, see A.3)

3. **Arity/name check — the one genuinely new analysis.** Nothing in the repo compares a signature to
   a call site; `def`/sigtypes only display. Build it from `callsite.go`'s existing raw material plus
   the symbol's signature: for each edited symbol whose parameter list changed, walk its resolved call
   sites and report arity mismatches and unresolved field/method names. This is the class of defect
   that makes a patch fail to build, which is what the post-edit loop is burning turns on.

4. **Fix the cost wall — precondition, not optional.** Every worktree-aware verb costs **14.2 s warm
   or cold** (`index_latency_ms ≈ 14,188` vs `query_latency_ms ≈ 3`); it is a full re-index, caused by
   `MaxDirtyFilesForDigest = 64` (gitutil/worktree.go:61) plus `hashDirectory` (worktree.go:177)
   walking nested worktrees. `postedit` must reuse a `--head` snapshot and incrementally reparse only
   the changed files. **Target < 1 s.** A verb called after every edit at 14 s is worse than useless.

5. **Housekeeping that changes measurement.** Add `changed`, `postedit`, `def`, `verify` to
   `graphVerbs` (internal/cli/stats.go:62) — today every call to them is invisible to `stats`. Add
   `changed`/`postedit` to `printHelp` and to the embedded `agentGuide` (internal/cli/agents.go).
   Filter inventory-only languages out of `changed`'s ranking (Markdown `section`/`code_fence` records
   currently fill the top-20). Write the tests `changed` has never had (zero today).

### B. Harness (`~/graphmark-bench/agentic-swebench` — the live copy, **not** `devenv/graphmark`)

6. **Un-break the knob surface.** `run_3arm.sh:457` hardcodes the variable list baked into
   `eg-q.run`; anything absent is dead for agent calls. Forward the 13 dead knobs. Restore
   `EG_TOPK=10`.
7. **Fix the `grep` verb.** It takes `rx="$*"`, so `eg-q grep -i wikidata` searched for the literal
   string `-i wikidata`. Apply the post-REP50 vendor/minified filter and the never-refuse
   grep→search fallback (`b5473b0b`), both already written.
8. **Deliver post-edit at zero turn cost.** A verb costs a turn; a rider costs none, and bytes are
   nearly free while turns price at elasticity 1.682. Wire `postedit` output as a `PostToolUse` rider
   on Edit/Write (`EG_CHANGED_RIDER` already exists in LIVE) and gate it — fire on the first edit per
   file, cap hard, never on a no-op edit.
9. **Port the fairness gate.** `_assert_prompt_symmetry` exists only in `devenv/graphmark`
   (run_3arm.sh:1002-1029). LIVE has no machine-checked prompt-symmetry gate. Port it before any cell.
   Prompt changes stay **capability description only** — the harness's own rule (`run_3arm.sh:1203`):
   the arm block says what the tool *is and returns*, never *when to use it*.

### C. Interface lever, measured separately (phase 2)

10. `EG_MCP=1` (run_3arm.sh:787) puts the graph in the model's native tool list beside `Grep`/`Read`.
    It is mutually exclusive with `--safe-mode`, which silently strips all MCP servers.
    **`--safe-mode` must be dropped for both arms or it is an arm confound** — and doing so makes the
    cell non-comparable to every prior cell, which is why it gets its own cell.

---

## Verification

**Gate 1 — offline replay, zero model cost (do this before spending anything).**
Per the forensics drill §5: replay the 105 recorded queries in `results/REP50_r1_eg/eg/*/gq_calls.log`
against the new binary, and reconstruct the 606 post-edit shell commands from the transcripts. Measure
what fraction `postedit` would actually have answered. **Proceed only if it answers ≥ 40%** — below
that the arithmetic cannot reach even 20% and the cells are wasted.

**Gate 2 — sealed pre-registration.**
Draw the holdout by set-difference against every burned selector: rep50 ∪ val30/h30 ∪ ho5/10/20 ∪
gate_5/10/20/30/60/300 ∪ prereg30/100 ∪ GEM300 ∪ fab82 ∪ SW_* ∪ G1/G2/G3. Freeze the id list, the
predicted effect and the falsification bounds to a file **before** the run, with sha256.

**Gate 3 — the cells.** Opus at effort `high`, `xhigh`, `max`. Gate a pair only if both arms have
`usd > 0` and a non-empty patch; drop symmetrically. Report cache_read / cache_creation / output
**separately**, geomean plus bootstrap CI, never a bare point estimate.

**Cost:** ~$307 per 49-instance 2-arm cell at Opus (rep50's 196 sessions cost $614). Three effort
levels ≈ **$920**; the phase-2 interface cell adds ~$307. Budget **~$1,200–1,900**.

**Power caveat:** at n=49 a single cell detects roughly a 25-point effect. The three effort levels can
each answer "does eg save at this effort", but **cannot reliably rank each other** — config-vs-config
MDE is ~94 points against ~74 points of observed spread. Do not read the ordering.

---

## Honest expected value, and the stop rule

Post-edit pool is 19.5 turns/session. Reaching 35% needs 13.1 — **67% of the entire post-edit phase
displaced**. Answering 40% of post-edit shell plus the env/build greps is ~7 turns/session, which the
elasticity curve prices at **≈20%**.

So: **15–25% is the realistic outcome of this plan; 35% requires near-total post-edit displacement and
is not something I can promise from the arithmetic.** The project's own drill records ≥35% as
*refuted, not unproven* — favourable CI bound −27.8%, independent rep30 Haiku −24.1% [−36.6, −8.3].

**Stop rule:** if Gate 1 shows `postedit` answering < 40% of post-edit shell calls, stop and report
rather than spending the cells. If the sealed cell lands below the pre-registered lower bound, the
result is published as a miss — no post-hoc subsetting, no matched-success filter, no re-drawing the
set.

# Plan — move Entire Graph toward 35% token savings on SWE-bench Multilingual

## Context

The goal is 35% token savings. The current honest measurement is **+1.35%** on REP50_r1
(49 instances × 4 arms, Opus max), bootstrap 95% CI **[−17.0%, +18.2%]**. This plan exists because
the forensics say the shortfall has one cause, and it is not retrieval quality.

**Why tokens move at all.** `log(tokens) ~ log(messages)`, elasticity **1.682**, r=0.957;
message-adjusted residual saving is 0.000. Turns are the only thing that prices. Measured on rep50:
`corr(Δturns, token saving) = −0.854`.

**What that costs us.** To hit 35% the eg arm must run **2067 turns** against baseline's 2671 —
**641 fewer than the 2709 it actually ran**, i.e. **13.1 turns/session** removed (55.3 → 42.2).

**Where the turns are** (49 sessions, corrected to exclude `entire graph *` invocations from the
shell counts — my first pass miscounted them and reported "zero grep elimination", which was wrong):

| | baseline | eg | |
|---|--:|--:|---|
| shell exploration, pre-edit | 725 | 683 | −5.8% ✅ |
| shell exploration, post-edit | 542 | **606** | **+11.8%** ❌ |
| build/test runs | 508 | 493 | −3.0% ✅ |
| edits | 397 | 414 | +4.3% |
| graph calls | 0 | 105 (**98 pre / 7 post**) | 93% pre-edit |

**Displacement ratio: −0.21 shell calls removed per graph call.** The tool wins the phase it is
present in and loses more in the phase it is absent from. The post-edit pool is **19.5 turns/session**
(12.4 shell + 7.1 build) and the graph makes **0.14 calls/session** there. It is the only pool large
enough to fund 13.1 turns.

**Retrieval is not the problem.** Payload named the file the agent actually edited in **28/33 = 84.8%**
of sessions that logged a payload. Stop tuning ranking.

**REP50 also measured a stale, misconfigured tool** — nine relevant commits landed after it ran
(`changed`, riders, `--path`, batched `def`, never-refuse, payload logging), it ran `EG_TOPK=5`
instead of 10, its `grep` verb ran raw `grep -rInE` across `node_modules/`, and **13 knobs
`run_REP50.sh` exported were silently dead** because `eg-q.run` hardcodes a fixed variable list.

---

## Design

One idea: **anchor the post-edit answer on the diff instead of on query hits.**

Every block that answers "what else must change / what will break" already exists and is wired to the
wrong anchor. `changed.go:318 symbolOverlapsHunks` already computes the edited-span anchor set and
discards it on everything except caller counts.

| existing block | answers | currently anchored on |
|---|---|---|
| `internal/sem/search_related.go` (950 L) | what else must change | query hits |
| `internal/sem/search_closedset.go` (996 L) | what breaks silently at runtime | query hits |
| `internal/cli/callsite.go` (25 KB) | real call line + enclosing guards | query hits |
| `internal/sem/search_verify.go` (1867 L) | the narrowest test command | query hits, **unexported** |

### A. entire-graph (`/Users/suhaan/devenv/entire-graph`)

1. **Make VERIFY askable.** `buildSearchVerifyCommand` (search_verify.go:199) is unexported and takes
   `[]SearchResult`. Extract a subject-based entry point taking `(repo, sourcePath, testPath)`;
   `SearchRepository` (search.go:1225) becomes one caller. Keep the four-tier ladder and the residual
   floor exactly as-is. Do **not** use the `--path` hack — verified to misfire (scoping to
   `changed.go` emitted a VERIFY for `TestDoctorPrintsEntireEnvironment`).

2. **New verb `entire graph postedit`.** Model on `internal/cli/changed.go`; reuse
   `gitutil.WorktreeChangedFiles` (worktree.go:277) and `symbolOverlapsHunks` (changed.go:318).
   Emits, budgeted, for the edited spans only:
   - callers of each changed definition (already in `changed`)
   - **related sites** — re-anchor `selectSearchRelatedSites` (search_related.go:345) on edited spans
   - **closed-set warning** — re-anchor `buildSearchClosedSet` (search_closedset.go:142) on edited spans
   - **VERIFY** for the edited file, from A.1
   - **arity/name check** (new, see A.3)

3. **Arity/name check — the one genuinely new analysis.** Nothing in the repo compares a signature to
   a call site; `def`/sigtypes only display. Build it from `callsite.go`'s existing raw material plus
   the symbol's signature: for each edited symbol whose parameter list changed, walk its resolved call
   sites and report arity mismatches and unresolved field/method names. This is the class of defect
   that makes a patch fail to build, which is what the post-edit loop is burning turns on.

4. **Fix the cost wall — precondition, not optional.** Every worktree-aware verb costs **14.2 s warm
   or cold** (`index_latency_ms ≈ 14,188` vs `query_latency_ms ≈ 3`); it is a full re-index, caused by
   `MaxDirtyFilesForDigest = 64` (gitutil/worktree.go:61) plus `hashDirectory` (worktree.go:177)
   walking nested worktrees. `postedit` must reuse a `--head` snapshot and incrementally reparse only
   the changed files. **Target < 1 s.** A verb called after every edit at 14 s is worse than useless.

5. **Housekeeping that changes measurement.** Add `changed`, `postedit`, `def`, `verify` to
   `graphVerbs` (internal/cli/stats.go:62) — today every call to them is invisible to `stats`. Add
   `changed`/`postedit` to `printHelp` and to the embedded `agentGuide` (internal/cli/agents.go).
   Filter inventory-only languages out of `changed`'s ranking (Markdown `section`/`code_fence` records
   currently fill the top-20). Write the tests `changed` has never had (zero today).

### B. Harness (`~/graphmark-bench/agentic-swebench` — the live copy, **not** `devenv/graphmark`)

6. **Un-break the knob surface.** `run_3arm.sh:457` hardcodes the variable list baked into
   `eg-q.run`; anything absent is dead for agent calls. Forward the 13 dead knobs. Restore
   `EG_TOPK=10`.
7. **Fix the `grep` verb.** It takes `rx="$*"`, so `eg-q grep -i wikidata` searched for the literal
   string `-i wikidata`. Apply the post-REP50 vendor/minified filter and the never-refuse
   grep→search fallback (`b5473b0b`), both already written.
8. **Deliver post-edit at zero turn cost.** A verb costs a turn; a rider costs none, and bytes are
   nearly free while turns price at elasticity 1.682. Wire `postedit` output as a `PostToolUse` rider
   on Edit/Write (`EG_CHANGED_RIDER` already exists in LIVE) and gate it — fire on the first edit per
   file, cap hard, never on a no-op edit.
9. **Port the fairness gate.** `_assert_prompt_symmetry` exists only in `devenv/graphmark`
   (run_3arm.sh:1002-1029). LIVE has no machine-checked prompt-symmetry gate. Port it before any cell.
   Prompt changes stay **capability description only** — the harness's own rule (`run_3arm.sh:1203`):
   the arm block says what the tool *is and returns*, never *when to use it*.

### C. Interface lever, measured separately (phase 2)

10. `EG_MCP=1` (run_3arm.sh:787) puts the graph in the model's native tool list beside `Grep`/`Read`.
    It is mutually exclusive with `--safe-mode`, which silently strips all MCP servers.
    **`--safe-mode` must be dropped for both arms or it is an arm confound** — and doing so makes the
    cell non-comparable to every prior cell, which is why it gets its own cell.

---

## Verification

**Gate 1 — offline replay, zero model cost (do this before spending anything).**
Per the forensics drill §5: replay the 105 recorded queries in `results/REP50_r1_eg/eg/*/gq_calls.log`
against the new binary, and reconstruct the 606 post-edit shell commands from the transcripts. Measure
what fraction `postedit` would actually have answered. **Proceed only if it answers ≥ 40%** — below
that the arithmetic cannot reach even 20% and the cells are wasted.

**Gate 2 — sealed pre-registration.**
Draw the holdout by set-difference against every burned selector: rep50 ∪ val30/h30 ∪ ho5/10/20 ∪
gate_5/10/20/30/60/300 ∪ prereg30/100 ∪ GEM300 ∪ fab82 ∪ SW_* ∪ G1/G2/G3. Freeze the id list, the
predicted effect and the falsification bounds to a file **before** the run, with sha256.

**Gate 3 — the cells.** Opus at effort `high`, `xhigh`, `max`. Gate a pair only if both arms have
`usd > 0` and a non-empty patch; drop symmetrically. Report cache_read / cache_creation / output
**separately**, geomean plus bootstrap CI, never a bare point estimate.

**Cost:** ~$307 per 49-instance 2-arm cell at Opus (rep50's 196 sessions cost $614). Three effort
levels ≈ **$920**; the phase-2 interface cell adds ~$307. Budget **~$1,200–1,900**.

**Power caveat:** at n=49 a single cell detects roughly a 25-point effect. The three effort levels can
each answer "does eg save at this effort", but **cannot reliably rank each other** — config-vs-config
MDE is ~94 points against ~74 points of observed spread. Do not read the ordering.

---

## GATE 1 RESULT — run 2026-08-09, read-only, zero model cost: **PASS**

Classified all 606 post-edit shell calls in the REP50 eg arm:

| class | n | % | answerable by diff-anchored postedit |
|---|--:|--:|---|
| re-read the edited region | 105 | 17.3% | yes (the rider carries it) |
| find-or-run the right test | 97 | 16.0% | yes (VERIFY) |
| error from a failed build | 21 | 3.5% | yes (arity/name check) |
| other call sites | 13 | 2.1% | yes (callers/related) |
| does this symbol exist | 13 | 2.1% | yes (def/arity) |
| env / toolchain hunting | 54 | 8.9% | no |
| unclassified | 303 | 50.0% | see below |
| **answerable** | **249** | **41.1%** | **≥40% threshold met** |

**The unclassified half is the real finding.** It is dominated by agents writing and running
throwaway reproduction harnesses (`cat > /tmp/repro.mjs <<EOF`, `node repro.mjs`, `cat > edge.cc`).
Sized separately, post-edit:

| per session | baseline | eg |
|---|--:|--:|
| improvised repro-harness calls | 8.3 | **8.4** |
| real test-suite runs | 2.7 | 2.3 |
| sessions that improvise at all | 46/49 | **46/49** |

Agents improvise a harness **3.6× more often than they run the real suite**, and eg does not reduce
it at all. This is the known mechanism — throwaway harnesses are 79% of the gain and 43% of the loss —
and it is the one class the tool has never attacked.

against the **13.1 needed for 35%**. The lever is not "answer greps"; it is

fires pre-edit, inside `search`, and is ignored by 46/49 sessions.

| if postedit eliminates | turns/session | predicted saving |
|---|--:|--:|
| half the improvisation + answerable shell | ~8 | **≈21%** |
| most of both | ~12 | **≈32%** |
| the whole addressable pool | 13.5 | ≈35% |

displacement, which no prior config has achieved. Realistic band: **20–32%**. The project's drill
still records ≥35% as *refuted* on prior evidence (favourable bound −27.8%; rep30 Haiku −24.1%
[−36.6, −8.3]), and nothing here overturns that yet — it only shows a pool big enough to try.

**Stop rule:** if the sealed cell lands below the pre-registered lower bound, it is published as a
miss — no post-hoc subsetting, no matched-success filter, no re-drawing the set.

---

entire-graph src `c500baa` branch `r1r2`, **310 prebuilt graphs**, 9.4 GB repo-cache, docker running,

now snapshotted). `graphbench-e`/`-f` are memory-bench's and must not be touched.

`graphbench-c:~/go50.sh` and `~/go50b.sh` (`export AT=sk-ant-…`) and was catalogued during the

## Context

The goal is 35% token savings. The current honest measurement is **+1.35%** on REP50_r1

the forensics say the shortfall has one cause, and it is not retrieval quality.

**Why tokens move at all.** `log(tokens) ~ log(messages)`, elasticity **1.682**, r=0.957;
message-adjusted residual saving is 0.000. Turns are the only thing that prices. Measured on rep50:
`corr(Δturns, token saving) = −0.854`.

**What that costs us.** To hit 35% the eg arm must run **2067 turns** against baseline's 2671 —
**641 fewer than the 2709 it actually ran**, i.e. **13.1 turns/session** removed (55.3 → 42.2).

shell counts — my first pass miscounted them and reported "zero grep elimination", which was wrong):

| build/test runs | 508 | 493 | −3.0% ✅ |
| edits | 397 | 414 | +4.3% |
| graph calls | 0 | 105 (**98 pre / 7 post**) | 93% pre-edit |

present in and loses more in the phase it is absent from. The post-edit pool is **19.5 turns/session**
(12.4 shell + 7.1 build) and the graph makes **0.14 calls/session** there. It is the only pool large
enough to fund 13.1 turns.

**Retrieval is not the problem.** Payload named the file the agent actually edited in **28/33 = 84.8%**
of sessions that logged a payload. Stop tuning ranking.

(`changed`, riders, `--path`, batched `def`, never-refuse, payload logging), it ran `EG_TOPK=5`
instead of 10, its `grep` verb ran raw `grep -rInE` across `node_modules/`, and **13 knobs

   - **VERIFY** for the edited file, from A.1
   - **arity/name check** (new, see A.3)

3. **Arity/name check — the one genuinely new analysis.** Nothing in the repo compares a signature to
   a call site; `def`/sigtypes only display. Build it from `callsite.go`'s existing raw material plus
   the symbol's signature: for each edited symbol whose parameter list changed, walk its resolved call
   sites and report arity mismatches and unresolved field/method names. This is the class of defect

   the arm block says what the tool *is and returns*, never *when to use it*.

# AGENTS.md — operating guide for coding agents

Hand this to any coding agent working in a repo where the `entire graph` plugin
is installed. It moves initial code-location work from broad grep/read
exploration to targeted graph queries; token impact depends on the task and
model, and no end-to-end savings claim is current.

## What this gives you

A precomputed, **deterministic** code graph is available through the `entire graph` command — functions, classes, methods, types, routes, and the calls/inheritance/field/service relations between them, parsed with tree-sitter, 100% locally (no network, no model, no keys). Use it to **LOCATE** and **UNDERSTAND** code *before* broad grep / find / cat / whole-file exploration. Every command is no-egress and safe to run inside a sandboxed session. The same commit yields the same graph, but static relations can be heuristic or incomplete; inspect focused source and verify the resulting change.

Default flags to remember: pass `--repo .` when you're not inside an Entire session; the graph reads your **working tree by default** (your uncommitted edits are visible), and `--head` switches to committed-tree semantics with a cached, reusable index.

---

## The parts of the graph

Reach for the smallest tool that answers your question.

### 🔍 search — *find the code for a task* (your first move)
Ranked source regions for a plain-language description, with the source and `file:line` inline. Hybrid ranking over bodies, identifiers (camelCase/snake_case aware), signatures, paths, and graph neighbors. Output is budgeted (16 KiB by default) to drop straight into context.

```sh
entire graph search --repo . --query "<the task or bug in one plain sentence>" --format text --top-k 8
```

- `--format agent` for compact ranked output with latency telemetry; `json`/`ndjson` for the full schema (completeness, partial failures, diagnostics).
- `--top-k N` result count; `--max-context-bytes N` byte budget (`0` = unbounded).
- Working tree by default; add `--head` for committed-tree + cache reuse.
- `--profile syntax-only|fast|full` (default `fast`); `--index-all-files` or `--max-indexed-files N` to widen/bound cold-search parsing.

**When:** the start of essentially every task. One good query lands you on the fix area.

### 🕸️ neighbors — *who calls this / what does it call* (targeted relations)
Direct incoming/outgoing relations for **one** symbol, with definition locations, plus bounded two-hop paths at `--depth 2`. For the full blast radius of a change, prefer `impact`; use `neighbors` when you want one specific relation/direction. Never `edges` for this (full stream).

```sh
entire graph neighbors --repo . --symbol NAME --relation CALLS --direction in   # who calls NAME
entire graph neighbors --repo . --symbol NAME --relation CALLS --direction out  # what NAME calls
```

- `--file path` — **required** when the symbol name is ambiguous (multiple defs); the graph returns definitions only until you disambiguate.
- `--relation CALLS` (default is the call family) — pick another relation to follow it instead.
- `--direction both|in|out`, `--depth 1|2`, `--limit N`.
- `--internal-only` drops unresolved external endpoints; `--exclude-tests` drops test-only neighbors.
- `--format agent|text|json`; `--head` for cached committed-tree; `--profile fast` for shallow call resolution (default `full` favors correctness).

**When:** "what breaks if I change X", "who uses this", tracing a call chain — after search has given you a concrete symbol name.

### 💥 impact — *one-shot blast radius for a change*
Everything the graph knows about changing **one** symbol, in a single bounded explanation: direct + transitive callers (depth ≤ 2), callees, type consumers (`USES_TYPE`/`PARAM_TYPE`/`RETURNS_TYPE`), data flows, files that historically change together with the symbol's file, and same-container siblings. Text output is sectioned, `file:line` per entry, capped per section and ~4 KB total.

```sh
entire graph impact --repo . --symbol NAME [--file path] [--depth 1|2] [--format text|json]
```

- Ambiguous names return the definition list — rerun with `--file` to pick one.
- `--depth` 1|2 (default: 2); `--limit N` per-section entry cap; `--max-context-bytes N` total text budget; `--exclude-tests`; `--head` / `--profile` as in `neighbors`.

**When:** before changing behavior of a specific function/type — "you're changing ordering: here is every place results are ordered, limited, or consumed downstream" — one command instead of chaining neighbors + edges + git log.

### 📇 symbols — *definitions*
Full stream of symbol records (stable `compound-v1` ID, kind, qualified name, source range, signature, language, container). This is a **bulk NDJSON stream of the whole repo**, filtered to the symbol record type — there is **no positional name argument** and no server-side name filter; grep the stream client-side, or prefer `search`/`neighbors` for a targeted single-symbol lookup.

```sh
entire graph symbols --repo . --format ndjson [--worktree]
```

**When:** you need the complete definition inventory (e.g. ingesting into a store), not a single lookup.

### 🔗 edges — *relations*
Full stream of relation records across all 30 types (`CALLS`, `IMPORTS`, `EXTENDS`, `HANDLES_ROUTE`, …), each tagged with resolution and confidence. The stream is whole-repo by default; `--to`, `--from`, and `--relation` filter it server-side. For one symbol's callers/callees, prefer `neighbors` because it annotates resolved definitions and call sites from source.

```sh
entire graph edges --repo . --format ndjson [--worktree] [--to ID|NAME] [--from ID|NAME] [--relation TYPE[,TYPE...]]
```

**When:** you want every relation (bulk export / ingestion) or a filtered relation stream. For a targeted one-symbol question, use `neighbors`.

### 🗺️ snapshot — *the whole graph*
One header record, then file, external-endpoint, symbol, and relation records, streamed so memory stays bounded. Superset of `symbols` + `edges` + files.

```sh
entire graph snapshot --repo . --format ndjson [--worktree]
```

**When:** ingesting the full graph into agent memory or a store such as Entire Brain.

### 🧬 diff / analyze / commit / checkpoint — *what changed + risk*
Entity-level change list (added / removed / renamed / signature-changed / body-changed) with a heuristic **dependent count**, so a signature change with many dependents stands out.

```sh
entire graph commit HEAD --json                     # a commit vs its first parent
entire graph diff --base main --head HEAD --json    # between two refs (analyze is an alias)
entire graph checkpoint <id> --json                 # the commit behind an Entire-Checkpoint trailer
```

**When:** judging whether a change is safe to keep / revert / continue, or reviewing a branch/PR. High dependent counts on a signature change = run tests first.

### 🏗️ index — *build / warm the cache*
Prebuilds the durable, query-independent committed-tree index and verifies it was written, before latency-sensitive work.

```sh
entire graph index --repo . --head --profile full --cache-dir /path/to/cache --format json
```

**When:** once, up front, on a large repo before a batch of `--head` searches/neighbors queries. Re-running it is also how you "refresh" a committed-tree cache — same tree hits, changed tree rebuilds.

### 🧭 capabilities / doctor / version — *feature-detect*
```sh
entire graph capabilities --json    # semantic vs inventory-only languages, relation types, features
entire graph doctor --json          # environment, repo resolution, no_egress=true
entire graph version [--json]       # provider name + plugin version
```

**When:** before assuming a language is semantically parsed, or to confirm the no-egress environment.

### 📊 stats — *did the graph actually save anything?* (for humans, not for you)
```sh
entire graph stats --repo . [--since 30d|7d|all] [--format text|json] [--sessions-dir path|--transcript path]
```

Local, read-only report over the coding-agent session transcripts already on disk
(`~/.claude/projects/<path-slug>/*.jsonl`; `--sessions-dir` overrides the lookup). Reports graph
calls per verb vs. exploration calls (`Read` whole-file / `Read` line-range / `Grep` / `Glob` /
shell `grep|find|cat|head|tail|sed|awk`), the bytes each path pulled into context, billed session
tokens read from transcript `usage`, a graph-first rate (share of sessions whose first locate-ish
tool call was a graph call), and an **estimated** token saving. The savings model is an explicit
assumption printed next to the number: each `search`/`neighbors`/`impact` call is credited with the
one whole-file read it replaced — on-disk size of the top-hit file it pointed at (repo median
tracked-file size when unresolvable) minus the bytes that call returned, floored at 0, at 4 bytes =
1 token. It is not a measured counterfactual. No network, no writes. `--transcript <path>` narrows
the whole report to one session (that transcript plus its `<session>/subagents/*.jsonl`), which is
what `scripts/entire-graph-statusline.sh` renders as a live Claude Code status line badge.

**When:** a human asks what the graph is buying them. Agents should not run it as part of a coding task.

---

## Resolution-first agent prompt (copy-paste this)

The former “measured-best” early-stop prompt and its 54.9%/57.7% token claims
are withdrawn. It optimized token use without preserving resolution parity and
could reward a cheap wrong patch. Use this correctness-first guidance instead;
substitute your search invocation for `<search-cmd>`:

```text
A precomputed code-search tool is available: <search-cmd> . Use it to LOCATE the fix BEFORE any
grep/find. Your FIRST action must be ONE search:
  <search-cmd> "<the bug in one sentence>"   <-- ranked relevant code (file:line + source)
Then open the top hit's file with your native Read tool (pass a line range around the reported
line), inspect enough surrounding behavior to justify the change, and make the smallest complete
edit. Treat graph output as evidence, not an oracle. Check callers/impact when the change can affect
other sites. If the result prints a `VERIFY:` line, run that exact command after editing before
claiming the task is done; it may be a per-file command or a whole-suite fallback when no narrow
command can be derived. Never report that tests pass without executing the command. If verification
cannot be run, state why and perform a bounded source-level check. Optimize turns only after
correctness.
```

For bug-fix/locate tasks, run search at `--profile full` (call-graph expansion active) with default
text output (tiered: full snippet for the top hits, terse locators after). Prefer
targeted follow-up queries over whole-graph dumps, but use the graph and source
checks needed to make and verify a complete fix.

## Operating doctrine

1. **Search first for location tasks.** Start with one `entire graph search --query "<task>"` before broad grep/find exploration.
2. **Treat results as evidence, not truth.** Read focused source around the result and widen the check when behavior, aliases, generated code, or dynamic dispatch could matter.
3. **Use graph follow-ups when they answer a real question.** `impact`, `callers`, and `neighbors` are appropriate for blast radius and related-site checks; avoid exploratory whole-graph dumps.
4. **Make the smallest complete change.** Check sibling sites and contracts when the task implies them.
5. **Verify before stopping.** Run the `VERIFY:` command when search prints one; it may be a whole-suite fallback when no narrow command exists. Never report that tests pass without having run them. If execution is unavailable, perform a bounded source-level verification and disclose the limitation.
6. **Optimize context after correctness.** Prefer precise queries and line ranges, but never trade resolution for fewer turns.
7. **Feature-detect before you trust.** If a language might be inventory-only, check `capabilities --json` first — inventory-only files have file records but no semantic relations.

Quick mental model:

```text
locate  →  entire graph search --query "..."          (ranked code + file:line)
impact  →  entire graph impact --symbol X              (one-shot blast radius: callers, types, data flow, co-change)
callers →  entire graph neighbors --symbol X ...       (targeted callers/callees of X)
change  →  entire graph diff --base A --head B          (entity-level, with dependents)
ingest  →  entire graph snapshot --format ndjson        (whole graph)
report  →  entire graph stats --repo .                  (human-facing: graph vs grep/read usage + estimated token savings)
```

---

## Working on entire-graph itself

If your task is modifying this repository (not just using it), the build/test surface is in `mise.toml`:

```sh
mise run build   # go build -o entire-graph ./cmd/entire-graph  (needs CGO for tree-sitter)
mise run test    # go test ./...
mise run check   # fmt + vet + race tests + build
```

Contract rules that must not break: schema `1.x` is frozen and additive-only (`docs/adr/0001-ga-schema-contract.md`); the provider is **no-egress** (never add remote fetches, hosted API calls, telemetry, or runtime grammar downloads); `compound-v1` symbol IDs must stay stable across ordinary edits; unsupported/unparseable files must surface as machine-readable partial failures, never silent drops. All logic lives under `internal/` (`sem` = parsing/graph/search, `cli` = hand-rolled dispatch, `gitutil` = git subprocess); `cmd/entire-graph/main.go` is a thin entry point. The plugin manifest (`entire-plugin.yml`) registers the subcommand `graph`, so users type `entire graph ...`. This project was **previously named `entire-sem`** — do not reintroduce the old name. **Entire Brain** (`entire-brain`) is the separate downstream consumer of this provider's NDJSON — not an old name for this project.

This repo has the entire-graph code graph installed. Before exploring code with
grep/find/whole-file reads, read .entire/graph-agent.md — the search-first, verify-once
doctrine for coding agents: search instead of grepping, then check the sibling sites and
compile (or run the nearest existing test) once before you finish.
@.entire/graph-agent.md

# entire-graph — instructions for coding agents (follow directly)

You have a deterministic local code graph: `entire graph` (functions, classes, methods,
types, routes + call/inheritance relations; no network). These instructions are FOR YOU, the
agent reading this file.

**No token-savings claim is current.** The "roughly half" figure this file used to carry came
from a measurement that gave the tool arm frugality instructions the no-tool arm did not get;
removing them moved the same cell from −14.9% to +9.1%, and `AGENTS.md` withdraws the 54.9%
/ 57.7% numbers for the same reason. The best fair paired measurement to date is a single-digit
to mid-teens token saving that varies by model and task, and is *negative* on short sessions.
Follow the workflow below because it finds code faster and verifies the change — not because a
number promises a saving.

## The workflow (mandatory for locate/fix/change tasks)

Your FIRST action on any task that requires finding code must be ONE search:

    entire graph search --repo . --profile full --format text --query "<the task or bug in one sentence>"

The first five hits come back as the COMPLETE body of their enclosing function/method (marked
`complete-symbol`; `snippet_start_line`..`snippet_end_line` is the whole callable, verbatim).
When the hit you want is one of them, EDIT DIRECTLY FROM THE SEARCH OUTPUT — you already have
the entire function, and opening the file costs a whole extra turn for nothing. Only when the
hit you want carries a two-line locator window instead, open its file at the reported line
range. Either way: make the minimal edit that fixes the root cause. The top hit is the fix site
on most tasks — go straight there; do NOT re-search or grep to "confirm".

Then finish the job. Two bounded steps, not a loop:

**1. Complete the fix.** A fix is often not one edit in one place. Before you call it done, ask
the graph once for the sites that share the defect:

    entire graph impact --repo . --symbol X

One shot: callers, callees, type consumers, data flow, co-change files, and same-container
siblings. Apply the same change to the ones that carry the same bug; ignore the rest.

**2. Verify once.** Compile what you touched, or run the nearest existing test. This is NOT
optional overhead. An unverified edit is how a patch ships an unused variable, a wrong field or
method name, or the wrong arity — and a patch that does not build fails 100% of the task. One
verification turn costs one turn; a patch that does not compile costs everything.

The output is grouped, and the groups mean different things:

* the ranked list is **candidate fix sites** — start at the top.
* **RELATED SITES** (`section: "related"`) are the other places this change usually has to
  land: a near-duplicate body needs the SAME edit, a sibling implementation needs the same edit
  in its own terms, a caller needs adjusting to the changed contract. Before you finish, check
  them — a patch applied to one site of a family is the commonest way a correct fix still fails.
* **DOCS & FIXTURES** (`section: "docs-and-fixtures"`) matched your words but hold no program
  text. Do not spend a read there looking for the bug unless the task IS the document.

## Rules, in order of how much evidence stands behind them

Correctness first: `AGENTS.md` is the contract, and it says never trade resolution for fewer
turns. Nothing below overrides that.

**Measured, and the largest effect by far — bound your verification.**

1. VERIFY ONCE, THEN STOP CHASING. Run the narrowest command that would catch a syntax, type,
   name, or arity error; read the error; fix exactly what it names; re-run. A couple of
   iterations, not a loop. Do not "fix" failures that were already failing before you started.
   This is where sessions actually burn their budget: across 8 decomposed losing sessions,
   **97.7% of the excess cost landed after the first edit**, in repeated harness invocations —
   `./runtest` 11 times, `cargo test` 7, `javac` 19 — each dragging in `sleep`, `pkill`, port
   juggling and log re-reading. The sessions that won ran the suite **once or twice** and
   stopped. Localization was, by comparison, free.
2. AFTER EDITING, ASK THE GRAPH WHAT YOU TOUCHED rather than grepping for it:
       entire graph changed --repo .
   Paths you changed, the definitions in them, and what calls those — most-depended-on first.

**Sound practice, not a measured saving.**

3. Search before grep/find/cat for locate tasks; one good query usually lands the fix site.
4. Prefer a line range around the reported line over a whole-file read when the hit is a
   locator. A `complete-symbol` hit is already the whole function — you can edit from it.
5. For "who calls X" / "what breaks", one targeted query beats chaining:
       entire graph impact --repo . --symbol X

**Explicitly NOT claimed.** That a second search is wasteful, that re-reading is always wrong,
or that fewer turns is itself the goal. Retrieval quality and token cost are different axes —
in one 49-instance cell the sessions where the graph ranked the gold file first *lost* more
often than the ones where it missed. If the first answer is not enough, ask again.

## When NOT to use the graph

If the task already names the exact file and it is small, just read it — the graph earns its
keep by eliminating exploration, so when there is nothing to explore, skip it. Short sessions
are where the tool measures WORST: on instances whose no-tool run was already cheap, the graph
arm cost 27.8% more. Verification still applies: it is about the edit you made, not about how
you found it.

## Reference

    locate  ->  entire graph search --repo . --profile full --format text --query "..."
    impact  ->  entire graph impact --repo . --symbol X   (one shot: callers, callees, type consumers, data flow, co-change, siblings)
    callers ->  entire graph neighbors --repo . --symbol X --relation CALLS --direction in
    changed ->  entire graph changed --repo .   (what you edited, and what calls it)
    change  ->  entire graph diff --base A --head B --json
    detect  ->  entire graph capabilities --json   (inventory-only languages have no relations)
    verify  ->  this project's own narrowest build/test command, once, after editing
                (e.g. `go build ./internal/foo/...`, `pytest tests/test_foo.py -k name`, `cargo check -p crate`)
    stats   ->  entire graph stats --repo .        (human-facing token-savings report; not part of your workflow — do not run it unless asked)

Both infra blockers cleared, and one of them was never real.

## Progress

**Done**

| | |
|---|---|
| ✅ **graphbench-c is now STANDARD** | `preemptible: false`, `automaticRestart: true`, `onHostMaintenance: MIGRATE`. Preemption risk gone, all 310 graphs / 9.4 GB cache / rep50 corpus preserved in place. Snapshot held as rollback. |
| ✅ **Go toolchain** | Already installed at `/usr/local/go` — go1.25.7 linux/amd64, `CGO_ENABLED=1`, gcc present. My earlier "go MISSING" was a PATH artifact (Ubuntu's `.bashrc` early-returns for non-interactive shells), not a real blocker. Withdrawn. |
| ✅ **A.1 VERIFY askable** | `sem.VerifyCommandForFile` landed, 4 tests green, ladder proven byte-identical to search's. Probe confirms the `--path` misfire is fixed: with only `doctor_test.go` present it refuses to borrow it. |
| ✅ **A.4 diagnosed** | 14.0 s per edit (cache invalidates on every keystroke) vs 0.14 s for `--head`. Design validated at ~0.25 s. |
| ✅ **Gate 2 holdout** | **125 clean, graph-ready instances**, 9 languages. MDE drops ~31% → **~15%**, so a 20–32% effect is finally detectable. |
| ✅ **Auth smoke** | OAuth + `--model opus --effort max` works. `total_cost_usd` **is** populated — my "OAuth voids the gate" blocker was wrong and is withdrawn, so no scoring change and rep50 comparability is preserved. |

**In flight** — agent implementing the `postedit` verb + arity/name check.

**Left** — A.5 housekeeping (`graphVerbs`, help, inventory-language filter, `changed` tests) · B.6–B.9 harness fixes · seal the pre-registration · then the cell.

## One open risk, your call

The token you gave me is the **same one bridged to graphbench-f**, where the 8-arm memory run is live and writing ~1,400 artifacts per 15 min. A 98-session Opus-max cell on that token will throttle both and inject the load-pressure arm confound — the one that's known to flip the sign on this benchmark.

Two clean ways out: **mint a second token** for the SWE-bench cell, or I **sequence the cell after the memory run finishes**. I'll keep building either way; this only binds at launch time.

**Task 2 conservatism** (all measured against real repos during the build):
- Arity is reported only when the call site **provably matched the old count and provably does not match the new one**. This is what makes Python's `self` harmless — the offset makes "matched before" false, so it goes silent instead of flagging every method call in the repo. Verified: already-updated call sites, variadic tails, and Python `self` all stay silent while the genuinely stale call is reported.
- Signature scan bails on `...`, `=`, `->`, `=>`, quotes, leading `*`. Angle brackets tracked in signatures (Java generics), **not** at call sites (`<` is a comparison there).
- Extended the unresolved check to `READS_FIELD`/`WRITES_FIELD`/`ACCESSES` — the spec said "field/method name", and those carry `field_access` evidence, not `call_site`. Added a local `posteditEvidenceSpan` rather than widening the shared `callEvidenceSpan`, which `neighbors`/`impact` depend on.

**Tests** — `internal/cli/postedit_test.go` (478 lines, 11 tests) and `internal/cli/changed_test.go` (216 lines, 5 tests; `changed` had zero). Hermetic: `t.TempDir()` + `git init`, `--no-cache` or a temp `--cache-dir`, all `t.Parallel()`.

go test ./internal/... -count=1 -> 2285 passed in 18 packages   (was 2229 before; +56)

## Measured wall time (this repo, 3 changed paths, committed index warm)

First call *after an edit* — the only number that matters, since that is when the worktree digest is invalidated:

| | 1st edit | 2nd edit |
|---|---|---|
| `postedit` | **0.49 s** | **0.51 s** |
| `changed` | 14.19 s | 14.19 s |

**~28x.** With 6 changed paths, `postedit` was 0.58 s cold / 0.18 s warm against `changed`'s 14.65 s.

## Things in the spec that were wrong or incomplete

1. **`changed` is not 14 s on *every* invocation** — it is 14 s on the *first* call after each edit; back-to-back calls on an unchanged dirty tree hit the cache at 0.16 s (`worktreeCacheDigest` keys dirty trees by content digest). The 14 s figure is right for the agent's actual usage pattern (call after each edit), and the comment in `postedit.go` states it that way, but the "every invocation" phrasing is not literally true.
2. **`changed` is not in `printHelp` at all** — the spec said to register `postedit` "beside `changed`" and add it to `printHelp`. I added `postedit` only, as instructed; `changed` remains undocumented in help. Worth a follow-up.
3. **`sem.RenderSearchVerifyCommand` fit as-is**, but `VerifyCommandForFile`'s test-path argument is a foot-gun the spec didn't flag: passing an edited test file from a *different* package makes the Go deriver read its package selector off the test path. On this very repo it emitted `go test ./internal/sem` for an edit to `internal/cli/root.go`. Fixed inside `posteditVerify` by only offering a test path from the subject's own directory — no change to `sem`.
4. **Masked source cannot be used for argument text.** `maskedSourceLines` blanks string literals, so `f("hello")` masks to `f(       )` and a naive scanner counts zero arguments — a guaranteed false "arity mismatch". The scanner reads *delimiters* from masked text and *item text* from raw text at the same offsets (masking is length-preserving, and that invariant is asserted at runtime).
5. **Symbol IDs are `repoKey:language:path:kind:qualifiedName`** with no line numbers, so cross-snapshot comparison by stable ID works exactly as the spec assumed. Confirmed rather than trusted.</result>

## Background you must not re-derive
- The eg arm is a plain executable on PATH invoked via the Bash tool. Chain: agent runs `entire graph <verb>` -> `$out/entire` -> `tools/entire-frontend` -> `$out/eg-q.run` -> `tools/eg-q` -> `bin/entire-graph-linux`.

Determine whether Claude Code **hooks fire at all** under the harness's invocation:
`claude -p "$PROMPT" --model ... --effort ... --output-format json --dangerously-skip-permissions --max-turns N --safe-mode --disable-slash-commands --disallowedTools ...`

In `tools/run_3arm.sh`, make the generated `eg-q.run` forward every knob `eg-q` actually reads, rather than a hardcoded subset. Keep it explicit and readable; do not `env | grep` the whole environment into it.
Also: the REP50 cell ran `EG_TOPK=5` while eg-q's own default is 10. Make the default 10 unless a driver overrides it.

## TASK 2 — fix the `grep` verb
`tools/eg-q`'s grep verb builds its regex as `rx="$*"`, so `eg-q grep -i wikidata` searches for the literal string `-i wikidata`. Two REP50 calls did exactly this and got nothing. Fix argument handling so leading flags are either honoured or stripped, not concatenated into the pattern. `_assert_prompt_symmetry` exists only in `/Users/suhaan/devenv/graphmark/agentic-swebench/tools/run_3arm.sh` (around :1002-1029). Port it into the LIVE copy and make it run before any cell. #!/usr/bin/env bash
# Cross-language validation of `postedit` on REAL agent edits left in the REP50 checkouts.
# Read-only w.r.t. the checkouts: postedit never writes.
S=~/work/graphmark/agentic-swebench
BIN=/tmp/eg-pe-linux
CO=$S/checkouts/REP50_r1_eg/eg

printf "%-34s %-6s %6s %5s %-7s %s\n" INSTANCE LANG DIRTY WALL SECTIONS VERIFY
for d in $(ls -d $CO/*/ 2>/dev/null); do
  iid=$(basename "$d")
  wt="$d"
  [ -d "$wt/.git" ] || continue
  dirty=$(git -C "$wt" status --porcelain -uno 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
  [ "$dirty" = "0" ] && continue
  # crude language label from the dominant changed extension
  lang=$(git -C "$wt" status --porcelain -uno 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $NF}' | sed 's/.*\.//' | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head -1 | awk '{print $2}')
  t0=$(date +%s.%N)
  out=$(cd "$wt" && timeout 180 $BIN postedit --repo . --no-cache 2>&1)
  rc=$?
  t1=$(date +%s.%N)
  wall=$(echo "$t1 - $t0" | bc)
  secs=""
  echo "$out" | grep -q "^CHANGED "        && secs="${secs}C"
  echo "$out" | grep -q "^CHANGED DEF"     && secs="${secs}D"
  echo "$out" | grep -q "^CALLERS"         && secs="${secs}L"
  echo "$out" | grep -q "SIGNATURE RISK"   && secs="${secs}S"
  echo "$out" | grep -q "^VERIFY:"         && secs="${secs}V"
  [ $rc -ne 0 ] && secs="ERR($rc)"
  v=$(echo "$out" | grep -m1 "^VERIFY:" | cut -c1-58)
  printf "%-34s %-6s %6s %5.1f %-7s %s\n" "${iid:0:34}" "$lang" "$dirty" "$wall" "${secs:--}" "${v:-<none>}"
done
echo
echo "legend: C=CHANGED D=CHANGED-DEFS L=CALLERS S=SIGNATURE-RISK V=VERIFY"

  case $ext in
    php|rs|java|js|go|c|ts) printf '\n// postedit probe\n' >> "$d/$f" ;;

  esac
  t0=$(date +%s.%N)
  out=$(cd "$d" && timeout 300 $BIN postedit --repo . --no-cache 2>&1); rc=$?
  wall=$(echo "$(date +%s.%N) - $t0" | bc)
  secs=""
  echo "$out" | grep -q "^CHANGED "      && secs="${secs}C"
  echo "$out" | grep -q "^CHANGED DEF"   && secs="${secs}D"
  echo "$out" | grep -q "^CALLERS"       && secs="${secs}L"
  echo "$out" | grep -q "^VERIFY:"       && secs="${secs}V"
  [ $rc -ne 0 ] && secs="ERR$rc"
  v=$(echo "$out" | grep -m1 "^VERIFY:" | cut -c9-62)
  printf "%-24s %-5s %5.1f %-8s %s\n" "$repo" "$ext" "$wall" "${secs:--}" "${v:-<none>}"
  rm -rf "$d"
done
rm -rf "$W"
echo
echo "legend: C=CHANGED D=DEFS L=CALLERS V=VERIFY  (edited file = largest non-test .EXT source file)"

The A.4 design is **proven**, and it holds on a 7,000-file repo:

| repo | files | prewarm (once/instance) | **per-edit `postedit`** | stability |
|---|--:|--:|--:|---|
| lucene (Java) | 7,083 | 122.9 s | **4.5 s** | 4.52 / 4.50 / 4.51 |

| carbon (PHP) | 2,022 | 13.2 s | **0.44 s** | 0.44 / 0.43 / 0.44 |

Flat across successive edits — the committed index holds while only the changed files re-parse, which is exactly what `changed`'s 14.2 s-per-edit could never do. And since the delivery is a rider, that wall time costs **zero turns**, which is the only currency that prices.

=== O35_STRIP_ADVICE: what does it strip, and does it cover postedit? ===
    # O35_STRIP_ADVICE=1 -- remove the GENERIC METHODOLOGY sentences the binary appends to its
    # VERIFY block, while keeping the derived COMMAND and its `targets` line.
    #
    # Why this exists. The command is tool output: the graph derives it from the repo's own build
    # files plus the ranked test class, and the no-tool arm has no way to get it -- that asymmetry
    # IS the thing being measured. The trailing sentences are different in kind:
    #   "run it ONCE after editing; if it fails, fix the code and re-run THIS command."
    #   "do not build an alternative test harness, hand-assemble a classpath, or re-verify by
    #    reverting and reapplying the edit."
    # Those need no graph. They are generic agent methodology, and handing them to one arm only is
    # exactly the class of asymmetry that turned a published -35% into +9.1% once it was removed.
    # tools/_pf_verify.py already sets its own ANTI_HARNESS to '' for this reason; but with
    # O35_VERIFY_ONLY=0 the BINARY's native copy passes straight through, which reintroduced the
    # clamp into ~30/30 prompts instead of the 3-8/30 the older cells carried.
    # EXTENDED 2026-08-06: testing four literal strings was not enough. An imperative-mood scan of

content.text:
The harness agent surfaced something that goes to the heart of whether any number from this survives. Three findings, in order of importance.

## 1. My lever may be the very thing fairness forbids

`postedit` emits a VERIFY contract note: *"run it ONCE after editing…"*, *"do not build an alternative test harness, hand-assemble a classpath, or re-verify by reverting and reapplying the edit."*

That is **exactly** the anti-harness clamp I identified as the mechanism worth 8.4 calls/session. And the harness already has `O35_STRIP_ADVICE=1` to delete it, with this in its own source comment:

> *"Those need no graph. They are generic agent methodology, and handing them to one arm only is exactly the class of asymmetry that turned a published −35% into +9.1% once it was removed."*

REP50 ran with that stripper **on**. Apply the project's own fairness test — *would this sentence help an arm with no tool?* — and "don't build an alternative test harness" plainly would. So the sentence can't go to one arm.

What *is* legitimately eg-only is **the derived command itself** (`cd src && make test`, `vendor/bin/phpunit`) — the baseline has no way to obtain it. So the honest question narrows to: **does handing an agent the correct command, with no advice attached, stop it improvising a harness?** That's a real effect and a fair one, but it is smaller than the raw 8.4-call pool I sized.

## 2. Hooks are dead under `--safe-mode` — but there's a symmetric door

Established three ways, including a zero-cost empirical test via `--init-only`: `--safe-mode` collapses hook config to enterprise policy only, so `PostToolUse` never fires. The agent therefore shipped the verb, not the rider.

But `CC_NO_SAFE_MODE=1` already exists and drops `--safe-mode` from **every arm symmetrically**. That restores the zero-turn rider — the only delivery mechanism that adds information without paying the elasticity tax.

## 3. Two of my stated facts were wrong

- **"13 knobs were dead" is false.** Claude Code passes `{...process.env}` to children, so exported knobs did reach `eg-q`. Whatever misconfigured REP50, it wasn't that mechanism.
- **`EG_TOPK`'s default is already 10**; the 5 came from the driver's own `export EG_TOPK=5`, not the wrapper.

Also: no binary in `bin/` supports `postedit`, so the feat-branch build must be pinned or the capability line self-suppresses.

These two decisions change what gets measured, so they're yours.

You were right that it fails the fairness test. Resolution: neutralise it as a confound rather than delete the effect.

1. Add the anti-harness contract sentences to the **SHARED** prompt block — the one both arms receive byte-identically. Wording should be tool-agnostic, e.g.: "Verify with the project's own test command. Run it once; if it fails, fix the code and re-run the same command. Do not build an alternative test harness, hand-assemble a classpath, or re-verify by reverting and reapplying the edit." No mention of any tool.
2. Set `O35_STRIP_ADVICE=1` for the eg arm so the binary's native copy does not double-ship it.
3. Net effect must be: BOTH arms get the methodology; ONLY eg gets the derived command (`cd src && make test`, `vendor/bin/phpunit`). That is the isolation we want — eg's advantage reduces to graph-derived information the baseline cannot obtain.
4. Confirm `_assert_prompt_symmetry` still passes: the new sentences live in the shared block, so the tool-block digest must be unchanged and the shared digest must be identical across arms.

## DECISION 2 — zero-turn rider via CC_NO_SAFE_MODE=1

Wire delivery option (a) after all, using the symmetric door you found.
1. Cell config sets `CC_NO_SAFE_MODE=1` so `--safe-mode` is dropped from **every** arm. Verify it is genuinely symmetric — if any arm keeps safe-mode, stop and report.
2. `PostToolUse` hook on `Edit|Write` that runs `entire graph postedit` and appends its output to the tool result. Gate it: fire at most once per file per session, skip no-op edits, hard byte cap (suggest 2048), and never fail the tool call if postedit errors — degrade silently.
3. The hook must exist ONLY for the eg arm (baseline has no tool, that is the counterfactual). But `--safe-mode` must be dropped for both.
4. Keep the `postedit` verb working too — the agent may call it explicitly.

## ALSO
5. **Per-instance prewarm.** I measured `postedit` per-edit cost as 4.5s (lucene, 7,083 files), 0.71s (redis), 0.44s (carbon) — but only with a pre-warmed committed index. Cold it is 13–123s. Add a one-time `entire graph index --repo . --profile full --cache-dir <per-instance>` step to instance provisioning, before the session starts, and point the eg wrapper at that same cache dir. It costs no model tokens.
6. **Pin the binary.** No `bin/` binary supports `postedit`. The build is at `graphbench-c:/tmp/eg-pe-linux` (built from `feat/postedit-diff-anchored`). Make the cell config reference an explicit pinned path and FAIL LOUDLY if the binary lacks `postedit` rather than self-suppressing the capability line.

## Report
Caveman-ultra compressed. For each: what changed (file:line), and the verification that the shared block is byte-identical across arms while the tool block differs only by capability text. Flag anything that makes the symmetry claim untrue.

# PRE-REGISTRATION — postedit cell (PE1)

Written and sealed BEFORE any session runs. Sha256 of this file is recorded at seal time.
Nothing below may be edited after the seal; a superseding prereg must be a new file.

## 1. Claim under test

Anchoring entire-graph's post-edit answer on the diff — callers, related sites, signature/arity risk
and a derived VERIFY command, delivered at zero turn cost — reduces total tokens on SWE-bench
Multilingual relative to a no-tool baseline.

## 2. Why a number is expected at all

Turns are the only thing that prices: `log(tokens) ~ log(messages)`, elasticity **1.682**, r=0.957,
message-adjusted residual 0.000. On REP50, `corr(Δturns, token saving) = −0.854`.

REP50 measured the tool at **+1.35%** (CI [−17.0%, +18.2%]) with 98 of 105 graph calls pre-edit and
**zero** post-edit presence, while post-edit held 19.5 turns/session and eg's post-edit shell was
+11.8% WORSE than baseline.

## 3. What is NEW in this cell, and what is deliberately NOT

NEW (eg arm only, all graph-derived — the baseline cannot obtain them):
- the derived VERIFY command for the edited file (`cd src && make test`, `vendor/bin/phpunit`, …)
- callers of each changed definition
- SIGNATURE RISK: call sites whose arity provably broke, or that name a removed definition
- delivered as a `PostToolUse` rider on Edit/Write at **zero turn cost**

DELIBERATELY NOT eg-only — moved to the SHARED prompt block, byte-identical to both arms:
- "run it once; if it fails, fix the code and re-run the same command"
- "do not build an alternative test harness, hand-assemble a classpath, or re-verify by reverting
  and reapplying the edit"

Rationale: those sentences need no graph and would help a no-tool arm equally. Handing them to one
arm is the asymmetry class that turned a published −35% into +9.1%. Giving them to BOTH arms
neutralises the confound and **is expected to shrink the measured effect**, because it removes
improvisation from the baseline too. That is the intended trade: a smaller real number over a
larger retractable one.

`--safe-mode` is dropped from **both** arms (`CC_NO_SAFE_MODE=1`) so the hook mechanism exists; the
hook itself is eg-only because the baseline has no tool, which is the counterfactual being measured.

## 4. Population

SWE-bench Multilingual test split, drawn by set-difference against every burned selector:
executed-anywhere (results dir present) ∪ val30/h30/hk30 ∪ ho5/ho10/ho20 ∪ screen6 ∪ f5/o10/s20 ∪
fb5/op10/sn20 ∪ ties/tier ∪ rep50/rep50_run ∪ g1/g2/g3 ∪ rep30_tasks.

Frozen eval pools (`gate_300`, `prereg100`, `strat60`) are NOT treated as burned by membership —
they were created as eval sets by `freeze_eval_sets.py`; only their executed members are excluded.

Result: **n = 125**, graph-ready, languages PHP 23 · Rust 23 · Ruby 17 · Java 17 · C 15 · JS 13 ·
Go 12 · TS 3 · C++ 2. The exact id list is sealed alongside this file as `PE1-instances.txt`.

## 5. Configuration

- model Opus, effort **max** (primary). `high` and `xhigh` are SECONDARY cells, run only if the
  primary clears its bound. The three efforts may NOT be ranked against each other:
  config-vs-config MDE is ~94pt against ~74pt of observed spread.
- arms: `baseline` (no tool) and `eg` (pinned `feat/postedit-diff-anchored` build). Two arms only.
- `CC_MAX_TURNS=120`, `PUBLISHED_EXACT=1`, `O35_STRIP_ADVICE=1`, `CC_NO_SAFE_MODE=1`.
- committed index pre-warmed once per instance before the session; not counted in session cost.
- arms INTERLEAVED per instance, concurrency capped ~8, to keep rate-limit throttling symmetric.
  Throttling that hits one arm harder is a known sign-flipping confound on this benchmark.

## 6. Gate

A pair is scored iff BOTH arms have `total_cost_usd > 0` AND a non-empty `patch.diff`. Drops are
symmetric: if either arm fails, the instance leaves both. (Verified 2026-08-09 that OAuth
`-p --output-format json` DOES populate `total_cost_usd`, so no gate change is needed.)

Tokens are read from `modelUsage`, not `usage.*` — `usage` is a lossy accumulator, arm-asymmetric on
at least one prior cohort (ml300 baseline mean ratio 1.2691 vs eg 1.0000, max 36x), while
`sum(modelUsage[*].costUSD)` reconciles to `total_cost_usd` to 4.1e-16 across 7,203 sessions.

## 7. PREDICTION (the falsifiable part)

Primary outcome: paired geometric mean of total-token delta, positive = eg saves.

- **point prediction: +12%**
- **95% CI predicted to fall within: +5% to +20%**

Turn-level mechanism prediction, stated so it can fail independently:
- eg post-edit shell calls per session FALL below baseline's (REP50: eg 12.4 vs base 11.1 — eg worse)
- eg total turns/session fall by **4 to 6** versus baseline

## 8. FALSIFICATION

The mechanism is REFUTED as a token lever if any of these hold:
- the 95% CI upper bound is **below +5%**
- eg's turns/session do not fall below baseline's
- eg's post-edit shell-call rate does not fall below baseline's

35% is NOT predicted. Prior evidence records ≥35% as refuted (favourable bound −27.8%; independent
rep30 Haiku −24.1% [−36.6, −8.3]). A result at or above +20% would be a genuine surprise and would
require replication on a second, disjoint draw before being quoted anywhere.

## 9. Reporting rules, fixed now

- report cache_read / cache_creation / output SEPARATELY; the aggregate hides which moved
- report geomean AND median AND bootstrap CI; never a bare point estimate
- report n launched, n gated, n dropped and WHY, per arm
- NO post-hoc subsetting, NO matched-success-only filter, NO re-drawing the population
- if the result misses, it is published as a miss in TokensNotes.md with this prereg's sha256
