1. **`bat-1892` eg re-run** — the failed arm, archived not deleted (`.sharkdp__bat-1892.error_during_execution` kept for diagnosis)
2. **redis-12472 / redis-11510** — the last two pairs finishing
3. **Ten deep analysts** — one per rep50 top-10 loser, then synthesis, then an explicit winner-risk pass

I set the workflow up in the order you asked, with one addition I think is essential: **a third phase that checks each proposed fix against the winners before it goes in the plan.** That's the step this project has historically skipped — per-loser repair previously bought exactly +0.0pt because the fixes cost the winners what they gained on the losers. The winner-risk agent has to show the arithmetic (loser gain − winner cost) per fix and drop any that nets negative.

On your point that eg should also win on the winners: it already does, and that's the tension. The winners aren't neutral — they're where the token mass is, and the current treatment *regressed* four of them (lombok +71%→−17.7% being the worst). So "make the losers save while the winners keep saving" is exactly the right target, and it's why the fix has to be **selective suppression** rather than more output. The tool needs to detect that a session doesn't need help.

The 14.47 points in those ten instances is the honest prize: every one is a turn blowout, six of ten on 1–2 file patches, and retrieval is already correct 84.8% of the time. So it's not a "find the code better" problem — it's a "stop talking when the agent is already on track" problem.

I'll report when the analysts land: the defect classes ranked by points, the exact bugs with file:line where they exist, the winner-risk arithmetic, and a projected pooled rep50 with the surviving plan. Then PE1SAMP vs rep50 once bat and the two redis pairs close out.

3. **Preservation operation** — snapshot the at-risk disks and archive irreplaceable metadata. Explicit prohibitions: *"Do not: start a paid model call; run a benchmark; modify raw benchmark artifacts; edit Entire Graph; edit GraphMark's scoring logic; stop or interfere with graphbench-e or graphbench-f; stop the active memory-benchmark process; delete any VM, disk, snapshot, artifact, branch, worktree, or file; merge any PR; expose credentials."*

4. **Explain token savings mechanism** — why eg should save 35% navigating big codebases, would I use it, is there a bug, why winners won and losers lost.

5. **Goal: get rep50 to 35% token savings** (later revised: *"startwith 15% and build in incremets of 5% from there"*).

## 2. Key Technical Concepts

- **Elasticity law**: `log(tokens) ~ log(messages)`, elasticity **1.682**, r=0.957; message-adjusted residual saving 0.000. Turns are the only thing that prices.
- `corr(Δturns, token saving) = −0.854` on rep50.
- **entire-graph**: 75 MB Go binary, 85% tree-sitter parse tables, cgo, no network. 30 relation types, `compound-v1` symbol IDs (`repoKey:language:path:kind:qualifiedName`), 36 semantic / 149 inventory-only languages.
- **Fairness test** (project doctrine): *"would this sentence help an arm with no tool? If yes, both arms or neither."*
- **Withdrawn headlines**: 54.9%, 57.7%, 31.6% — all killed by arm-asymmetric frugality prompts.
- `usage.*` is lossy (up to 36×, arm-asymmetric); `modelUsage` reconciles to `total_cost_usd` at 4.1e-16.
- **netjail**: PATH-shim sandbox blocking egress and history access in benchmark sessions.
- **Wide-change gate**: `posteditWideChangeFiles = 4`.
- Measurement gate: `total_cost_usd > 0 AND non-empty patch.diff`, dropped symmetrically.

1. **My forensics counted `entire graph grep` as shell grep** — the third explorer caught it before dying. Corrected: eg pre-edit shell −5.8%, post-edit **+11.8% worse**, displacement ratio **−0.21**.

12. **I scored a partial cell** — a background waiter hit its own 10-minute cap and reported "completed"; I read 6 of 12 pairs as a result and had to retract the −1.64%. The Bash tool caps any single wait at 10 minutes.

# PRE-REGISTRATION — PE1 v2 (postedit cell)

**v1 (sha256 d213937e6ebc85ad…) IS VOID.** It claimed 125 instances / 9 languages / fully disjoint;
independent recount showed the draw re-admitted previously-run instances, and adversarial review
found the treatment did not execute at all under the harness sandbox. v1 is retained in the
evidence bucket as a record of the error, not as a live prediction.

Sealed BEFORE any session runs. Nothing here may be edited after the seal.

## 1. Claim under test

Anchoring entire-graph's post-edit answer on the diff — callers, related sites, signature/arity
risk and a derived VERIFY command — reduces total tokens versus a no-tool baseline on SWE-bench
Multilingual.

## 2. Population — two pre-specified strata

Universe: `tasks/multilingual_300.json` (300). Excluded: any instance with a result directory
(156 ever-run) and any without a prebuilt graph.

| stratum | definition | n | languages |
|---|---|--:|---|
| **A** | never run, never tuned-on, not in a nested gate cell | **80** | PHP 17, Rust 16, Java 12, C 10, Ruby 9, JS 7, Go 7, C++ 2 |
| **B** | never run, but a member of a set that informed config | **64** | Ruby 11, Rust 10, C 9, JS 9, PHP 8, Java 7, Go 7, TS 3 |
| **PRIMARY** | A ∪ B | **144** | all 9 |

- **Primary outcome is computed on A+B (n=144).**
- **Secondary, pre-specified: the same statistic on A alone (n=80).** Divergence between A and A+B
  IS the set-level-contamination signal and must be reported whether or not it is convenient.
- No other subgroup may be quoted. Per-language n is 2–26; at ~16/language the MDE exceeds 25%.

## 3. Power, stated honestly

sd in log space from this project's own five prior cells: usd 0.34, tok 0.43.

| | CI half-width | MDE(80%) |
|---|--:|--:|
| n=144 tokens | ±7.0pp | 10.0% |
| n=144 usd | ±5.6pp | 7.9% |
| n=80 tokens | ±9.4pp | 13.5% |

**The dominant uncertainty is BETWEEN cells, not within.** The usd point estimate across five prior
cells was +2.5, −2.5, −10.1, −6.7, +7.0 — a spread of 6.9pp, as large as this cell's own CI. One
cell therefore cannot establish the value of the tool; it can only test this prediction.

## 4. Treatment

eg arm gets, all graph-derived and unobtainable by the baseline:
- `entire graph postedit` — diff-anchored callers, related sites, arity/name risk, derived VERIFY
- a `PostToolUse` rider injecting that output after the first Edit of each file
- `search / def / callers / impact / grep`

Equalised into the SHARED, byte-identical prompt block for BOTH arms:
- the anti-harness verification mandate ("run it once… do not build an alternative test harness…")

### Pre-specified design rule: the wide-change gate

Derived on rep50 (the tuning set) BEFORE this cell runs, and stated here so it cannot be added
post hoc. Bucketing rep50's 49 gated pairs by how many files the NO-TOOL arm's patch touched — a
pre-treatment property, so not division bias — pooled sum-based:

| baseline fan-out | n | share of baseline tokens | pooled delta |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 1 file | 26 | 33.7% | −0.91% |
| 2–3 files | 14 | 38.2% | **+19.36%** |
| 4+ files | 9 | 28.1% | **−20.40%** |

Note the median disagrees with the sum on the 2–3 bucket (−2.4% median vs +19.36% pooled); the
sum is reported because it is what "tokens saved" means.

The loss mechanism is NOT retrieval (payload named the edited file in 84.8%, and misses did no
worse). It is that losing sessions do more work AFTER the first edit: corr(Δ post-edit shell,
saving) = −0.747, losers +6 shell calls and +1 edit, to the SAME files (fan-out identical at 1.0
in both arms).

**Rule: `postedit` withholds CALLERS and SIGNATURE RISK once the edit spans ≥4 files, emitting
only CHANGED and VERIFY.** Suppression is reported, never silent.

This is DEFENSIVE, not a lever, and the prediction is NOT raised for it. The −20.40% was measured
with the pre-postedit tool, so the gate cannot recover it; it exists because `postedit` injects
more post-edit information into precisely the loop that is already losing there, and would
otherwise risk amplifying it.

This equalisation is expected to SHRINK the measured effect, because it removes improvisation from
the baseline too. That trade is deliberate: a smaller real number over a larger retractable one.

## 5. LAUNCH GATES — the cell may not start unless all pass

1. **Functional treatment probe.** In a dirty scratch checkout, under the real cell PATH
   (`netjail` first), `postedit` output must contain BOTH `CHANGED vs ` and a line starting
   `VERIFY:`. A `help`-grep is NOT sufficient: netjail blocked `git diff HEAD` and the verb
   degraded to a 76-byte false "unavailable in this build" line while every prior check passed.
2. **Rider/strip coupling.** Abort if `EG_POSTEDIT_HOOK=1` and `O35_STRIP_ADVICE != 1`.
3. **Injected-byte audit.** Every post-truncation injected byte is written to `hook_injected.txt`
   and scanned for imperative-mood methodology; a hit fails the instance.
4. **Arm order alternates** per instance; `PKG_ISO` asserted unset or arm-scoped.
5. **Cross-arm digest equality** of `shared_block.sha256` checked at runtime, not just written.
6. **No instance identifier in either prompt** (wrapper emitted at a neutral hashed path).
7. `enabledPlugins` empty, no user settings.json, no user CLAUDE.md on the host.

## 6. Gate and accounting

Pair scored iff BOTH arms have `total_cost_usd > 0` AND non-empty `patch.diff`; drops symmetric.
Report per-arm gate-failure counts AND their cost distribution — gate failure is arm-specific and
cost-correlated, so the symmetric drop deletes outliers rather than neutralising them.
Tokens from `modelUsage`. Report cache_read / cache_creation / output separately.
Model Opus, effort max. `CC_MAX_TURNS=120` and `CC_TIMEOUT` pinned explicitly.

## 7. PREDICTION

Revised DOWN from +12% before sealing, after computing the lever's ceiling on rep50's real
per-instance data. Counterfactual re-pricing through the elasticity, holding baseline fixed:

| counterfactual (perfect displacement, zero rider cost — UPPER bounds) | turns/session | delta |
|---|--:|--:|
| remove the answerable post-edit class (eg-only after the fairness fix) | −4.5 | **+14.78%** |
| remove improvised harnesses (now shared with baseline, so ~0 differential) | −3.7 | +11.75% |
| remove both | −8.2 | +24.59% |
| remove ALL eg post-edit shell | −22.9 | +60.38% |

35% would require −13.1 turns/session. The fair addressable pool is **4.5**. So +14.78% is a hard
ceiling for this lever, before subtracting the rider's own cost (~0.54% of session tokens per
injection, uncapped across a fan-out with median 1 and max 172 files) and before any displacement
inefficiency.

Primary: paired geometric mean token delta on A+B, positive = eg saves.
- **point: +7%**
- **95% CI predicted within [0%, +15%]**
- a result above **+14.78%** would exceed the perfect-displacement ceiling and must be treated as a
  measurement defect until explained, not as a win

Mechanism predictions, independently falsifiable:
- eg turns/session fall by 4–6 versus baseline
- eg post-edit shell-call rate falls below baseline's (REP50: eg 12.4 vs base 11.1 — eg was worse)
- stratum A and A+B agree within 5pp

## 8. FALSIFICATION

Refuted as a token lever if ANY holds:
- 95% CI upper bound below **+3%**
- eg turns/session do not fall below baseline
- eg post-edit shell-call rate does not fall
- A and A+B differ by more than 5pp (indicates set-level contamination is driving the result)

**35% IS NOT REACHABLE BY THIS LEVER AND IS NOT PREDICTED.** This is now arithmetic, not judgement:
35% requires removing 13.1 turns/session; the entire fair addressable pool measured on rep50 is 4.5.
Reaching 35% would require deleting essentially all post-edit shell exploration (−22.9/session),
which is not an information problem — it requires the patch to be correct on the FIRST attempt.
That is a correctness capability, not a retrieval one, and no payload change closes it.

Prior evidence already recorded ≥35% as refuted (favourable bound −27.8%; rep30 Haiku −24.1%
[−36.6, −8.3]). This cell does not re-open that question; it tests a +7% mechanism.

## 9. Reporting limits, fixed now

Any published sentence MUST carry, in the same paragraph:
1. nothing is graded — the gate is "produced a patch", so this measures cost, not correctness;
2. this is a tool-PLUS-RIDER contrast; the rider's scheduling is methodology the baseline lacks,
   so the figure is an UPPER BOUND on the shipped product's value;
3. instance-level but not repo-level out-of-sample; retrieval constants and the VERIFY ladder were
   fitted on earlier cells drawn from the same repos;
4. between-cell spread (6.9pp) is as large as this CI, so this is not a point estimate of "the
   value of a code graph";
5. per-arm gate-failure counts and the all-gated sensitivity row beside the headline.

No post-hoc subsetting. No matched-success-only filter. No re-drawing the population. If it misses,
it is published as a miss in TokensNotes.md with this file's sha256.

Rider cost is real: injected context is ~0.54% of session tokens PER injection, replayed every
later turn, uncapped across a fan-out with median 1 / max 172 files per patch. "Zero turn cost"
is true of the turn counter and false of the metric.

**How to apply:** do not accept a >+14.78% postedit result without explaining it — it exceeds the
perfect-displacement ceiling and is a defect signal. Related: [[rep50-35pct-arithmetically-unreachable]],
[[harness-building-is-the-whole-mechanism]], [[eg-route-to-35-falsified]].

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""What is the CEILING of the postedit lever, computed on rep50's real per-instance data?
Counterfactual: remove from eg's turn count exactly the post-edit calls postedit could answer,
hold baseline fixed, re-price through the project's own elasticity (tokens ~ messages^1.682).
This is an UPPER bound: it assumes perfect displacement and zero rider cost."""
import json, os, re, glob, statistics, math, collections

S = os.path.expanduser("~/work/graphmark/agentic-swebench")
PROJ = os.path.expanduser("~/.claude/projects")
tx = {}
for f in glob.glob(f"{PROJ}/**/*.jsonl", recursive=True):
    tx.setdefault(os.path.basename(f)[:-6], []).append(f)

GRAPH = re.compile(r'(?:^|[;&|]\s*|\s)(?:entire\s+graph|eg-q(?:\.run)?|entire-graph)\s+(\w+)')
SHELL = re.compile(r'(?:^|[;&|]\s*)\s*(?:sudo\s+|time\s+|env\s+\S+=\S+\s+)*(grep|egrep|fgrep|rg|ag|ack|find|locate|cat|head|tail|sed|awk|ls)\b')
BUILD = re.compile(r'\b(make|cmake|go\s+(build|test|vet)|cargo|mvn|gradle|npm|npx|pnpm|yarn|pytest|phpunit|composer|bundle|rake|rspec|ctest|javac|tsc|jest|vitest|runtest)\b')
# what postedit can answer, POST-EDIT only
ANSWERABLE = re.compile(
 r'(test|spec|__tests__|package\.json|Makefile|CMakeLists|go\.mod|Cargo\.toml|pom\.xml|build\.gradle|composer\.json'  # find the test/build
 r'|def |func |function |class |fn |struct |interface '                                                              # does symbol exist
 r'|error|Error|undefined|not defined|no such|cannot find|unresolved|expected'                                        # build error
 r'|sed -n|head -n|tail -n)', re.I)                                                                                   # reread edited region
SCRATCH = re.compile(r"(cat\s*>|tee\s+)[^|]*(/tmp/|repro|scratch)|(\bnode\b|\bpython3?\b|\bruby\b|\bphp\b)[^|;]*(/tmp/|repro|scratch)", re.I)

def arm(a):
    base = f"{S}/results/REP50_r1_{a}/{a}"; out = {}
    for iid in sorted(os.listdir(base)):
        d = f"{base}/{iid}"; cc = f"{d}/cc_out.json"
        if not os.path.exists(cc) or os.path.getsize(cc) == 0: continue
        j = json.load(open(cc)); u = j.get("usage") or {}
        r = dict(turns=j.get("num_turns") or 0,
                 tot=sum(u.get(k,0) for k in ("input_tokens","output_tokens","cache_read_input_tokens","cache_creation_input_tokens")),
                 sid=j.get("session_id"), ans=0, scratch=0, post=0)
        phase = 0
        for f in tx.get(r["sid"] or "", []):
            for line in open(f, errors="replace"):
                try: o = json.loads(line)
                except Exception: continue
                m = o.get("message") or {}
                for b in (m.get("content") or []) if isinstance(m.get("content"), list) else []:
                    if not isinstance(b, dict) or b.get("type") != "tool_use": continue
                    nm = b.get("name")
                    if nm in ("Edit","MultiEdit","Write","NotebookEdit"): phase = 1; continue
                    if nm != "Bash" or not phase: continue
                    cmd = (b.get("input") or {}).get("command") or ""
                    rest = GRAPH.sub(' ', cmd)
                    if GRAPH.search(cmd) and not SHELL.search(rest): continue
                    r["post"] += 1
                    if SCRATCH.search(cmd): r["scratch"] += 1
                    elif SHELL.search(rest) and not BUILD.search(rest) and ANSWERABLE.search(cmd): r["ans"] += 1
        out[iid] = r
    return out

B, E = arm("baseline"), arm("eg")
ids = [i for i in sorted(set(B) & set(E)) if B[i]["tot"] and E[i]["tot"]]
EL = 1.682

def pooled(newturns):
    """re-price eg's tokens by the turn ratio change, pooled sum-based"""
    sb = sum(B[i]["tot"] for i in ids)
    se = sum(E[i]["tot"] * ((newturns(i) / E[i]["turns"]) ** EL if E[i]["turns"] else 1) for i in ids)
    return 1 - se / sb

print(f"gated pairs: {len(ids)}")
print(f"as-run pooled token delta                     : {100*pooled(lambda i: E[i]['turns']):+6.2f}%")
print()
tot_ans = sum(E[i]["ans"] for i in ids); tot_scr = sum(E[i]["scratch"] for i in ids)
print(f"eg post-edit calls postedit could answer      : {tot_ans}  ({tot_ans/len(ids):.1f}/session)")
print(f"eg post-edit improvised-harness calls         : {tot_scr}  ({tot_scr/len(ids):.1f}/session)")
print()
print("CEILING SCENARIOS (perfect displacement, zero rider cost — all UPPER bounds):")
for lab, fn in [
    ("remove answerable post-edit only",      lambda i: max(1, E[i]["turns"] - E[i]["ans"])),
    ("remove improvised harness only",        lambda i: max(1, E[i]["turns"] - E[i]["scratch"])),
    ("remove BOTH (the pre-fairness pool)",   lambda i: max(1, E[i]["turns"] - E[i]["ans"] - E[i]["scratch"])),
    ("remove ALL eg post-edit shell",         lambda i: max(1, E[i]["turns"] - E[i]["post"])),
]:
    d = 100 * pooled(fn)
    avg = statistics.mean(E[i]["turns"] - fn(i) for i in ids)
    print(f"  {lab:<36} {d:+6.2f}%   (−{avg:.1f} turns/session)")

print()
print("WHAT SURVIVES THE FAIRNESS CORRECTION")
print("  the improvised-harness suppression is generic methodology -> now given to BOTH arms,")
print("  so eg's DIFFERENTIAL access to it is ~0. Only the answerable class stays eg-only.")
d_fair = 100 * pooled(lambda i: max(1, E[i]["turns"] - E[i]["ans"]))
print(f"  => fair ceiling for postedit alone          : {d_fair:+6.2f}%")
need = (1 - 0.35) ** (1 / EL)
tb = sum(B[i]["turns"] for i in ids); te = sum(E[i]["turns"] for i in ids)
print(f"  turns needed for 35%: eg={int(tb*need)} vs actual {te}  -> −{(te-tb*need)/len(ids):.1f}/session")
print(f"  answerable pool is only {tot_ans/len(ids):.1f}/session")

# Plan — move Entire Graph toward 35% token savings on SWE-bench Multilingual

## Context

The goal is 35% token savings. The current honest measurement is **+1.35%** on REP50_r1
(49 instances × 4 arms, Opus max), bootstrap 95% CI **[−17.0%, +18.2%]**. This plan exists because
the forensics say the shortfall has one cause, and it is not retrieval quality.

**Why tokens move at all.** `log(tokens) ~ log(messages)`, elasticity **1.682**, r=0.957;
message-adjusted residual saving is 0.000. Turns are the only thing that prices. Measured on rep50:
`corr(Δturns, token saving) = −0.854`.

**What that costs us.** To hit 35% the eg arm must run **2067 turns** against baseline's 2671 —
**641 fewer than the 2709 it actually ran**, i.e. **13.1 turns/session** removed (55.3 → 42.2).

**Where the turns are** (49 sessions, corrected to exclude `entire graph *` invocations from the
shell counts — my first pass miscounted them and reported "zero grep elimination", which was wrong):

| | baseline | eg | |
|---|--:|--:|---|
| shell exploration, pre-edit | 725 | 683 | −5.8% ✅ |
| shell exploration, post-edit | 542 | **606** | **+11.8%** ❌ |
| build/test runs | 508 | 493 | −3.0% ✅ |
| edits | 397 | 414 | +4.3% |
| graph calls | 0 | 105 (**98 pre / 7 post**) | 93% pre-edit |

**Displacement ratio: −0.21 shell calls removed per graph call.** The tool wins the phase it is
present in and loses more in the phase it is absent from. The post-edit pool is **19.5 turns/session**
(12.4 shell + 7.1 build) and the graph makes **0.14 calls/session** there. It is the only pool large
enough to fund 13.1 turns.

**Retrieval is not the problem.** Payload named the file the agent actually edited in **28/33 = 84.8%**
of sessions that logged a payload. Stop tuning ranking.

**REP50 also measured a stale, misconfigured tool** — nine relevant commits landed after it ran
(`changed`, riders, `--path`, batched `def`, never-refuse, payload logging), it ran `EG_TOPK=5`
instead of 10, its `grep` verb ran raw `grep -rInE` across `node_modules/`, and **13 knobs
`run_REP50.sh` exported were silently dead** because `eg-q.run` hardcodes a fixed variable list.

---

## Design

One idea: **anchor the post-edit answer on the diff instead of on query hits.**

Every block that answers "what else must change / what will break" already exists and is wired to the
wrong anchor. `changed.go:318 symbolOverlapsHunks` already computes the edited-span anchor set and
discards it on everything except caller counts.

| existing block | answers | currently anchored on |
|---|---|---|
| `internal/sem/search_related.go` (950 L) | what else must change | query hits |
| `internal/sem/search_closedset.go` (996 L) | what breaks silently at runtime | query hits |
| `internal/cli/callsite.go` (25 KB) | real call line + enclosing guards | query hits |
| `internal/sem/search_verify.go` (1867 L) | the narrowest test command | query hits, **unexported** |

### A. entire-graph (`/Users/suhaan/devenv/entire-graph`)

1. **Make VERIFY askable.** `buildSearchVerifyCommand` (search_verify.go:199) is unexported and takes
   `[]SearchResult`. Extract a subject-based entry point taking `(repo, sourcePath, testPath)`;
   `SearchRepository` (search.go:1225) becomes one caller. Keep the four-tier ladder and the residual
   floor exactly as-is. Do **not** use the `--path` hack — verified to misfire (scoping to
   `changed.go` emitted a VERIFY for `TestDoctorPrintsEntireEnvironment`).

2. **New verb `entire graph postedit`.** Model on `internal/cli/changed.go`; reuse
   `gitutil.WorktreeChangedFiles` (worktree.go:277) and `symbolOverlapsHunks` (changed.go:318).
   Emits, budgeted, for the edited spans only:
   - callers of each changed definition (already in `changed`)
   - **related sites** — re-anchor `selectSearchRelatedSites` (search_related.go:345) on edited spans
   - **closed-set warning** — re-anchor `buildSearchClosedSet` (search_closedset.go:142) on edited spans
   - **VERIFY** for the edited file, from A.1
   - **arity/name check** (new, see A.3)

3. **Arity/name check — the one genuinely new analysis.** Nothing in the repo compares a signature to
   a call site; `def`/sigtypes only display. Build it from `callsite.go`'s existing raw material plus
   the symbol's signature: for each edited symbol whose parameter list changed, walk its resolved call
   sites and report arity mismatches and unresolved field/method names. This is the class of defect
   that makes a patch fail to build, which is what the post-edit loop is burning turns on.

4. **Fix the cost wall — precondition, not optional.** Every worktree-aware verb costs **14.2 s warm
   or cold** (`index_latency_ms ≈ 14,188` vs `query_latency_ms ≈ 3`); it is a full re-index, caused by
   `MaxDirtyFilesForDigest = 64` (gitutil/worktree.go:61) plus `hashDirectory` (worktree.go:177)
   walking nested worktrees. `postedit` must reuse a `--head` snapshot and incrementally reparse only
   the changed files. **Target < 1 s.** A verb called after every edit at 14 s is worse than useless.

5. **Housekeeping that changes measurement.** Add `changed`, `postedit`, `def`, `verify` to
   `graphVerbs` (internal/cli/stats.go:62) — today every call to them is invisible to `stats`. Add
   `changed`/`postedit` to `printHelp` and to the embedded `agentGuide` (internal/cli/agents.go).
   Filter inventory-only languages out of `changed`'s ranking (Markdown `section`/`code_fence` records
   currently fill the top-20). Write the tests `changed` has never had (zero today).

### B. Harness (`~/graphmark-bench/agentic-swebench` — the live copy, **not** `devenv/graphmark`)

6. **Un-break the knob surface.** `run_3arm.sh:457` hardcodes the variable list baked into
   `eg-q.run`; anything absent is dead for agent calls. Forward the 13 dead knobs. Restore
   `EG_TOPK=10`.
7. **Fix the `grep` verb.** It takes `rx="$*"`, so `eg-q grep -i wikidata` searched for the literal
   string `-i wikidata`. Apply the post-REP50 vendor/minified filter and the never-refuse
   grep→search fallback (`b5473b0b`), both already written.
8. **Deliver post-edit at zero turn cost.** A verb costs a turn; a rider costs none, and bytes are
   nearly free while turns price at elasticity 1.682. Wire `postedit` output as a `PostToolUse` rider
   on Edit/Write (`EG_CHANGED_RIDER` already exists in LIVE) and gate it — fire on the first edit per
   file, cap hard, never on a no-op edit.
9. **Port the fairness gate.** `_assert_prompt_symmetry` exists only in `devenv/graphmark`
   (run_3arm.sh:1002-1029). LIVE has no machine-checked prompt-symmetry gate. Port it before any cell.
   Prompt changes stay **capability description only** — the harness's own rule (`run_3arm.sh:1203`):
   the arm block says what the tool *is and returns*, never *when to use it*.

### C. Interface lever, measured separately (phase 2)

10. `EG_MCP=1` (run_3arm.sh:787) puts the graph in the model's native tool list beside `Grep`/`Read`.
    It is mutually exclusive with `--safe-mode`, which silently strips all MCP servers.
    **`--safe-mode` must be dropped for both arms or it is an arm confound** — and doing so makes the
    cell non-comparable to every prior cell, which is why it gets its own cell.

---

## Verification

**Gate 1 — offline replay, zero model cost (do this before spending anything).**
Per the forensics drill §5: replay the 105 recorded queries in `results/REP50_r1_eg/eg/*/gq_calls.log`
against the new binary, and reconstruct the 606 post-edit shell commands from the transcripts. Measure
what fraction `postedit` would actually have answered. **Proceed only if it answers ≥ 40%** — below
that the arithmetic cannot reach even 20% and the cells are wasted.

**Gate 2 — sealed pre-registration.**
Draw the holdout by set-difference against every burned selector: rep50 ∪ val30/h30 ∪ ho5/10/20 ∪
gate_5/10/20/30/60/300 ∪ prereg30/100 ∪ GEM300 ∪ fab82 ∪ SW_* ∪ G1/G2/G3. Freeze the id list, the
predicted effect and the falsification bounds to a file **before** the run, with sha256.

**Gate 3 — the cells.** Opus at effort `high`, `xhigh`, `max`. Gate a pair only if both arms have
`usd > 0` and a non-empty patch; drop symmetrically. Report cache_read / cache_creation / output
**separately**, geomean plus bootstrap CI, never a bare point estimate.

**Cost:** ~$307 per 49-instance 2-arm cell at Opus (rep50's 196 sessions cost $614). Three effort
levels ≈ **$920**; the phase-2 interface cell adds ~$307. Budget **~$1,200–1,900**.

**Power caveat:** at n=49 a single cell detects roughly a 25-point effect. The three effort levels can
each answer "does eg save at this effort", but **cannot reliably rank each other** — config-vs-config
MDE is ~94 points against ~74 points of observed spread. Do not read the ordering.

---

## GATE 1 RESULT — run 2026-08-09, read-only, zero model cost: **PASS**

Classified all 606 post-edit shell calls in the REP50 eg arm:

| class | n | % | answerable by diff-anchored postedit |
|---|--:|--:|---|
| re-read the edited region | 105 | 17.3% | yes (the rider carries it) |
| find-or-run the right test | 97 | 16.0% | yes (VERIFY) |
| error from a failed build | 21 | 3.5% | yes (arity/name check) |
| other call sites | 13 | 2.1% | yes (callers/related) |
| does this symbol exist | 13 | 2.1% | yes (def/arity) |
| env / toolchain hunting | 54 | 8.9% | no |
| unclassified | 303 | 50.0% | see below |
| **answerable** | **249** | **41.1%** | **≥40% threshold met** |

**The unclassified half is the real finding.** It is dominated by agents writing and running
throwaway reproduction harnesses (`cat > /tmp/repro.mjs <<EOF`, `node repro.mjs`, `cat > edge.cc`).
Sized separately, post-edit:

| per session | baseline | eg |
|---|--:|--:|
| improvised repro-harness calls | 8.3 | **8.4** |
| real test-suite runs | 2.7 | 2.3 |
| sessions that improvise at all | 46/49 | **46/49** |

Agents improvise a harness **3.6× more often than they run the real suite**, and eg does not reduce
it at all. This is the known mechanism — throwaway harnesses are 79% of the gain and 43% of the loss —
and it is the one class the tool has never attacked.

**Addressable pool ≈ 13.5 turns/session** (8.4 improvised + 5.1 answerable shell, some overlap)
against the **13.1 needed for 35%**. The lever is not "answer greps"; it is
**stop the agent improvising a verification harness**, which is what VERIFY exists for and which today
fires pre-edit, inside `search`, and is ignored by 46/49 sessions.

## Honest expected value, and the stop rule

| if postedit eliminates | turns/session | predicted saving |
|---|--:|--:|
| half the improvisation + answerable shell | ~8 | **≈21%** |
| most of both | ~12 | **≈32%** |
| the whole addressable pool | 13.5 | ≈35% |

So 35% is **arithmetically in range** — it was not before this gate. It requires near-total post-edit
displacement, which no prior config has achieved. Realistic band: **20–32%**. The project's drill
still records ≥35% as *refuted* on prior evidence (favourable bound −27.8%; rep30 Haiku −24.1%
[−36.6, −8.3]), and nothing here overturns that yet — it only shows a pool big enough to try.

**Stop rule:** if the sealed cell lands below the pre-registered lower bound, it is published as a
miss — no post-hoc subsetting, no matched-success filter, no re-drawing the set.

---

## Infrastructure, credentials, blockers

**Fleet:** `graphbench-c` RUNNING (SPOT, 32 vCPU / 117 GB, 698 GB free) — harness `4a2ea82`,
entire-graph src `c500baa` branch `r1r2`, **310 prebuilt graphs**, 9.4 GB repo-cache, docker running,
`claude` 2.1.224, node v22. `graphbench-a`/`-b` TERMINATED (SPOT, preempted 2026-08-07, disks intact +
now snapshotted). `graphbench-e`/`-f` are memory-bench's and must not be touched.

**Credential — Claude Code OAuth token (user is supplying).** Verified on graphbench-e, which already
runs under OAuth (`.claude.json` carries `oauthAccount`). Place in `~/.authenv` (mode 600) or the
Mac keychain; never in a launcher script. The existing plaintext API key in
`graphbench-c:~/go50.sh` / `~/go50b.sh` (`export AT=sk-ant-…`) should be **rotated regardless** — it
was catalogued during the preservation audit.

**OAUTH CHANGES THE MEASUREMENT — measured, not assumed.** On a live OAuth session:

| field | API-key sessions (REP50) | OAuth session (graphbench-e) |
|---|---|---|
| `usage` / output_tokens | populated | **populated** (191 msgs, 47,402 out) |
| `costUSD` / `total_cost_usd` | reconciles to 4.1e-16 | **0 records, $0.0000** |

Cost comes from the API billing path. The scored-pair gate is `usd > 0 AND non-empty patch`
(`tools/metrics.py:152-154`; same in `sc50.py`, `score_ladder.py`) — **under OAuth every pair
gate-fails and the cell yields nothing.**
**Required change: gate on `output_tokens > 0 AND non-empty patch`.** Auth-agnostic, and tokens are
the metric of record anyway. This is a scoring-gate change and must be applied identically to both
arms and recorded in the pre-registration.

**Rate limits replace dollars.** 98 sessions/cell × 3 effort levels at Opus max will throttle.
Throttling is a known arm confound here (starvation inflates whichever arm runs under it and can flip
the sign). Mitigations, both mandatory: **interleave baseline/eg per instance** instead of running
arms in blocks, and cap concurrency (~8-way). Run one smoke instance first to confirm
`--effort max` behaves on a subscription tier.

**Blockers, all requiring your approval:**
1. **`go` is not installed on graphbench-c** — cannot build the modified binary. Build inside a
   `golang` docker container (docker is up; tree-sitter needs CGO and the Mac is arm64), or install
   the toolchain on the VM.
2. **graphbench-c is SPOT and was already preempted once** (all three spot VMs died in one 9-second
   window). A multi-hour Opus cell can vanish. Recommend a STANDARD VM for the measurement cell.
3. Token placement + rotation of the leaked API key.

Base directory for this skill: /Users/suhaan/.claude/skills/graph-bench-forensics

# Graph benchmark forensics

Measure a context tool honestly, at the level of individual sessions and individual token classes.
This drill exists because aggregates on this benchmark are routinely wrong in *both* directions, and
every headline that was ever withdrawn was withdrawn for a reason this checklist catches.

## The cost model — get this right first, everything else follows

**Cost is not "tokens".** Solve for per-token prices from recorded `total_cost_usd` (least squares
over cache_read / cache_creation / output, n≈30) rather than assuming. Measured on rep30:

| model | $/Mtok cache_read | cache_creation | output | **cost share** cr / cc / out |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Fable 5 | 1.00 | 20.31 | 49.63 | 22% / 39% / 39% |
| Opus 5 | 0.50 | 10.19 | 24.73 | 26% / 38% / 36% |
| Sonnet | 0.29 | 6.33 | 14.78 | 41% / 31% / 28% |
| Haiku | 0.10 | 2.09 | 4.96 | 46% / 28% / 25% |

Two traps, both of which produced wrong conclusions:

- **"95% of tokens are cache_read" is a token COUNT, not a cost share.** Output is priced 20–50×
  higher, so it is 25–39% of the bill. A tool that cuts reading and raises writing LOSES money.
  Fable is the clean case: turns fell 10% and cost rose 15%, because output rose 14.7%.
- **Cost ≈ MESSAGES × context.** At a large context a message costs ~446k cache-read tokens. Count
  messages, not tool calls. (Note: parallel tool calls were not reachable in this harness — 0 of
  10,374 messages carried more than one — so "batch your calls" is un-actionable advice, and any
  prompt rule telling an agent to batch is dead weight given to both arms.)

Always report cache_read / cache_creation / output **separately**. The aggregate usd hides which
one moved, and which one moved is the finding.

## The noise floor — respect it or you will publish noise

- Same-instance spread across repeated cells: **45pt median**, tail to 335pt. One instance measured
  +404% / +97% / +69% across three configs.
- Every single-cell CI on this benchmark spans zero for the weaker models. **MDE ≈ CI width ≈ 31%
  at n=30**, so only effects ≥ ~30pt are detectable in one cell.
- **0/30 instances produce the same agent query twice** (median token overlap 0.55). Retrieval
  itself varies run to run, so any replay that fixes the query measures one sample of the input.

Rules that follow:
1. **Never score a partial cell.** A Sonnet geomean moved 47 points between n=9 and n=25.
2. **Never bucket one cell into sub-groups of 3–7 and read the differences.** That is how the
   "VERIFY-off is a −12pt lever" and "payload width costs 10.6pt" claims were produced, and both
   were retracted.
3. **Compare configs with replicates of the SAME config**, not two different configs' point
   estimates. Pooling different configs estimates "expected value across configs tried".
4. **Report bootstrap CIs, never a bare point estimate.**
5. Trust **deterministic offline replays** (re-issuing recorded queries against the binary) far
   more than single-session attributions.

## The measurement gate

A session counts only if `total_cost_usd > 0` **AND** `patch.diff` is non-empty. Drop pairs
**symmetrically** — if either arm gate-fails on an instance, the instance leaves both arms.
Otherwise a cheap gate-failure reads as a saving.

Also check before trusting any per-instance delta: `result` length, `num_turns`, and `subtype`
(`error_max_turns` sessions are right-censored, so their true cost is ≥ recorded).

## Fairness — the failure mode that has invalidated the most results

Every withdrawn headline on this benchmark came from **asymmetric prompts**, not from the tool.

- Diff the two arms' `prompt.txt` and account for **every** differing line. A "−35%" result once
  came from two extra instructions the tool arm had and the baseline did not (*"never write a
  throwaway test script"*, *"no `which`, no `ls vendor/`, no `find / -name php*`"*). Removing them
  moved the same cell from −14.9% to +9.1%.
- Frugality clamps belong in the **shared** block or nowhere.
- A tool-side default change (ranking, payload content, a flag) is legitimate. Extra *instructions*
  to one arm are not.
- Distinguish "tool as shipped, including its recommended prompt" from "the tool's marginal value
  under one contract". Both are real questions; say which you measured.

## The drill

### 1. Verify the data before analysing it
- Confirm inputs exist: repo clones, graphs, and **`patch.diff` for every gated session**.
- Check for silent loss: a driver that skips on the session log alone will skip forever a session
  whose patch vanished. On this suite a `/private/tmp` reap destroyed 4 patches, 27 graphs and
  every packfile — and the lost instances were ones the tool won by 20+ turns, biasing *against* it.
- Keep the suite off volatile paths.

### 2. Score the cell
Per-instance paired table: usd, turns, cache_read/cache_creation/output, gate status. Then geomean
+ bootstrap CI. Then per-language, then per-instance sorted by contribution to the shortfall.

### 3. Decompose the transcripts — this is where the answers are
For each session (`~/.claude/projects/*/<session_id>.jsonl`, keyed off `cc_out.json:session_id`):

- **Phase split at the first Edit/Write.** Post-edit is typically ~65% of output and is where every
  losing instance's delta lives.
- **Per-tool token attribution.** Dedupe by `message.id`, credit each message's `output_tokens` to
  its tool. This tells you whether the delta is Edit bodies, Bash commands, or prose.
- **Count**: Edit/Write calls, distinct files touched, throwaway/repro scripts, prose length.
- **Classify every grep/find/read** the tool arm still ran (see below).

### 4. The single strongest predictor found: grep elimination
Compute `eg_greps / baseline_greps` per instance.

| greps eliminated | Haiku | Sonnet |
|---|---|---|
| >75% | **−46.1%** | — |
| 40–75% | −39.6% | −17.3% |
| <40% | +1.9% | +31.8% |

corr(grep ratio, log usd) = **+0.615 Haiku / +0.712 Sonnet**, while corr(**baseline** greps,
outcome) ≈ 0 — so it is not task difficulty leaking through. **This is the metric to optimise.**

Then classify the *residual* greps to decide what to fix:

| what the grep was for | share | fix |
|---|---|---|
| finding something NEW | 38% | recall / ranking |
| searching inside a file the payload returned | 29% | payload under-delivery |
| re-finding a symbol the payload already gave | 25% | payload under-delivery |
| env / build hunting | 8% | verify-command quality |

### 5. Falsify offline before spending a cell
Recorded queries live at `results/<tag>/eg/<instance>/gq_calls.log`, emitted payloads at the same
path + `.payload`, worktrees at `replay-wt/<instance>`. Replay against the binary at **zero model
cost** and assert the change does what you claim — *and* that nothing else moved.

Replay across **every** recorded query variant, not one, because the agent rephrases every run.

### 6. Only then run a cell, and pre-register
Write the prediction and its falsification bounds to a file **before** the run. An out-of-sample
prediction that survives is worth more than ten post-hoc explanations. (Worked: Opus predicted
−0.1% from band effects fitted on cells excluding it; measured −0.5%, n=30.)

## Known results — do not re-derive these

- **≥35% is refuted, not unproven.** The favourable CI bound on total tokens is −27.8%
  (`eg-consolidated/AGENTS.md`). Independent rep30 measurement: Haiku −24.1% CI [−36.6, −8.3].
- Four models, rep30, paired: Fable +14.9%, Opus −0.5%, Sonnet +9.4%, Haiku −24.1%. **The tool
  saves on one of four.**
- Savings depend on how much the *no-tool* arm explores: pooled n=175, corr −0.238
  [−0.346, −0.134]; costs money under ~12 baseline turns, peaks ≈ −30% at 20–49, tapers above.
  **It does not explain Sonnet** (predicted −14.5%, measured +9.4% — a 24pt miss).
- Raising the turn cap does **not** help — both arms grow proportionally (−24.1% → −21.3%).
- Prefetching the search from the issue text is **dominated**: gold-visible@5 0.567 vs 0.715 for the
  agent's own distilled query, 8 losses to 0 wins. The invocation turn is irreducible.
- Retrieval quality and token savings are **different axes**. A config that improved gold-visible
  0.729 → 0.829 across 167 real queries measured *worse* on tokens.

## Discipline

- Keep an **audit ledger**: every claim tagged solid / moderate / retracted, with its basis. Publish
  the retractions.
- When a result contradicts an earlier one, find the mechanism before believing either.
- Correct memory notes in place when they are falsified; a wrong note propagates.
- **Do not stop at a negative finding.** Every apparent dead end here dissolved one layer down — in
  the transcripts, the harness, or the tool's source. But going deeper is the way through, not a
  licence to loosen the standard of evidence: report the interval, report what you retracted, and
  say plainly when a target is not reached.


ARGUMENTS: decompose REP50_r1 (49 instances × 4 arms) per-turn: pre-edit vs post-edit token cost, size the post-edit lever toward 35%

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""PE1SAMP vs its own REP50 pairs. Tokens from modelUsage; gate = cost>0 AND non-empty patch."""
import json, os, glob, math

def toks(cc):
    """sum of all four token classes, preferring modelUsage (reconciles to usd at 4.1e-16)."""
    mu = cc.get("modelUsage") or {}
    if mu:
        t = 0
        for m in mu.values():
            for k in ("inputTokens","outputTokens","cacheReadInputTokens","cacheCreationInputTokens"):
                t += m.get(k, 0) or 0
        if t: return t
    u = cc.get("usage") or {}
    return sum(u.get(k,0) or 0 for k in
               ("input_tokens","output_tokens","cache_read_input_tokens","cache_creation_input_tokens"))

def load(root, tag, arm):
    base = f"{root}/results/{tag}_r1_{arm}/{arm}"
    out = {}
    if not os.path.isdir(base): return out
    for iid in sorted(os.listdir(base)):
        if iid.startswith('.'): continue
        d = f"{base}/{iid}"; cc = f"{d}/cc_out.json"; pf = f"{d}/patch.diff"
        if not os.path.exists(cc) or os.path.getsize(cc) == 0: continue
        try: j = json.load(open(cc))
        except Exception: continue
        out[iid] = dict(
            tok=toks(j), usd=j.get("total_cost_usd") or 0, turns=j.get("num_turns") or 0,
            sub=j.get("subtype"), err=j.get("is_error"),
            patch=(os.path.getsize(pf) if os.path.exists(pf) else 0))
    return out

PE1 = os.path.expanduser("~/pe1/graphmark/agentic-swebench")
R50 = os.path.expanduser("~/work/graphmark/agentic-swebench")

pe_e, pe_b = load(PE1,"PE1SAMP","eg"), load(PE1,"PE1SAMP","baseline")
r_e,  r_b  = load(R50,"REP50","eg"),   load(R50,"REP50","baseline")

def gated(E,B):
    return [i for i in sorted(set(E)&set(B))
            if E[i]["usd"]>0 and B[i]["usd"]>0 and E[i]["patch"]>0 and B[i]["patch"]>0]

print("=== PE1SAMP per-instance state ===")
print(f"{'instance':<34} {'eg tok':>10} {'base tok':>10} {'delta':>8} {'eg t':>5} {'b t':>5}  eg-sub / b-sub")
allids = sorted(set(pe_e)|set(pe_b))
for i in allids:
    e, b = pe_e.get(i), pe_b.get(i)
    et = f"{e['tok']:,}" if e else "-"
    bt = f"{b['tok']:,}" if b else "-"
    d  = f"{100*(1-e['tok']/b['tok']):+.1f}%" if (e and b and b['tok']) else "-"
    print(f"{i:<34} {et:>10} {bt:>10} {d:>8} {e['turns'] if e else '-':>5} {b['turns'] if b else '-':>5}"
          f"  {(e['sub'] if e else '-')} / {(b['sub'] if b else '-')}"
          + ("  [eg no-patch]" if e and not e['patch'] else "")
          + ("  [base no-patch]" if b and not b['patch'] else ""))

g = gated(pe_e, pe_b)
print(f"\ngated PE1SAMP pairs: {len(g)} of {len(allids)} instances present")
if g:
    se, sb = sum(pe_e[i]['tok'] for i in g), sum(pe_b[i]['tok'] for i in g)
    gm = math.exp(sum(math.log(pe_b[i]['tok']/pe_e[i]['tok']) for i in g)/len(g))
    print(f"  PE1SAMP pooled token saving : {100*(1-se/sb):+.2f}%   (eg {se:,} vs base {sb:,})")
    print(f"  PE1SAMP geomean             : {100*(1-1/gm):+.2f}%")
    print(f"  turns  eg {sum(pe_e[i]['turns'] for i in g)}  base {sum(pe_b[i]['turns'] for i in g)}")

    # SAME instances under REP50
    common = [i for i in g if i in r_e and i in r_b and r_e[i]['usd']>0 and r_b[i]['usd']>0
              and r_e[i]['patch']>0 and r_b[i]['patch']>0]
    print(f"\n=== HEAD-TO-HEAD on the {len(common)} instances gated in BOTH cells ===")
    print(f"{'instance':<34} {'REP50':>9} {'PE1SAMP':>9} {'move':>9}")
    for i in common:
        r = 100*(1-r_e[i]['tok']/r_b[i]['tok']); p = 100*(1-pe_e[i]['tok']/pe_b[i]['tok'])
        print(f"{i:<34} {r:>8.1f}% {p:>8.1f}% {p-r:>+8.1f}pt")
    if common:
        rse, rsb = sum(r_e[i]['tok'] for i in common), sum(r_b[i]['tok'] for i in common)
        pse, psb = sum(pe_e[i]['tok'] for i in common), sum(pe_b[i]['tok'] for i in common)
        print(f"\n  REP50   pooled on these : {100*(1-rse/rsb):+.2f}%")
        print(f"  PE1SAMP pooled on these : {100*(1-pse/psb):+.2f}%")
        print(f"  MOVE                    : {100*(1-pse/psb)-100*(1-rse/rsb):+.2f}pt")
        print(f"  decomposition: eg arm {100*(pse/rse-1):+.1f}% tokens, baseline arm {100*(psb/rsb-1):+.1f}%")

# full rep50 for reference
gr = gated(r_e, r_b)
if gr:

import json, os, glob, math

    """sum of all four token classes, preferring modelUsage (reconciles to usd at 4.1e-16)."""
    mu = cc.get("modelUsage") or {}
    if mu:
        t = 0
        for m in mu.values():
            for k in ("inputTokens","outputTokens","cacheReadInputTokens","cacheCreationInputTokens"):
                t += m.get(k, 0) or 0
        if t: return t
    u = cc.get("usage") or {}
    return sum(u.get(k,0) or 0 for k in
               ("input_tokens","output_tokens","cache_read_input_tokens","cache_creation_input_tokens"))

def load(root, tag, arm):
    base = f"{root}/results/{tag}_r1_{arm}/{arm}"
    out = {}
    if not os.path.isdir(base): return out
    for iid in sorted(os.listdir(base)):
        if iid.startswith('.'): continue
        d = f"{base}/{iid}"; cc = f"{d}/cc_out.json"; pf = f"{d}/patch.diff"

            tok=toks(j), usd=j.get("total_cost_usd") or 0, turns=j.get("num_turns") or 0,

| turns | eg 589 vs base 551 |

**Same 9 instances under REP50: +9.21%. So the cell moved −13.1pt.**

```

framework-53914     -123.9%    +31.6%   +155.5pt   ← repaired
```

Every rep50 loser rose. Every rep50 winner fell. **corr(rep50 delta, move) = −0.913** — where −1.0 is pure regression to the mean and 0.0 is a real treatment effect. The sample was *selected* on being extreme in rep50, so this is exactly what the noise floor predicts (93% of losers flip sign between cells; 45pt median same-instance spread). None of the five "repairs" is evidence the fix worked, and none of the four "regressions" is evidence it hurt.

The arm decomposition points one way: **baseline arm −9.3% tokens, eg arm +3.7%.** The baseline getting systematically cheaper is the shared anti-harness instruction working — which the pre-registration predicted would shrink the measured effect ("removes improvisation from the baseline too… a smaller real number over a larger retractable one"). My fault, relaunching through the proper driver.
3. **redis-12472** has directories in both arms but no scoreable `cc_out.json` yet; redis-11510 baseline is still running.

The ten loser analysts are still working. Given the −0.913 correlation, their job just got more important and narrower: per-instance "why did this one lose" is now known to be mostly noise, so the only findings worth acting on are ones that name a **mechanism reproducible across instances** — which is precisely what I told them to separate out.

content.text:
## No. Undo one component, not the plan.

The plan's diagnosis is intact. What just failed is the intervention, and it failed against its own pre-registered criterion.

### The falsification fired

The prereg said: *"Refuted as a token lever if eg turns/session do not fall below baseline."* It predicted eg turns would **fall by 4–6/session**.

| | eg | baseline | gap |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| REP50 full (49) | 55.3 | 54.5 | **+0.8** |
| REP50, the same 9 | 65.3 | 62.0 | **+3.3** |
| PE1SAMP (9) | 65.4 | 61.2 | **+4.2** |

Predicted −4 to −6. Measured **+4.2**, and on identical instances the treatment **widened** the gap from +3.3 to +4.2. This one is *not* regression to the mean — the gap is measured within-cell against a concurrent baseline, and it points the same way at n=49 and at n=9.

That is the whole theory inverted. The plan assumed injecting post-edit information **displaces** post-edit turns. It **generates** them. The displacement ratio was already −0.21 before the rider existed; the rider made it worse. Unrequested information creates work — the agent gets told about callers and risks, and then goes and checks them.

### What to undo — three things

1. **The PostToolUse rider** (`EG_POSTEDIT_HOOK=1`). It is the only component with a measured cost (+3.7% eg tokens, +0.9 turns/session of widened gap) and no measured benefit. This is one env flag, not a code revert — `postedit` stays available as an on-demand verb, which is a different contract: the agent pays a turn and gets what it asked for.
2. **Reading 9–12 instance cells.** That's the drill's first prohibition and I broke it. Back to Gate 1 offline replay, which costs nothing.
3. Nothing else.

### What must NOT be undone

**The fairness correction.** It cost ~9 of the 13.1pt — baseline arm −9.3% tokens because both arms now get the anti-harness instruction. Removing it would recover most of the "loss" on paper, and that manoeuvre is precisely what produced and then killed 54.9%, 57.7%, and 31.6%. Also keeping: the netjail answer-leak fix, the clamp-scan fix, `df -Pk`, `stats.go` verb accounting, `VerifyCommandForFile`, the arity check.

### The number that decides this

The plan's own ceiling arithmetic: fair addressable pool **4.5 turns/session** → **+14.78%** maximum. The intervention currently runs **+4.2 turns/session in the wrong direction**. So before it can save anything it has to climb back 4.2 out of a 4.5-turn budget. There is no version of "tune the payload" that closes that. The rider has to go.

### One thing worth keeping from the result

Variance collapsed: PE1SAMP turn deltas span −20..+22 against rep50's −55..+42. The treatment does stabilise sessions. That's genuinely useful — just not for a token-savings goal, where the mean is what's being scored.

I'm not touching the config while redis-11510's baseline is still running. When the cell drains I'll flip the rider off, re-score, and run the offline replay to test the one open question the analysts might answer: **does `postedit` output, when asked for rather than pushed, reduce follow-up work or generate it?** If it generates it on-demand too, the verb is dead as a token lever and the honest number for this whole line is the +14.78% ceiling minus a cost we can't recover — and I'll say so plainly rather than keep spending.

set -euo pipefail
S=$HOME/pe1/graphmark/agentic-swebench
T=$(mktemp -d)

# run_pe1.sh is the RECORD of what produced the PE1SAMP numbers. Never mutate it.
# PE2 changes exactly ONE variable: the rider. Everything else stays byte-identical so the
# next cell is a clean A/B against PE1SAMP rather than a confounded new config.
sed -e 's|^export EG_POSTEDIT_HOOK=1 .*$|export EG_POSTEDIT_HOOK=0        # RIDER OFF. Falsified 2026-08-09: prereg predicted eg turns\n                                 # would FALL 4-6/session; measured +4.2, and the treatment WIDENED\n                                 # the gap on identical instances (+3.3 -> +4.2). Unrequested post-edit\n                                 # information generates follow-up work instead of displacing it.\n                                 # postedit survives as an ON-DEMAND verb: the agent pays a turn and\n                                 # gets what it asked for. That is a different, untested contract.|' \

---
name: postedit-rider-falsified
description: The zero-turn PostToolUse rider ADDS turns instead of displacing them — falsified by its own prereg criterion 2026-08-09
metadata:
  type: project
---

PE1SAMP (9 gated pairs, Opus max) vs the same 9 instances in REP50_r1.

PREREG-PE1-v2 predicted **eg turns/session fall 4–6 below baseline** and listed
*"refuted if eg turns/session do not fall below baseline"* as a falsification criterion.

| | eg | baseline | gap |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| REP50 full (49) | 55.3 | 54.5 | +0.8 |
| REP50, the same 9 | 65.3 | 62.0 | +3.3 |
| PE1SAMP (9) | 65.4 | 61.2 | **+4.2** |

**The rider widened the gap on identical instances (+3.3 → +4.2).** Unrequested post-edit
information *generates* follow-up work rather than displacing it — the agent gets told about
callers and risks, then goes and checks them. Consistent with the pre-existing displacement ratio
of −0.21 (the tool adds shell calls in the phase it operates in).

This is NOT regression to the mean: the gap is measured within-cell against a concurrent baseline
and points the same way at n=49 and n=9.

**The pooled −3.90% headline IS mostly regression to the mean.** Sample was selected on rep50
extremes; corr(rep50 delta, move) = **−0.913** (−1.0 = pure RTM). All 5 rep50 losers rose, all 4
rep50 winners fell. Do not read the per-instance "repairs".

The real non-noise signal is the arm decomposition: **baseline −9.3% tokens, eg +3.7%**. The
baseline half is the *fairness correction working as designed* (shared anti-harness block), not a
loss of tool value. Never undo it — that is the manoeuvre that produced and killed 54.9/57.7/31.6%.

**Action taken:** `run_pe2.sh` = `run_pe1.sh` with `EG_POSTEDIT_HOOK=0`, one variable changed so
PE2 is a clean A/B against PE1SAMP. `O35_STRIP_ADVICE=1` and `CC_NO_SAFE_MODE=1` deliberately
retained. `run_pe1.sh` left untouched (md5 d5b59eaa1e40d290d4905b73cdcfaced) as the record.

**How to apply:** the ceiling arithmetic in [[postedit-ceiling-15pct]] assumed displacement. With
the rider costing +4.2 turns/session against a 4.5-turn total addressable pool, push-mode delivery
is dead as a token lever. `postedit` as an on-demand verb is a different, still-untested contract.
Related: [[graph-absent-where-cost-is]], [[losers-are-not-stable]], [[eg-per-call-economics]].

content.text:
**Found the crash cause, and it's a real tool defect — not a crash at all.**

Both "crashed" sessions were killed mid-`cargo test` / `make test`:

```
ERR: The tool use was rejected ... [Request interrupted by user for tool use]
TOOL:Bash {"command": "cargo test 2>&1 | grep -vE ... | tail -45"}
```

`permission_denials: 0`, so that's the harness wall-clock timeout, not a refusal. And the redis session's injected payload says why:

```
VERIFY: cd src && make test
  targets whole test suite (no covering test identified)
```

**The VERIFY ladder's residual floor emits a whole-suite command when it can't identify a covering test.** On a large compiled repo that's a full rebuild plus every test — the agent obeys it, the session runs out of wall clock, and dies. It's eg-only because only eg gets a VERIFY line. That's arm-asymmetric session death caused by the tool, which is worse than a token loss.

Quantifying how often the floor fires:

# AGENTS.md — operating guide for coding agents

Hand this to any coding agent working in a repo where the `entire graph` plugin
is installed. It moves initial code-location work from broad grep/read
exploration to targeted graph queries; token impact depends on the task and
model, and no end-to-end savings claim is current.

## What this gives you

A precomputed, **deterministic** code graph is available through the `entire graph` command — functions, classes, methods, types, routes, and the calls/inheritance/field/service relations between them, parsed with tree-sitter, 100% locally (no network, no model, no keys). Use it to **LOCATE** and **UNDERSTAND** code *before* broad grep / find / cat / whole-file exploration. Every command is no-egress and safe to run inside a sandboxed session. The same commit yields the same graph, but static relations can be heuristic or incomplete; inspect focused source and verify the resulting change.

Default flags to remember: pass `--repo .` when you're not inside an Entire session; the graph reads your **working tree by default** (your uncommitted edits are visible), and `--head` switches to committed-tree semantics with a cached, reusable index.

---

## The parts of the graph

Reach for the smallest tool that answers your question.

### 🔍 search — *find the code for a task* (your first move)
Ranked source regions for a plain-language description, with the source and `file:line` inline. Hybrid ranking over bodies, identifiers (camelCase/snake_case aware), signatures, paths, and graph neighbors. Output is budgeted (16 KiB by default) to drop straight into context.

```sh
entire graph search --repo . --query "<the task or bug in one plain sentence>" --format text --top-k 8
```

- **Pass `--format text`.** The parser default is `json`, which measures **1.89x** the bytes of the
  text payload for the same result (8,071 B vs 4,274 B on a real query) — every one of those bytes is
  re-read on every later turn. The default is left as `json` for backwards compatibility with scripts
  that pipe to `jq`; agents should always be explicit.
- `--format agent` for compact ranked output with latency telemetry; `json`/`ndjson` for the full schema (completeness, partial failures, diagnostics).
- `--top-k N` result count; `--max-context-bytes N` byte budget (`0` = unbounded).
- Working tree by default; add `--head` for committed-tree + cache reuse.
- `--profile syntax-only|fast|full` (default `fast`); `--index-all-files` or `--max-indexed-files N` to widen/bound cold-search parsing.

**When:** the start of essentially every task. One good query lands you on the fix area.

### 🕸️ neighbors — *who calls this / what does it call* (targeted relations)
Direct incoming/outgoing relations for **one** symbol, with definition locations, plus bounded two-hop paths at `--depth 2`. For the full blast radius of a change, prefer `impact`; use `neighbors` when you want one specific relation/direction. Never `edges` for this (full stream).

```sh
entire graph neighbors --repo . --symbol NAME --relation CALLS --direction in   # who calls NAME
entire graph neighbors --repo . --symbol NAME --relation CALLS --direction out  # what NAME calls
```

- `--file path` — **required** when the symbol name is ambiguous (multiple defs); the graph returns definitions only until you disambiguate.
- `--relation CALLS` (default is the call family) — pick another relation to follow it instead.
- `--direction both|in|out`, `--depth 1|2`, `--limit N`.
- `--internal-only` drops unresolved external endpoints; `--exclude-tests` drops test-only neighbors.
- `--format agent|text|json`; `--head` for cached committed-tree; `--profile fast` for shallow call resolution (default `full` favors correctness).

**When:** "what breaks if I change X", "who uses this", tracing a call chain — after search has given you a concrete symbol name.

### 💥 impact — *one-shot blast radius for a change*
Everything the graph knows about changing **one** symbol, in a single bounded explanation: direct + transitive callers (depth ≤ 2), callees, type consumers (`USES_TYPE`/`PARAM_TYPE`/`RETURNS_TYPE`), data flows, files that historically change together with the symbol's file, and same-container siblings. Text output is sectioned, `file:line` per entry, capped per section and ~4 KB total.

```sh
entire graph impact --repo . --symbol NAME [--file path] [--depth 1|2] [--format text|json]
```

- Ambiguous names return the definition list — rerun with `--file` to pick one.
- `--limit N` per-section entry cap; `--max-context-bytes N` total text budget; `--exclude-tests`; `--head` / `--profile` as in `neighbors`.

**When:** before changing behavior of a specific function/type — "you're changing ordering: here is every place results are ordered, limited, or consumed downstream" — one command instead of chaining neighbors + edges + git log.

### 📇 symbols — *definitions*
Full stream of symbol records (stable `compound-v1` ID, kind, qualified name, source range, signature, language, container). This is a **bulk NDJSON stream of the whole repo**, filtered to the symbol record type — there is **no positional name argument** and no server-side name filter; grep the stream client-side, or prefer `search`/`neighbors` for a targeted single-symbol lookup.

```sh
entire graph symbols --repo . --format ndjson [--worktree]
```

**When:** you need the complete definition inventory (e.g. ingesting into a store), not a single lookup.

### 🔗 edges — *relations*
Relation records across all 30 types (`CALLS`, `IMPORTS`, `EXTENDS`, `HANDLES_ROUTE`, …), each tagged with resolution and confidence, plus the call-site `evidence` for resolved calls. Unfiltered it is the **whole-repo stream**, but it also takes `--to`, `--from` and `--relation`, and that is the ONLY route to the 13 relation types no other verb surfaces (`READS_FIELD`, `WRITES_FIELD`, `ACCESSES`, `HANDLES_ROUTE`, `HANDLES_GRPC`/`GRAPHQL`/`TRPC`, `HTTP_CALLS`, `EMITS`, `LISTENS_ON`, `HANDLES_TOOL`, `RESOURCE_DEPENDS_ON`, `DEFINES`):

```sh
entire graph edges --repo . --to NAME --relation CALLS --format ndjson   # who calls NAME
entire graph edges --repo . --from NAME --relation IMPORTS --format ndjson
```

For a single symbol's callers/callees `neighbors` is still the better answer — it resolves definitions and prints locations. Reach for `edges --to/--relation` when you want a relation type `neighbors` does not expose, or the raw evidence records.

```sh
entire graph edges --repo . --format ndjson [--worktree]
```

**When:** you want every relation (bulk export / ingestion). For a targeted question, use `neighbors`.

### 🗺️ snapshot — *the whole graph*
One header record, then file, external-endpoint, symbol, and relation records, streamed so memory stays bounded. Superset of `symbols` + `edges` + files.

```sh
entire graph snapshot --repo . --format ndjson [--worktree]
```

**When:** ingesting the full graph into agent memory or a store such as Entire Brain.

### 🧬 diff / analyze / commit / checkpoint — *what changed + risk*
Entity-level change list (added / removed / renamed / signature-changed / body-changed) with a heuristic **dependent count**, so a signature change with many dependents stands out.

```sh
entire graph commit HEAD --json                     # a commit vs its first parent
entire graph diff --base main --head HEAD --json    # between two refs (analyze is an alias)
entire graph checkpoint <id> --json                 # the commit behind an Entire-Checkpoint trailer
```

**When:** judging whether a change is safe to keep / revert / continue, or reviewing a branch/PR. High dependent counts on a signature change = run tests first.

### 🏗️ index — *build / warm the cache*
Prebuilds the durable, query-independent committed-tree index and verifies it was written, before latency-sensitive work.

```sh
entire graph index --repo . --head --profile full --cache-dir /path/to/cache --format json
```

**When:** once, up front, on a large repo before a batch of `--head` searches/neighbors queries. Re-running it is also how you "refresh" a committed-tree cache — same tree hits, changed tree rebuilds.

### 🧭 capabilities / doctor / version — *feature-detect*
```sh
entire graph capabilities --json    # semantic vs inventory-only languages, relation types, features
entire graph doctor --json          # environment, repo resolution, no_egress=true
entire graph version [--json]       # provider name + plugin version
```

**When:** before assuming a language is semantically parsed, or to confirm the no-egress environment.

### 📊 stats — *did the graph actually save anything?* (for humans, not for you)
```sh
entire graph stats --repo . [--since 30d|7d|all] [--format text|json] [--sessions-dir path|--transcript path]
```

Local, read-only report over the coding-agent session transcripts already on disk
(`~/.claude/projects/<path-slug>/*.jsonl`; `--sessions-dir` overrides the lookup). Reports graph
calls per verb vs. exploration calls (`Read` whole-file / `Read` line-range / `Grep` / `Glob` /
shell `grep|find|cat|head|tail|sed|awk`), the bytes each path pulled into context, billed session
tokens read from transcript `usage`, a graph-first rate (share of sessions whose first locate-ish
tool call was a graph call), and an **estimated** token saving. The savings model is an explicit
assumption printed next to the number: each `search`/`neighbors`/`impact` call is credited with the
one whole-file read it replaced — on-disk size of the top-hit file it pointed at (repo median
tracked-file size when unresolvable) minus the bytes that call returned, floored at 0, at 4 bytes =
1 token. It is not a measured counterfactual. No network, no writes. `--transcript <path>` narrows
the whole report to one session (that transcript plus its `<session>/subagents/*.jsonl`), which is
what `scripts/entire-graph-statusline.sh` renders as a live Claude Code status line badge.

**When:** a human asks what the graph is buying them. Agents should not run it as part of a coding task.

---

## Resolution-first agent prompt (copy-paste this)

The former “measured-best” early-stop prompt and its 54.9%/57.7% token claims
are withdrawn. It optimized token use without preserving resolution parity and
could reward a cheap wrong patch. Use this correctness-first guidance instead;
substitute your search invocation for `<search-cmd>`:

```text
A precomputed code-search tool is available: <search-cmd> . Use it to LOCATE the fix BEFORE any
grep/find. Your FIRST action must be ONE search:
  <search-cmd> "<the bug in one sentence>"   <-- ranked relevant code (file:line + source)
Then open the top hit's file with your native Read tool (pass a line range around the reported
line), inspect enough surrounding behavior to justify the change, and make the smallest complete
edit. Treat graph output as evidence, not an oracle. Check callers/impact when the change can affect
other sites. If the result prints a `VERIFY:` line, run that exact command after editing before
claiming the task is done; it may be a per-file command or a whole-suite fallback when no narrow
command can be derived. Never report that tests pass without executing the command. If verification
cannot be run, state why and perform a bounded source-level check. Optimize turns only after
correctness.
```

For bug-fix/locate tasks, run search at `--profile full` (call-graph expansion active) with default
text output (tiered: full snippet for the top hits, terse locators after). Prefer
targeted follow-up queries over whole-graph dumps, but use the graph and source
checks needed to make and verify a complete fix.

## Operating doctrine

1. **Search first for location tasks.** Start with one `entire graph search --query "<task>"` before broad grep/find exploration.
2. **Treat results as evidence, not truth.** Read focused source around the result and widen the check when behavior, aliases, generated code, or dynamic dispatch could matter.
3. **Use graph follow-ups when they answer a real question.** `impact`, `callers`, and `neighbors` are appropriate for blast radius and related-site checks; avoid exploratory whole-graph dumps.
4. **Make the smallest complete change.** Check sibling sites and contracts when the task implies them.
5. **Verify before stopping.** Run the `VERIFY:` command when search prints one; it may be a whole-suite fallback when no narrow command exists. Never report that tests pass without having run them. If execution is unavailable, perform a bounded source-level verification and disclose the limitation.
6. **Optimize context after correctness.** Prefer precise queries and line ranges, but never trade resolution for fewer turns.
7. **Feature-detect before you trust.** If a language might be inventory-only, check `capabilities --json` first — inventory-only files have file records but no semantic relations.

Quick mental model:

```text
locate  →  entire graph search --query "..."          (ranked code + file:line)
declare →  entire graph def NAME [NAME...]             (declaration + members, several names in one call)
impact  →  entire graph impact --symbol X              (one-shot blast radius: callers, types, data flow, co-change)
callers →  entire graph neighbors --symbol X ...       (targeted callers/callees of X)
edges   →  entire graph edges --to X --relation R       (the only route to 13 relation types; raw evidence)
changed →  entire graph changed --repo .                (what you just edited, and what calls it)
change  →  entire graph diff --base A --head B          (entity-level, with dependents)
ingest  →  entire graph snapshot --format ndjson        (whole graph)
report  →  entire graph stats --repo .                  (human-facing: graph vs grep/read usage + estimated token savings)
```

---

## Working on entire-graph itself

If your task is modifying this repository (not just using it), the build/test surface is in `mise.toml`:

```sh
mise run build   # go build -o entire-graph ./cmd/entire-graph  (needs CGO for tree-sitter)
mise run test    # go test ./...
mise run check   # fmt + vet + race tests + build
```

Contract rules that must not break: schema `1.x` is frozen and additive-only (`docs/adr/0001-ga-schema-contract.md`); the provider is **no-egress** (never add remote fetches, hosted API calls, telemetry, or runtime grammar downloads); `compound-v1` symbol IDs must stay stable across ordinary edits; unsupported/unparseable files must surface as machine-readable partial failures, never silent drops. All logic lives under `internal/` (`sem` = parsing/graph/search, `cli` = hand-rolled dispatch, `gitutil` = git subprocess); `cmd/entire-graph/main.go` is a thin entry point. The plugin manifest (`entire-plugin.yml`) registers the subcommand `graph`, so users type `entire graph ...`. This project was **previously named `entire-sem`** — do not reintroduce the old name. **Entire Brain** (`entire-brain`) is the separate downstream consumer of this provider's NDJSON — not an old name for this project.

This repo has the entire-graph code graph installed. Before exploring code with
grep/find/whole-file reads, read .entire/graph-agent.md — the search-first, verify-once
doctrine for coding agents: search instead of grepping, then check the sibling sites and
compile (or run the nearest existing test) once before you finish.

3. **Use graph follow-ups when they answer a real question.** `impact`, `callers`, and `neighbors` are appropriate for blast radius and related-site checks; avoid exploratory whole-graph dumps.
4. **Make the smallest complete change.** Check sibling sites and contracts when the task implies them.
5. **Verify before stopping.** Run the `VERIFY:` command when search prints one; it may be a whole-suite fallback when no narrow command exists. Never report that tests pass without having run them. If execution is unavailable, perform a bounded source-level verification and disclose the limitation.
6. **Optimize context after correctness.** Prefer precise queries and line ranges, but never trade resolution for fewer turns.
7. **Feature-detect before you trust.** If a language might be inventory-only, check `capabilities --json` first — inventory-only files have file records but no semantic relations.

Quick mental model:

```text
locate  →  entire graph search --query "..."          (ranked code + file:line)
declare →  entire graph def NAME [NAME...]             (declaration + members, several names in one call)
impact  →  entire graph impact --symbol X              (one-shot blast radius: callers, types, data flow, co-change)
callers →  entire graph neighbors --symbol X ...       (targeted callers/callees of X)
edges   →  entire graph edges --to X --relation R       (the only route to 13 relation types; raw evidence)
changed →  entire graph changed --repo .                (what you just edited, and what calls it)
change  →  entire graph diff --base A --head B          (entity-level, with dependents)
ingest  →  entire graph snapshot --format ndjson        (whole graph)
report  →  entire graph stats --repo .                  (human-facing: graph vs grep/read usage + estimated token savings)
```

---

## Working on entire-graph itself

If your task is modifying this repository (not just using it), the build/test surface is in `mise.toml`:

```sh
mise run build   # go build -o entire-graph ./cmd/entire-graph  (needs CGO for tree-sitter)
mise run test    # go test ./...
mise run check   # fmt + vet + race tests + build
```

Contract rules that must not break: schema `1.x` is frozen and additive-only (`docs/adr/0001-ga-schema-contract.md`); the provider is **no-egress** (never add remote fetches, hosted API calls, telemetry, or runtime grammar downloads); `compound-v1` symbol IDs must stay stable across ordinary edits; unsupported/unparseable files must surface as machine-readable partial failures, never silent drops. All logic lives under `internal/` (`sem` = parsing/graph/search, `cli` = hand-rolled dispatch, `gitutil` = git subprocess); `cmd/entire-graph/main.go` is a thin entry point. The plugin manifest (`entire-plugin.yml`) registers the subcommand `graph`, so users type `entire graph ...`. This project was **previously named `entire-sem`** — do not reintroduce the old name. **Entire Brain** (`entire-brain`) is the separate downstream consumer of this provider's NDJSON — not an old name for this project.
