# entire-graph — instructions for coding agents (follow directly)

You have a deterministic local code graph: `entire graph` (functions, classes, methods,
types, routes + call/inheritance relations; no network). These instructions are FOR YOU, the
agent reading this file.

**No token-savings claim is current.** The "roughly half" figure this file used to carry came
from a measurement that gave the tool arm frugality instructions the no-tool arm did not get;
removing them moved the same cell from −14.9% to +9.1%, and `AGENTS.md` withdraws the 54.9%
/ 57.7% numbers for the same reason. The best fair paired measurement to date is a single-digit
to mid-teens token saving that varies by model and task, and is *negative* on short sessions.
Follow the workflow below because it finds code faster and verifies the change — not because a
number promises a saving.

## The workflow (mandatory for locate/fix/change tasks)

Your FIRST action on any task that requires finding code must be ONE search:

    entire graph search --repo . --profile full --format text --query "<the task or bug in one sentence>"

The first five hits come back as the COMPLETE body of their enclosing function/method (marked
`complete-symbol`; `snippet_start_line`..`snippet_end_line` is the whole callable, verbatim).
When the hit you want is one of them, EDIT DIRECTLY FROM THE SEARCH OUTPUT — you already have
the entire function, and opening the file costs a whole extra turn for nothing. Only when the
hit you want carries a two-line locator window instead, open its file at the reported line
range. Either way: make the minimal edit that fixes the root cause. The top hit is the fix site
on most tasks — go straight there; do NOT re-search or grep to "confirm".

Then finish the job. Two bounded steps, not a loop:

**1. Complete the fix.** A fix is often not one edit in one place. Before you call it done, ask
the graph once for the sites that share the defect:

    entire graph impact --repo . --symbol X

One shot: callers, callees, type consumers, data flow, co-change files, and same-container
siblings. Apply the same change to the ones that carry the same bug; ignore the rest.

**2. Verify once.** Compile what you touched, or run the nearest existing test. This is NOT
optional overhead. An unverified edit is how a patch ships an unused variable, a wrong field or
method name, or the wrong arity — and a patch that does not build fails 100% of the task. One
verification turn costs one turn; a patch that does not compile costs everything.

The output is grouped, and the groups mean different things:

* the ranked list is **candidate fix sites** — start at the top.
* **RELATED SITES** (`section: "related"`) are the other places this change usually has to
  land: a near-duplicate body needs the SAME edit, a sibling implementation needs the same edit
  in its own terms, a caller needs adjusting to the changed contract. Before you finish, check
  them — a patch applied to one site of a family is the commonest way a correct fix still fails.
* **DOCS & FIXTURES** (`section: "docs-and-fixtures"`) matched your words but hold no program
  text. Do not spend a read there looking for the bug unless the task IS the document.

## Rules, in order of how much evidence stands behind them

Correctness first: `AGENTS.md` is the contract, and it says never trade resolution for fewer
turns. Nothing below overrides that.

**Measured, and the largest effect by far — bound your verification.**

1. VERIFY ONCE, THEN STOP CHASING. Run the narrowest command that would catch a syntax, type,
   name, or arity error; read the error; fix exactly what it names; re-run. A couple of
   iterations, not a loop. Do not "fix" failures that were already failing before you started.
   This is where sessions actually burn their budget: across 8 decomposed losing sessions,
   **97.7% of the excess cost landed after the first edit**, in repeated harness invocations —
   `./runtest` 11 times, `cargo test` 7, `javac` 19 — each dragging in `sleep`, `pkill`, port
   juggling and log re-reading. The sessions that won ran the suite **once or twice** and
   stopped. Localization was, by comparison, free.
2. AFTER EDITING, ASK THE GRAPH WHAT YOU TOUCHED rather than grepping for it:
       entire graph changed --repo .
   Paths you changed, the definitions in them, and what calls those — most-depended-on first.

**Sound practice, not a measured saving.**

3. Search before grep/find/cat for locate tasks; one good query usually lands the fix site.
4. Prefer a line range around the reported line over a whole-file read when the hit is a
   locator. A `complete-symbol` hit is already the whole function — you can edit from it.
5. For "who calls X" / "what breaks", one targeted query beats chaining:
       entire graph impact --repo . --symbol X

**Explicitly NOT claimed.** That a second search is wasteful, that re-reading is always wrong,
or that fewer turns is itself the goal. Retrieval quality and token cost are different axes —
in one 49-instance cell the sessions where the graph ranked the gold file first *lost* more
often than the ones where it missed. If the first answer is not enough, ask again.

## When NOT to use the graph

If the task already names the exact file and it is small, just read it — the graph earns its
keep by eliminating exploration, so when there is nothing to explore, skip it. Short sessions
are where the tool measures WORST: on instances whose no-tool run was already cheap, the graph
arm cost 27.8% more. Verification still applies: it is about the edit you made, not about how
you found it.

## Reference

    locate  ->  entire graph search --repo . --profile full --format text --query "..."
    impact  ->  entire graph impact --repo . --symbol X   (one shot: callers, callees, type consumers, data flow, co-change, siblings)
    callers ->  entire graph neighbors --repo . --symbol X --relation CALLS --direction in
    changed ->  entire graph changed --repo .   (what you edited, and what calls it)
    change  ->  entire graph diff --base A --head B --json
    detect  ->  entire graph capabilities --json   (inventory-only languages have no relations)
    verify  ->  this project's own narrowest build/test command, once, after editing
                (e.g. `go build ./internal/foo/...`, `pytest tests/test_foo.py -k name`, `cargo check -p crate`)
    stats   ->  entire graph stats --repo .        (human-facing token-savings report; not part of your workflow — do not run it unless asked)

#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail
S=$HOME/pe1/graphmark/agentic-swebench
F=$S/tools/run_3arm.sh
cp "$F" "$F.bak.preverifyremoval"
T=$(mktemp -d)

python3 - "$F" "$T/out.sh" <<'PY'
import sys,re
src=open(sys.argv[1]).read(); orig=src

# 1) LAUNCH GATE: VERIFY is no longer emitted by default, so requiring it would abort every cell.
#    Replace it with a STRONGER functional assertion. The probe makes an arity change with a
#    provably broken call site, so a live treatment must report the changed definition AND the
#    risk it created -- neither of which a false "unavailable in this build" banner can fake.
old_ok = """  if printf '%s' "$_pe_probe_out" | grep -q 'CHANGED vs ' \\
     && printf '%s' "$_pe_probe_out" | grep -q '^VERIFY:'; then"""
new_ok = """  if printf '%s' "$_pe_probe_out" | grep -q 'CHANGED vs ' \\
     && printf '%s' "$_pe_probe_out" | grep -q '^CHANGED DEFINITIONS' \\
     && printf '%s' "$_pe_probe_out" | grep -q '^SIGNATURE RISK'; then"""
assert old_ok in src, "gate condition not found verbatim"
src = src.replace(old_ok, new_ok)

src = src.replace(
  """      echo "  A functional probe on a deliberately dirty checkout did not return BOTH" >&2
      echo "  'CHANGED vs ' and a 'VERIFY:' line. Probe output follows verbatim:" >&2""",
  """      echo "  A functional probe on a deliberately dirty checkout did not return ALL of" >&2
      echo "  'CHANGED vs ', 'CHANGED DEFINITIONS' and 'SIGNATURE RISK'. VERIFY is NO LONGER" >&2
      echo "  part of this gate: emission is off at source (sem.VerifyEmissionEnabled) because a" >&2
      echo "  whole-suite command is generic methodology handed to one arm. Probe verbatim:" >&2""")

# 2) The probe pinned EG_VERIFY_MODE=full to test the capability. That capability is now
#    deliberately unreachable; asking for it would make the probe unrepresentative of the cell.
src = src.replace("    EG_VERIFY_MODE=full EG_VERIFY_PROBE=0 EG_LIT_DROP=0 \\",
                  "    EG_VERIFY_PROBE=0 EG_LIT_DROP=0 \\")

# 3) CAPABILITY LINE: stop advertising a verify command the tool no longer emits. Leaving it would
#    be an arm-asymmetric promise of verification methodology with nothing behind it.
src = src.replace("post-edit callers, signature risk and verify command",
                  "post-edit callers and signature risk")

# 4) Probe doc comment.
src = src.replace('a real changed definition, real callers, a provably broken call site, and a derivable\n# VERIFY command)',
                  'a real changed definition, real callers, and a provably broken call site)')
src = src.replace('''# netjail first, $out second -- and requires stdout to carry BOTH "CHANGED vs " and a line starting
# "VERIFY:". Anything less and the treatment is inert.''',
                  '''# netjail first, $out second -- and requires stdout to carry "CHANGED vs ", "CHANGED DEFINITIONS"
# and "SIGNATURE RISK". Anything less and the treatment is inert.''')

assert src != orig
open(sys.argv[2],"w").write(src)
PY

bash -n "$T/out.sh" || { echo "FATAL: syntax"; exit 1; }
# refuse to install if any live VERIFY requirement survives in the gate
if grep -q "grep -q '\^VERIFY:'" "$T/out.sh"; then echo "FATAL: VERIFY gate survived"; exit 1; fi
if grep -q "signature risk and verify command" "$T/out.sh"; then echo "FATAL: capability line survived"; exit 1; fi

# atomic install: never write in place, sessions read this file lazily
cp "$T/out.sh" "$F.new" && mv "$F.new" "$F"
rm -rf "$T"

set -euo pipefail
S=$HOME/pe1/graphmark/agentic-swebench

cp "$F" "$F.bak.preverifyremoval"
T=$(mktemp -d)

import sys,re
src=open(sys.argv[1]).read(); orig=src

# 1) LAUNCH GATE: VERIFY is no longer emitted by default, so requiring it would abort every cell.
#    Replace it with a STRONGER functional assertion. The probe makes an arity change with a
#    provably broken call site, so a live treatment must report the changed definition AND the
#    risk it created -- neither of which a false "unavailable in this build" banner can fake.
old_ok = """  if printf '%s' "$_pe_probe_out" | grep -q 'CHANGED vs ' \\
     && printf '%s' "$_pe_probe_out" | grep -q '^VERIFY:'; then"""
new_ok = """  if printf '%s' "$_pe_probe_out" | grep -q 'CHANGED vs ' \\
     && printf '%s' "$_pe_probe_out" | grep -q '^CHANGED DEFINITIONS' \\
     && printf '%s' "$_pe_probe_out" | grep -q '^SIGNATURE RISK'; then"""
assert old_ok in src, "gate condition not found verbatim"
src = src.replace(old_ok, new_ok)

src = src.replace(
  """      echo "  A functional probe on a deliberately dirty checkout did not return BOTH" >&2
      echo "  'CHANGED vs ' and a 'VERIFY:' line. Probe output follows verbatim:" >&2""",
  """      echo "  A functional probe on a deliberately dirty checkout did not return ALL of" >&2
      echo "  'CHANGED vs ', 'CHANGED DEFINITIONS' and 'SIGNATURE RISK'. VERIFY is NO LONGER" >&2
      echo "  part of this gate: emission is off at source (sem.VerifyEmissionEnabled) because a" >&2
      echo "  whole-suite command is generic methodology handed to one arm. Probe verbatim:" >&2""")

# 2) The probe pinned EG_VERIFY_MODE=full to test the capability. That capability is now
#    deliberately unreachable; asking for it would make the probe unrepresentative of the cell.
src = src.replace("    EG_VERIFY_MODE=full EG_VERIFY_PROBE=0 EG_LIT_DROP=0 \\",
                  "    EG_VERIFY_PROBE=0 EG_LIT_DROP=0 \\")

# 3) CAPABILITY LINE: stop advertising a verify command the tool no longer emits. Leaving it would
#    be an arm-asymmetric promise of verification methodology with nothing behind it.
src = src.replace("post-edit callers, signature risk and verify command",
                  "post-edit callers and signature risk")

# 4) Probe doc comment.
src = src.replace('a real changed definition, real callers, a provably broken call site, and a derivable\n# VERIFY command)',
                  'a real changed definition, real callers, and a provably broken call site)')
src = src.replace('''# netjail first, $out second -- and requires stdout to carry BOTH "CHANGED vs " and a line starting
# "VERIFY:". Anything less and the treatment is inert.''',
                  '''# netjail first, $out second -- and requires stdout to carry "CHANGED vs ", "CHANGED DEFINITIONS"
# and "SIGNATURE RISK". Anything less and the treatment is inert.''')

assert src != orig
open(sys.argv[2],"w").write(src)
PY

bash -n "$T/out.sh" || { echo "FATAL: syntax"; exit 1; }
# refuse to install if any live VERIFY requirement survives in the gate
if grep -q "grep -q '\^VERIFY:'" "$T/out.sh"; then echo "FATAL: VERIFY gate survived"; exit 1; fi
if grep -q "signature risk and verify command" "$T/out.sh"; then echo "FATAL: capability line survived"; exit 1; fi

# atomic install: never write in place, sessions read this file lazily
cp "$T/out.sh" "$F.new" && mv "$F.new" "$F"
rm -rf "$T"

diff "$F.bak.preverifyremoval" "$F" || true

gate = '''

// VerifyEmissionEnabled reports whether the VERIFY block may be emitted at all. DEFAULT OFF.
//
// The block hands the agent a test command. On this project's own fairness test -- "would this
// sentence help an agent with no tool?" -- the answer is yes, and the measurement says so plainly:
// of the VERIFY lines emitted across the PE1 cell, 80% were the whole-suite residual floor
// (`cargo test`, `make test`, `npm test`, `vendor/bin/phpunit`). A whole-suite command carries no
// graph-derived content whatsoever; it is generic "run the tests" advice wearing a tool's output
// format, and handing it to one arm is the defect that withdrew the 54.9/57.7/31.6% headlines.
//
// Harm beyond the fairness objection, measured: postedit raised VERIFY emission 28x (REP50 0.2
// lines/session -> PE1 5.6, because the rider re-derived one after every edit), and two of eleven
// PE1 eg sessions were killed on wall clock executing a whole-suite command this block emitted,
// against zero baseline deaths. An arm-asymmetric session kill is worse than a token loss, because
// the pair leaves the gate entirely.
//

// test located through the graph -- are legitimate tool output; only the suite floor is not. Set
// EG_EMIT_VERIFY=1 to restore emission, and suppress searchVerifySuiteCommand before you do.
func VerifyEmissionEnabled() bool {
	return os.Getenv("EG_EMIT_VERIFY") == "1"
}
'''

s = s[:i] + gate + s[i:]
assert s != o; open(p,"w").write(s); print("patched", p)

#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail
S=$HOME/pe1/graphmark/agentic-swebench
# Install alongside, never over: the pinned binary is the record of what PE1SAMP ran.
cp "$HOME/pe-build/entire-graph-noverify" "$HOME/pe-bin/.entire-graph-noverify.new"
chmod +x "$HOME/pe-bin/.entire-graph-noverify.new"
mv "$HOME/pe-bin/.entire-graph-noverify.new" "$HOME/pe-bin/entire-graph-noverify"

# Point PE2 at it. One line, atomic.
T=$(mktemp -d)
sed 's|^export ENTIRE_GRAPH=.*$|export ENTIRE_GRAPH="${ENTIRE_GRAPH:-$HOME/pe-bin/entire-graph-noverify}"|' \
  "$S/tools/run_pe2.sh" > "$T/x"
grep -q 'entire-graph-noverify' "$T/x" || { echo "FATAL: binary not repointed"; exit 1; }
bash -n "$T/x" || exit 1
chmod +x "$T/x"; mv "$T/x" "$S/tools/.run_pe2.sh.new"; mv "$S/tools/.run_pe2.sh.new" "$S/tools/run_pe2.sh"
rmdir "$T" 2>/dev/null || true

echo "=== binaries ==="
sha256sum "$HOME/pe-bin/entire-graph-postedit" "$HOME/pe-bin/entire-graph-noverify"
ls -la "$HOME/pe-bin/"
echo
echo "=== PE2 treatment block ==="
sed -n '/--- the treatment/,/--- fairness/p' "$S/tools/run_pe2.sh"
echo "=== live procs ==="
pgrep -af "run_3arm|run_paired|claude -p" | head -5

## Done, and the forensics came back with something that inverts the plan

**Undone as asked.** Rider off; VERIFY removed at source from *both* emitters (`postedit` and `search`), not stripped downstream. Rebuilt on the VM in a golang container, full suite green (`TEST-EXIT=0`), three-way probe verified:

| binary / env | postedit VERIFY | search VERIFY | CHANGED + DEFS + RISK |
|---|---|---|---|
| old pinned (what PE1SAMP ran) | `go test .` | 1 | all present |
| **new, default** | **absent** | **0** | **all present** |
| new + `EG_EMIT_VERIFY=1` | emitted | 1 | all present |

Old binary preserved, `run_pe1.sh` untouched as the record, harness launch gate re-anchored on `CHANGED DEFINITIONS` + `SIGNATURE RISK` (a stronger functional check than VERIFY was), and the capability line no longer advertises a verify command.

---

## The number that matters

Ten deep analysts + a winner-risk pass on all 49 REP50 pairs. The top-10 losers hold **14.47 points**. After subtracting what each fix costs the winners, the surviving winner-safe recovery is:

**+0.6 to +1.3 points. Projected pooled: +1.35% → ~+2.2%.**

Not 15. The gap is real and here's where it went:

- **3.3 pt has no tool fingerprint at all.** ansible-395e5e (2.58 pt) made one graph call with clean output, produced a *smaller* patch than baseline with *fewer* edits and *fewer* test runs. lombok-3326 (0.70 pt) used **15 fewer turns** than baseline while spending 1.02M more tokens — the brief's "every loser is a turn blowout" premise is false for it.
- **Losers flip.** tokio-4867 was −114.4% in REP50 and **+17.2%** in PE1SAMP — same instance, sign reversed. Its REP50 baseline was the fastest of six runs on that problem (38 turns against 51/55/61/61/69), so the loss was measured against an outlier.

## The finding that changes the strategy

**eg's edge *is* verification restraint. It already verifies less than baseline.**

Run-wide build + whole-suite calls: **eg 419 vs baseline 470**. On the 24 winners: eg 157+9 vs base 284+12 — **130 fewer calls**. Post-edit build tokens: **eg 9.67M vs base 22.44M**. Pre-edit, eg makes *nine fewer* tool calls than baseline.

So the obvious fix — a symmetric "scope-lock the repro, use the narrowest test target, no whole-suite runs" prompt, worth a claimed 3.0–3.5 pt on the losers — was measured **sign-reversing**: at f=20% it's +0.98 pt worse, at f=30% **eg loses outright**, at f=50% +2.79 pt worse. It takes 284→199 from the winners' *baselines* and only 157→110 from eg. It hands the baseline eg's only advantage.

That kills the whole post-edit-suppression thesis, including the rider I just removed and the +14.78% ceiling that assumed displacement. **Every "make eg do less post-edit work" lever attacks the arm that is already frugal.** Dropping that fix is the single most valuable result of this review.

## Where 15% actually lives

Winners win by **collapsing the pre-edit prefix**. The clearest case is the biggest winner in the cell:

> **lombok-3674, −8,871,879 tokens = −6.09 pt** (2.2× the biggest loser, more than the top three losers combined). One call: `entire graph grep "StandardException" | head -50` → 1,359 bytes naming both handlers. eg reached its first edit at call 40 with 23 build/test calls. **Baseline reached its first edit at call 71 with 68 build/test calls — 40 of them before writing a single line.**

Top-8 winners = 15.87 pt = **75% of all winner mass**. One instance delivered 6.09 points off 1.4 KB. The question worth answering is not why ten losers lost — it's **why the prefix collapsed on lombok and not on the other 48.**

## Two caveats I owe you

1. **My VERIFY removal is broader than the evidence-optimal fix.** The analysts' census of all 8 REP50 VERIFY lines: two winners (`npm test`) ran it **zero times**, and qutebrowser-f631cd ran `python -m pytest` **16 times** and won. Their surgical version was a precondition gate (+0.18 pt, zero winner cost). Removing it wholesale is a **fairness** decision — your call, and I think the right one, since 80% of emitted lines were whole-suite advice and it killed two sessions — but it may cost a fraction of a point versus the gate. It's one env var to restore.
2. **PE1SAMP stays at 9 pairs.** I'm not rerunning bat-1892 or redis-11510 under the rider-on config we just abandoned — that's money on a dead configuration. The cell did its job: it falsified the rider.

## Plan

**Ship now (all winner-verified, near-disjoint sessions, ~+0.6 pt):** symmetric wall-clock reaper on *backgrounded* Bash only (+0.30 — note a 600s foreground ceiling already exists and lowering it hits winners' baselines); vendor/dist/min filter on the grep verb, **never extending to `doc/` or `website/`** because the biggest winner draws 4 of its 10 hits there (+0.12); def-honesty on index misses, one line, no auto-search (+0.05); enclosure narrowing gated to usage-only *and* rank≥3 *and* span>80 lines (+0.02); per-instance checkout roots for validity.

**Then the real question, offline and free:** classify all 49 sessions by pre-edit prefix length in both arms, and find what distinguishes the 8 instances where eg collapsed it. That's a 15.87-point pool and I have every transcript already.

**Before any paid cell:** n=49 cannot see a +2% effect. Per your own prereg the primary needs n≈144. I'd rather spend the next dollar on the prefix analysis than on another underpowered cell.

Want me to start the prefix analysis, or ship the five fixes first?

# Plan — move Entire Graph toward 35% token savings on SWE-bench Multilingual

## Context

The goal is 35% token savings. The current honest measurement is **+1.35%** on REP50_r1
(49 instances × 4 arms, Opus max), bootstrap 95% CI **[−17.0%, +18.2%]**. This plan exists because
the forensics say the shortfall has one cause, and it is not retrieval quality.

**Why tokens move at all.** `log(tokens) ~ log(messages)`, elasticity **1.682**, r=0.957;
message-adjusted residual saving is 0.000. Turns are the only thing that prices. Measured on rep50:
`corr(Δturns, token saving) = −0.854`.

**What that costs us.** To hit 35% the eg arm must run **2067 turns** against baseline's 2671 —
**641 fewer than the 2709 it actually ran**, i.e. **13.1 turns/session** removed (55.3 → 42.2).

**Where the turns are** (49 sessions, corrected to exclude `entire graph *` invocations from the
shell counts — my first pass miscounted them and reported "zero grep elimination", which was wrong):

| | baseline | eg | |
|---|--:|--:|---|
| shell exploration, pre-edit | 725 | 683 | −5.8% ✅ |
| shell exploration, post-edit | 542 | **606** | **+11.8%** ❌ |
| build/test runs | 508 | 493 | −3.0% ✅ |
| edits | 397 | 414 | +4.3% |
| graph calls | 0 | 105 (**98 pre / 7 post**) | 93% pre-edit |

**Displacement ratio: −0.21 shell calls removed per graph call.** The tool wins the phase it is
present in and loses more in the phase it is absent from. The post-edit pool is **19.5 turns/session**
(12.4 shell + 7.1 build) and the graph makes **0.14 calls/session** there. It is the only pool large
enough to fund 13.1 turns.

**Retrieval is not the problem.** Payload named the file the agent actually edited in **28/33 = 84.8%**
of sessions that logged a payload. Stop tuning ranking.

**REP50 also measured a stale, misconfigured tool** — nine relevant commits landed after it ran
(`changed`, riders, `--path`, batched `def`, never-refuse, payload logging), it ran `EG_TOPK=5`
instead of 10, its `grep` verb ran raw `grep -rInE` across `node_modules/`, and **13 knobs
`run_REP50.sh` exported were silently dead** because `eg-q.run` hardcodes a fixed variable list.

---

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""ALL 49 REP50 pairs: turns-to-first-edit (TTFE) in both arms, pre/post split, outcome.
The winner mechanism is 'eg reaches the first edit sooner, deleting the baseline's pre-edit
flail'. This measures it on every instance so we can see where it fired and where it did not.
READ-ONLY."""
import json, os, glob, math, statistics

S = os.path.expanduser("~/work/graphmark/agentic-swebench")
PROJ = os.path.expanduser("~/.claude/projects")
tx = {}
for f in glob.glob(f"{PROJ}/**/*.jsonl", recursive=True):
    tx.setdefault(os.path.basename(f)[:-6], []).append(f)

EDIT = {"Edit", "MultiEdit", "Write", "NotebookEdit"}
BUILDRX = ("make", "cmake", "cargo", "mvn", "gradle", "npm", "npx", "pnpm", "yarn", "pytest",
           "phpunit", "composer", "bundle", "rake", "rspec", "ctest", "javac", "tsc", "jest",
           "vitest", "runtest", "go build", "go test", "go vet", "tox", "nose")

def toks(cc):
    mu = cc.get("modelUsage") or {}
    if mu:
        t = sum((m.get(k, 0) or 0) for m in mu.values()
                for k in ("inputTokens","outputTokens","cacheReadInputTokens","cacheCreationInputTokens"))
        if t: return t
    u = cc.get("usage") or {}
    return sum(u.get(k,0) or 0 for k in
               ("input_tokens","output_tokens","cache_read_input_tokens","cache_creation_input_tokens"))

def walk(sid):
    """returns (ttfe, total_calls, pre_build, post_build, pre_calls, post_calls, graph_calls)"""
    ttfe = None; n = 0; pre_b = post_b = 0; pre_n = post_n = 0; g = 0
    for f in tx.get(sid or "", []):
        for line in open(f, errors="replace"):
            try: o = json.loads(line)
            except Exception: continue
            m = o.get("message") or {}
            c = m.get("content")
            if not isinstance(c, list): continue
            for b in c:
                if not isinstance(b, dict) or b.get("type") != "tool_use": continue
                n += 1
                nm = b.get("name")
                if nm in EDIT:
                    if ttfe is None: ttfe = n
                    continue
                cmd = ((b.get("input") or {}).get("command") or "") if nm == "Bash" else ""
                isg = ("entire graph" in cmd) or ("eg-q" in cmd) or ("entire-graph" in cmd)
                if isg: g += 1
                isb = (not isg) and any(k in cmd for k in BUILDRX)
                if ttfe is None:
                    pre_n += 1;  pre_b  += 1 if isb else 0
                else:
                    post_n += 1; post_b += 1 if isb else 0
    return ttfe, n, pre_b, post_b, pre_n, post_n, g

def arm(a):
    base = f"{S}/results/REP50_r1_{a}/{a}"; out = {}
    for iid in sorted(os.listdir(base)):
        if iid.startswith('.'): continue
        d = f"{base}/{iid}"; cc = f"{d}/cc_out.json"; pf = f"{d}/patch.diff"
        if not os.path.exists(cc) or not os.path.getsize(cc): continue
        try: j = json.load(open(cc))
        except Exception: continue
        sid = j.get("session_id")
        ttfe, n, pb, qb, pn, qn, g = walk(sid)
        out[iid] = dict(tok=toks(j), usd=j.get("total_cost_usd") or 0, turns=j.get("num_turns") or 0,
                        patch=os.path.getsize(pf) if os.path.exists(pf) else 0,
                        ttfe=ttfe, calls=n, preb=pb, postb=qb, pren=pn, postn=qn, graph=g)
    return out

B, E = arm("baseline"), arm("eg")
ids = [i for i in sorted(set(B) & set(E))
       if B[i]["usd"]>0 and E[i]["usd"]>0 and B[i]["patch"] and E[i]["patch"]]
TOT_B = sum(B[i]["tok"] for i in ids); TOT_E = sum(E[i]["tok"] for i in ids)
PT = TOT_B/100.0

print(f"n={len(ids)}  pooled {100*(1-TOT_E/TOT_B):+.2f}%   1 point = {PT:,.0f} tok")
print(f"{'instance':<34} {'delta%':>8} {'points':>7} | {'ttfe e':>6} {'ttfe b':>6} {'d':>5} | "
      f"{'preB e':>6} {'preB b':>6} | {'postB e':>7} {'postB b':>7} | {'gr':>3}")
rows = []

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Is the TTFE/prefix split CAUSAL, or is it just collinear with 'eg used more turns'?
This project has killed 11 metrics that looked like levers and were outcomes. Gate the whole
route on this. READ-ONLY."""
import json, os, glob, math, statistics

S = os.path.expanduser("~/work/graphmark/agentic-swebench")
PROJ = os.path.expanduser("~/.claude/projects")
tx = {}
for f in glob.glob(f"{PROJ}/**/*.jsonl", recursive=True):
    tx.setdefault(os.path.basename(f)[:-6], []).append(f)
EDIT = {"Edit","MultiEdit","Write","NotebookEdit"}
BUILDRX = ("make","cmake","cargo","mvn","gradle","npm","npx","pnpm","yarn","pytest","phpunit",
           "composer","bundle","rake","rspec","ctest","javac","tsc","jest","vitest","runtest",
           "go build","go test","go vet","tox","nose")

def toks(cc):
    mu=cc.get("modelUsage") or {}
    if mu:
        t=sum((m.get(k,0) or 0) for m in mu.values() for k in
              ("inputTokens","outputTokens","cacheReadInputTokens","cacheCreationInputTokens"))
        if t: return t
    u=cc.get("usage") or {}
    return sum(u.get(k,0) or 0 for k in ("input_tokens","output_tokens","cache_read_input_tokens","cache_creation_input_tokens"))

def walk(sid):
    ttfe=None; n=0; pre=0; post=0; preb=0; postb=0
    for f in tx.get(sid or "",[]):
        for line in open(f,errors="replace"):
            try: o=json.loads(line)
            except Exception: continue
            m=o.get("message") or {}; c=m.get("content")
            if not isinstance(c,list): continue
            for b in c:
                if not isinstance(b,dict) or b.get("type")!="tool_use": continue
                n+=1; nm=b.get("name")
                if nm in EDIT:
                    if ttfe is None: ttfe=n
                    continue
                cmd=((b.get("input") or {}).get("command") or "") if nm=="Bash" else ""
                isg=("entire graph" in cmd) or ("eg-q" in cmd)
                isb=(not isg) and any(k in cmd for k in BUILDRX)
                if ttfe is None: pre+=1;  preb+=1 if isb else 0
                else:            post+=1; postb+=1 if isb else 0
    return ttfe or n, n, pre, post, preb, postb

def arm(a):
    base=f"{S}/results/REP50_r1_{a}/{a}"; o={}
    for iid in sorted(os.listdir(base)):
        if iid.startswith('.'): continue
        cc=f"{base}/{iid}/cc_out.json"; pf=f"{base}/{iid}/patch.diff"
        if not os.path.exists(cc) or not os.path.getsize(cc): continue
        try: j=json.load(open(cc))
        except Exception: continue
        t,n,pre,post,preb,postb=walk(j.get("session_id"))
        o[iid]=dict(tok=toks(j),usd=j.get("total_cost_usd") or 0,turns=j.get("num_turns") or 0,
                    patch=os.path.getsize(pf) if os.path.exists(pf) else 0,
                    ttfe=t,calls=n,pre=pre,post=post,preb=preb,postb=postb)
    return o

B,E=arm("baseline"),arm("eg")
ids=[i for i in sorted(set(B)&set(E)) if B[i]["usd"]>0 and E[i]["usd"]>0 and B[i]["patch"] and E[i]["patch"]]
y=[100*(1-E[i]["tok"]/B[i]["tok"]) for i in ids]

def c(x,z):
    n=len(x); mx=sum(x)/n; mz=sum(z)/n
    num=sum((a-mx)*(b-mz) for a,b in zip(x,z))
    den=math.sqrt(sum((a-mx)**2 for a in x)*sum((b-mz)**2 for b in z))
    return num/den if den else 0.0
def partial(x,y,z):
    """corr(x,y) controlling for z"""
    rxy,rxz,ryz=c(x,y),c(x,z),c(y,z)
    d=math.sqrt((1-rxz**2)*(1-ryz**2))
    return (rxy-rxz*ryz)/d if d else 0.0

dTTFE=[E[i]["ttfe"]-B[i]["ttfe"] for i in ids]
dPre =[E[i]["pre"] -B[i]["pre"]  for i in ids]
dPost=[E[i]["post"]-B[i]["post"] for i in ids]
dTurn=[E[i]["turns"]-B[i]["turns"] for i in ids]
dPreB=[E[i]["preb"]-B[i]["preb"] for i in ids]
dPostB=[E[i]["postb"]-B[i]["postb"] for i in ids]

print("=== RAW correlations with token saving (n=%d) ===" % len(ids))
for lab,x in (("d turns (known lever)",dTurn),("d TTFE",dTTFE),("d PRE-edit calls",dPre),
              ("d POST-edit calls",dPost),("d pre-edit BUILD",dPreB),("d post-edit BUILD",dPostB)):
    print(f"  {lab:<24} {c(x,y):+.3f}")

print("\n=== IS TTFE ANYTHING BEYOND 'eg took more turns'? ===")
print(f"  corr(dTTFE, dTurns)                        = {c(dTTFE,dTurn):+.3f}   <- collinearity")
print(f"  PARTIAL corr(dTTFE, saving | dTurns)       = {partial(dTTFE,y,dTurn):+.3f}")
print(f"  PARTIAL corr(dPre , saving | dPost)        = {partial(dPre,y,dPost):+.3f}")
print(f"  PARTIAL corr(dPost, saving | dPre)         = {partial(dPost,y,dPre):+.3f}")
print("  (if the dTTFE partial collapses to ~0, the prefix story is a restatement of dTurns)")

print("\n=== SPLIT dTurns INTO ITS TWO HALVES: which half carries the loss? ===")
tb=sum(B[i]["tok"] for i in ids)
for lab,sel in (("eg PRE-edit calls  <= base", lambda i: E[i]["pre"]  <= B[i]["pre"]),
                ("eg PRE-edit calls  >  base", lambda i: E[i]["pre"]  >  B[i]["pre"]),
                ("eg POST-edit calls <= base", lambda i: E[i]["post"] <= B[i]["post"]),
                ("eg POST-edit calls >  base", lambda i: E[i]["post"] >  B[i]["post"])):
    g=[i for i in ids if sel(i)]
    if not g: continue
    se=sum(E[i]["tok"] for i in g); sb=sum(B[i]["tok"] for i in g)
    print(f"  {lab:<28} n={len(g):<3} pooled {100*(1-se/sb):+7.2f}%  pts {(sb-se)/(tb/100):+6.2f}")

print("\n=== PRE-TREATMENT PREDICTORS (baseline-only properties: can we TARGET the fix?) ===")
for lab,x in (("baseline turns",[B[i]["turns"] for i in ids]),
              ("baseline TTFE",[B[i]["ttfe"] for i in ids]),
              ("baseline total calls",[B[i]["calls"] for i in ids]),
              ("baseline pre-edit calls",[B[i]["pre"] for i in ids]),
              ("baseline post-edit BUILD",[B[i]["postb"] for i in ids]),
              ("baseline patch bytes",[B[i]["patch"] for i in ids])):
    print(f"  corr({lab:<26}, saving) = {c(x,y):+.3f}")
print("  (a strong pre-treatment predictor is the ONLY basis for a targeted gate; weak = untargetable)")

print("\n=== WHAT 15% COSTS, in the currency we can actually spend ===")
te=sum(E[i]["turns"] for i in ids); tbn=sum(B[i]["turns"] for i in ids)
EL=1.682
need=(tb*0.85/sum(E[i]["tok"] for i in ids))**(1/EL)
print(f"  eg turns now {te}  baseline {tbn}")
print(f"  eg must reach {te*need:.0f} turns = -{(te-te*need)/len(ids):.1f}/session")
print(f"  eg pre-edit calls  {sum(E[i]['pre'] for i in ids)}  vs base {sum(B[i]['pre'] for i in ids)}")
print(f"  eg post-edit calls {sum(E[i]['post'] for i in ids)} vs base {sum(B[i]['post'] for i in ids)}")
print(f"  eg pre-edit BUILD  {sum(E[i]['preb'] for i in ids)}  vs base {sum(B[i]['preb'] for i in ids)}"
      f"   <- pure waste: nothing has been changed yet")

content.text:
Two results, and the first one kills my own hypothesis:

**TTFE is metric #12 to die.** The bucket split looked spectacular (+18.68% vs −24.36%) but `partial corr(dTTFE, saving | dTurns) = +0.121` — it collapses. It was a restatement of "eg took more turns."

**The pre/post decomposition survives, and it's strong.** Both partials hold controlling for each other: `dPre | dPost = −0.585`, `dPost | dPre = −0.838`.

| | n | pooled | points |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| eg post-edit calls ≤ base | 23 | **+29.87%** | +16.98 |
| eg post-edit calls > base | 26 | **−36.22%** | −15.63 |

Run-wide: eg is **29 calls ahead pre-edit** (1036 vs 1065) and **50 calls behind post-edit** (1210 vs 1160). And critically — eg's post-edit excess is **not** verification: eg runs 373 post-edit builds vs baseline's 394. It's shell exploration. Meanwhile **93% of graph calls are pre-edit (98 pre / 7 post)**. The tool is absent from the phase that costs.

**15% needs eg at 2480 turns vs its actual 2709 — 4.7 fewer per session**, i.e. eg running ~7% *below* baseline instead of 1.4% above. Bringing those 26 instances to parity recovers up to +15.6 pt, which overshoots 15%. So it is arithmetically reachable — through exactly one door.

One hard constraint I have to flag: **every pre-treatment predictor is weak** (baseline turns +0.284, baseline TTFE +0.167, patch size −0.062). We cannot predict which instances will lose, so no "suppress when X" gate is possible. The fix must be universal.

Two forks I can't resolve from the data:

questions.question: The post-edit gap is an affordance problem: 98 of 105 graph calls happen pre-edit, 7 post-edit, while the excess turns are all post-edit. The push-rider fix is already falsified (+4.2 turns/session). What is the eg arm allowed to do to make the post-edit verb actually get used?

options.label: Single n=49 cell, wide CI
options.description: Cheapest paid option (~$300). Gives a point estimate we cannot defend if it lands near 15%. I would not recommend publishing anything from it.

## What the workflow found — and exactly where to fix

Ten analysts on the top-10 losers, then a winner-risk pass that priced every fix against the 24 winners. Here is the whole thing.

### The five defect classes

| class | covers | points | what it is |
|---|--:|--:|---|
| **C1** unbounded post-edit verification (no wall-clock reaper, env-repair to make a suite runnable) | 6 of 10 | 6.5–7.5 | mixed harness bug + tool |
| **C4** self-authored repro asserts beyond the issue → over-scoped fix → regression sweep | 3 of 10 | 3.0–3.5 | agent, not tool |
| **C3** sibling-checkout mining (answer leak) | 3 of 10 | 1.9–2.9 | harness — **variance, not bias** |
| **C2** degenerate `grep`/`def` output (refusals, vendor-only hits, 11-byte answers) | 4 of 10 | 0.7–1.5 | **tool bug, 3 of them** |
| **C5** payload widening of usage-only hits | 1 of 10 | <0.3 | policy |

### Where to fix — exact locations

**Harness** (`~/pe1/graphmark/agentic-swebench/tools/`):
- `run_3arm.sh` — **no per-command wall-clock reaper exists at all** (verified: grep for `reaper|BASH_TIMEOUT|timeout_ms` returns nothing). One deadlocked background `cargo test` cost 16 turns of sleep/pgrep/kill polling. Add it **before the arm branch**, on **backgrounded** jobs only — a 600s foreground ceiling already exists and lowering it only bites the winners' baselines.
- `eg-q:507` — `if istest(rel): continue` is the *only* filter on the grep verb. Add vendor/node_modules/dist/static/min exclusion. This is what turned prometheus's true zero into `web/ui/static/vendor/rickshaw/vendor/d3.v3.js:1`.
- `eg-q:462` + a bare `except Exception: return ''` — prints `(no symbol named X)` on subprocess failure. **Proven false negative**: `def DatabaseManager` refused while `graph.symbols.ndjson:3812` holds the class. 9 of 24 `def` calls refused; **9 of the 11 refused sessions never called the graph again.**
- `run_3arm.sh:133` and `:201-203` — every sibling instance of the same repo sits one `ls ..` away, and `/tmp/w` is a flat never-pruned symlink farm that dumps 40+ sibling ids into a single tool result.

**Tool** (`/Users/suhaan/devenv/eg-postedit/`):
- `internal/sem/search_verify.go:1571` `searchVerifyRunnerMissing` — only does `lookPath`. Maven is installed but `~/.m2/repository` doesn't exist, so `mvn -pl X -am test` is guaranteed to fail. It already handles this correctly for `bundle`→Gemfile.lock and `npx`→node_modules/.bin. *(Moot now that VERIFY emission is off, but it's the bug behind javaparser's 21-turn Maven odyssey.)*
- `internal/sem/search_enclosure.go:746` `widenSearchResultToEnclosure` — narrowed to fire only on usage-only **and** rank≥3 **and** span>80 lines.

### The two fixes that got DROPPED — this is the valuable part

**F8, the scope-lock prompt** (claimed 3.0–3.5 pt, the second-biggest prize): **measured sign-reversing.** At f=20% it's +0.98 pt worse; **at f=30% eg loses outright**; at f=50% +2.79 pt worse. Because eg *already* verifies less — 419 build calls vs baseline's 470 run-wide, 130 fewer on the winners, post-edit build tokens 9.67M vs 22.44M. Any clamp on verification breadth hands the baseline eg's only edge.

**F3b, escalate-to-search on a bad grep**: **measured +0.149 pt worse.** qutebrowser-f631cd got an 11-byte `(0 matches)` and pivoted to the gold site in **one turn**. Replacing that with a 2–4 KB ranked payload costs a winner and gains nothing. Absence is the highest-value answer that verb gives.

### The bottom line on loser repair

**+0.6 to +1.3 points. Projected pooled +1.35% → ~+2.2%.** Out of 14.47 available. Because 3.3 pt has no tool fingerprint at all (ansible-395e5e made *one* clean graph call and produced a *smaller* patch with *fewer* edits than baseline), and the biggest class can only be captured by a fix that loses more than it gains.

**Loser repair cannot reach 15%.** But the pre/post decomposition I just ran can — and I've confirmed it survives the collinearity test that killed my TTFE hypothesis. Writing that up as the plan now.

# Plan — Entire Graph to 15% token savings on SWE-bench Multilingual

## Context

Target revised from 35% to **15%**. Current honest measurement: **+1.35%** on REP50_r1 (49 gated
pairs, Opus max, 0 gate failures). This plan replaces the 35% plan, whose central lever —
injecting post-edit context — was **falsified on 2026-08-09**.

### What we now know, measured, and must not re-litigate

**Turns are the only thing that prices.** `log(tokens) ~ log(messages)`, elasticity 1.682, r=0.957.
`corr(dTurns, saving) = -0.855`.

**The loss is post-edit, and it is NOT verification.** Decomposing every one of the 49 pairs, both
partials survive controlling for each other:

| | partial corr with saving |
|---|--:|
| d PRE-edit calls (given post) | **-0.585** |
| d POST-edit calls (given pre) | **-0.838** |

| bucket | n | pooled | points |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| eg post-edit calls <= base | 23 | **+29.87%** | +16.98 |
| eg post-edit calls > base | 26 | **-36.22%** | -15.63 |

Run-wide: eg is **29 calls AHEAD pre-edit** (1036 vs 1065) and **50 calls BEHIND post-edit**
(1210 vs 1160). The excess is **shell exploration, not builds** — eg runs 373 post-edit builds vs
baseline's 394. Meanwhile **98 of 105 graph calls are pre-edit; 7 are post-edit.**
**The tool is absent from the phase that costs.**

### The arithmetic for 15%

eg must reach **2480 turns vs its actual 2709 = -4.7/session**, i.e. run ~7% *below* baseline
instead of 1.4% above. Bringing the 26 post-edit-excess instances to parity recovers up to
**+15.6 pt**, which clears 15%. That is the only door the data leaves open.

### Dead ends — measured, do not retry

| lever | verdict |
|---|---|
| Push rider (`EG_POSTEDIT_HOOK`) | **+4.2 turns/session WORSE**; widened the gap +3.3 -> +4.2 on identical instances. Off in `run_pe2.sh`. |
| VERIFY command | 80% of emissions were the whole-suite floor; killed 2 of 11 eg sessions on wall clock; generic methodology to one arm. **Removed at source** (`sem.VerifyEmissionEnabled`, default off). |
| Symmetric "verify less" prompt | **Sign-reversing**: f=20% -> +0.98 pt worse, f=30% -> eg loses outright, f=50% -> +2.79 pt worse. eg already verifies less. |
| Escalate-to-search on a bad grep | **+0.149 pt worse** (measured on qutebrowser-f631cd). |
| Per-loser patching | 14.47 pt available, **+0.6 to +1.3 pt winner-safe**. 3.3 pt has no tool fingerprint. |
| TTFE / "prefix collapse" | **Metric #12 dead.** Raw corr -0.342 but `partial(dTTFE, saving \| dTurns) = +0.121`. |
| Targeting a gate by prediction | **Impossible.** Best pre-treatment predictor is baseline turns at +0.284; patch size -0.062. |

---

## Design

Two workstreams. **W1 pays for the measurement floor; W2 is the 15%.**

### W1 — ship the winner-verified loser fixes (+0.6 to +1.3 pt)

Every one was priced against the 24 winners with real token counts. Sessions touched are
near-disjoint, so the points add to within ~0.1 pt.

1. **Wall-clock reaper**, `tools/run_3arm.sh`, symmetric, **before the arm branch**, on
   **backgrounded** jobs only. Verified absent today. +0.30 pt.
   *A 600s foreground ceiling already exists (4 calls land exactly on it); lowering it hits the
   winners' baselines, not eg.*
2. **Vendor filter on the grep verb**, `tools/eg-q:507` (today `if istest(rel): continue` is the
   only filter). Byte deletion only, **no escalation**. +0.12 pt.
   **HARD CONSTRAINT: never extend to `doc/` or `website/`** — lombok-3674, the largest winner in
   the cell (-8,871,879), draws 4 of its 10 grep hits from exactly there.
3. **`def` honesty**, `tools/eg-q:462` + the bare `except Exception: return ''`. On a subprocess
   failure or scan miss emit one line and **do not auto-run search**. +0.05 pt, and the real prize
   is retention: 9 of 24 def calls refused, 9 of those 11 sessions never called the graph again.
   `def DatabaseManager` is a proven false negative against `graph.symbols.ndjson:3812`.
4. **Enclosure narrowing**, `internal/sem/search_enclosure.go:746` — suppress widening only when
   usage-only **AND** rank>=3 **AND** span>80 lines. +0.02 pt. Fires on exactly 2 of 49, both
   losers. *The unnarrowed rule strips the gold body from a winner's rank-1 hit.*
5. **VERIFY precondition gate**, `internal/sem/search_verify.go:1571` — extend from `lookPath` to a
   precondition probe (mvn without a non-empty `~/.m2/repository`, gradle without `~/.gradle/caches`),
   mirroring what it already does for `bundle`->Gemfile.lock. Dormant while emission is off; fix it
   so re-enabling is safe.
6. **Validity, scored 0.0 pt:** one checkout root per instance and a per-run `/tmp/w` subdir
   (`run_3arm.sh:133`, `:201-203`); confirm the `~/.cargo/bin` PATH export (`:395`, `:401-403`) is
   live in every cell — it landed 2026-08-08, REP50 ran 2026-08-07.

### W2 — close the post-edit gap: make the graph reachable AFTER the edit

This is the 15%. The mechanism is established (`dPost | dPre = -0.838`, 26 instances at -36.22%)
and the diagnosis is specific: **the excess is post-edit shell exploration, and the graph answers
exactly those questions but is called 7 times in 49 sessions.**

Push delivery is falsified. **Pull is untested.** The constraint chosen: **capability text only** —
the arm block may say what `changed`/`postedit` RETURN, never when to use them
(`run_3arm.sh:1203`). This is fair by construction.

1. **Make the post-edit verbs discoverable at the moment of need, without instruction.** Today the
   capability line is one entry in a list read once at turn 0, ~40 turns before it is relevant.
   Candidates, offline-testable, in order of fairness safety:
   - `changed`/`postedit` named in the affordance block with a **return-shape** description
     ("paths you edited, the definitions in them, and what calls those") — already present, and
     already insufficient at 7/105.
   - The verbs' own `--help`/error surfaces made self-describing so a mistyped or exploratory call
     lands somewhere useful rather than refusing.
   - **Latency**: `postedit` measured 0.44-4.5s vs `changed` at 14.2s (`MaxDirtyFilesForDigest = 64`,
     `gitutil/worktree.go:61` forces a full re-index). A 14s verb will not be called twice.
2. **Instrument first, decide second.** Before changing anything, classify all 1210 eg post-edit
   calls into (a) answerable by `changed`/`postedit` as they exist, (b) answerable by a verb we
   could build, (c) not a graph question. The 35% plan's Gate 1 did this for a different cut and
   found 41.1% answerable; redo it for the post-edit shell class specifically.
   **Gate: proceed only if >=40% is answerable AND the answer is shorter than the shell sequence
   it replaces.**

### Complete the loser map

The top 10 are done. An Explore agent is censusing **losers 11-25** (the 15 nobody has examined),
separating turn blowouts from fat-turn losses, counting how many had the tool effectively absent,
and grouping into <=5 mechanisms with point totals. Fold into W1 only where a fix is winner-safe.

---

## Verification

**The winner regression gate — every change clears this before it ships.**
Fixed set: the 8 winners carrying 15.87 pt = **75% of all winner mass** — lombok-3674, fmt-2457,
qutebrowser-c580, vuejs-11739, redis-11510, babel-15649, redis-12472, caddy-5870. For each proposed
change, replay its recorded `gq_calls.log` queries and assert the payload still contains the file
the arm actually edited. A change that alters any of these 8 payloads is rejected unless the
alteration is proven neutral. *This is the step per-loser repair has always skipped, and why it has
historically bought +0.0 pt.*

**Offline first, no paid cell until the arithmetic clears.**
- Replay all 105 recorded queries against the rebuilt binary (`results/REP50_r1_eg/eg/*/gq_calls.log`,
  payloads at `+.payload`, worktrees at `replay-wt/`). Zero model cost.
- Re-score all 49 transcripts against each candidate, summing points with the winner gate applied.
- `go test ./internal/...` in the golang container on `~/pe-build` — currently green (TEST-EXIT=0)
  with the new `TestPosteditEmitsNoVerifyByDefault` guard.
- Functional probe under the real cell PATH (netjail first): `CHANGED vs` + `CHANGED DEFINITIONS`
  + `SIGNATURE RISK` present, `VERIFY:` absent. Already passing on `entire-graph-noverify`
  (sha256 `2bed0487...`).

**Then the cell: full rep50, all 50 instances.** REP50_r1 ran only **49** instance dirs, all of
which gated (0 failures). Resolve the 50th from `tasks/rep50.json` and include it.
Interleave arms per instance, cap concurrency ~8-way, gate on `usd>0 AND non-empty patch`, drop
symmetrically, report cache_read / cache_creation / output separately with a bootstrap CI.

**Power, stated honestly:** MDE at n=49 is ~25 points, so this cell can confirm a large effect but
cannot certify "+15%" to a tight interval. Between-cell spread on this project is 6.9pp. If the
offline arithmetic says 15% and the cell lands near it, that is corroboration, not proof — and the
writeup must say so.

**Stop rule:** if the offline gate cannot assemble +15% from winner-safe changes, publish the real
ceiling in `graph-bench-results/TokensNotes.md` rather than run the cell. Three headlines have
already been withdrawn here; a fourth is not affordable.

~/work/graphmark/agentic-swebench/results/REP50_r1_{eg,baseline}/{eg,baseline}/<iid>/

## Losers 11–25: the whole band is noise

The census came back and it's decisive.

| iid | excess tok | pts | eg T | base T | dT | gq calls | why |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|---|
| openlib-dbbd9d5 | +912,330 | 0.63 | 61 | 58 | +3 | 6 | grep/def churn, search never fired |
| laravel-53696 | +694,525 | 0.48 | 53 | 37 | +16 | 3 | **duplicate identical grep call**; patch trivial |

| fmt-3729 | +521,856 | 0.36 | 49 | 53 | **−4** | 1 | **fat turns** — fewer turns, verbose edit |
| qb-f91ace9 | +518,898 | 0.36 | 44 | 38 | +6 | 2 | grep-only; patch byte-near-identical |
| preact-3454 | +514,036 | 0.35 | 40 | 25 | +15 | **0** | **zero graph calls, byte-identical patch** |
| gson-2024 | +337,406 | 0.23 | 32 | 28 | +4 | 2 | byte-identical patch |
| gson-1093 | +311,035 | 0.21 | 41 | 32 | +9 | 2 | near-identical patch |
| jq-2919 | +217,004 | 0.15 | 54 | 43 | +11 | 2 | search hit delivered, still blowout |
| hugo-12579 | +205,913 | 0.14 | 35 | 33 | +2 | 3 | full toolset used, **eg patch smaller** |
| openlib-4a5d2a7 | +168,522 | 0.12 | 35 | 36 | −1 | 3 | fat turns |
| ansible-a26c325 | +145,443 | 0.10 | 63 | 67 | −4 | 1 | fat turns |
| gin-4003 | +142,060 | 0.10 | 20 | 16 | +4 | 2 | byte-identical patch |
| laravel-51890 | +130,184 | 0.09 | 53 | 51 | +2 | 3 | negligible |
| caddy-5761 | +45,632 | 0.03 | 30 | 29 | +1 | 1 | **eg patch smaller than base** |

**Total for all fifteen: 3.72 points.** Largest single instance: **0.63**, against a documented same-instance spread of **45 points median**. Not one of them clears the noise floor.

**Three patterns, and two are explicitly noise:**
1. **Tool absent** — 0.48 pt, 3 instances. preact-3454 made *zero* graph calls and produced a byte-identical patch while burning 15 more turns. Not attributable to the tool by definition.
2. **grep/def churn, search never fired** — 1.91 pt, 5 instances. The only candidate worth an offline replay. 4 of 5 produced identical patches to baseline, so the tool changed nothing about the fix.
3. **Search fired, good payload, still lost** — 1.33 pt, 7 instances. The best available evidence that payload quality is not the culprit.

**Zero of 15 over-scoped the patch.** Every one matched baseline's file count; two were *smaller*.

**One methodological correction that matters:** the `0 bytes` in `.payload` is a **capture artifact** — the harness only tees `search` results, not `grep`/`def`. So those calls did return content. That also means my earlier "payload named the edited file in 84.8%" covers `search` calls only, not the full 105.

## What this settles

Loser repair is now **independently confirmed dead** as a route to 15%:

- Losers 11–25: **3.72 pt, all noise**
- Losers 1–10: ~16.1 pt, of which after winner-cost arithmetic **+0.6 to +1.3 pt** is safely recoverable
- **Total winner-safe loser repair: ~+1.3 pt → rep50 lands ~+2.7%**

Fixing every loser you can legitimately fix gets you to 2.7%, not 15%.

## What's still running

Twelve deep analysts on the ≥10% losers, and their real deliverable isn't another why-column — it's the **post-edit shell census**: classifying every one of eg's 1,210 post-edit calls into *(a)* what-else-calls-this, *(b)* re-read-my-edit, *(c)* find/fix the test invocation, *(d)* env repair, *(e)* other.

**(a)+(b) is the fraction a post-edit graph verb could answer in one call instead of six shell calls — and it is the single number the 15% target lives or dies on.** eg is 50 calls behind baseline post-edit while making 7 of its 105 graph calls there. If (a)+(b) is large, closing that gap is worth the 15.6 points sitting in those 26 instances. If it's small, 15% isn't reachable either and I'll say so and publish the ceiling.

The plan file is written and holds everything above. I'll finalise it against that census the moment it lands.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Does the graph help A LITTLE ON EVERYTHING (noise cancels, mean is the signal),
or is it a COIN FLIP (big wins, big losses, median ~0)?
These imply completely different fixes. READ-ONLY."""
import json, os, math, statistics

S = os.path.expanduser("~/work/graphmark/agentic-swebench")

def toks(cc):
    mu = cc.get("modelUsage") or {}
    if mu:
        t = sum((m.get(k,0) or 0) for m in mu.values() for k in
                ("inputTokens","outputTokens","cacheReadInputTokens","cacheCreationInputTokens"))
        if t: return t
    u = cc.get("usage") or {}
    return sum(u.get(k,0) or 0 for k in ("input_tokens","output_tokens",
               "cache_read_input_tokens","cache_creation_input_tokens"))

def arm(a):
    base = f"{S}/results/REP50_r1_{a}/{a}"; o = {}
    for i in sorted(os.listdir(base)):
        if i.startswith('.'): continue
        cc = f"{base}/{i}/cc_out.json"; pf = f"{base}/{i}/patch.diff"
        if not os.path.exists(cc) or not os.path.getsize(cc): continue
        try: j = json.load(open(cc))
        except Exception: continue
        o[i] = dict(tok=toks(j), usd=j.get("total_cost_usd") or 0, turns=j.get("num_turns") or 0,
                    patch=os.path.getsize(pf) if os.path.exists(pf) else 0)
    return o

B, E = arm("baseline"), arm("eg")
ids = [i for i in sorted(set(B)&set(E))
       if B[i]["usd"]>0 and E[i]["usd"]>0 and B[i]["patch"] and E[i]["patch"]]
d = sorted(100*(1-E[i]["tok"]/B[i]["tok"]) for i in ids)
n = len(d)

print(f"n={n}   (positive = eg saves)")
print(f"  POOLED (token-weighted) : {100*(1-sum(E[i]['tok'] for i in ids)/sum(B[i]['tok'] for i in ids)):+7.2f}%")
print(f"  MEAN   (unweighted)     : {statistics.mean(d):+7.2f}%")
print(f"  MEDIAN                  : {statistics.median(d):+7.2f}%   <-- 'helps a little on everything' lives or dies here")
gm = math.exp(sum(math.log(B[i]['tok']/E[i]['tok']) for i in ids)/n)
print(f"  GEOMEAN                 : {100*(1-1/gm):+7.2f}%")
print(f"  stdev                   : {statistics.pstdev(d):7.2f} pts")
print(f"  min / max               : {d[0]:+.1f}% / {d[-1]:+.1f}%")
q = lambda p: d[max(0, min(n-1, int(round(p*(n-1)))))]
print(f"  quartiles  p10 {q(.10):+6.1f}  p25 {q(.25):+6.1f}  p50 {q(.50):+6.1f}  p75 {q(.75):+6.1f}  p90 {q(.90):+6.1f}")

print("\n=== SHAPE OF THE DISTRIBUTION ===")
for lo, hi, lab in ((-1e9,-50,"catastrophic loss  < -50%"), (-50,-20,"big loss    -50..-20%"),
                    (-20,-5,"small loss  -20..-5%"), (-5,5,"~NEUTRAL      -5..+5%"),
                    (5,20,"small win    +5..+20%"), (20,50,"big win     +20..+50%"),
                    (50,1e9,"huge win      > +50%")):
    k = [x for x in d if lo <= x < hi]
    bar = "#"*len(k)
    print(f"  {lab:<26} {len(k):>3}  {bar}")
neutral = len([x for x in d if -5 <= x <= 5])
print(f"\n  instances within +-5%  : {neutral}/{n} = {100*neutral/n:.0f}%")
print(f"  instances within +-20% : {len([x for x in d if -20<=x<=20])}/{n} = {100*len([x for x in d if -20<=x<=20])/n:.0f}%")
print(f"  |delta| > 50%          : {len([x for x in d if abs(x)>50])}/{n}")

print("\n=== THE TWO HYPOTHESES ===")
print("  H1 'helps a little on everything, noise cancels'  predicts: median clearly > 0, tight spread,")
print("     most instances in a narrow positive band.")
print("  H2 'coin flip: trajectory divergence'             predicts: median ~ 0, huge symmetric spread,")
print("     few instances near zero, mean = the small residue of two big offsetting tails.")
pos = len([x for x in d if x > 0])
print(f"\n  instances where eg saves AT ALL : {pos}/{n} = {100*pos/n:.0f}%   (a coin flip is 50%)")
import random
random.seed(7)
bs = sorted(statistics.median(random.choice(d) for _ in d) for _ in range(20000))
print(f"  median 95% CI (bootstrap)       : [{bs[500]:+.1f}%, {bs[19500]:+.1f}%]")
bm = sorted(statistics.mean(random.choice(d) for _ in d) for _ in range(20000))
print(f"  mean   95% CI (bootstrap)       : [{bm[500]:+.1f}%, {bm[19500]:+.1f}%]")

print("\n=== IF THE SPREAD WERE REMOVED, WHERE WOULD WE LAND? ===")
print("  The user's claim: a context tool should never LOSE — worst case you ignore the bytes.")
print("  So: what if every negative instance were merely clamped to 0 (tool never hurts)?")
clamped = [max(0.0, x) for x in d]
print(f"    unweighted mean if no instance ever lost : {statistics.mean(clamped):+.2f}%")
sb = sum(B[i]['tok'] for i in ids)
se = sum(min(E[i]['tok'], B[i]['tok']) for i in ids)
print(f"    POOLED if no instance ever lost          : {100*(1-se/sb):+.2f}%   <-- the prize for eliminating downside ONLY")

print("\n=== PER-CALL ECONOMICS: what actually moves a MEAN ===")
tot_calls = 105  # recorded graph calls across the 49 eg sessions
te = sum(E[i]['turns'] for i in ids)
print(f"  graph calls / session          : {tot_calls/n:.2f}")
print(f"  eg turns / session             : {te/n:.1f}")
EL = 1.682
need = (sum(B[i]['tok'] for i in ids)*0.85/sum(E[i]['tok'] for i in ids))**(1/EL)
cut = (te - te*need)/n
print(f"  turns/session to remove for 15%: {cut:.1f}")
print(f"  => eliminations needed PER CALL at today's usage : {cut/(tot_calls/n):.2f}")
print(f"     (measured today: 1.10)")
print(f"  => OR calls/session needed at today's 1.10 value : {cut/1.10:.1f}  (today: {tot_calls/n:.2f})")


**The graph does not help a little on everything. It's a coin flip with ±51-point swings.** Only 2 instances in 49 land in the "small consistent help" band you'd expect. Noise doesn't cancel to a positive — it cancels to *zero*, and the +1.35% pooled is only positive because eg happens to win on the expensive instances (unweighted mean is **−10.50%**).

**But the design principle behind your point is exactly right, and it's worth more than everything else on the table:**

```
POOLED if no instance ever lost : +21.20%
```

# Plan — Entire Graph to 15% token savings on SWE-bench Multilingual

## Context

Target revised from 35% to **15%**. Current honest measurement: **+1.35%** pooled on REP50_r1
(49 gated pairs, Opus max, zero gate failures).

This plan replaces the 35% plan. That plan's lever — injecting post-edit context — was falsified on
2026-08-09, and the loser-repair strategy that followed it was measured out at +1.3 points. The plan
is rebuilt around a distributional finding that reframes the whole problem.

### The finding: the tool is a coin flip, and the SPREAD is the defect

| | value |
|---|--:|
| pooled (token-weighted) | **+1.35%** |
| mean (unweighted) | **-10.50%** |
| **median** | **-4.27%** |
| stdev | **51.28 pts** |
| min / max | -142.1% / +71.0% |
| instances where eg saves at all | **24/49 = 49%** |
| instances within +-5% | **2/49 = 4%** |
| \|delta\| > 50% | **15/49** |

A tool that "helps a little on everything" would show a positive median and a tight spread. This
shows a **50% win rate and +-51 points of swing**. The pooled figure is positive only because eg
wins on the expensive instances.

**The loss is not byte cost.** Total recorded payload across all 33 sessions is 141,420 B (1.3-7.7 KB
each). It is **trajectory divergence**: the tool's output changes the next action, and half the time
the new trajectory is worse. eg is not "baseline plus information" — it is a different draw.

**Therefore the prize is bounding the downside, not repairing losers:**

```
POOLED if no instance ever lost : +21.20%
```

### The arithmetic of the two routes that move a mean

| route | today | needed for 15% |
|---|--:|--:|
| **A. Bound the downside** | 25 of 49 lose | prize **+21.20%** pooled |
| **B. Value per call** | 1.10 eliminations/call | **2.19** |
| **B'. Calls per session** | 2.14 | **4.3** |

15% = removing **4.7 turns/session** (eg 2709 -> 2480, i.e. running ~7% *below* baseline rather
than 1.4% above).

### Supporting mechanics, measured

* Turns are the only thing that prices: elasticity 1.682, r=0.957, `corr(dTurns, saving) = -0.855`.
* **The loss is post-edit and it is NOT verification.** Partials, each controlling for the other:
  `dPRE = -0.585`, `dPOST = -0.838`. Run-wide eg is **29 calls ahead pre-edit** (1036 vs 1065) and
  **50 behind post-edit** (1210 vs 1160). eg runs **fewer** post-edit builds than baseline (373 vs
  394) — the excess is **shell exploration**.
* **98 of 105 graph calls are pre-edit; 7 are post-edit.** The tool is absent where the cost is.

### Dead ends — measured. Do not retry.

| lever | verdict |
|---|---|
| Push rider (`EG_POSTEDIT_HOOK`) | **+4.2 turns/session worse**; widened the gap +3.3 -> +4.2 on identical instances. Off in `run_pe2.sh`. |
| VERIFY command | 80% of emissions were the whole-suite floor; killed 2 of 11 eg sessions on wall clock; generic methodology to one arm. **Removed at source** (`sem.VerifyEmissionEnabled`, default off). |
| Symmetric "verify less" prompt | **Sign-reversing**: f=30% -> eg loses outright. eg already verifies less. |
| Escalate-to-search on a bad grep | **+0.149 pt worse** (measured, qutebrowser-f631cd). |
| Per-loser repair | 22 losers examined. Ranks 11-25 total **3.72 pt, max 0.63 each**, against a 45-pt median same-instance spread — pure variance. Winner-safe total across all 22: **+0.6 to +1.3 pt**. |
| TTFE / "prefix collapse" | **Metric #12 dead.** raw -0.342, but `partial(dTTFE, saving \| dTurns) = +0.121`. |
| Gating by pre-treatment prediction | Best predictor is baseline turns at **+0.284**; patch bytes -0.062. Untargetable from instance properties alone. |

---

## Design

### W1 — Bound the downside (the 15%)

The goal is not to win more. It is to **stop losing**, which is worth +21.20% pooled on its own.
Every candidate must be evaluated as "does this reduce the left tail without shaving the right one".

1. **Find what the 25 losing trajectories have in common that is visible AT CALL TIME.** Instance
   properties do not predict (max corr 0.284), but the *tool's own output* might: payload size,
   number of distinct files named, rank-1 score, score gap between rank 1 and 2, whether the top hit
   is a definition or a usage, whether the query was a bare identifier. These are all knowable
   inside the tool at the moment it answers. Offline, on all 105 recorded calls with their payloads:
   fit each against instance outcome and look for a threshold that separates the tails.
   **Gate: proceed only if some at-call-time signal separates losers from winners at |corr| > 0.4.**
   If nothing does, the downside is not bounded by output policy and route A is closed — say so.
2. **The abstention rule, if a signal exists.** When the tool cannot answer confidently, return the
   smallest honest answer rather than the best available guess. Note: a previous abstention
   experiment measured *worse*, so any rule here must be validated against the winner gate before
   it ships, not after.
3. **Do not lose on cheap sessions.** The unweighted mean (-10.50%) being far below the pooled
   (+1.35%) means the losses are concentrated in the cheap instances, consistent with the standing
   band finding (costs money under ~12 baseline turns). The tool's own doctrine already says "if
   the task names the exact file and it is small, just read it" — measure whether that sentence is
   reaching the agent and whether it fires.

### W2 — Raise value per call (1.10 -> 2.19 eliminations)

At 2.14 calls/session, doubling elimination-per-call is worth the same as doubling usage, and usage
has proven invariant across six configs (~1.5-2.1 calls/session regardless of what we do).

**The single largest concentration of answerable work is post-edit shell exploration**, where eg is
50 calls behind baseline and makes 7 of its 105 graph calls. A running workflow is classifying every
one of eg's 1,210 post-edit calls into: (a) what-else-calls-this, (b) re-read-my-edit, (c) find/fix
the test invocation, (d) env repair, (e) other.
**(a)+(b) is the addressable share. Gate: >=40%, and the graph answer must be shorter than the
shell sequence it replaces.**

Delivery constraint, decided: **capability text only.** The arm block may say what `changed` /
`postedit` RETURN, never when to use them (`run_3arm.sh:1203`). Push delivery is falsified.
Note the affordance line already exists and still yields 7/105 — so the realistic levers are the
verbs' own discoverability and **latency**: `postedit` runs 0.44-4.5s but `changed` takes 14.2s
(`MaxDirtyFilesForDigest = 64`, `gitutil/worktree.go:61` forces a full re-index). A 14-second verb
will not be called twice.

### W3 — Ship the winner-verified fixes (+0.6 to +1.3 pt)

Not the route to 15%, but real, cheap, and each priced against the 24 winners with real token counts.

1. **Wall-clock reaper**, `tools/run_3arm.sh`, symmetric, before the arm branch, **backgrounded jobs
   only** (+0.30). A 600s foreground ceiling already exists; lowering it hits the winners' baselines.
2. **Vendor filter on the grep verb**, `tools/eg-q:507` — today `if istest(rel): continue` is the
   only filter. Byte deletion, no escalation (+0.12).
   **HARD CONSTRAINT: never extend to `doc/` or `website/`** — lombok-3674, the largest winner
   (-8,871,879), draws 4 of its 10 grep hits from exactly there.
3. **`def` honesty**, `tools/eg-q:462` + the bare `except Exception: return ''` (+0.05, and
   retention: 9 of 24 def calls refused, 9 of those 11 sessions never called the graph again;
   `def DatabaseManager` is a proven false negative vs `graph.symbols.ndjson:3812`).
4. **Enclosure narrowing**, `internal/sem/search_enclosure.go:746` — only when usage-only AND
   rank>=3 AND span>80 lines (+0.02). Fires on 2 of 49, both losers.
5. **VERIFY precondition gate**, `internal/sem/search_verify.go:1571` — dormant while emission is
   off; fix so re-enabling is safe.
6. **Validity, scored 0.0:** one checkout root per instance, per-run `/tmp/w` subdir
   (`run_3arm.sh:133`, `:201-203`); confirm the `~/.cargo/bin` export (`:395`, `:401-403`) is live.

---

## Verification

**The winner regression gate — every change clears this first.**
Fixed set: the 8 winners carrying **15.87 pt = 75% of all winner mass** — lombok-3674, fmt-2457,
qutebrowser-c580, vuejs-11739, redis-11510, babel-15649, redis-12472, caddy-5870. Replay each
change's recorded `gq_calls.log` queries and assert the payload still names the file that arm
actually edited. Any change that alters these 8 payloads is rejected unless proven neutral.
*This is the step per-loser repair has always skipped, and why it has bought +0.0 pt.*

**Offline first. No paid cell until the arithmetic clears 15%.**
- Replay all 105 recorded queries against the rebuilt binary (`results/REP50_r1_eg/eg/*/gq_calls.log`,
  payloads at `+.payload`, worktrees at `replay-wt/`). Zero model cost.
  *Caveat found today: `.payload` captures `search` only, not `grep`/`def` — a "0 bytes" payload is
  a capture artifact, not an empty answer. Fix the capture before drawing conclusions from it.*
- Re-score all 49 transcripts per candidate, summing points with the winner gate applied.
- `go test ./internal/...` in the golang container on `~/pe-build` — currently green (TEST-EXIT=0)
  with the new `TestPosteditEmitsNoVerifyByDefault` guard.
- Functional probe under the real cell PATH (netjail first): `CHANGED vs` + `CHANGED DEFINITIONS`
  + `SIGNATURE RISK` present, `VERIFY:` absent. Passing on `entire-graph-noverify`
  (sha256 `2bed0487...`).

**Then the cell: full rep50.** REP50_r1 ran **49** instance dirs, all gated. Resolve the 50th from
`tasks/rep50.json` and include it. Interleave arms per instance, cap concurrency ~8-way, gate on
`usd>0 AND non-empty patch`, drop symmetrically, report cache_read / cache_creation / output
separately with a bootstrap CI.

**Power, stated honestly.** MDE at n=49 is ~25 points and the median's own 95% CI is
[-23.2%, +17.1%]. This cell can corroborate a large effect; it cannot certify "+15%" to a tight
interval. Between-cell spread on this project is 6.9pp. Report it as corroboration, not proof.

**Stop rule.** If the offline gate cannot assemble +15% from winner-safe changes, publish the real
ceiling in `graph-bench-results/TokensNotes.md` rather than run the cell. Three headlines have been
withdrawn here already; a fourth is not affordable.

# Plan — Entire Graph to 15% token savings on SWE-bench Multilingual

## Context

Target: **15%**. Current honest measurement: **+1.35%** pooled on REP50_r1 (49 gated pairs, Opus
max, zero gate failures). This plan replaces the 35% plan, whose lever (injecting post-edit context)
was falsified on 2026-08-09.

### 15% is much closer than it looks

Turns price tokens at elasticity **1.682** (r=0.957), so small turn cuts pay enormously:

| eg turns/session | vs baseline |
|--:|--:|
| 7.0 | +96.9% |
| 20.0 | +82.2% |
| 40.0 | +42.8% |
| **50.6** | **+15.0%**  <-- the target |
| 55.3 | +1.35% (today) |

**15% = cutting 4.7 turns/session. An 8.5% turn reduction.** Not the 13.1 turns that made 35%
arithmetically impossible.

### A quarter of the cell already clears it

| per session | cheapest 12 eg | dearest 12 eg |
|---|--:|--:|
| explore | 13.2 | **37.8** |
| edit | 3.2 | **15.8** |
| build | 5.2 | **17.5** |
| read | 3.7 | 6.9 |
| **graph** | **2.5** | **2.0** |
| **pooled vs baseline** | **+25.2%** | **-21.8%** |

**Everything triples between the two groups except graph calls, which are flat.** The tool is called
about twice whether the session runs 30 turns or 90. Two calls is enough for a session going well;
in a session spiralling into 38 explores and 16 edits the agent is flying blind exactly when it most
needs help.

**The defect is that the tool does not scale with trouble.** Not ranking, not payload quality
(payload named the edited file in 84.8% of logged sessions), not post-edit delivery.

Corroborating, and not circular: median gold patch is **1 file** while eg makes **8.4 edit calls**;
explore runs **24.1/session** against **2.1** graph calls. *(Bucketing by eg's own session length is
partly circular — these two anchors and `corr(baseline turns, saving) = +0.284` are not.)*

### Why usage is stuck at 2.1 — the causal chain, measured at every link

1. **46% of lexical-verb calls return degenerate output.** Census of all 105 recorded graph calls:
   33 of 71 `grep`+`def` calls came back useless — `def` refused 9 of 24 times (37.5%), `grep`
   returned "pattern too broad" 4x, <=2 hits 15x, 11-byte answers 3x, vendor-only 1x. `search` was
   degenerate **0 of 34** times.
2. **At least one refusal is a proven false negative.** `entire graph def DatabaseManager` returned
   `(no symbol named DatabaseManager)` while `graph.symbols.ndjson:3812` holds the class at
   `DatabaseManager.php:18-475`.
3. **9 of the 11 refused sessions (82%) never called the graph again.** One bad answer ends the
   relationship for the rest of the session.
4. => usage collapses to **2.1 calls/session** and cannot rise when the session gets hard.
5. => at **1.10 eliminations per call**, the tool removes ~2.4 turns/session. **15% needs 4.7.**

**Reaching 4.3 calls/session at today's per-call value is exactly 15%.** That is the thesis.

**Weakest link, stated up front:** step 3->4 assumes repairing refusals raises usage, which is
untested. Usage has been invariant (~1.5-2.1 calls/session) across six prior configs — but every one
of those changed *payload enrichment*, none repaired the *refusal path*. Untested, not refuted, and
falsifiable offline (see Gate 1).

### Dead ends — measured. Do not retry.

| lever | verdict |
|---|---|
| Push rider (`EG_POSTEDIT_HOOK`) | **+4.2 turns/session worse**; widened the gap +3.3 -> +4.2 on identical instances. Off in `run_pe2.sh`. |
| VERIFY command | 80% of emissions were the whole-suite floor; killed 2 of 11 eg sessions on wall clock; generic methodology to one arm. **Removed at source** (`sem.VerifyEmissionEnabled`, default off). |
| Symmetric "verify less" prompt | **Sign-reversing**: f=30% -> eg loses outright. eg already verifies less (419 build calls vs 470). |
| Escalate-to-search on a degenerate grep | **+0.149 pt worse**. Keep the byte deletion, drop the escalation. |
| Per-loser repair | All 22 losers >10% examined. Ranks 11-25 total **3.72 pt, max 0.63 each** vs a 45-pt noise floor. Winner-safe total: **+0.6 to +1.3 pt**. |
| TTFE / "prefix collapse" | Metric #12 dead: raw -0.342, `partial(dTTFE, saving \| dTurns) = +0.121`. |
| Gating on instance properties | Best pre-treatment predictor +0.284; patch bytes -0.062. Untargetable. |

---

## Design

### W1 — Repair the refusal path so usage can scale (the 15%)

All tool-output changes. No prompt change, no fairness exposure, and **every winner's `def` call
already succeeded**, so the success path is untouched by construction.

1. **`def` must never refuse on a subprocess failure or cold index.** `tools/eg-q:462` plus a bare
   `except Exception: return ''` currently print `(no symbol named X)` — indistinguishable from a
   true absence. Emit one honest line naming the real condition, and **do not auto-run search**
   (escalation measured +0.149 pt worse).
2. **`grep` must not return junk.** `tools/eg-q:507` — `if istest(rel): continue` is the only filter
   today. Add vendor/node_modules/dist/static/min/generated exclusion. Pure byte deletion.
   **HARD CONSTRAINT: never extend to `doc/` or `website/`** — lombok-3674, the largest winner in the
   cell (-8,871,879), draws 4 of its 10 grep hits from exactly there.
3. **"Pattern too broad" must return the best N hits, not a refusal.** A truncated useful answer
   beats an empty one; a refusal ends the session's tool use 82% of the time.
4. **Latency is a usage tax.** `changed` costs 14.2s (`MaxDirtyFilesForDigest = 64`,
   `gitutil/worktree.go:61` forces a full re-index) against `postedit`'s 0.44-4.5s. A 14-second verb
   does not get called twice. Reuse the `--head` snapshot and reparse only changed files.
5. **Fix the payload capture before measuring anything from it.** `.payload` tees `search` only —
   a "0 bytes" grep/def payload is a capture artifact, not an empty answer. Several conclusions in
   this estate rest on that file.

### W2 — Attack edit thrash

**Median gold patch is 1 file; eg makes 8.4 edit calls (15.8 in the dearest quartile).** Each
re-edit re-reads context, and jq-2919's loss is **102.3% cache-read** — the cost of extra turns is
context residency, not new work.

Diagnose before prescribing: classify all 412 eg edit calls into (a) first edit to a file, (b)
refinement of one's own prior edit, (c) revert/reapply, (d) edit to a file later reverted.
**(b)+(c)+(d) on a 1-file patch is pure waste.** No fix proposed until this census exists — the
last three "obvious" prescriptions here were all sign-reversing.

### W3 — Ship the winner-verified fixes (+0.6 to +1.3 pt)

Real, cheap, each priced against the 24 winners with actual token counts. Near-disjoint sessions,
so the points add to within ~0.1 pt.

- **Wall-clock reaper**, `tools/run_3arm.sh`, symmetric, before the arm branch, **backgrounded jobs
  only** (+0.30). Verified absent today. A 600s foreground ceiling already exists; lowering it hits
  the winners' baselines, not eg.
- **Enclosure narrowing**, `internal/sem/search_enclosure.go:746` — only when usage-only AND rank>=3
  AND span>80 lines (+0.02). Fires on 2 of 49, both losers. The unnarrowed rule strips the gold body
  from a winner's rank-1 hit.
- **VERIFY precondition gate**, `internal/sem/search_verify.go:1571` — dormant while emission is off;
  fix so re-enabling is safe.
- **Validity, scored 0.0:** one checkout root per instance and a per-run `/tmp/w` subdir
  (`run_3arm.sh:133`, `:201-203`); confirm the `~/.cargo/bin` export (`:395`, `:401-403`) is live in
  every cell — it landed 2026-08-08, REP50 ran 2026-08-07.

---

## Verification

**Gate 1 — the thesis, offline, zero model cost. Run this FIRST; everything depends on it.**
Replay all 33 degenerate `grep`/`def` calls against the repaired binary and count how many now
return a usable answer. Then, for each of the 11 sessions that abandoned the tool after a refusal,
read what the agent did in the next 5 turns and ask whether a good answer would have replaced them.
**Proceed only if >=60% of degenerate calls become useful AND the abandoned sessions show
replaceable follow-up work.** If not, the usage thesis is refuted and 15% is not reachable this way
— publish that instead.

**Gate 2 — the winner regression gate. Every change clears it before shipping.**
Fixed set: the 8 winners carrying **15.87 pt = 75% of all winner mass** — lombok-3674, fmt-2457,
qutebrowser-c580, vuejs-11739, redis-11510, babel-15649, redis-12472, caddy-5870. Replay each
change's recorded `gq_calls.log` queries and assert the payload still names the file that arm
actually edited. Reject any change that alters these 8 payloads unless proven neutral.
*This is the step per-loser repair always skipped, and why it has bought +0.0 pt.*

**Gate 3 — build and probe.** `go test ./internal/...` in the golang container on `~/pe-build`
(currently green, TEST-EXIT=0, with the new `TestPosteditEmitsNoVerifyByDefault` guard). Functional
probe under the real cell PATH, netjail first: `CHANGED vs` + `CHANGED DEFINITIONS` +
`SIGNATURE RISK` present, `VERIFY:` absent. Passing on `entire-graph-noverify` (sha256 `2bed0487...`).

**Then the cell: full rep50.** REP50_r1 ran **49** instance dirs, all gated; resolve the 50th from
`tasks/rep50.json` and include it. Interleave arms per instance, cap concurrency ~8-way, gate on
`usd>0 AND non-empty patch`, drop symmetrically, report cache_read / cache_creation / output
separately with a bootstrap CI.

**Primary mechanism check, pre-registered:** graph calls/session must rise from **2.14** toward
**4.3**, and explore must fall from **24.1**. If tokens improve while calls/session stays flat, the
stated mechanism is wrong even if the number is right — report that.

**Power, honestly.** MDE at n=49 is ~25 points; the median's own 95% CI is [-23.2%, +17.1%].
Between-cell spread on this project is 6.9pp. One cell corroborates; it does not certify.

**Stop rule.** If Gate 1 fails or the offline arithmetic cannot assemble +15% from winner-safe
changes, publish the real ceiling in `graph-bench-results/TokensNotes.md` rather than run the cell.
Three headlines have been withdrawn here; a fourth is not affordable.
