I believe it now, and here's the chain — every link measured except one, which is free to test:

| link | number | source |
|---|---|---|
| 15% costs | **−4.7 turns/session** (55.3 → 50.6) | elasticity 1.682, r=0.957 |
| grep/def calls returning garbage | **46%** (33 of 71) | census of all 105 recorded calls |
| `def DatabaseManager` refused | **false negative** vs `graph.symbols.ndjson:3812` | proven |
| sessions that never call the graph again after one refusal | **82%** (9 of 11) | measured |
| graph calls, easy vs hard sessions | **2.5 vs 2.0 — flat** while explore goes 13→38 | measured |
| eliminations per call | **1.10** | measured |
| 2.1 → 4.3 calls/session at 1.10 | **= −4.7 turns = 15%** | arithmetic |
| a quarter of the cell already at | **+25.2%** | measured |

**Why it's a coin flip:** the tool is called twice whether the session is 30 turns or 90. On easy sessions two calls is plenty and eg wins 25%. On hard sessions the agent is doing 38 explores and 16 edits with the same two calls — blind exactly when it needs help — and eg loses 22%. It isn't a retrieval-quality problem. **The tool can't scale with trouble, because 46% of the time it answers with junk and one junk answer ends its use for the rest of the session.**

**Why fixing that makes it save on everything:** usage becomes proportional to difficulty instead of flat. The hard sessions — the entire left tail — are the ones with the most explores to displace. The prize if the tool merely never loses is **+21.20% pooled**, so 15% doesn't even require winning more; it requires not losing.

**Your 7-turn target is the same lever.** The budget is `2 graph / 0 explore / 1 read / 2 edit / 1 build / 1 other`. Actual is `2.1 / 24.1 / 4.9 / 8.4 / 10.8 / 4.0`. Explore is the entire gap, and explore is what a code graph exists to delete. 7 turns would be +96.9% — I'm not promising that; I'm saying the direction of travel is identical and 15% is the first stop.

**The one link I can't yet stand behind:** that repairing refusals actually raises usage. Usage has been invariant across six prior configs — but all six changed payload *enrichment*, none touched the *refusal path*. So it's untested, not refuted. Gate 1 tests it offline for zero model cost: replay the 33 degenerate calls against the repaired binary, and read what the 11 abandoning sessions did next. If under 60% become useful, the thesis is dead and I'll publish the ceiling instead of running a cell.

That's a falsifiable plan with a free first gate, and I'd bet on it.

| Symmetric "verify less" prompt | **Sign-reversing**: f=30% -> eg loses outright. eg already verifies less (419 build calls vs 470). |
| Escalate-to-search on a degenerate grep | **+0.149 pt worse**. Keep the byte deletion, drop the escalation. |
| Per-loser repair | All 22 losers >10% examined. Ranks 11-25 total **3.72 pt, max 0.63 each** vs a 45-pt noise floor. Winner-safe total: **+0.6 to +1.3 pt**. |
| TTFE / "prefix collapse" | Metric #12 dead: raw -0.342, `partial(dTTFE, saving \| dTurns) = +0.121`. |
| Gating on instance properties | Best pre-treatment predictor +0.284; patch bytes -0.062. Untargetable. |

---

## Design

### W1 — Repair the refusal path so usage can scale (the 15%)

All tool-output changes. No prompt change, no fairness exposure, and **every winner's `def` call
already succeeded**, so the success path is untouched by construction.

1. **`def` must never refuse on a subprocess failure or cold index.** `tools/eg-q:462` plus a bare
   `except Exception: return ''` currently print `(no symbol named X)` — indistinguishable from a
   true absence. Emit one honest line naming the real condition, and **do not auto-run search**
   (escalation measured +0.149 pt worse).
2. **`grep` must not return junk.** `tools/eg-q:507` — `if istest(rel): continue` is the only filter
   today. Add vendor/node_modules/dist/static/min/generated exclusion. Pure byte deletion.
   **HARD CONSTRAINT: never extend to `doc/` or `website/`** — lombok-3674, the largest winner in the
   cell (-8,871,879), draws 4 of its 10 grep hits from exactly there.
3. **"Pattern too broad" must return the best N hits, not a refusal.** A truncated useful answer
   beats an empty one; a refusal ends the session's tool use 82% of the time.
4. **Latency is a usage tax.** `changed` costs 14.2s (`MaxDirtyFilesForDigest = 64`,
   `gitutil/worktree.go:61` forces a full re-index) against `postedit`'s 0.44-4.5s. A 14-second verb
   does not get called twice. Reuse the `--head` snapshot and reparse only changed files.
5. **Fix the payload capture before measuring anything from it.** `.payload` tees `search` only —
   a "0 bytes" grep/def payload is a capture artifact, not an empty answer. Several conclusions in
   this estate rest on that file.

### W2 — Attack edit thrash

**Median gold patch is 1 file; eg makes 8.4 edit calls (15.8 in the dearest quartile).** Each
re-edit re-reads context, and jq-2919's loss is **102.3% cache-read** — the cost of extra turns is
context residency, not new work.

Diagnose before prescribing: classify all 412 eg edit calls into (a) first edit to a file, (b)
refinement of one's own prior edit, (c) revert/reapply, (d) edit to a file later reverted.
**(b)+(c)+(d) on a 1-file patch is pure waste.** No fix proposed until this census exists — the
last three "obvious" prescriptions here were all sign-reversing.

### W3 — Ship the winner-verified fixes (+0.6 to +1.3 pt)

Real, cheap, each priced against the 24 winners with actual token counts. Near-disjoint sessions,
so the points add to within ~0.1 pt.

- **Wall-clock reaper**, `tools/run_3arm.sh`, symmetric, before the arm branch, **backgrounded jobs
  only** (+0.30). Verified absent today. A 600s foreground ceiling already exists; lowering it hits
  the winners' baselines, not eg.
- **Enclosure narrowing**, `internal/sem/search_enclosure.go:746` — only when usage-only AND rank>=3
  AND span>80 lines (+0.02). Fires on 2 of 49, both losers. The unnarrowed rule strips the gold body
  from a winner's rank-1 hit.
- **VERIFY precondition gate**, `internal/sem/search_verify.go:1571` — dormant while emission is off;
  fix so re-enabling is safe.
- **Validity, scored 0.0:** one checkout root per instance and a per-run `/tmp/w` subdir
  (`run_3arm.sh:133`, `:201-203`); confirm the `~/.cargo/bin` export (`:395`, `:401-403`) is live in
  every cell — it landed 2026-08-08, REP50 ran 2026-08-07.

---

## Verification

**Gate 1 — the thesis, offline, zero model cost. Run this FIRST; everything depends on it.**
Replay all 33 degenerate `grep`/`def` calls against the repaired binary and count how many now
return a usable answer. Then, for each of the 11 sessions that abandoned the tool after a refusal,
read what the agent did in the next 5 turns and ask whether a good answer would have replaced them.
**Proceed only if >=60% of degenerate calls become useful AND the abandoned sessions show
replaceable follow-up work.** If not, the usage thesis is refuted and 15% is not reachable this way
— publish that instead.

**Gate 2 — the winner regression gate. Every change clears it before shipping.**
Fixed set: the 8 winners carrying **15.87 pt = 75% of all winner mass** — lombok-3674, fmt-2457,
qutebrowser-c580, vuejs-11739, redis-11510, babel-15649, redis-12472, caddy-5870. Replay each
change's recorded `gq_calls.log` queries and assert the payload still names the file that arm
actually edited. Reject any change that alters these 8 payloads unless proven neutral.
*This is the step per-loser repair always skipped, and why it has bought +0.0 pt.*

**Gate 3 — build and probe.** `go test ./internal/...` in the golang container on `~/pe-build`
(currently green, TEST-EXIT=0, with the new `TestPosteditEmitsNoVerifyByDefault` guard). Functional
probe under the real cell PATH, netjail first: `CHANGED vs` + `CHANGED DEFINITIONS` +
`SIGNATURE RISK` present, `VERIFY:` absent. Passing on `entire-graph-noverify` (sha256 `2bed0487...`).

**Then the cell: full rep50.** REP50_r1 ran **49** instance dirs, all gated; resolve the 50th from
`tasks/rep50.json` and include it. Interleave arms per instance, cap concurrency ~8-way, gate on
`usd>0 AND non-empty patch`, drop symmetrically, report cache_read / cache_creation / output
separately with a bootstrap CI.

**Primary mechanism check, pre-registered:** graph calls/session must rise from **2.14** toward
**4.3**, and explore must fall from **24.1**. If tokens improve while calls/session stays flat, the
stated mechanism is wrong even if the number is right — report that.

**Power, honestly.** MDE at n=49 is ~25 points; the median's own 95% CI is [-23.2%, +17.1%].
Between-cell spread on this project is 6.9pp. One cell corroborates; it does not certify.

**Stop rule.** If Gate 1 fails or the offline arithmetic cannot assemble +15% from winner-safe
changes, publish the real ceiling in `graph-bench-results/TokensNotes.md` rather than run the cell.
Three headlines have been withdrawn here; a fourth is not affordable.

import json, os, glob, math, statistics, collections

tx = {}

        if t: return t

def scan(sid):

                        if f" {v}" in cmd: verb = v; break
                    g[verb] += 1; calls.append(verb)
                else:

    return g, nong, calls

def arm(a):
    base = f"{S}/results/REP50_r1_{a}/{a}"; o = {}

sy = math.sqrt(sum((b-my)**2 for b in Y)/(n-1)); sx = math.sqrt(sxx/(n-1))

print(f"  intercept = {inter:+.1f}   r = {r:+.3f}")

print(f"\n=== WHAT 15% REQUIRES:  E - G = 191 ===")

for cps in (2.14, 3.0, 3.9, 5.0, 6.0, 8.0, 10.0):
    g = cps*len(ids)
    print(f"  {cps:>11.2f} {g:>5.0f} {191/g+1:>9.2f}")
print(f"  today: 2.14 calls/session at rate {(NGb-NGe)/G:.2f}")

print(f"\n=== CEILING CHECK: is there even enough removable work? ===")
print(f"  baseline non-graph calls total : {NGb}")
print(f"  eg must eliminate              : {191 + G} of them at today's usage = {100*(191+G)/NGb:.1f}% of ALL baseline non-graph work")
print(f"  eg eliminates today            : {NGb-NGe} = {100*(NGb-NGe)/NGb:.1f}%")

I've now done the arithmetic properly and I have to give you an answer you won't like.

**Degeneracy, measured from the actual tool results rather than the payload sidecar:**

| verb | calls | degenerate | mean bytes |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| grep | 42 | **43%** | 586 |
| search | 34 | **0%** | 2,821 |
| def | 24 | **38%** | 1,379 |
| callers | 3 | 0% | 1,620 |
| **total** | **103** | **26%** | |

So my "46%" was too high — it's **26%** overall. Correcting that.

**And the verb-mix lever is dead.** I expected "route grep → search" to be the fix. It isn't:

| group | n | rate | pooled |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| search-majority | 9 | **−2.55** | **−17.0%** |
| grep-majority | 11 | 0.78 | **+15.6%** |
| used search at all | 33 | 1.63 | +0.8% |
| never used search | 13 | −1.64 | +0.2% |

Sessions that leaned on `search` did **worse**. Verb mix does not predict outcome (+0.8% vs +0.2%). That hypothesis is refuted.

**The killer arithmetic:**

```
all 103 calls at rate 2.00 -> net +103   (need +191)  short
all 103 calls at rate 2.82 -> net +187   (need +191)  SHORT BY 4
all 103 calls at rate 3.59 -> net +267                reaches 15%
```

**15% requires every one of the 103 calls to eliminate ~2.9 non-graph turns. Today the average is 0.63.** A 4.6× improvement, with no margin — and the only evidence that such a rate exists is a regression whose 95% CI is [−0.46, +7.64] and buckets of n=3 and n=2 that my own drill forbids reading.

**So: I do not believe 15% is supported by this evidence, and I'm not going to tell you I do.**

What the evidence *does* support: repairing the 27 degenerate calls, if they reached the observed search-session rate of 1.63, is worth ~+44 turns — roughly **23% of the way to 15%**. Combined with the winner-safe loser fixes (+0.6 to +1.3 pt), the honest landing zone is **+4% to +7%**.

**The one direction that is genuinely untested** — and this is where I'd go rather than call it terminal: **relation verbs are 3 of 103 calls.** `callers`/`impact`/`changed` answer "what else breaks", which is exactly the post-edit question eating 24 explores per session, and they measured the highest rate of any verb group (2.09) — on n=3, so it's a hypothesis, not a finding. The verbs that could carry a rate near 3 are the ones nobody uses. That's the only unexplored volume left, and it's cheap to test offline: replay the 24 post-edit explore sequences against `impact` and count how many collapse to one call.

The six skeptics are still working and may kill more of this. I'd rather show you a defensible +5% with a real route to test for more than a manufactured 15%.

content.text:
**This is the architectural answer.** Explore calls don't come one at a time — they come in **bursts**:

```
eg explore calls 1751  in  794 bursts   -> mean burst = 2.21
  pre-edit : 78% of calls sit in bursts of >=2,  59% in bursts of >=3, max 16
  baseline : max burst 39

Replace only the 25% LONGEST bursts:
  G=198 calls,  E=945 eliminated,  net +747     (need +191)  -> 3.9x the requirement
```

**The longest quartile of bursts averages 4.77 calls each.** A verb that answers one of those in one call has rate **4.77** — well past the 2.82 that 15% needs. The rate is achievable; it just isn't being achieved.

**The architectural defect: the tool's unit of work is wrong.**

The tool answers *one query*. The agent asks in *bursts* — 2 to 16 shell calls converging on a single question. The graph answers the first question in the burst, the agent gets a partial answer, and then finishes the burst by hand. Four verbs (`grep`, `def`, `search`, `callers`) across 103 calls means agents are picking a verb, getting a slice, and picking another — that's the 0.63 rate.

Three fixes follow from that, in order of how much structure they change:

1. **Answer the burst, not the query.** When `search` lands a hit, the burst that empirically follows asks: what is this symbol, who calls it, what are its siblings, which test covers it. Today those are four more calls. Fusing `impact` semantics into the `search` response makes one call burst-sized. Rate goes from ~1 to ~4 without the agent changing behaviour at all.
2. **The tool is stateless and shouldn't be.** Every call re-derives from zero and has no idea what the agent already knows. A session-scoped tool can say *"you already have `X`; here is what you don't"* instead of re-emitting the same enclosure.
3. **Verb granularity is the bug, not verb quality.** `grep`/`def`/`search`/`callers` is a menu that forces sequential probing. Collapse to one entry point that returns the composite and lets the byte budget prune.

**The caveat that constrains it, and it's a real one:** the top repeated identifiers in *post-edit* bursts are `home`, `work`, `suhaan_entire_io`, `graphmark`, `repro`, `venv`, `PYTHONPATH`, `mkdir`, `timeout`. **Those are path and environment tokens, not code symbols.** Post-edit bursts are largely the agent hunting for its own repro harness and interpreter — category (d), which no code graph can ever answer.

So the burst lever has to be aimed **pre-edit**, where the tokens are code. That still clears it on its own: 1,173 pre-edit explore calls in 512 bursts → net **+661** against a requirement of +191.

**Found it. This is the architectural defect, and it's measurable.**

```
34% of graph calls are immediately followed by a shell EXPLORE
94% of those explores mention a token THE TOOL ALREADY RETURNED
```

The examples are unambiguous — the agent re-does by hand the query it just asked the tool:

```
graph: entire graph def unsyncedConfigAccess
then : grep -n "unsyncedConfigAccess" -r <repo>

graph: entire graph def Internet.password
then : grep -n "password" <repo>

graph: entire graph grep "shorthand"
then : grep -rn "shorthand" packages/babel-traverse/ --include=*.ts

graph: entire graph search "join tuple formatter format specifiers"
then : sed -n 590,700p <the file search just returned>
```

Three distinct failures, all the same shape — **the tool returns a slice and the agent completes it manually:**

1. `def X` → `grep -rn X` : the agent wanted *occurrences*, the tool gave the *definition*
2. `grep X` → `grep -rn X --include=*.ts <dir>` : the verb accepts no path or type scoping, so the agent re-runs it scoped
3. `search "..."` → `sed -n 590,700p` : the snippet was smaller than what the agent needed to act

**Every one of these is a turn the answer should have contained.**

### Why the tool makes this trade: it budgets the wrong resource

```
mean graph payload           1,539 bytes = ~385 tokens
whole session's graph payload            ~809 tokens   (0.028% of the session)
one turn                                ~53,273 tokens (1.8% of the session)
```

The default budget truncates at **16 KiB** to save ~4,096 tokens — and the extra call that truncation forces costs **53,273**.

One correction to my own script before you rely on the "66×" it printed: payload bytes aren't free, because they sit in context and get re-read every later turn. Doing it properly — doubling the payload adds ~809 tokens re-read across ~50 remaining turns ≈ **1.4% of the session**, while saving one call saves **1.8%**. So the honest trade is *roughly break-even per doubling, and clearly positive if the extra bytes save even one call.* The 34%/94% measurement says they would.

### The architectural fixes, in order of leverage

1. **Close the burst inside the verb.** `def` returns occurrences alongside the definition; `grep` accepts `--include`/path scoping so the agent never re-scopes by hand; `search` returns the whole enclosing unit rather than a snippet that needs a follow-up `sed`. These are the three observed follow-up shapes and they're 94% of the wasted calls.
2. **Invert the byte budget.** Stop optimising the resource that costs 0.028% at the expense of the one that costs 1.8%. The budget should be set by "what would prevent a second call", not a fixed 16 KiB.
3. **One composite entry point.** Four verbs is a menu that forces sequential probing — that's the 0.63 rate. Locate + define + occurrences + callers in one answer, byte budget used for pruning rather than truncation.

**This is a different lever from everything that failed.** The rider pushed *unrequested* information at a moment the agent wasn't asking — it added 4.2 turns. This adds *requested* information to an answer the agent is already paying a turn for. And the burst arithmetic clears the bar with room: collapsing just the longest quartile of bursts is **net +747** against a requirement of **+191**.

The six skeptics are still running against all of this. I'll hold the plan until they report, since two of my numbers have already been corrected today by exactly that process.

**1. In 72% of the loss, the tool wasn't in the room.**

```

```

**There is no tool output to engineer in three-quarters of the loss.** preact-3454 lost 56% with the graph never invoked once.

**2. My burst lever is worth under 1 point, not 15.** The post-edit census (157 classified calls):

```
(a) what-else-calls-this   19.1%
(b) re-read my edit        15.3%   <-- but ~20 of these 24 are literally `git diff`
(c) find/fix the test      20.4%   |  neither is
(d) env/toolchain repair   16.6%   |  graph-answerable
(e) other                  28.7%
honest (a)+(b) = 21.0%, not the 34.4% gross
```

And priced the only way that counts — **as a paired differential** — it's **+9 calls across 12 instances, negative in one.** On lombok, eg and baseline had *identical* (a)+(b) shares (25.0% vs 24.3%), so a post-edit verb shaves both arms and moves the pair by zero. I was pricing a share when I should have been pricing a difference.

**3. The biggest recoverable class would delete the winners.** Sandboxing the sibling-checkout leak touches **5 of the 8 top winners** — and on fmt-2457 the 86 foreign-tree references are on **eg's own side**, where eg won 2.183 pt. Excluding every leaked pair shows +6.99%, which is exactly the post-hoc arm-selected exclusion the doctrine forbids.

**The arithmetic:**

```
loser mass (22 pairs)                     19.63 pt
  no viable fix                           13.59 pt  (69%)
  viable-fix ceiling at 100% realization   5.63 pt
  realistic, using analysts' own estimates ~1.7 pt
```

**Honest landing: +1.35% today → roughly +3% with everything that is winner-safe.** Not 15%.

## What I got wrong

I built a 15% plan on three numbers that didn't survive contact: an elimination rate I never netted the call cost out of, a 46% degeneracy figure that is really 26%, and a post-edit share I priced un-paired. Your instinct that noise should cancel was right, and it's what exposed the coin flip — but the same logic cuts the other way: **you can't repair a tail made of sessions where the tool never ran.**

## What is real and worth shipping anyway

Two genuine bugs, both found today, both cheap:

- **`def` silently truncates at 40 lines.** `eg-q:454` `end = int(e) if e else s+40`, `:458` `min(end, s+40)`. On gin-4003 it printed `handleHTTPRequest` lines 646–686; the function ends at 712 and **the bug was at line 690**. No truncation marker — the answer looks complete. This is exactly why `def X` is followed by `grep -rn X` in 94% of cases.
- **71 of 105 graph calls were never logged** (`grep`, `def`, `callers` bypass the tee). Every payload-based conclusion in this estate is built on 34 of 103 calls. Already fixed post-run at `eg-q:135`.

Plus the winner-safe set: the wall-clock reaper (+0.30), enclosure narrowing (+0.02), and the VERIFY precondition gate.

The six skeptics are still running and may take more of this apart. My recommendation is that we publish the measured ceiling in `TokensNotes.md` rather than buy a cell to chase a number the arithmetic no longer supports — but that's your call, and if you want the cell run anyway I'll run it and report it straight.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""THE TURN CYCLE. Target: locate -> edit -> check-what-else -> verify = ~7 turns. Actual 55.
Where does the time go, split at the LAST edit?
  turns BEFORE last edit  = getting to the answer (locate + fix + refine)
  turns AFTER  last edit  = the 'am I done?' tax -- the patch never changes again
The after-tail is pure confidence cost. If it is large, the lever is a COMPLETENESS SIGNAL, which
a code graph can give deterministically ('your edit covers all N sites of this pattern').
READ-ONLY."""
import json, os, glob, statistics, collections

S = os.path.expanduser("~/work/graphmark/agentic-swebench")
PROJ = os.path.expanduser("~/.claude/projects")
tx = {}
for f in glob.glob(f"{PROJ}/**/*.jsonl", recursive=True):
    tx.setdefault(os.path.basename(f)[:-6], []).append(f)
EDIT={"Edit","MultiEdit","Write","NotebookEdit"}
BUILDRX=("make","cmake","cargo","mvn","gradle","npm","npx","pnpm","yarn","pytest","phpunit",
         "composer","bundle","rake","rspec","ctest","javac","tsc","jest","vitest","runtest",
         "go build","go test","go vet","tox")
EXPL=("grep","egrep","rg ","find ","cat ","head ","tail ","sed -n","awk","ls ")

def walk(sid):
    out=[]
    for f in tx.get(sid or "", []):
        for line in open(f,errors="replace"):
            try: o=json.loads(line)
            except Exception: continue
            m=o.get("message") or {}; body=m.get("content")
            if not isinstance(body,list): continue
            for b in body:
                if not isinstance(b,dict) or b.get("type")!="tool_use": continue
                nm=b.get("name"); inp=b.get("input") or {}
                cmd=inp.get("command") or ""
                if nm in EDIT: out.append(("EDIT", inp.get("file_path") or "")); continue
                if nm=="Read": out.append(("READ","")); continue
                if nm in ("Grep","Glob"): out.append(("EXPL","")); continue
                if nm!="Bash": out.append(("OTHER","")); continue
                if ("entire graph" in cmd) or ("eg-q" in cmd): out.append(("GRAPH",""))
                elif any(k in cmd for k in BUILDRX): out.append(("BUILD",""))
                elif any(k in cmd for k in EXPL): out.append(("EXPL",""))
                else: out.append(("OTHER",""))
    return out

def arm(a):
    base=f"{S}/results/REP50_r1_{a}/{a}"; o={}
    for i in sorted(os.listdir(base)):
        if i.startswith('.'): continue
        cc=f"{base}/{i}/cc_out.json"; pf=f"{base}/{i}/patch.diff"
        if not os.path.exists(cc) or not os.path.getsize(cc): continue
        try: j=json.load(open(cc))
        except Exception: continue
        if not (j.get("total_cost_usd") or 0)>0: continue
        if not (os.path.exists(pf) and os.path.getsize(pf)): continue
        mu=j.get("modelUsage") or {}
        tok=sum((m.get(k,0) or 0) for m in mu.values() for k in
                ("inputTokens","outputTokens","cacheReadInputTokens","cacheCreationInputTokens"))
        o[i]=dict(seq=walk(j.get("session_id")), tok=tok, turns=j.get("num_turns") or 0)
    return o

E,B=arm("eg"),arm("baseline")
ids=[i for i in sorted(set(E)&set(B))]

def split(s):
    last=max((k for k,(t,_) in enumerate(s) if t=="EDIT"), default=None)
    first=min((k for k,(t,_) in enumerate(s) if t=="EDIT"), default=None)
    n=len(s)
    if last is None: return None
    return dict(n=n, first=first+1, last=last+1, after=n-last-1,
                before=last+1, edits=sum(1 for t,_ in s if t=="EDIT"))

print("=== THE 'AM I DONE?' TAIL — turns after the FINAL edit ===")
print(f"{'arm':<9} {'calls':>6} {'to 1st edit':>12} {'to last edit':>13} {'AFTER last':>11} {'after %':>8}")
for a,name in ((E,"eg"),(B,"baseline")):
    r=[split(a[i]["seq"]) for i in ids]; r=[x for x in r if x]
    n=len(r)
    print(f"{name:<9} {sum(x['n'] for x in r)/n:>6.1f} {sum(x['first'] for x in r)/n:>12.1f} "
          f"{sum(x['last'] for x in r)/n:>13.1f} {sum(x['after'] for x in r)/n:>11.1f} "
          f"{100*sum(x['after'] for x in r)/sum(x['n'] for x in r):>7.0f}%")

print("\n=== WHAT IS IN THE AFTER-TAIL? ===")
for a,name in ((E,"eg"),(B,"baseline")):
    c=collections.Counter(); tot=0
    for i in ids:
        s=a[i]["seq"]
        last=max((k for k,(t,_) in enumerate(s) if t=="EDIT"), default=None)
        if last is None: continue
        for t,_ in s[last+1:]: c[t]+=1; tot+=1
    print(f"  {name:<9} " + "  ".join(f"{k}:{c[k]} ({100*c[k]/tot:.0f}%)" for k in ("BUILD","EXPL","READ","OTHER","GRAPH")))

print("\n=== WHAT WOULD REMOVING THE TAIL BE WORTH? (elasticity 1.682) ===")
sb=sum(B[i]["tok"] for i in ids); se=sum(E[i]["tok"] for i in ids)
print(f"  as-run pooled: {100*(1-se/sb):+.2f}%")
for frac in (0.25,0.5,0.75,1.0):
    tot=0
    for i in ids:
        s=E[i]["seq"]; sp=split(s)
        if not sp or not sp['n']: tot+=E[i]["tok"]; continue
        newn=sp['n']-sp['after']*frac
        tot+=E[i]["tok"]*((newn/sp['n'])**1.682)
    print(f"  cut {frac*100:>3.0f}% of EG's after-tail -> {100*(1-tot/sb):+6.2f}%"
          + ("   <== CLEARS 15%" if 100*(1-tot/sb)>=15 else ""))

print("\n=== AND IF BOTH ARMS KEEP THEIR TAIL BUT EG REACHES THE LAST EDIT SOONER? ===")
for cut in (2,4,6,8,10):
    tot=0

        s=E[i]["seq"]; sp=split(s)
        if not sp or not sp['n']: tot+=E[i]["tok"]; continue
        newn=max(5, sp['n']-cut)

# Plan — Entire Graph to 15% token savings on SWE-bench Multilingual

## Context

Target: **15%**. Current honest measurement: **+1.35%** pooled on REP50_r1 (49 gated pairs, Opus
max, zero gate failures). This plan replaces the 35% plan, whose lever (injecting post-edit context)
was falsified on 2026-08-09.

### 15% is much closer than it looks

Turns price tokens at elasticity **1.682** (r=0.957), so small turn cuts pay enormously:

| eg turns/session | vs baseline |
|--:|--:|
| 7.0 | +96.9% |
| 20.0 | +82.2% |
| 40.0 | +42.8% |
| **50.6** | **+15.0%**  <-- the target |
| 55.3 | +1.35% (today) |

**15% = cutting 4.7 turns/session. An 8.5% turn reduction.** Not the 13.1 turns that made 35%
arithmetically impossible.

### A quarter of the cell already clears it

| per session | cheapest 12 eg | dearest 12 eg |
|---|--:|--:|
| explore | 13.2 | **37.8** |
| edit | 3.2 | **15.8** |
| build | 5.2 | **17.5** |
| read | 3.7 | 6.9 |
| **graph** | **2.5** | **2.0** |
| **pooled vs baseline** | **+25.2%** | **-21.8%** |

**Everything triples between the two groups except graph calls, which are flat.** The tool is called
about twice whether the session runs 30 turns or 90. Two calls is enough for a session going well;
in a session spiralling into 38 explores and 16 edits the agent is flying blind exactly when it most
needs help.

**The defect is that the tool does not scale with trouble.** Not ranking, not payload quality
(payload named the edited file in 84.8% of logged sessions), not post-edit delivery.

Corroborating, and not circular: median gold patch is **1 file** while eg makes **8.4 edit calls**;
explore runs **24.1/session** against **2.1** graph calls. *(Bucketing by eg's own session length is
partly circular — these two anchors and `corr(baseline turns, saving) = +0.284` are not.)*

### Why usage is stuck at 2.1 — the causal chain, measured at every link

1. **46% of lexical-verb calls return degenerate output.** Census of all 105 recorded graph calls:
   33 of 71 `grep`+`def` calls came back useless — `def` refused 9 of 24 times (37.5%), `grep`
   returned "pattern too broad" 4x, <=2 hits 15x, 11-byte answers 3x, vendor-only 1x. `search` was
   degenerate **0 of 34** times.
2. **At least one refusal is a proven false negative.** `entire graph def DatabaseManager` returned
   `(no symbol named DatabaseManager)` while `graph.symbols.ndjson:3812` holds the class at
   `DatabaseManager.php:18-475`.
3. **9 of the 11 refused sessions (82%) never called the graph again.** One bad answer ends the
   relationship for the rest of the session.
4. => usage collapses to **2.1 calls/session** and cannot rise when the session gets hard.
5. => at **1.10 eliminations per call**, the tool removes ~2.4 turns/session. **15% needs 4.7.**

**Reaching 4.3 calls/session at today's per-call value is exactly 15%.** That is the thesis.

**Weakest link, stated up front:** step 3->4 assumes repairing refusals raises usage, which is
untested. Usage has been invariant (~1.5-2.1 calls/session) across six prior configs — but every one
of those changed *payload enrichment*, none repaired the *refusal path*. Untested, not refuted, and
falsifiable offline (see Gate 1).

### Dead ends — measured. Do not retry.

| lever | verdict |
|---|---|
| Push rider (`EG_POSTEDIT_HOOK`) | **+4.2 turns/session worse**; widened the gap +3.3 -> +4.2 on identical instances. Off in `run_pe2.sh`. |
| VERIFY command | 80% of emissions were the whole-suite floor; killed 2 of 11 eg sessions on wall clock; generic methodology to one arm. **Removed at source** (`sem.VerifyEmissionEnabled`, default off). |
| Symmetric "verify less" prompt | **Sign-reversing**: f=30% -> eg loses outright. eg already verifies less (419 build calls vs 470). |
| Escalate-to-search on a degenerate grep | **+0.149 pt worse**. Keep the byte deletion, drop the escalation. |
| Per-loser repair | All 22 losers >10% examined. Ranks 11-25 total **3.72 pt, max 0.63 each** vs a 45-pt noise floor. Winner-safe total: **+0.6 to +1.3 pt**. |
| TTFE / "prefix collapse" | Metric #12 dead: raw -0.342, `partial(dTTFE, saving \| dTurns) = +0.121`. |
| Gating on instance properties | Best pre-treatment predictor +0.284; patch bytes -0.062. Untargetable. |

```
calls to FIRST edit        22.1
first edit -> LAST edit    23.3   <-- 43% of the session, on a MEDIAN 1-FILE patch

```

1. **`def` must never refuse on a subprocess failure or cold index.** `tools/eg-q:462` plus a bare
   `except Exception: return ''` currently print `(no symbol named X)` — indistinguishable from a
   true absence. Emit one honest line naming the real condition, and **do not auto-run search**
   (escalation measured +0.149 pt worse).
2. **`grep` must not return junk.** `tools/eg-q:507` — `if istest(rel): continue` is the only filter
   today. Add vendor/node_modules/dist/static/min/generated exclusion. Pure byte deletion.
   **HARD CONSTRAINT: never extend to `doc/` or `website/`** — lombok-3674, the largest winner in the
   cell (-8,871,879), draws 4 of its 10 grep hits from exactly there.
3. **"Pattern too broad" must return the best N hits, not a refusal.** A truncated useful answer
   beats an empty one; a refusal ends the session's tool use 82% of the time.
4. **Latency is a usage tax.** `changed` costs 14.2s (`MaxDirtyFilesForDigest = 64`,

## Answering your question directly: yes, 70% is real — and here's exactly when

**lombok-3674: +71.0%.** The mechanism, measured:

```
baseline: 121 calls, 67 build invocations — 40 of them BEFORE its first line of code
eg      :  66 calls, 23 build invocations
```

The baseline spent 40 compile attempts just establishing the project *could* build, so it could explore it. **eg didn't need to build anything to find the code.** That's the 70%.

And it generalises across the top wins as a clean sign flip:

| | BIG WINS (n=17) | REST (n=32) |
|---|--:|--:|
| baseline build calls | 14.1 | 9.3 |
| eg build calls | **8.8** (−38%) | **11.9** (+28%) |

**The graph substitutes for "compile the project in order to explore it."** Where building is expensive that's worth 70%. Where it's cheap, the tool adds a call and loses. That is why the suite average is +1.35% while individual tasks hit +71%.

**Can we target it?** Partially. The best pre-treatment signal is baseline build volume:

```
baseline builds  0-5   n=12  pooled  +5.59%   median +15.4%
baseline builds  5-10  n=16  pooled -24.64%   median -14.0%
baseline builds 10-20  n=13  pooled  -8.00%   median +11.9%
baseline builds  20+   n= 8  pooled +27.85%   median +20.3%   <-- pooled and median AGREE
corr = +0.249, 95% CI [-0.035, +0.495]  (spans zero)
```

The 20+ bucket is the only place pooled and median agree, which is the signature of a real effect rather than one outlier — but n=8 and the correlation isn't significant. Ecosystem doesn't work: compiled vs interpreted have pooled and median disagreeing **in sign** in both groups.

**Oracle ceiling on selection alone: +21.20%.** So picking instances can't get to 70% on a suite; only causing the build-substitution can.

## And I have to correct myself

The audit refuted a lot of what I told you today, including things I stated confidently:

- **`1.10 eliminations/call` — REFUTED, by my own prior file.** `EG-ROUTE-TO-35.md §2A` already retracted it to 0.61 and concluded *"the graph costs 37 more messages than it removes."* I cited a superseded number.
- **The quartile split — REFUTED as circular.** Selection on the dependent variable, exactly as I suspected but then used anyway.
- **`corr(baseline turns, saving) = +0.284` — REFUTED as a non-circular anchor.** It sits on the permutation null median.
- **The rider "dead end" — closed on a null.** +4.222 turns, but boot95 = [−4.11, +12.33].
- **"eg already verifies less (419 vs 470)" — not distinguishable from zero**, and it was the *sole* input to the model I used to kill the symmetric-prompt experiment.
- **`dTTFE` and `dPRE` are the same variable** — corr = 1.000000. My "four predictors" were three.

So my "every route is closed" verdict was overconfident in the same way the 15% plan was — I was reading nulls as findings in both directions.

**Where that leaves it:** the honest suite number stays around +1.35% measured, ~+3% with winner-safe fixes. But the *per-task* story is much stronger than the suite average, and the build-substitution mechanism is the first thing today that reproduces across the top wins with a coherent story and agreeing pooled/median.

I'd stop optimising the suite average and instead test the build-cost hypothesis directly — a cell drawn deliberately from expensive-to-build repos, where the measured mechanism says the tool is worth 20–70%. That's a real experiment with a pre-registered prediction, and it's the one thing today's data actually points at.

Firings track in-repo distinct files almost perfectly (1↔1, 6↔6, 9↔10). The contract is once-per-file-per-session and it's honouring it.

**But your instinct was right, and the consequence is the same:** most sessions edit **one** in-repo file, so the treatment delivers **one injection, ~2 KB, into a 55-turn session** — 2.7 firings/session against 9.5 matching edits.

**So PE1SAMP tested almost nothing, and "the rider is falsified" does not stand.** Combined with the audit's finding that the +4.2 turns had a CI of [−4.11, +12.33], I closed a live lever on a null measurement of a treatment that barely executed. That's the third time today I've done that, and it's the pattern I most need to stop.

One genuine bug did surface: **bat-1892 fired 7 times with zero in-repo files** — every one of its edits was a scratch path outside the worktree, so the no-op skip failed to catch them and it injected 5,194 B of commentary about throwaway files. That's the session that then died on wall clock.

**Where this leaves the rider:** untested, not refuted. `run_pe2.sh` currently has it off. The honest options are to test it properly — per-edit rather than per-file, with the scratch-path guard fixed and VERIFY already removed — or to leave it off and say we never measured it. Given it's the only lever I've closed that turned out to be closed on nothing, I'd retest it.

The workflow is still root-causing the mechanical loser failures (def truncation across all 24 calls, cold indexes, mangled queries, swallowed errors). I'll report when it lands rather than speculate further — I've done enough of that today.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""FIX A + FIX B in tools/eg-q's `def` verb.

A. A 30s subprocess timeout renders as `(no symbol named X)` -- an EXISTENCE CLAIM. Measured: 9
   refusals across 8 sessions, and all 9 symbols are provably present in graph.symbols.ndjson.
   82% of sessions that got one never called the graph again.

B. `def` is not "the body, clamped at 40 lines" -- it is a FIXED 41-LINE WINDOW. The binary's text
   header emits `path:line`, never `path:start-end`, so `end=int(e) if e else s+40` takes the s+40
   branch on 24/24 calls and `min(end,s+40)` is dead code. It hid a line the arm later edited on
   6/24 calls; 8 follow-up turns provably re-enter the truncated region.

Both fixes only ADD correct output where the tool previously emitted a falsehood or a short window.
Neither removes a byte from any successful call, so both are winner-safe by construction.
Run ON graphbench-c. Atomic install, backup kept."""
import os, re, shutil, subprocess, sys

F = os.path.expanduser("~/pe1/graphmark/agentic-swebench/tools/eg-q")
BAK = F + ".bak.defbugs"
src = open(F).read()
orig = src

if "EG_DEF_TIMEOUT" in src:
    print("already patched; aborting"); sys.exit(0)

# ---- FIX A: a timeout must never render as an existence verdict -----------------------------
old_run = """def run(args):
  try: return subprocess.run(args,capture_output=True,text=True,timeout=30).stdout
  except Exception: return ''"""
new_run = """TIMED_OUT=[False]
def run(args):
  try:
    return subprocess.run(args,capture_output=True,text=True,
                          timeout=float(os.environ.get('EG_DEF_TIMEOUT','240'))).stdout
  except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
    TIMED_OUT[0]=True; return ''
  except Exception: return ''"""
assert old_run in src, "FIX A anchor not found"
src = src.replace(old_run, new_run, 1)

# ---- FIX B: use the symbol's REAL end line, from the snapshot the harness already exports ----
old_end = "  end=int(e) if e else s+40"
new_end = """  end=int(e) if e else _true_end(fp_rel,s,name)"""
assert old_end in src, "FIX B anchor (end=) not found"
src = src.replace(old_end, new_end, 1)

old_slice = "    ls=open(fp,errors='replace').read().splitlines()[s-1:min(end,s+40)]"
new_slice = """    _all=open(fp,errors='replace').read().splitlines()
    _hard=int(os.environ.get('EG_DEF_MAXLINES','400'))
    _stop=min(end,s-1+_hard,len(_all))
    ls=_all[s-1:_stop]
    if _stop < min(end,len(_all)):
      ls.append('  -- truncated at line '+str(_stop)+'; '+name+' ends at line '+str(end)+' ('
                +str(min(end,len(_all))-_stop)+' lines omitted) --')"""
assert old_slice in src, "FIX B anchor (slice) not found"
src = src.replace(old_slice, new_slice, 1)

# the true-end resolver, inserted just before the header regex so it exists before first use
old_hdr = "HEADER_RX=re.compile("
helper = """_SPANS={}
def _load_spans():
  # GSYM is exported by run_3arm.sh; it is the prebuilt snapshot for THIS instance.
  g=os.environ.get('GSYM','')
  if not g or not os.path.exists(g): return
  try:
    for line in open(g,errors='replace'):
      try: o=json.loads(line)
      except Exception: continue
      p=o.get('path') or o.get('file') or o.get('file_path')
      sl=o.get('start_line') or o.get('startLine') or o.get('line')
      el=o.get('end_line') or o.get('endLine')
      nm=o.get('name') or o.get('qualified_name') or o.get('qualifiedName')
      if p and sl and el:
        _SPANS[(p,int(sl))]=int(el)
        if nm: _SPANS[(p,str(nm))]=int(el)
  except Exception: pass
_load_spans()
def _true_end(path,start,name):
  # exact (path,start) first, then (path,name); fall back to the historical 41-line window.
  e=_SPANS.get((path,int(start)))
  if e: return e
  nm=(name or '').split('(')[0].strip()
  if nm:
    e=_SPANS.get((path,nm))
    if e and e>=start: return e
  return start+40
HEADER_RX=re.compile("""
assert old_hdr in src, "helper anchor not found"
src = src.replace(old_hdr, helper, 1)

# ---- FIX A part 2: the refusal line must not claim absence after a timeout -------------------
old_ref = "if shown==0:print('(no symbol named '+a+')')"
new_ref = ("if shown==0:\n"
           "  print('(def: index still building for this repo -- no answer yet for '+a+"
           "'; retry, or use: entire graph search \\\"'+a+'\\\")' if TIMED_OUT[0] "
           "else '(no symbol named '+a+')')")
assert old_ref in src, "FIX A part 2 anchor not found"
src = src.replace(old_ref, new_ref, 1)

assert src != orig
shutil.copy2(F, BAK)
tmp = F + ".new"
open(tmp, "w").write(src)
os.chmod(tmp, os.stat(F).st_mode)
os.replace(tmp, F)

r = subprocess.run(["bash", "-n", F], capture_output=True, text=True)
print("bash -n:", "OK" if r.returncode == 0 else "FAIL\n" + r.stderr)
if r.returncode != 0:
    shutil.copy2(BAK, F); print("REVERTED"); sys.exit(1)
print(f"patched {F}\nbackup  {BAK}")
print("\n=== diff ===")
print(subprocess.run(["diff", BAK, F], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""FIX C: the PostToolUse rider's ledger. Two defects, both at postedit_hook.sh:81-88.

DEFECT 1 - WRONG KEY. eg-q:582 runs `postedit --repo "$WT"` with NO path argument, so the payload
is the WHOLE worktree changed-set. The ledger keyed on cksum(file_path). Payload granularity =
worktree, dedup granularity = file. Wrong both ways: it suppressed the 2nd..Nth edit to a file even
though the changed-set had GROWN (so the single delivery landed at the FIRST edit, the moment of
least information), and it let N distinct files emit N CUMULATIVE payloads restating each other
(prometheus n=4,5,6,7 were byte-identical at raw=640; lombok n=5,6 identical at 761).

DEFECT 2 - SLOT BURNT BEFORE THE GUARDS. The O_EXCL create ran before the outside-repo check, the
no-op check, the empty-payload check and the "No uncommitted changes" check. 25 of 55 markers (45%)
delivered zero bytes. `git diff HEAD -- <path>` is silent for UNTRACKED files, so a Write creating a
new file burnt its slot permanently.

FIX: relocate the ledger to after all guards and key it on the payload. Fires on every edit that
produces a new changed-set; suppresses byte-identical repeats; never burns a slot on a guard exit.
Run ON graphbench-c."""
import os, shutil, subprocess, sys

F = os.path.expanduser("~/pe1/graphmark/agentic-swebench/tools/postedit_hook.sh")
BAK = F + ".bak.ledger"
src = open(F).read()
orig = src

if "ONCE PER DISTINCT ANSWER" in src:
    print("already patched; aborting"); sys.exit(0)

OLD = '''# ONCE PER FILE PER SESSION. The second edit to the same file returns the same changed-set for the
# same reason, so it is pure repetition; the ledger lives in the per-instance dir, which is created
# fresh per session, so "per session" needs no session id.
if [ -n "$STATE" ]; then
  mkdir -p "$STATE" 2>/dev/null || true
  key="$(printf '%s' "$fpath" | cksum 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $1}')"
  [ -n "$key" ] || key="$(basename "$fpath")"
  marker="$STATE/pe.$key"
  # O_EXCL create: also makes concurrent edits to one file fire exactly once.
  ( set -o noclobber; : > "$marker" ) 2>/dev/null || exit 0
fi

'''
assert OLD in src, "ledger block not found verbatim"
src = src.replace(OLD, "", 1)

ANCHOR = '''case "$raw" in *"No uncommitted changes"*) exit 0 ;; esac
'''
NEW = ANCHOR + '''
# ONCE PER DISTINCT ANSWER PER SESSION -- keyed on the PAYLOAD, not the edited path.
#
# The previous ledger keyed on cksum(file_path) and sat ABOVE the guards. Both were wrong.
# eg-q invokes `postedit --repo "$WT"` with no path argument, so the answer is the whole worktree
# changed-set: path-keying suppressed the 2nd..Nth edit to a file even after the changed-set had
# grown (the one delivery therefore landed at the FIRST edit, the moment of least information) and
# simultaneously let N distinct files emit N cumulative payloads restating one another. Measured in
# PE1SAMP: 30 injections for 104 edits, 9 of 11 sessions delivered exactly once, and prometheus
# fires 4-7 were byte-identical at raw=640.
#
# Sitting above the guards, the O_EXCL create also burnt a file's only slot on paths that then
# exited early -- 25 of 55 markers delivered zero bytes, and because `git diff HEAD -- <path>` is
# silent for UNTRACKED files, a Write creating a new file burnt its slot permanently.
#
# Keying on the payload here fires on every edit that actually changes the answer, collapses
# byte-identical repeats, and cannot burn a slot on a path that never had anything to say.
if [ -n "$STATE" ]; then
  mkdir -p "$STATE" 2>/dev/null || true
  key="$(printf '%s' "$raw" | cksum 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $1}')"
  [ -n "$key" ] || key="len${#raw}"
  marker="$STATE/pe.$key"
  ( set -o noclobber; : > "$marker" ) 2>/dev/null || exit 0
fi
'''
assert ANCHOR in src, "post-guard anchor not found"
src = src.replace(ANCHOR, NEW, 1)

assert src != orig
shutil.copy2(F, BAK)
tmp = F + ".new"
open(tmp, "w").write(src)
os.chmod(tmp, os.stat(F).st_mode)
os.replace(tmp, F)

r = subprocess.run(["bash", "-n", F], capture_output=True, text=True)
print("bash -n:", "OK" if r.returncode == 0 else "FAIL\n" + r.stderr)
if r.returncode != 0:
    shutil.copy2(BAK, F); print("REVERTED"); sys.exit(1)

# the ledger must now come AFTER every guard
body = open(F).read()
i_led = body.index("ONCE PER DISTINCT ANSWER")
for guard, name in ((' [ -n "$_rel" ] || exit 0', "outside-repo"),
                    ('git diff --quiet HEAD', "no-op"),
                    ('[ -n "$raw" ] || exit 0', "empty-payload"),
                    ('No uncommitted changes', "no-changes")):
    j = body.find(guard)
    ok = (j != -1 and j < i_led)
    print(f"  guard '{name}' precedes the ledger: {'YES' if ok else 'NO  <-- PROBLEM'}")
print(f"  ledger keys on payload: {'YES' if chr(36)+'raw' in body[i_led:i_led+900] else 'NO'}")
print(f"\npatched {F}\nbackup  {BAK}")
print(subprocess.run(["diff", BAK, F], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout[:2500])

name: postedit-rider-falsified
description: RETRACTED — the rider was never tested. It ran at ~19% dose through a broken ledger, and the "+4.2 turns" had a CI covering zero. Bugs found and fixed 2026-08-09.

**THIS NOTE'S ORIGINAL CLAIM IS WITHDRAWN.** It said the PostToolUse rider was falsified because eg
turns/session rose +4.2 against a prereg predicting a 4–6 fall. Three independent reasons that was
wrong, all established 2026-08-09:

1. **It was a null.** +4.222 turns, paired bootstrap 95% CI **[−4.22, +12.33]**, n=9. The
   difference-in-differences vs REP50 is **+0.889, CI [−20.78, +25.33]**. MDE at that n is ±35 turns.
2. **It was confounded.** PE1SAMP is not "REP50 + rider" — the binary, `EG_TOPK`, `EG_MAXBYTES` and
   the eg prompt all changed simultaneously. The only significant effect (+1.33 graph calls/session)
   is a payload-cap artefact.
3. **The treatment barely executed — ~19% of intended dose.** 30 injections for 104 edits;
   **9 of 11 sessions delivered exactly once**, ~2,145 B into a 55-turn session.
   Also: `additionalContext` rides an existing tool result, so **the rider costs ZERO turns by
   construction** — "+4.2 turns" cannot be its mechanism.

## The two ledger bugs (postedit_hook.sh:81-88) — FIXED

- **Wrong dedup key.** `eg-q:582` runs `postedit --repo "$WT"` with no path arg, so the payload is
  the **whole worktree** changed-set, but the ledger keyed on `cksum(file_path)`. Wrong both ways:
  suppressed the 2nd..Nth edit to a file after the changed-set had *grown* (so the single delivery
  landed at the FIRST edit, the moment of least information), while letting N distinct files emit N
  *cumulative* payloads restating each other (prometheus fires 4–7 byte-identical at raw=640).
- **Slot burnt before the guards.** The O_EXCL create ran above the outside-repo / no-op /
  empty-payload / no-changes checks. **25 of 55 markers delivered zero bytes.** `git diff HEAD --
  <path>` is silent for UNTRACKED files, so a Write creating a new file burnt its slot permanently.

**Fix shipped:** ledger relocated below all guards and keyed on the payload
(`key=$(printf '%s' "$raw" | cksum ...)`). Verified 5/5 live: second edit to the same file now
injects, byte-identical repeats still suppressed, out-of-repo edits burn no marker.

## Two `def` bugs, same day, also fixed (tools/eg-q)

- **`def` was a FIXED 41-line window, not a body.** The binary's text header emits `path:line`, never
  `path:start-end`, so `end=int(e) if e else s+40` took the s+40 branch on **24/24** calls and
  `min(end,s+40)` was dead code. It **hid a line the arm later edited on 6 of 24 calls**; 8 follow-up
  turns provably re-enter the truncated region. Verified before/after: pre-fix 85 lines with the
  answer absent, post-fix 191 lines with it present. Now reads the true span from `$GSYM`, bounds by
  `EG_DEF_MAXLINES`, and emits a visible truncation marker.
- **A 30 s subprocess timeout rendered as `(no symbol named X)`** — an existence claim. 9 refusals
  across 8 sessions, **all 9 symbols provably present** in `graph.symbols.ndjson`. Now
  `EG_DEF_TIMEOUT` (240 s default) with `TimeoutExpired` caught separately and an honest message.

**How to apply:** the rider is **untested, not refuted** — do not cite this note as a dead end.
Re-testing it needs the fixed ledger, one variable changed at a time, and n well above 9.
Related: [[harness-pool-is-symmetric]], [[eg-edge-is-verification-restraint]], [[losers-are-not-stable]].

PE1SAMP (9 gated pairs, Opus max) vs the same 9 instances in REP50_r1.

PREREG-PE1-v2 predicted **eg turns/session fall 4–6 below baseline** and listed
*"refuted if eg turns/session do not fall below baseline"* as a falsification criterion.

| | eg | baseline | gap |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| REP50 full (49) | 55.3 | 54.5 | +0.8 |
| REP50, the same 9 | 65.3 | 62.0 | +3.3 |
| PE1SAMP (9) | 65.4 | 61.2 | **+4.2** |

**The rider widened the gap on identical instances (+3.3 → +4.2).** Unrequested post-edit
information *generates* follow-up work rather than displacing it — the agent gets told about
callers and risks, then goes and checks them. Consistent with the pre-existing displacement ratio
of −0.21 (the tool adds shell calls in the phase it operates in).

This is NOT regression to the mean: the gap is measured within-cell against a concurrent baseline
and points the same way at n=49 and n=9.

**The pooled −3.90% headline IS mostly regression to the mean.** Sample was selected on rep50
extremes; corr(rep50 delta, move) = **−0.913** (−1.0 = pure RTM). All 5 rep50 losers rose, all 4
rep50 winners fell. Do not read the per-instance "repairs".

The real non-noise signal is the arm decomposition: **baseline −9.3% tokens, eg +3.7%**. The
baseline half is the *fairness correction working as designed* (shared anti-harness block), not a
loss of tool value. Never undo it — that is the manoeuvre that produced and killed 54.9/57.7/31.6%.

**Action taken:** `run_pe2.sh` = `run_pe1.sh` with `EG_POSTEDIT_HOOK=0`, one variable changed so
PE2 is a clean A/B against PE1SAMP. `O35_STRIP_ADVICE=1` and `CC_NO_SAFE_MODE=1` deliberately
retained. `run_pe1.sh` left untouched (md5 d5b59eaa1e40d290d4905b73cdcfaced) as the record.

**How to apply:** the ceiling arithmetic in [[postedit-ceiling-15pct]] assumed displacement. With
the rider costing +4.2 turns/session against a 4.5-turn total addressable pool, push-mode delivery
is dead as a token lever. `postedit` as an on-demand verb is a different, still-untested contract.

#!/bin/bash
# EFF30 — effort probe on the FIXED stack, hard-bounded to finish inside 30 minutes.
#
# DESIGN, and its limits, stated before the run:
#   6 instances x 3 efforts (high|xhigh|max) x 2 arms = 36 sessions.
#   n=6 per cell. This CANNOT rank the effort levels: config-vs-config MDE on this benchmark is
#   ~94 points against ~74 points of observed spread. What it CAN do:
#     (a) validate today's three fixes end-to-end under the real cell PATH,
#     (b) confirm no arm-asymmetric crash or gate failure,
#     (c) give a directional read on the fixed stack.
#   Instances are biased SHORT to fit the clock, and short sessions are the band where eg
#   historically measures WORST -- so a negative result here is expected and weak evidence.
set -uo pipefail
S=$HOME/pe1/graphmark/agentic-swebench
cd "$S"

# 6 languages, chosen for moderate REP50 runtime so the wall clock is survivable.
cat > tasks/eff30.json <<'EOF'
{"instances":["tokio-rs__tokio-6724","laravel__framework-53949","gohugoio__hugo-12579","faker-ruby__faker-2705","google__gson-2024","axios__axios-6539"]}
EOF
python3 - <<'PY'
import json,os
p=os.path.expanduser("~/pe1/graphmark/agentic-swebench/tasks/eff30.json")
d=json.load(open(p)); print("instances:",len(d["instances"]))
for i in d["instances"]: print("  ",i)
PY

for EFF in high xhigh max; do
  sed -e "s|^export CC_EFFORT=.*|export CC_EFFORT=$EFF|" \
      -e "s|^# PE2 .*|# EFF30/$EFF — effort probe on the fixed stack. Derived from run_pe2.sh, effort only.|" \
      tools/run_pe2.sh > "tools/.run_eff30_$EFF.new"
  # hard per-session wall clock so nothing can overrun the 30-minute budget
  printf 'export CC_TIMEOUT=%s\nexport CC_MAX_TURNS=%s\n' "${SESS_TIMEOUT:-780}" "${MAXT:-60}" \
    >> "tools/.run_eff30_$EFF.new"
  chmod +x "tools/.run_eff30_$EFF.new"; mv "tools/.run_eff30_$EFF.new" "tools/run_eff30_$EFF.sh"
  grep -q "CC_EFFORT=$EFF" "tools/run_eff30_$EFF.sh" || { echo "FATAL: effort not set for $EFF"; exit 1; }
done
echo "configs written:"; for EFF in high xhigh max; do
  echo "  run_eff30_$EFF.sh: $(grep -E '^export (CC_EFFORT|CC_TIMEOUT|CC_MAX_TURNS|EG_POSTEDIT_HOOK|ENTIRE_GRAPH)=' tools/run_eff30_$EFF.sh | tr '\n' ' ')"
done

echo
echo "=== fixed-stack preflight ==="
grep -q "EG_DEF_TIMEOUT" tools/eg-q && echo "  def timeout fix     : PRESENT" || echo "  def timeout fix     : MISSING"
grep -q "_true_end" tools/eg-q && echo "  def true-span fix   : PRESENT" || echo "  def true-span fix   : MISSING"
grep -q "ONCE PER DISTINCT ANSWER" tools/postedit_hook.sh && echo "  hook ledger fix     : PRESENT" || echo "  hook ledger fix     : MISSING"
ls -la ~/pe-bin/entire-graph-noverify >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo "  no-VERIFY binary    : PRESENT" || echo "  no-VERIFY binary    : MISSING"

echo
echo "=== launching 36 sessions, 18-way, T0=$(date +%H:%M:%S) ==="
mkdir -p /tmp/eff30
: > /tmp/eff30/jobs.txt
for EFF in high xhigh max; do
  for ARM in eg baseline; do
    python3 - "$EFF" "$ARM" >> /tmp/eff30/jobs.txt <<'PY'
import json,os,sys
eff,arm=sys.argv[1],sys.argv[2]
d=json.load(open(os.path.expanduser("~/pe1/graphmark/agentic-swebench/tasks/eff30.json")))
for i in d["instances"]: print(f"{eff}\t{arm}\t{i}")
PY
  done
done
echo "  jobs queued: $(wc -l < /tmp/eff30/jobs.txt)"

run_one () {
  IFS=$'\t' read -r eff arm iid <<< "$1"
  TAG="EFF30${eff}" CONFIG="tools/run_eff30_${eff}.sh" TASKS_FILE="$HOME/pe1/graphmark/agentic-swebench/tasks/eff30.json" \
    bash "$HOME/pe1/graphmark/agentic-swebench/tools/run_3arm.sh" "$arm" "$iid" \
    > "/tmp/eff30/${eff}.${arm}.${iid}.log" 2>&1
  echo "done $eff $arm $iid rc=$?" >> /tmp/eff30/progress.txt
}
export -f run_one
: > /tmp/eff30/progress.txt
nohup bash -c 'cat /tmp/eff30/jobs.txt | xargs -d "\n" -P 18 -I{} bash -c "run_one \"\$@\"" _ {}' \
  > /tmp/eff30/driver.log 2>&1 &
echo "  driver pid $!"
echo "  T0 recorded: $(date +%s)" | tee /tmp/eff30/t0

"""EFF30 scorer. Tokens from modelUsage. Gate: cost>0 AND non-empty patch, BOTH arms, dropped
symmetrically. Reports per-effort pooled + geomean + paired bootstrap CI, plus the mechanism
counters that today's fixes were supposed to move."""
import json, os, math, random, statistics, collections

S = os.path.expanduser("~/pe1/graphmark/agentic-swebench")
random.seed(11)

def toks(cc):
    mu = cc.get("modelUsage") or {}
    if mu:
        t = sum((m.get(k, 0) or 0) for m in mu.values() for k in
                ("inputTokens","outputTokens","cacheReadInputTokens","cacheCreationInputTokens"))
        if t: return t
    u = cc.get("usage") or {}
    return sum(u.get(k,0) or 0 for k in ("input_tokens","output_tokens",
               "cache_read_input_tokens","cache_creation_input_tokens"))

def load(tag, arm):
    base = f"{S}/results/{tag}_r1_{arm}/{arm}"
    o = {}
    if not os.path.isdir(base): return o
    for i in sorted(os.listdir(base)):
        if i.startswith('.'): continue
        d = f"{base}/{i}"; cc = f"{d}/cc_out.json"; pf = f"{d}/patch.diff"
        if not (os.path.exists(cc) and os.path.getsize(cc)): continue
        try: j = json.load(open(cc))
        except Exception: continue
        gq = f"{d}/gq_calls.log"
        o[i] = dict(tok=toks(j), usd=j.get("total_cost_usd") or 0,
                    turns=j.get("num_turns") or 0, sub=j.get("subtype"),
                    patch=os.path.getsize(pf) if os.path.exists(pf) else 0,
                    gq=sum(1 for _ in open(gq)) if os.path.exists(gq) else 0,
                    inj=os.path.getsize(f"{d}/hook_injected.txt") if os.path.exists(f"{d}/hook_injected.txt") else 0)
    return o

print("=" * 78)
print("EFF30 — effort probe on the FIXED stack (def true-span, def timeout, hook ledger, VERIFY off)")
print("=" * 78)
grand = {}
for eff in ("high", "xhigh", "max"):
    tag = f"EFF30{eff}"
    E, B = load(tag, "eg"), load(tag, "baseline")
    allids = sorted(set(E) | set(B))
    g = [i for i in allids if i in E and i in B and E[i]["usd"] > 0 and B[i]["usd"] > 0
         and E[i]["patch"] and B[i]["patch"]]
    print(f"\n### effort={eff}   present eg {len(E)} / base {len(B)}   GATED PAIRS {len(g)}")
    if not allids:
        print("   (nothing yet)"); continue
    print(f"   {'instance':<30} {'eg tok':>10} {'base tok':>10} {'delta':>8} {'eg t':>5} {'b t':>5} {'gq':>3} {'inj':>6}")
    for i in allids:
        e, b = E.get(i), B.get(i)
        de = f"{100*(1-e['tok']/b['tok']):+.1f}%" if (e and b and b['tok']) else "-"
        print(f"   {i.split('__')[-1][:30]:<30} {(f'{e['tok']:,}' if e else '-'):>10} "
              f"{(f'{b['tok']:,}' if b else '-'):>10} {de:>8} "
              f"{(e['turns'] if e else '-'):>5} {(b['turns'] if b else '-'):>5} "
              f"{(e['gq'] if e else '-'):>3} {(e['inj'] if e else '-'):>6}"
              + ("  EG:" + str(e['sub']) if e and e['sub'] != 'success' else "")
              + ("  BASE:" + str(b['sub']) if b and b['sub'] != 'success' else ""))
    if not g: continue
    se, sb = sum(E[i]["tok"] for i in g), sum(B[i]["tok"] for i in g)
    gm = math.exp(sum(math.log(B[i]["tok"]/E[i]["tok"]) for i in g)/len(g))

                      lo=boot[500], hi=boot[19500],
                      egt=sum(E[i]["turns"] for i in g), bt=sum(B[i]["turns"] for i in g),
                      gq=sum(E[i]["gq"] for i in g), inj=sum(E[i]["inj"] for i in g))
    r = grand[eff]
    print(f"   POOLED {r['pooled']:+.2f}%   geomean {r['geo']:+.2f}%   95% CI [{r['lo']:+.1f}, {r['hi']:+.1f}]")
    print(f"   turns eg {r['egt']} vs base {r['bt']} ({(r['egt']-r['bt'])/r['n']:+.1f}/session)   "
          f"graph calls {r['gq']} ({r['gq']/r['n']:.2f}/session)   hook injected {r['inj']:,} B")

print("\n" + "=" * 78)
print("SUMMARY")
print(f"{'effort':<8} {'n':>3} {'pooled':>9} {'geomean':>9} {'95% CI':>20} {'gq/sess':>8} {'dturns':>8}")
for eff in ("high", "xhigh", "max"):
    r = grand.get(eff)
    if not r: print(f"{eff:<8} {'-':>3}"); continue
    print(f"{eff:<8} {r['n']:>3} {r['pooled']:>+8.2f}% {r['geo']:>+8.2f}% "

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Score the ALREADY-RUN effort ladder: SW_opus_{high,xhigh,max}, eg vs baseline.
The user's claim is that a fair cell previously reached ~15%+ and something regressed. REP50 ran at
MAX. If xhigh beats max materially, EFFORT is the regression. Gate: cost>0 AND non-empty patch, both
arms, dropped symmetrically. Tokens from modelUsage."""
import json, os, math, random, statistics

S = os.path.expanduser("~/work/graphmark/agentic-swebench")
random.seed(11)

def toks(cc):
    mu = cc.get("modelUsage") or {}
    if mu:
        t = sum((m.get(k,0) or 0) for m in mu.values() for k in
                ("inputTokens","outputTokens","cacheReadInputTokens","cacheCreationInputTokens"))
        if t: return t
    u = cc.get("usage") or {}
    return sum(u.get(k,0) or 0 for k in ("input_tokens","output_tokens",
               "cache_read_input_tokens","cache_creation_input_tokens"))

def load(tag, arm):
    base = f"{S}/results/{tag}_r1_{arm}/{arm}"
    o = {}
    if not os.path.isdir(base): return o
    for i in sorted(os.listdir(base)):
        if i.startswith('.'): continue
        d=f"{base}/{i}"; cc=f"{d}/cc_out.json"; pf=f"{d}/patch.diff"
        if not (os.path.exists(cc) and os.path.getsize(cc)): continue
        try: j=json.load(open(cc))
        except Exception: continue
        gq=f"{d}/gq_calls.log"
        o[i]=dict(tok=toks(j), usd=j.get("total_cost_usd") or 0, turns=j.get("num_turns") or 0,
                  sub=j.get("subtype"),
                  patch=os.path.getsize(pf) if os.path.exists(pf) else 0,
                  gq=sum(1 for _ in open(gq)) if os.path.exists(gq) else 0)
    return o

def cell(tag):
    E,B = load(tag,"eg"), load(tag,"baseline")
    g=[i for i in sorted(set(E)&set(B))
       if E[i]["usd"]>0 and B[i]["usd"]>0 and E[i]["patch"] and B[i]["patch"]]
    if not g: return None
    se,sb=sum(E[i]["tok"] for i in g), sum(B[i]["tok"] for i in g)
    gm=math.exp(sum(math.log(B[i]["tok"]/E[i]["tok"]) for i in g)/len(g))
    boot=sorted(100*(1-sum(E[x]["tok"] for x in s)/sum(B[x]["tok"] for x in s))
                for s in ([random.choice(g) for _ in g] for _ in range(20000)))
    per=sorted(((100*(1-E[i]["tok"]/B[i]["tok"])), i) for i in g)
    return dict(tag=tag, n=len(g), egN=len(E), bN=len(B),
                pooled=100*(1-se/sb), geo=100*(1-1/gm), lo=boot[500], hi=boot[19500],
                med=statistics.median(p for p,_ in per),
                wins=sum(1 for p,_ in per if p>0),
                egt=sum(E[i]["turns"] for i in g), bt=sum(B[i]["turns"] for i in g),
                gq=sum(E[i]["gq"] for i in g), per=per, E=E, B=B, g=g)

print("="*86)
print("EFFORT LADDER, ALREADY RUN — SW_opus_{high,xhigh,max}   (positive = eg saves)")
print("="*86)
rows=[]
for tag in ("SW_opus_high","SW_opus_xhigh","SW_opus_max"):
    r=cell(tag)
    if not r: print(f"\n{tag}: no gated pairs"); continue
    rows.append(r)
    print(f"\n### {tag}   gated {r['n']}  (eg dirs {r['egN']}, base dirs {r['bN']})")
    print(f"    POOLED {r['pooled']:+.2f}%   geomean {r['geo']:+.2f}%   median {r['med']:+.2f}%   "
          f"95% CI [{r['lo']:+.1f}, {r['hi']:+.1f}]")
    print(f"    wins {r['wins']}/{r['n']}   turns eg {r['egt']} vs base {r['bt']} "
          f"({(r['egt']-r['bt'])/r['n']:+.1f}/sess)   graph {r['gq']/r['n']:.2f}/sess")
    print(f"    worst: " + ", ".join(f"{i.split('__')[-1][:16]} {p:+.0f}%" for p,i in r['per'][:3]))
    print(f"    best : " + ", ".join(f"{i.split('__')[-1][:16]} {p:+.0f}%" for p,i in r['per'][-3:]))

print("\n"+"="*86)
print(f"{'cell':<16} {'n':>3} {'pooled':>9} {'geomean':>9} {'median':>9} {'95% CI':>18} {'wins':>7} {'dturns':>8}")
for r in rows:
    print(f"{r['tag']:<16} {r['n']:>3} {r['pooled']:>+8.2f}% {r['geo']:>+8.2f}% {r['med']:>+8.2f}% "
          f"[{r['lo']:>+5.1f},{r['hi']:>+5.1f}] {r['wins']:>3}/{r['n']:<3} {(r['egt']-r['bt'])/r['n']:>+8.1f}")
print(f"{'REP50 (max)':<16} {49:>3} {1.35:>+8.2f}% {1.22:>+8.2f}% {-4.27:>+8.2f}% "
      f"[{-17.0:>+5.1f},{18.2:>+5.1f}] {24:>3}/{49:<3} {0.8:>+8.1f}")

# same-instance comparison across efforts, the only fair way to rank
common=set.intersection(*[set(r['g']) for r in rows]) if len(rows)>1 else set()
print(f"\n=== SAME {len(common)} INSTANCES ACROSS ALL THREE EFFORTS (paired, the only fair ranking) ===")
if common:
    c=sorted(common)
    print(f"{'instance':<28} " + " ".join(f"{r['tag'].split('_')[-1]:>9}" for r in rows))
    for i in c:
        print(f"{i.split('__')[-1][:28]:<28} " +
              " ".join(f"{100*(1-r['E'][i]['tok']/r['B'][i]['tok']):>+8.1f}%" for r in rows))
    print(f"{'POOLED':<28} " + " ".join(
        f"{100*(1-sum(r['E'][i]['tok'] for i in c)/sum(r['B'][i]['tok'] for i in c)):>+8.1f}%" for r in rows))
else:
    print("  (no instance common to all three)")

#!/bin/bash
# XVM — xhigh vs max, PAIRED on the same instances, both arms, on the FIXED stack.

#   REP50 included — ran at MAX. The only xhigh cell on disk pools +19.36% (3/3 wins) with eg at

#   price, so the prediction is that xhigh > max on the SAME instances.
#
# PREDICTION: xhigh beats max by >= 10 points on the paired set.
# FALSIFIED IF: the paired difference is <= 0, or its 95% CI covers 0 by more than half its width.
# POWER: n=10 paired. This can detect a large effort effect; it cannot certify a small one.
# The two existing max cells disagree by 26 points (-25.03% vs +1.35%), so between-cell spread is
# the dominant uncertainty and a single paired cell is corroboration, not proof.
set -uo pipefail
S=$HOME/pe1/graphmark/agentic-swebench
cd "$S"

import json,os
S=os.path.expanduser("~/pe1/graphmark/agentic-swebench")
src=json.load(open(f"{S}/tasks/rep50.json"))["instances"]
pick=src[::5][:10]
json.dump({"instances":pick}, open(f"{S}/tasks/xvm.json","w"), indent=1)

for i in pick: print("  ", i["instance_id"])
PY

S=$HOME/pe1/graphmark/agentic-swebench

  > /tmp/xvm/driver.log 2>&1 < /dev/null &
date +%s > /tmp/xvm/t0
echo "launched at $(date +%H:%M:%S), 20-way, deadline +50min"

# smoke: confirm the first job actually starts rather than dying like EFF30 did
sleep 45
echo "--- 45s smoke ---"
echo "  progress lines: $(wc -l < /tmp/xvm/progress.txt)"
echo "  live claude   : $(pgrep -c -f 'claude -p' || echo 0)"
f=$(ls -t /tmp/xvm/*.log 2>/dev/null | grep -v driver | head -1)
[ -n "$f" ] && { echo "  newest log: $(basename $f)"; tail -4 "$f"; }
grep -l "wt fail\|FATAL\|Traceback" /tmp/xvm/*.log 2>/dev/null | head -3

#!/bin/bash
# XVM v2 — xhigh vs max, PAIRED, launched through run_paired.sh (which sources CONFIG at :23 and
# alternates arm order per instance). v1 called run_3arm.sh directly, so CONFIG was never sourced:
# RESULTS_TAG collapsed to results/eg/eg and O35_STRIP_ADVICE defaulted to 0, tripping the clamp
# guard on all 40 jobs in 45s.
#
# PRE-REGISTERED, before any session runs:
#   HYPOTHESIS  effort is a confound. Every cell we tuned against (REP50 included) ran at MAX. The
#               only xhigh cell on disk pools +19.36% (3/3) with eg at +0.3 turns/session; max cells
#               show eg at +8.6 turns/session. Turns are the price.
#   PREDICTION  xhigh beats max by >= 10 points on the paired set.
#   FALSIFIED   if the paired xhigh-minus-max difference is <= 0.
#   POWER       n=8 paired. Detects a large effort effect only. Between-cell spread is the dominant
#               uncertainty: the two existing max cells disagree by 26 points (-25.03% vs +1.35%).
#   LOAD        16 concurrent sessions. Above this project's ~8-way guidance; load pressure is a
#               known sign-flipper, but it applies to BOTH arms and run_paired alternates arm order.
#               Flag it in the writeup.
set -uo pipefail
S=$HOME/pe1/graphmark/agentic-swebench; cd "$S"

python3 - <<'PY'
import json,os
S=os.path.expanduser("~/pe1/graphmark/agentic-swebench")
src=json.load(open(f"{S}/tasks/rep50.json"))["instances"]
pick=src[::6][:8]                      # systematic, not outcome-selected
json.dump({"instances":pick}, open(f"{S}/tasks/xvm.json","w"), indent=1)
print(f"drawn {len(pick)}:")
for i in pick: print("   ", i["instance_id"][:62])
PY
N=8

for EFF in xhigh max; do
  [ -f "tools/run_xvm_$EFF.sh" ] || { echo "FATAL: missing tools/run_xvm_$EFF.sh"; exit 1; }
  grep -q "^export CC_EFFORT=$EFF" "tools/run_xvm_$EFF.sh" || { echo "FATAL effort $EFF"; exit 1; }
done
echo "preflight: def-timeout=$(grep -c EG_DEF_TIMEOUT tools/eg-q) true-span=$(grep -c _true_end tools/eg-q) ledger=$(grep -c 'ONCE PER DISTINCT ANSWER' tools/postedit_hook.sh)"
echo "binary: $(grep -o 'entire-graph-[a-z]*' tools/run_xvm_max.sh | head -1)"

rm -rf /tmp/xvm2; mkdir -p /tmp/xvm2; : > /tmp/xvm2/progress.txt
unset PKG_ISO
for EFF in xhigh max; do
  for SH in $(seq 0 $((N-1))); do
    setsid nohup env TAG="XVM${EFF}" CONFIG="tools/run_xvm_${EFF}.sh" \
      TASKS_FILE="$S/tasks/xvm.json" NSHARD=$N SHARD=$SH \
      bash "$S/tools/run_paired.sh" > "/tmp/xvm2/${EFF}.s${SH}.log" 2>&1 < /dev/null &
  done
done
date +%s > /tmp/xvm2/t0
echo "launched $(date +%H:%M:%S): 2 efforts x $N shards = $((2*N)) parallel pairs = $((4*N)) sessions"

sleep 75
echo "--- 75s smoke ---"
echo "  live claude sessions : $(pgrep -c -f 'claude -p' || echo 0)"
echo "  run_paired procs     : $(pgrep -c -f run_paired || echo 0)"
echo "  load                 : $(uptime | sed 's/.*load average: //')"
echo "  result dirs so far   : xhigh_eg=$(ls results/XVMxhigh_r1_eg/eg 2>/dev/null|wc -l) xhigh_base=$(ls results/XVMxhigh_r1_baseline/baseline 2>/dev/null|wc -l) max_eg=$(ls results/XVMmax_r1_eg/eg 2>/dev/null|wc -l) max_base=$(ls results/XVMmax_r1_baseline/baseline 2>/dev/null|wc -l)"
echo "  --- head of one shard log ---"
head -12 /tmp/xvm2/xhigh.s0.log
echo "  --- any aborts? ---"
grep -l "FATAL\|clamp\|wt fail" /tmp/xvm2/*.log 2>/dev/null | head -3 || echo "  none"

python3 - <<'PY'
import json,os
S=os.path.expanduser("~/pe1/graphmark/agentic-swebench")
src=json.load(open(f"{S}/tasks/rep50.json"))["instances"]
pick=src[::6][:8]                      # systematic, not outcome-selected

PY
N=8

for EFF in xhigh max; do

unset PKG_ISO
for EFF in xhigh max; do

**XVM: xhigh vs max, paired on the same 8 instances, both arms, on the fixed stack.** Systematic sample (every 6th of rep50) so the draw isn't outcome-selected. Pre-registered before launch: *xhigh beats max by ≥10 points; falsified if the paired difference is ≤0.* ETA ~20:00–20:10.

| `def` fixed 41-line window | pre-fix 85 lines, answer **absent**; post-fix 191 lines, answer present. Hid the edited line on **6/24** calls |

I burned three launch attempts on my own bugs — calling `run_3arm.sh` directly so `CONFIG` was never sourced, then losing `PATH` under `setsid`, then dropping the credential with an `env` wrapper. The first two I had already hit earlier today and failed to carry forward.

Progress is normal (0/16 shards, 18 live), but the dir counts expose a flaw in my launch I should flag now rather than at scoring time: **xhigh eg=8, base=0; max eg=8, base=0** — every shard is running its **eg arm first**.

With `NSHARD=8` each shard holds one instance, so `run_paired`'s alternation index is always 0 and the "even idx: eg first" rule never flips. That means eg sessions run under 16-way concurrent load and baseline sessions will run later under lighter load — and load pressure is a documented sign-flipper on this benchmark.

The saving grace: **the same ordering bias applies identically to both efforts**, so the xhigh-vs-max contrast — the actual hypothesis — is protected. What's compromised is the absolute eg-vs-baseline delta *within* each effort, biased against eg. I'll report both with that caveat attached rather than quietly.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""XVM scorer: xhigh vs max, PAIRED on the same 8 instances, both arms, fixed stack.

PRIMARY  = the paired xhigh-minus-max difference in eg-vs-baseline saving, on instances gated in
           BOTH efforts. Protected against the arm-order flaw below, because the flaw is identical
           in both efforts.
SECONDARY= the absolute eg-vs-baseline saving per effort. BIASED AGAINST EG: with NSHARD=8 every
           shard held one instance, so run_paired's alternation index was always 0 and every shard
           ran its eg arm FIRST, under 16-way load, while baselines ran later under lighter load.
           Report it, do not headline it.
"""
import json, os, math, random, statistics

S = os.path.expanduser("~/pe1/graphmark/agentic-swebench")
random.seed(11)

def toks(cc):
    mu = cc.get("modelUsage") or {}
    if mu:
        t = sum((m.get(k,0) or 0) for m in mu.values() for k in

#!/bin/bash
# Is SW_fable_max (n=19, +18.00%) FAIR? Every withdrawn headline on this benchmark came from
# arm-asymmetric PROMPTS, not from the tool. Diff the two arms' delivered prompts and account for
# every differing line. Compare against REP50 (n=49, +1.35%) as the known-fair control.
set -uo pipefail
W=$HOME/work/graphmark/agentic-swebench

check () {
  TAG=$1
  echo "################ $TAG"
  eg=$(ls -d $W/results/${TAG}_r1_eg/eg/*/ 2>/dev/null | head -1)
  bl=$(ls -d $W/results/${TAG}_r1_baseline/baseline/*/ 2>/dev/null | head -1)
  [ -n "$eg" ] && [ -n "$bl" ] || { echo "  missing arms"; return; }
  # prefer the same instance in both arms
  i=$(basename "$eg")
  [ -d "$W/results/${TAG}_r1_baseline/baseline/$i" ] && bl="$W/results/${TAG}_r1_baseline/baseline/$i/"
  echo "  instance: $(basename $eg)"
  echo "  eg prompt   : $(wc -lc < ${eg}prompt.txt 2>/dev/null | tr -s ' ')"
  echo "  base prompt : $(wc -lc < ${bl}prompt.txt 2>/dev/null | tr -s ' ')"
  echo "  --- lines ONLY in the eg prompt (the fairness surface) ---"
  diff <(sed 's/[[:space:]]*$//' "${bl}prompt.txt" 2>/dev/null) \
       <(sed 's/[[:space:]]*$//' "${eg}prompt.txt" 2>/dev/null) \
    | grep '^>' | sed 's/^> /    /' | head -40
  n=$(diff <(cat "${bl}prompt.txt" 2>/dev/null) <(cat "${eg}prompt.txt" 2>/dev/null) | grep -c '^>')
  echo "  eg-only lines: $n"
  echo "  --- lines ONLY in the BASELINE prompt ---"
  diff <(cat "${bl}prompt.txt" 2>/dev/null) <(cat "${eg}prompt.txt" 2>/dev/null) \
    | grep '^<' | sed 's/^< /    /' | head -10
  echo "  --- clamp scan on the DELIVERED eg prompt ---"
  grep -Eni 'as few turns|fewest|minimi[sz]e (turns|calls|tokens)|do not (read|grep|search)|never (read|grep|search|write)|STOP the moment|budget' \
    "${eg}prompt.txt" 2>/dev/null | head -8 || echo "    (none)"
  echo "  --- same on BASELINE (if these match, the clamp is SHARED = fair) ---"
  grep -Eni 'as few turns|fewest|minimi[sz]e (turns|calls|tokens)|do not (read|grep|search)|never (read|grep|search|write)|STOP the moment|budget' \
    "${bl}prompt.txt" 2>/dev/null | head -8 || echo "    (none)"
  echo "  --- shared-block digests, if recorded ---"
  for f in shared_block.sha256 tool_block.sha256; do
    a=$(cat "${eg}$f" 2>/dev/null); b=$(cat "${bl}$f" 2>/dev/null)
    [ -n "$a$b" ] && echo "    $f  eg=${a:0:12} base=${b:0:12} $([ "$a" = "$b" ] && echo SAME || echo DIFFER)"
  done
  echo
}
check SW_fable_max
check REP50
echo "################ config that produced SW_fable_max"
sed -n '1,40p' $W/tools/run_SW_fable_max.sh 2>/dev/null | grep -E '^export|^#' | head -25

REP50 is **fair** — clean audit. The 14 eg-only lines are the checkout path (differs by arm by construction) plus the capability block that names what the verbs *return*. **Clamp scan: none on either arm.** So +1.35% is an honest number.

But the `SW_fable_max` config header is the real find:

```
O35_VERIFY_ONLY    1 -> 0   inject the FULL payload instead of one line
EG_PREFETCH_IMPACT 0 -> 1   callers/callees/siblings
EG_PREFETCH_TEST   0 -> 1   covering-test bodies -- NEVER ENABLED IN ANY CELL
EG_LITERALS        0 -> 1   SAME-CONCEPT LITERAL sweep
EG_SIBLINGS        0 -> 1
FAIRNESS: ANTI_HARNESS = '' -- the generic methodology clamp is GONE
```

**The best credible cell on disk delivers the full graph payload prefetched at session start — zero turns — and it's the only cell where eg runs *fewer* turns than baseline (−2.1).** REP50, the cell I've spent all day optimising, has `EG_PREFETCH=0`. So does `run_pe2.sh`, where I explicitly turned it off.

Correcting myself — I read the config header as if it described the run. **It doesn't.** The actual flags are identical:

```
FLAG                  SW_fable_max   run_REP50   run_pe2
EG_PREFETCH                      0           0         0
EG_PREFETCH_IMPACT               1           1     unset
EG_PREFETCH_TEST                 1           1     unset
O35_VERIFY_ONLY                  0           0     unset
O35_STRIP_ADVICE                 1           1         1
CC_EFFORT                      max         max       max
CC_MODEL                     fable        opus      opus   <-- the only difference
```

No `prefetch.payload` files exist in either cell, so prefetch never ran in either. The header I quoted was design intent from an earlier revision, not what executed. **The sole difference between the +18.00% cell and the +1.35% cell is the model.**

And I'm going to stop short of claiming "Fable is the answer," because the same disk holds **two opus-max cells that disagree by 26 points** (+1.35% vs −25.03%). Between-cell noise is at least as large as the model effect I'd be asserting. That's the fourth time today I've had a clean story dissolve under one more check, so I'm holding this one at "lead, not finding."

**What survives all the checks:**

| finding | strength |
|---|---|
| `dturns` is monotone with saving across all **12 independent cells** — every cell where eg ran ≤ baseline turns cleared +18%, every cell at +4 or more lost | cross-cell, escapes the within-cell tautology |
| REP50 is **fair** — clamp scan clean on both arms, eg-only lines are paths + capability text | verified today |
| Three real tool bugs fixed and proven (def window, def timeout, hook ledger) | before/after tested |
| The rider was **never tested** — 19% dose, null CI | withdrawn, not refuted |

XVM is at 5 of 16 baselines with 18 sessions live — it's the only properly **paired within-cell** effort comparison in the estate, so it's the one number today that won't dissolve. I'll hold further speculation until it lands.
