name: substitution-rate-is-015
description: "A graph call removes 0.40 searches but costs 2.72 calls — substitution rate 0.15, needs >1.0 to break even. 25% requires displacing 25% of the 33-call locate pool: a 15x shortfall."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: b0108f24-43a4-413e-94c9-bd361b6fafc5
  modified: 2026-08-10T07:35:53.571Z
---

Measured 2026-08-10 on REP50X — 100 fresh transcripts, both arms, repaired harness, the
representative draw. This is the number that explains why entire-graph landed at **+2.89%**.

```
                     eg/sess   base/sess    delta
  graph                2.72        0.00     +2.72   <- what the tool COSTS
  search              19.08       19.48     -0.40   <- what the tool REMOVES
  read                13.86       14.00     -0.14
  build                7.50        8.12     -0.62
  scratch              1.74        2.22     -0.48
  TOTAL               54.60       53.86     +0.74   <- eg spends MORE than baseline
```

**Substitution rate = 0.40 / 2.72 = 0.15.** It must exceed 1.0 to break even. The agent calls the
graph ~2.5 times pre-edit and then greps **12.7 more times** before it edits anything. Being told
where the code is does not stop it looking.

## The target, as arithmetic

Elasticity 1.784 ⇒ 25% tokens needs ≈ **−7.6 calls/session**. eg is at **+0.74**. Required swing
**−8.3 calls/session**. The only pool big enough:

```
search 19.08 + read 13.86 = 32.94 calls/session = 60% of the session
must displace 8.3  = 25% of the pool
now displacing 0.54 = 1.6% of the pool      -> 15x shortfall
a session is 7.8x the 7-call find->edit->verify ideal (54.6 calls)
```

## Why the obvious fix is already dead

- eleven payload-quality metrics measured null
- **enrichment RAISED grep counts** ([[eg-usage-is-invariant]])
- more graph calls correlate with *worse* results, corr −0.166 ([[usage-is-not-the-lever]])

So the shortfall is not "ship a bigger payload". The unsolved problem is making the agent **stop
searching once it has the answer**.

## CORRECTED: 35% of the session is environment work, and it is symmetric

The "redundant verification pool" below was **retracted the same night**. The classifier counted any
shell command containing `find`/`grep`/`ls` as a *search*, which lumped in build-environment
construction (hunting the JDK, listing `.ivy2`, hand-rolling `javac`, writing `/tmp` build scripts).
Query shapes: 63.2% complex shell expressions, **0% bare identifiers** — the agent barely greps for
symbols at all. The nulls were sound; the interpretation was wrong.

Reclassified by what commands actually do:

```
eg 54.6 calls/session               baseline 53.9    delta
  read            10.56  (19%)        11.30         -0.74
  scratch_build   10.26  (19%)        10.32         -0.06   <- throwaway build scripts
  locate_symbol    9.24  (17%)         9.98         -0.74
  edit             6.16                5.98         +0.18
  build_run        4.56                4.28         +0.28
  env_toolchain    4.44                4.82         -0.38
  locate_file      3.06                3.24         -0.18
  graph            2.72                0.00         +2.72
                                              TOTAL +0.74

environment/build:  eg 19.26  base 19.42  delta -0.16  = 35% of the session, SYMMETRIC
code location+read: eg 22.86  base 24.52
```

**Corrected target:** the graph displaces 1.66 calls and costs 2.72. To net −8.3 it must displace
~11 gross calls from the 22.86-call locate+read pool = **48% of it; it currently displaces 7%.** A
**7×** improvement, against a pool that is big enough — but only 65% of the session is even in play.

**Method lesson:** a metric can pass a shuffled null and a query-echo null and still measure the
wrong thing. Always print the raw commands before believing a category count.

## Retracted analysis (kept as a worked example)

Of the 18.2 searches issued *after* the graph answered, the share aimed at something the graph
already provided, with two nulls applied:

```
                                 OWN      SHUFFLED null        excess       p
raw       searches              76.8%   24.7% [19.3,30.2]   +52.1pt    0.000
          reads                 68.9%    0.3% [0.0, 2.0]    +68.6pt    0.000
graph-CONTRIBUTED only:
          searches              50.9%   17.8% [12.8,23.1]   +33.2pt  <0.0001
          reads                 56.6%    0.3% [0.0, 2.0]    +56.3pt  <0.0001

chance-corrected pool = 6.02 searches + 2.35 reads = 8.37 calls/session
requirement for 25%   = 8.3 calls/session
```

Null 1 (shuffled payload) was necessary because a 7.5KB payload holds ~170 identifiers, so common
code words collide by chance. Null 2 (contributed-only = payload minus problem-statement minus
query) was necessary because the payload echoes the query, so raw overlap could merely prove "both
are about the same task". **Both passed.**

**Read the margin, not the headline: 8.37 available vs 8.3 needed means 25% requires capturing
~100% of the redundancy.** Capture half → ~12–13%. And that the pool is *removable at all* is
untested — the agent may re-search for legitimate reasons (line context, call sites, confirmation),
and every pool this project has previously located proved symmetric or uncapturable
([[harness-pool-is-symmetric]], [[postedit-ceiling-15pct]]).

**How to apply:** judge any future graph change by substitution rate — searches+reads removed per
graph call — measured on both arms of a fresh draw. Below 1.0 it cannot pay for itself however good
the payload looks. Report it beside any savings claim.
Related: [[r50fix-headline-was-in-sample]], [[session-length-is-the-mechanism]],
[[usage-is-not-the-lever]], [[eg-usage-is-invariant]].

## Done. The goal is not met, and I can now show that from every angle without building anything.

**REP50X, the benchmark the goal is defined on: +2.89%, n=48, CI [−15.1, +18.4].** Pre-registered, both criteria refuted, published with shas. The +16.10% is withdrawn as in-sample.

I kept going past that at **$0** and closed the question properly:

```
today                              eg 54.60 calls/sess   -2.5% model / +2.89% observed
call-sites component alone (42.6%) eg 49.36             +14.4%
full composed answer (H1b 59.6%)   eg 47.27             +20.8%   <- best buildable route
oracle: perfect locate displacement eg 42.30             +35.0%
25% TARGET                         eg 45.84             +25.0%   <- 1.43 calls/sess beyond best route
```

**25% is inside the oracle and outside every route that can actually be built.** H1b — the one variant never tested — reached 59.6% addressability against its 60% bar, failing by 0.4 points and landing at ~21%.

**The one positive result, and it's worth acting on:** 42.6% of all greps are the agent re-searching a symbol it already found, wanting its **call sites**. `callers` and `impact` already exist as `eg-q` verbs and are **not in the default payload**. Estimated **+14.4%** alone — the largest single lever this campaign has measured. It needs testing, not shipping: enrichment has raised grep counts before, and the estimate assumes zero-cost replacement.

**Also settled:** 35% of every session is environment/build construction — `scratch_build` 10.26 vs 10.32 across arms, delta −0.06. Identical in both arms, and no retrieval tool will ever touch it. That's the real ceiling on this whole approach.

**Two of my own findings retracted tonight** after adversarial checks: the 8.37-call "redundant verification pool" (my classifier counted hand-rolled `javac` as *search*), and my claim that the grep shim capped at 38.9% (it caps at **+8.6%** — 38.9% was the addressable fraction, not the saving). Both would have sent you down dead routes.

**Spend:** $362 tonight. Lifetime 33.4M tokens saved, +8.10%, $817.

Everything is in `TokensNotes.md` (§1.2c, §3.0 H1b, §3.4 closed, §1.4 struck, §5 with five new silent-failure modes), `OVERNIGHT-2026-08-10.md`, and five memories. Machine idle, `/tmp` purged, all shas sealed.

I'm stopping here — not because the goal is met, but because it isn't, and the remaining step is building the call-sites payload and revalidating it, which shouldn't happen unattended against the one benchmark that still has integrity. That's the decision waiting for you.

content.text:
I'll stop the build here, and for a much stronger reason than caution — **the arithmetic says it cannot meet the goal even if implemented perfectly.**

H1b measured the composed answer's ceiling at 59.6% addressability → **+20.8%**. The goal is 25%. So a flawless implementation of the best remaining route still lands **1.43 calls/session short**. Building it unattended tonight could not have met the goal; it would only have produced a better tool and an unmet target.

Reading `eg-q` also showed the payload-composition space is already heavily searched — the script carries a graveyard of measured variants (`EG_SNIPPET`, `EG_NO_SNIPCAP`, `EG_BODY_HEAD_RANKS`, `EG_CTX_LINES`, and `EG_TOPK=20 + EG_HEAD_WINDOW=60` recorded as an outright regression). One comment in there independently explains my `def_body` result: *"80% of the reads that re-open an already-printed body want lines OUTSIDE it (median gap 42 lines)."* Bodies are already shipped; the agent needs the neighbours.

## Final answer

**The goal is not met. REP50X = +2.89%, n=48, CI [−15.1, +18.4]**, pre-registered, both criteria refuted, published with shas. And 25% is not reachable by anything buildable:

```
today                                +2.89%  (observed)
call-sites inline (42.6% of greps)   +14.4%  <- best single available improvement
full composed answer (H1b 59.6%)     +20.8%  <- ceiling of the best route
25% TARGET                           +25.0%  <- 1.43 calls/sess beyond that ceiling
oracle: all locating displaced        +35.0%  <- requires 100% displacement, not achievable
```

Three things I established tonight that hold regardless:

1. **The +16.10% was in-sample.** eg's turns didn't change (56.3 → 54.0); the *baseline's* fell (62.2 → 52.9). The headline was a flailing baseline, not a good tool.
2. **35% of every session is environment/build construction**, `scratch_build` 10.26 vs 10.32 across arms — delta −0.06. No retrieval tool will ever touch it. That's the structural ceiling.
3. **The best real improvement available is inlining call sites**, worth an estimated +14.4%, because 42.6% of greps are the agent re-searching a symbol it already found. The `callers` verb exists and the payload merely *advertises* it, costing a second call the agent won't make.

I retracted two of my own findings tonight after adversarial checks — the 8.37-call "redundant pool" (my classifier counted hand-rolled `javac` as search) and my misreading of the grep shim as a 38.9% ceiling when it's **+8.6%**.

**Spend:** $362. Lifetime 33.4M tokens saved, +8.10%, $817. Machine idle, `/tmp` purged, everything sealed in `TokensNotes.md` (§1.2c, §3.0, §3.4, §5) and five memories.

The goal as specified is out of reach of the tool. What's in reach is +14.4% from one specific change, and that's the decision I'm leaving you: build call-sites-inline and validate it, or move the graph's value case off token savings.

content.text:
One assumption in that conclusion doesn't survive scrutiny, and it's the load-bearing one.

My "+20.8%, short by 1.43 calls" comes from a **call-count elasticity model** — and tonight that model demonstrably mispredicted *this very cell*: it predicted **−2.46%** while the measured result was **+2.89%**, an error of **+5.35pt in the favourable direction**. Because eg's calls are individually cheaper than the greps/reads they replace, token savings aren't a pure function of call count. Apply that same residual and the composed answer lands near **26%** — above the target.

So the conclusion rests on a model I know is biased low here. Measuring the actual marginal token cost per call type instead:

input.content:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""The elasticity model mispredicted this cell by +5.35pt, so "calls" is the wrong unit.
Fit per-CATEGORY marginal token cost across all 96 sessions (both arms pooled), then price the
H1b intervention directly instead of through a call-count proxy."""
import json, glob, os, re, collections, statistics
S = os.path.expanduser("~/pe1/graphmark/agentic-swebench")
CELL = "REP50X"

ENVJ = re.compile(r'(/usr/lib/jvm|\.ivy2|\.m2|\.gradle|\.cargo/registry|javac|-classpath|-cp |\.jar\b|jdk|CLASSPATH)', re.I)
BUILDRUN = re.compile(r'\b(mvn|gradlew?|cargo|go test|go build|npm|yarn|pnpm|pytest|tox|make|cmake|ctest|composer|bundle|rake|phpunit|jest|mocha|dotnet|ant)\b')
SCRATCH = re.compile(r'(>\s*/tmp/|cat\s*>\s*/tmp|mkdir\s+-p\s+/tmp|/tmp/\w+/)')
SYMLOOK = re.compile(r'\b(grep|rg|ag|ack)\b')
FILELOOK = re.compile(r'\b(find|fd)\b')
LISTDIR = re.compile(r'^\s*(ls|tree)\b')
CATS = ["graph", "locate", "read", "edit", "envbuild", "git", "other"]

def classify(nm, inp):
    if nm == "Grep": return "locate"
    if nm == "Glob": return "locate"
    if nm == "Read": return "read"
    if nm in ("Edit", "MultiEdit", "NotebookEdit"): return "edit"
    if nm == "Write":
        p = (inp or {}).get("file_path", "") or ""
        return "envbuild" if ("/tmp" in p or "scratch" in p) else "edit"
    if nm != "Bash": return "other"
    c = (inp or {}).get("command", "") or ""
    if re.search(r'(entire[- ]graph|eg-q)', c): return "graph"
    if ENVJ.search(c) or SCRATCH.search(c) or BUILDRUN.search(c): return "envbuild"
    if FILELOOK.search(c) or LISTDIR.search(c) or SYMLOOK.search(c): return "locate"
    if re.search(r'\bgit\b', c): return "git"
    if re.search(r'\b(cat|head|tail|sed -n)\b', c): return "read"
    return "other"

def toks(cc):
    mu = cc.get("modelUsage") or {}
    if mu:
        t = sum((m.get(k, 0) or 0) for m in mu.values() for k in
                ("inputTokens", "outputTokens", "cacheReadInputTokens", "cacheCreationInputTokens"))
        if t: return t
    u = cc.get("usage") or {}
    return sum(u.get(k, 0) or 0 for k in ("input_tokens", "output_tokens", "cache_read_input_tokens", "cache_creation_input_tokens"))

rows = []   # (counts vector, tokens)
for arm in ("eg", "baseline"):
    base = f"{S}/results/{CELL}_r1_{arm}/{arm}"
    for iid in sorted(os.listdir(base)) if os.path.isdir(base) else []:
        cc = f"{base}/{iid}/cc_out.json"
        pf = f"{base}/{iid}/patch.diff"
        if not (os.path.exists(cc) and os.path.getsize(cc) > 1): continue
        try: j = json.load(open(cc))
        except Exception: continue
        if j.get("subtype") != "success" or not (os.path.exists(pf) and os.path.getsize(pf) > 0): continue
        slug = iid.replace("_", "-").lower()
        tf = None
        for d in glob.glob(f"{S}/results/{CELL}_r1_{arm}/ccfg/projects/*/"):
            if os.path.basename(d.rstrip("/")).lower().endswith(slug):
                js = glob.glob(d + "*.jsonl")
                if js: tf = max(js, key=os.path.getsize); break
        if not tf: continue
        cnt = collections.Counter()
        for line in open(tf, errors="ignore"):
            line = line.strip()
            if not line: continue
            try: e = json.loads(line)
            except Exception: continue
            if e.get("type") != "assistant": continue
            for c in ((e.get("message") or {}).get("content") or []):
                if isinstance(c, dict) and c.get("type") == "tool_use":
                    cnt[classify(c.get("name", ""), c.get("input") or {})] += 1
        if sum(cnt.values()) == 0: continue
        rows.append(([cnt[k] for k in CATS], toks(j), arm))

print(f"{CELL}: marginal token cost per call category  (n={len(rows)} gated sessions, both arms)")
if len(rows) < 20:
    print("  too few rows"); raise SystemExit

# ordinary least squares with intercept, solved via normal equations (pure python)
import itertools
X = [[1.0] + [float(v) for v in r[0]] for r in rows]
y = [float(r[1]) for r in rows]
p = len(X[0])
A = [[sum(X[i][a]*X[i][b] for i in range(len(X))) for b in range(p)] for a in range(p)]
bv = [sum(X[i][a]*y[i] for i in range(len(X))) for a in range(p)]
# gaussian elimination
M = [A[i][:] + [bv[i]] for i in range(p)]
for c in range(p):
    piv = max(range(c, p), key=lambda r: abs(M[r][c]))
    M[c], M[piv] = M[piv], M[c]
    if abs(M[c][c]) < 1e-9: continue
    for r in range(p):
        if r == c: continue
        f = M[r][c]/M[c][c]
        for k in range(c, p+1): M[r][k] -= f*M[c][k]
coef = [M[i][p]/M[i][i] if abs(M[i][i]) > 1e-9 else 0.0 for i in range(p)]
names = ["intercept"] + CATS
print()
for n_, c_ in zip(names, coef):
    print(f"    {n_:<12}{c_:>14,.0f} tokens per call")

yhat = [sum(X[i][k]*coef[k] for k in range(p)) for i in range(len(X))]
ybar = statistics.mean(y)
r2 = 1 - sum((y[i]-yhat[i])**2 for i in range(len(y)))/sum((v-ybar)**2 for v in y)
print(f"\n    R^2 = {r2:.3f}")

egr = [r for r in rows if r[2] == "eg"]; br = [r for r in rows if r[2] == "baseline"]
te = sum(r[1] for r in egr); tb = sum(r[1] for r in br)
print(f"    observed pooled saving on these rows: {100*(1-te/tb):+.2f}%")

c_loc = coef[1+CATS.index("locate")]; c_rd = coef[1+CATS.index("read")]; c_g = coef[1+CATS.index("graph")]
print(f"\n  PRICING THE H1b INTERVENTION DIRECTLY")
print(f"    marginal cost: locate {c_loc:,.0f}  read {c_rd:,.0f}  graph {c_g:,.0f} tokens/call")

CELL = "REP50X"

ENVJ = re.compile(r'(/usr/lib/jvm|\.ivy2|\.m2|\.gradle|\.cargo/registry|javac|-classpath|-cp |\.jar\b|jdk|CLASSPATH)', re.I)

SCRATCH = re.compile(r'(>\s*/tmp/|cat\s*>\s*/tmp|mkdir\s+-p\s+/tmp|/tmp/\w+/)')
SYMLOOK = re.compile(r'\b(grep|rg|ag|ack)\b')
FILELOOK = re.compile(r'\b(find|fd)\b')
LISTDIR = re.compile(r'^\s*(ls|tree)\b')
CATS = ["graph", "locate", "read", "edit", "envbuild", "git", "other"]

def classify(nm, inp):
    if nm == "Grep": return "locate"
    if nm == "Glob": return "locate"
    if nm == "Read": return "read"
    if nm in ("Edit", "MultiEdit", "NotebookEdit"): return "edit"
    if nm == "Write":
        p = (inp or {}).get("file_path", "") or ""
        return "envbuild" if ("/tmp" in p or "scratch" in p) else "edit"
    if nm != "Bash": return "other"
    c = (inp or {}).get("command", "") or ""
    if re.search(r'(entire[- ]graph|eg-q)', c): return "graph"
    if ENVJ.search(c) or SCRATCH.search(c) or BUILDRUN.search(c): return "envbuild"
    if FILELOOK.search(c) or LISTDIR.search(c) or SYMLOOK.search(c): return "locate"
    if re.search(r'\bgit\b', c): return "git"
    if re.search(r'\b(cat|head|tail|sed -n)\b', c): return "read"
    return "other"

    mu = cc.get("modelUsage") or {}
    if mu:
        t = sum((m.get(k, 0) or 0) for m in mu.values() for k in
                ("inputTokens", "outputTokens", "cacheReadInputTokens", "cacheCreationInputTokens"))

    u = cc.get("usage") or {}
    return sum(u.get(k, 0) or 0 for k in ("input_tokens", "output_tokens", "cache_read_input_tokens", "cache_creation_input_tokens"))

        if j.get("subtype") != "success" or not (os.path.exists(pf) and os.path.getsize(pf) > 0): continue
        slug = iid.replace("_", "-").lower()
        tf = None
        for d in glob.glob(f"{S}/results/{CELL}_r1_{arm}/ccfg/projects/*/"):

That attempt failed, and I'm reporting it as a failure rather than a result.

```
intercept   -2,008,960 tokens   <- nonsense
graph          -25,233 tokens/call   <- negative
locate          41,853
read            95,617
R^2 = 0.863
observed pooled saving on these rows: -14.90%   <- but REP50X is +2.89%
```

Two independent tells. The intercept and the `graph` coefficient are **negative**, which is my own script's collinearity warning firing — per-category token pricing is **not identifiable** from 92 sessions. And the sanity check disagrees with the known cell result (−14.90% vs +2.89%), because I selected each arm's passing sessions *independently* instead of paired, so the totals compare different instance sets. The projection built on that (−3.58%) is garbage.

## Corrected final position

I withdraw the false precision on both sides of my earlier claim.

- **What is measured and solid:** REP50X = **+2.89%**, n=48, CI [−15.1, +18.4]. Goal not met. The +16.10% was in-sample — eg's turns unchanged (56.3 → 54.0), the baseline's fell (62.2 → 52.9). 35% of every session is environment/build work, symmetric across arms (delta −0.06), untouchable by retrieval. 42.6% of greps are the agent re-searching a symbol it already found, wanting call sites the payload only *advertises*.
- **What I over-claimed:** that the composed answer tops out at +20.8% and is therefore "1.43 calls short". That figure comes from an elasticity model whose residual on this very cell is **+5.35pt** (predicted −2.46%, observed +2.89%). So the honest range for the composed answer is roughly **+21% to +26%** — **25% sits at the edge of the error bars, not clearly outside them.** My "out of reach of the tool" statement was too strong, and my attempt to replace the model with something better just now was not identifiable.

So the truthful answer to whether 25% is reachable is: **not known, and not knowable by more analysis.** The single change worth making — inlining call sites — sits precisely where the uncertainty lives, and only building and measuring it settles the question.

**Tonight:** goal not met at +2.89%. $362 spent; lifetime 33.4M tokens saved, +8.10%, $817. Two of my findings retracted after adversarial checks, plus this third failed measurement. Eight harness fixes verified firing 100/100. REP50X refutation sealed and published in `TokensNotes.md` and `OVERNIGHT-2026-08-10.md` with shas, five memories written, machine idle and clean.

I've stopped generating analysis because the next honest step is a build-and-measure cycle, and I've now demonstrated three times tonight that pushing past the data's resolution produces retractions rather than progress.

content.text:
Validation caught a real bug — and this is exactly why it runs before a cell. The top hit was `symbol=Handler.reverseProxy`, but my regex `[A-Za-z0-9_]*` stopped at the dot and looked up **`Handler`** — a hopelessly generic name — returning 13 unrelated `Handler` definitions for **+2308 bytes of noise**. Shipping that would have been textbook enrichment-backfire.

Fixing the symbol extraction to capture dotted names:

input.command:
gcloud compute ssh graphbench-c --zone us-east1-b --tunnel-through-iap --command 'S=$HOME/pe1/graphmark/agentic-swebench
cat > /tmp/eg-q-cs <<'"'"'EOF'"'"'
#!/bin/bash
# eg-q-cs — eg-q with CALL SITES inlined on the top search/grep hit.
# Composition only; eg-q itself is unmodified. Targets the measured 42.6% of greps that are the
# agent re-searching a symbol it already found, wanting usages.
set -uo pipefail
EGQ="${EGQ_REAL:-$(dirname "$0")/eg-q}"
verb="${1:-}"; [ $# -gt 0 ] && shift
out="$("$EGQ" "$verb" "$@" 2>&1)"; rc=$?
printf "%s\n" "$out"
case "$verb" in
  search|grep)
    # capture DOTTED symbols whole: Handler.reverseProxy, not Handler
    sym="$(printf "%s\n" "$out" | grep -m1 -oE "symbol=[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_.]*" | head -1 | cut -d= -f2)"
    # a bare generic name is useless to look up; require either a dot or >=8 chars
    if [ -n "${sym:-}" ] && { case "$sym" in *.*) true;; *) [ ${#sym} -ge 8 ];; esac; }; then
      cs="$("$EGQ" callers "$sym" 2>/dev/null)"
      # reject the degrade path: a definitions listing is NOT call sites
      if [ -n "${cs:-}" ] && ! printf "%s" "$cs" | grep -qiE "matches [0-9]+ definitions|no .*caller|\(0 non-test"; then
        echo "---"
        echo "CALL SITES for $sym — inlined, no second lookup needed:"
        printf "%s\n" "$cs"
      fi
    fi ;;
esac
exit $rc
EOF
chmod +x /tmp/eg-q-cs; bash -n /tmp/eg-q-cs && echo "  syntax OK"

export EG=$HOME/pe-bin/entire-graph-fixed EGI=$EG

Q="reverse proxy sets upstream header incorrectly"

b=$(/tmp/eg-q-cs search "$Q" 2>&1)
na=$(printf %s "$a" | wc -c); nb=$(printf %s "$b" | wc -c)
echo "  plain $na B   wrapper $nb B   delta $((nb-na)) B"
echo "  extracted symbol: $(printf "%s\n" "$a" | grep -m1 -oE "symbol=[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_.]*" | cut -d= -f2)"

#!/bin/bash
# eg-q — CALL SITES variant. Delegates to eg-q.orig (byte-identical original) and, for
# search/grep, appends the top hit symbol's call sites so the agent needs no second lookup.
#
# Rationale (measured on REP50X, 564 real greps, 49 instances): 42.6% of all greps are the agent
# re-searching a symbol it already found, wanting its usages. The `callers` verb already existed
# but the payload only ADVERTISED it, costing a second call the agent does not make.
# Validated offline on Go/Ruby/PHP: correct dotted-symbol extraction, real call sites,
# +944 B (caddy) / +1797 B (jekyll) / +2631 B (laravel).
#
# Tool-output change only — no prompt text, so arm symmetry is unaffected.
# REVERT: mv tools/eg-q.orig tools/eg-q
set -uo pipefail
EGQ="${EGQ_REAL:-$(dirname "$0")/eg-q.orig}"
verb="${1:-}"; [ $# -gt 0 ] && shift
out="$("$EGQ" "$verb" "$@" 2>&1)"; rc=$?
printf "%s\n" "$out"
case "$verb" in
  search|grep)
    # dotted symbols must be captured WHOLE: Handler.reverseProxy, not Handler.
    # A bare generic name is useless to look up (measured: "Handler" returned 13 unrelated
    # definitions for +2308 B of noise), so require a dot or >=8 chars.
    sym="$(printf "%s\n" "$out" | grep -m1 -oE "symbol=[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_.]*" | head -1 | cut -d= -f2)"
    if [ -n "${sym:-}" ] && { case "$sym" in *.*) true ;; *) [ ${#sym} -ge 8 ] ;; esac; }; then
      cs="$(timeout "${EG_CS_TIMEOUT:-90}" "$EGQ" callers "$sym" 2>/dev/null)"
      # reject the degrade path: a definitions listing is NOT call sites
      if [ -n "${cs:-}" ] && ! printf "%s" "$cs" | grep -qiE "matches [0-9]+ definitions|no .*caller|\(0 non-test"; then
        echo "---"
        echo "CALL SITES for $sym — inlined, no second lookup needed:"
        printf "%s\n" "$cs"
      fi
    fi
    ;;
esac
exit $rc

content.text:
**I built the thing and it's now measuring.** Status:

```
CS50: 50 instances x 2 arms, 17 shards, 0 aborts, ETA ~10:00, ~$351
intervention verified live: 10 callers / 10 search (1:1), 4/16 transcripts carry CALL SITES
sealed: PREREG-CS50.md 32fbb31adb736552 (0 results) + Amendment 1 6a5664868ffea192
tools/eg-q wrapper 58bdce383c8d5e6c  |  eg-q.orig preserved 84663a4c1511dbf7
```

**What changed my mind about building it:** my reason for refusing was that the composed answer's ceiling (+20.8%) sits below 25% — but that came from an elasticity model whose residual on this very cell is **+5.35pt in the favourable direction**. When I tried to replace the model with per-call-cost regression, it came back unidentifiable (negative intercept, negative `graph` coefficient, and a sanity check that disagreed with the known cell result). So "25% is out of reach" was not something I could actually support, and the only way to settle it is to measure.

**The intervention:** 42.6% of all greps are the agent re-searching a symbol it already found. `callers` existed but was merely *advertised* in the payload, costing a second call the agent doesn't make. Now the top hit's call sites ship inline.

**Offline validation caught two real bugs before spending** — a bare-name extraction that returned 13 unrelated `Handler` definitions for +2308 B of noise, and the definitions-listing degrade path. Both guarded. Then validated on Go/Ruby/PHP: +944/+1797/+2631 B, correct dotted symbols, real callers with source.

**Falsification is binding and sharp:** refuted if pooled ≤ **+2.89%** (it must beat the cell it's improving, same 50 instances), and mechanism-refuted if `locate_symbol` calls/session ≥ **9.24**. If the agent greps just as much, the block changed nothing and any token delta is noise. Enrichment has backfired on this benchmark before — that outcome gets published too.

Also recorded: `eg-q.orig` must be restored when this is done (`mv tools/eg-q.orig tools/eg-q`), announced in `AGENT-COMMS.md` since `tools/` is shared with the memory-bench agent.

Tonight so far: $362 + ~$351 = ~$713. I'll score CS50 against the prereg when it lands and publish either way.

Not stopping. The open question is whether call-sites works with proper coverage — and I can answer it far more cheaply than last time.

**Key design insight:** `locate_symbol` is *arm-internal*. Asking "does the agent grep less when handed call sites?" compares eg-with-callsites against eg-without — **no baseline arm needed.** That halves the cost to ~$175 and makes the endpoint immune to the baseline drift that ruined CS50's attribution.

First, fixing the coverage gap. The `grep` verb emits no `symbol=`, but its *patterns are usually bare identifiers* (`CLIENT_NO_TOUCH`, `touchCommand`):

input.content:
#!/bin/bash
# eg-q — CALL SITES variant v2. Delegates to eg-q.orig and appends the top hit's call sites.
#
# v1 (CS50) covered `search` only: the `grep` verb emits no `symbol=` field, so extraction found
# nothing and delivery reached just 12/50 transcripts (24%). Measured verb mix: 16 grep vs 11 search,
# so the uncovered path was the MORE used one.
#
# v2 adds grep coverage by using the grep PATTERN as the symbol when it is a bare identifier
# (measured: patterns are usually bare identifiers -- CLIENT_NO_TOUCH, touchCommand, NO_TOUCH).
# Patterns containing regex metacharacters are skipped rather than guessed at.
#
# REVERT: mv tools/eg-q.orig tools/eg-q
set -uo pipefail
EGQ="${EGQ_REAL:-$(dirname "$0")/eg-q.orig}"
verb="${1:-}"; arg1="${2:-}"; [ $# -gt 0 ] && shift
out="$("$EGQ" "$verb" "$@" 2>&1)"; rc=$?
printf "%s\n" "$out"

_emit_callsites() {
  local sym="$1"
  [ -n "$sym" ] || return 0
  # a bare generic name is useless (v1 measured: "Handler" -> 13 unrelated defs, +2308 B noise)
  case "$sym" in *.*) : ;; *) [ ${#sym} -ge 8 ] || return 0 ;; esac
  local cs
  cs="$(timeout "${EG_CS_TIMEOUT:-90}" "$EGQ" callers "$sym" 2>/dev/null)" || return 0
  [ -n "$cs" ] || return 0
  # reject the degrade path: a definitions listing is NOT call sites
  printf "%s" "$cs" | grep -qiE "matches [0-9]+ definitions|no .*caller|\(0 non-test" && return 0
  echo "---"
  echo "CALL SITES for $sym — inlined, no second lookup needed:"
  printf "%s\n" "$cs"
}

case "$verb" in
  search)
    # ranked lines carry symbol=Name.method — capture dotted names WHOLE
    _emit_callsites "$(printf "%s\n" "$out" | grep -m1 -oE "symbol=[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_.]*" | head -1 | cut -d= -f2)"
    ;;
  grep)
    # v2: no symbol= in grep output. Use the PATTERN when it is a plain identifier.
    sym=""
    case "$arg1" in
      *[\|\(\)\[\]\*\+\?\^\$\\\ ]*) sym="" ;;                  # regex/multi-token -> skip, do not guess
      [A-Za-z_]*) sym="$arg1" ;;
    esac
    # if the pattern was regex-y, fall back to a symbol= line if eg-q happened to emit one
    [ -z "$sym" ] && sym="$(printf "%s\n" "$out" | grep -m1 -oE "symbol=[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_.]*" | head -1 | cut -d= -f2)"
    _emit_callsites "$sym"
    ;;
esac
exit $rc

  GOAL: pooled >= 25% AND primary passes.

content.text:
Yes — **withdrawn.** It's the fourth headline withdrawn on this benchmark.

**What's withdrawn:** the claim that +16.10% is entire-graph's savings. **What still stands:** it was a correct measurement *of that cell* — R50FIX, n=48, strict gate. It just doesn't generalize, because those 50 instances are the set this entire campaign was tuned against.

The out-of-sample number on a representative draw (45 of 50 instances never used to tune anything, identical harness and config):

```
                       R50FIX (in-sample)   REP50X (representative)
pooled                     +16.10%               +2.89%
median                     +13.32%               +6.60%   CI [-7.0,+20.2] includes 0
eg turns/session             56.3                 54.0
baseline turns/session       62.2                 52.9
delta                        -5.9                 +1.1
```

**The reason it collapsed is the important part: eg didn't change — the baseline did.** eg ran 56.3 → 54.0 turns (essentially identical). The baseline ran 62.2 → **52.9**. Every point of that +16.10% was a baseline that happened to flail on that particular instance set. Give the tool a representative workload where the baseline behaves, and there's nothing left to save.

Pre-registered before the cell ran (`e798c78e38961f7d`), so it wasn't rationalised afterward: predicted +14%, floor +5%, and **+2.89% failed it.** All three tail hypotheses failed too. The harness was audited clean first — graph engaged 2.80 calls/session, `toolchain PATH` and memory-scoping 100/100, gate failures 1 per arm symmetric — so it's a real result about the tool, not a measurement bug.

Published in `TokensNotes.md` §3.4 (with §1.4 struck), `OVERNIGHT-2026-08-10.md`, and memory `r50fix-headline-was-in-sample`.

**The honest number to quote is +2.89%, CI [−15.1, +18.4]** — indistinguishable from zero at n=48. Lifetime across every gated pair ever measured: **53.6M tokens saved, +9.40%, $1,143** of measurement.

CS50B is at 53/100, delivery 36%, ETA ~12:20 — and per its prereg, its pooled number is explicitly *not* claim-bearing unless `locate_symbol` drops below 9.24 first.

content.text:
The partial mechanism check is **inconclusive — and for exactly the reason your staging point implies.**

```
CS50B partial (40 eg sessions)   REP50X (50)    CS50 (50)
locate_symbol   8.38/sess            9.24         10.04    <- looks like a PASS
total calls    45.9/sess            54.60         56.02    <- but sessions are 16% shorter
locate_symbol as a SHARE  18.2%      17.9%        17.9%    <- slightly WORSE, not better
env/build      13.25/sess           19.26        19.20
```

`locate_symbol` at 8.38 appears to clear the 9.24 bar, but **every** category is down because these 40 are the fastest-finishing sessions. As a *share* of the session it's 18.2% vs REP50X's 17.9% — marginally worse. So the apparent pass is completion-order bias, not signal, and it can't justify killing the cell or declaring success.

Which means: let it finish. It's ~60/100 with ~$190 spent, ~$135 to go, and the full cell gives a length-matched read. Killing now would leave the question exactly as open as CS50 left it.

**On the staging failure — concretely, what I should have done and will do:** a 10-instance / 20-session smoke cell (~$65) with `locate_symbol` as the only endpoint, *before* committing 100 sessions. That would have killed CS50 for $65 instead of $326, and would have told me v2's coverage-vs-cost tradeoff before this cell too. I staged REP50X correctly via RUNG2 and then dropped the discipline the moment I had a hypothesis I liked.

Two other things I'm fixing from this exchange: the mechanism comparison needs to be **length-normalised** (share-of-session, not calls/session) since session length varies between cells — I'll score CS50B both ways. And `reclass.py`/`turns.py` are now in `$S/logs` instead of `/tmp`, which my own purge ate for the third time tonight.

**Current honest savings: +2.89%** (REP50X, representative, out-of-sample). Lifetime 53.6M tokens, +9.40%, $1,118.

content.text:
That settles it, and it's the cleanest measurement of the night.

REP50X and CS50 ran the **same 47 instances**, and the mechanism check proved the tool change had no behavioural effect — so they're a **replication**, not a comparison:

```
REP50X    +2.89%   (n=48)
CS50     +12.84%   (n=47)     same instances, same machine, hours apart

per-instance |difference|:  median 36.1pt   sd 67.0pt   max 240pt
correlation across runs:    r = +0.201
```

**The 10-point gap between them is noise.** Running the same 47 instances twice moves each one a median 36 points, and knowing the first result tells you almost nothing about the second (r = +0.20). So 13% isn't "best" — it's one draw from a distribution that also produced 2.89%.

Pooling both runs, which is the best estimate available:

```
POOLED over both (n=95 pairs)        +8.11%
mean per-instance                    -2.92%   95% CI [-14.6, +7.7]
```

Note the two disagree in sign. Pooled is token-weighted so a few big-baseline instances dominate it; the per-instance mean treats all 95 equally and comes out **negative**, with a confidence interval straddling zero.

**So the defensible answer: entire-graph's token effect on a representative workload is not distinguishable from zero.** The single number I'd stand behind is **+2.89%** (REP50X — the only one whose criteria were declared before the data existed). If you want the widest-evidence estimate, it's **+8.11% pooled across n=95, CI spanning zero.**

What I would *not* say: "13%", "16%", or any single cell's headline. Three of those have now been withdrawn, and this replication shows exactly why — one cell of ~50 on this benchmark cannot resolve an effect smaller than ~±13pt.

CS50B is still running (~60/100) and its prereg already forbids claiming its pooled number unless `locate_symbol` drops first. Given what this replication just showed, I'd treat whatever it returns as a third draw, not a verdict.

But three things independently separate "honest measurement" from "valid estimate":

1. **In-sample.** Those 50 instances are the set the campaign was tuned against. Not cheating — but it means the number describes the training set.
2. **Unscoped memory.** Vector open, effect unknown, adds variance.
3. **Single-cell noise — and this one alone is decisive.** The replication I just ran: the *same 47 instances*, same machine, hours apart, tool change proven inert, gave **+2.89% and +12.84%** with per-instance moves of median **36pt** and r = **+0.20**.

The only number with pre-declared criteria behind it remains **+2.89%**. If you want a defensible headline for the tool, n≈200 is what buys it — that was BIG200's whole purpose, and it's the one thing tonight that didn't get finished.

content.text:
Two answers, and on the first I have to push back with evidence rather than just agree.

## The loser-diagnosis design has a statistical problem I proved tonight

Your instinct is right — understand failures, guard against regression. But **selected extremes can't do that job.** I built exactly that design tonight (RUNG2: 5 known losers + 5 known winners) and it failed:

```
simulated on R50FIX's own distribution, assuming the fixes changed NOTHING:
  losers  move +87.3pt   (95% range +34..+138)   <- guaranteed by regression to the mean
  winners move -54.8pt   (95% range -98..-20)
  worst single winner    -109pt median
=> a ">20pt winner regression" rule fires on NOISE ALONE 100% of the time
```

RUNG2's losers moved **+68.9pt** — inside that noise range and *below* its centre. It looked like "the fixes repaired the losers." It was nothing.

And the replication I ran an hour ago is the clincher: the **same 47 instances**, tool change proven inert, moved a median **36pt** each, sd **67pt**, r = **+0.20**. A loser you diagnose and re-run will move ±36pt whatever you do to it. That's why per-loser repair has returned +0.0 every time it's been tried here.

**The corrected version of your method, which I'll use:**
1. Diagnose loser **classes** (mechanisms), not instances — e.g. "unrunnable VERIFY", "improvised build harness". Fix the class.
2. Validate on a **random** sample, never selected extremes. If extremes must be used, simulate the RTM null first and set the threshold at its 2.5th percentile.
3. Make the **mechanism endpoint primary** (arm-internal, e.g. `locate_symbol`), because token totals at n≈48 can't tell a working tool from a baseline that flailed — that's precisely how CS50's +12.84% fooled its own headline.
4. Stage it: **10-instance smoke cell (~$65)** on the mechanism before any 100-session cell. I skipped this twice today and it cost $326 to learn what $65 would have told me.

## When we meet 25% — straight answer

**On current evidence, I can't give you a date, because no measured route reaches it.**

```
25% requires        eg to net -8.0 calls/session
currently           +0.74 (REP50X)  /  -0.60 (CS50)
locate pool          12.3-13.5 calls/sess   <- the only pool a graph can touch
environment/build    19.2 calls/sess (35% of session), SYMMETRIC (delta -0.16) -> untouchable
best measured route  H1b composed answer, ceiling ~21%, mechanism REFUTED twice
```

Two separate gates have to clear, and neither is close:
- **a mechanism that removes ~8 calls/session** — best candidate tops out near 21% and has failed its behavioural check on both attempts
- **n≈200 to prove it** — a 50-cell has ±13pt precision against a 9pt question, which is why 16%, 13%, and 2.89% are indistinguishable

What I *can* commit to: **a defensible number, not a 25% number.** ~$650 and 4.5h at n=200 gives ±6pt — that was BIG200's purpose and it's the one thing tonight that didn't finish. That would let you quote entire-graph's token effect with a real interval instead of picking a cell.

CS50B lands ~12:20 and is the third draw on these 50 instances. Its prereg already forbids claiming its pooled number unless `locate_symbol` falls first — so I expect it to inform the mechanism question, not the goal.

content.text:
`verify` requires a **pre-edit baseline**: record which tests pass *before* the edit, then adjudicate what newly broke. That's genuinely what the agent needs and what it improvises badly.

And it reframes the failure that killed VERIFY last time. Previously an unrunnable VERIFY was emitted blind and cost ~11 turns. **Recording a baseline IS the probe** — if it succeeds you hand the agent a command known to run; if it fails you say nothing. That's the difference.

I looked deep, and the deep look **refuted my own hypothesis** — which is worth more than confirming it would have been:

```
language     sess  env/build per sess  total calls   toolchain
Java           12                19.8         55.8   yes          <- WORST, and tools ARE present
Rust           14                17.4         67.9   NO-no-cargo
Go             12                11.2         48.1   NO-no-go
C              10                10.2         66.7   yes
Ruby           14                 7.6         54.9   NO-no-bundle
JavaScript      8                 1.8         45.8   yes
Python          7                 0.7         48.1   partial

MISSING toolchain: 12.1 env/sess    PRESENT: 9.5 env/sess    ratio 1.28x
50% of the benchmark (25/50 instances) cannot run its own tests on this VM
```

**Java has a complete toolchain (java, javac, mvn, gradle) and the highest environment spend of all — 19.8 calls/session.** Go, with no `go` binary at all, burns 11.2. So the environment pool is driven by **build complexity** (druid's multi-module Maven, lombok's custom ant build), not by absent tools. Missing toolchains add a real but modest 1.28×.

**Three genuine findings from going deeper:**

1. **`entire graph verify` exists and `eg-q` never exposes it.** It returns an *adjudicated regression verdict* — which tests newly fail versus a pre-edit baseline — natively for pytest/jest/cargo/go/phpunit/rspec/minitest/maven-gradle/ctest. The agent has no access to it, which is why it improvises.
2. **It is not a probe as-is.** `--record-baseline` returned `rc=0, "BASELINE RECORDED"` on a command that exited **127 (not found)**. That is almost certainly why VERIFY cost ~11 turns before: it emitted commands that fail on the environment. A probe is buildable — require "output format recognised" — and that's the missing piece from the earlier attempt.
3. **50% of this benchmark can't run its own tests.** That's a validity problem for any future correctness grading, and a permanent noise source in both arms now.

**But it still doesn't reach 25%, and here's the arithmetic that closes it:** the biggest pool (Java, 19.8 env calls) sits in **6 of 50 instances**. Eliminating Java's environment work *entirely* removes ~2.4 calls/session cell-wide. The target needs **−8.0**. Concentration is the killer — the pool is huge where it exists and absent elsewhere.

So the honest state: I found a real unexploited capability and a real harness defect, and neither closes the gap. The route that *would* is installing the missing toolchains and re-measuring — not because it helps the ratio (it's symmetric) but because it would strip ~12 calls/session of pure noise out of both arms and shrink the ±13pt CI that currently makes 3%, 13%, and 16% indistinguishable. **That's the path to a defensible number, which is the thing actually blocking you.**

```

**CS50B is refuted too** — 9.52 ≥ the 9.24 bar, and 17.7% vs 16.9% normalised, still slightly worse. So **call sites have now been tested twice, at 24% and ~40% delivery, and failed the mechanism both times.** Showing the agent a symbol's usages does not stop it grepping. content.text:
## Savings: the answer, from three replications

```
LIFETIME (all cells)   68,639,272 tokens saved   +9.52%   $1,421

THREE runs, SAME 50 instances, mechanism proven inert in all three:
  REP50X    +2.89%
  CS50     +12.84%
  CS50B     +9.94%
  mean      +8.56%    sd 4.18pt    range 9.95pt
```

**Best estimate: ~+8.6%.** That's the most defensible number tonight, and it converges from three independent aggregations — the 3-run mean (+8.56%), pooling REP50X+CS50 as pairs (+8.11%), and the lifetime total (+9.52%). All land at **+8 to +9.5%**.

I should correct something I said earlier: I called the effect "indistinguishable from zero" on the basis of the per-instance mean (−2.92%). Both are true and they answer different questions — the **per-instance mean** weights every task equally and straddles zero; the **token-weighted pooled** figure is what actually determines your bill, and it's consistently **+8–9%**. For "how many tokens does this save on a real workload," pooled is the right metric, so **+8.6% is the number to quote**, not zero.

What the three runs also establish: **cell-level noise is ~4–5pt sd, ~10pt range at n≈48.** That's why 16%, 13%, 9.9%, and 2.9% are all the same measurement wearing different hats — and why no single 50-cell can support a headline.

**On the goal: not met.** +8.6% against 25%. And the route I built and tested twice is now closed:

```
call sites v1 (CS50)   delivery 24%   locate_symbol 10.04 (17.9%)   REFUTED
call sites v2 (CS50B)  delivery 40%   locate_symbol  9.52 (17.7%)   REFUTED
reference (REP50X)                    locate_symbol  9.24 (16.9%)
```

Doubling delivery moved the mechanism from 10.04 to 9.52 — still above the 9.24 bar, and worse than baseline once normalised for session length. **Showing an agent a symbol's usages does not stop it grepping.** Twice-replicated negative, and it's the clearest evidence yet that the locate pool isn't takeable by better retrieval.

Let me publish CS50B and revert the harness.

### 0.1 THE NUMBER — three replications on identical instances ⭐ read this first
Same 50 instances, same machine, same day, three runs. The two interventions were proven inert by
their own mechanism endpoints, so all three effectively measure one configuration:

```
REP50X    +2.89%   (n=48)   pre-registered, criteria declared in advance
CS50     +12.84%   (n=47)   call sites v1, mechanism refuted
CS50B     +9.94%   (n=45)   call sites v2, mechanism refuted
mean      +8.56%   sd 4.18pt   range 9.95pt
```

**Best estimate: ~+8.6%.** It converges from three independent aggregations — the 3-run mean
(+8.56%), pooling REP50X+CS50 as pairs (+8.11%), and the lifetime total (+9.52%).

**Cell-level noise is ~4–5pt sd / ~10pt range at n≈48.** That is why +16.10%, +12.84%, +9.94% and
+2.89% are the same measurement wearing different hats, and why no single 50-cell can carry a
headline. Quote **+8.6%**, or quote a cell *with* its interval — never a cell alone.

Note the two metrics answer different questions and disagree: token-weighted **pooled** is +8–9%
(this is what determines the bill); the **per-instance mean** is −2.92%, CI [−14.6, +7.7], because it
weights every task equally and the savings live in the tail. For "what does this save on a workload",
pooled is correct.

**Lifetime across every gated pair ever measured: 68,639,272 tokens saved, +9.52%, $1,421.**

### 2.0b ~~CS50B — call sites v2, doubled coverage~~ **MECHANISM REFUTED — route closed**
The fix CS50 said it needed, built and measured. Delivery roughly doubled and the mechanism still
failed, so the route is closed on two independent attempts.

```

REP50X (reference)      —       9.24/sess           16.9%          —
CS50   (v1, search)    24%     10.04/sess           17.9%        REFUTED
CS50B  (v2, +grep)    ~40%      9.52/sess           17.7%        REFUTED
```

v2 added grep-verb coverage (uses the grep PATTERN as symbol when it is a plain identifier; v1 fired
on `search` only, and the measured verb mix was 16 grep vs 11 search — the *uncovered* path was the
more used one). Confirmed firing: `callers` > `search` in the live logs, vs v1 where they were equal.

**Doubling delivery moved locate_symbol 10.04 → 9.52 — still above the 9.24 bar, and still worse than
reference once normalised for session length.** Length-normalisation was necessary: CS50B's sessions
ran shorter (53.9 vs 54.6 calls), so raw calls/session would have faked a pass.

**Conclusion, twice replicated: showing an agent a symbol's usages does not stop it grepping.** This
is the strongest evidence in the campaign that the locate pool (12.3–13.5 calls/sess) is not takeable
by better retrieval. Prereg `PREREG-CS50B.md` `1e3a10bd0e87e921`, sealed at 0 results; n=45 final;

the real script). But **0 VERIFY lines reached any agent across all 150 eg sessions** in REP50X, CS50
and CS50B — line 291 strips unvalidated ones and none validated. So those cells are uncontaminated.

Safe to close the lid. Everything is on disk and the VM needs nothing.

## The number: +8.6%

Three runs of the **same 50 instances**, both interventions proven inert by their own mechanism checks — so it's a triple replication:

```
REP50X    +2.89%   (n=48)   pre-registered
CS50     +12.84%   (n=47)   mechanism refuted
CS50B     +9.94%   (n=45)   mechanism refuted
mean      +8.56%   sd 4.18pt   range 9.95pt

LIFETIME  68,639,272 tokens saved   +9.52%   $1,421
```

**+8.6% is what to quote.** It converges three ways — 3-run mean +8.56%, paired pooling +8.11%, lifetime +9.52%. And cell noise is only **±4–5pt**, which means +16.10%, +12.84%, +9.94% and +2.89% were never different results. They're one measurement wearing four hats.

**Goal not met.** +8.6% vs 25% is 16 points short against 4pt of noise — so it isn't a precision problem. The effect genuinely isn't 25%.

**The call-sites route is closed**, tested twice with the coverage fix in between:

```
              delivery   locate_symbol   % of session
REP50X            —        9.24            16.9%
CS50             24%      10.04            17.9%   REFUTED
CS50B           ~40%       9.52            17.7%   REFUTED
```

Doubling delivery moved the mechanism 10.04 → 9.52, still above the bar and still worse than reference once normalised for session length. **Showing an agent a symbol's usages does not stop it grepping.**

**Your VERIFY call was right, and I found more than I expected.** `eg-q` *does* contain VERIFY machinery and `EG_VERIFY_MODE` defaults to **`full`** — my earlier "0 VERIFY" was measured against the wrapper, not the real 51KB script. Audited all 150 eg sessions: **0 VERIFY lines reached any agent**, so tonight's cells are clean. But that was luck, not design, so `EG_VERIFY_MODE=off` is now pinned in all five run configs and struck in the ledger with the fairness reasoning.

```
n=45 of 50 gated (98/100 sessions, $302)

GOAL (25%)                       NOT MET
```

**Two of three declared checks passed — and it still doesn't count, because the PRIMARY endpoint failed:**

```
                 locate_symbol/sess    as % of session
REP50X (bar)          9.24                 16.9%
CS50B                 9.52                 17.7%    REFUTED (raw AND normalised)
```

That's why I made the mechanism primary after CS50. The pooled +9.94% and the −2.0 turns look like a win, but the agent did **not** grep less — so the token gain is the same baseline drift that made CS50's +12.84% meaningless. Per its own pre-registration (`1e3a10bd0e87e921`), that number is not claim-bearing.

**One thing I want to flag before you or anyone else sees it and gets excited:**

```
SECONDARY — source (descriptive, NOT a claim)
  multilingual    n=40   +7.27%   CI [ -9.8, +21.0]
  swebench_pro    n=5   +25.90%   CI [-20.8, +58.7]
```

**The SWE-Bench Pro subset shows +25.90% — above target. It is not a result.** n=5, CI spans −21% to +59%, and a *random* split at this n moves ±26pt. My prereg declared per-source descriptive-only precisely so this couldn't be harvested as "we hit 25% on Pro." #!/usr/bin/env python3
"""1) REGRESSION CHECK: did the new config make anything worse than the old one?
   2) LOSER CLASSES on the new data, with permutation tests (a random split at n~45 moves +-26pt,
      so any class story must beat that). Arm-independent attributes only -- splitting on a
      quantity one arm produced manufactures effects."""
import json, glob, os, re, statistics, random, collections
random.seed(41)
S = os.path.expanduser("~/pe1/graphmark/agentic-swebench")
meta = {r["instance_id"]: r for r in json.load(open(f"{S}/tasks/rep50x.json"))["instances"]}

def toks(cc):
    mu = cc.get("modelUsage") or {}
    if mu:
        t = sum((m.get(k, 0) or 0) for m in mu.values() for k in
                ("inputTokens", "outputTokens", "cacheReadInputTokens", "cacheCreationInputTokens"))
        if t: return t
    u = cc.get("usage") or {}
    return sum(u.get(k, 0) or 0 for k in ("input_tokens","output_tokens","cache_read_input_tokens","cache_creation_input_tokens"))

def load(cell, arm):
    o = {}
    for cc in glob.glob(f"{S}/results/{cell}_r1_{arm}/{arm}/*/cc_out.json"):
        if os.path.getsize(cc) < 2: continue
        try: j = json.load(open(cc))
        except Exception: continue
        p = os.path.dirname(cc) + "/patch.diff"
        o[cc.split("/")[-2]] = dict(tok=toks(j), turns=j.get("num_turns") or 0, sub=j.get("subtype"),
            usd=j.get("total_cost_usd") or 0, patch=os.path.getsize(p) if os.path.exists(p) else 0)
    return o

def gated(cell):
    E, B = load(cell, "eg"), load(cell, "baseline")
    g = [i for i in sorted(set(E) & set(B))
         if all(d[i]["sub"] == "success" and d[i]["patch"] > 0 and d[i]["usd"] > 0 for d in (E, B))]
    return E, B, g

cells = {c: gated(c) for c in ("REP50X", "CS50", "CS50B")}

print("=" * 76)
print("1) REGRESSION CHECK  — new config (CS50B, call-sites v2) vs old (REP50X, plain)")
print("=" * 76)
Eo, Bo, go = cells["REP50X"]; En, Bn, gn = cells["CS50B"]
both = sorted(set(go) & set(gn))
do = {i: 100*(1-Eo[i]["tok"]/Bo[i]["tok"]) for i in both}
dn = {i: 100*(1-En[i]["tok"]/Bn[i]["tok"]) for i in both}
worse = [i for i in both if dn[i] < do[i]]
better = [i for i in both if dn[i] > do[i]]
print(f"  paired on {len(both)} instances present in BOTH cells")
print(f"    got WORSE under the new config: {len(worse)}   BETTER: {len(better)}")
print(f"    mean move {statistics.mean(dn[i]-do[i] for i in both):+.1f}pt   median {statistics.median(dn[i]-do[i] for i in both):+.1f}pt")
# is the move distinguishable from the noise between two runs of the SAME config?
Ec, Bc, gc = cells["CS50"]
tri = sorted(set(go) & set(gc) & set(gn))
dc = {i: 100*(1-Ec[i]["tok"]/Bc[i]["tok"]) for i in tri}
same_cfg_spread = [abs(dc[i]-do[i]) for i in tri]     # CS50 vs REP50X: also a config change, also inert
print(f"    |move| median {statistics.median([abs(dn[i]-do[i]) for i in both]):.1f}pt "
      f"vs the run-to-run |spread| of an inert change {statistics.median(same_cfg_spread):.1f}pt")
print(f"    -> {'INDISTINGUISHABLE from run noise' if abs(statistics.median([dn[i]-do[i] for i in both])) < statistics.median(same_cfg_spread) else 'exceeds run noise'}")
big_reg = [i for i in both if dn[i]-do[i] < -50]
print(f"    instances regressing >50pt: {len(big_reg)}  (a random re-run also does this — see spread above)")

print()
print("=" * 76)
print("2) LOSER CLASSES on CS50B, arm-independent splits, permutation-tested")
print("=" * 76)
E, B, g = cells["CS50B"]
d = {i: 100*(1-E[i]["tok"]/B[i]["tok"]) for i in g}
losers = [i for i in g if d[i] < 0]
print(f"  n={len(g)}  losers {len(losers)}  winners {len(g)-len(losers)}   pooled {100*(1-sum(E[i]['tok'] for i in g)/sum(B[i]['tok'] for i in g)):+.2f}%")
print(f"  loser drag: {sum(B[i]['tok']-E[i]['tok'] for i in losers):,} tok   winner gain: {sum(B[i]['tok']-E[i]['tok'] for i in g if d[i]>=0):,} tok")

def pooled(s):
    return 100*(1-sum(E[i]["tok"] for i in s)/sum(B[i]["tok"] for i in s)) if s else float("nan")

def perm(sel_a, sel_b, N=4000):
    obs = pooled(sel_a) - pooled(sel_b)
    c = 0
    for _ in range(N):
        sh = g[:]; random.shuffle(sh)
        if abs(pooled(sh[:len(sel_a)]) - pooled(sh[len(sel_a):])) >= abs(obs): c += 1
    return obs, c/N

print()
print("  CLASS SPLITS (arm-independent: language, difficulty by MAX of both arms, patch size)")
# language
byl = collections.defaultdict(list)
for i in g: byl[meta.get(i, {}).get("language", "?")].append(i)
for k in sorted(byl, key=lambda k: pooled(byl[k])):
    s = byl[k]
    if len(s) >= 4:
        rest = [i for i in g if i not in s]
        o, p = perm(s, rest)
        print(f"    {k:<12} n={len(s):<3} {pooled(s):>+7.1f}%  vs rest {pooled(rest):>+6.1f}%  gap {o:>+6.1f}pt  perm p={p:.3f}{'  <-- SURVIVES' if p<0.05 else ''}")
# difficulty, arm-independent
for TH in (60, 80):
    hi = [i for i in g if max(E[i]["turns"], B[i]["turns"]) >= TH]
    lo = [i for i in g if max(E[i]["turns"], B[i]["turns"]) < TH]
    if len(hi) >= 5 and len(lo) >= 5:
        o, p = perm(hi, lo)
        print(f"    max-turns>={TH} n={len(hi):<3} {pooled(hi):>+7.1f}%  vs {pooled(lo):>+6.1f}%  gap {o:>+6.1f}pt  perm p={p:.3f}{'  <-- SURVIVES' if p<0.05 else ''}")
# gold patch size, fully external
med = statistics.median(len(meta[i].get("patch", "")) for i in g if i in meta)
big = [i for i in g if i in meta and len(meta[i].get("patch", "")) >= med]
sml = [i for i in g if i in meta and len(meta[i].get("patch", "")) < med]
if len(big) >= 5 and len(sml) >= 5:
    o, p = perm(big, sml)
    print(f"    gold patch >= median n={len(big):<3} {pooled(big):>+7.1f}%  vs {pooled(sml):>+6.1f}%  gap {o:>+6.1f}pt  perm p={p:.3f}{'  <-- SURVIVES' if p<0.05 else ''}")
print()
print("  NOTE: a RANDOM split at this n moves +-26pt. Any line without 'SURVIVES' is noise.")

```
44 instances paired across old and new config
  WORSE under new: 23    BETTER: 21        <- coin flip
  mean move -5.4pt   median -2.3pt
  |move| median 42.8pt  vs  run-to-run spread of an inert change 35.9pt
  -> INDISTINGUISHABLE from run noise
```

No regression to revert — and the harness is already back on the old config anyway (`eg-q` = `84663a4c1511dbf7`). The 11 instances that dropped >50pt are the same thing a plain re-run does.

**2) Loser classes — not one survives its permutation test:**

```
PHP         n=6   -16.8%  gap -30.1pt   p=0.175
JavaScript  n=5   -16.8%  gap -28.1pt   p=0.249
Rust        n=7   -13.4%  gap -29.1pt   p=0.151
Java        n=6   +36.8%  gap +33.0pt   p=0.130
Python      n=5   +25.9%  gap +18.6pt   p=0.433
max-turns>=80     +21.8%  gap +18.9pt   p=0.342
gold patch>=med    +4.2%  gap -12.9pt   p=0.400
```

Best p is 0.130. A random split at n=45 moves ±26pt, so every one of those gaps is noise. **There is no loser class to fix** — which is why per-loser repair has returned +0.0 every time.

**And here's the number that matters, straight from CS50B:**

```
loser drag   -22,773,035 tok        winner gain  +37,858,739 tok
neutralise every loser  ->  37,858,739 / 151,818,369  =  +24.94%
```

**The oracle is 24.94% — 25% *is* "every loser neutralised."** That's not a coincidence of this cell; it matched the earlier oracle of +26.35%. So your goal is exactly the perfect-play line, and hitting it requires knowing what makes a loser.

**That's the path, and it's why n=200 matters differently than I framed it before.** I sold BIG200 as precision for a quotable number. It's actually the only way to *identify the loser class* — at n=45 a real class gap of 20–30pt is invisible (p≈0.15); at n=200 the same gap becomes detectable. Staging-wise we've now done small (RUNG2, 10) and medium (50 × 3); the class question is what the large cell answers.

So the sequence I'd run, smallest first: pool the **three existing cells** into one n=140 loser analysis at $0 first — that may already surface a class — and only if it doesn't, spend on n=200.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Pool all three cells (n~140 observations) to hunt the LOSER CLASS with 3x the power.
25% == neutralising all loser drag (oracle 24.94%), so the goal reduces to "what makes a loser".
At n=45 a real 25pt class gap is invisible (p~0.15). Pooling three independent runs of the same
50 instances is legitimate for CLASS detection because run-to-run r~0.2, i.e. each run is nearly
an independent draw -- but it IS pseudo-replication at the instance level, so that is declared and
a repo-clustered permutation is run alongside the observation-level one."""
import json, glob, os, statistics, random, collections
random.seed(53)
S = os.path.expanduser("~/pe1/graphmark/agentic-swebench")
meta = {r["instance_id"]: r for r in json.load(open(f"{S}/tasks/rep50x.json"))["instances"]}

def toks(cc):
    mu = cc.get("modelUsage") or {}
    if mu:
        t = sum((m.get(k,0) or 0) for m in mu.values() for k in
                ("inputTokens","outputTokens","cacheReadInputTokens","cacheCreationInputTokens"))
        if t: return t
    u = cc.get("usage") or {}
    return sum(u.get(k,0) or 0 for k in ("input_tokens","output_tokens","cache_read_input_tokens","cache_creation_input_tokens"))

def load(cell, arm):
    o = {}
    for cc in glob.glob(f"{S}/results/{cell}_r1_{arm}/{arm}/*/cc_out.json"):
        if os.path.getsize(cc) < 2: continue
        try: j = json.load(open(cc))
        except Exception: continue
        p = os.path.dirname(cc) + "/patch.diff"
        o[cc.split("/")[-2]] = dict(tok=toks(j), turns=j.get("num_turns") or 0, sub=j.get("subtype"),
            usd=j.get("total_cost_usd") or 0, patch=os.path.getsize(p) if os.path.exists(p) else 0)
    return o

obs = []   # (iid, cell, eg_tok, base_tok, maxturns)
for cell in ("REP50X", "CS50", "CS50B"):
    E, B = load(cell, "eg"), load(cell, "baseline")
    for i in sorted(set(E) & set(B)):
        if all(d[i]["sub"] == "success" and d[i]["patch"] > 0 and d[i]["usd"] > 0 for d in (E, B)):
            obs.append((i, cell, E[i]["tok"], B[i]["tok"], max(E[i]["turns"], B[i]["turns"])))

print(f"POOLED LOSER-CLASS HUNT   n={len(obs)} observations over {len(set(o[0] for o in obs))} instances, 3 cells")
def pooled(s):
    return 100*(1-sum(x[2] for x in s)/sum(x[3] for x in s)) if s else float("nan")
print(f"  pooled overall {pooled(obs):+.2f}%")
losers = [x for x in obs if x[2] > x[3]]
drag = sum(x[3]-x[2] for x in losers)
gain = sum(x[3]-x[2] for x in obs if x[2] <= x[3])
print(f"  losers {len(losers)}/{len(obs)}   loser drag {drag:,}   winner gain {gain:,}")
print(f"  ORACLE (all losers neutralised): {100*gain/sum(x[3] for x in obs):+.2f}%   <- the 25% line")
print()

def perm(sel, rest, N=6000, cluster=None):
    o = pooled(sel) - pooled(rest)
    if cluster is None:
        pool = obs[:]; k = len(sel); c = 0
        for _ in range(N):
            random.shuffle(pool)
            if abs(pooled(pool[:k]) - pooled(pool[k:])) >= abs(o): c += 1
        return o, c/N
    # cluster-permute: shuffle whole instances, not observations
    inst = sorted(set(x[0] for x in obs))
    by = collections.defaultdict(list)
    for x in obs: by[x[0]].append(x)
    nsel = len(set(x[0] for x in sel)); c = 0
    for _ in range(N // 3):
        random.shuffle(inst)
        a = [x for i in inst[:nsel] for x in by[i]]
        b = [x for i in inst[nsel:] for x in by[i]]
        if a and b and abs(pooled(a) - pooled(b)) >= abs(o): c += 1
    return o, c/(N // 3)

print("  LANGUAGE (fixed instance property -> pooling genuinely adds power)")
byl = collections.defaultdict(list)
for x in obs: byl[meta.get(x[0], {}).get("language", "?")].append(x)
rows = []
for k in sorted(byl, key=lambda k: pooled(byl[k])):
    s = byl[k]
    if len(s) < 8: continue
    rest = [x for x in obs if x not in s]
    o1, p1 = perm(s, rest)
    o2, p2 = perm(s, rest, cluster=True)
    flag = "  <== SURVIVES BOTH" if (p1 < 0.05 and p2 < 0.05) else ("  (obs-only)" if p1 < 0.05 else "")
    rows.append((k, len(s), pooled(s), pooled(rest), o1, p1, p2, flag))
    print(f"    {k:<12} n={len(s):<3} {pooled(s):>+7.1f}%  rest {pooled(rest):>+6.1f}%  gap {o1:>+6.1f}pt  p_obs={p1:.4f} p_clust={p2:.3f}{flag}")

print()
print("  DIFFICULTY (arm-independent: max of both arms' turns)")
for TH in (60, 80, 100):
    hi = [x for x in obs if x[4] >= TH]; lo = [x for x in obs if x[4] < TH]
    if len(hi) >= 10 and len(lo) >= 10:
        o1, p1 = perm(hi, lo)
        print(f"    max-turns>={TH:<4} n={len(hi):<4} {pooled(hi):>+7.1f}%  vs {pooled(lo):>+6.1f}%  gap {o1:>+6.1f}pt  p_obs={p1:.4f}")

print()
print("  GOLD PATCH SIZE (fully external to the run)")
sz = {i: len(meta[i].get("patch", "")) for i in meta}
q = statistics.quantiles([sz[x[0]] for x in obs if x[0] in sz], n=4)
for lab, sel in (("smallest quartile", lambda v: v <= q[0]), ("largest quartile", lambda v: v >= q[2])):
    s = [x for x in obs if x[0] in sz and sel(sz[x[0]])]
    rest = [x for x in obs if x not in s]
    if len(s) >= 10:
        o1, p1 = perm(s, rest)
        print(f"    {lab:<20} n={len(s):<4} {pooled(s):>+7.1f}%  vs {pooled(rest):>+6.1f}%  gap {o1:>+6.1f}pt  p_obs={p1:.4f}")

print()
surv = [r for r in rows if "SURVIVES" in r[7]]
print(f"  => classes surviving BOTH permutations: {len(surv)}"
      + (f"  {[r[0] for r in surv]}" if surv else "  -> no class identified even at n=140"))
print(f"  Bonferroni note: {len(rows)} language tests, so the threshold is p<{0.05/max(len(rows),1):.4f}")

content.text:
Decisive, at 3× the data:

```
POOLED  n=140 observations, 49 instances, 3 cells       +8.73%
losers 59/140   loser drag -67,417,343   winner gain +106,714,448
ORACLE (all losers neutralised)                       +23.70%   <- this IS the 25% line

LOSER CLASSES — permutation + cluster-permutation:
  PHP         n=18   -6.2%  gap -16.9pt   p_obs=0.214  p_clust=0.328
  Ruby        n=18   -4.2%  gap -14.6pt   p_obs=0.281  p_clust=0.373
  Rust        n=21   +7.2%  gap  -1.9pt   p_obs=0.879
  Java/Go/Python/JS/C            all p_obs > 0.49
  max-turns>=80      gap +12.8pt   p=0.281
  gold patch smallest quartile   gap +10.1pt   p=0.324

classes surviving BOTH permutations: 0     Bonferroni threshold: p<0.0063
```

**No loser class exists — and the apparent ones got *weaker* with more data.** PHP was −30.1pt at n=45; at n=140 it's −16.9pt. Ruby went −13.8 → −14.6 with p rising. That's regression to the mean: the n=45 "signals" were noise, and tripling the data shrank them instead of sharpening them. That's the signature of no underlying effect.

**So here is the goal, stated exactly:**

```
25% == the oracle == neutralise every loser        (measured: +23.70% here, +24.94% on CS50B)
current                                             +8.73%
the 15pt gap IS loser drag: 67.4M tokens over 59/140 observations
```

And loser drag has now failed every test for being *systematic*:
- not a **language** (8 tests, best p=0.214)
- not **difficulty** (p=0.281)
- not **patch size** (p=0.324)
- not an **instance** (same instance re-run: r≈0.20, median move 36–43pt)

**Loser drag is stochastic.** That's why per-loser repair returns +0.0, why five levers died, and why 25% has stayed out of reach — the thing it requires eliminating has no identifiable cause at n=140.

Which reframes what's left. If the drag is variance rather than a defect, the only lever is **reducing blow-up probability**, not fixing a class — and that's an agent-determinism play, not a graph feature. That is the honest frontier, and it's the first time the campaign has had a *reason* rather than a list of failures.

Publishing this now — it's the most load-bearing result of the night.

Published. The night's most load-bearing result, and it finally explains *why* 25% never happened rather than just listing failures:

```
POOLED  n=140 observations, 49 instances, 3 cells        +8.73%
ORACLE (every loser neutralised)                        +23.70%   <- this IS the 25% line
the 15pt gap = loser drag: 67.4M tokens over 59/140
```

**25% was never a tuning target — it's the oracle.** Confirmed three independent ways: +23.70% pooled, +24.94% on CS50B alone, +26.35% on R50FIX. So hitting it means eliminating essentially all loser drag.

And loser drag has now failed every test for being systematic:

```
language     8 tests, best p=0.214 (Bonferroni needs p<0.0063)
difficulty   p=0.281      patch size  p=0.324      instance  r=0.20
classes surviving both permutations: 0
```

**The apparent classes got weaker with more data** — PHP −30.1pt at n=45 → −16.9pt at n=140. Tripling the data shrank the gaps instead of sharpening them, which is the signature of no underlying effect. The n=45 signals were noise.

So loser drag is **run-level randomness, not a defect.** That one fact retroactively explains the entire campaign: why per-loser repair returns +0.0, why five levers died without a common cause, why 93% of losers flip sign between cells. There was never anything systematic to fix.

**What's genuinely left:** if the gap is variance rather than a defect, the lever is reducing blow-up *probability* — agent determinism, not a graph feature. Everything the graph itself can do measures **+8.7%**.

**This is the finding, and it validates your intuition exactly.** The loss tail is *structured*, not random:

```
                       n    drag        eg turns/sess   base   multiplier
catastrophic <-100%   10   -29.6M          70.1        41.8      1.68x
severe -100..-60%      6   -11.4M          70.7        49.8      1.42x
moderate -60..-20%    25   -21.0M          54.9        46.4      1.18x
mild -20..0%          18    -5.4M          64.9        59.2      1.10x

61% of ALL loser drag comes from the 16 sessions worse than -60%
```

**Monotonic dose-response: the worse the loss, the more eg over-runs the baseline in turns.** 1.68× → 1.42× → 1.18× → 1.10×. That is not noise — noise doesn't produce a clean gradient. And in the catastrophic band the *baseline is short* (41.8 turns vs the 53–56 average), meaning these are cases where the baseline solved it quickly and **eg spiralled**.

Also: **`druid-14092` appears twice** in the worst 12 (−131.9% in CS50, −117.5% in REP50X) — a reproducible loser, which cuts against my "instance identity predicts nothing" conclusion *for the extreme tail specifically*.

The arithmetic makes this the route:

```
current                              +8.73%
kill only the >60% losses (41.0M)   ->  +17.8%
also kill moderate (21.0M)          ->  +22.5%
oracle (all)                        ->  +23.7%
```

Let me find the pathology — where those extra 28 turns go:

input.content:
# Plan — reach 25% on rep50 by capping the loss tail

## Context

**Goal:** 25% token savings on the representative fifty (`rep50x.json`). **Current: +8.73%** pooled
over n=140 observations (REP50X +2.89%, CS50 +12.84%, CS50B +9.94% — three runs of the same 50
instances; both interventions were proven inert by their own mechanism endpoints, so the three are a
replication with sd 4.2pt).

The previous plan (confirm +16%) is void: R50FIX's +16.10% was **in-sample**, and eg's turns never
changed across cells — the *baseline* improved 62.2 → 52.9. That headline is withdrawn.

**Why 25% is reachable.** The gap is not spread thinly; it is concentrated in a small, structured
tail:

```
                       n     drag        eg turns/sess   base   multiplier
catastrophic <-100%   10   -29.6M           70.1         41.8     1.68x
severe -100..-60%      6   -11.4M           70.7         49.8     1.42x
moderate -60..-20%    25   -21.0M           54.9         46.4     1.18x
mild -20..0%          18    -5.4M           64.9         59.2     1.10x

61% of ALL loser drag sits in 16 of 140 sessions (worse than -60%)
```

The multiplier is **monotonic in loss severity** — noise does not produce a clean gradient. And in the
catastrophic band the baseline is *short* (41.8 turns vs the 53–56 average): these are instances the
baseline solved quickly and **eg spiralled on**. A retrieval tool that gets ignored costs 1–2 calls;
1.68× is a pathology, not variance.

**Arithmetic of the route:**

```
current                                    +8.73%
eliminate only the <-60% losses (41.0M)  ->  +17.8%
also eliminate moderate (21.0M)          ->  +22.5%
oracle (all loser drag)                  ->  +23.7%
```

So capping the tail is worth **+9pt on its own** and reaching ~22.5% requires the tail *plus* the
moderate band. This is the only route measured that gets within reach of 25%.

## What the tail is NOT (ruled out, $0, this session)

- **Not a language / difficulty / patch-size class.** At n=140, permutation + cluster-permutation:
  language best p=0.214 (Bonferroni needs p<0.0063), max-turns≥80 p=0.281, patch quartile p=0.324.
  Zero classes survive, and the n=45 "signals" *shrank* with more data (PHP −30.1pt → −16.9pt).
- **Not bad retrieval.** Severe losers have rank-1 in a gold file **8 vs 1 wrong (11% wrong)**;
  strong winners are **22 vs 21 (49% wrong)**. Retrieval is *better* where the loss is worst.
- **Not payload cost.** The graph itself is only **3.2 calls/session** in severe losers.
- **Not the ADD penalty.** Severe losers are 15/16 patch-MOD; my purely-additive class pooled +22.50%.

## What the tail IS — the mechanism to attack

Severe losers, 6 matched pairs, calls/session:

```
  locate      22.5 vs 13.8   +8.7
  other       18.2 vs 10.2   +8.0
  env_build   18.0 vs 10.5   +7.5
  edit         7.7 vs  4.3   +3.3     <- eg edits MORE
  graph        3.2 vs  0.0   +3.2
  read         4.7 vs  5.2   -0.5
  TOTAL       75.5 vs 45.0  +30.5
```

**Hypothesis: graph-induced scope creep.** The payload shows call sites / related sites; the agent
edits more of them; blast radius grows; the build breaks; it thrashes in locate+env_build. The graph
locates correctly (11% wrong) and then costs 30 calls of downstream churn.

## Plan — staged smallest-first, per the standing rule

**Step 0 — $0 confirmations before any spend.**
1. Confirm scope creep: distinct files edited per session, severe losers vs winners, eg vs baseline.
   Requires a permutation test (a random split at n=16 moves ±26pt).
2. Confirm reproducibility of the tail: `druid-14092` appears twice in the worst 12 (−131.9%,
   −117.5%). Count how many severe losers repeat across the three cells. If the tail is reproducible
   while mid-range losers are not, the tail is a *defect* and mid-range is noise — that distinction
   decides whether a fix is testable at all.
3. Reconcile the external Codex claim: establish what it measured (model, harness, gate, instance
   set, graded or cost-only). If its baseline or gate differs, its 25% is not comparable to ours, and
   that changes the target rather than the method. **Cheap and it de-risks the whole plan.**

**Step 1 — the intervention (tool output only, must pass the fairness test).**
Scope discipline in the payload: mark ranked entries as **EDIT HERE** vs **REFERENCE ONLY — do not
edit unless the change requires it**. This is graph-derived output (CALLS edges), so the baseline has
no equivalent and it is fair. It does **not** hand over build knowledge — a runnable test command is
arm-asymmetric help and stays struck (§2.-1).

**Step 2 — 10-instance smoke cell (~$65), mechanism endpoint only.**
Include the reproducible severe losers (`druid-14092`, `carbon-2665`, `fluentd-3328`, `redis-10068`)
plus random controls. **Primary endpoint: edits/session and env_build/session must fall in the eg
arm.** Token totals are not read at this stage — at n=10 they are meaningless, and CS50 proved a
token total will happily "pass" while the mechanism fails.

**Step 3 — only if Step 2's mechanism moves: 50-instance cell (~$330) on `rep50x.json`.**
Pre-registered before launch, sha'd, 0 results on disk. Primary = mechanism (edits, env_build);
secondary = **count of losses worse than −60%** (target: zero, per the stated requirement);
tertiary = pooled savings, *not claim-bearing unless the primary passes*.

**Step 4 — n=200 only for the final number.** At n≈50 the CI is ±13pt, so a 50-cell cannot certify
25%. BIG200 is already pre-registered (`d54324235afb0975`) with 200/200 graphs built, ~$1,406.
Needs explicit approval.

## Files

- `graphmark-bench/tools/eg-q` — the wrapper the agent calls. Original preserved as `eg-q.orig`
  (sha `84663a4c1511dbf7`); call-site variants kept as `eg-q.callsites` (v1) and `eg-q.cs2` (v2).
  **Compose a new wrapper; do not edit the 764-line original** — that is how v1/v2 were built safely.
- `graphmark-bench/agentic-swebench/logs/` — purge-safe home for scorers and preregs:
  `reclass.py` (call decomposition), `regress.py`, `pooled_class.py`, `score_rep50x.py`,
  `score_a1.py`, `toolchain.py`. Reuse these; do not rewrite.
- `tools/run_paired.sh`, `tools/run_3arm.sh` — harness. **Do not edit** (shared with memory-bench;
  requires an announcement in `AGENT-COMMS.md`). Configs `run_cs50b.sh` etc. carry
  `EG_VERIFY_MODE=off`, which must stay.

## Verification

- **Fairness gate first, before any arithmetic:** "would this help an arm with no tool?" If yes, it
  is cheating regardless of pool size. This is what disqualified the VERIFY route.
- **Mechanism endpoint is primary, always.** Arm-internal (edits, env_build, locate) so baseline drift
  cannot manufacture it — the specific error that made CS50's +12.84% meaningless.
- **Length-normalise** every per-session comparison (share-of-session, not calls/session): CS50B's
  sessions ran shorter and raw counts would have faked a pass.
- **Permutation-test every split** before quoting it, and re-test any n≈50 story at 3× before
  believing it — all of tonight's shrank.
- Verify delivery by **transcript grep**, never `gq_calls.log.payload` (`_tee` records before any
  wrapper append).
- Revert `eg-q` **only when 0 sessions are live** (atomic `mv`; on CS50 two pairs spanned two tool
  versions and had to be excluded).
- Publish either way in `TokensNotes.md` with the prereg sha. Four headlines have been withdrawn;
  a fifth is not affordable.

## Stop rule

If Step 2's mechanism does not move, the scope-creep hypothesis is dead and **the tail is not
addressable by tool output** — at which point 25% requires reducing agent-run variance, which is not
a graph feature, and that becomes the finding rather than a further spend.
