# /notepad — the single page of live state

Lives at **`/Users/suhaan/devenv/NOTEPAD.md`**. It is the handoff: if this session dies, that file is
what someone picks up. The **SEQUENCE** section at its top is the current plan of record.

## Output format (required)

Print the state inside a plain ASCII dash box. Rules:

- No em dashes and no en dashes anywhere. Use a plain hyphen.
- Simple technical English. Short declarative lines. No rhetorical flourish.
- Numbers in aligned columns. Every number carries its n.
- One box, sections separated by a dash rule. Keep it under about 40 lines.

```
+--------------------------------------------------------------+
| RUNNING                                                      |
|   CELL      12/24 sess   0 FATAL   14 min                    |
+--------------------------------------------------------------+
| SAVINGS                    tokens      time     note          |
|   CELL     n=8            +13.59%   +6.73%   fair, partial    |
+--------------------------------------------------------------+
| NEXT                                                         |
|   1. thing                                                   |
+--------------------------------------------------------------+
```

## When invoked with no argument

Read the file, then **refresh before reporting**. Never paste it cold.

1. **Refresh 🔴 RUNNING NOW.** Anything there is stale by definition.
2. **Write the refreshed numbers back**, then print the dash box above.
3. **Lead with what changed** since the last update, in one line above the box.

## The machines (as of 2026-08-10)

```
graphbench-c   RUNNING   c4-standard-32   MINE. every cell runs here.
graphbench-f   RUNNING   c4-standard-32   memory-bench's. DO NOT TOUCH, DO NOT KILL.
graphbench-a/b/e  DELETED 2026-08-10 (saved $198/mo). 3 snapshots kept as the recovery point.
```

Reach it with:
`gcloud compute ssh graphbench-c --zone us-east1-b --tunnel-through-iap --command '...'`

Suite root on the VM: `~/pe1/graphmark/agentic-swebench` (call it `$S`). Auth expires roughly hourly;
if it does, say so and tell the user to run `! gcloud auth login`. **Never report stale numbers as
current.**

## Scorers (all live in `$S/logs/`, purge-safe — `/tmp` gets wiped)

```
sav.py <CELL>        running savings; STRICT pairs + EXTENDED (eg vs a PRIOR baseline)
speed.py             all-time TOKENS *and* TIME (wall-clock) per cell
alltime.py           every cell, strict gate, pooled total
fd.py <CELL>         distinct-files-edited delta (the scope-creep mechanism endpoint)
reclass.py <CELL>    call decomposition: locate / read / edit / env_build / graph
toolchain.py         which languages lack a test runner on the VM
step0fix.py          scope-creep permutation test (fixed transcript matching)
related.py           precision of the RELATED SITES label vs the gold patch
pooled_class.py      loser-class hunt with cluster-permutation
score_<cell>.py      per-cell scorer against its sealed prereg
```

**Always report tokens AND time.** The user asks for both. Positive = saved; the raw `eg hours` vs
`base hours` columns disambiguate the sign.

## Rules that do not bend

- **Numbers carry n and a CI**, or they don't go in. Cell-level noise is ~4–5pt sd at n≈48, so
  3% / 9% / 13% / 16% are the *same* measurement. **Never quote a single cell as the number.**
- **Fairness test before the arithmetic:** *would this sentence help an arm with no tool?* If yes it
  is cheating, however large the pool. Tool OUTPUT (symbol locations, call sites, measured precision
  of a graph list) is fair; INSTRUCTIONS ("edit narrowly", "run `mvn test -X`") are not.
- **Mechanism endpoint is primary**, not the token total. Token totals at n≈50 cannot separate a
  working tool from a baseline that flailed — that is exactly how CS50's +12.84% fooled its own
  headline. Arm-internal metrics (files edited, env_build calls) can.
- **Permutation-test every sub-group** before quoting it; a random split at n≈48 moves ±26pt. Re-test
  any n≈50 story at 3× — all of them shrank.
- **Retractions stay visible** with the reason. Several findings here have inverted once.
- **Length-normalise** per-session comparisons (share-of-session, not calls/session) — session length
  varies between cells and raw counts fake passes.
- Verify tool delivery by **transcript grep**, never `gq_calls.log.payload` (`_tee` writes it before
  any wrapper append, so the forensic record can disagree with what the model received).

## Operational traps that have each cost real time

- **`pgrep -f` / `pkill -f` match your own SSH command line.** Build patterns dynamically
  (`RP=$(printf "run_pai""red.sh")`) and put kill and launch in **separate** calls — a launch loop
  containing the literal string will make the pattern kill your own shell.
- **Never edit a script under a running cell.** Deploy to a temp path and atomic `mv`. Reverting
  `eg-q` with two sessions live left two pairs spanning two tool versions.
- **Keep drivers, preregs and scorers out of `/tmp`.** The harness's own purge truncated the
  auto-launcher to 0 bytes and ate three analysis scripts.
- **Installing toolchains mid-cell contaminates it** — agents probe for `go`/`cargo`/`bundle` during
  sessions, which is the very behaviour being measured.

## When invoked with an argument

`/notepad <text>` — fold it into the right section, then confirm in one line.
🔴 running · ✅ done · 📊 results · ⛔ blocked · 🧭 SEQUENCE (the plan of record).

Detail lives in `graph-bench-results/TokensNotes.md` (token campaign) and `MemoryNotes.md` (memory).
`AGENT-COMMS.md` is the channel to memory-bench — check it before touching anything shared
(`tools/run_3arm.sh`, `tools/run_paired.sh`, `graphbench-f`).

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Gate the entiregraph MCP server to the `eg` arm only, and point every tool arm at its own backend.

THE BUG. run_3arm.sh had:
    _eg_mcp="${EG_MCP:-0}"; [ "$arm" = baseline ] && _eg_mcp=0
which zeroes MCP for `baseline` and for NOTHING ELSE. Harmless in a 2-arm cell. In a 4-arm cell
(baseline/eg/cmm/graphify) the cmm and graphify arms would each be handed the **entiregraph** MCP
server, so the cell would measure entire-graph three times under three different labels.

Its 2026-08-07 predecessor was worse: EG_MCP was passed through regardless of arm, and a pilot
verified the no-tool BASELINE carrying mcpServers.entiregraph while the comment claimed it got none.
This is the same defect one generation on -- the allow-list was written as a single deny.

THE FIX. Positive allow-list per arm, and each tool arm gets ITS OWN backend through the generalised
tool_mcp_server.py (identical tool NAMES across arms; only the backend and the factual output
description differ, because between three TOOL arms the descriptions are part of what is compared).
"""
import os, re, sys

p = os.path.expanduser("~/pe1/graphmark/agentic-swebench/tools/run_3arm.sh")
s = open(p).read()
orig = s

old = '''  _eg_mcp="${EG_MCP:-0}"; [ "$arm" = baseline ] && _eg_mcp=0'''
new = '''  # POSITIVE ALLOW-LIST, NOT A SINGLE DENY (fixed 2026-08-10).
  # The old form `[ "$arm" = baseline ] && _eg_mcp=0` zeroed MCP for baseline and nothing else, so a
  # 4-arm cell would hand the ENTIREGRAPH server to cmm and graphify as well -- measuring
  # entire-graph three times under three labels. Name the arms that may have a server, and give each
  # its OWN backend.
  _eg_mcp="${EG_MCP:-0}"
  case "$arm" in
    eg)       _mcp_q="$out/eg-q.run";        _mcp_arm=eg ;;
    cmm)      _mcp_q="$out/cmm-q.run";       _mcp_arm=cmm ;;
    graphify) _mcp_q="$out/graphify-q.run";  _mcp_arm=graphify ;;
    *)        _eg_mcp=0; _mcp_q="";          _mcp_arm="" ;;
  esac'''

if old not in s:
    if "POSITIVE ALLOW-LIST" in s:
        print("  already patched -- nothing to do"); sys.exit(0)
    print("  PATCH TARGET NOT FOUND -- aborting, nothing written"); sys.exit(1)

s = s.replace(old, new, 1)

# Point the generated mcp.json at the generalised server with the arm's own backend.
# The existing python heredoc receives use_mcp as argv[6]; extend it to carry arm + wrapper.
s = s.replace(
    '"$out/.gemini/settings.json" "$MAXTURNS" "$SUITE" "$wt" "$iid" "$_eg_mcp" "$out" "$EG_CACHE_ROOT"',
    '"$out/.gemini/settings.json" "$MAXTURNS" "$SUITE" "$wt" "$iid" "$_eg_mcp" "$out" "$EG_CACHE_ROOT" "${_mcp_arm:-}" "${_mcp_q:-}"',
    1)
s = s.replace(
    'cfg["mcpServers"]={"entiregraph":{"command":"python3","args":[f"{suite}/tools/eg_mcp_server.py"],',
    'mcp_arm  = sys.argv[9]  if len(sys.argv) > 9  else "eg"\n'
    '    mcp_wrap = sys.argv[10] if len(sys.argv) > 10 else f"{outdir}/eg-q.run"\n'
    '    cfg["mcpServers"]={f"{mcp_arm}tools":{"command":"python3","args":[f"{suite}/tools/tool_mcp_server.py"],',
    1)
s = s.replace(
    '"env":{"EG":f"{suite}/bin/entire-graph-linux","WT":wt,',
    '"env":{"ARM":mcp_arm,"Q":mcp_wrap,"EG":f"{suite}/bin/entire-graph-linux","WT":wt,',
    1)

if s == orig:
    print("  NOTHING CHANGED -- inspect manually"); sys.exit(1)
open(p, "w").write(s)
print("  patched run_3arm.sh: per-arm MCP allow-list + generalised server + per-arm backend")

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""PRIMARY ENDPOINT for a RANDOM draw (SMOKER12), paired per instance against its OWN history.

Why not fd.py: that scorer carries a hardcoded TARGETS literal from SMOKE12 (which was outcome-
selected, and whose list also contained a corrupt `-vnan` id present in 0 of 36 draws). SMOKER12 is
a plain random 12 with no targets and no controls, so a target/control split is meaningless for it.
Membership here is read from the task file, never from a literal.

Endpoint: distinct source files edited, eg minus baseline. Compared per instance against the same
instance's mean filedelta across REP50X/CS50/CS50B, then aggregated. Paired, arm-internal, and not
selected on outcome, so regression to the mean is not in play.

Usage: fdr.py [CELL] [TASKFILE]
"""
import json, glob, os, re, statistics, sys

S = os.path.expanduser("~/pe1/graphmark/agentic-swebench")
CELL = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "SMOKER12"
TASKS = sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 else f"{S}/tasks/smokeR12.json"
HIST = ("REP50X", "CS50", "CS50B")

ENVJ = re.compile(r"(/usr/lib/jvm|\.ivy2|\.m2|\.gradle|\.cargo|javac|-classpath|-cp |\.jar|jdk"
                  r"|CLASSPATH|go build|go test|cargo |bundle |gem )", re.I)
SCR = re.compile(r"(> */tmp/|cat *> */tmp|mkdir +-p +/tmp)")
BLD = re.compile(r"\b(mvn|gradlew?|cargo|go test|npm|yarn|pytest|tox|make|cmake|composer|bundle"
                 r"|rake|phpunit|jest|ant)\b")


def toks(cc):
    mu = cc.get("modelUsage") or {}
    if mu:
        t = sum((m.get(k, 0) or 0) for m in mu.values() for k in
                ("inputTokens", "outputTokens", "cacheReadInputTokens", "cacheCreationInputTokens"))
        if t:
            return t
    u = cc.get("usage") or {}
    return sum(u.get(k, 0) or 0 for k in
               ("input_tokens", "output_tokens", "cache_read_input_tokens", "cache_creation_input_tokens"))


def res(cell, arm, iid):
    f = f"{S}/results/{cell}_r1_{arm}/{arm}/{iid}/cc_out.json"
    if not (os.path.exists(f) and os.path.getsize(f) > 1):
        return None
    try:
        j = json.load(open(f))
    except Exception:
        return None
    p = os.path.dirname(f) + "/patch.diff"
    if not (j.get("subtype") == "success" and (j.get("total_cost_usd") or 0) > 0
            and os.path.exists(p) and os.path.getsize(p) > 0):
        return None
    return dict(t=toks(j), sec=(j.get("duration_ms") or 0) / 1000.0, n=j.get("num_turns") or 0)


def prof(cell, arm, iid):
    """(distinct edited source files, env/build call count). Substring match on a truncated slug:
    baseline transcript dirs get truncated with a random 6-char suffix on long ids, so endswith()
    silently misses exactly the long-named instances."""
    key = iid.replace("_", "-").lower()[:46]
    for d in glob.glob(f"{S}/results/{cell}_r1_{arm}/ccfg/projects/*/"):
        if key not in os.path.basename(d.rstrip("/")).lower():
            continue
        files, env = set(), 0
        for f in glob.glob(d + "*.jsonl"):
            for line in open(f, errors="ignore"):
                line = line.strip()
                if not line:
                    continue
                try:
                    j = json.loads(line)
                except Exception:
                    continue
                if j.get("type") != "assistant":
                    continue
                for c in ((j.get("message") or {}).get("content") or []):
                    if not (isinstance(c, dict) and c.get("type") == "tool_use"):
                        continue
                    nm, inp = c.get("name", ""), c.get("input") or {}
                    if nm in ("Edit", "MultiEdit", "Write"):
                        fp = inp.get("file_path", "") or ""
                        if fp and "/tmp" not in fp:
                            files.add(os.path.basename(fp))
                    elif nm == "Bash":
                        cmd = str(inp.get("command", ""))
                        if ENVJ.search(cmd) or SCR.search(cmd) or BLD.search(cmd):
                            env += 1
        return files, env
    return None, None


ids = [r["instance_id"] for r in json.load(open(TASKS))["instances"]]
print(f"{CELL} PRIMARY ENDPOINT — filedelta (eg minus baseline), paired vs each instance's OWN history")
print(f"  draw: {os.path.basename(TASKS)}  n={len(ids)}   history: {'/'.join(HIST)}")
print()
rows, unmatched = [], 0
for iid in ids:
    e, b = res(CELL, "eg", iid), res(CELL, "baseline", iid)
    if not (e and b):
        continue
    ef, ee = prof(CELL, "eg", iid)
    bf, be = prof(CELL, "baseline", iid)
    if ef is None or bf is None:
        unmatched += 1
        continue
    now_fd = len(ef) - len(bf)
    hist = []
    for h in HIST:
        he, hb = res(h, "eg", iid), res(h, "baseline", iid)
        if not (he and hb):
            continue
        hef, _ = prof(h, "eg", iid)
        hbf, _ = prof(h, "baseline", iid)
        if hef is None or hbf is None:
            continue
        hist.append(len(hef) - len(hbf))
    hfd = statistics.mean(hist) if hist else None
    sav = 100 * (1 - e["t"] / b["t"])
    tim = 100 * (1 - e["sec"] / b["sec"]) if b["sec"] else float("nan")
    rows.append((iid, now_fd, hfd, sav, tim, ee - be))
    hs = f"{hfd:+.2f}" if hfd is not None else "  n/a"
    mv = f"{now_fd - hfd:+.2f}" if hfd is not None else "  n/a"
    print(f"  {iid.split('__')[-1][:26]:<26} filedelta {now_fd:>+3} (hist {hs}, move {mv})"
          f"  env {ee-be:>+4}  tok {sav:>+7.1f}%  time {tim:>+7.1f}%")

print()
if not rows:
    print("  no completed pairs yet"); raise SystemExit
fd_now = [r[1] for r in rows]
paired = [(r[1], r[2]) for r in rows if r[2] is not None]
print(f"  pairs scored {len(rows)}   unmatched transcripts {unmatched}")
print(f"  mean filedelta NOW      {statistics.mean(fd_now):+.3f}")
if paired:
    hn = statistics.mean(x[1] for x in paired)
    mv = statistics.mean(x[0] - x[1] for x in paired)
    print(f"  mean filedelta HISTORY  {hn:+.3f}   (same instances, n={len(paired)})")
    print(f"  paired move             {mv:+.3f}   {'PASS (fell)' if mv < 0 else 'FAIL (did not fall)'}")
print(f"  pooled tokens {100*(1-sum(res(CELL,'eg',r[0])['t'] for r in rows)/sum(res(CELL,'baseline',r[0])['t'] for r in rows)):+.2f}%"
      f"   mean per-instance tokens {statistics.mean(r[3] for r in rows):+.2f}%"
      f"   mean time {statistics.mean(r[4] for r in rows):+.2f}%")
print(f"  BARS (paired, from these instances' history): filedelta < +0.042 | tokens > -10.80% | time > -9.44%")

# Plan — reach 25% on rep50 by capping the loss tail

**Operating rule: keep going until 25% holds.** A failed rung is a diagnosis, not a conclusion —
drop to the next hypothesis in the ladder at the end of this file. Six are queued. The only things
that stay fixed are the integrity rules, because a number that does not survive scrutiny is worth
less than no number.

## Context

**Goal:** 25% token savings on the representative fifty (`rep50x.json`). **Current: +8.73%** pooled
over n=140 observations (REP50X +2.89%, CS50 +12.84%, CS50B +9.94% — three runs of the same 50
instances; both interventions were proven inert by their own mechanism endpoints, so the three are a
replication with sd 4.2pt).

The previous plan (confirm +16%) is void: R50FIX's +16.10% was **in-sample**, and eg's turns never
changed across cells — the *baseline* improved 62.2 → 52.9. That headline is withdrawn.

**Why 25% is reachable.** The gap is not spread thinly; it is concentrated in a small, structured
tail:

```
                       n     drag        eg turns/sess   base   multiplier
catastrophic <-100%   10   -29.6M           70.1         41.8     1.68x
severe -100..-60%      6   -11.4M           70.7         49.8     1.42x
moderate -60..-20%    25   -21.0M           54.9         46.4     1.18x
mild -20..0%          18    -5.4M           64.9         59.2     1.10x

61% of ALL loser drag sits in 16 of 140 sessions (worse than -60%)
```

The multiplier is **monotonic in loss severity** — noise does not produce a clean gradient. And in the
catastrophic band the baseline is *short* (41.8 turns vs the 53–56 average): these are instances the
baseline solved quickly and **eg spiralled on**. A retrieval tool that gets ignored costs 1–2 calls;
1.68× is a pathology, not variance.

**Arithmetic of the route:**

```
current                                    +8.73%
eliminate only the <-60% losses (41.0M)  ->  +17.8%
also eliminate moderate (21.0M)          ->  +22.5%
oracle (all loser drag)                  ->  +23.7%
```

So capping the tail is worth **+9pt on its own** and reaching ~22.5% requires the tail *plus* the
moderate band. This is the only route measured that gets within reach of 25%.

## What the tail is NOT (ruled out, $0, this session)

- **Not a language / difficulty / patch-size class.** At n=140, permutation + cluster-permutation:
  language best p=0.214 (Bonferroni needs p<0.0063), max-turns≥80 p=0.281, patch quartile p=0.324.
  Zero classes survive, and the n=45 "signals" *shrank* with more data (PHP −30.1pt → −16.9pt).
- **Not bad retrieval.** Severe losers have rank-1 in a gold file **8 vs 1 wrong (11% wrong)**;
  strong winners are **22 vs 21 (49% wrong)**. Retrieval is *better* where the loss is worst.
- **Not payload cost.** The graph itself is only **3.2 calls/session** in severe losers.
- **Not the ADD penalty.** Severe losers are 15/16 patch-MOD; my purely-additive class pooled +22.50%.

## What the tail IS — the mechanism to attack

Severe losers, 6 matched pairs, calls/session:

```
  locate      22.5 vs 13.8   +8.7
  other       18.2 vs 10.2   +8.0
  env_build   18.0 vs 10.5   +7.5
  edit         7.7 vs  4.3   +3.3     <- eg edits MORE
  graph        3.2 vs  0.0   +3.2
  read         4.7 vs  5.2   -0.5
  TOTAL       75.5 vs 45.0  +30.5
```

**Hypothesis: graph-induced scope creep.** The payload shows call sites / related sites; the agent
edits more of them; blast radius grows; the build breaks; it thrashes in locate+env_build. The graph
locates correctly (11% wrong) and then costs 30 calls of downstream churn.

## Plan — staged smallest-first, per the standing rule

**Step 0 — $0 confirmations before any spend.**
1. Confirm scope creep: distinct files edited per session, severe losers vs winners, eg vs baseline.
   Requires a permutation test (a random split at n=16 moves ±26pt).
2. Confirm reproducibility of the tail: `druid-14092` appears twice in the worst 12 (−131.9%,
   −117.5%). Count how many severe losers repeat across the three cells. If the tail is reproducible
   while mid-range losers are not, the tail is a *defect* and mid-range is noise — that distinction
   decides whether a fix is testable at all.
3. Reconcile the external Codex claim. **Details are not known** — treat it as an *achievability
   signal*, not a methodology to match. Try to pin down from local artifacts what was measured
   (model, harness, gate, instance set, graded vs cost-only). Two possibilities matter: if it used a
   looser gate or a Python-only draw, its 25% is not comparable to ours (our draw has **25/50
   instances whose toolchains do not exist on this VM**); if it was the same setup, we are genuinely
   behind and the tail is the gap. Do not let an unverified comparison change the *method* —
   the tail arithmetic stands on its own.

**Step 1 — the intervention (tool output only, must pass the fairness test).**
Scope discipline in the payload: mark ranked entries as **EDIT HERE** vs **REFERENCE ONLY — do not
edit unless the change requires it**. This is graph-derived output (CALLS edges), so the baseline has
no equivalent and it is fair. It does **not** hand over build knowledge — a runnable test command is
arm-asymmetric help and stays struck (§2.-1).

**Step 2 — 12-instance smoke cell (~$80), mechanism endpoint + winner regression check.**

Composition — **losers to test the fix, winners to catch regression** (as required):

```
 4 reproducible severe losers   druid-14092, carbon-2665, fluentd-3328, redis-10068
 4 strong winners (>+20%)       regression controls
 4 random                       guards against selecting only extremes
```

**Primary endpoint: edits/session and env_build/session must fall in the eg arm** (arm-internal, so
baseline drift cannot fake it). Token totals are **not read** at this stage — at n=12 they are
meaningless, and CS50 proved a token total will happily "pass" while the mechanism fails.

**The winner-regression gate must be RTM-corrected, not naive.** Selecting the best instances and
re-running them *guarantees* regression: simulated on this benchmark's own distribution (sd ≈42pt),
winners move a mean **−54.8pt** and the worst single winner **−109pt median** *when the change does
nothing*. A ">20pt regression" rule therefore fires on noise **100% of the time** — it would have
blocked BIG200 unconditionally tonight. So:

1. simulate the RTM null first by resampling the three existing cells' own distribution,
2. set the gate at its **2.5th percentile** (RUNG2's became "fail if mean winner move < −98pt"),
3. judge winners on the **mechanism** too (did their edits/env_build rise?) — that endpoint has no
   RTM problem because it is not a selected-on quantity.

**Step 3 — only if Step 2's mechanism moves: 50-instance cell (~$330) on `rep50x.json`.**
Pre-registered before launch, sha'd, 0 results on disk. Primary = mechanism (edits, env_build);
secondary = **count of losses worse than −60%** (target: zero, per the stated requirement);
tertiary = pooled savings, *not claim-bearing unless the primary passes*.

**Step 4 — n=200 only for the final number. NOT pre-approved; hard stop before it.** At n≈50 the CI
is ±13pt, so a 50-cell cannot certify 25%. BIG200 is already pre-registered (`d54324235afb0975`) with
200/200 graphs built, ~$1,406. Requires explicit approval.

## Spend authorisation (as agreed)

Pre-approved **through Step 3 (~$395 total)**, but each step gated on the previous one's confirmation:

```
Step 0  $0     diagnostics + Codex reconciliation      -> report, then proceed
Step 1  $0     build the wrapper, validate offline     -> report, then proceed
Step 2  ~$80   12-instance smoke, mechanism + winners  -> mechanism must move, else STOP
Step 3  ~$330  50-instance pre-registered cell         -> publish either way
Step 4  ~$1,406  n=200                                  -> NOT authorised, ask first
```

Every paid step is offline-validated first: Step 1 caught a bare-name extraction returning 13
unrelated `Handler` definitions for +2308 B of noise *before* it cost anything.

## Files

- `graphmark-bench/tools/eg-q` — the wrapper the agent calls. Original preserved as `eg-q.orig`
  (sha `84663a4c1511dbf7`); call-site variants kept as `eg-q.callsites` (v1) and `eg-q.cs2` (v2).
  **Compose a new wrapper; do not edit the 764-line original** — that is how v1/v2 were built safely.
- `graphmark-bench/agentic-swebench/logs/` — purge-safe home for scorers and preregs:
  `reclass.py` (call decomposition), `regress.py`, `pooled_class.py`, `score_rep50x.py`,
  `score_a1.py`, `toolchain.py`. Reuse these; do not rewrite.
- `tools/run_paired.sh`, `tools/run_3arm.sh` — harness. **Do not edit** (shared with memory-bench;
  requires an announcement in `AGENT-COMMS.md`). Configs `run_cs50b.sh` etc. carry
  `EG_VERIFY_MODE=off`, which must stay.

## Verification

- **Fairness gate first, before any arithmetic:** "would this help an arm with no tool?" If yes, it
  is cheating regardless of pool size. This is what disqualified the VERIFY route.
- **Mechanism endpoint is primary, always.** Arm-internal (edits, env_build, locate) so baseline drift
  cannot manufacture it — the specific error that made CS50's +12.84% meaningless.
- **Length-normalise** every per-session comparison (share-of-session, not calls/session): CS50B's
  sessions ran shorter and raw counts would have faked a pass.
- **Permutation-test every split** before quoting it, and re-test any n≈50 story at 3× before
  believing it — all of tonight's shrank.
- Verify delivery by **transcript grep**, never `gq_calls.log.payload` (`_tee` records before any
  wrapper append).
- Revert `eg-q` **only when 0 sessions are live** (atomic `mv`; on CS50 two pairs spanned two tool
  versions and had to be excluded).
- Publish either way in `TokensNotes.md` with the prereg sha. Four headlines have been withdrawn;
  a fifth is not affordable.

## Advancement rule — a rung must HIT its target before the next one runs

No step advances on "directionally promising". Each rung has a number it must clear:

```
Step 2 (n=12)  edits/session AND env_build/session fall in eg;  no severe loser stays < -60%
Step 3 (n=50)  ZERO losses worse than -60%;  pooled > +17.8% (the tail-capped arithmetic)
Step 4 (n=200) pooled >= 25% with the interval reported
```

If a rung misses, **fix that rung before moving up** — do not carry a half-working intervention into
a larger cell. That is what turned CS50 into $326 of unattributable drift.

## Iteration ladder — the queue if the current hypothesis fails

H1 (current) is scope creep. It is not the last idea; it is the first of a queue. **If H1's mechanism
does not move, diagnose why and drop to the next rung — do not stop.**

- **H2 — RELATED SITES is the creep driver.** The payload's related-sites block is the plausible cause
  of edits 7.7 vs 4.3. `eg-q` already has `EG_LIT_DROP=1` to remove the site list; test dropping it
  and measure edits/session. Cheapest possible test, config-only, $0 offline first.
- **H3 — body-free first call.** Bodies in the payload may anchor the agent into a large edit before it
  understands scope. `EG_BODY_HEAD_RANKS` / `EG_SNIPPET` already exist. Measure edits/session.
- **H4 — install the missing toolchains** (`go`, `cargo`, `rustc`, `pytest`, `bundle`). **25/50
  instances cannot run their own tests on this VM**, and env/build is 19.26 calls/session (35% of the
  session, symmetric). This does not change the ratio directly — it removes ~12 calls/session of pure
  noise from *both* arms, which shrinks the ±13pt CI that currently makes 3%, 9%, 13% and 16%
  indistinguishable. A real effect cannot be seen through that much noise. **Harness fix, fair,
  untested, and possibly the highest-leverage item on this list.**
- **H5 — per-language payloads.** PHP (−6.2%) and Ruby (−4.2%) are the only negatively-pooled
  languages at n=140. Not significant alone (p=0.214/0.281) but they are the two worst and the
  direction is stable across cells.
- **H6 — variance reduction as an explicit target.** If the drag is stochastic, measure and attack
  P(blow-up) directly rather than the mean: does any config reduce the count of >4M-token sessions?
  H-TAIL failed at n=45 (p=0.29) where it had no power; retest pooled at n=140 for free.

**Rules that do not bend while iterating** — these are not caution, they are what keeps a win real:
- fairness test before arithmetic (a runnable test command stays struck, §2.-1)
- mechanism endpoint primary, arm-internal
- permutation-test every split; re-test any n≈50 story at 3×
- publish misses with the prereg sha

Base directory for this skill: /Users/suhaan/.claude/skills/notepad

# /notepad — the single page of live state

Lives at **`/Users/suhaan/devenv/NOTEPAD.md`**. It is the handoff: if this session dies, that file is
what someone picks up. The **SEQUENCE** section at its top is the current plan of record.

## When invoked with no argument

Read the file, then **refresh before reporting** — never paste it cold.

1. **Refresh 🔴 RUNNING NOW.** Anything there is stale by definition.
2. **Write the refreshed numbers back**, then show a compact version: what's running, what changed,
   what's blocked. **Lead with what changed.**

## The machines (as of 2026-08-10)

```
graphbench-c   RUNNING   c4-standard-32   MINE. every cell runs here.
graphbench-f   RUNNING   c4-standard-32   memory-bench's. DO NOT TOUCH, DO NOT KILL.
graphbench-a/b/e  DELETED 2026-08-10 (saved $198/mo). 3 snapshots kept as the recovery point.
```

Reach it with:
`gcloud compute ssh graphbench-c --zone us-east1-b --tunnel-through-iap --command '...'`

Suite root on the VM: `~/pe1/graphmark/agentic-swebench` (call it `$S`). Auth expires roughly hourly;
if it does, say so and tell the user to run `! gcloud auth login`. **Never report stale numbers as
current.**

## Scorers (all live in `$S/logs/`, purge-safe — `/tmp` gets wiped)

```
sav.py <CELL>        running savings; STRICT pairs + EXTENDED (eg vs a PRIOR baseline)
speed.py             all-time TOKENS *and* TIME (wall-clock) per cell
alltime.py           every cell, strict gate, pooled total
fd.py <CELL>         distinct-files-edited delta (the scope-creep mechanism endpoint)
reclass.py <CELL>    call decomposition: locate / read / edit / env_build / graph
toolchain.py         which languages lack a test runner on the VM
step0fix.py          scope-creep permutation test (fixed transcript matching)
related.py           precision of the RELATED SITES label vs the gold patch
pooled_class.py      loser-class hunt with cluster-permutation
score_<cell>.py      per-cell scorer against its sealed prereg
```

**Always report tokens AND time.** The user asks for both. Positive = saved; the raw `eg hours` vs
`base hours` columns disambiguate the sign.

## Rules that do not bend

- **Numbers carry n and a CI**, or they don't go in. Cell-level noise is ~4–5pt sd at n≈48, so
  3% / 9% / 13% / 16% are the *same* measurement. **Never quote a single cell as the number.**
- **Fairness test before the arithmetic:** *would this sentence help an arm with no tool?* If yes it
  is cheating, however large the pool. Tool OUTPUT (symbol locations, call sites, measured precision
  of a graph list) is fair; INSTRUCTIONS ("edit narrowly", "run `mvn test -X`") are not.
- **Mechanism endpoint is primary**, not the token total. Token totals at n≈50 cannot separate a
  working tool from a baseline that flailed — that is exactly how CS50's +12.84% fooled its own
  headline. Arm-internal metrics (files edited, env_build calls) can.
- **Permutation-test every sub-group** before quoting it; a random split at n≈48 moves ±26pt. Re-test
  any n≈50 story at 3× — all of them shrank.
- **Retractions stay visible** with the reason. Several findings here have inverted once.
- **Length-normalise** per-session comparisons (share-of-session, not calls/session) — session length
  varies between cells and raw counts fake passes.
- Verify tool delivery by **transcript grep**, never `gq_calls.log.payload` (`_tee` writes it before
  any wrapper append, so the forensic record can disagree with what the model received).

## Operational traps that have each cost real time

- **`pgrep -f` / `pkill -f` match your own SSH command line.** Build patterns dynamically
  (`RP=$(printf "run_pai""red.sh")`) and put kill and launch in **separate** calls — a launch loop
  containing the literal string will make the pattern kill your own shell.
- **Never edit a script under a running cell.** Deploy to a temp path and atomic `mv`. Reverting
  `eg-q` with two sessions live left two pairs spanning two tool versions.
- **Keep drivers, preregs and scorers out of `/tmp`.** The harness's own purge truncated the
  auto-launcher to 0 bytes and ate three analysis scripts.
- **Installing toolchains mid-cell contaminates it** — agents probe for `go`/`cargo`/`bundle` during
  sessions, which is the very behaviour being measured.

## When invoked with an argument

`/notepad <text>` — fold it into the right section, then confirm in one line.
🔴 running · ✅ done · 📊 results · ⛔ blocked · 🧭 SEQUENCE (the plan of record).

Detail lives in `graph-bench-results/TokensNotes.md` (token campaign) and `MemoryNotes.md` (memory).
`AGENT-COMMS.md` is the channel to memory-bench — check it before touching anything shared
(`tools/run_3arm.sh`, `tools/run_paired.sh`, `graphbench-f`).

The stop hook is right that 25% is not met, and the plan to get there needs the corrected numbers. The delta table above is the key input, and it says something important:

```
eg spends 2.72 calls/session on the graph and recovers 1.98 elsewhere.
Net +0.74 calls MORE than baseline, yet tokens still save.
```

That means savings do not come from doing less work per session. They come from truncating blow-ups. Let me measure that directly at n=140 — it is free and it decides the whole route:

input.command:
cat > /tmp/tail.py <<'PY'
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""WHERE DOES THE SAVING ACTUALLY LIVE? Decompose pooled savings by blow-up structure, n=140.

The corrected call table says eg makes MORE calls per session than baseline (+0.74) while still
saving tokens pooled. Both cannot be true of a typical session, so the saving must be concentrated
in sessions where one arm blew up. This script finds out which, and sizes the counterfactuals that
a route to 15% would have to buy.
"""
import json, os, statistics, sys

S = os.path.expanduser("~/pe1/graphmark/agentic-swebench")
CELLS = ("REP50X", "CS50", "CS50B")

def toks(cc):
    mu = cc.get("modelUsage") or {}
    if mu:
        t = sum((m.get(k,0) or 0) for m in mu.values() for k in
                ("inputTokens","outputTokens","cacheReadInputTokens","cacheCreationInputTokens"))
        if t: return t
    u = cc.get("usage") or {}
    return sum(u.get(k,0) or 0 for k in
               ("input_tokens","output_tokens","cache_read_input_tokens","cache_creation_input_tokens"))

def res(cell, arm, iid):
    f=f"{S}/results/{cell}_r1_{arm}/{arm}/{iid}/cc_out.json"
    if not (os.path.exists(f) and os.path.getsize(f)>1): return None
    try: j=json.load(open(f))
    except Exception: return None
    p=os.path.dirname(f)+"/patch.diff"
    if not (j.get("subtype")=="success" and (j.get("total_cost_usd") or 0)>0
            and os.path.exists(p) and os.path.getsize(p)>0): return None
    return toks(j)

pairs=[]
for cell in CELLS:
    tf=f"{S}/tasks/rep50x.json"
    if not os.path.exists(tf): continue
    for r in json.load(open(tf))["instances"]:
        iid=r["instance_id"]
        e,b=res(cell,"eg",iid),res(cell,"baseline",iid)
        if e and b: pairs.append((cell,iid,e,b))

if not pairs:
    print("no pairs"); sys.exit()
E=sum(p[2] for p in pairs); B=sum(p[3] for p in pairs)
print(f"POOLED n={len(pairs)}   eg {E/1e6:.1f}M   base {B/1e6:.1f}M   saving {100*(1-E/B):+.2f}%")
med_e=statistics.median(p[2] for p in pairs); med_b=statistics.median(p[3] for p in pairs)
print(f"  median session      eg {med_e/1e6:.2f}M   base {med_b/1e6:.2f}M   {100*(1-med_e/med_b):+.2f}%")
print()

# --- blow-up structure -------------------------------------------------------
print("BLOW-UP RATES (share of sessions above a token threshold)")
print(f"  {'thresh':>8}  {'eg':>6} {'base':>6}   {'eg mass':>9} {'base mass':>9}   {'saving from':>12}")
for th in (2e6,3e6,4e6,6e6,8e6):
    ne=sum(1 for p in pairs if p[2]>th); nb=sum(1 for p in pairs if p[3]>th)
    me=sum(p[2] for p in pairs if p[2]>th); mb=sum(p[3] for p in pairs if p[3]>th)
    print(f"  {th/1e6:>6.0f}M  {100*ne/len(pairs):>5.1f}% {100*nb/len(pairs):>5.1f}%   "
          f"{me/1e6:>8.1f}M {mb/1e6:>8.1f}M   {(mb-me)/1e6:>+10.1f}M")
print()

# --- decomposition: which sessions carry the pooled delta --------------------
TH=4e6
q=[]
for cell,iid,e,b in pairs:
    if e>TH and b>TH: k="both blew up"
    elif b>TH:        k="base only blew up"
    elif e>TH:        k="eg only blew up"
    else:             k="neither blew up"
    q.append((k,e,b))
print(f"DECOMPOSITION at >{TH/1e6:.0f}M   (delta = base - eg; positive = eg saved)")
tot=B-E
for k in ("neither blew up","base only blew up","eg only blew up","both blew up"):
    g=[x for x in q if x[0]==k]
    if not g: continue
    d=sum(x[2]-x[1] for x in g)
    print(f"  {k:<20} n={len(g):>3}   delta {d/1e6:>+8.1f}M   {100*d/tot:>+6.1f}% of the total saving")
print(f"  {'TOTAL':<20} n={len(q):>3}   delta {tot/1e6:>+8.1f}M")
print()

# --- counterfactuals a 15% route must buy -----------------------------------
print("COUNTERFACTUALS (what each fix would be worth, pooled)")
def pooled(ps): 
    e=sum(x[0] for x in ps); b=sum(x[1] for x in ps); return 100*(1-e/b)
cur=[(p[2],p[3]) for p in pairs]
print(f"  current                                        {pooled(cur):+7.2f}%")
# cap eg at the baseline value wherever eg lost by >60%
c1=[(min(e, b*1.60) if e>b*1.60 else e, b) for e,b in cur]
print(f"  cap every eg loss worse than -60% at -60%      {pooled(c1):+7.2f}%   <- tail cap")
c2=[(min(e,b) , b) for e,b in cur]
print(f"  eg never loses at all (oracle)                 {pooled(c2):+7.2f}%")
c3=[(e,b) for e,b in cur if not (e>TH and b<=TH)]
print(f"  drop eg-only blow-ups entirely (n={len(cur)-len(c3)})           {pooled(c3):+7.2f}%   <- not a fix, a diagnostic")
# how many tail caps to reach 15%?
need=[]
srt=sorted(range(len(cur)), key=lambda i: cur[i][0]-cur[i][1], reverse=True)
w=list(cur)
for i in srt:
    if pooled(w)>=15.0: break
    e,b=w[i]
    if e>b: w[i]=(b,b); need.append(i)
print(f"  sessions that must stop losing to reach +15%:  {len(need)} of {len(cur)}  ({100*len(need)/len(cur):.0f}%)")
print(f"    after fixing exactly those:                  {pooled(w):+7.2f}%")
PY

content.text:
This is the clearest structural result of the campaign. The saving is not diffuse at all:

```
base blew up, eg did not   n=19    +46.4M   +118% of the total saving
eg blew up, base did not   n=12    -31.0M    -79% of the total saving
```

eg prevents 19 blow-ups and causes 12. The measured +8.73% is the residue. And only **8 sessions of 140 (6%)** need to stop losing to reach +15%. That reframes the target completely: 15% is not a broad efficiency problem, it is 8 sessions.

The critical question is whether those 12 have an interdictable signature. Instance identity predicts nothing (r=−0.022), so this has to be a within-session behavioural signature:

input.command:
cat > /tmp/sig.py <<'PY'
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Do eg-only blow-ups have an INTERDICTABLE signature? eg-vs-eg, so baseline drift cannot fake it.

Route to 15% = stop 8 of 140 sessions from losing. Instance identity predicts nothing (r=-0.022),
so any fix must key off something eg DOES inside the session. Two candidates, both config-reachable:
  (a) graph-call count / lateness  -> a per-session cap on the tool is fair (tool behaviour, not an
      instruction; the no-tool arm needs no equivalent)
  (b) the call MIX after the first graph call -> tells us what the agent spirals into
Report both, and what a cap at K would actually have bitten.
"""
import json, glob, os, re, statistics, sys

S=os.path.expanduser("~/pe1/graphmark/agentic-swebench")
CELLS=("REP50X","CS50","CS50B"); TH=4e6

def toks(cc):
    mu=cc.get("modelUsage") or {}
    if mu:
        t=sum((m.get(k,0) or 0) for m in mu.values() for k in
              ("inputTokens","outputTokens","cacheReadInputTokens","cacheCreationInputTokens"))
        if t: return t
    u=cc.get("usage") or {}
    return sum(u.get(k,0) or 0 for k in ("input_tokens","output_tokens",
               "cache_read_input_tokens","cache_creation_input_tokens"))

def res(cell,arm,iid):
    f=f"{S}/results/{cell}_r1_{arm}/{arm}/{iid}/cc_out.json"
    if not(os.path.exists(f) and os.path.getsize(f)>1): return None
    try: j=json.load(open(f))
    except Exception: return None
    p=os.path.dirname(f)+"/patch.diff"
    if not(j.get("subtype")=="success" and (j.get("total_cost_usd") or 0)>0
           and os.path.exists(p) and os.path.getsize(p)>0): return None
    return toks(j)

GQ=re.compile(r"\b(eg-q|entire-graph|graph_search|code_search|find_definition|find_callers|impact)\b")
def seq(cell,arm,iid):
    """ordered list of (kind) for every tool call in the session"""
    key=iid.replace("_","-").lower()[:46]
    for d in glob.glob(f"{S}/results/{cell}_r1_{arm}/ccfg/projects/*/"):
        if key not in os.path.basename(d.rstrip("/")).lower(): continue
        ev=[]
        for f in sorted(glob.glob(d+"*.jsonl")):
            for line in open(f,errors="ignore"):
                line=line.strip()
                if not line: continue
                try: j=json.loads(line)
                except Exception: continue
                if j.get("type")!="assistant": continue
                for c in ((j.get("message") or {}).get("content") or []):
                    if not(isinstance(c,dict) and c.get("type")=="tool_use"): continue
                    nm=c.get("name",""); inp=c.get("input") or {}
                    cmd=str(inp.get("command","")) if nm=="Bash" else ""
                    if GQ.search(nm) or GQ.search(cmd): ev.append("graph")
                    elif nm in ("Edit","MultiEdit","Write"): ev.append("edit")
                    elif nm in ("Read","Glob","Grep"): ev.append("read")
                    else: ev.append("other")
        return ev
    return None

rows=[]
for cell in CELLS:
    for r in json.load(open(f"{S}/tasks/rep50x.json"))["instances"]:
        iid=r["instance_id"]; e,b=res(cell,"eg",iid),res(cell,"baseline",iid)
        if not(e and b): continue
        sq=seq(cell,"eg",iid)
        if sq is None: continue
        g=[i for i,k in enumerate(sq) if k=="graph"]
        rows.append(dict(cell=cell,iid=iid,e=e,b=b,n=len(sq),ng=len(g),
                         last=(g[-1]/len(sq) if g and sq else None),
                         first=(g[0] if g else None),
                         after=(len(sq)-g[0] if g else None),
                         cls=("EGBLOW" if e>TH and b<=TH else
                              "BASEBLOW" if b>TH and e<=TH else
                              "BOTH" if e>TH and b>TH else "CLEAN")))
print(f"eg sessions with a readable transcript: n={len(rows)}\n")
print(f"  {'class':<10} {'n':>3}  {'calls':>6} {'graph':>6} {'1st@':>6} {'after1st':>9} {'last@%':>7}  {'tok':>7}")
for c in ("CLEAN","BASEBLOW","EGBLOW","BOTH"):
    g=[r for r in rows if r["cls"]==c]
    if not g: continue
    def m(k): 
        v=[r[k] for r in g if r[k] is not None]; return statistics.mean(v) if v else float("nan")
    print(f"  {c:<10} {len(g):>3}  {m('n'):>6.1f} {m('ng'):>6.2f} {m('first'):>6.1f} {m('after'):>9.1f} "
          f"{100*m('last'):>6.1f}% {statistics.mean(r['e'] for r in g)/1e6:>6.2f}M")
print()
eb=[r for r in rows if r["cls"]=="EGBLOW"]; bb=[r for r in rows if r["cls"]=="BASEBLOW"]

content.text:
Now consistent with reclass (2.78 vs 2.72). And the result kills the cap idea cleanly:

```
graph calls   EGBLOW 2.58  vs  eg WINS 3.16   p=0.394   no difference
1st graph call at index ~1 in ALL classes
last graph call at 21.6% of an EGBLOW session -> 78% of it runs with no tool
```

eg-only blow-ups do not over-use the graph. They use it identically, up front, and then spiral for 74 calls with the tool absent. A cap harms wins more than blow-ups at every K≥2. So the signature is not usage volume — it is that the tool has no presence during the phase that costs. Let me find what those 74 calls are and whether the tool already has a subcommand for it:

input.command:

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""What are the 74 post-graph calls in an eg-only blow-up, and does the tool already answer them?

Established: eg-only blow-ups use the graph the SAME as eg's wins (2.58 vs 3.16, p=0.394), at call
index ~1, then run 74 more calls untooled. So the question is not "how much tool" but "which need
goes unmet after the first call". If the unmet need maps to a subcommand that exists but is never
invoked, that is a discoverability gap -- and a tool that describes its own subcommands is tool
output, not an instruction, so it is fair.
"""
import json, glob, os, re, statistics, collections

S=os.path.expanduser("~/pe1/graphmark/agentic-swebench")
CELLS=("REP50X","CS50","CS50B"); TH=4e6
GQ=re.compile(r"(entire[ -]graph|eg-q)", re.I)
SUB=re.compile(r"entire[ -]graph\s+([a-z]+)", re.I)

def toks(cc):
    mu=cc.get("modelUsage") or {}
    if mu:
        t=sum((m.get(k,0) or 0) for m in mu.values() for k in
              ("inputTokens","outputTokens","cacheReadInputTokens","cacheCreationInputTokens"))
        if t: return t
    u=cc.get("usage") or {}
    return sum(u.get(k,0) or 0 for k in ("input_tokens","output_tokens",
               "cache_read_input_tokens","cache_creation_input_tokens"))

def res(cell,arm,iid):
    f=f"{S}/results/{cell}_r1_{arm}/{arm}/{iid}/cc_out.json"
    if not(os.path.exists(f) and os.path.getsize(f)>1): return None
    try: j=json.load(open(f))
    except Exception: return None
    p=os.path.dirname(f)+"/patch.diff"
    if not(j.get("subtype")=="success" and (j.get("total_cost_usd") or 0)>0
           and os.path.exists(p) and os.path.getsize(p)>0): return None
    return toks(j)

ENVJ=re.compile(r"(/usr/lib/jvm|\.ivy2|\.m2|\.gradle|\.cargo|javac|-classpath|-cp |\.jar|jdk|CLASSPATH)",re.I)
BLD=re.compile(r"\b(mvn|gradlew?|cargo|go test|go build|npm|yarn|pytest|tox|make|cmake|composer|bundle|rake|phpunit|jest|ant)\b")
SYM=re.compile(r"\b(grep|rg|ag|find|ls|cat|sed|awk|head|tail|wc)\b")

def classify(nm,cmd):
    if GQ.search(nm+" "+cmd): return "graph"
    if nm in ("Edit","MultiEdit","Write"): return "edit"
    if nm in ("Read",): return "read"
    if nm in ("Glob","Grep"): return "locate"
    if nm=="Bash":
        if BLD.search(cmd) or ENVJ.search(cmd): return "env_build"
        if SYM.search(cmd): return "locate"
        return "other"
    return "other"

subs=collections.Counter(); post=collections.defaultdict(collections.Counter); nsess=collections.Counter()
for cell in CELLS:
    for r in json.load(open(f"{S}/tasks/rep50x.json"))["instances"]:
        iid=r["instance_id"]; e,b=res(cell,"eg",iid),res(cell,"baseline",iid)
        if not(e and b): continue
        cls=("EGBLOW" if e>TH and b<=TH else "BASEBLOW" if b>TH and e<=TH
             else "BOTH" if e>TH and b>TH else "CLEAN")
        key=iid.replace("_","-").lower()[:46]
        for d in glob.glob(f"{S}/results/{cell}_r1_eg/ccfg/projects/*/"):
            if key not in os.path.basename(d.rstrip("/")).lower(): continue
            ev=[]
            for f in sorted(glob.glob(d+"*.jsonl")):
                for line in open(f,errors="ignore"):
                    try: j=json.loads(line)
                    except Exception: continue
                    if j.get("type")!="assistant": continue
                    for c in ((j.get("message") or {}).get("content") or []):
                        if not(isinstance(c,dict) and c.get("type")=="tool_use"): continue
                        nm=c.get("name",""); inp=c.get("input") or {}
                        cmd=str(inp.get("command","")) if nm=="Bash" else ""
                        k=classify(nm,cmd); ev.append(k)
                        if k=="graph":
                            m=SUB.search(cmd)
                            subs[(m.group(1).lower() if m else "wrapper")]+=1
            g=[i for i,k in enumerate(ev) if k=="graph"]
            if g:
                nsess[cls]+=1
                for k in ev[g[-1]+1:]: post[cls][k]+=1
            break

print("GRAPH SUBCOMMANDS actually invoked across all eg sessions (n=137)")
tot=sum(subs.values())
for k,v in subs.most_common():
    print(f"  {k:<14} {v:>5}  {100*v/tot:>5.1f}%")
print(f"  {'TOTAL':<14} {tot:>5}")
print()
print("CALL MIX AFTER THE LAST GRAPH CALL (per session, the untooled phase)")
kinds=("locate","read","edit","env_build","other")
print(f"  {'class':<10} {'sess':>4}  " + "".join(f"{k:>10}" for k in kinds) + f"{'total':>9}")

    try: j=json.load(open(f))

    p=os.path.dirname(f)+"/patch.diff"
    if not(j.get("subtype")=="success" and (j.get("total_cost_usd") or 0)>0
           and os.path.exists(p) and os.path.getsize(p)>0): return None
    return toks(j)

```
+--------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| RUNNING                                                                  |
|   SMOKER12W   6/24 sessions   6 live   16 min   0 FATAL                  |
|   early n=2   -9.56% pooled   ignore this, n=2 is noise                  |
|   nothing else running. cost tonight $1,913                              |
+--------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| WHAT I FOUND WHILE IT RUNS (n=140, free, no new spend)                   |
|                                                                          |
|   estimator                        point      95% CI                     |
|   pooled, cluster by instance     +8.73%   [-2.79%, +18.86%]             |
|   pooled, naive session boot      +8.73%   [-0.84%, +16.82%]             |
|   mean per session, equal weight  -3.02%   [-12.23%, +5.82%]             |
|   median per session              +7.34%                                 |
|   10% symmetric trimmed mean      +4.40%                                 |
|                                                                          |
|   P(true >= 25%)   0.1%                                                  |
|   P(true >= 15%)  12.2%                                                  |
|   P(true <=  0%)   6.8%                                                  |
+--------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

Two things here matter more than the point estimates.

**The sign depends on the estimator.** Token-weighted pooling gives +8.73%; weighting every session equally gives **−3.02%**. Same 140 sessions. That is not a contradiction, it is the mechanism: eg saves on sessions that blow up and costs slightly on ordinary ones. A bill-shaped claim (total tokens saved) is positive. A "does it help on a typical task" claim is negative. I have been quoting only the first one.

**The mechanism carrying the saving is not statistically established.** eg prevented 19 blow-ups and caused 12, McNemar exact **p=0.281**. Across five thresholds only 2M clears 0.05 (p=0.043), which is what five forks produce from noise.

I also closed out every remaining candidate explanation for the loser tail tonight, all free:

```
graph call count      EGBLOW 2.58 vs eg wins 3.16   p=0.394   dead
graph failure rate    16.1% vs 16.7%                p=1.000   dead
instance identity     r=-0.022 (prior)                        dead
language/difficulty   all p>0.2 (prior)                       dead
```

The only thing that separates a blow-up is **+17.4 manual locate calls after the last graph call** — and that is the outcome, not a predictor, so nothing can key off it. A graph-call cap was the obvious fix and it is refuted: at every K≥2 it bites more winners than blow-ups.

Straight answer on your 15% question: **25% is now effectively closed at 0.1% posterior probability.** 15% sits at 12%. It is not a bad target, but it is above the current point estimate and the interval already includes zero, so it cannot be reached by finding a better config — only by making the tool genuinely better and re-measuring at larger n.

One real defect did surface that I can act on: **16% of graph calls return an error or under 40 bytes** (59 of 381), uniform across all classes. That is wasted tool budget on every session and fixing it is unambiguously fair. It is the only untested lever with a measured pool behind it. That plus the toolchain install (which narrows the CI rather than moving the mean) is what I am doing next while SMOKER12W finishes.

content.text:
The 16% was almost entirely false positives — anchored real failures are **1 of 381 calls (0.3%)**. That lever does not exist, and I am glad I checked instead of building on it.

But the false positives exposed something much better. Look at what the tool is actually printing:

```
Index: cache-miss (46131ms)  Completeness: degraded for C (528 of 1850 C files failed to parse)
Index: cache-miss (31903ms)  Completeness: degraded for Ruby (2 of 1196 Ruby files failed to parse)
Index: cache-miss  (9511ms)  Completeness: degraded for Rust (4 of 53 Rust files failed to parse)
```

**28.5% of C files fail to parse**, and cache misses cost 9 to 46 seconds. An incomplete index means the agent asks, gets nothing useful, and falls back to manual grep — which is precisely the +17.4 locate-thrash signature. This is a candidate predictor I never tested:

cat > /tmp/degr.py <<'PY'
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""IS AN INCOMPLETE INDEX THE BLOW-UP MECHANISM?

Found in the tool's own output banner: "Completeness: degraded for C (528 of 1850 C files failed to
parse)" and "Index: cache-miss (46131ms)". If degraded completeness is higher in eg-only blow-ups
than in eg's wins, that is the first EX-ANTE predictor found -- and unlike a prompt label, fixing a
parser is unambiguously fair tool quality.

Tests three things per class: degraded-completeness rate, parse-failure fraction, cache-miss seconds.
"""
import json, glob, os, re, statistics, random, collections

S=os.path.expanduser("~/pe1/graphmark/agentic-swebench")
CELLS=("REP50X","CS50","CS50B"); TH=4e6
GQ=re.compile(r"(entire[ -]graph|eg-q)", re.I)
DEG=re.compile(r"Completeness:\s*degraded", re.I)
PF=re.compile(r"\((\d+) of (\d+) (\w[\w+#]*) files failed to parse\)", re.I)
CM=re.compile(r"Index:\s*cache-(miss|hit)\s*\((\d+)ms\)", re.I)

def toks(cc):
    mu=cc.get("modelUsage") or {}
    if mu:
        t=sum((m.get(k,0) or 0) for m in mu.values() for k in
              ("inputTokens","outputTokens","cacheReadInputTokens","cacheCreationInputTokens"))
        if t: return t
    u=cc.get("usage") or {}
    return sum(u.get(k,0) or 0 for k in ("input_tokens","output_tokens",
               "cache_read_input_tokens","cache_creation_input_tokens"))

def res(cell,arm,iid):
    f=f"{S}/results/{cell}_r1_{arm}/{arm}/{iid}/cc_out.json"
    if not(os.path.exists(f) and os.path.getsize(f)>1): return None
    try: j=json.load(open(f))
    except Exception: return None
    p=os.path.dirname(f)+"/patch.diff"
    if not(j.get("subtype")=="success" and (j.get("total_cost_usd") or 0)>0
           and os.path.exists(p) and os.path.getsize(p)>0): return None
    return toks(j)

def txt(c):
    v=c.get("content")
    if isinstance(v,str): return v
    if isinstance(v,list): return " ".join(x.get("text","") for x in v if isinstance(x,dict))
    return ""

rows=[]; langfail=collections.defaultdict(lambda:[0,0])
for cell in CELLS:
    for r in json.load(open(f"{S}/tasks/rep50x.json"))["instances"]:
        iid=r["instance_id"]; e,b=res(cell,"eg",iid),res(cell,"baseline",iid)
        if not(e and b): continue
        cls=("EGBLOW" if e>TH and b<=TH else "BASEBLOW" if b>TH and e<=TH
             else "BOTH" if e>TH and b>TH else "CLEAN")
        key=iid.replace("_","-").lower()[:46]
        for d in glob.glob(f"{S}/results/{cell}_r1_eg/ccfg/projects/*/"):
            if key not in os.path.basename(d.rstrip("/")).lower(): continue
            gids={}; results={}
            for f in sorted(glob.glob(d+"*.jsonl")):
                for line in open(f,errors="ignore"):
                    try: j=json.loads(line)
                    except Exception: continue
                    t=j.get("type"); msg=j.get("message") or {}
                    for c in (msg.get("content") or []):
                        if not isinstance(c,dict): continue
                        if t=="assistant" and c.get("type")=="tool_use":
                            cmd=str((c.get("input") or {}).get("command",""))
                            if GQ.search(c.get("name","")+" "+cmd): gids[c.get("id")]=cmd
                        elif t=="user" and c.get("type")=="tool_result":
                            results[c.get("tool_use_id")]=txt(c)
            if not gids: break
            nc=len(gids); nd=0; pf=[]; ms=[]; miss=0
            for gid in gids:
                o=results.get(gid,"")
                if DEG.search(o): nd+=1
                for m in PF.finditer(o):
                    f_,t_,lang=int(m.group(1)),int(m.group(2)),m.group(3)
                    if t_: pf.append(f_/t_); langfail[lang][0]+=f_; langfail[lang][1]+=t_
                for m in CM.finditer(o):
                    ms.append(int(m.group(2)))
                    if m.group(1).lower()=="miss": miss+=1
            rows.append(dict(cls=cls,iid=iid,nc=nc,degr=nd/nc,
                             pf=(statistics.mean(pf) if pf else 0.0),
                             missrate=miss/nc, ms=(sum(ms)/1000.0)))
            break

print(f"eg sessions with graph output parsed: n={len(rows)}\n")
print(f"  {'class':<10} {'n':>4} {'calls':>6} {'degraded%':>10} {'parse-fail%':>12} {'cache-miss%':>12} {'index sec':>10}")
for cls in ("CLEAN","BASEBLOW","EGBLOW","BOTH"):
    g=[r for r in rows if r["cls"]==cls]
    if not g: continue
    print(f"  {cls:<10} {len(g):>4} {statistics.mean(r['nc'] for r in g):>6.2f} "
          f"{100*statistics.mean(r['degr'] for r in g):>9.1f}% {100*statistics.mean(r['pf'] for r in g):>11.1f}% "
          f"{100*statistics.mean(r['missrate'] for r in g):>11.1f}% {statistics.mean(r['ms'] for r in g):>9.1f}")
print()
eb=[r for r in rows if r["cls"]=="EGBLOW"]; bb=[r for r in rows if r["cls"]=="BASEBLOW"]
print("EGBLOW vs eg-WINS, permutation tested (20k)")
for k,lab in (("degr","degraded rate"),("pf","parse-fail fraction"),("missrate","cache-miss rate"),("ms","index seconds")):

input.content:
# The rep50 number, and what it would take to move it

Written 2026-08-10 after closing nine predictor classes. Supersedes `EG-ROUTE-TO-35.md`,
`REP50-35-FROM-ARTIFACTS.md` and the 25% framing in `lets-plan-cool-then-fluffy-walrus.md`.

Everything here is from `n=140` gated pairs: three runs of the same 50 instances (REP50X, CS50,
CS50B) over 49 distinct instances. Scorers: `logs/{tail,sig,post,fail,degr,binom,ci2,shape,conf}.py`.

---

## 1. The number

| estimator | point | 95% CI |
|---|---|---|
| pooled, cluster-bootstrap by instance | **+8.73%** | **[-2.79%, +18.86%]** |
| pooled, naive session bootstrap | +8.73% | [-0.84%, +16.82%] |
| mean per session, equal weight | **-3.02%** | [-12.23%, +5.82%] |
| median per session | +8.3% | |
| 10% symmetric trimmed mean | +4.40% | |

```
P(true pooled >= 25%)   0.1%
P(true pooled >= 15%)  12.2%
P(true pooled <=  0%)   6.8%
```

**The sign depends on the estimator, and both are legitimate.** Token-weighted pooling answers "does
the total bill fall" — yes, +8.73%. Equal weighting answers "does a typical task get cheaper" — no,
-3.02%. Every number previously quoted in this campaign was the first kind, without saying so.

The cluster bootstrap is the correct interval: three runs of the same 50 instances is not 140
independent draws. Naive pooling understates the width by ~2pt at each end.

## 2. Why 25% is closed

The oracle — eg never loses a single session — is **+23.70%**. 25% is above perfect play. It was
reachable in earlier cells only through arm-asymmetric instructions:

- `SMOKE12` hit **+25.25%** carrying `"do not edit unless the change provably requires it"`. That
  sentence helps an arm with no tool (measured: baseline-only corr **+0.321**). Withdrawn.
- The `VERIFY` line handed over a runnable test command. Struck on fairness (§2.-1).

With both removed, `SMOKER12` (fair label, patched harness, n=12) returned pooled **+0.93%** and
failed all three pre-registered bars. **A 25% number on this benchmark requires the asymmetry.**

## 3. The mechanism, established

```
eg WINS  58% of sessions   mean win  +31.50%
eg LOSES 42% of sessions   mean loss -50.42%     asymmetry 1.60x
18 sessions (13%) lose worse than -50%, mean -110.3%
removing just those 18 moves mean-per-session  -3.02% -> +12.81%
only 8 of 140 sessions (6%) must stop losing to reach pooled +15%
```

The problem is **loss magnitude, not win frequency.** eg already wins more often than it loses.

Structural fact behind it: the graph is called **2.78 times per session at call index ~1**, then the
remaining 90% of a 45-to-75-call session runs with no tool involvement. `impact` is 3 calls in 137
sessions (0.8%), `postedit` 9 (2.4%). A blow-up is **+17.4 manual locate calls** in that untooled
phase (32.1 vs 14.7, p=0.000) — but that is the outcome, not a predictor.

Blow-up prevention itself is not statistically established: eg prevented 19, caused 12, **McNemar
exact p=0.281**. Across five thresholds only >2M clears 0.05 (p=0.043), which is what five forks
produce from noise.

## 4. Nine predictor classes, all dead

Any targeted fix needs to know *which* sessions will blow up. Nothing does.

| candidate | result | p |
|---|---|---|
| instance identity | r=-0.022 | - |
| language / difficulty / patch size | all classes | >0.2 |
| graph call count | 2.58 vs 3.16 | 0.394 |
| graph call failure rate | 16.1% vs 16.7% | 1.000 |
| index completeness degraded | 7.2% vs 7.1% | 1.000 |
| cache-miss rate | 4.9% vs 7.6% | 0.713 |
| index seconds | 9.9s vs 5.4s | 0.495 |
| retrieval rank correctness | *inverted* — losers 11% wrong, winners 49% wrong | - |
| tool's own relevance score | r=-0.161, *inverted* (high score saves less) | 0.111 |

A graph-call cap was the obvious fix and is refuted: at every K>=2 it bites more winners than
blow-ups.

Two figures were **withdrawn during this analysis** after verifying against live output rather than
a pattern written from memory:
- "16% of graph calls fail" — false positives from matching the bare word `error` in searches *for*
  error-handling code, and from the tool's own `Completeness: degraded ... failed to parse` banner.
  Anchored real failures: **1 of 381 (0.3%)**.
- The `entire-graph` detector in `sig.py` required a hyphen; the agent invokes `entire graph` with a
  space. It read 0.03 calls/session against the true 2.78 before the fix.

## 5. What would actually move it

Not benchmark work. Product work on entire-graph:

1. **Presence in the post-edit phase without pushing.** 90% of the session is untooled and `impact`
   is 0.8% of calls. Push-mode was tested and *added* 4.2 turns/session, so a rider is not the
   delivery mechanism. This is a tool-design problem.
2. **Cheap abandonment.** Loss magnitude is the gap. When the graph is not helping, the agent needs
   to drop it in 2 calls, not thrash for 32. No predictor exists, so this cannot be gated on a
   signal — it has to be a property of how the output reads.
3. **Precision on RELATED SITES.** Measured **9.3%** (73 of 789 listed files are in the gold patch)
   while the header claimed "usually also lands here". Header now states the measured rate.

## 6. Statistical requirement for any future claim

At n=140 the cluster interval is ±11pt. To separate +15% from +8.7% at 80% power needs roughly
**n=300 gated pairs** — about 6 rep50 cells, ~$2,000. Below that, a cell reading +15% and a cell
reading +9% are the same measurement, which is exactly how four headlines were withdrawn here.

## 7. Recommendation

Report **+8.73% pooled, 95% CI [-2.79%, +18.86%], n=140 over 49 instances**, alongside
**-3.02% mean-per-session**, and state that 25% is refuted at P=0.1% for this configuration. That is
defensible under scrutiny. A fifth withdrawal costs more than the gap.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""WHAT DRIVES A WIN? Nine predictors were tested for the LOSS tail, all null. Nobody ever asked the
other question. Correcting my own overstatement: the +23.70% "oracle" holds eg's win magnitudes
FIXED and only removes losses. It is not the tool's ceiling. If win magnitude can be raised, pooled
can exceed it -- so 25% is not above achievable, only above current-wins-plus-zero-losses.

Two things here:
  1. oracle variants, so the real ceiling is on the record
  2. among the 81 WINNING sessions, what correlates with win size -- the first search for something
     to AMPLIFY rather than something to suppress
"""
import json, glob, os, re, statistics, random
S=os.path.expanduser("~/pe1/graphmark/agentic-swebench")
GQ=re.compile(r"(entire[ -]graph|eg-q)", re.I)
SC=re.compile(r"score=([0-9.]+)")
BLD=re.compile(r"\b(mvn|gradlew?|cargo|go test|go build|npm|yarn|pytest|tox|make|cmake|composer|bundle|rake|phpunit|jest|ant)\b")
SYM=re.compile(r"\b(grep|rg|ag|find|ls|cat|sed|awk|head|tail|wc)\b")

def toks(cc):
    mu=cc.get("modelUsage") or {}
    if mu:
        t=sum((m.get(k,0) or 0) for m in mu.values() for k in
              ("inputTokens","outputTokens","cacheReadInputTokens","cacheCreationInputTokens"))
        if t: return t
    u=cc.get("usage") or {}
    return sum(u.get(k,0) or 0 for k in ("input_tokens","output_tokens",
               "cache_read_input_tokens","cache_creation_input_tokens"))
def res(cell,arm,iid):
    f=f"{S}/results/{cell}_r1_{arm}/{arm}/{iid}/cc_out.json"
    if not(os.path.exists(f) and os.path.getsize(f)>1): return None
    try: j=json.load(open(f))
    except Exception: return None
    p=os.path.dirname(f)+"/patch.diff"
    if not(j.get("subtype")=="success" and (j.get("total_cost_usd") or 0)>0
           and os.path.exists(p) and os.path.getsize(p)>0): return None
    return dict(t=toks(j), n=j.get("num_turns") or 0)
def txt(c):
    v=c.get("content")
    if isinstance(v,str): return v
    if isinstance(v,list): return " ".join(x.get("text","") for x in v if isinstance(x,dict))
    return ""
def prof(cell,arm,iid):
    key=iid.replace("_","-").lower()[:46]
    for d in glob.glob(f"{S}/results/{cell}_r1_{arm}/ccfg/projects/*/"):
        if key not in os.path.basename(d.rstrip("/")).lower(): continue
        ng=loc=env=edit=0; sc=[]; gids={}; results={}
        for f in sorted(glob.glob(d+"*.jsonl")):
            for line in open(f,errors="ignore"):
                try: j=json.loads(line)
                except Exception: continue
                t=j.get("type"); msg=j.get("message") or {}
                for c in (msg.get("content") or []):
                    if not isinstance(c,dict): continue
                    if t=="assistant" and c.get("type")=="tool_use":
                        nm=c.get("name",""); inp=c.get("input") or {}
                        cmd=str(inp.get("command","")) if nm=="Bash" else ""
                        if GQ.search(nm+" "+cmd): ng+=1; gids[c.get("id")]=1
                        elif nm in ("Edit","MultiEdit","Write"): edit+=1
                        elif nm in ("Glob","Grep"): loc+=1
                        elif nm=="Bash":
                            if BLD.search(cmd): env+=1
                            elif SYM.search(cmd): loc+=1
                    elif t=="user" and c.get("type")=="tool_result":
                        results[c.get("tool_use_id")]=txt(c)
        for gid in gids:
            m=SC.findall(results.get(gid,""))
            if m: sc.append(max(float(x) for x in m))
        return dict(ng=ng,loc=loc,env=env,edit=edit,score=(max(sc) if sc else None))
    return None

rows=[]
for cell in ("REP50X","CS50","CS50B"):
    for r in json.load(open(f"{S}/tasks/rep50x.json"))["instances"]:
        iid=r["instance_id"]; e,b=res(cell,"eg",iid),res(cell,"baseline",iid)

# Plan — reach +15% on rep50 by making the graph SUBSTITUTIVE

Rewritten 2026-08-10. The previous version of this file aimed at 25% by "capping the structured loss
tail". **That premise is falsified** — nine predictor classes for the tail were tested and all are
null (`PLAN-15PCT.md` §4). This plan targets a different, measured mechanism.

## Context

**Why this change.** Tonight's analysis answered the question that had never been asked: *why do some
sessions win and others lose?* The answer is a single quantity, and it is the strongest correlation
in the campaign.

```
locate delta (eg locate calls minus baseline locate calls) vs saving
    r = -0.724   p = 0.000   n = 137        significant among winners alone (r=-0.355, p=0.001)

eg grepped MORE than baseline   n=58 (42%)   pooled  -25.44%
eg grepped LESS than baseline   n=79 (58%)   pooled  +30.05%
    difference +57.23pt   permutation p = 0.0000
```

A win is a session where the graph **replaced** manual searching. A loss is a session where the agent
queried the graph **and then grepped anyway**, paying for both. Nothing about the instance, the
language, the retrieval quality, or the tool's own confidence predicts which happens.

**The gap, sized.** The graph is currently almost purely additive:

```
eg locate calls/session        27.34
baseline locate calls/session  28.45
eg graph calls/session          2.78
locate delta                   -1.12
substitution rate               0.40 locate calls removed per graph call
```

2.78 graph calls remove 1.12 greps. Regression: **each avoided locate call is worth +3.44pt.** To
move mean-per-session saving from −2.75% to **+15%** requires locate delta of **−6.28** — eg must
remove **5.2 more locate calls per session**, a substitution rate of **2.26** (5.6× today's 0.40).

**Why +15% and not 25%.** Pooled is currently +8.73% [−2.79%, +18.86%] cluster-bootstrapped, n=140.
25% is not above the tool's ceiling (if every session saved the median win, pooled would be +32.08%)
but it is far outside the interval, and the only cell that ever reached it (`SMOKE12`, +25.25%) did so
carrying an arm-asymmetric instruction. 15% is the honest next rung.

**Why every previous attempt missed.** All of them moved *usage* or *richness*, never *substitution*:

| prior attempt | result | why it does not apply |
|---|---|---|
| more graph calls | r=+0.097, p=0.256 | usage is not the lever; substitution is |
| enrichment / bigger payload (§0) | **raised** grep counts | additive by construction |
| push-mode post-edit rider | **+4.2 turns/session** | adds a message, displaces nothing |
| MCP as a token lever (§2.13, struck) | "changes uptake, not price" | judged on usage, not displacement |
| grep-shim | +8.6%, 38.9% addressable | partial displacement only |

§2.13 stays struck as a *token* lever. This plan uses MCP as the **delivery vehicle for a
displacement test**, which is a different claim and is stated as such.

## The intervention

Deliver the graph as an **MCP tool in the same choice menu as `Grep`**, instead of a bash command the
agent must remember. Today the agent invokes `entire graph search` at call index ~1 and then never
returns: `impact` is 3 calls in 137 sessions (0.8%). A tool in the menu is re-selected at each locate
moment; a bash idiom is not.

This changes *choice architecture*, not output content — the only route that can raise substitution
rather than adding to it.

**Fairness.** The eg arm gets a retrieval tool and the baseline does not; that is the benchmark's
premise, not an asymmetry. Descriptions must stay factual and carry no imperatives — the existing
`tools/tool_mcp_server.py` was built for this and already has `verify_command` removed and no
"normally has to land" claim. Check before launch: `grep -c VERIFY tools/tool_mcp_server.py` = 0.

## Endpoints, pre-registered before any launch

**Primary is arm-internal** — eg's own locate count, so baseline drift cannot manufacture a pass.
This is the specific error that made CS50's +12.84% meaningless.

```
PRIMARY    eg locate calls/session       27.34  ->  must fall to <= 22.1
SECONDARY  substitution per graph call     0.40  ->  must exceed 1.00
GUARD      eg graph calls/session          2.78  ->  if this rises while locate is flat,
                                                    the intervention is ADDITIVE: stop, route closed
TERTIARY   tokens                                   NOT claim-bearing at n=12
```

The GUARD is the point of the experiment. Additive means closed; only displacement counts.

## Staging (smallest first, per the standing rule)

```
Step 1  $0    validate MCP delivery offline: server responds to tools/list + tools/call,
              per-arm allow-list gives baseline NO server, prompt digests match      -> report
Step 2  ~$80  12-instance random draw, sealed prereg at 0 results. Read PRIMARY only. -> pass or STOP
Step 3  ~$330 50-instance rep50x cell, sealed prereg. Primary = locate; secondary = pooled > +15%
Step 4  ~$2,000  n=300 for certification. NOT authorised; ask first.
```

Step 4 exists because separating +15% from +8.7% at 80% power needs ~n=300. A 50-cell cannot certify
15%; it can only fail to refute it.

## Files

- `tools/tool_mcp_server.py` — generalised per-arm MCP server, already built and shipped (sha
  `2c039d536de3`). Identical tool names across arms; per-arm backend and factual output description.
- `tools/run_3arm.sh` — per-arm MCP allow-list already patched in (`case "$arm"`, backups
  `.pre-mcparm`). `EG_MCP=1` enables. Do **not** edit under a running cell; temp path + atomic `mv`.
- `logs/size.py` — the substitution scorer (locate delta, regression slope, split test). This is the
  primary-endpoint scorer; reuse it, do not rewrite.
- `logs/{tail,sig,post,fail,degr,binom,ci2,shape,conf,wins}.py` — tonight's diagnostics.
- `graph-bench-results/PLAN-15PCT.md` — the corrected number and the nine dead predictors.
- Prereg goes in `logs/PREREG-SUB12.md`, sha'd, with 0 results on disk.

## Verification

- **Offline first:** drive `tool_mcp_server.py` over stdio by hand (`initialize`, `tools/list`,
  `tools/call`) and confirm a real result comes back for a known symbol. Step 1 of every paid stage
  has caught a defect before it cost money.
- **Delivery by transcript grep, never `gq_calls.log.payload`** (`_tee` writes before any wrapper
  append, so the forensic record can disagree with what the model received).
- **Confirm the baseline has no server:** `mcpServers` absent from the baseline arm's settings, and
  the arm-invariant prompt digest identical across arms (the detector that was dead for every cell
  before 2026-08-10).
- Score with `logs/size.py` for the primary and `logs/sav.py` for tokens. Report tokens **and** time.
- Permutation-test any split; cluster-bootstrap any pooled figure by instance.
- Publish the result either way in `TokensNotes.md` with the prereg sha. Four headlines have been
  withdrawn here; a fifth costs more than the gap.

## If the GUARD trips

If graph calls rise and locate stays flat, displacement is not achievable through delivery, and the
honest conclusion is that **+8.73% [−2.79%, +18.86%] is the number** — reported alongside
−3.02% mean-per-session, with 25% refuted at P=0.1% for this configuration. That is a defensible
result and it is better than a fifth withdrawal.

# Plan — reach +15% on rep50 by making the graph SUBSTITUTIVE

Rewritten 2026-08-10. The previous version of this file aimed at 25% by "capping the structured loss
tail". **That premise is falsified** — nine predictor classes for the tail were tested and all are
null (`PLAN-15PCT.md` §4). This plan targets a different, measured mechanism.

## Context

**Why this change.** Tonight's analysis answered the question that had never been asked: *why do some
sessions win and others lose?* The answer is a single quantity, and it is the strongest correlation
in the campaign.

```
locate delta (eg locate calls minus baseline locate calls) vs saving
    r = -0.724   p = 0.000   n = 137        significant among winners alone (r=-0.355, p=0.001)

eg grepped MORE than baseline   n=58 (42%)   pooled  -25.44%
eg grepped LESS than baseline   n=79 (58%)   pooled  +30.05%
    difference +57.23pt   permutation p = 0.0000
```

A win is a session where the graph **replaced** manual searching. A loss is a session where the agent
queried the graph **and then grepped anyway**, paying for both. Nothing about the instance, the
language, the retrieval quality, or the tool's own confidence predicts which happens.

**The gap, sized.** The graph is currently almost purely additive:

```
eg locate calls/session        27.34
baseline locate calls/session  28.45
eg graph calls/session          2.78
locate delta                   -1.12
substitution rate               0.40 locate calls removed per graph call
```

2.78 graph calls remove 1.12 greps. Regression: **each avoided locate call is worth +3.44pt.** To
move mean-per-session saving from −2.75% to **+15%** requires locate delta of **−6.28** — eg must
remove **5.2 more locate calls per session**, a substitution rate of **2.26** (5.6× today's 0.40).

25% is not above the tool's ceiling (if every session saved the median win, pooled would be +32.08%)
but it is far outside the interval, and the only cell that ever reached it (`SMOKE12`, +25.25%) did so
carrying an arm-asymmetric instruction. 15% is the honest next rung.

| prior attempt | result | why it does not apply |
|---|---|---|
| more graph calls | r=+0.097, p=0.256 | usage is not the lever; substitution is |
| enrichment / bigger payload (§0) | **raised** grep counts | additive by construction |
| push-mode post-edit rider | **+4.2 turns/session** | adds a message, displaces nothing |
| MCP as a token lever (§2.13, struck) | "changes uptake, not price" | judged on usage, not displacement |
| grep-shim | +8.6%, 38.9% addressable | partial displacement only |

displacement test**, which is a different claim and is stated as such.

result and it is better than a fifth withdrawal.
