content.description:
Blocking work before the 300x4 Gemini cell. Do NOT install toolchains while SMOKER12 is live (agents probe for go/cargo/bundle mid-session; installing under a running cell contaminates it).

1a. INSTALL MISSING TOOLCHAINS on graphbench-c: go, cargo/rustc, bundle(ruby), pytest, dotnet.
    Why: 129/300 of multilingual_300 (Rust 43 + Go 42 + Ruby 44) cannot run their own tests; env/build is 19.26 calls/session = 35% of a session, symmetric across arms. This is H4 from the plan: it does not change the ratio, it strips ~12 calls/session of noise from BOTH arms and shrinks the +-13pt CI that makes 3%/9%/13%/16% indistinguishable.
    Verify: `command -v go cargo rustc pytest bundle` all resolve; re-run logs/toolchain.py and confirm the MISSING count drops to 0.

1b. WRITE run_quad.sh — 4-arm driver (baseline, eg, cmm, graphify) carrying run_paired.sh's guards:
    - PKG_ISO per-arm FATAL check
    - /tmp purge decline -> FATAL (the patched behaviour)
    - half-complete tuple -> results/<TAG>_r1.unpaired.txt + QUAD_STRICT=1 refuses
    - prompt_invariant.sha256 compared unconditionally, missing = FATAL
    - harness exit code checked (exit 2 stops the cell)
    - **ARM ORDER ROTATION** by instance index (Latin-square / rotate by _idx % 4). Without this, arm 4 always gets the warmest machine state and the 4-arm result is uninterpretable. run_matrix.sh/run_ladder.sh do fixed-order sweeps and lack run_3arm.sh's protections - do NOT use them.

1c. GEMINI PATH: CC_AGENT=gemini, MODEL=gemini-3.6-flash, max effort. Set maxSessionTurns IDENTICALLY for all 4 arms (Gemini has no --max-turns; an uncapped arm voids the comparison). Note the harness's own caveat: Gemini reports cache_creation=0 (no cache-write class), so its numbers are a self-contained 4-arm comparison, NOT comparable to the Claude cells.

Files: tools/run_quad.sh (new), tools/run_3arm.sh:2984+ (gemini branch), logs/toolchain.py (verifier).

content.text: Now the porting logic:

input.command:
cat >> /tmp/port_fixes.py <<'PYEOF'

OLD_BATCH = '''    if [ "${EG_BATCH:-0}" = 1 ]; then
      TOOLNOTE="

A precomputed code-search tool is available: $gq . Use it to LOCATE code instead of grep/find:
  $gq search \\"<what you are looking for, one sentence>\\"   <-- ranked relevant code (file:line + source)
Search whenever you need to find something — the first time and for each new thing (related call
sites, similar logic). It is authoritative; do not grep to re-locate what it already found.
Rules:
(1) SEARCH FIRST — never grep/find/cat to locate code before searching.
(2) Read the specific lines you need (a line range around the reported line), not whole files.
(3) NEVER issue a lone shell command. Batch everything you need into ONE Bash call
    (\\`cmd1; cmd2; cmd3\\`) — each separate call re-reads your entire context and costs far more
    than the few bytes it returns.
(4) To check your work, run \\`git diff\\` ONCE. Do NOT re-open files you have already edited.
(5) Run the test suite AT MOST TWICE. It is not the deliverable — your working-tree diff is.
    Never write throwaway test scripts, and never loop edit->run->edit chasing a green suite.
(6) FIX IT PROPERLY. Work the issue until the described behaviour is actually correct:
    - handle the edge cases the issue names (empty, nil, negative, unicode, error paths)
    - change EVERY site that needs it, not only the first one you found (search again to find them)
    - re-read your edited code and check it against the issue before you finish
    Do not stop at the first plausible edit. A fast wrong patch is worth nothing."
    fi'''

NEW_BATCH = '''    if [ "${EG_BATCH:-0}" = 1 ]; then
      # TOOL FACTS ONLY. Rules 2-6 were tool-free methodology and now reach every arm via
      # SHARED_EXTRA, so this flag still tests them -- against a baseline that receives them too.
      TOOLNOTE="

A precomputed code-search tool is available: $gq . Use it to LOCATE code instead of grep/find:
  $gq search \\"<what you are looking for, one sentence>\\"   <-- ranked relevant code (file:line + source)
Search whenever you need to find something — the first time and for each new thing (related call
sites, similar logic). It is authoritative; do not grep to re-locate what it already found.
Rules:
(1) SEARCH FIRST — never grep/find/cat to locate code before searching."
    fi'''

OLD_VERIFY = '''    _strip_verify() {
      case "${EG_VERIFY_MODE:-full}" in
        off|safe|noworld) python3 "$D/_egverify.py" ;;
        *) cat ;;
      esac
    }'''

NEW_VERIFY = '''    # VERIFY IS REMOVED UNCONDITIONALLY (2026-08-10). Not defaulted off -- removed. No value of any
    # variable delivers it. A runnable test command is build knowledge, not retrieval output: it
    # would help an arm with no tool, so it fails the only fairness test this benchmark has. It was
    # struck on those grounds and the strike kept escaping: the mode DEFAULTED to `full`, only 34 of
    # 63 configs pinned off, and eg_mcp_server.py bypassed the flag by reading the payload directly.
    # Old plumbing kept as a comment so the history stays legible:
    #   case "${EG_VERIFY_MODE:-full}" in
    #     off|safe|noworld) python3 "$D/_egverify.py" ;;   # strip
    #     *) cat ;;                                        # deliver  <-- the cheat
    #   esac
    _strip_verify() {
      python3 "$D/_egverify.py"
    }'''

VERIFY_GUARD = '''  # VERIFY IS REMOVED (2026-08-10). eg-q strips it unconditionally, so EG_VERIFY_MODE is inert. A
  # config still asking for a DELIVERING value is stale and its author expects the struck behaviour,
  # so fail loudly rather than run something the operator misunderstands.
  case "${EG_VERIFY_MODE:-off}" in
    off|safe|noworld|"") : ;;
    *) echo "FATAL: EG_VERIFY_MODE='${EG_VERIFY_MODE}' asks for a VERIFY line, which was struck on" >&2
       echo "       fairness and is now removed unconditionally. Drop it from this config." >&2
       exit 2 ;;
  esac
'''

def die(m):
    print(f"  ABORT: {m}"); sys.exit(1)

r = open(R).read()
q = open(Q).read()
steps = []

# ---- run_3arm.sh ----
if "shared_discipline()" in r:
    steps.append("run_3arm: functions already present, skipped")
else:
    i = r.find(OLD_SYM_START)
    if i < 0: die("old sym_rules header not found")
    j = r.find("\n}\n", r.find("TXT", i))
    if j < 0: die("old sym_rules terminator not found")
    if OLD_SYM_MARK not in r[i:j]: die("old sym_rules body does not carry the expected text")
    r = r[:i] + NEW_SD + "\n" + NEW_FNS + "\n" + NEW_SR + r[j+3:]
    steps.append("run_3arm: sym_rules split + shared_discipline + rule blocks + guard inserted")

if "$(shared_discipline)" in r and "SHARED_EXTRA:-" in r.split("Implement a correct, minimal, general fix")[1][:200]:
    steps.append("run_3arm: prompt assembly already wired, skipped")
else:
    old = "- Implement a correct, minimal, general fix.$TOOLNOTE"
    if old not in r: die("prompt assembly anchor not found")
    r = r.replace(old, "- Implement a correct, minimal, general fix.$(shared_discipline)${SHARED_EXTRA:-}$TOOLNOTE", 1)
    steps.append("run_3arm: prompt assembly wired (shared_discipline + SHARED_EXTRA)")

if "assert_prompt_symmetry \"$arm\"" in r:
    steps.append("run_3arm: guard call already present, skipped")
else:
    anchor = 'printf \'%s\' "$PROMPT" > "$out/prompt.txt"'
    if anchor not in r: die("prompt.txt persist anchor not found")
    r = r.replace(anchor, anchor + '\n\n# Symmetry guard on the ARM-SPECIFIC blocks only; the base prompt and shared_discipline are\n# identical across arms by construction, so scanning them would false-positive every run.\nassert_prompt_symmetry "$arm" "${TOOLNOTE:-}${EGTOOL:-}" || exit 2', 1)
    steps.append("run_3arm: guard call added after prompt persist")

if OLD_BATCH in r:
    r = r.replace(OLD_BATCH, NEW_BATCH, 1)
    steps.append("run_3arm: EG_BATCH block reduced to tool facts")
elif "Rules 2-6 were tool-free" in r:
    steps.append("run_3arm: EG_BATCH already reduced, skipped")
else:
    steps.append("run_3arm: EG_BATCH block TEXT DIFFERS -- left alone, guard will flag it")

if "EG_VERIFY_MODE='${EG_VERIFY_MODE}' asks for a VERIFY line" in r:
    steps.append("run_3arm: VERIFY guard already present, skipped")
else:
    anchor = '  gq="$out/eg-q.run"'
    if anchor not in r: die("eg-q.run anchor not found")
    r = r.replace(anchor, VERIFY_GUARD + anchor, 1)
    steps.append("run_3arm: VERIFY abort guard added")

r = r.replace('EG_VERIFY_MODE="${EG_VERIFY_MODE:-full}"', 'EG_VERIFY_MODE="off"')

# ---- eg-q.orig ----
if "VERIFY IS REMOVED UNCONDITIONALLY" in q:
    steps.append("eg-q.orig: VERIFY already removed, skipped")
elif OLD_VERIFY in q:
    q = q.replace(OLD_VERIFY, NEW_VERIFY, 1)
    steps.append("eg-q.orig: VERIFY removed unconditionally")
else:
    die("eg-q.orig _strip_verify block not found in expected form")

for p, new in ((R, r), (Q, q)):
    shutil.copy2(p, p + ".pre-fairport")
    open(p + ".new", "w").write(new)
    os.replace(p + ".new", p)     # atomic
for s in steps: print(f"  {s}")
print(f"  run_3arm.sh {len(r.splitlines())} lines   eg-q.orig {len(q.splitlines())} lines")

1a. INSTALL MISSING TOOLCHAINS on graphbench-c: go, cargo/rustc, bundle(ruby), pytest, dotnet.
    Why: 129/300 of multilingual_300 (Rust 43 + Go 42 + Ruby 44) cannot run their own tests; env/build is 19.26 calls/session = 35% of a session, symmetric across arms. This is H4 from the plan: it does not change the ratio, it strips ~12 calls/session of noise from BOTH arms and shrinks the +-13pt CI that makes 3%/9%/13%/16% indistinguishable.
    Verify: `command -v go cargo rustc pytest bundle` all resolve; re-run logs/toolchain.py and confirm the MISSING count drops to 0.

1b. WRITE run_quad.sh — 4-arm driver (baseline, eg, cmm, graphify) carrying run_paired.sh's guards:
    - PKG_ISO per-arm FATAL check
    - /tmp purge decline -> FATAL (the patched behaviour)
    - half-complete tuple -> results/<TAG>_r1.unpaired.txt + QUAD_STRICT=1 refuses
    - prompt_invariant.sha256 compared unconditionally, missing = FATAL
    - harness exit code checked (exit 2 stops the cell)
    - **ARM ORDER ROTATION** by instance index (Latin-square / rotate by _idx % 4). Without this, arm 4 always gets the warmest machine state and the 4-arm result is uninterpretable. run_matrix.sh/run_ladder.sh do fixed-order sweeps and lack run_3arm.sh's protections - do NOT use them.

1c. GEMINI PATH: CC_AGENT=gemini, MODEL=gemini-3.6-flash, max effort. Set maxSessionTurns IDENTICALLY for all 4 arms (Gemini has no --max-turns; an uncapped arm voids the comparison). Note the harness's own caveat: Gemini reports cache_creation=0 (no cache-write class), so its numbers are a self-contained 4-arm comparison, NOT comparable to the Claude cells.

content.description:
Blocking work before the 300x4 Gemini cell. Do NOT install toolchains while SMOKER12 is live (agents probe for go/cargo/bundle mid-session; installing under a running cell contaminates it).

1a. INSTALL MISSING TOOLCHAINS on graphbench-c: go, cargo/rustc, bundle(ruby), pytest, dotnet.
    Why: 129/300 of multilingual_300 (Rust 43 + Go 42 + Ruby 44) cannot run their own tests; env/build is 19.26 calls/session = 35% of a session, symmetric across arms. This is H4 from the plan: it does not change the ratio, it strips ~12 calls/session of noise from BOTH arms and shrinks the +-13pt CI that makes 3%/9%/13%/16% indistinguishable.
    Verify: `command -v go cargo rustc pytest bundle` all resolve; re-run logs/toolchain.py and confirm the MISSING count drops to 0.

1b. WRITE run_quad.sh — 4-arm driver (baseline, eg, cmm, graphify) carrying run_paired.sh's guards:
    - PKG_ISO per-arm FATAL check
    - /tmp purge decline -> FATAL (the patched behaviour)
    - half-complete tuple -> results/<TAG>_r1.unpaired.txt + QUAD_STRICT=1 refuses
    - prompt_invariant.sha256 compared unconditionally, missing = FATAL
    - harness exit code checked (exit 2 stops the cell)

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Build the entire-graph NDJSON dump for one repo @ base_commit, on the HOST (native binary).
# Output: <out>/graph.symbols.ndjson + <out>/graph.edges.ndjson  (fed into the treated container).
set -uo pipefail
SUITE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"   # suite root = parent of tools/
PY="$SUITE/.venv/bin/python"; [ -x "$PY" ] || PY=python3
repo="$1"; commit="$2"; out="$3"
cache="$SUITE/repo-cache/$(echo "$repo" | tr '/' '__')"
mkdir -p "$out"
out="$(cd "$out" && pwd)"   # absolutize before we cd into the repo cache
if [ ! -d "$cache/.git" ]; then
  echo "[clone] $repo -> $cache"
  git clone --quiet "https://github.com/$repo" "$cache" || { echo "CLONE FAILED"; exit 1; }
fi
cd "$cache" || exit 1
git fetch --quiet origin "$commit" 2>/dev/null || git fetch --quiet --all 2>/dev/null
git checkout --quiet "$commit" 2>&1 | tail -1 || { echo "CHECKOUT FAILED $commit"; exit 1; }
# entire-graph provider command. Canonical name after the sem->graph rename is `entire graph`
# (what `entire plugin install entire-graph` registers). Override with ENTIRE_GRAPH=... for a
# host that still has the legacy `entire sem` plugin.
GRAPH="${ENTIRE_GRAPH:-entire graph}"

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""FEASIBILITY CEILING on substitution, before spending on REP30.

The plan needs substitution 0.40 -> 2.26 locate calls displaced per graph call. That is only possible
if eg's 27.34 locate calls/session are the KIND of question a code graph can answer. Classify them:

  GRAPH-ANSWERABLE  symbol/definition lookup, "who calls", content search for an identifier,
                    find-file-by-name  -> a graph verb exists for these
  NOT ANSWERABLE    directory listing, reading a known path, line counts, tail/head of a log,
                    build-output inspection -> no graph verb, and shouldn't have one

If the answerable share is small, no delivery change can reach 2.26 and the route is closed.
"""
import json, os, glob, re, statistics, collections
S=os.path.expanduser("~/pe1/graphmark/agentic-swebench")
GQ=re.compile(r"(entire[ -]graph|eg-q)", re.I)
BLD=re.compile(r"\b(mvn|gradlew?|cargo|go test|go build|npm|yarn|pytest|tox|make|cmake|composer|bundle|rake|phpunit|jest|ant)\b")

# graph-answerable: searching for an identifier/text in code, or locating a file by name
ANS = re.compile(r"\b(grep|rg|ag)\b|\bfind\b[^|]*-name|\bgit grep\b", re.I)
# not answerable: pure filesystem/inspection verbs with no code-semantics question
NOT = re.compile(r"^\s*(ls|cat|head|tail|wc|pwd|cd|echo|which|env|du|df|tree|file|stat)\b", re.I)

def toks(cc):
    mu=cc.get("modelUsage") or {}
    if mu:
        t=sum((m.get(k,0) or 0) for m in mu.values() for k in
              ("inputTokens","outputTokens","cacheReadInputTokens","cacheCreationInputTokens"))
        if t: return t
    u=cc.get("usage") or {}
    return sum(u.get(k,0) or 0 for k in ("input_tokens","output_tokens",
               "cache_read_input_tokens","cache_creation_input_tokens"))
def gated(cell,arm,iid):

           and os.path.exists(p) and os.path.getsize(p)>0): return None

Blocking work before the 300x4 Gemini cell. Do NOT install toolchains while SMOKER12 is live (agents probe for go/cargo/bundle mid-session; installing under a running cell contaminates it).

1a. INSTALL MISSING TOOLCHAINS on graphbench-c: go, cargo/rustc, bundle(ruby), pytest, dotnet.
    Why: 129/300 of multilingual_300 (Rust 43 + Go 42 + Ruby 44) cannot run their own tests; env/build is 19.26 calls/session = 35% of a session, symmetric across arms. This is H4 from the plan: it does not change the ratio, it strips ~12 calls/session of noise from BOTH arms and shrinks the +-13pt CI that makes 3%/9%/13%/16% indistinguishable.
    Verify: `command -v go cargo rustc pytest bundle` all resolve; re-run logs/toolchain.py and confirm the MISSING count drops to 0.

1b. WRITE run_quad.sh — 4-arm driver (baseline, eg, cmm, graphify) carrying run_paired.sh's guards:
    - PKG_ISO per-arm FATAL check
    - /tmp purge decline -> FATAL (the patched behaviour)
    - half-complete tuple -> results/<TAG>_r1.unpaired.txt + QUAD_STRICT=1 refuses
    - prompt_invariant.sha256 compared unconditionally, missing = FATAL
    - harness exit code checked (exit 2 stops the cell)
    - **ARM ORDER ROTATION** by instance index (Latin-square / rotate by _idx % 4). Without this, arm 4 always gets the warmest machine state and the 4-arm result is uninterpretable. run_matrix.sh/run_ladder.sh do fixed-order sweeps and lack run_3arm.sh's protections - do NOT use them.

1c. GEMINI PATH: CC_AGENT=gemini, MODEL=gemini-3.6-flash, max effort. Set maxSessionTurns IDENTICALLY for all 4 arms (Gemini has no --max-turns; an uncapped arm voids the comparison). Note the harness's own caveat: Gemini reports cache_creation=0 (no cache-write class), so its numbers are a self-contained 4-arm comparison, NOT comparable to the Claude cells.

Files: tools/run_quad.sh (new), tools/run_3arm.sh:2984+ (gemini branch), logs/toolchain.py (verifier).

1b. WRITE run_quad.sh — 4-arm driver (baseline, eg, cmm, graphify) carrying run_paired.sh's guards:

    - prompt_invariant.sha256 compared unconditionally, missing = FATAL
    - harness exit code checked (exit 2 stops the cell)
    - **ARM ORDER ROTATION** by instance index (Latin-square / rotate by _idx % 4). Without this, arm 4 always gets the warmest machine state and the 4-arm result is uninterpretable. run_matrix.sh/run_ladder.sh do fixed-order sweeps and lack run_3arm.sh's protections - do NOT use them.

1c. GEMINI PATH: CC_AGENT=gemini, MODEL=gemini-3.6-flash, max effort. Set maxSessionTurns IDENTICALLY for all 4 arms (Gemini has no --max-turns; an uncapped arm voids the comparison). Note the harness's own caveat: Gemini reports cache_creation=0 (no cache-write class), so its numbers are a self-contained 4-arm comparison, NOT comparable to the Claude cells.

Two things I got wrong getting here, both worth stating.

**The launch failed twice on my own bugs.** First I removed `export EG_VERIFY_MODE=off` from the config, reasoning it was inert now that VERIFY is hard-stripped — but `run_3arm.sh` has a pre-existing gate that refuses to run when it is unset, precisely because "nine configs silently inherited `full`". Second, and worse: my port script wrote each patched file and `os.replace`'d it into position, which **dropped the executable bit** — `eg-q.orig` went 755 → 664 and every shard died with `Permission denied` inside a postedit probe. `os.replace` does not inherit mode. Both files are back at 755.

**I deleted the running cell's shard logs.** My relaunch command started with `rm -f logs/rep30/*.log`, and the launch you interrupted had already started remotely — so I wiped the logs of a live run. The shards hold open file descriptors to the deleted inodes, so the run itself is unaffected and results write to `results/`, not the logs. What I lost is the `order=` lines I use for the arm-order fairness check. That is recoverable: arm order is deterministic from shard index, and the per-instance `prompt_invariant` digests are on disk, which is the stronger check anyway.

Also corrected while in there: the live `eg-q` wrapper still labelled RELATED SITES precision as 10%; it now says 9%, matching the measured 9.3%.

I'll report at completion with the primary endpoint — eg's locate calls per session against baseline's, which must beat the in-sample 0.40 substitution rate — plus pooled tokens with the cluster interval, and wall-clock. At n=30 the interval will be roughly ±20pt, so it can refute the mechanism or show the sign survives out of sample; it cannot certify a target.

Killed cleanly — 0 shards, 0 live, 8 partial sessions to discard.

On your question, three effects, only one of which matters:

**The primary endpoint is safe.** REP30's claim is eg vs baseline *on the same instance*, and arm order alternates across the 30 pairs. Higher load hits both arms, and any order-linked bias cancels across the draw. Load headroom is not the issue either — 8 sessions ran at load 0.87 on 32 vCPU, so these are API-bound, not CPU-bound.

**Wall-clock numbers stop being comparable to earlier cells.** Every prior cell ran 6-8 wide. A 20-wide cell's minutes-per-session will be inflated by queueing, so I will report REP30 time as within-cell only and not put it in the all-time time table next to SMOKER12W.

**The real risk is API rate limiting.** 20 concurrent sessions can hit throughput limits, and retries burn turns — which would land in the token numbers, not just the clock. That is the one thing that could bias the result, and it hits whichever arm is running when the limit bites, so it is noise rather than systematic. I will check retry/error rates early and drop to 12-wide if they show up.

content.description:
Blocking work before the 300x4 Gemini cell. Do NOT install toolchains while SMOKER12 is live (agents probe for go/cargo/bundle mid-session; installing under a running cell contaminates it).

1a. INSTALL MISSING TOOLCHAINS on graphbench-c: go, cargo/rustc, bundle(ruby), pytest, dotnet.
    Why: 129/300 of multilingual_300 (Rust 43 + Go 42 + Ruby 44) cannot run their own tests; env/build is 19.26 calls/session = 35% of a session, symmetric across arms. This is H4 from the plan: it does not change the ratio, it strips ~12 calls/session of noise from BOTH arms and shrinks the +-13pt CI that makes 3%/9%/13%/16% indistinguishable.
    Verify: `command -v go cargo rustc pytest bundle` all resolve; re-run logs/toolchain.py and confirm the MISSING count drops to 0.

1b. WRITE run_quad.sh — 4-arm driver (baseline, eg, cmm, graphify) carrying run_paired.sh's guards:
    - PKG_ISO per-arm FATAL check
    - /tmp purge decline -> FATAL (the patched behaviour)
    - half-complete tuple -> results/<TAG>_r1.unpaired.txt + QUAD_STRICT=1 refuses
    - prompt_invariant.sha256 compared unconditionally, missing = FATAL
    - harness exit code checked (exit 2 stops the cell)
    - **ARM ORDER ROTATION** by instance index (Latin-square / rotate by _idx % 4). Without this, arm 4 always gets the warmest machine state and the 4-arm result is uninterpretable. run_matrix.sh/run_ladder.sh do fixed-order sweeps and lack run_3arm.sh's protections - do NOT use them.

1c. GEMINI PATH: CC_AGENT=gemini, MODEL=gemini-3.6-flash, max effort. Set maxSessionTurns IDENTICALLY for all 4 arms (Gemini has no --max-turns; an uncapped arm voids the comparison). Note the harness's own caveat: Gemini reports cache_creation=0 (no cache-write class), so its numbers are a self-contained 4-arm comparison, NOT comparable to the Claude cells.

Files: tools/run_quad.sh (new), tools/run_3arm.sh:2984+ (gemini branch), logs/toolchain.py (verifier).

The emitted block is clean. That is the sixth comment-vs-code false positive tonight, this time inside my own verification, and it is the reason I now check emitted output rather than file text.

REP30 worst pairs, 7 of 30 gated
  instance            lang      tokens      time    turns eg/base
  micropython-15898   C        -96.5%   -352.5%       46/30
  lucene-13170        Java     -46.5%    -21.6%       48/37

  fastlane-19765      Ruby     +17.4%    +21.1%       36/35

  fluentd-4655        Ruby     +37.3%    +43.6%       38/41
  gson-2479           Java     +52.6%    +16.2%       49/55
```

The turn column is the story and it matches the mechanism cleanly. **Every loser has eg taking more turns than baseline** (46/30, 48/37, 36/30); **every winner has eg equal or fewer** (36/35, 39/41, 38/41, 49/55). No exceptions in 7 pairs. That is the substitution mechanism showing up in a fresh draw — eg loses exactly when it adds work rather than replacing it.

micropython is the extreme: 16 extra turns and 3.5× the wall-clock. C was also the language with the worst parse coverage in the graph build (528 of 1850 files failed on one C repo), which is a plausible link but n=1 and I am not claiming it.

**On representativeness — they are exactly tied.**

```
L1 distance from the stratified 100-instance reference
  rep30    22.0%
  rep50x   22.0%
```

Identical. My script printed "rep50x is CLOSER" purely from a `<` comparison on equal values, which is a bug in my own output, not a finding. Per-language both sit within a few points of the reference on everything.

The one real difference: rep50x has 10% labelled Python; rep30's 10% are the three instances with no `language` field (django, pylint, scikit-learn — the ones whose graphs I rebuilt tonight). So rep30 carries the same Python weight, just untagged.

So rep30 is **not more representative** than rep50 — it is equally representative. Its value is different: 27 of its 30 instances have never been used, so it is the only out-of-sample test available. That is the reason to run it, not better composition.

returned, what the repeated commands were, and whether eg reached the gold files.

import json, os, glob, re, collections
S = os.path.expanduser("~/pe1/graphmark/agentic-swebench")
GQ  = re.compile(r"(entire[ -]graph|eg-q)", re.I)
BLD = re.compile(r"\b(mvn|gradlew?|cargo|go test|go build|npm|yarn|pytest|tox|make|cmake|composer|bundle|rake|phpunit|jest|ant|node|python -m)\b")
SYM = re.compile(r"\b(grep|rg|ag|find|ls|cat|sed|awk|head|tail|wc)\b")
TARGETS = ["immutable-js-2006","carbon-3098","micropython-15898","preact-3010",
           "lucene-13170","nushell-13246","docusaurus-9183"]

def toks(cc):
    mu = cc.get("modelUsage") or {}
    if mu:
        t = sum((m.get(k,0) or 0) for m in mu.values() for k in
                ("inputTokens","outputTokens","cacheReadInputTokens","cacheCreationInputTokens"))
        if t: return t
    u = cc.get("usage") or {}
    return sum(u.get(k,0) or 0 for k in ("input_tokens","output_tokens",
               "cache_read_input_tokens","cache_creation_input_tokens"))

def cls(nm, cmd):
    if GQ.search(nm + " " + cmd): return "graph"
    if nm in ("Edit","MultiEdit","Write"): return "edit"
    if nm == "Read": return "read"
    if nm in ("Glob","Grep"): return "locate"
    if nm == "Bash":
        if BLD.search(cmd): return "build/test"
        if SYM.search(cmd): return "locate"
        return "other"
    return "other"

def profile(arm, iid):
    key = iid.replace("_","-").lower()[:46]
    for d in glob.glob(f"{S}/results/REP30_r1_{arm}/ccfg/projects/*/"):
        if key not in os.path.basename(d.rstrip("/")).lower(): continue
        cat = collections.Counter(); cmds = collections.Counter()
        gout = []; files = collections.Counter(); ids = {}
        res = {}
        for f in sorted(glob.glob(d + "*.jsonl")):
            for line in open(f, errors="ignore"):
                try: j = json.loads(line)
                except Exception: continue
                t = j.get("type"); msg = j.get("message") or {}
                for c in (msg.get("content") or []):
                    if not isinstance(c, dict): continue
                    if t == "assistant" and c.get("type") == "tool_use":
                        nm = c.get("name",""); inp = c.get("input") or {}
                        cmd = str(inp.get("command","")) if nm == "Bash" else ""
                        k = cls(nm, cmd); cat[k] += 1
                        if k == "graph": ids[c.get("id")] = cmd
                        if nm in ("Edit","MultiEdit","Write"):
                            fp = inp.get("file_path","") or ""
                            if fp: files[os.path.basename(fp)] += 1
                        sig = (cmd.split()[0] if cmd else nm)
                        if k in ("locate","build/test","other"): cmds[sig[:22]] += 1
                    elif t == "user" and c.get("type") == "tool_result":
                        v = c.get("content")
                        txt = v if isinstance(v,str) else " ".join(
                            x.get("text","") for x in v if isinstance(x,dict)) if isinstance(v,list) else ""
                        res[c.get("tool_use_id")] = txt
        for gid in ids: gout.append(len(res.get(gid,"")))
        return cat, cmds, gout, files
    return None, None, None, None

for tgt in TARGETS:
    iid = next((r["instance_id"] for r in json.load(open(f"{S}/tasks/rep30_tasks.json"))["instances"]
                if r["instance_id"].endswith(tgt)), None)
    if not iid: continue
    ec, ecm, eg_out, ef = profile("eg", iid)
    bc, bcm, _, bf = profile("baseline", iid)
    if ec is None or bc is None:
        print(f"\n=== {tgt}: transcripts not matched ==="); continue
    print(f"\n=== {tgt} ===")
    keys = ["graph","locate","read","edit","build/test","other"]
    print("  calls      " + "".join(f"{k:>12}" for k in keys) + f"{'TOTAL':>8}")
    print("    eg       " + "".join(f"{ec[k]:>12}" for k in keys) + f"{sum(ec.values()):>8}")
    print("    baseline " + "".join(f"{bc[k]:>12}" for k in keys) + f"{sum(bc.values()):>8}")
    print("    delta    " + "".join(f"{ec[k]-bc[k]:>+12}" for k in keys) + f"{sum(ec.values())-sum(bc.values()):>+8}")
    print(f"  graph calls: {len(eg_out)}  payload bytes: {eg_out if len(eg_out)<8 else eg_out[:8]}")
    top = [f"{k}x{v}" for k,v in ecm.most_common(5)]
    print(f"  eg top repeated: {', '.join(top)}")
    topb = [f"{k}x{v}" for k,v in bcm.most_common(5)]
    print(f"  base top repeated: {', '.join(topb)}")
    print(f"  eg files edited ({sum(ef.values())} edits, {len(ef)} files): {list(ef)[:6]}")
    print(f"  base files edited ({sum(bf.values())} edits, {len(bf)} files): {list(bf)[:6]}")

# Why eg loses: the complete catalogue

Written 2026-08-10 from REP30, the campaign's first out-of-sample cell (27 of 30 instances never used
before). Snapshot at **17 of 30 pairs gated** — the cell was still running, so counts will grow.

Every row here comes from reading the actual session transcripts (`logs/why30.py`), not from inferring
cause from token totals.

---

## 1. The losers

| instance | lang | tokens | time | turns eg/base | dturn | tokens lost |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| immutable-js-2006 | JavaScript | −320.1% | −164.9% | 78/31 | +47 | −3,850,559 |
| carbon-3098 | PHP | −264.9% | −95.8% | 90/42 | +48 | −4,001,830 |
| micropython-15898 | C | −96.5% | −352.5% | 46/30 | +16 | −757,631 |
| preact-3010 | JavaScript | −54.2% | −56.4% | 67/53 | +14 | −1,281,506 |
| lucene-13170 | Java | −46.5% | −21.6% | 48/37 | +11 | −745,147 |
| nushell-13246 | Rust | −34.3% | −74.2% | 36/30 | +6 | −311,664 |
| docusaurus-9183 | TypeScript | −30.0% | +1.1% | 80/75 | +5 | −1,222,497 |
| ruff-15626 | Rust | −20.2% | −10.6% | 84/68 | +16 | −688,839 |

Totals: losers **−12,859,673** tokens at mean dturn **+20.4**; winners **+7,658,511** at mean dturn
**−4.2**.

**The cleanest signal in the cell:** every loser has eg taking *more* turns than baseline (+5 to +48),
and 7 of 9 winners have eg taking *fewer* (−17 to −1). The two exceptions are marginal (+2, +1). There
is no overlap in the middle. This reproduces the substitution mechanism (r=−0.724, n=140) on instances
it was never fitted to.

---

## 2. The reasons, per loser

### A. Improvised harness — the agent writes its own exploration scaffolding

**`carbon-3098`** (−264.9%, +48 turns) — the clearest case in the campaign.

```
eg   89 calls: 5 graph, 34 locate, 8 read, 18 edit, 13 build, 11 other
base 41 calls: 0 graph, 20 locate, 3 read,  3 edit, 12 build,  3 other

eg edited 13 files / 18 edits:  repro.php, repro_autoload.php, explore.php,
                                explore2.php, revert.php, CarbonInterval.php
base edited 1 file / 3 edits:   CarbonInterval.php
```

Baseline fixed one file and ran phpunit four times. eg built two `explore` scripts, an autoloader
shim, and a `revert` script. **The graph worked** — payloads 4802 / 1415 / 605 / 1641 / 2859 bytes.
The tool located the answer and the agent then went exploring anyway.

**`micropython-15898`** (−96.5%, +16) — both arms fixed the same file (`mpz.c`). eg additionally wrote
`repro.py` and `fuzz_comma.py`, ran +8 locate calls and extra `make` builds. Worst wall-clock in the
cell (−352.5%) because each native build is expensive.

### B. Scope creep — blast radius grows after a correct lookup

**`immutable-js-2006`** (−320.1%, +47).

```
eg   77 calls: 4 graph, 21 locate, 10 read, 15 edit, 21 build, 6 other
base 30 calls: 0 graph, 10 locate,  5 read,  4 edit,  9 build, 2 other

eg edited 9 files:  repro.js, Operations.js, TrieUtils.js, edge.js, build.js, sources.js
base edited 3 files: build-and-repro.js, Operations.js, edge-cases.js
```

Both fixed `Operations.js`. eg additionally touched `TrieUtils.js`, `build.js`, `sources.js`, then
spent 21 calls on builds. Edits +11, builds +12. Graph payloads were healthy (1994/580/1704/1794).

This is the mechanism `RELATED SITES` was suspected of driving: measured precision **9.3%** (73 of 789
listed files are in a gold patch), so a list of graph-adjacent files invites edits that are wrong ~91%
of the time.

### C. Tool-independent build churn — not attributable to eg

**`lucene-13170`** (−46.5%, +11) — **eg made ZERO graph calls.**

```
graph calls: 0
build/test 20 vs 5  (+15)
eg edited: Stress.java, lucene-offline-verification.md, MEMORY.md
```

The tool was never invoked. The loss is +15 build/test calls plus self-written scaffolding and notes.
This pair is run-level variance and must not be counted as a tool effect. **1 of 8 losers.**

**`nushell-13246`** (−34.3%, +6) — locate flat (+2); the entire delta is build/test 12 vs 6, with
`cargo` invoked 7 times against 3. Graph payloads fine. Also tool-independent in substance.

### D. The tool returned a poor answer

**`preact-3010`** (−54.2%, +14) — the only loser where retrieval itself underperformed.

```
graph called ONCE, returned 260 bytes  (a near-empty payload)
locate 34 vs 24 (+10)   build 16 vs 9 (+7)
```

One call, almost nothing back, then the agent abandoned the tool and fell back to grepping and
building. **1 of 8 losers.**

### E. Extra file reads

**`docusaurus-9183`** (−30.0%, +5) — locate −3, build −4, but `Read` 10 vs 2 (+8). The only loser
where eg searched and built *less* than baseline. Smallest loss.

**`ruff-15626`** (−20.2%, +16) — Rust; build/test dominated, same shape as nushell.

---

## 3. Cause tally

| cause | instances | share of loss |
|---|---|---|
| improvised harness / scaffolding | carbon, micropython | 4.76M |
| scope creep after a good lookup | immutable-js | 3.85M |
| tool-independent build churn | lucene (0 graph calls), nushell, ruff | 1.75M |
| tool returned a poor answer | preact | 1.28M |
| extra file reads | docusaurus | 1.22M |

**The dominant cause is not bad retrieval.** In 6 of 8 losers the graph returned healthy payloads or
was not used at all. The loss comes *after* a successful lookup: the agent widens scope, writes its own
exploration scripts, and thrashes on builds.

---

## 4. What is NOT the reason — ruled out with data

Nine predictor classes were tested at n=140 and every one is null. None of these explains the tail:

| candidate | result |
|---|---|
| instance identity | r=−0.022 |
| language / difficulty / patch size | all p>0.2 |
| graph call count | 2.58 vs 3.16, p=0.394 |
| graph call failure rate | 16.1% vs 16.7%, p=1.000 (real failure rate 0.3%) |
| index completeness degraded | 7.2% vs 7.1%, p=1.000 |
| cache-miss rate | 4.9% vs 7.6%, p=0.713 |
| index build seconds | 9.9s vs 5.4s, p=0.495 |
| retrieval rank correctness | *inverted* — losers 11% wrong, winners 49% wrong |
| the tool's own relevance score | r=−0.161, *inverted*, p=0.111 |

Also refuted, both my own hypotheses: **cache warmth** (cells with near-identical miss rates span +3%
to +33%; the coldest cell scored +25.25%) and **arm order** (p=0.4466, direction backwards).

A graph-call cap was the obvious fix and is refuted: at every K≥2 it bites more winners than losers.

---

## 5. What follows

- **Loss is a post-lookup behaviour problem, not a retrieval problem.** Fixing precision or payload
  size does not address 6 of 8 cases.
- **~20% of the tail is not the tool's fault at all** (lucene made zero graph calls; nushell's delta is
  pure cargo churn). Any "fix the losers" plan is partly chasing noise.
- **The actionable quantity is turn delta.** It separates winners from losers with no overlap, and it
  is measurable inside a single arm.
- **`RELATED SITES` at 9.3% precision is a live suspect** for the scope-creep class. Its header now
  states the measured rate rather than claiming the change "normally has to land" there.

Per-instance detail: `logs/why30.py`. Cell prereg: `logs/PREREG-REP30.md`
sha `add564b094cacc9c`. Ledger: `TokensNotes.md` §6.

input.command:
cat > /tmp/payload30.py <<'PY'
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Is the graph PAYLOAD itself costing the tokens, or is it the behaviour change?

Direct cost  = payload bytes / ~4 bytes-per-token, once.
Carry cost   = that payload sits in context and is re-read every subsequent turn, so it is charged
               (mostly as cache reads) turns_remaining times.
Compare both against the ACTUAL token delta per session.
"""
import json, os, glob, re, statistics
S = os.path.expanduser("~/pe1/graphmark/agentic-swebench")
GQ = re.compile(r"(entire[ -]graph|eg-q)", re.I)

def toks(cc):
    mu = cc.get("modelUsage") or {}
    if mu:
        t = sum((m.get(k,0) or 0) for m in mu.values() for k in
                ("inputTokens","outputTokens","cacheReadInputTokens","cacheCreationInputTokens"))
        if t: return t
    u = cc.get("usage") or {}
    return sum(u.get(k,0) or 0 for k in ("input_tokens","output_tokens",
               "cache_read_input_tokens","cache_creation_input_tokens"))
def g(arm, iid):
    f = f"{S}/results/REP30_r1_{arm}/{arm}/{iid}/cc_out.json"
    if not (os.path.exists(f) and os.path.getsize(f) > 1): return None
    try: j = json.load(open(f))
    except Exception: return None
    p = os.path.dirname(f) + "/patch.diff"
    if not (j.get("subtype") == "success" and (j.get("total_cost_usd") or 0) > 0
            and os.path.exists(p) and os.path.getsize(p) > 0): return None
    return dict(t=toks(j), n=j.get("num_turns") or 0)

def payload(iid):
    key = iid.replace("_","-").lower()[:46]
    for d in glob.glob(f"{S}/results/REP30_r1_eg/ccfg/projects/*/"):
        if key not in os.path.basename(d.rstrip("/")).lower(): continue
        ids = {}; res = {}; order = []
        seq = 0
        for f in sorted(glob.glob(d + "*.jsonl")):
            for line in open(f, errors="ignore"):
                try: j = json.loads(line)
                except Exception: continue
                t = j.get("type"); msg = j.get("message") or {}
                for c in (msg.get("content") or []):
                    if not isinstance(c, dict): continue
                    if t == "assistant" and c.get("type") == "tool_use":
                        seq += 1
                        cmd = str((c.get("input") or {}).get("command",""))
                        if GQ.search(c.get("name","") + " " + cmd):
                            ids[c.get("id")] = seq
                    elif t == "user" and c.get("type") == "tool_result":
                        v = c.get("content")
                        res[c.get("tool_use_id")] = v if isinstance(v,str) else " ".join(
                            x.get("text","") for x in v if isinstance(x,dict)) if isinstance(v,list) else ""
        tot = 0; carry = 0
        for gid, at in ids.items():
            b = len(res.get(gid, "")); tot += b
            carry += b * max(seq - at, 0)          # bytes x turns it remains in context
        return tot, carry, len(ids), seq
    return None, None, None, None

ids = [r["instance_id"] for r in json.load(open(f"{S}/tasks/rep30_tasks.json"))["instances"]]
rows = []
for i in ids:
    e, b = g("eg", i), g("baseline", i)
    if not (e and b): continue
    pb, carry, ncalls, seq = payload(i)
    if pb is None: continue
    rows.append(dict(i=i, pb=pb, carry=carry, nc=ncalls, dtok=e["t"]-b["t"],
                     sav=100*(1-e["t"]/b["t"]), et=e["t"]))
print(f"  n={len(rows)} pairs\n")
print(f"  {'':<22} {'graph':>6} {'payload':>10} {'direct':>9} {'carry':>11} {'ACTUAL':>12} {'payload as':>11}")
print(f"  {'instance':<22} {'calls':>6} {'bytes':>10} {'tokens':>9} {'tokens':>11} {'delta tok':>12} {'% of delta':>11}")
for r in sorted(rows, key=lambda x: x["sav"])[:8]:
    d_tok = r["pb"] / 4
    c_tok = r["carry"] / 4
    pct = 100 * c_tok / abs(r["dtok"]) if r["dtok"] else float("nan")
    print(f"  {r['i'].split('__')[-1][:22]:<22} {r['nc']:>6} {r['pb']:>10,} {d_tok:>9,.0f} {c_tok:>11,.0f} "
          f"{r['dtok']:>+12,} {pct:>10.1f}%")
print()
tp = sum(r["pb"] for r in rows) / 4
tc = sum(r["carry"] for r in rows) / 4
td = sum(r["dtok"] for r in rows)
te = sum(r["et"] for r in rows)
print(f"  TOTALS across {len(rows)} pairs")
print(f"    payload bytes            {sum(r['pb'] for r in rows):>14,}")
print(f"    direct payload tokens    {tp:>14,.0f}   = {100*tp/te:.3f}% of eg's total tokens")
print(f"    carry-cost tokens (max)  {tc:>14,.0f}   = {100*tc/te:.3f}% of eg's total tokens")
print(f"    ACTUAL extra tokens eg spent {td:>+11,}")
print(f"    payload explains         {100*tc/abs(td) if td else 0:>13.1f}% of the loss (carry, upper bound)")
print(f"    mean payload/session     {statistics.mean(r['pb'] for r in rows):>14,.0f} bytes"
      f" over {statistics.mean(r['nc'] for r in rows):.2f} calls")
PY

Measured, and the answer is no — the payload is not what's costing us:

```
                        graph   payload   direct     carry      ACTUAL   payload as
instance                calls     bytes   tokens    tokens   delta tok   % of delta
immutable-js-2006           4     6,072    1,518   104,870  +3,850,559        2.7%
carbon-3098                 5    11,322    2,830   205,812  +4,001,830        5.1%
caddy-5995                  3     4,139    1,035    56,236  +4,828,830        1.2%
preact-3010                 1       260       65     4,160  +1,281,506        0.3%
lucene-13170                0         0        0         0    +745,147        0.0%

TOTALS, 23 pairs
  direct payload tokens        29,489   = 0.040% of eg's total tokens
  carry cost (upper bound)  1,495,901   = 2.044% of eg's total tokens
  ACTUAL extra tokens        +12,793,521
  payload explains at most       11.7% of the loss
```

Mean payload is **5,129 bytes over 3.22 calls** — about 400 tokens per call. Directly that is 0.04% of a session. Even charging it as if it were re-read at full price on every subsequent turn (the "carry" column, a deliberate over-estimate) it reaches only 2% of eg's tokens and explains at most 11.7% of the loss.

So **88%+ of the loss is behavioural, not payload.** eg is not losing because the tool says too much; it is losing because of what the agent does after reading it — extra edits, extra builds, self-written exploration scripts.

Two cases make that unambiguous:

- **`preact-3010`** returned a 260-byte payload — 0.3% of its own token delta — and still lost 54.2%. It lost because the payload was *useless*, not because it was expensive.
- **`lucene-13170`** had **zero** payload and lost 46.5%.

This also means shrinking the payload is not a lever, which matches the eight payload-quality metrics already in the graveyard. The lever remains post-lookup behaviour: turn count, edit scope, build churn.

## Key Findings on MCP Tool Design and Token Efficiency (2026)

**The Core Problem:**
Without MCP, agents interact with codebases through generic file-system tools that have no concept of code structure, relevance, or scope, causing agents to read far more than necessary based on file names and grep results.

**Reducing Agent Turns and Token Costs:**
Practical strategies can cut AI agent token costs by 60-80% through signature-only retrieval, tree-sitter indexing, scoped MCP context, and model routing strategies. Code intelligence MCP servers provide symbol lookup, call graphs, type hierarchies, and signature extraction.

**Managing Context Over Multiple Turns:**
Long agent sessions accumulate massive context—if you're on turn 20, every message from turns 1-19 is being re-sent as input, so it's better to start new sessions for new tasks instead of continuing old ones.

**Tool Design Best Practices:**
Most MCP servers are built to return complete, accurate data rather than minimal data, and the single highest-leverage change is to return only the fields the agent actually needs.

**Tool Schema Overhead:**
Tool definitions reload on every conversation turn, and MCP's automatic tool schema injection occurs whether you use those tools or not. Many developers in 2026 use the enable-experimental-mcp-cli flag, which keeps tool schemas out of the main context window until they are actually invoked.

I found relevant search results about this topic. Here's what the current discussion around LLM coding agents and scope creep reveals:

## The Problem

When asked to add bounded retry logic to one client, an agent may return a diff across 14 files, including retry code, changes to dependency injection wiring, a new interface nobody asked for, test movement, and edits in bootstrap code that were never part of the request. The agent solves the local task by increasing the scope of the change until the local problem disappears.

If the same model defines the scope, executes the edits, explains the result, and justifies the extra changes, then the process has no independent control point where it needs one most.

## Solutions Being Implemented

One practical approach: Making scope-creep a first-class anti-pattern with concrete enforcement, where if the task is "fix function X", you fix function X—not also rename a variable or reformat the file. Teams have paired this with a PreToolUse hook on the Edit action that flags any edit outside the file list declared at plan time, blocking edits if the planned scope was auth/token.py and the model tries to edit auth/middleware.py.

Results: Before implementing scope controls, ~35% of one-line-ask PRs contained unrelated changes; after, ~4%.

The broader recommendation: Coding agents need a change budget.

Blocking work before the 300x4 Gemini cell. Do NOT install toolchains while SMOKER12 is live (agents probe for go/cargo/bundle mid-session; installing under a running cell contaminates it).

1a. INSTALL MISSING TOOLCHAINS on graphbench-c: go, cargo/rustc, bundle(ruby), pytest, dotnet.
    Why: 129/300 of multilingual_300 (Rust 43 + Go 42 + Ruby 44) cannot run their own tests; env/build is 19.26 calls/session = 35% of a session, symmetric across arms. This is H4 from the plan: it does not change the ratio, it strips ~12 calls/session of noise from BOTH arms and shrinks the +-13pt CI that makes 3%/9%/13%/16% indistinguishable.
    Verify: `command -v go cargo rustc pytest bundle` all resolve; re-run logs/toolchain.py and confirm the MISSING count drops to 0.

1b. WRITE run_quad.sh — 4-arm driver (baseline, eg, cmm, graphify) carrying run_paired.sh's guards:
    - PKG_ISO per-arm FATAL check
    - /tmp purge decline -> FATAL (the patched behaviour)
    - half-complete tuple -> results/<TAG>_r1.unpaired.txt + QUAD_STRICT=1 refuses
    - prompt_invariant.sha256 compared unconditionally, missing = FATAL
    - harness exit code checked (exit 2 stops the cell)
    - **ARM ORDER ROTATION** by instance index (Latin-square / rotate by _idx % 4). Without this, arm 4 always gets the warmest machine state and the 4-arm result is uninterpretable. run_matrix.sh/run_ladder.sh do fixed-order sweeps and lack run_3arm.sh's protections - do NOT use them.

1c. GEMINI PATH: CC_AGENT=gemini, MODEL=gemini-3.6-flash, max effort. Set maxSessionTurns IDENTICALLY for all 4 arms (Gemini has no --max-turns; an uncapped arm voids the comparison). Note the harness's own caveat: Gemini reports cache_creation=0 (no cache-write class), so its numbers are a self-contained 4-arm comparison, NOT comparable to the Claude cells.

Files: tools/run_quad.sh (new), tools/run_3arm.sh:2984+ (gemini branch), logs/toolchain.py (verifier).

content.text:
Two genuinely useful findings from the research, one of which changes the MCP plan.

**Scope enforcement has a measured result elsewhere.** A `PreToolUse` hook that blocks edits outside a file list declared at plan time took unrelated changes in one-line PRs from ~35% to ~4% ([the-main-thread.com](https://www.the-main-thread.com/p/coding-agents-change-budget)). That targets our exact top-loss class — carbon edited 13 files where baseline edited 1. **Fairness caveat: a change-budget hook helps any arm, so it must go to both arms**, with each declaring its own scope. That is still a good experiment — it measures whether the graph helps declare a *better* scope — but eg-only would be the same cheat I spent tonight removing.

**MCP is not free, which the old strike never accounted for.** Tool definitions reload every turn, so 5 MCP tools cost schema tokens on all ~50 turns ([bswen](https://docs.bswen.com/blog/2026-04-24-mcp-token-overhead/), [MindStudio](https://www.mindstudio.ai/blog/reduce-token-usage-ai-agents-mcp-optimization)). At n=1 turn that is trivial; at 50 turns it may exceed the entire 5,129-byte payload. I should measure schema cost before betting on MCP.

Updating the reasons file with the new losers, the payload finding, and this:

it was never fitted to.""",
"""**The turn-delta signal, and its limit.** At n=17 every loser had a positive turn delta and every
winner (bar two marginal cases) a negative one, with no overlap. **That clean separation broke at n=23**
and I retract the "no overlap" claim: `phpspreadsheet-4214` lost **59.9% on a turn delta of +1** and
`terraform-34814` lost 8.3% on +2, while winners `hugo-12562` (+2), `hugo-12204` (+2) and
`fastlane-19765` (+1) sit in the same band.

So turn delta predicts the **large** losses (all six worst have +11 to +48) but does not separate the
margin. `phpspreadsheet` burned 1.28M tokens in essentially the same turn count, meaning **cost per
turn** grew rather than turn count — a second failure mode I have not characterised.""")

s = s.replace("""## 4. What is NOT the reason — ruled out with data""",
"""## 3b. The payload is NOT the cost — measured

The obvious suspicion is that the graph's own output is what we are paying for. It is not
(`logs/payload30.py`, n=23):

```
direct payload tokens        29,489   = 0.040% of eg's total tokens
carry cost (upper bound)  1,495,901   = 2.044% of eg's total tokens
ACTUAL extra tokens        +12,793,521
payload explains at most       11.7% of the loss
mean payload                  5,129 bytes over 3.22 calls (~400 tokens/call)
```

"Carry cost" deliberately over-charges: it bills the payload as if fully re-read at full price on every
later turn. Even so it reaches 2% of eg's tokens. **88%+ of the loss is behavioural.**

Two cases settle it: `preact-3010` returned a **260-byte** payload (0.3% of its own delta) and still
lost 54.2% — it lost because the payload was *useless*, not expensive. `lucene-13170` had **zero**
payload and lost 46.5%.

Corollary: shrinking or tuning the payload is not a lever, consistent with the eight payload-quality
metrics already in the graveyard.

## 4. What is NOT the reason — ruled out with data""")

s = s.replace("""Per-instance detail: `logs/why30.py`. Cell prereg: `logs/PREREG-REP30.md`
sha `add564b094cacc9c`. Ledger: `TokensNotes.md` §6.""",
"""## 6. Candidate interventions, with fairness verdicts

| intervention | evidence | fairness verdict |
|---|---|---|
| **Change-budget hook** — `PreToolUse` blocks edits outside a scope declared at plan time. Reported elsewhere to cut unrelated changes in one-line PRs from ~35% to ~4%. | targets the top loss class directly (carbon 13 files vs 1) | **Both arms or neither.** A change budget helps a no-tool arm, so eg-only would be the cheat just removed. Symmetric version is still informative: it measures whether the graph declares a *better* scope. |
| **MCP delivery** — graph verbs in the same menu as `Grep`, so the tool is reachable at every later locate moment rather than remembered once at turn 1. | **never actually tested**: 0 of every cell ever run delivered `mcpServers`. The §2.13 strike came from a 4-session Gemini probe. | Fair — same information, different channel. But **MCP tool schemas reload every turn**, so 5 tools cost schema tokens ×50 turns. Measure schema overhead before betting on it; it may exceed the 5,129-byte payload. |
| **Signature-only / minimal-field retrieval** | industry reports 60–80% savings | Fair, but **low leverage here**: payload is only 11.7% of our loss. |
| **Shrink the payload** | — | Fair and **refuted for our case** by §3b. |
| **Cap graph calls** | — | **Refuted**: at every K≥2 it bites more winners than losers. |

## 7. The honest summary

Loss is a **post-lookup behaviour** problem. Retrieval mostly works: in 6 of 8 early losers the graph
returned healthy payloads or was never called, and the payload accounts for at most 11.7% of the cost.
What costs money is what the agent does next — widening edit scope, writing its own exploration
scripts, and re-running builds. Roughly a fifth of the tail is not the tool's doing at all.

Per-instance detail: `logs/why30.py`, `logs/losers30.py`, `logs/payload30.py`. Cell prereg:
`logs/PREREG-REP30.md` sha `add564b094cacc9c`. Ledger: `TokensNotes.md` §6.

Sources for the intervention table: [coding-agent change budget](https://www.the-main-thread.com/p/coding-agents-change-budget),
[MCP token overhead](https://docs.bswen.com/blog/2026-04-24-mcp-token-overhead/),
[MCP optimisation techniques](https://www.mindstudio.ai/blog/reduce-token-usage-ai-agents-mcp-optimization).""")
open(p,"w").write(s)
print(f"  updated: {len(s)} bytes")

# Plan — reach +15% on rep50 by making the graph SUBSTITUTIVE

Rewritten 2026-08-10. The previous version of this file aimed at 25% by "capping the structured loss
tail". **That premise is falsified** — nine predictor classes for the tail were tested and all are
null (`PLAN-15PCT.md` §4). This plan targets a different, measured mechanism.

## Context

**Why this change.** Tonight's analysis answered the question that had never been asked: *why do some
sessions win and others lose?* The answer is a single quantity, and it is the strongest correlation
in the campaign.

```
locate delta (eg locate calls minus baseline locate calls) vs saving
    r = -0.724   p = 0.000   n = 137        significant among winners alone (r=-0.355, p=0.001)

eg grepped MORE than baseline   n=58 (42%)   pooled  -25.44%
eg grepped LESS than baseline   n=79 (58%)   pooled  +30.05%
    difference +57.23pt   permutation p = 0.0000
```

A win is a session where the graph **replaced** manual searching. A loss is a session where the agent
queried the graph **and then grepped anyway**, paying for both. Nothing about the instance, the
language, the retrieval quality, or the tool's own confidence predicts which happens.

**The gap, sized.** The graph is currently almost purely additive:

```
eg locate calls/session        27.34
baseline locate calls/session  28.45
eg graph calls/session          2.78
locate delta                   -1.12
substitution rate               0.40 locate calls removed per graph call
```

2.78 graph calls remove 1.12 greps. Regression: **each avoided locate call is worth +3.44pt.** To
move mean-per-session saving from −2.75% to **+15%** requires locate delta of **−6.28** — eg must
remove **5.2 more locate calls per session**, a substitution rate of **2.26** (5.6× today's 0.40).

**Why +15% and not 25%.** Pooled is currently +8.73% [−2.79%, +18.86%] cluster-bootstrapped, n=140.

the target equals perfect play, and hitting it by loss-elimination alone is not achievable. I am
stating this before the plan rather than after it.

The oracle does hold eg's *win magnitudes* fixed, so the true ceiling is higher than +11.55% if wins

**Why +15% and not 25%.** Pooled is currently +8.73% [−2.79%, +18.86%] cluster-bootstrapped, n=140.
25% is not above the tool's ceiling (if every session saved the median win, pooled would be +32.08%)
but it is far outside the interval, and the only cell that ever reached it (`SMOKE12`, +25.25%) did so
carrying an arm-asymmetric instruction. 15% is the honest next rung.

**Why every previous attempt missed.** All of them moved *usage* or *richness*, never *substitution*:

| prior attempt | result | why it does not apply |
|---|---|---|
| more graph calls | r=+0.097, p=0.256 | usage is not the lever; substitution is |
| enrichment / bigger payload (§0) | **raised** grep counts | additive by construction |
| push-mode post-edit rider | **+4.2 turns/session** | adds a message, displaces nothing |
| MCP as a token lever (§2.13, struck) | "changes uptake, not price" | judged on usage, not displacement |
| grep-shim | +8.6%, 38.9% addressable | partial displacement only |

§2.13 stays struck as a *token* lever. This plan uses MCP as the **delivery vehicle for a
displacement test**, which is a different claim and is stated as such.

## The intervention

Deliver the graph as an **MCP tool in the same choice menu as `Grep`**, instead of a bash command the
agent must remember. Today the agent invokes `entire graph search` at call index ~1 and then never
returns: `impact` is 3 calls in 137 sessions (0.8%). A tool in the menu is re-selected at each locate
moment; a bash idiom is not.

This changes *choice architecture*, not output content — the only route that can raise substitution
rather than adding to it.

**Fairness.** The eg arm gets a retrieval tool and the baseline does not; that is the benchmark's
premise, not an asymmetry. Descriptions must stay factual and carry no imperatives — the existing
`tools/tool_mcp_server.py` was built for this and already has `verify_command` removed and no
"normally has to land" claim. Check before launch: `grep -c VERIFY tools/tool_mcp_server.py` = 0.

## Endpoints, pre-registered before any launch

**Primary is arm-internal** — eg's own locate count, so baseline drift cannot manufacture a pass.
This is the specific error that made CS50's +12.84% meaningless.

```
PRIMARY    eg locate calls/session       27.34  ->  must fall to <= 22.1
SECONDARY  substitution per graph call     0.40  ->  must exceed 1.00
GUARD      eg graph calls/session          2.78  ->  if this rises while locate is flat,
                                                    the intervention is ADDITIVE: stop, route closed
TERTIARY   tokens                                   NOT claim-bearing at n=12
```

The GUARD is the point of the experiment. Additive means closed; only displacement counts.

## Staging (smallest first, per the standing rule)

```
Step 1  $0    validate MCP delivery offline: server responds to tools/list + tools/call,
              per-arm allow-list gives baseline NO server, prompt digests match      -> report
Step 2  ~$80  12-instance random draw, sealed prereg at 0 results. Read PRIMARY only. -> pass or STOP
Step 3  ~$330 50-instance rep50x cell, sealed prereg. Primary = locate; secondary = pooled > +15%
Step 4  ~$2,000  n=300 for certification. NOT authorised; ask first.
```

Step 4 exists because separating +15% from +8.7% at 80% power needs ~n=300. A 50-cell cannot certify
15%; it can only fail to refute it.

## Files

- `tools/tool_mcp_server.py` — generalised per-arm MCP server, already built and shipped (sha
  `2c039d536de3`). Identical tool names across arms; per-arm backend and factual output description.
- `tools/run_3arm.sh` — per-arm MCP allow-list already patched in (`case "$arm"`, backups
  `.pre-mcparm`). `EG_MCP=1` enables. Do **not** edit under a running cell; temp path + atomic `mv`.
- `logs/size.py` — the substitution scorer (locate delta, regression slope, split test). This is the
  primary-endpoint scorer; reuse it, do not rewrite.
- `logs/{tail,sig,post,fail,degr,binom,ci2,shape,conf,wins}.py` — tonight's diagnostics.
- `graph-bench-results/PLAN-15PCT.md` — the corrected number and the nine dead predictors.
- Prereg goes in `logs/PREREG-SUB12.md`, sha'd, with 0 results on disk.

## Verification

- **Offline first:** drive `tool_mcp_server.py` over stdio by hand (`initialize`, `tools/list`,
  `tools/call`) and confirm a real result comes back for a known symbol. Step 1 of every paid stage
  has caught a defect before it cost money.
- **Delivery by transcript grep, never `gq_calls.log.payload`** (`_tee` writes before any wrapper
  append, so the forensic record can disagree with what the model received).
- **Confirm the baseline has no server:** `mcpServers` absent from the baseline arm's settings, and
  the arm-invariant prompt digest identical across arms (the detector that was dead for every cell
  before 2026-08-10).
- Score with `logs/size.py` for the primary and `logs/sav.py` for tokens. Report tokens **and** time.
- Permutation-test any split; cluster-bootstrap any pooled figure by instance.
- Publish the result either way in `TokensNotes.md` with the prereg sha. Four headlines have been
  withdrawn here; a fifth costs more than the gap.

## If the GUARD trips

If graph calls rise and locate stays flat, displacement is not achievable through delivery, and the
honest conclusion is that **+8.73% [−2.79%, +18.86%] is the number** — reported alongside
−3.02% mean-per-session, with 25% refuted at P=0.1% for this configuration. That is a defensible
result and it is better than a fifth withdrawal.

# Plan — get rep30 to +11%, and the honest test of whether that is possible

Written 2026-08-10, replacing the rep50/+15% plan (different draw, different target). Written against
REP30 at **n=24 of 30 gated**; the cell was still running.

## Context

REP30 is the campaign's first out-of-sample cell — 27 of its 30 instances had never been used. It is
currently **−21.44% pooled, −14.25% median, 11 wins of 24**. The rep50x figure of +8.73% is not
surviving on fresh instances, and the trims no longer rescue it (symmetric 2-and-2 trim: −18.63%), so
the loss is spread across the draw rather than sitting in two outliers.

**What +11% actually is.** I computed the per-class values by neutralising each loss class
(`logs/econ30.py`). Neutralising **every** class — eg never losing a single pair — gives **+11.55%**.

**So "+11% on rep30" is the never-lose oracle.** It is the same structural situation as 25% on rep50:
the target equals perfect play, and hitting it by loss-elimination alone is not achievable. I am
stating this before the plan rather than after it.

The oracle does hold eg's *win magnitudes* fixed, so the true ceiling is higher than +11.55% if wins
grow. That is the only honest route to the number, and it is unmeasured on this draw.

## What the money is

| class | instances | worth | pooled after | is it eg-only? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Unclassified** — caddy-5995, fmt-2457 | 2 | **9.9pt** | −11.52% | **unknown — forensics not run** |
| Improvised harness | carbon, micropython | 7.5pt | −13.92% | **mostly symmetric** (see below) |
| Scope creep | immutable-js | 6.1pt | −15.36% | eg-heavy (9 files vs 3) |
| Build/test churn | lucene, nushell, ruff, terraform | 3.5pt | −17.96% | **not eg's fault** (lucene: 0 graph calls) |
| Useless payload | preact (260 bytes) | 2.0pt | −19.42% | **eg-only, legitimately fixable** |
| Cost-per-turn growth | phpspreadsheet (+1 turn, −59.9%) | 2.0pt | −19.41% | uncharacterised |
| Extra file reads | docusaurus | 1.9pt | −19.51% | baseline read less |
| Payload shrink | all | 2.4pt | −19.08% | eg-only but tiny ($0.03 total) |

**The blocking fact.** Files edited per arm, from transcripts:

```
carbon-3098        eg 13  base 1    eg-heavy
immutable-js-2006  eg  9  base 3    eg-heavy
micropython-15898  eg  5  base 5    SYMMETRIC
lucene-13170       eg  6  base 6    SYMMETRIC
preact-3010        eg 10  base 8    near-symmetric
nushell-13246      eg  1  base 2    baseline heavier
docusaurus-9183    eg  5  base 6    baseline heavier
```

Baseline writes `Repro.java`, `build-and-repro.js`, `repro_comma.py` too. **Harness-writing is
symmetric in 5 of 7.** A generic "don't write throwaway scripts" instruction must go to both arms
(it helps a no-tool arm), and because the behaviour is symmetric it will move the *ratio* only on the
two eg-heavy cases. This is why the 7.5pt and 6.1pt rows cannot simply be banked.

Only **4.4pt** of the table is legitimately eg-only: the useless payload (2.0) and payload shrink (2.4).

## The plan — all diagnosis before any spend

**Step 0 — forensics on caddy-5995 and fmt-2457. $0. The largest block by far.**
9.9pt is unclassified, which is more than every eg-only lever combined. Run `logs/why30.py` extended
to these two: call decomposition per arm, files edited per arm, graph payload sizes, and what the extra
turns were spent on. Decision output: is this a fixable eg-only defect, a symmetric behaviour, or noise?

**Step 1 — per-class asymmetry, properly measured. $0.**
The 7-instance table above is eyeballed from filenames. Measure it: for every REP30 pair, count
(a) files edited, (b) files matching a repro/explore/scratch pattern, (c) build/test calls, per arm.
Decision output: which classes are genuinely eg-heavy. Only those can yield relative gain from a
symmetric fix.

**Step 2 — MCP schema overhead. $0.**
MCP has never been delivered in any cell (0 sessions across every cell ever run), so the §2.13 strike
rests on a 4-session Gemini probe. But tool schemas reload every turn, so 5 tools × ~50 turns may
exceed the entire 5,129-byte payload. Measure the schema token cost by driving
`tools/tool_mcp_server.py` and sizing its `tools/list` response against a 50-turn session.
Decision output: is MCP net-positive before it is worth a cell?

**Step 3 — build the one intervention Steps 0–2 justify, and validate offline. $0.**
Candidates in priority order, contingent on the above:
- if caddy/fmt show an eg-only defect → fix that first (largest block)
- retrieval fallback for empty payloads (preact's 260-byte answer) — eg-only and fair
- MCP delivery, if Step 2 shows the schema cost is small
- symmetric anti-harness / change-budget instruction, delivered to **both** arms, valued only on the
  eg-heavy residue

**Step 4 — 12-instance smoke on a REP30 subset. ~$80.**
Primary endpoint arm-internal, pre-registered, sealed at 0 results. Reuse the REP30 instances so the
comparison is paired against known values.

**Step 5 — re-run REP30, 30 instances, ~$330.** Only if Step 4's mechanism moves.

## The decision rule, stated in advance

After Steps 0–2 there are two possible states, and I will report which one we are in:

1. **caddy/fmt reveal a fixable eg-only defect** worth several points → a route to double-digit
   improvement exists; proceed to Steps 3–5.
2. **caddy/fmt are symmetric or noise** → the eg-only levers total ~4.4pt, which moves REP30 from
   −21.44% to roughly −17%. **+11% is then not reachable on this draw**, and the honest deliverable is
   that eg costs tokens out of sample, published with the loser forensics.

I will not narrow the target or re-cut the draw to manufacture state 1.

## Files

- `logs/econ30.py` — per-class valuation and the oracle. Reuse; do not rewrite.
- `logs/why30.py` — per-loser call decomposition. Extend the `TARGETS` list for Step 0.
- `logs/losers30.py`, `logs/payload30.py`, `logs/trim30.py` — loser list, payload economics, trims.
- `tools/tool_mcp_server.py` — the generalised per-arm MCP server, built but never run in a cell.
- `graph-bench-results/LOSS-REASONS.md` — the catalogue; update it as classes get resolved.
- `logs/PREREG-REP30.md` sha `add564b094cacc9c` — the current cell's sealed prereg.

## Verification

- Every claim from transcripts, not from token totals. Six comment-vs-code false positives happened
  tonight, including inside my own fairness guard — **verify against emitted output, never file text**.
- Permutation-test any split; cluster-bootstrap any pooled figure by instance.
- `FAIRNESS_STRICT=1` on every future cell so it refuses to run on arm asymmetry.
- One-sided trims are not robustness: report symmetric trims and the median beside any pooled figure.
- Publish the result either way with the prereg sha. Five headlines have been withdrawn in this
  project and one of tonight's retractions was a valid cell I struck for a reason I had not computed.

# Plan — rep30 to +11%

Written 2026-08-10 against REP30 at n=25 of 30 gated. Replaces the rep50/+15% plan.

## Context

REP30 is the campaign's first out-of-sample cell — 27 of 30 instances never used before. It currently
reads **−21.01% pooled, 11 wins of 25**. The rep50x +8.73% did not survive on fresh instances.

I first drafted this plan claiming +11% was the never-lose oracle and therefore unreachable. **I
verified that and it was wrong**, the same error I made with the rep50 oracle:

```
current                                        -21.01%
A: eg never LOSES (win sizes held fixed)       +12.41%
B: every session saves the MEDIAN win (23.3%)  +23.32%
B: every session saves the p75 win   (38.4%)   +38.39%
```

**+11% sits below even the never-lose oracle, and well below the win-magnitude ceiling.** If every
session merely matched the median win eg *already produces*, pooled would be +23.32%. The target needs
about half of that. It is reachable.

## The mechanism, measured on this draw

Verified across all 25 pairs, not eyeballed:

```
                        eg     baseline    delta
files edited (ALL)     5.48      4.44      +1.04
scratch/repro files    1.60      1.04      +0.56
build+test calls       8.52      8.04      +0.48

split by outcome (eg minus baseline)
  LOSERS      files +2.36   scratch +1.07   build +3.21
  WINNERS     files -0.64   scratch -0.09   build -3.00

corr(files delta,   saving)  r = -0.742    <- strongest predictor in the campaign
corr(scratch delta, saving)  r = -0.656
corr(locate delta,  saving)  r = -0.724    (the rep50x mechanism, reproduced)
corr(build delta,   saving)  r = -0.284
```

**Edit-scope delta beats locate delta.** I had also claimed harness-writing was symmetric; measured, it
is not — eg writes 54% more scratch files and edits 23% more files. That claim came from eyeballing
filenames on losers only and is withdrawn.

Per-loser forensics confirm one class, not many:

| instance | signature |
|---|---|
| carbon-3098 | 13 files vs 1; wrote explore.php, explore2.php, repro_autoload.php, revert.php |
| immutable-js-2006 | 9 files vs 3; edits +11, builds +12 |
| fmt-2457 | edge_join.cc, edge_join2.cc, edge_join3.cc at **identical** locate count |
| caddy-5995 | locate +21, never edited `replacer.go` — the file baseline fixed |
| micropython-15898 | wrote repro.py, fuzz_comma.py; locate +8 |

Graph payloads were healthy in every one of these. **Retrieval is not the problem.** The payload costs
$0.03 across 24 pairs (0.038% of eg tokens) and eliminating it entirely buys 2.4pt.

## The route to +11%

```
now                                                    -21.01%
+ close the eg-heavy scratch/scope classes (verified eg-heavy):
    caddy + fmt          9.9pt
    carbon + micropython 7.5pt
    immutable-js         6.1pt                          ~ +2.5%
+ eg-only retrieval fixes (empty-payload fallback, payload trim)  4.4pt   ~ +7%
+ win-magnitude headroom (median-win oracle is +23.32%)          remainder
```

The first block is the plan. It is 23.5 of the 32-point gap and it is the class every loser shares.

## The intervention

**A symmetric change budget.** Both arms are told the same thing: declare the files you intend to
change, and edits outside that set are refused unless re-declared. Reported elsewhere to cut unrelated
changes in one-line PRs from ~35% to ~4%
([the-main-thread](https://www.the-main-thread.com/p/coding-agents-change-budget)).

**Why symmetric delivery still helps eg.** A change budget helps a no-tool arm, so eg-only delivery
would be the exact cheat removed in PR #69. Delivered to both arms it constrains eg *more*, because eg
edits more (5.48 vs 4.44) and writes more scratch (1.60 vs 1.04). The relative gain is legitimate and
comes from eg having more excess to remove — not from an instruction the baseline never saw.

**Second, eg-only and fair: an empty-payload fallback.** `preact-3010` got a 260-byte answer on its one
call and abandoned the tool (−54.2%). When a query returns under a threshold, the tool should widen or
say so explicitly rather than return near-nothing. That is retrieval quality, legitimately eg-only.

## Staging

```
Step 1  $0    build both, validate offline. Confirm the change budget appears in BOTH arms'
              emitted prompts, and that FAIRNESS_STRICT does not trip.
Step 2  $0    measure MCP schema overhead (5 tools x ~50 turns) before considering MCP at all;
              it has NEVER run in a cell, so the S2.13 strike rests on a 4-session probe.
Step 3  ~$80  12-instance smoke on REP30 instances, sealed prereg, paired against known values.
              PRIMARY: files-edited delta must fall below +1.04 -- arm-internal, r=-0.742.
Step 4  ~$330 re-run REP30, all 30, only if Step 3's primary moves.
```

## Endpoints, pre-registered

```
PRIMARY    files-edited delta (eg minus baseline)   now +1.04  ->  must reach <= 0.00
SECONDARY  scratch-file delta                       now +0.56  ->  must reach <= 0.00
GUARD      if the budget lands on BOTH arms and the delta does not move, the class is not
           addressable by instruction; stop and report.
TERTIARY   pooled tokens with the cluster interval. Not claim-bearing at n=12.
```

## Files

- `logs/econ30.py` — per-class valuation and oracle variants. Reuse.
- `logs/why30.py`, `logs/losers30.py`, `logs/payload30.py`, `logs/trim30.py` — forensics set.
- `tools/run_3arm.sh` — `shared_discipline()` is where a symmetric budget belongs (it already reaches
  every arm); `assert_prompt_symmetry()` + `FAIRNESS_STRICT=1` enforce the fairness.
- `tools/eg-q` — empty-payload fallback goes in the wrapper, not the 810-line original.
- `graph-bench-results/LOSS-REASONS.md` — catalogue; update as classes resolve.

## Verification

- Claims from **emitted output**, never file text: six comment-vs-code false positives tonight,
  including inside my own fairness guard.
- Both arms' prompts must differ only by the tool block — check the per-pair `prompt_invariant` digests.
- `FAIRNESS_STRICT=1` on every cell.
- Symmetric trims and the median beside any pooled figure; one-sided trims are not robustness.
- Publish either way with the prereg sha.
- **Compute oracles and ceilings before declaring anything unreachable.** I have now made that mistake
  twice in one night, on rep50 and again in the first draft of this plan.

currently **−21.44% pooled, −14.25% median, 11 wins of 24**. The rep50x figure of +8.73% is not
surviving on fresh instances, and the trims no longer rescue it (symmetric 2-and-2 trim: −18.63%), so
the loss is spread across the draw rather than sitting in two outliers.

**What +11% actually is.** I computed the per-class values by neutralising each loss class
(`logs/econ30.py`). Neutralising **every** class — eg never losing a single pair — gives **+11.55%**.

**So "+11% on rep30" is the never-lose oracle.** It is the same structural situation as 25% on rep50:
the target equals perfect play, and hitting it by loss-elimination alone is not achievable. I am
stating this before the plan rather than after it.

The oracle does hold eg's *win magnitudes* fixed, so the true ceiling is higher than +11.55% if wins
grow. That is the only honest route to the number, and it is unmeasured on this draw.

# Plan — rep30 to +11%

Written 2026-08-10 against REP30 at n=25 of 30 gated. Replaces the rep50/+15% plan.

## Context

REP30 is the campaign's first out-of-sample cell — 27 of 30 instances never used before. It currently
reads **−21.01% pooled, 11 wins of 25**. The rep50x +8.73% did not survive on fresh instances.

I first drafted this plan claiming +11% was the never-lose oracle and therefore unreachable. **I
verified that and it was wrong**, the same error I made with the rep50 oracle:

```
current                                        -21.01%
A: eg never LOSES (win sizes held fixed)       +12.41%
B: every session saves the MEDIAN win (23.3%)  +23.32%
B: every session saves the p75 win   (38.4%)   +38.39%
```

**+11% sits below even the never-lose oracle, and well below the win-magnitude ceiling.** If every
session merely matched the median win eg *already produces*, pooled would be +23.32%. The target needs
about half of that. It is reachable.

## The mechanism, measured on this draw

Verified across all 25 pairs, not eyeballed:

```
                        eg     baseline    delta
files edited (ALL)     5.48      4.44      +1.04
scratch/repro files    1.60      1.04      +0.56
build+test calls       8.52      8.04      +0.48

split by outcome (eg minus baseline)
  LOSERS      files +2.36   scratch +1.07   build +3.21
  WINNERS     files -0.64   scratch -0.09   build -3.00

corr(files delta,   saving)  r = -0.742    <- strongest predictor in the campaign
corr(scratch delta, saving)  r = -0.656
corr(locate delta,  saving)  r = -0.724    (the rep50x mechanism, reproduced)
corr(build delta,   saving)  r = -0.284
```

**Edit-scope delta beats locate delta.** I had also claimed harness-writing was symmetric; measured, it
is not — eg writes 54% more scratch files and edits 23% more files. That claim came from eyeballing
filenames on losers only and is withdrawn.

Per-loser forensics confirm one class, not many:

| instance | signature |
|---|---|
| carbon-3098 | 13 files vs 1; wrote explore.php, explore2.php, repro_autoload.php, revert.php |
| immutable-js-2006 | 9 files vs 3; edits +11, builds +12 |
| fmt-2457 | edge_join.cc, edge_join2.cc, edge_join3.cc at **identical** locate count |
| caddy-5995 | locate +21, never edited `replacer.go` — the file baseline fixed |
| micropython-15898 | wrote repro.py, fuzz_comma.py; locate +8 |

Graph payloads were healthy in every one of these. **Retrieval is not the problem.** The payload costs
$0.03 across 24 pairs (0.038% of eg tokens) and eliminating it entirely buys 2.4pt.

## The route to +11%

```
now                                                    -21.01%
+ close the eg-heavy scratch/scope classes (verified eg-heavy):
    caddy + fmt          9.9pt
    carbon + micropython 7.5pt
    immutable-js         6.1pt                          ~ +2.5%
+ eg-only retrieval fixes (empty-payload fallback, payload trim)  4.4pt   ~ +7%
+ win-magnitude headroom (median-win oracle is +23.32%)          remainder
```

The first block is the plan. It is 23.5 of the 32-point gap and it is the class every loser shares.

## The intervention

**A symmetric change budget.** Both arms are told the same thing: declare the files you intend to
change, and edits outside that set are refused unless re-declared. Reported elsewhere to cut unrelated
changes in one-line PRs from ~35% to ~4%
([the-main-thread](https://www.the-main-thread.com/p/coding-agents-change-budget)).

**Why symmetric delivery still helps eg.** A change budget helps a no-tool arm, so eg-only delivery
would be the exact cheat removed in PR #69. Delivered to both arms it constrains eg *more*, because eg
edits more (5.48 vs 4.44) and writes more scratch (1.60 vs 1.04). The relative gain is legitimate and
comes from eg having more excess to remove — not from an instruction the baseline never saw.

**Second, eg-only and fair: an empty-payload fallback.** `preact-3010` got a 260-byte answer on its one
call and abandoned the tool (−54.2%). When a query returns under a threshold, the tool should widen or
say so explicitly rather than return near-nothing. That is retrieval quality, legitimately eg-only.
