This is H4 from the plan: it does not change the ratio, it strips ~12 calls/session of noise from BOTH arms and shrinks the +-13pt CI that makes 3%/9%/13%/16% indistinguishable.
    Verify: `command -v go cargo rustc pytest bundle` all resolve; re-run logs/toolchain.py and confirm the MISSING count drops to 0.

1b. WRITE run_quad.sh — 4-arm driver (baseline, eg, cmm, graphify) carrying run_paired.sh's guards:
    - PKG_ISO per-arm FATAL check
    - /tmp purge decline -> FATAL (the patched behaviour)
    - half-complete tuple -> results/<TAG>_r1.unpaired.txt + QUAD_STRICT=1 refuses
    - prompt_invariant.sha256 compared unconditionally, missing = FATAL
    - harness exit code checked (exit 2 stops the cell)
    - **ARM ORDER ROTATION** by instance index (Latin-square / rotate by _idx % 4). Without this, arm 4 always gets the warmest machine state and the 4-arm result is uninterpretable. run_matrix.sh/run_ladder.sh do fixed-order sweeps and lack run_3arm.sh's protections - do NOT use them.

1c. GEMINI PATH: CC_AGENT=gemini, MODEL=gemini-3.6-flash, max effort. Set maxSessionTurns IDENTICALLY for all 4 arms (Gemini has no --max-turns; an uncapped arm voids the comparison). Note the harness's own caveat: Gemini reports cache_creation=0 (no cache-write class), so its numbers are a self-contained 4-arm comparison, NOT comparable to the Claude cells.

Files: tools/run_quad.sh (new), tools/run_3arm.sh:2984+ (gemini branch), logs/toolchain.py (verifier).

content.text:
Measured, and it does not explain REP30 — the opposite of what we'd expect if cache were the driver:

```
cell        n    tokens    cache-miss   index s/sess
REP30      26   -17.66%      62.5%         5.3
CS50       47   +12.84%      66.7%         7.7      <- COLDER, scored 30pt better
CS50B      45    +9.94%      47.2%         8.7      <- more index time, scored better
REP50X     48    +2.89%      44.4%         2.3
SMOKER12W  12   +33.45%      50.0%         4.6

rep30 instances with a pre-existing cache dir: 30/30
cache dirs on disk: 145
```

REP30's cache conditions are unremarkable — its miss rate sits mid-range and its index time (5.3s) is *lower* than CS50's 7.7s and CS50B's 8.7s. **CS50 was colder on both counts and scored +12.84% against REP30's −17.66%.** So warmth cannot be carrying the difference.

Two reasons the "fresh instances = cold cache" intuition doesn't hold here: I built all 30 graphs before launching, and the 20 shards populate cache entries as they go, so by mid-cell most instances had entries regardless of never having been benchmarked.

This is the third time cache has been proposed as the explanation — twice by me — and the third time the per-cell numbers refuse it. I've stopped treating it as a live hypothesis; the index build is real (9–46s) but it is charged once and is small against 3.2M-token sessions.

One genuine piece of good news in that output: REP30 has moved from **−21.01% to −17.66%** as the last pairs land, so the tail pairs are net winners. 4 pairs left.

Two findings, and the second answers your question directly.

**First, a bug I just caught:** `shared_discipline` reached **0 of 30** REP30 prompts. I wired it into the non-published prompt branch only, and REP30 inherits `PUBLISHED_EXACT=1` which takes the other branch. So my fairness fix never landed in this cell. That needs fixing before any further cell, and it also means my hypothesis for REP30's result is refuted.

**Second — the arms swapped, and this is the real answer:**

```
              eg tok/sess   eg turns    baseline tok/sess   baseline turns
SMOKER12W      2,612,495       50.2         3,925,750           59.6
REP30          3,614,026       61.2         2,878,175           52.5
```

It is not that eg got worse against a fixed baseline. **Both moved, in opposite directions.** eg went from 2.61M to 3.61M tokens (+11 turns) and the baseline went from 3.93M to 2.88M (−7 turns).

On SMOKER12W's instances the **baseline flails** — 59.6 turns — and eg looks efficient by comparison. On REP30's fresh instances the baseline is tidy at 52.5 turns and eg is the one flailing at 61.2.

The two cells share only 3 instances. SMOKER12W's 12 are all drawn from rep50x — the set this tool has been tuned against for the entire campaign. REP30's 27 are not. So the honest reading is: **eg's historical advantage came substantially from the baseline being expensive on rep50x, not from eg being cheap.** Remove the familiar instances and the baseline's cost drops by a third while eg's rises.

That is the same pattern already in the ledger from R50FIX — the withdrawn +16.10% turned out to be eg's turns unchanged while the *baseline* improved 62.2 → 52.9. This is the third independent confirmation, and it is why the out-of-sample cell mattered more than another rep50 run.

It also reframes the plan: the change budget targets eg's excess edits and scratch files, which is exactly the +11 turns eg gained here. That lever is still pointed at the right thing.

content.text:
Right to interrogate it. Three distinct states, and only one is cheating:

**1. eg-only frugality — that WAS cheating.** The original `sym_rules()` shipped "the cost is dominated by HOW MANY TURNS you take", "NEVER read a whole file", "minimal fix and STOP" to eg/cmm/graphify and **not** baseline. Every one of those helps an arm with no tool. That is what PR #69 removes, and the harness's own comments valued those instructions at −26.2%, −18.0%, −16.4% — larger than any tool effect ever measured here.

**2. Both arms get it — not cheating, but it changes the benchmark.** Identical text to both arms means no arm asymmetry. It is fair. But it makes both arms cheaper and compresses the difference you are trying to measure, so it is a choice about baseline conditions, not a neutral fix.

**3. Neither arm gets it — the cleanest control.** And this is what REP30 actually ran:

```
shared_discipline text in delivered prompts
  REP30      eg 0/30    baseline 0/30
  SMOKER12W  eg 0/12    baseline 0/12
```

**Zero, both arms, both cells.** So REP30's −17.66% was measured with *neither* arm receiving frugality advice. That is a clean comparison, and it means the negative result is not an artifact of me handing the baseline help.

Now the part I should flag rather than let slide. My approved plan proposes adding a change budget to **both** arms, with the stated rationale that it constrains eg more because eg edits more (5.48 vs 4.44 files). That is fair by the letter — identical text — but choosing an instruction *because* it will help eg more is selection, and a skeptic could reasonably call it tuning the benchmark toward the tool.

The defensible way to run it is to measure both conditions and report both: budget-on and budget-off, each with both arms symmetric. If eg's advantage only appears with the budget on, that is a finding about the budget, not about the graph — and it should be stated that way rather than banked as a tool win.

I would rather tell you that now than have it become a sixth withdrawal.

**Same 12 instances, same tool, five runs, spanning 49.5 points** — and pooled is a perfectly monotone function of the turn delta. Every row orders correctly.

So SMOKER12W was not a good cell, it was a **lucky** one: eg hit its lowest turn count across all five runs (50.2) while the baseline hit its highest (59.6), both extremes in eg's favour simultaneously. REP30 sits at eg 59.1 / base 52.2 → −6.9 → −17.66%, exactly where that relationship predicts.

SMOKER12W's tasks need **3.5× larger patches**. A bigger fix has more places to find, which is where a code graph should help; REP30's small-patch tasks give it less to do. The practical consequence: no 12-instance cell can support a claim, including the +33.45% I retracted and then un-retracted earlier tonight. Blocking work before the 300x4 Gemini cell. Do NOT install toolchains while SMOKER12 is live (agents probe for go/cargo/bundle mid-session; installing under a running cell contaminates it).

1a. INSTALL MISSING TOOLCHAINS on graphbench-c: go, cargo/rustc, bundle(ruby), pytest, dotnet.
    Why: 129/300 of multilingual_300 (Rust 43 + Go 42 + Ruby 44) cannot run their own tests; env/build is 19.26 calls/session = 35% of a session, symmetric across arms. This is H4 from the plan: it does not change the ratio, it strips ~12 calls/session of noise from BOTH arms and shrinks the +-13pt CI that makes 3%/9%/13%/16% indistinguishable.
    Verify: `command -v go cargo rustc pytest bundle` all resolve; re-run logs/toolchain.py and confirm the MISSING count drops to 0.

1b. WRITE run_quad.sh — 4-arm driver (baseline, eg, cmm, graphify) carrying run_paired.sh's guards:
    - PKG_ISO per-arm FATAL check
    - /tmp purge decline -> FATAL (the patched behaviour)
    - half-complete tuple -> results/<TAG>_r1.unpaired.txt + QUAD_STRICT=1 refuses
    - prompt_invariant.sha256 compared unconditionally, missing = FATAL
    - harness exit code checked (exit 2 stops the cell)
    - **ARM ORDER ROTATION** by instance index (Latin-square / rotate by _idx % 4). Without this, arm 4 always gets the warmest machine state and the 4-arm result is uninterpretable. run_matrix.sh/run_ladder.sh do fixed-order sweeps and lack run_3arm.sh's protections - do NOT use them.

1c. GEMINI PATH: CC_AGENT=gemini, MODEL=gemini-3.6-flash, max effort. Set maxSessionTurns IDENTICALLY for all 4 arms (Gemini has no --max-turns; an uncapped arm voids the comparison). Note the harness's own caveat: Gemini reports cache_creation=0 (no cache-write class), so its numbers are a self-contained 4-arm comparison, NOT comparable to the Claude cells.

Files: tools/run_quad.sh (new), tools/run_3arm.sh:2984+ (gemini branch), logs/toolchain.py (verifier).

content.text:
Patch size is **refuted**, and backwards from my story:

```
corr(log gold patch, saving)
  REP30    n=28  r=+0.036  p=0.8578
  REP50X   n=48  r=-0.104  p=0.4778
  CS50     n=47  r=-0.064  p=0.6686
  CS50B    n=45  r=+0.003  p=0.9827
  pooled  n=140  r=-0.058  p=0.4976

tercile split (pooled)
  small patch  median   652 chars   +5.51%
  mid          median 1,326 chars   -6.67%
  large patch  median 4,687 chars   -7.70%
```

eg does **better** on small patches, not large. So the 7,350-vs-2,096 gap is not the mechanism — my "a graph pays off on big spread-out fixes" story is inverted. Eleventh predictor dead.

The repo comparison is more interesting:

```
SMOKER12W 11 repos | REP30 28 repos | shared: 5
shared repos: caddy, carbon, faker, micropython, preact
```

**Four of those five shared repos are REP30 losers** — caddy, carbon, micropython, preact — while carbon and faker were SMOKER12W *winners*. `carbon` is the sharpest case: `carbon-2665` scored **+36.7%** in SMOKER12W and `carbon-3098` scored **−264.9%** in REP30. Same repo, same language, different issue, opposite sign by 300 points. So it is not a repo property either.

On your fairness question — by measurement both cells were equally fair:

```
              VERIFY   frugality   tool block   prompt delta
SMOKER12W       0/0       0/0       eg only       857 bytes
REP30           0/0       0/0       eg only       857 bytes
```

REP30 is the first cell where that is enforced *structurally* (VERIFY removed unconditionally, `FAIRNESS_STRICT=1`) rather than by a pinned flag, but the delivered prompts were equivalent. One gap I should name: I verified `VERIFY=0` for REP50X/CS50/CS50B from their configs, but I have **not** checked those three cells' prompts for the frugality curriculum the way I checked these two. Since they produce the +8.73%, that is worth closing before anyone quotes it.

content.text:
GCP auth expired — it lapses roughly hourly and the workflow agents will need VM access too, so this blocks the whole thing.

Please run this in the session:

```
! gcloud auth login
```

While you do that, here's the workflow I'll fire the moment it's back, so you can redirect it if the shape is wrong:

```
Phase 1  FORENSICS       one agent per loser worse than -20% (11 of them)
                         each reads its own transcripts on the VM, eg vs baseline:
                         call decomposition, files edited, graph payloads, what the
                         extra turns went on -> returns a structured defect record

Phase 2  DEDUP           one agent folds 11 defect records into distinct classes,
                         since carbon/fmt/micropython already look like one class

Phase 3  WINNER CHECK    3 adversarial agents, each told to REFUTE: take the proposed
                         fix classes and find winners they would damage. Default to
                         "this fix hurts winners" unless they can show otherwise.

Phase 4  SYNTHESIS       SOLUTIONS.md: per class -> defect, fix, expected value in
                         points, fairness verdict (both-arms or eg-only), and which
                         winners are at risk
```

Two things I'll build into it rather than leave to chance. Every agent gets told to report **caveman-compressed** output, because their tool output doesn't reach me — only their report does. And the winner-check agents are prompted to *default to refuted*, since that adversarial framing has killed roughly 45% of claims in this project including several of my own tonight.

One caveat I want on the record before it runs: this workflow finds **per-loser** defects, and per-loser repair has already been measured at **+0.0pt** in this campaign — 93% of losers flip sign between cells, and the same 12 instances just spanned 49.5 points across five runs. So the likely honest output is "these are noise, not defects." I'd rather run it and find that cleanly than assume it, but I don't want the workflow's existence to imply I expect it to find 11 fixable bugs.

content.text: REP30 is done: **n=28, pooled −18.09%, median −7.29%, 12 wins of 28.** 13 losers are worse than −20%. Launching the workflow over them:

input.script:
export const meta = {
  name: 'rep30-loser-forensics',
  description: 'Per-loser forensics on REP30, dedup into defect classes, adversarially check winner damage, emit SOLUTIONS.md',
  phases: [
    { title: 'Forensics', detail: 'one agent per loser worse than -20%' },
    { title: 'Dedup', detail: 'fold defect records into distinct classes' },
    { title: 'WinnerCheck', detail: 'adversarial: find winners each fix would damage' },
    { title: 'Synthesis', detail: 'write SOLUTIONS.md' },
  ],
}

const VM = 'gcloud compute ssh graphbench-c --zone us-east1-b --tunnel-through-iap --command'
const S = '$HOME/pe1/graphmark/agentic-swebench'

const LOSERS = [
  { id: 'immutable-js-2006',   lang: 'JavaScript', tok: '-320.1%', dturn: '+47' },
  { id: 'carbon-3098',         lang: 'PHP',        tok: '-264.9%', dturn: '+48' },
  { id: 'caddy-5995',          lang: 'Go',         tok: '-193.0%', dturn: '+27' },
  { id: 'micropython-15898',   lang: 'C',          tok: '-96.5%',  dturn: '+16' },
  { id: 'redis-10095',         lang: 'C',          tok: '-92.6%',  dturn: '+15' },
  { id: 'phpspreadsheet-4214', lang: 'PHP',        tok: '-59.9%',  dturn: '+1'  },
  { id: 'preact-3010',         lang: 'JavaScript', tok: '-54.2%',  dturn: '+14' },
  { id: 'fmt-2457',            lang: 'C++',        tok: '-53.2%',  dturn: '+13' },
  { id: 'lucene-13170',        lang: 'Java',       tok: '-46.5%',  dturn: '+11' },
  { id: 'nushell-13246',       lang: 'Rust',       tok: '-34.3%',  dturn: '+6'  },
  { id: 'docusaurus-9183',     lang: 'TypeScript', tok: '-30.0%',  dturn: '+5'  },
  { id: 'pylint-7080',         lang: 'Python',     tok: '-26.8%',  dturn: '+8'  },
  { id: 'ruff-15626',          lang: 'Rust',       tok: '-20.2%',  dturn: '+16' },
]

const DEFECT = {
  type: 'object',
  required: ['instance', 'root_cause', 'defect_class', 'is_tool_fault', 'evidence', 'proposed_fix', 'fix_is_generic'],
  properties: {
    instance: { type: 'string' },
    root_cause: { type: 'string', description: 'one sentence, what the extra turns went on' },
    defect_class: { type: 'string', description: 'short slug e.g. scratch-harness, scope-creep, build-churn, thin-payload, missed-fix-file, unknown' },
    is_tool_fault: { type: 'boolean', description: 'true only if the GRAPH caused it; false if the agent would have done this without the tool' },
    graph_calls: { type: 'integer' },
    graph_payload_bytes: { type: 'string' },
    eg_files_edited: { type: 'integer' },
    base_files_edited: { type: 'integer' },
    eg_edited_the_fix_file: { type: 'boolean' },
    evidence: { type: 'string', description: 'concrete numbers and filenames from the transcripts' },
    proposed_fix: { type: 'string', description: 'a specific change to tool output or harness. empty string if none is justified' },
    fix_is_generic: { type: 'boolean', description: 'true if the fix would ALSO help an arm with no tool (then it must go to both arms or neither)' },
    verdict_noise: { type: 'boolean', description: 'true if this looks like run-level variance rather than a defect' },
  },
}

const CLASSES = {
  type: 'object',
  required: ['classes'],
  properties: {
    classes: {
      type: 'array',
      items: {
        type: 'object',
        required: ['class_slug', 'instances', 'defect', 'fix', 'fix_is_generic', 'tokens_at_stake'],
        properties: {
          class_slug: { type: 'string' },
          instances: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
          defect: { type: 'string' },
          fix: { type: 'string' },
          fix_is_generic: { type: 'boolean' },
          tokens_at_stake: { type: 'string' },
          confidence: { type: 'string' },
        },
      },
    },
    noise_instances: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
  },
}

const REFUTE = {
  type: 'object',
  required: ['verdict', 'damaged_winners', 'reasoning'],
  properties: {
    verdict: { type: 'string', description: 'REFUTED if the fix would damage winners or is unjustified; SURVIVES only if you could not break it' },
    damaged_winners: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
    reasoning: { type: 'string' },
    fix_class: { type: 'string' },
  },
}

phase('Forensics')
log(`forensics on ${LOSERS.length} REP30 losers worse than -20%`)

const records = await parallel(LOSERS.map(L => () => agent(
`You are doing forensics on ONE benchmark loser. Report in CAVEMAN-ULTRA-COMPRESSED form: numbers and
filenames only, no prose padding. Use rtk for git/file ops where it applies.

CONTEXT. A paired A/B benchmark compares two arms on the same SWE-bench instance:
  arm "eg"       has a code-graph retrieval tool (entire-graph, invoked as \`entire graph search|def|callers|grep\`)
  arm "baseline" has no such tool, only Grep/Glob/Read/Bash
Both arms get byte-identical prompts apart from an 857-byte tool block. Cell name is REP30.
Instance: ${L.id}   language: ${L.lang}   eg lost ${L.tok} tokens with a turn delta of ${L.dturn}.

YOUR JOB. Read the actual session transcripts on the VM and determine why eg spent more. Run commands
via:  ${VM} '<remote command>'
Suite root on the VM is ${S} (call it S).

Transcripts live at:
  S/results/REP30_r1_eg/ccfg/projects/<dir>/*.jsonl        (eg arm)
  S/results/REP30_r1_baseline/ccfg/projects/<dir>/*.jsonl  (baseline arm)
The <dir> name contains a slugified instance id; match on the first 46 chars of
the id with underscores turned into hyphens, lowercased. Session result JSON:
  S/results/REP30_r1_<arm>/<arm>/<full_instance_id>/cc_out.json

Existing scorers you should reuse rather than rewrite (run them, read their source if needed):
  S/logs/why30.py       per-loser call decomposition (edit its TARGETS list in a /tmp copy)
  S/logs/losers30.py    loser table
  S/logs/payload30.py   payload economics

DETERMINE, with numbers:
 1. call decomposition per arm: graph / locate / read / edit / build+test / other
 2. how many distinct files each arm EDITED, and their basenames
 3. whether eg edited the same file(s) the baseline edited (the likely real fix)
 4. graph call count and each payload's byte size
 5. what the EXTRA turns were actually spent on — quote the repeated commands
 6. any harness error, crash, timeout, permission failure, or tool error in either arm

CRITICAL JUDGEMENT — be skeptical, this is the part that matters:
 - is_tool_fault must be TRUE only if the GRAPH caused the extra work. If the agent wrote its own
   repro scripts, thrashed on builds, or wandered — and would plausibly have done so with no tool —
   that is NOT a tool fault. Note that the baseline also writes repro files in this benchmark.
 - If eg made ZERO graph calls, the loss cannot be a tool effect. Say so.
 - Set verdict_noise TRUE if this looks like ordinary run-to-run variance. Context you must weigh:
   the same 12 instances re-run five times in this project spanned 49.5 percentage points, and
   93% of losers flip sign between cells. A single loss is weak evidence of a defect.
 - proposed_fix must be a concrete change to TOOL OUTPUT or the HARNESS. If nothing is justified,
   return an empty string. Do not invent a fix to have something to say.
 - fix_is_generic: TRUE if your fix would also help an arm with no tool at all (e.g. "write fewer
   scratch files", "run tests less"). Those must go to both arms or neither, so they cannot be
   counted as a tool win.`,
  { schema: DEFECT, label: `forensics:${L.id}`, phase: 'Forensics' }
))).then(r => r.filter(Boolean))

log(`${records.length}/${LOSERS.length} forensics records returned`)

phase('Dedup')
const classes = await agent(
`Fold these ${records.length} per-loser defect records into DISTINCT defect classes. Caveman-compressed.

RECORDS:
${JSON.stringify(records, null, 1)}

RULES:
 - Merge instances whose root cause is the same mechanism even if the surface differs.
 - A class whose members are mostly verdict_noise=true or is_tool_fault=false is NOT a defect class;
   list those instances under noise_instances instead of inventing a fix for them.
 - fix_is_generic=true for the class if the fix would help a no-tool arm. Be honest: "write fewer
   throwaway scripts" and "run the test suite less" are generic.
 - tokens_at_stake: sum the losses of the class members, from these known values:
   immutable-js-2006 3.85M, carbon-3098 4.00M, caddy-5995 4.83M, micropython-15898 0.76M,
   redis-10095 1.19M, phpspreadsheet-4214 1.28M, preact-3010 1.28M, fmt-2457 1.45M,
   lucene-13170 0.75M, nushell-13246 0.31M, docusaurus-9183 1.22M, pylint-7080 0.78M,
   ruff-15626 0.69M.
 - confidence: state it plainly, including "low - single instance" where that is the truth.`,
  { schema: CLASSES, label: 'dedup', phase: 'Dedup' }
)

const fixClasses = (classes && classes.classes ? classes.classes : []).filter(c => c.fix && c.fix.length > 0)
log(`${fixClasses.length} candidate fix classes; ${(classes && classes.noise_instances || []).length} instances judged noise`)

phase('WinnerCheck')
const LENSES = [
  'winner-damage: name specific REP30 winners this fix would make WORSE and say through what mechanism',
  'fairness: decide whether this fix is arm-asymmetric help, i.e. whether it would help an arm with no tool at all',
  'evidence-strength: decide whether the underlying defect is established at all, or is a single noisy instance',
]

const refutations = await parallel(LENSES.map(lens => () => agent(
`You are an adversarial reviewer. Your DEFAULT verdict is REFUTED. Only return SURVIVES for a fix you
genuinely could not break. Caveman-compressed output.

YOUR LENS: ${lens}

PROPOSED FIX CLASSES:
${JSON.stringify(fixClasses, null, 1)}

REP30 WINNERS you must protect (instance, saving, turn delta eg-minus-base):
  gson-2479 +52.6% -6 | gson-2158 +42.2% -17 | django-13821 +38.4% -10
  fluentd-4655 +37.3% -3 | hugo-12562 +29.5% +2 | core-11870 +23.3% -2
  framework-48636 +20.3% -2 | fastlane-19765 +17.4% +1 | rubocop-13680 +16.3% -8
  faker-2970 +10.8% -1 | hugo-12204 +2.5% +2
You may inspect them on the VM:  ${VM} '<remote command>'   suite root ${S}
Winner transcripts: S/results/REP30_r1_eg/ccfg/projects/<dir>/*.jsonl

FACTS YOU MUST WEIGH — these have killed most claims in this project:
 - The same 12 instances re-run five times spanned 49.5 percentage points. 93% of losers flip sign
   between cells. Per-loser repair has previously measured +0.0pt.
 - Eleven predictor classes for the loss tail have been tested and ALL are null: instance identity
   (r=-0.022), language, difficulty, patch size (p=0.50, and small patches do BETTER), graph call
   count (p=0.394), tool failure rate, index completeness, cache-miss rate, index seconds, retrieval
   rank correctness (inverted), tool relevance score (inverted), payload size (inverted: sessions
   with a thin payload averaged +3.70% vs -52.43% for sessions without one).
 - The payload costs $0.03 across 24 pairs, 0.038% of tokens. Payload-shrinking fixes are worthless.
 - A fix that helps a no-tool arm is CHEATING if delivered to the tool arm only. The strongest
   predictors measured are files-edited delta (r=-0.742) and scratch-file delta (r=-0.656) — and eg
   edits 5.48 files vs baseline 4.44, writes 1.60 scratch files vs 1.04. So a scope fix is generic.

Return one verdict for the WHOLE set under your lens, naming the specific winners at risk.`,
  { schema: REFUTE, label: `refute:${lens.split(':')[0]}`, phase: 'WinnerCheck' }
))).then(r => r.filter(Boolean))

phase('Synthesis')
const md = await agent(
`Write SOLUTIONS.md for this benchmark investigation. Dense, technical, no filler. Markdown.

CELL RESULT: REP30, the first out-of-sample cell (27 of 30 instances never used before).
  n=28 pairs, pooled -18.09%, median -7.29%, 12 wins of 28, 23.2M tokens lost by the eg arm.
  Oracle variants: eg-never-loses +12.41%; every-session-at-median-win +23.32%; at-p75-win +38.39%.

DEFECT CLASSES (post-dedup):
${JSON.stringify(classes, null, 1)}

ADVERSARIAL VERDICTS (reviewers defaulted to REFUTED):
${JSON.stringify(refutations, null, 1)}

REQUIRED SECTIONS:
 1. Result and what it means — the out-of-sample number, stated plainly.
 2. Defect classes — table: class, instances, tokens at stake, is_tool_fault, confidence.
 3. Fixes that SURVIVED adversarial review — with expected value in points and fairness verdict
    (both-arms vs eg-only). If none survived, say so in one clear sentence; do not pad.
 4. Fixes REJECTED and why — name the reviewer's reason.
 5. Instances judged NOISE, with the reason (five runs of the same 12 spanned 49.5pt).
 6. What must NOT be attempted — the eleven dead predictor classes and the $0.03 payload, so nobody
    re-runs them.
 7. Honest bottom line — is there a route to a positive out-of-sample number, and what would it take?

RULES:
 - Never present a generic discipline fix (fewer scratch files, fewer test runs, narrower edits) as a
   tool win. It must be labelled both-arms.
 - Every number carries its n. Do not quote a single-cell figure as settled.
 - If the honest answer is "eg costs tokens out of sample and no fix in this set changes that", write
   exactly that.`,
  { label: 'write-solutions-md', phase: 'Synthesis' }
)

return { solutions_md: md, classes, refutations, n_records: records.length }

content.text:
Workflow running — 17 agents across 4 phases. `/workflows` shows live progress.

```
+---------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| REP30 FINAL   n=28 pairs   0 FATAL                                        |
|   pooled  -18.09%   median  -7.29%   wins 12/28                           |
|   23.2M tokens lost by the eg arm                                         |

| WORKFLOW  rep30-loser-forensics                                           |
|   Forensics    13 agents, one per loser worse than -20%                   |
|   Dedup         1 agent, folds records into defect classes                |
|   WinnerCheck   3 adversarial agents, DEFAULT VERDICT = REFUTED           |
|                 lenses: winner-damage / fairness / evidence-strength      |
|   Synthesis     1 agent writes SOLUTIONS.md                               |
+---------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

Three things I built in deliberately, since they're where this kind of investigation usually goes wrong.

**Every forensics agent is told not to invent a fix.** `proposed_fix` may be an empty string, and they must set `is_tool_fault=false` when the agent would have thrashed without the tool — which is the honest answer for `lucene-13170`, where eg made zero graph calls and still lost 46.5%.

**They're given the noise context up front:** five runs of the same 12 instances spanned 49.5 points, and 93% of losers flip sign between cells. Without that an agent looking at one loss will always find a story.

**The winner-check agents default to REFUTED** and are handed all eleven dead predictor classes plus the $0.03 payload figure, so they can reject anything that re-treads ground already measured. They're also told the strongest predictors — files-edited delta r=−0.742, scratch delta r=−0.656 — are *generic*, since eg edits 5.48 files against baseline's 4.44. That means a scope fix cannot be booked as a tool win.

My honest expectation, stated before I see the output: **most of these will come back as noise, not defects.** The instance-level evidence is one observation each against a ±49-point run-to-run spread. The classes I'd give real odds to are the two with mechanism behind them — `carbon-3098` (13 files edited vs 1) and `caddy-5995` (51 locate calls, never touched `replacer.go`). If the workflow returns 13 confident fixes, I'll distrust it rather than the noise finding.

I'll report the md and my read when it lands.

content.text:
Honest answer, with the arithmetic rather than a vibe.

**The two targets are structurally different:**

```
REP30 (out-of-sample, n=28)          current -18.09%
  eg never loses                              +12.41%   <- 11% lives HERE
  every session at eg's median win (23.3%)    +23.32%
  every session at p75 win (38.4%)            +38.39%

rep50x (in-sample, n=140)            current  +8.73%
  eg never loses                              +23.76%   <- 25% lives just past HERE
  every session at median win (32.1%)         +32.08%
```

**11% is reachable by loss elimination alone** — it sits below the never-lose oracle, so you never have to make a single win bigger. That's why I said it's reachable.

**25% is not, on either draw.** On rep30 it needs never-losing *plus* about 13 points of win growth. On rep50 it needs essentially perfect loss elimination — beating the +23.76% oracle by a point. Those are different problems and only the first is a "stop losing" problem.

**Why loss elimination is hard anyway:** eleven predictor classes for which sessions lose have been tested and all are null — instance identity, language, difficulty, patch size (inverted), graph call count, tool failure rate, index completeness, cache warmth, index seconds, retrieval rank (inverted), relevance score (inverted), payload size (inverted). You cannot target what you cannot predict.

**And the one lever that does work is generic.** The strongest predictors are edit-scope delta (r=−0.742) and locate delta (r=−0.724). eg edits 5.48 files against baseline's 4.44 and writes 1.60 scratch files against 1.04. A discipline that fixes that helps a no-tool arm too, so it goes to both arms — eg gains only from having more excess to remove. Real, but bounded.

**What 25% would actually require:** the tool becoming substitutive. Today 2.78 graph calls displace 1.12 greps — a rate of 0.40. Getting big wins on most sessions needs roughly 2.26, a 5.6× improvement. That is not a config search, it is tool design: the graph would have to be the thing the agent reaches for at every locate moment instead of once at turn 1 and never again.

So my view: **chase 11% on rep30, and treat 25% as a product roadmap item, not a benchmark target.** If the scope mechanism holds up in the smoke cell, 11% is a defensible out-of-sample number and would be the first positive one this campaign has produced on fresh instances. Quoting 25% would require either the in-sample draw or an asymmetric prompt — and both of those are how the four withdrawn headlines happened.

One thing that would change my mind: if the workflow comes back with a genuine eg-only defect worth several points in the caddy/carbon class, the loss side has more headroom than I've credited and the gap to 25% narrows. I'll tell you either way when it lands.

content.text:
Two answers, and the second is the more useful one.

**15% depends on which draw:**

```
rep50x   never-lose oracle +23.76%   -> 15% is BELOW it, reachable by loss elimination alone
REP30    never-lose oracle +12.41%   -> 15% is ABOVE it, needs win growth too
```

So 15% is reachable in-sample and slightly out of reach out-of-sample without making wins bigger.

**Now the better question — why don't I use it.** I've been working in a repo with entire-graph installed and `.entire/graph-agent.md` telling me to search first. Across this entire session I used it approximately **zero times** and ran dozens of greps, finds and Python scripts. Honestly, here's why:

**1. I needed exact text, not symbols.** Every code change I made tonight — `sym_rules`, `_strip_verify`, `published_exact_eg_tool` — required byte-exact `old_string` for an Edit. The graph returns a symbol body; I still had to read the file to get the surrounding text right. It saved the *search* and not the *read*, which is exactly why 2.78 graph calls displaced only 1.12 greps.

**2. The comments were the thing that mattered.** I hit **six** comment-vs-code false positives tonight, including inside my own fairness guard. The graph strips comments. On those six occasions it would not have helped — it would have actively misled me, because the answer lived in a comment saying "deliberately absent".

**3. My question was usually "does this string exist anywhere", not "where is this symbol".** Grep answers the first. The graph answers the second. Agents ask the first far more often.

**4. It's a bash idiom I have to remember; grep is reflex.** I reach for it at turn 1 if prompted, then never again — which is precisely the measured pattern: 2.78 calls at call index ~1, then 27 manual locate calls.

**The big changes that would follow from that:**

- **Return edit-ready text.** Output that can be pasted directly as an Edit `old_string` — the exact region including comments and whitespace — eliminates the follow-up Read entirely. That is the single biggest one, because the Read is what the tool currently fails to displace.
- **Answer the grep question.** A content search over the indexed corpus, comments included, so it competes with `grep -rn` rather than only with "find the definition".
- **Be in the tool menu, not the shell.** MCP puts it where the agent chooses tools at every locate moment. Measured cost: 403 tokens per turn, 0.63% of a session — a third of what the payload already costs, so affordable.
- **Stop indexing only symbols.** Roughly a third of my locate calls were for config, build files, test fixtures and log output — things a symbol graph doesn't hold.

If those landed, the substitution rate goes from 0.40 toward the 2.26 that 15% needs — and it would get there by removing Reads, which is the half of the pool the tool has never touched. That is a product change, not a benchmark change, and it's the honest version of "how do we hit 15%".

The design that does work is a **2×2 factorial on the same instances, in one cell**:

content.text:
Confirmed — it's selection, not cache. Pure Gaussian noise with no cache, no tool and no intervention reproduces the same signature:

```
                       simulated (noise only)      measured (real benchmark)
selected WORST 13      -68.4 -> -8.3   +60.1pt     -138.7 -> -7.5   +131.1pt
selected BEST   5      +96.9 -> +11.1  -85.8pt      +69.6 -> +23.3   -46.3pt
```

Opposite signs in both, from arithmetic alone. Nothing physical is required to produce it.

The mechanism: every observation is *true effect + noise*. When you pick the 13 worst, you are partly picking the 13 unluckiest. Re-run them and the bad luck doesn't repeat, so they rise — regardless of what you changed. Same in reverse for the best.

Three independent reasons it isn't cache:

1. **Opposite directions.** A warm cache makes every session cheaper, so it would move both groups the same way. Selection moves them apart.
2. **No re-run was involved.** I measured RTM by comparing the *same instances across five cells that already exist*. No cache state changed to produce +131pt.
3. **Cache has been refuted three times already** — CS50 ran colder than REP30 on both miss rate (66.7% vs 62.5%) and index time (7.7s vs 5.3s), and scored 30 points better.

The magnitude difference between my simulation and reality is real though, and worth naming: my Gaussian model understates the loser tail (real losses reach −320%) and overstates the winner side. The distribution is heavy-tailed and asymmetric, so treat +131pt as the measured figure and +60pt as the idealised one.

1  drop or gate RELATED SITES     eg-only, fair, 9.3% precision, directly feeds extra edits
2  change budget, both arms       targets files-edited delta r=-0.742

Here's the quantified route:

```
REGRESSION on REP30, n=28

  each extra file eg edits costs 19.55 points
  current files_delta  +1.14   (eg 5.48 files vs baseline 4.44)

```

**So 15% needs eg to stop editing roughly one extra file per session.** Not a heroic change — from 5.48 files down to the baseline's 4.44. That alone brackets past the target, because each extra file costs nearly 20 points.

The route, concretely:

```
1  change budget, BOTH arms         declare intended files; edits outside require a reason
                                    targets files_delta directly (r=-0.742)
2  gate RELATED SITES               9.3% precision, 8.7 files listed per call — the most
                                    likely source of the +1.14. EG_LIT_DROP=1 already exists,
                                    testable offline for $0
3  measure with a 2x2, random draw  baseline | baseline+fix | eg | eg+fix, 16 instances,
                                    64 sessions, ~$215. RTM-immune because the fix effect
                                    is measured within-cell on identical instances
4  PRIMARY endpoint = files_delta    arm-internal, doesn't need to beat the ±131pt RTM wall
```

Two risks I want on the record, because they could make this a fifth withdrawal.

**Causality could run backwards.** `files_delta` may be a *symptom* of a session going badly rather than its cause — a flailing agent edits more files. If so, capping edits won't recover the tokens; the session will just flail differently. The 2×2 settles this: if the fix moves `files_delta` but not tokens, the correlation was downstream.

**Capping edits can break correctness, and we are not grading it.** Forcing eg to touch only the gold file could produce a cheaper *wrong* patch — which our token-only measurement would score as a win. Given that `eg edited the gold file 100%` in both groups already, some of those extra edits may be genuinely required. Before shipping any scope constraint as a win, that needs one graded cell, which we have deliberately not run.

The honest sequence is therefore: test item 2 offline for free tonight (does RELATED SITES actually feed the extra edits), then the 2×2 at ~$215, and only then a graded confirmation. I'd rather find out that item 2 is the whole mechanism for $0 than assume it.

**eg's savings are real at the retrieval stage and get spent downstream.** It reaches the fix with less searching, ends up with spare turns, and spends them exploring instead of stopping. All three verified independently:

```
1  /tmp/w/00868e71 -> checkouts/REP30_r1_eg/eg/google__gson-2158
   CONFIRMED. The advertised scratch dir is a SYMLINK into the live checkout.

2  fmtlib__fmt-2457   baseline patch 518,275 B   eg patch 4,050 B   (128x)
   CONFIRMED. A patch of copied files passed the non-empty-patch gate.

3  /usr/local/go/bin/go exists, `go` NOT on PATH
   CONFIRMED. netjail exits 127 on bare `go`; whichever arm guesses the
   absolute path gets a real toolchain.
```

These are real defects and they change the answer to your question.

**The biggest single loss in the cell was a coin flip.** `caddy-5995` cost 4.83M tokens. The two arms issued **byte-identical** first probes, then the baseline guessed `/usr/local/go/bin/go` and got a real `go test`, while eg concluded there was no toolchain and wrote Python reimplementations of `replacer.go` and `lexer.go`. Nothing about the graph decided that.

**One pair should never have counted.** fmt's baseline "patch" is 518KB of copied `orig/include/**` — not a fix. It passed the gate, and that pair is in the −18.09%.

**And there's a feedback loop I hadn't imagined:** because scratch lands inside the checkout, the graph **re-indexes the agent's own scratch files**, which then outrank `src/` in search results. The agent's scaffolding actively degrades its own tool.

So the route to 15% is not primarily a tool change:

```
harness defects, all measured SYMMETRIC (28/30 sessions in EACH arm)
  toolchain lottery           6 instances   9.14M tokens
  scratch-in-repo symlink     5 instances  11.27M nominal
  blocked git stash/log       5 instances   hand-rolled before/after at 5-10x
```

Being symmetric, fixing them does **not** move the mean — it cuts the variance. With run-to-run sd at 76.6pt, that is precisely what's blocking measurement. A real effect of 15% is invisible through a ±131pt RTM wall; remove the toolchain lottery and the scratch pollution and the wall comes down.

Honest sequence for 15%, revised:

```
1  fix the harness         drop the symlink, provision toolchains once before the arm
                           split, build patch.diff from tracked files only, flag
                           untracked-path patches instead of passing them
2  re-run REP30            same 30 instances, clean harness. This is now a
                           MEASUREMENT fix, so the number it produces is the
                           first trustworthy out-of-sample figure
3  only then a tool change  the 2x2 scope test, if step 2 still shows a gap
```

`SOLUTIONS.md` is written to `graph-bench-results/`. Its §7 concludes "eg costs tokens out of sample and no fix in this set changes that" — which is correct as stated, since none of these are *tool* fixes. But it undersells the consequence: they are measurement fixes, and the measurement is currently too noisy to see 15% even if it were there.

Blocking work before the 300x4 Gemini cell. Do NOT install toolchains while SMOKER12 is live (agents probe for go/cargo/bundle mid-session; installing under a running cell contaminates it).

1a. INSTALL MISSING TOOLCHAINS on graphbench-c: go, cargo/rustc, bundle(ruby), pytest, dotnet.
    Why: 129/300 of multilingual_300 (Rust 43 + Go 42 + Ruby 44) cannot run their own tests; env/build is 19.26 calls/session = 35% of a session, symmetric across arms. This is H4 from the plan: it does not change the ratio, it strips ~12 calls/session of noise from BOTH arms and shrinks the +-13pt CI that makes 3%/9%/13%/16% indistinguishable.
    Verify: `command -v go cargo rustc pytest bundle` all resolve; re-run logs/toolchain.py and confirm the MISSING count drops to 0.

1b. WRITE run_quad.sh — 4-arm driver (baseline, eg, cmm, graphify) carrying run_paired.sh's guards:
    - PKG_ISO per-arm FATAL check
    - /tmp purge decline -> FATAL (the patched behaviour)
    - half-complete tuple -> results/<TAG>_r1.unpaired.txt + QUAD_STRICT=1 refuses
    - prompt_invariant.sha256 compared unconditionally, missing = FATAL
    - harness exit code checked (exit 2 stops the cell)
    - **ARM ORDER ROTATION** by instance index (Latin-square / rotate by _idx % 4). Without this, arm 4 always gets the warmest machine state and the 4-arm result is uninterpretable. run_matrix.sh/run_ladder.sh do fixed-order sweeps and lack run_3arm.sh's protections - do NOT use them.

1c. GEMINI PATH: CC_AGENT=gemini, MODEL=gemini-3.6-flash, max effort. Set maxSessionTurns IDENTICALLY for all 4 arms (Gemini has no --max-turns; an uncapped arm voids the comparison). Note the harness's own caveat: Gemini reports cache_creation=0 (no cache-write class), so its numbers are a self-contained 4-arm comparison, NOT comparable to the Claude cells.

Files: tools/run_quad.sh (new), tools/run_3arm.sh:2984+ (gemini branch), logs/toolchain.py (verifier).

All four launchers fixed, no live `unset PKG_ISO` remains, all parse clean.

```
+---------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| HARNESS DEFECT 1 of 4 — FIXED                                             |
|   unset PKG_ISO removed from go_rep30, go_sub12, auto_smoke12b,           |
|   auto_big200. run_3arm.sh derives GOMODCACHE/GOCACHE/GOPATH/npm/gem/     |
|   composer/cargo/m2 from it, so unsetting it made every package cache     |
|   SHARED across arms and instances.                                       |
+---------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

Two consequences worth stating plainly.

**This was my defect and it affected more than REP30.** `auto_smoke12b.sh` also unset it, which means SMOKE12B — the cell that produced the withdrawn +25.25% — ran without package isolation too. So did BIG200. The isolation was written specifically to close three documented gold leaks (`docusaurus-10130` npm pack, `carbon-2752` composer cache, `caddy-5995` module cache) and it was being disabled at launch time in every launcher I inherited from.

**I could not determine whether a leak actually fired.** The symmetric pattern in the scan argues against it, and caddy — the one case I traced properly — was a genuine solve, not a leak. But the checkouts are deleted, so the question is unanswerable now. That's a permanent gap in the audit trail for this cell.

Three defects remain, in value order:

```
2  toolchain lottery      _pkgguard exits 127 when the real binary isn't on PATH.
                          /usr/local/go/bin/go exists but isn't on PATH, so a bare
                          `go` dies and whichever arm guesses the absolute path wins.
                          Worth 9.14M tokens across 6 instances.
3  /tmp/w symlink         scratch lands inside the checkout, gets re-indexed, and
                          agent-written bundles outrank src/ in the graph.
4  patch gate             a 518KB patch of copied files passed as valid.
```

Item 2 is the biggest and needs care, because making `go` reachable is exactly what the module-cache leak note warns about — so it has to land *together* with the isolation fix I just made, not before it. I'll do that next, plus keeping checkouts after a run so this audit gap can't recur.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Defect 2: the toolchain lottery.

_pkgguard resolves the real binary by stripping its own dir from PATH. If the result is empty it
exits 127 with "no real '<name>' found on PATH behind the guard." That message is
indistinguishable from "this toolchain is not installed", so agents conclude the language is
unavailable and hand-roll a simulator.

Measured on REP30: /usr/local/go/bin/go EXISTS but /usr/local/go/bin is not on PATH. On caddy-5995
both arms issued byte-identical first probes; the baseline then guessed the absolute path, ran real
`go test`, and wrote a correct one-line fix. eg concluded there was no toolchain and wrote Python
reimplementations of replacer.go and lexer.go. That single coin flip cost 4.83M tokens -- the largest
loss in the cell -- and it is symmetric noise, not a tool effect.

FIX: search well-known install locations before giving up, and when it still fails, NAME what was
looked for so the agent can tell "absent" from "not on PATH".

SAFE ONLY WITH ISOLATION: a reachable `go` plus a SHARED module cache is the documented caddy-5995
leak channel. PKG_ISO was restored in all four launchers first, so GOMODCACHE/GOPATH are now
per-instance and this cannot re-open it.
"""
import os, sys

p = os.path.expanduser("~/pe1/graphmark/agentic-swebench/tools/netjail/_pkgguard")
s = open(p).read()

OLD = '''real="$(PATH="$newpath" command -v "$name" 2>/dev/null)"
if [ -z "$real" ]; then
  echo "netjail: no real '$name' found on PATH behind the guard." >&2
  exit 127
fi'''

NEW = '''real="$(PATH="$newpath" command -v "$name" 2>/dev/null)"
# TOOLCHAIN FALLBACK (2026-08-10). Several toolchains are installed in this image but NOT on PATH --
# /usr/local/go/bin/go is the measured case. Exiting 127 here reads to the agent as "the language is
# not installed", so it hand-rolls a simulator instead of running the real thing. On caddy-5995 both
# arms probed identically, the baseline happened to guess the absolute path and the eg arm did not;
# that coin flip decided a 4.83M-token gap. Searching the known locations removes the lottery for
# BOTH arms symmetrically -- it grants no arm anything the other cannot have.
if [ -z "$real" ]; then
  for _d in /usr/local/go/bin /usr/lib/go/bin /usr/lib/go-*/bin "$HOME/.cargo/bin" \\
            /usr/local/bin /usr/bin /opt/*/bin /snap/bin; do
    if [ -x "$_d/$name" ]; then real="$_d/$name"; break; fi
  done
fi
if [ -z "$real" ]; then
  # Say WHERE we looked, so "absent" is distinguishable from "not on PATH".
  echo "netjail: '$name' is not installed in this image." >&2
  echo "         searched PATH behind the guard, plus /usr/local/go/bin /usr/lib/go*/bin" >&2
  echo "         \\$HOME/.cargo/bin /usr/local/bin /usr/bin /opt/*/bin /snap/bin" >&2
  exit 127
fi'''

if "TOOLCHAIN FALLBACK (2026-08-10)" in s:
    print("  already patched"); sys.exit(0)
if OLD not in s:
    print("  PATCH TARGET NOT FOUND -- nothing written"); sys.exit(1)

mode = os.stat(p).st_mode
open(p + ".new", "w").write(s.replace(OLD, NEW, 1))
os.chmod(p + ".new", mode)          # os.replace does NOT inherit mode -- this cost a launch earlier
import shutil; shutil.copy2(p, p + ".pre-toolchain")
os.replace(p + ".new", p)
os.chmod(p, mode)
print("  _pkgguard patched; mode preserved %o" % (mode & 0o777))

input.command:
cat > /tmp/fix_collect.py <<'OUTER'
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Defect 4: the patch gate accepted 518KB of agent scaffolding as a valid fix.

collect_patch.sh already excludes untracked scratch (repro_*, reproduce*, build/, tests, lockfiles),
but fmt-2457's baseline fell through two gaps:
  orig/include/fmt/*.h   -- a wholesale copy of the original headers, made to hand-roll a before/after
                            comparison because netjail blocks `git stash`. No `orig/` pattern existed.
  fix.diff               -- a saved patch file. Only `patch.diff`/`patch.txt` were excluded.
Result: a 25-file, 518,275-byte "patch" passed the non-empty-patch gate. eg's patch for the same
instance was 4,050 bytes -- a 128x difference that scored as a legitimate pair.

Adding only UNTRACKED-file patterns, so nothing a repo genuinely tracks is affected. Deliberately NOT
excluding changelog/ or similar: rubocop-13680 legitimately adds a new changelog file and is the only
new-file patch in the cell, so a blanket new-file drop would delete a real result.
"""
import os, sys, shutil

p = os.path.expanduser("~/pe1/graphmark/agentic-swebench/tools/collect_patch.sh")
s = open(p).read()

ANCHOR = """      *.log|patch.txt|patch.diff)                                            continue ;;"""
NEW = """      *.log|patch.txt|patch.diff)                                            continue ;;
      # ADDED 2026-08-10 after fmt-2457 shipped 518KB of scaffolding through the gate.
      # A hand-made copy of the pre-fix tree, used to fake a before/after because netjail
      # blocks `git stash`/`git checkout`:
      orig/*|*/orig/*|original/*|*/original/*|pre/*|*/pre/*|before/*|*/before/*) continue ;;
      # Saved patches and backups the agent writes to diff against itself:
      *.diff|*.patch|*.rej|*.bak|*.orig|*.old|*.save)                        continue ;;
      # Exploration scaffolding, the measured top loss class (carbon wrote explore.php,
      # explore2.php, revert.php; fmt wrote edge_join{,2,3}.cc; caddy wrote lexer_cases.py):
      explore*|*/explore*|scratch*|*/scratch*|debug_*|*/debug_*)              continue ;;
      revert*|*/revert*|fuzz_*|*/fuzz_*|stress*|*/stress*|edge_*|*/edge_*)    continue ;;"""

if "ADDED 2026-08-10 after fmt-2457" in s:
    print("  already patched"); sys.exit(0)
if ANCHOR not in s:
    print("  ANCHOR NOT FOUND -- nothing written"); sys.exit(1)

mode = os.stat(p).st_mode
shutil.copy2(p, p + ".pre-gatefix")
open(p + ".new", "w").write(s.replace(ANCHOR, NEW, 1))
os.chmod(p + ".new", mode)
os.replace(p + ".new", p)
os.chmod(p, mode)
print("  collect_patch.sh patched, mode %o preserved" % (mode & 0o777))
OUTER

```

Item 3 I'm declining to "fix" because the workflow was wrong about it. The symlink is a deliberate solution to a real problem, and the harm it was blamed for — scratch landing in the repo — happens regardless, since the agent's cwd *is* the checkout either way. The actual harm was patch pollution, which item 4 addresses directly.

One honest correction to my own earlier alarm: I said the module-cache gold leak may have fired in REP30. Traced properly, **caddy's baseline wrote that line itself** as an `Edit` to `replacer.go` — it derived the fix, it didn't lift it. The broader leak scan flagged many pairs but the pattern is symmetric across both arms, which argues against leakage, and the checkouts needed to settle it are deleted. So: no leak demonstrated, none excluded, and that audit gap is permanent for this cell.

What this changes about the numbers: all three fixes are **symmetric**, so they won't move the mean. They remove variance — and with run-to-run sd at 76.6pt and an RTM wall of ±131pt, variance is what's currently making a 15% effect unmeasurable. A clean re-run of REP30 is now the first thing worth spending on, and it would produce the first out-of-sample figure I'd actually defend.

# eg token-loss: verified solutions

> Companion to `LOSS-REASONS.md`. For every proposed fix, the bar for **VERIFIED** is hard:
> backed by (a) a MEASURED number+CI in `TokensNotes.md`, (b) a deterministic OFFLINE REPLAY
> (`$0`, no model calls), or (c) a source-level proof. A plausible idea with no number is
> **UNVERIFIED (needs a cell; MDE ~25pt at n=30)** — not a solution. Struck ideas stay struck.
>
> Data provenance: graphbench-c REP30 payloads / `gq_calls.log` / `why30.py` (live);
> graphbench-b absent from the project (its replays N/A). Verdicts run maker↔verifier to
> consensus (see footer).

---

## 0. The honest headline — read before proposing anything

**The verifiable token win is ≈ 0.** LOSS-REASONS establishes, and offline replay confirms, that
across the **8 forensicated losers** (n=23 snapshot: immutable, carbon, micropython, preact,
lucene, nushell, docusaurus, ruff) the gold file was *in the payload* (or the tool was never
called). The loss is **post-lookup behaviour**, and TokensNotes §0 is that tokens track **message
count**, not payload content — 11 payload-quality metrics are already dead as levers (§2.3). So:

> **Tail now fully forensicated (update 2026-08-10).** LOSS-REASONS §1 lists **12** losers. The 4
> formerly-parked — **caddy-5995 (−4.83M, the largest single loss in the campaign), fmt-2457,
> phpspreadsheet-4214, terraform-34814** = **8.02M = 38.4% of the −20.88M 12-loser drag** — are now
> decomposed (§§F–I below, $0 transcript-decomp pass, graphbench-c REP30_r1). Verdict holds and
> **strengthens**: every one is post-lookup behaviour, gold in-payload where the tool was called
> (caddy/fmt/terraform all reached & edited the gold), none is a retrieval defect. The denominators:
> **−20.88M** = the 12-loser drag (LOSS-REASONS §1, the §0 canonical figure); **−12.86M** = the
> 8-forensicated subset used for §C's bucket-% arithmetic. Both are stated where used; the
> reconciliation is: 12.86M (8 examined earlier) + 8.02M (4 examined now) = 20.88M (all 12). ✓

- Fixing retrieval / payload size addresses **at most 2 of 8** losers, and even a *lossless*
  payload trim is predicted ~0 tokens unless it removes edit→build **messages**.
- **~14–20% of the tail isn't the tool at all** (lucene made 0 graph calls; nushell/ruff are pure
  cargo churn) — the honest fix there is a **measurement gate**, not a token saver.
- The known behaviour lever (suppress improvised harnesses) is **fairness-fraught and struck**:
  eg-only is the withdrawn-headline fraud; a fair both-arms version nets ~0 because scratch-build
  is symmetric (delta −0.06).

**Two deliverables clear the bar — both are correctness/hygiene, neither is a measurable token
win:** a `gq=0` attribution gate, and a `RELATED SITES` trim (lossless for immutable-js **only** — the
general trim hurts ≥1 winner, ruff-15309, so it ships **only** with a carve-out that never drops a
gold-bearing RS line; harm-check §1). Everything else is needs-a-cell or refuted. Do not inflate this.

| solution | verdict | fairness | token effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| A · runnable-verify / anti-harness clamp | **REFUTED-in-ledger** | instruction = risk | eg-only illegitimate; fair ≈ 0 |
| B · drop/gate `RELATED SITES` | **PARTIAL** — lossless for immutable-js ONLY (harm-check §1: general trim hurts ≥1 winner, ruff-15309); loss-cut UNVERIFIED | tool-output = legit | ledger prior ≈ 0 |
| C · `gq=0` attribution gate | **VERIFIED** (as a measurement fix) | measurement = legit | 0 (corrects attribution) |
| D · near-empty-payload query fallback | **UNVERIFIED-needs-cell** (ADD-class, low prior) | tool-output = legit | negative prior |
| E · docusaurus extra-reads | **REFUTED / noise** | n/a | 0 |
| F · caddy improvised harness (no toolchain) | **REFUTED-in-ledger** (class A) | instruction = risk | eg-only illegitimate; fair ≈ 0 |
| G · fmt improvised harness | **REFUTED-in-ledger** (class A) | instruction = risk | eg-only illegitimate; fair ≈ 0 |
| H · phpspreadsheet context-accumulation | **REFUTED-as-tool-defect** | tool-output = legit | 0 (own-output growth, payload 0.10%) |
| I · terraform build-churn | **noise; tool NET-HELPFUL** (−10 locate) | tool-output = legit | 0 (n=1 inside ±40–90pt) |
| J · change-budget hook (block out-of-scope edits) | **UNVERIFIED-needs-cell** | **both-arms-only** (eg-only = struck cheat) | differential sign unknown; correctness-regression risk |
| K · deliver graph via MCP | **REFUTED-on-mechanism / net-negative** | n/a | **negative** — additive ~1,750 tok/turn schema cacheRead the payload-text arm never pays (payloads persist in both arms) |
| L · signature-only / minimal-field payload | **CONFIRMED low-leverage** | tool-output = legit | ≈ **0** (payload 0.04% of eg total ≈ 0.23% of loss; carry-cost ceiling 11.7%) |

---

## 0.5 The loss is cacheRead, not payload — the load-bearing spine

**Finding (VERIFIED, $0 transcript-decomp, graphbench-c REP30_r1 per-message modelUsage).** Decompose
the **four newly-decomposed losers**' token bills by usage bucket and the answer is monotone:
**95–102% of the loss is `cacheRead`** across all four — the accumulated conversation context
re-read on each turn. Output tokens are **1–2.4%**. The graph **payload itself is ≤0.42%** of the
loss in each (caddy 0.02%, phpspreadsheet 0.10%, fmt / terraform comparably negligible). Per-loser:
caddy 96.8% cacheRead, phpspreadsheet 95.4%, fmt 98.6%, terraform 102% (rounding on n=1).

**Scope (honest — do not overgeneralize).** The per-loser cacheRead split is **directly measured
only for these four** (the REP30_r1 decomp pass). For the **8 earlier-forensicated losers** —
including the two largest, **immutable −3.85M and carbon −4.0M (61% of the 12.86M subset)** — there
is no cacheRead-specific decomposition in this doc; for them we have only the **weaker §3b bound**
(behavioural payload ≤11.7% of loss). That bound is **consistent with** a cacheRead-dominated bill
but is **not** the same measurement. So: "cacheRead is the loss" is **proven on 4** and **inferred
on the other 8** via §3b + [[session-length-is-the-mechanism]] (r=0.947), not per-loser-verified.
Read the "95–102%" as "across the four decomposed losers," not literally "every loss."

**Two behavioural axes drive cacheRead** (and nothing else moves the needle):
1. **More assistant-messages at the same size** — each new turn re-reads the whole prefix. fmt **+13**
   asst-msgs, terraform **+2**, caddy **+48**.
2. **A fatter prefix / larger messages** — eg's own output inflates the context it then re-reads.
   caddy **+87%** fatter prefix; phpspreadsheet **+33%** fatter per-message (eg emitted 75K vs 45K
   output tok) on **+7** asst-msgs.

**Why this is the spine, not a side-note:**
- It **strengthens the ≈0 headline.** The loss lives in a bucket payload edits barely touch:
  trimming what the tool returns shrinks cacheRead **only by the payload's carry-cost** — bounded
  by §L's ≤11.7%-of-loss ceiling (§3b), realized far below it — so it is a **low-leverage** lever,
  not a zero one; the bulk of cacheRead moves only by removing edit→build **messages**. (Precisely:
  once emitted, the payload sits in the prefix and is re-read every turn as cacheRead — that carry
  cost is the ≤11.7% channel §L/§3b quantify — so "cannot touch cacheRead" would be too strong;
  "touches ≤11.7%, realized far less" is the honest statement.) This is the mechanism behind §0's
  "tokens track message count, not payload."
- It **reinforces [[session-length-is-the-mechanism]]** (r=0.947 msg-delta↔token-delta): cacheRead
  *is* the channel through which message count converts to tokens — every extra assistant turn pays
  the whole accumulated prefix again.
- It **explains the payload graveyard** (§2.3, 11 dead payload-quality metrics): they are dead
  because they operate on ≤0.42% of the bill. No payload metric can be a lever when payload is
  sub-1% of the loss.

**Measurement correction — `num_turns` undercounts.** `num_turns` is a coarse counter that misses
intra-turn assistant messages; it labelled phpspreadsheet **+1** when the real delta is **+7
assistant-messages** (90 vs 83). Rank losers by **assistant-message-delta + cacheRead/msg**, not
`num_turns` — those two separate winners from losers cleanly where `num_turns` blurs them.

**Consequence for interventions (see §§J–L):** any fix must attack cacheRead — i.e. cut
assistant-messages or shrink eg's *own* output — to matter. A fix that changes only the payload
(MCP delivery, signature-only fields) touches the wrong bucket by construction and is refuted or
low-leverage on arithmetic alone.

---

## A · Improvised harness — carbon-3098, micropython-15898

**Proposed:** hand the agent a runnable verification command so it stops writing its own
repro/explore/revert scripts.

**Mechanism (real, measured):** an improvised throwaway harness costs **+39,527 tok/call**, CI
[+16.5K, +63.7K] (TokensNotes §1.3). carbon wrote `repro.php` / `explore.php` / `explore2.php` /
`revert.php` (+48 turns); micropython wrote `repro.py` + `fuzz_comma.py` (+16).

**Verdict — REFUTED-in-ledger.**
- The graph *worked*: carbon's gold `CarbonInterval.php` appears **12×** in the payload (healthy
  4802/1415/605/1641/2859 B); micropython — both arms fixed `mpz.c`. Loss is **100% post-lookup**.
- The fix is already struck (§2.-1): a runnable verify command *fails the §6 fairness test* (it
  would help a no-tool arm), *inflates payload (context rot)*, and was *measured harmful* — the
  VERIFY line cost ~11 turns, and `EG_VERIFY_MODE=off` shipped. Harness failure-mode #17 struck
  the MCP `verify_command` tool for the same reason.
- A **fair both-arms** version nets ~0: `scratch_build` is **symmetric, delta −0.06** (§1.2c),
  19% of every session, identical in both arms.

**Fairness:** instruction/build-knowledge = **fairness-risk** (eg-only = withdrawn-headline fraud,
§6.6). **Token effect:** eg-only illegitimate; fair version ≈ **0 differential**.

---

## B · Scope creep / `RELATED SITES` — immutable-js-2006

**Proposed:** remove or gate the `RELATED SITES` block from the payload (it lists ~8.7
graph-adjacent files at ~9% precision and invites wrong edits).

**Verdict — PARTIAL: removal-is-lossless is VERIFIED FOR immutable-js ONLY (does NOT generalize —
harm-check §1); loss-reduction is UNVERIFIED.**
- **Lossless for immutable-js (offline replay, graphbench-c):** gold `src/Operations.js` = **rank 1,
  line 1** (`sliceFactory`). All three `RELATED SITES` headers sit at lines 134/301/451 — **strictly
  below the gold**. Removing the block provably cannot lose the gold **for this instance**. **VERIFIED
  (immutable-js).**
- **DOES NOT GENERALIZE (harm-check §1):** across REP50X+CS50+CS50B, `astral-sh__ruff-15309`
  (REP50X **+30.2% WINNER**) carries its gold `crates/ruff_linter/src/rules/pyflakes/fixes.rs`
  **only under the RELATED SITES header** — the primary body has it 0×. A blanket trim deletes the
  **sole in-payload pointer to the gold for a winner.** So B ships **only with a carve-out that never
  drops a gold-bearing RS line**, or accepts a 1-winner risk.
- **Precision 73/789 = 9.3%** (authoritative `logs/related.py` on graphbench-c; the current `eg-q`
  wrapper header states "measured precision 9%") — 91% of listed files non-gold. **MEASURED.**
  (The old 73/726 = 10.1% is the superseded upper bound — `related.py` line 38 flags it as a
  first-block-only count before it accumulated every `RELATED SITES` block.)
- **But the causal link to *this* blow-up is weak:** of eg's 4 wrong-edit files, `sources.js` and
  `edge.js` appear **0×** in the payload (agent-invented, not tool-induced); the compiled bundle
  `immutable.build.js` (definitively wrong) appears **only** in the agent's own `callers` output
  (line 457+), not in `RELATED SITES`. Only the `TrieUtils` siblings trace to `RELATED SITES`.
- §0 law + §2.3 (11 dead payload metrics): even a lossless trim is predicted ~0 tokens unless it
  removes edit→build **messages** — **UNVERIFIED**.

**Fairness:** **legitimate tool-output** change (removing a graph-derived feature only makes eg
leaner; baseline has no such list). **Ship it as a precision-honesty change; do not claim a token
win without a cell.**

---

## C · Tool-independent build churn — lucene-13170, nushell-13246, ruff-15626

**Proposed:** GATE — exclude `gq=0` instances from tool-loss **attribution**; always report
pooled-all **and** pooled-`gq≥1`.

**Verdict — VERIFIED (as a measurement fix).**
- `why30`: lucene "graph calls: 0". Independent recount (graphbench-c `REP30_r1_eg/eg`, empty
  `gq_calls.log`): **2 zero-call eg sessions** (apache__lucene-13170, scikit-learn__scikit-learn-14629)
  — **both are gated losers**: lucene −46.5% and scikit-learn-14629 −6.3% (eg 1,986,657 vs base
  1,869,628 = ~117,029 tok; both arms subtype=success, patch 2301B/2486B). Numerator reproduces
  exactly; denominator is **2 of 28 gated pairs** (eg has 29 dirs with cc_out >2B; only
  valkey-io__valkey-1499 fails the size gate, cc=0 — 28 is the correct final gated-pair count, not
  a stale snapshot). (redis-10095 is NOT zero-call: its `gq_calls.log` has 6 lines of real
  queries — recounted directly on graphbench-c.) The full **23→28 gated-pair delta was enumerated**
  on graphbench-c (all 28 eg dirs seen in the recount above): the **only** new loser in that delta is
  scikit-learn-14629; the remaining new pairs are winners, so the "no loser is a retrieval defect"
  generalization holds over the **final n=28 draw**, not merely the n=23 snapshot + scikit.
- Bucket (the three churn/zero-call losers **that are inside the 12.86M subset**) = lucene −745,147 +
  nushell −311,664 + ruff −688,839 = **−1,745,650 = 13.6% of the −12.86M loser drag**, none of it
  tool-caused (consistent with LOSS-REASONS "~20%"). Do **not** average a scikit-inclusive numerator
  over a scikit-exclusive denominator — the earlier "1,862,679 = 14.5%" was that error.
- **scikit-learn__scikit-learn-14629 is a 13th zero-call loser** (−117,029 tok, both arms
  subtype=success), discovered in this pass and **not yet in LOSS-REASONS §1's n=23 snapshot** (which
  lists 12). It is absent from **both** headline denominators. Its loss is zero-call = cannot be the
  tool, so it belongs to this churn/uptake bucket in kind. If catalogued as loser #13, both denominators
  grow by 117,029 (−20.88M → −20.99M; −12.86M → −12.98M) and the bucket becomes
  1,862,679 / 12.98M = **14.35%**. Stated separately here rather than smuggled into the 13.6% figure.

**Fairness:** measurement/attribution = **legitimate**. **Caveat:** for the question "cost of
*shipping* the tool on a workload," a `gq=0` session is a real **uptake** outcome (§6.4 one-shot,
§2.13) — so **do not silently drop it; report both cuts.** **Token effect:** 0 (corrects
attribution, saves nothing).

---

## D · Poor answer — preact-3010

**Proposed:** detect a near-empty payload → broader/semantic-query fallback to recover the gold.

**Verdict — UNVERIFIED-needs-cell, with a reframing that lowers the prior.**
- The single call was a **grep verb**: `grep "typeof .* === 'string'"` → 3 *legitimate* literal
  matches. The graph's grep behaved correctly — this was the agent choosing a narrow regex, **not
  a semantic-search failure.**
- The task is **"Add support for bigint" = an ADD task** → the §1.1 known-negative class (ADD
  pooled **−3.37%** vs MOD **+14.35%**; a confident wrong hit costs more than no hit). preact
  belongs to the structural ADD penalty, not a fixable retrieval defect.
- The gold `src/diff/children.js` *is* indexed, so a fallback *could* surface it — but the real
  fix site (primitive-child coercion) isn't where "bigint / typeof string" semantically points,
  so recovery is doubtful. Live replay to settle it was impossible (checkout deleted post-cell).

**Fairness:** payload/tool-output = legitimate. **Token effect:** UNVERIFIED; ADD-class prior is
negative.

---

## E · Extra file reads — docusaurus-9183

**Proposed:** none defensible.

**Verdict — REFUTED-as-fixable / noise.** Reads were 10 vs 2 (+8), but locate −3 and build −4 —
eg **substituted reads for greps/builds**. Gold `codeBlockUtils.ts` present **10×** in the payload
(tool found it; both arms edited it). Smallest loss, and the only loser where eg searched *and*
built **less** than baseline. Per §2.6, 93% of losers flip sign between cells; per-instance repair
= +0.0pt. Nothing to fix.

---

## F · Improvised harness, no toolchain — caddy-5995 (Go, −193%, −4,828,830 · LARGEST single loss)

**Class A improvised-harness — the biggest loss in the campaign.**

**Verdict — REFUTED-in-ledger (post-lookup behaviour, not the tool).**
- **Retrieval worked, both arms reached gold.** Gold is a 1-line change in `replacer.go`; eg edited
  it **correctly** (both arms reached the gold site).
- **The loss is a scratch toolchain sim.** The sandbox had **no Go toolchain**, so eg PORTED the Go
  lexer to Python to verify — `sim_replacer.py` / `sim_lexer.py` / `lexer_cases.py` / `repro.py`.
  This is the carbon/micropython pattern (§A) at maximal scale: **+48 assistant-messages, +87%
  fatter prefix**, 96.8% cacheRead.
- **Payload is not the cause:** the graph payload for this instance is **1,035 tok = 0.02% of the
  −4.83M loss.** VERIFIED transcript + modelUsage. Purely **post-lookup** behaviour.

**Fairness:** any "give it a runnable Go verify" fix = instruction/build-knowledge, **fairness-risk**
(eg-only = withdrawn-headline fraud, §6.6); the toolchain absence is symmetric across arms.
**Token effect:** eg-only illegitimate; fair both-arms ≈ **0 differential** (scratch-build symmetric,
§1.2c).

---

## G · Improvised harness — fmt-2457 (C++, −53.2%, +13 asst-msgs)

**Class A improvised-harness.**

**Verdict — REFUTED-in-ledger.**
- **Retrieval worked, both arms edited gold.** Gold `include/fmt/ranges.h` is **in the payload**;
  both arms edited it.
- **The loss is scratch C++ repros + builds:** eg wrote 4 repro files (`repro_join.cc`,
  `edge_join.cc`, `edge_join2.cc`, `edge_join3.cc`) + **2 cmake** invocations, **9 builds vs 4**.
  **+13 assistant-messages**, **98.6% cacheRead**. VERIFIED.
- Payload negligible (same ≤0.42% mechanism as §0.5). Post-lookup.

**Fairness:** runnable-verify instruction = **fairness-risk** (§6.6); build churn symmetric.
**Token effect:** eg-only illegitimate; fair ≈ **0**.

---

## H · Context accumulation, NOT a tool defect — phpspreadsheet-4214 (PHP, −59.9%)

This is the **cost-per-turn mode** (num_turns delta only +1) now fully characterized — and it is
**not** a tool defect.

**Verdict — REFUTED-as-tool-defect; it is context accumulation.**
- **Tool output is near-identical between arms:** `tool_result` bytes **71,061 (eg) vs 70,823
  (base)** — payload is **0.10% of the loss.** The tool did not deliver more.
- **`num_turns` UNDERCOUNTS badly:** the real delta is **+7 assistant-messages** (90 vs 83), not +1.
  Each message is **+33% fatter prefix**, driven by **eg's OWN output** (75K vs 45K output tok) plus
  locate churn (`cat` **×19 vs ×8**). **95.4% cacheRead.** VERIFIED per-message usage.
- So the cost is eg talking more and re-reading its own growing context — the §0.5 axis-2 mechanism —
  not the graph returning bloat.

**Fairness:** tool-output legitimate (near-identical bytes). **Token effect:** **0** attributable to
payload; the loss is own-output growth, addressable only by cutting eg's messages.

---

## I · Build-churn / measurement-gate — terraform-34814 (Go, −8.3%, +2 asst-msgs)

**The tool was NET-HELPFUL here.**

**Verdict — noise; tool net-helpful, loss inside the ±40–90pt single-run band.**
- **Graph SAVED locate calls:** **17 vs 27 locate = −10** — the graph did its job.
- **Retrieval worked:** gold `resource_provisioner.go` in payload, both arms edited it.
- **Small residual churn:** eg wrote 3 `zz_repro_*_test.go` + **16 `go` invocations**; **+2
  assistant-messages**, cacheRead/msg **identical** between arms, **102% cacheRead** (rounding on
  n=1). The **−8.3% is a single instance well inside ±40–90pt single-run noise** ([[rep30 single-run
  noise]]). VERIFIED.

**Fairness:** tool-output legitimate. **Token effect:** **0** — a measurement-gate / noise case, not
a fixable defect; if anything the locate saving is a small win swamped by build noise.

---

## J · Change-budget hook (PreToolUse blocks out-of-scope edits)

**Proposed:** a PreToolUse hook that blocks edits outside the declared change scope, on the theory it
stops the improvised-harness / scratch-file churn that dominates §§A,F,G.

**Verdict — UNVERIFIED-needs-cell; and it MUST be both-arms.**
- The cited **"35% → 4%" is an EXTERNAL blog number, not our measurement.** Zero cells here.
- **Baseline also writes repros** (the harness pool is symmetric, §1.2c). An eg-only hook = the
  **struck cheat** (withdrawn-headline fraud, §6.6). A fair version blocks **both arms**, which
  removes ~25% of *each* — differential sign **unknown**.
- The only version that could help is **differential**: does the graph let eg declare a *better*
  scope than baseline? That is verified **NOWHERE** (0 cells).
- **Correctness-regression risk:** blocking edits can suppress legitimate multi-site fixes.

**Fairness:** **both-arms-only**; eg-only is struck. **Token effect:** UNVERIFIED — needs a paired
cell; differential sign unknown, regression risk real.

---

## K · Deliver the graph via MCP instead of payload text

**Proposed:** ship graph results through an MCP server (typed verbs) rather than inlined payload text.

**Verdict — REFUTED-on-mechanism / net-negative by arithmetic.**
- MCP loads the **5 graph-verb schemas (~1,750 tok) as cacheRead EVERY turn** × ~90–140 messages =
  **~150,000 cacheRead/session tax.**
- This schema tax is **purely additive — MCP does NOT replace the payload.** The graph result still
  comes back as an MCP `tool_result` (~the same bytes as the inlined payload) and, exactly like the
  inlined payload, persists in the prefix and is re-read every turn (the §L/§3b carry-cost). So
  **both** delivery modes carry the payload every turn; MCP **also** carries the schema every turn.
  The payload therefore **cancels** in the comparison and is not "delivered once."
- Net cost of MCP vs payload-text delivery = the schema overhead alone: **~1,750 tok/turn
  (≈150K/session)** added to the **exact bucket (cacheRead) that is 95–102% of the loss** (§0.5) —
  additive, on top of tool-result payloads that don't go away. (The earlier "~120× the payload"
  framing was apples-to-oranges: it divided schema-carried-every-turn by payload-counted-once, but
  the doc's own carry-cost model re-reads the payload every turn too, so only the schema is the
  delta. Struck.)
- **Never tested (0 cells delivered `mcpServers`)** — but no cell can rescue the arithmetic: an
  additive ~1,750-tok/turn schema tax that the payload-text arm never pays cannot come out ahead.

**Fairness:** n/a (delivery mechanism). **Token effect:** **negative** — refuted on mechanism.

---

## L · Signature-only / minimal-field payload

**Proposed:** shrink each payload entry to a bare signature / minimal fields to cut tokens.

**Verdict — CONFIRMED low-leverage.**
- One denominator, stated consistently (LOSS-REASONS §3b): direct payload = **29,489 tok = 0.04% of
  eg's TOTAL tokens ≈ 0.23% of the loss** (29,489 / 12,793,521). Per-instance the direct payload/loss
  ratio is **≤0.42%** (§0.5, caddy 0.02%, phpspreadsheet 0.10%). The over-charged **carry-cost
  ceiling** (crediting every payload byte to cacheRead re-reads on every turn) is **≤11.7% of the
  loss** (§3b). (The earlier "0.04% of the loss" and "<0.1% realized share" were denominator errors —
  0.04% is of eg's total tokens, and 0.23%-of-loss exceeds both; struck.)
- Shrinking a payload entry from **~1,200 → ~400 tok** removes ~0.15% of eg's total tokens — a rounding
  error on a loss whose 95–102% lives in cacheRead. Refuted as a meaningful lever — it is real but
  sub-1%-of-loss, dominated entirely by the cacheRead / message-count channel (§0.5).

**Fairness:** tool-output legitimate. **Token effect:** ≈ **0** (payload 0.04% of eg total ≈ 0.23% of
loss; carry-cost ceiling 11.7%).

`gq_calls.log` already in the ledger, plus the recorded outputs of `harm_related.py` / `harm_budget.py` /

re-run live and are reproduced here from the committed ledger only. Re-run when auth is restored to

Across **all gated pairs in REP50X+CS50+CS50B** (`/tmp/harm_related.py`): of the gold files that ever
appear inside a `RELATED SITES` block, **71 are SAFE** (the same gold basename also appears OUTSIDE the

  carve-out that never drops a gold-bearing RS line**, or accept a 1-winner risk.

  proven claim is "removal deletes the only payload delivery of the gold for a winner." That is the
  strongest payload-level statement the data supports, and it already refutes *hurts-nobody*.

### 2 · Change-budget hook — HURTS ≥5 WINNERS (quantifies the §J "regression risk")

had eg legitimately edit >1 gold file** — a plan-scoped budget declared from the turn-1 localization
would block the 2nd+ edit, converting a win into a correctness regression **and** a token-loss:
