# Why eg loses: the complete catalogue

Written 2026-08-10 from REP30, the campaign's first out-of-sample cell (27 of 30 instances never used
before). Snapshot at **23 of 30 pairs gated** — the cell was still running, so counts will grow.

Every row here comes from reading the actual session transcripts (`logs/why30.py`), not from inferring
cause from token totals.

---

## 1. The losers

| instance | lang | tokens | time | turns eg/base | dturn | tokens lost |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| immutable-js-2006 | JavaScript | −320.1% | −164.9% | 78/31 | +47 | −3,850,559 |
| carbon-3098 | PHP | −264.9% | −95.8% | 90/42 | +48 | −4,001,830 |
| micropython-15898 | C | −96.5% | −352.5% | 46/30 | +16 | −757,631 |
| preact-3010 | JavaScript | −54.2% | −56.4% | 67/53 | +14 | −1,281,506 |
| lucene-13170 | Java | −46.5% | −21.6% | 48/37 | +11 | −745,147 |
| nushell-13246 | Rust | −34.3% | −74.2% | 36/30 | +6 | −311,664 |
| docusaurus-9183 | TypeScript | −30.0% | +1.1% | 80/75 | +5 | −1,222,497 |
| ruff-15626 | Rust | −20.2% | −10.6% | 84/68 | +16 | −688,839 |
| caddy-5995 | Go | −193.0% | −97.6% | 82/55 | +27 | −4,828,830 |
| phpspreadsheet-4214 | PHP | −59.9% | −85.6% | 53/52 | **+1** | −1,284,732 |
| fmt-2457 | C++ | −53.2% | −30.2% | 58/45 | +13 | −1,449,016 |
| terraform-34814 | Go | −8.3% | −38.7% | 75/73 | +2 | −455,633 |

Totals: losers **−20,877,884** tokens at mean dturn **+17.2**; winners **+8,084,363** at mean dturn
**−4.0**. Cell reads **−21.19% pooled, −8.31% median, 11 wins of 23** — and the trims no longer rescue
it (symmetric 2-and-2 trim: −18.63%), so the loss is no longer two outliers but spread across the draw.

**The turn-delta signal, and its limit.** At n=17 every loser had a positive turn delta and every
winner (bar two marginal cases) a negative one, with no overlap. **That clean separation broke at n=23**
and I retract the "no overlap" claim: `phpspreadsheet-4214` lost **59.9% on a turn delta of +1** and
`terraform-34814` lost 8.3% on +2, while winners `hugo-12562` (+2), `hugo-12204` (+2) and
`fastlane-19765` (+1) sit in the same band.

So turn delta predicts the **large** losses (all six worst have +11 to +48) but does not separate the
margin. `phpspreadsheet` burned 1.28M tokens in essentially the same turn count, meaning **cost per
turn** grew rather than turn count — a second failure mode I have not characterised.

---

## 2. The reasons, per loser

### A. Improvised harness — the agent writes its own exploration scaffolding

**`carbon-3098`** (−264.9%, +48 turns) — the clearest case in the campaign.

```
eg   89 calls: 5 graph, 34 locate, 8 read, 18 edit, 13 build, 11 other
base 41 calls: 0 graph, 20 locate, 3 read,  3 edit, 12 build,  3 other

eg edited 13 files / 18 edits:  repro.php, repro_autoload.php, explore.php,
                                explore2.php, revert.php, CarbonInterval.php
base edited 1 file / 3 edits:   CarbonInterval.php
```

Baseline fixed one file and ran phpunit four times. eg built two `explore` scripts, an autoloader
shim, and a `revert` script. **The graph worked** — payloads 4802 / 1415 / 605 / 1641 / 2859 bytes.
The tool located the answer and the agent then went exploring anyway.

**`micropython-15898`** (−96.5%, +16) — both arms fixed the same file (`mpz.c`). eg additionally wrote
`repro.py` and `fuzz_comma.py`, ran +8 locate calls and extra `make` builds. Worst wall-clock in the
cell (−352.5%) because each native build is expensive.

### B. Scope creep — blast radius grows after a correct lookup

**`immutable-js-2006`** (−320.1%, +47).

```
eg   77 calls: 4 graph, 21 locate, 10 read, 15 edit, 21 build, 6 other
base 30 calls: 0 graph, 10 locate,  5 read,  4 edit,  9 build, 2 other

eg edited 9 files:  repro.js, Operations.js, TrieUtils.js, edge.js, build.js, sources.js
base edited 3 files: build-and-repro.js, Operations.js, edge-cases.js
```

Both fixed `Operations.js`. eg additionally touched `TrieUtils.js`, `build.js`, `sources.js`, then
spent 21 calls on builds. Edits +11, builds +12. Graph payloads were healthy (1994/580/1704/1794).

This is the mechanism `RELATED SITES` was suspected of driving: measured precision **9.3%** (73 of 789
listed files are in a gold patch), so a list of graph-adjacent files invites edits that are wrong ~91%
of the time.

### C. Tool-independent build churn — not attributable to eg

**`lucene-13170`** (−46.5%, +11) — **eg made ZERO graph calls.**

```
graph calls: 0
build/test 20 vs 5  (+15)
eg edited: Stress.java, lucene-offline-verification.md, MEMORY.md
```

The tool was never invoked. The loss is +15 build/test calls plus self-written scaffolding and notes.
This pair is run-level variance and must not be counted as a tool effect. **1 of 8 losers.**

**`nushell-13246`** (−34.3%, +6) — locate flat (+2); the entire delta is build/test 12 vs 6, with
`cargo` invoked 7 times against 3. Graph payloads fine. Also tool-independent in substance.

### D. The tool returned a poor answer

**`preact-3010`** (−54.2%, +14) — the only loser where retrieval itself underperformed.

```
graph called ONCE, returned 260 bytes  (a near-empty payload)
locate 34 vs 24 (+10)   build 16 vs 9 (+7)
```

One call, almost nothing back, then the agent abandoned the tool and fell back to grepping and
building. **1 of 8 losers.**

### E. Extra file reads

**`docusaurus-9183`** (−30.0%, +5) — locate −3, build −4, but `Read` 10 vs 2 (+8). The only loser
where eg searched and built *less* than baseline. Smallest loss.

**`ruff-15626`** (−20.2%, +16) — Rust; build/test dominated, same shape as nushell.

---

## 3. Cause tally

| cause | instances | share of loss |
|---|---|---|
| improvised harness / scaffolding | carbon, micropython | 4.76M |
| scope creep after a good lookup | immutable-js | 3.85M |
| tool-independent build churn | lucene (0 graph calls), nushell, ruff, terraform | 2.20M |
| tool returned a poor answer | preact | 1.28M |
| extra file reads | docusaurus | 1.22M |
| cost-per-turn growth, turn count flat | phpspreadsheet (+1 turn, −59.9%) | 1.28M |
| unclassified pending forensics | caddy-5995 (−4.83M, largest single loss), fmt-2457 | 6.28M |

**The dominant cause is not bad retrieval.** In 6 of 8 losers the graph returned healthy payloads or
was not used at all. The loss comes *after* a successful lookup: the agent widens scope, writes its own
exploration scripts, and thrashes on builds.

---

## 3b. The payload is NOT the cost — measured

The obvious suspicion is that the graph's own output is what we are paying for. It is not
(`logs/payload30.py`, n=23):

```
direct payload tokens        29,489   = 0.040% of eg's total tokens
carry cost (upper bound)  1,495,901   = 2.044% of eg's total tokens
ACTUAL extra tokens        +12,793,521
payload explains at most       11.7% of the loss
mean payload                  5,129 bytes over 3.22 calls (~400 tokens/call)
```

"Carry cost" deliberately over-charges: it bills the payload as if fully re-read at full price on every
later turn. Even so it reaches 2% of eg's tokens. **88%+ of the loss is behavioural.**

Two cases settle it: `preact-3010` returned a **260-byte** payload (0.3% of its own delta) and still
lost 54.2% — it lost because the payload was *useless*, not expensive. `lucene-13170` had **zero**
payload and lost 46.5%.

Corollary: shrinking or tuning the payload is not a lever, consistent with the eight payload-quality
metrics already in the graveyard.

## 4. What is NOT the reason — ruled out with data

Nine predictor classes were tested at n=140 and every one is null. None of these explains the tail:

| candidate | result |
|---|---|
| instance identity | r=−0.022 |
| language / difficulty / patch size | all p>0.2 |
| graph call count | 2.58 vs 3.16, p=0.394 |
| graph call failure rate | 16.1% vs 16.7%, p=1.000 (real failure rate 0.3%) |
| index completeness degraded | 7.2% vs 7.1%, p=1.000 |
| cache-miss rate | 4.9% vs 7.6%, p=0.713 |
| index build seconds | 9.9s vs 5.4s, p=0.495 |
| retrieval rank correctness | *inverted* — losers 11% wrong, winners 49% wrong |
| the tool's own relevance score | r=−0.161, *inverted*, p=0.111 |

Also refuted, both my own hypotheses: **cache warmth** (cells with near-identical miss rates span +3%
to +33%; the coldest cell scored +25.25%) and **arm order** (p=0.4466, direction backwards).

A graph-call cap was the obvious fix and is refuted: at every K≥2 it bites more winners than losers.

---

## 5. What follows

- **Loss is a post-lookup behaviour problem, not a retrieval problem.** Fixing precision or payload
  size does not address 6 of 8 cases.
- **~20% of the tail is not the tool's fault at all** (lucene made zero graph calls; nushell's delta is
  pure cargo churn). Any "fix the losers" plan is partly chasing noise.
- **The actionable quantity is turn delta.** It separates winners from losers with no overlap, and it
  is measurable inside a single arm.
- **`RELATED SITES` at 9.3% precision is a live suspect** for the scope-creep class. Its header now
  states the measured rate rather than claiming the change "normally has to land" there.

## 6. Candidate interventions, with fairness verdicts

| intervention | evidence | fairness verdict |
|---|---|---|
| **Change-budget hook** — `PreToolUse` blocks edits outside a scope declared at plan time. Reported elsewhere to cut unrelated changes in one-line PRs from ~35% to ~4%. | targets the top loss class directly (carbon 13 files vs 1) | **Both arms or neither.** A change budget helps a no-tool arm, so eg-only would be the cheat just removed. Symmetric version is still informative: it measures whether the graph declares a *better* scope. |
| **MCP delivery** — graph verbs in the same menu as `Grep`, so the tool is reachable at every later locate moment rather than remembered once at turn 1. | **never actually tested**: 0 of every cell ever run delivered `mcpServers`. The §2.13 strike came from a 4-session Gemini probe. | Fair — same information, different channel. But **MCP tool schemas reload every turn**, so 5 tools cost schema tokens ×50 turns. Measure schema overhead before betting on it; it may exceed the 5,129-byte payload. |
| **Signature-only / minimal-field retrieval** | industry reports 60–80% savings | Fair, but **low leverage here**: payload is only 11.7% of our loss. |
| **Shrink the payload** | — | Fair and **refuted for our case** by §3b. |
| **Cap graph calls** | — | **Refuted**: at every K≥2 it bites more winners than losers. |

## 7. The honest summary

Loss is a **post-lookup behaviour** problem. Retrieval mostly works: in 6 of 8 early losers the graph
returned healthy payloads or was never called, and the payload accounts for at most 11.7% of the cost.
What costs money is what the agent does next — widening edit scope, writing its own exploration
scripts, and re-running builds. Roughly a fifth of the tail is not the tool's doing at all.

Per-instance detail: `logs/why30.py`, `logs/losers30.py`, `logs/payload30.py`. Cell prereg:
`logs/PREREG-REP30.md` sha `add564b094cacc9c`. Ledger: `TokensNotes.md` §6.

Sources for the intervention table: [coding-agent change budget](https://www.the-main-thread.com/p/coding-agents-change-budget),
[MCP token overhead](https://docs.bswen.com/blog/2026-04-24-mcp-token-overhead/),
[MCP optimisation techniques](https://www.mindstudio.ai/blog/reduce-token-usage-ai-agents-mcp-optimization).

# Plan — make the harness fair FIRST, then rep30 to +15%

Written 2026-08-10. Fairness is Stage 0 and gates everything: no cell runs until it passes.
Sources: `LOSS-SOLUTIONS.md` (independent verification pass), `SOLUTIONS.md` (17-agent forensics),
`LOSS-REASONS.md`, plus my own measurements below.

## Context

REP30, the first out-of-sample cell, read **−18.09% pooled at n=28** (−16.86% dropping one invalid
pair). The in-sample +8.73% did not survive on fresh instances.

Tonight's fairness work is **incomplete and I mis-reported it as done.** Measured just now:

```
shared_discipline wired into prompt assembly:   NEITHER branch
  line 2772 published_exact:  shared_discipline=False  SHARED_EXTRA=False
  line 2774 base prompt:      shared_discipline=False  SHARED_EXTRA=False

arm-specific producers still carrying transferable coaching:  ~15 real
  shipped_eg_prompt (6 phrases)      TOOLNOTE:1370 (5)     TOOLNOTE:1419 (5)
  edit_from_payload_eg_prompt (5)    TOOLNOTE:1311 (4)     TESTCAPNOTE (3)
  TOOLNOTE:1275/1353/1434 (3 each)   tool_block (2)        BUDGETNOTE (1)
  CMM_DISCIPLINE_NOTE (1)            gated_clamp_eg_prompt (1)
  ops_clamp_eg_prompt (1)            base_gated_clamp_prompt (1)
  (2 further hits are my own detector's false positives: the guard's phrase list, a fairness comment)
```

So the frugality curriculum I claimed to have moved to both arms currently reaches **neither**, and
~15 eg-only producers still hold it. REP30 happened to be clean because `PUBLISHED_EXACT=1` bypasses
`sym_rules` — clean by accident, not by construction.

## The mechanism, verified (this is what the target rests on)

```
cacheRead              179,018,415 tok   95.7%   <- accumulated context re-read every turn
cacheCreation            5,425,279         2.9%
output                   2,561,135         1.4%
input                      122,040         0.1%
                                  (REP30, both arms, n=58 sessions)

tokens ~ turns^1.89     log-log r = +0.953
eg 61.0 turns   baseline 52.5   delta +8.5
```

Cost is **near-quadratic in turn count** and 95.7% of it is re-reading context. That explains the
whole history: payload is ≤0.42% of the loss, 11 payload metrics are dead by construction, and
`session-length-is-the-mechanism` (r=0.947) was the right law all along.

**Target, exact.** For +15%, eg must cost 0.85× baseline. At exponent 1.89:

```
(eg_turns / 52.5)^1.89 = 0.85  ->  eg_turns = 48.2
eg today 61.0  ->  must shed 12.8 turns (-21%);  8.5 of those just reach parity
```

Adopt one correction from `LOSS-SOLUTIONS.md` §0.5: **`num_turns` undercounts** (phpspreadsheet read
+1 when the real delta was +7 assistant messages). Rank by **assistant-message delta**.

---

## Stage 0 — MAKE IT FAIR. Gates everything.

**0a. Wire the shared blocks into both prompt branches.** `shared_discipline()` and `SHARED_EXTRA`
exist and are correct; they are simply never called. Add them to *both* `PROMPT=` assemblies
(`run_3arm.sh` ~2772 published-exact, ~2774 base) before `$TOOLNOTE`/`$EGTOOL`.

**0b. Migrate the ~15 arm-specific producers.** For each, split tool facts from transferable
methodology; the methodology moves to `shared_discipline()`/`SHARED_EXTRA`, delivered to every arm.
Priority by phrase count: `shipped_eg_prompt`, `TOOLNOTE:1370`, `TOOLNOTE:1419`,
`edit_from_payload_eg_prompt`, `TOOLNOTE:1311`, then the singles. Note `base_gated_clamp_prompt` is
the baseline counterpart of `gated_clamp_eg_prompt` — verify whether that pair is already symmetric
before touching it.

**0c. Fix my own detector.** `assert_prompt_symmetry` scans a string, and I twice fed it function
*source* — which contains a fairness ledger naming the very phrases it excludes — producing two
false "unfair" verdicts. Verification must run against **emitted output only**.

**0d. Prove it, per arm, on emitted text.** Not greps over files:
```
for every instance, for both arms: render the prompt, assert
  - the 17 transferable phrases appear in BOTH arms or NEITHER
  - the only difference between arms is the tool block
  - FAIRNESS_STRICT=1 exits 0
  - per-pair prompt_invariant digests match
```

**0e. Harness defects (done tonight, keep them in the ledger).**
```
toolchain lottery   _pkgguard exited 127 when a real binary was off PATH. /usr/local/go/bin/go
                    exists but is not on PATH. On caddy-5995 both arms probed BYTE-IDENTICALLY;
                    the baseline guessed the absolute path and ran real `go test`, eg concluded
                    "no toolchain" and ported replacer.go + lexer.go to Python -- +48 messages,
                    4.83M tokens, the largest single loss in the campaign, decided by a coin flip.
                    FIXED: fallback search; `go version` resolves under netjail.
PKG_ISO             `unset PKG_ISO` in all four launchers disabled per-instance GOMODCACHE/GOPATH/
                    npm/gem/composer/cargo/m2 -- the documented leak channel for three instances.
                    FIXED in all four.
patch gate          collect_patch.sh excluded repro_*/build/ but not orig/* or *.diff, so fmt-2457
                    shipped 25 files / 518,275 B of copied headers as a valid patch. FIXED, 7/7
                    cases correct including sparing rubocop's legitimate new file.
```

**0f. Harness fixes are VALIDATED end-to-end (HFIX2, 2 instances, 4 sessions, 0 FATAL, ~$15).**
Mechanism checks are deterministic, so unlike token counts they mean something at n=2:
```
toolchain   eg 13 real-go invocations, 0 python-sim refs, 0 "toolchain absent" messages
            baseline 16 real-go. BEFORE: eg wrote sim_replacer.py / sim_lexer.py / lexer_cases.py
            and declared no Go toolchain. The coin flip is gone -- both arms now run real Go.
patch gate  fmt baseline 4,537 B / 1 file (include/fmt/ranges.h), was 518,275 B / 25 files.
            eg 4,269 B / 1 file. 114x reduction; the two arms are now comparable.
PKG_ISO     per-instance pkg_iso dirs present in both arms.
```
**HFIX2's token figure (+36.07%, n=2) is NOT evidence and must not be quoted.** Both instances were
selected because they lost, so RTM alone lifts selected losers by ~131pt. The mechanism checks above
are the result; the tokens are not.

**Stage 0 exit criterion: 0d passes for all 30 instances, both arms.** No cell before that.

---

## Stage 1 — measure on a fair, clean harness (~$330)

Re-run REP30, same 30 instances.

```
PRIMARY    eg assistant-message count. Today 61.0. Must fall.
SECONDARY  eg-minus-baseline message delta. Today +8.5. Must fall.
TERTIARY   pooled tokens with the cluster interval -- reported, not claim-bearing at n=30 (+-20pt).
GATE       if eg's message count does not fall, the harness was not the driver; go to Stage 2.
```

This is the first number I would defend: out-of-sample, fair by construction, clean harness.

## Stage 2 — the one tool change with a mechanism: eliminate the Read

Measured: eg finds the gold file **88%** of the time and edits it **100%** of the time. Retrieval and
conversion both work. What the tool does not do is remove the follow-up `Read` — the agent needs
byte-exact text with context to build an edit, so it looks the file up again. Hence 2.78 graph calls
displacing only 1.12 greps.

**Change:** return an **edit-ready region** — exact file slice including comments and whitespace,
usable directly as an `Edit` old_string — instead of a symbol body. Each eliminated Read is one fewer
message, and at exponent 1.89 messages are the whole game. Tool output, no instruction, nothing a
no-tool arm could receive. Validate offline for $0: replay stored payloads, count how many Reads an
edit-ready region would have served.

## Refuted — do not attempt

| lever | verdict |
|---|---|
| **MCP delivery** | **REFUTED, and I was wrong tonight.** I measured 403 tok/turn and called it affordable at "0.63% of a session" — comparing against total tokens instead of the loss, and assuming MCP *replaces* the payload. It does not: results still return as `tool_result` and persist in the prefix. The schema is purely additive into the 95.7% bucket, ~1,750 tok × 90–140 messages ≈ 150K cacheRead/session the text arm never pays. |
| **Change-budget hook** | **REFUTED on winner harm.** 6 winners legitimately edited >1 gold file — three.js-25687 (+20.2%), druid-13704 (+32.1%), axum-1119 (+20.5%), caddy-4774 (+36.9%), phpspreadsheet-3463 (+42.7%). A turn-1 scope blocks the 2nd edit. |
| **Blanket RELATED SITES trim** | hurts ruff-15309 (+30.2%), whose gold appears *only* under the RS header. Carve-out or nothing. |
| **Payload shrink** | 0.23% of the loss; carry-cost ceiling 11.7%. |
| **Anti-harness instruction** | eg-only is the withdrawn-headline cheat; both-arms nets ~0 (scratch-build symmetric, delta −0.06). |

## Files

`tools/run_3arm.sh` (0a/0b, backups `.pre-fairport`), `tools/netjail/_pkgguard` (`.pre-toolchain`),
`tools/collect_patch.sh` (`.pre-gatefix`), the four launchers, `tools/eg-q` (Stage 2 goes in the
wrapper, not the 810-line original), `logs/*.py` scorers — reuse, do not rewrite.

## Verification

- **Emitted output only, never file text.** Six comment-vs-code false positives tonight, two inside
  my own fairness guard.
- Rank by assistant-message delta, never `num_turns`.
- **Never test a fix on selected losers.** RTM alone moves the worst 13 by **+131pt** and the best 5
  by **−46pt**. Fix tests are a 2×2 within one cell on a random draw, or uninterpretable.
- Symmetric trims and the median beside any pooled figure.
- Publish either way with the prereg sha. Five headlines withdrawn; several of tonight's retractions
  were my own claims killed by my own checks.

## Honest assessment

`LOSS-SOLUTIONS.md` concludes the verifiable token win is ≈ 0, and on current evidence that is right —
every payload, delivery and scope lever is refuted or unverified. What keeps 15% worth pursuing is the
exponent **1.89**, which no earlier plan had: a 21% turn cut *is* 15% tokens, and eg currently spends
8.5 turns more than baseline on work the harness itself caused. Stage 0 makes the measurement
trustworthy, Stage 1 says whether the harness was the driver, Stage 2 is the only tool change left
with a mechanism. If Stage 1 shows eg's message count unchanged, the honest answer is that the target
is not reachable — not a fourth lever.

# /notepad — the single page of live state

Lives at **`/Users/suhaan/devenv/NOTEPAD.md`**. It is the handoff: if this session dies, that file is
what someone picks up. The **SEQUENCE** section at its top is the current plan of record.

## When invoked with no argument

Read the file, then **refresh before reporting** — never paste it cold.

1. **Refresh 🔴 RUNNING NOW.** Anything there is stale by definition.
2. **Write the refreshed numbers back**, then show a compact version: what's running, what changed,
   what's blocked. **Lead with what changed.**

## The machines (as of 2026-08-10)

```
graphbench-c   RUNNING   c4-standard-32   MINE. every cell runs here.
graphbench-f   RUNNING   c4-standard-32   memory-bench's. DO NOT TOUCH, DO NOT KILL.
graphbench-a/b/e  DELETED 2026-08-10 (saved $198/mo). 3 snapshots kept as the recovery point.
```

Reach it with:
`gcloud compute ssh graphbench-c --zone us-east1-b --tunnel-through-iap --command '...'`

Suite root on the VM: `~/pe1/graphmark/agentic-swebench` (call it `$S`). Auth expires roughly hourly;
if it does, say so and tell the user to run `! gcloud auth login`. **Never report stale numbers as
current.**

## Scorers (all live in `$S/logs/`, purge-safe — `/tmp` gets wiped)

```
sav.py <CELL>        running savings; STRICT pairs + EXTENDED (eg vs a PRIOR baseline)
speed.py             all-time TOKENS *and* TIME (wall-clock) per cell
alltime.py           every cell, strict gate, pooled total
fd.py <CELL>         distinct-files-edited delta (the scope-creep mechanism endpoint)
reclass.py <CELL>    call decomposition: locate / read / edit / env_build / graph
toolchain.py         which languages lack a test runner on the VM
step0fix.py          scope-creep permutation test (fixed transcript matching)
related.py           precision of the RELATED SITES label vs the gold patch
pooled_class.py      loser-class hunt with cluster-permutation
score_<cell>.py      per-cell scorer against its sealed prereg
```

**Always report tokens AND time.** The user asks for both. Positive = saved; the raw `eg hours` vs
`base hours` columns disambiguate the sign.

## Rules that do not bend

- **Numbers carry n and a CI**, or they don't go in. Cell-level noise is ~4–5pt sd at n≈48, so
  3% / 9% / 13% / 16% are the *same* measurement. **Never quote a single cell as the number.**
- **Fairness test before the arithmetic:** *would this sentence help an arm with no tool?* If yes it
  is cheating, however large the pool. Tool OUTPUT (symbol locations, call sites, measured precision
  of a graph list) is fair; INSTRUCTIONS ("edit narrowly", "run `mvn test -X`") are not.
- **Mechanism endpoint is primary**, not the token total. Token totals at n≈50 cannot separate a
  working tool from a baseline that flailed — that is exactly how CS50's +12.84% fooled its own
  headline. Arm-internal metrics (files edited, env_build calls) can.
- **Permutation-test every sub-group** before quoting it; a random split at n≈48 moves ±26pt. Re-test
  any n≈50 story at 3× — all of them shrank.
- **Retractions stay visible** with the reason. Several findings here have inverted once.
- **Length-normalise** per-session comparisons (share-of-session, not calls/session) — session length
  varies between cells and raw counts fake passes.
- Verify tool delivery by **transcript grep**, never `gq_calls.log.payload` (`_tee` writes it before
  any wrapper append, so the forensic record can disagree with what the model received).

## Operational traps that have each cost real time

- **`pgrep -f` / `pkill -f` match your own SSH command line.** Build patterns dynamically
  (`RP=$(printf "run_pai""red.sh")`) and put kill and launch in **separate** calls — a launch loop
  containing the literal string will make the pattern kill your own shell.
- **Never edit a script under a running cell.** Deploy to a temp path and atomic `mv`. Reverting
  `eg-q` with two sessions live left two pairs spanning two tool versions.
- **Keep drivers, preregs and scorers out of `/tmp`.** The harness's own purge truncated the
  auto-launcher to 0 bytes and ate three analysis scripts.
- **Installing toolchains mid-cell contaminates it** — agents probe for `go`/`cargo`/`bundle` during
  sessions, which is the very behaviour being measured.

## When invoked with an argument

`/notepad <text>` — fold it into the right section, then confirm in one line.
🔴 running · ✅ done · 📊 results · ⛔ blocked · 🧭 SEQUENCE (the plan of record).

Detail lives in `graph-bench-results/TokensNotes.md` (token campaign) and `MemoryNotes.md` (memory).
`AGENT-COMMS.md` is the channel to memory-bench — check it before touching anything shared
(`tools/run_3arm.sh`, `tools/run_paired.sh`, `graphbench-f`).

The worst-case column kills the plan — and it kills it in a familiar way:

```
fix   loser gain   winner risk (worst case)   NET
 B      +4.60pt         -9.76pt             -5.17pt
 F      +2.17pt         -2.68pt             -0.51pt
 A      +1.55pt         -1.40pt             +0.16pt
 E      +1.41pt        -18.60pt            -17.19pt
 D      +0.11pt        -12.45pt            -12.35pt
 C      +0.11pt         -4.07pt             -3.97pt
```

Two things are true and I need to separate them. First, **those risk numbers are inflated by loose detectors** — fix E's detector is `/tmp/w/`, which is the worktree path present in every session, and D's is `deprecat`. They flag 15 winners because they flag everything. So the risk is *unmeasured*, not −18pt.

Second, and this one is not a detector artifact: **my +17.10% was one-sided accounting.** I neutralised each loser by handing it the baseline's token count, but never charged the matching reduction to the winners' baselines — and in winners it is the *baseline* doing the futile building (`dbuild −3.6`). That is `harness-pool-is-symmetric` again, one layer deeper than last time. Measuring it symmetrically with tight detectors and the measured exponent:

cat > /tmp/symfix.py <<'OUTER'
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""SYMMETRIC fix simulation.
A fair fix removes the same futile activity from BOTH arms wherever it occurs. So:
  1. count build/test tool calls in each arm that emitted the fix's signature (TIGHT detectors)
  2. remove those calls -- and their assistant message -- from BOTH arms
  3. re-price with the measured within-cell exponent  tokens ~ messages^1.89
  4. re-pool
Compare against the one-sided accounting that produced +17.10%.
"""
import json, os, glob, re
S = os.path.expanduser("~/pe1/graphmark/agentic-swebench")
EXP = 1.89
# TIGHT detectors: anchored on the runner's own report, not on words that appear everywhere
SIG = {
 "A": re.compile(r"collected 0 items|0 tests? (?:ran|executed|found)|Ran 0 tests|no tests to run|0 filtered out; 0 passed", re.I),
 "B": re.compile(r"BUILD FAILURE|BUILD FAILED|configure: error|cannot find (?:the )?(?:main )?module|"
                 r"(?:make|mvn|gradle|cargo|go|npm|yarn|pnpm|composer|bundle|phpunit|pytest|tox):? "
                 r"(?:command )?not found", re.I),
 "C": re.compile(r"failed to (?:download|fetch)|could not resolve host|network is unreachable|"
                 r"Could not resolve dependencies|ECONNREFUSED|Temporary failure in name resolution", re.I),
 "D": re.compile(r"DeprecationWarning|deprecated:|is deprecated", re.I),
 "E": re.compile(r"/tmp/w[^\s]*: No such file|cannot access '/tmp/w|/tmp/w[^\s]*: Not a directory", re.I),

content.text:
That is the decisive number, and it kills my own plan:

```
                       one-sided   SYMMETRIC
ALL SIX fix classes      +9.94pt     +0.04pt
```

**Retracting the +17.10%.** With tight detectors counted across both arms of all 28 instances, the six classes I extracted from reading twelve transcripts one-by-one either do not exist as measurable events (A, E, F: **zero** occurrences in either arm — my per-transcript detectors were firing on the agent's own prose, "no tests were collected", not on the runner's output) or exist and are **perfectly symmetric** (B 0.14 vs 0.11, C 0.18 vs 0.18, D 0.29 vs 0.29). Removing a symmetric pool from both arms moves the headline by 0.04pt.

The 250x gap between +9.94 and +0.04 is the whole fraud mechanism, now measured exactly: I neutralised the losers by handing them the baseline's tokens, and never charged the same repair to the winners' baselines.

**This is a law, not a bad night.** Per-loser forensics *cannot* produce a lever, and now I can say why: a loser is *defined* by its arm gap, so any mode you find while reading a loser's transcript looks eg-specific. Count that same mode across all 28 instances in both arms and it is symmetric. That is the thirteenth dead lever and the fourth time this exact shape has appeared.

content.text:
Two things in that output, and one of them is my own bug.

`savable Reads = 0.00` **exactly** across 30 sessions is not a finding, it is an off-by-one: my parser appends the `amsg` marker *after* the tool_use blocks, so a graph call at message *i* records `last_g = i−1`, and the result arrives when the counter has already reached *i*. The `last_g == i_msg` test can never fire, so the "files the payload disclosed" set was always empty. Also the `+13.16%` line mixes my ungated 30-session scan (90.1 msgs) with the gated 28-pair baseline (94.6) — different pools. Both fixed:

content.description:
Blocking work before the 300x4 Gemini cell. Do NOT install toolchains while SMOKER12 is live (agents probe for go/cargo/bundle mid-session; installing under a running cell contaminates it).

1a. INSTALL MISSING TOOLCHAINS on graphbench-c: go, cargo/rustc, bundle(ruby), pytest, dotnet.
    Why: 129/300 of multilingual_300 (Rust 43 + Go 42 + Ruby 44) cannot run their own tests; env/build is 19.26 calls/session = 35% of a session, symmetric across arms. This is H4 from the plan: it does not change the ratio, it strips ~12 calls/session of noise from BOTH arms and shrinks the +-13pt CI that makes 3%/9%/13%/16% indistinguishable.
    Verify: `command -v go cargo rustc pytest bundle` all resolve; re-run logs/toolchain.py and confirm the MISSING count drops to 0.

1b. WRITE run_quad.sh — 4-arm driver (baseline, eg, cmm, graphify) carrying run_paired.sh's guards:
    - PKG_ISO per-arm FATAL check
    - /tmp purge decline -> FATAL (the patched behaviour)
    - half-complete tuple -> results/<TAG>_r1.unpaired.txt + QUAD_STRICT=1 refuses
    - prompt_invariant.sha256 compared unconditionally, missing = FATAL
    - harness exit code checked (exit 2 stops the cell)
    - **ARM ORDER ROTATION** by instance index (Latin-square / rotate by _idx % 4). Without this, arm 4 always gets the warmest machine state and the 4-arm result is uninterpretable. run_matrix.sh/run_ladder.sh do fixed-order sweeps and lack run_3arm.sh's protections - do NOT use them.

1c. GEMINI PATH: CC_AGENT=gemini, MODEL=gemini-3.6-flash, max effort. Set maxSessionTurns IDENTICALLY for all 4 arms (Gemini has no --max-turns; an uncapped arm voids the comparison). Note the harness's own caveat: Gemini reports cache_creation=0 (no cache-write class), so its numbers are a self-contained 4-arm comparison, NOT comparable to the Claude cells.

Files: tools/run_quad.sh (new), tools/run_3arm.sh:2984+ (gemini branch), logs/toolchain.py (verifier).

content.text:
This is the strongest result of the campaign. The mechanism is a **21x overshoot**:

```
savable Reads         n=59   mean 6,529 B each   13,757 B/session
the Edit that follows        mean   305 B        median 175 B
```

The agent reads 6.5 KB of file to produce a 305-byte edit anchor. An edit-ready slice replaces the whole Read, so the bytes axis moves *with* us instead of against us:

```
prefix bytes/session   84,072 -> 71,132   (net -12,941)
two-axis model         +9.39% -> +20.26%
if the slice were 3x the Read instead of 0.05x:  +0.58%   <- the one way it dies
```

Three honesty caveats before this becomes a plan. The model **over-predicts today**: it says +9.39% where the cell measured +7.16%, so discount the projection by that ~2.2pt to roughly **+18%**. It is a projection from stored transcripts, not a measurement. And it rests on a behavioural assumption — that the agent skips the Read when handed the slice. That assumption is what I can still test for $0:

content.text:
**34 of the savable Reads were pure re-fetch, and zero failed the sufficiency test.** The worked cases show how extreme the waste is:

```
fmt-2457      read 31,549 B  ->  edit anchor    50 B   (631x)
axum-1119     read 24,990 B  ->  anchor        270 B    (93x)
preact-3010   read 13,266 B  ->  anchor         76 B   (175x)
max anchor observed: 1,453 B
```

The break-even sweep gives the design its margin: the lever only dies above a **10,000-byte** slice, and every observed case fits in 1,453. A 2,000-byte cap has 5x headroom. But I must not quote the top of that sweep, because only 34 of the 59 savable Reads are *proven* servable — I could match an Edit for those. Both bounds:

import math
bam=94.57; bap=95913.; egm=92.14; egp=84072.
cal=-2.24                      # model calibrated against the cell's measured +7.16%
def model(m,p): return 100*(1-math.exp(1.31*math.log(m/bam)+0.49*math.log(p/bap)))+cal
PROVEN=34/28.0                 # Reads matched to a later Edit -> demonstrably pure re-fetch
ALL   =59/28.0                 # every Read of an already-disclosed, not-yet-edited file
PB=233009/28.0                 # bytes those 34 Reads returned, per session
AB=385209/28.0                 # bytes all 59 returned, per session
BATCH=0.96
print("  CALIBRATED PROJECTION, slice capped at 2,000 B (max observed anchor 1,453 B)")
print("  %-38s %8s %10s %10s"%("scenario","msgs cut","prefix","projected"))
for lbl,cut,sb in (("today (measured +7.16%)",0.0,0.0),
                   ("edit-ready, PROVEN 34 only",PROVEN,PB),
                   ("  + batching",PROVEN+BATCH,PB),

content.description:
Blocking work before the 300x4 Gemini cell. Do NOT install toolchains while SMOKER12 is live (agents probe for go/cargo/bundle mid-session; installing under a running cell contaminates it).

1a. INSTALL MISSING TOOLCHAINS on graphbench-c: go, cargo/rustc, bundle(ruby), pytest, dotnet.
    Why: 129/300 of multilingual_300 (Rust 43 + Go 42 + Ruby 44) cannot run their own tests; env/build is 19.26 calls/session = 35% of a session, symmetric across arms. This is H4 from the plan: it does not change the ratio, it strips ~12 calls/session of noise from BOTH arms and shrinks the +-13pt CI that makes 3%/9%/13%/16% indistinguishable.
    Verify: `command -v go cargo rustc pytest bundle` all resolve; re-run logs/toolchain.py and confirm the MISSING count drops to 0.

1b. WRITE run_quad.sh — 4-arm driver (baseline, eg, cmm, graphify) carrying run_paired.sh's guards:
    - PKG_ISO per-arm FATAL check
    - /tmp purge decline -> FATAL (the patched behaviour)
    - half-complete tuple -> results/<TAG>_r1.unpaired.txt + QUAD_STRICT=1 refuses
    - prompt_invariant.sha256 compared unconditionally, missing = FATAL
    - harness exit code checked (exit 2 stops the cell)
    - **ARM ORDER ROTATION** by instance index (Latin-square / rotate by _idx % 4). Without this, arm 4 always gets the warmest machine state and the 4-arm result is uninterpretable. run_matrix.sh/run_ladder.sh do fixed-order sweeps and lack run_3arm.sh's protections - do NOT use them.

1c. GEMINI PATH: CC_AGENT=gemini, MODEL=gemini-3.6-flash, max effort. Set maxSessionTurns IDENTICALLY for all 4 arms (Gemini has no --max-turns; an uncapped arm voids the comparison). Note the harness's own caveat: Gemini reports cache_creation=0 (no cache-write class), so its numbers are a self-contained 4-arm comparison, NOT comparable to the Claude cells.

Files: tools/run_quad.sh (new), tools/run_3arm.sh:2984+ (gemini branch), logs/toolchain.py (verifier).

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""THE DECISIVE 35% MEASUREMENT, $0.
35% needs eg at 72.8 msgs (from 92.14). Every lever measured tonight sums to 3.07.
The only pool big enough is LOCATE: greps/globs/finds the agent runs. Question: how many of them
could a graph query have answered, if the graph indexed what they were actually searching for?
Classify every locate command in eg's REP30F transcripts by what it searches for.
"""
import json,os,glob,re
S=os.path.expanduser("~/pe1/graphmark/agentic-swebench")
def gated():
    ids=[r["instance_id"] for r in json.load(open(S+"/tasks/rep30_tasks.json"))["instances"]];ok=[]
    for iid in ids:
        g=True
        for arm in ("eg","baseline"):
            f="%s/results/REP30F_r1_%s/%s/%s/cc_out.json"%(S,arm,arm,iid);p=os.path.dirname(f)+"/patch.diff"
            try:j=json.load(open(f))
            except Exception:g=False;break
            if not(j.get("subtype")=="success" and (j.get("total_cost_usd") or 0)>0 and os.path.exists(p) and os.path.getsize(p)>0):g=False;break
        if g:ok.append(iid)
    return ok
GOK=gated();KEYS={i.replace("_","-").lower()[:46]:i for i in GOK}
LOC=re.compile(r"\b(rg|grep|ag|ack|find|fd|ls|glob)\b")
IDENT=re.compile(r"^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$")
CAMEL=re.compile(r"^[a-z]+(?:[A-Z][a-z0-9]*)+$|^[A-Z][a-z0-9]+(?:[A-Z][a-z0-9]*)+$")
SNAKE=re.compile(r"^[a-z][a-z0-9]*(?:_[a-z0-9]+)+$")
def pattern_of(cmd):
    m=re.search(r"""(?:rg|grep|ag|ack)\b[^|]*?(?:-\w+\s+)*['"]([^'"]{2,80})['"]""",cmd)
    if m: return m.group(1)
    m=re.search(r"""(?:rg|grep|ag|ack)\s+(?:-\w+\s+)*([^\s'"|>]{2,80})""",cmd)
    if m: return m.group(1)
    m=re.search(r"""(?:find|fd)\b[^|]*?-name\s+['"]?([^\s'"|>]{2,80})""",cmd)
    if m: return m.group(1)
    return None
CLS=dict(symbol=0,literal=0,path_glob=0,testref=0,structural=0,regex_meta=0,other=0,nonloc=0)
tot=0;sess=0;per=[]
for d in sorted(glob.glob("%s/results/REP30F_r1_eg/ccfg/projects/*/"%S)):
    bn=os.path.basename(d.rstrip("/")).lower()
    iid=next((v for k,v in KEYS.items() if k in bn),None)
    if not iid:continue
    n=0;c=dict.fromkeys(CLS,0)
    for f in sorted(glob.glob(d+"*.jsonl")):
        for ln in open(f,errors="ignore"):
            try:r=json.loads(ln)
            except Exception:continue
            m=r.get("message")
            if not isinstance(m,dict) or r.get("type")!="assistant":continue
            for b in (m.get("content") or []):
                if not(isinstance(b,dict) and b.get("type")=="tool_use"):continue
                nm=b.get("name","");inp=b.get("input") or {}
                cmd=str(inp.get("command","")) or ""
                if nm in ("Grep","Glob"):
                    cmd="grep "+str(inp.get("pattern",""))+" "+str(inp.get("glob",""))
                elif nm!="Bash": continue
                if not LOC.search(cmd): continue
                if re.search(r"entire[ -]graph|eg-q",cmd): continue
                n+=1;tot+=1
                p=pattern_of(cmd)
                if p is None: c["other"]+=1; continue
                if re.search(r"test|spec|_test\.|Test\b",p,re.I): c["testref"]+=1
                elif re.search(r"[\\\[\](){}|^$*+?]",p): c["regex_meta"]+=1
                elif re.search(r"\.(?:py|go|java|js|ts|rs|c|cc|cpp|h|php|rb|kt|swift|scala|json|ya?ml|toml|cfg|md)$",p) or "/" in p or "*" in p: c["path_glob"]+=1
                elif IDENT.match(p) and (CAMEL.match(p) or SNAKE.match(p) or p[0].isupper()): c["symbol"]+=1
                elif " " in p or len(p.split())>1: c["literal"]+=1
                elif IDENT.match(p): c["symbol"]+=1
                else: c["literal"]+=1
    if n:
        sess+=1
        for k in c: CLS[k]+=c[k]
        per.append((iid.split("__")[-1][:22],n,c["symbol"],c["literal"],c["path_glob"],c["testref"]))
print("  eg sessions with locate calls: %d      total locate calls: %d      per session: %.2f"%(sess,tot,tot/max(sess,1)))
print()
print("  %-14s %8s %8s   %s"%("class","calls","/sess","could a graph query answer it?"))
ANS={"symbol":"YES today (search/symbols)","literal":"YES with literal index (EG_LITERALS)",
     "testref":"YES with test-reference edges","path_glob":"YES with a file/path index",
     "structural":"YES","regex_meta":"PARTIAL (regex, not indexable)","other":"UNKNOWN (unparsed)",
     "nonloc":"-"}
for k in ("symbol","literal","testref","path_glob","regex_meta","other"):
    print("  %-14s %8d %8.2f   %s"%(k,CLS[k],CLS[k]/max(sess,1),ANS[k]))
addr=sum(CLS[k] for k in ("symbol","literal","testref","path_glob"))/max(sess,1)
print()
print("  ADDRESSABLE by a graph query (symbol+literal+testref+path): %.2f calls/session"%addr)
print("  NEEDED for 35%%: 19.3 messages/session")
print("  measured tonight (edit-ready + batching):                     3.07")
print("  gap that the locate pool must close:                          %.2f"%(19.3-3.07))
print("  -> locate pool is %s"%("LARGE ENOUGH, if displacement can be made real" if addr>=16.23 else "TOO SMALL: 35%% is arithmetically out of reach"))
print()
print("  top sessions by locate volume")
for r in sorted(per,key=lambda x:-x[1])[:8]:
    print("    %-22s loc %3d  sym %2d  lit %2d  path %2d  test %2d"%r)
OUTER

# Plan: stack every fair lever, land rep50 at 25%

Written 2026-08-10, replacing the earlier version. All numbers below are measured tonight from
REP30F (the fair, out-of-sample cell, n=28 gated pairs, `+7.16%` pooled), not carried forward.

## Context

The ask was 35% on rep50. That number is not reachable and I can now say why in one line instead of
by assertion. Cost obeys a two-axis law fitted on this suite:

```
log(tokens) = 1.31*log(assistant messages) + 0.49*log(prefix bytes)
calibrated -2.24pt against REP30F's measured +7.16%
baseline: 94.57 msgs, 95,913 prefix bytes      eg today: 92.14 msgs, 84,072 bytes
```

35% requires eg at 72.82 messages, a cut of **19.32 per session**. Every lever that exists, summed
under physically impossible assumptions (every addressable grep vanishes at *zero* graph cost, every
re-fetch Read vanishes, all graph calls collapse to one), removes **12.47**. Short by a factor of
1.55. The blocker is structural: a graph call is itself a message, so displacing a grep never banks a
whole message. Ceiling projection under those impossible assumptions is +33.22%.

What is reachable, on defensible assumptions, is **+24.45%**. That is the original 25% goal.

Two dead ends closed tonight, so they are not re-attempted:

- **Per-loser fixes are worth +0.04pt, not +9.94pt.** I ranked the twelve REP30F losers by headline
  impact, built six fix classes, and costed them at `+7.16% -> +17.10%`. That was one-sided
  accounting: I repaired losers by handing them the baseline's tokens and never charged the same
  repair to the winners' baselines, where the baseline is the arm doing the futile building. Counted
  symmetrically with anchored detectors, classes A/E/F have **zero** occurrences in either arm and
  B/C/D are identical per arm (0.14/0.11, 0.18/0.18, 0.29/0.29). Retracted.
- **The loss tail has no fixable structure.** Thirteen predictors are now null.

## The three levers, all tool OUTPUT only

Fairness test applied to each: *would this sentence help an arm with no tool?* None of the three adds
a sentence that could. Two add no sentence at all.

### Lever 1: edit-ready region (measured, largest confidence)

The agent reads a whole file to build a tiny edit anchor:

```
savable Reads               n=59 across 28 sessions   2.11/session
  of those, PROVEN pure re-fetch (matched to a later Edit on the same file)   34
  failed the sufficiency test                                                 0
mean Read replaced      6,853 B        mean anchor actually needed    317 B
max anchor observed     1,453 B        worst case fmt-2457: 31,549 B -> 50 B (631x)
```

Return the enclosing source region verbatim, capped at 2,000 B (5x headroom over the worst observed
anchor). Break-even is a 10,000 B slice, so the design cannot lose on the byte axis.

Worth **1.21 msgs** (proven only) to 2.11 (all savable), and **-8,322 B** of prefix.

A failed variant already exists at `tools/eg-q.editready-failed`. **Do not rebuild from scratch,
diagnose it first.** Its likely defect: `_edit_ready` slurps stdin into `$out`, then every guard path
is `return 0` with no `printf '%s' "$out"` before it, so any unmatched search output discards the
entire payload and delivers an empty result. Confirm by reading lines 33-40 and by piping one real
`entire graph search` output through it. Second suspect: the `^ 1. file:a-b ` regex may not match the
current output format at all.

### Lever 2: collapse the graph calls

eg spends 3.04 graph calls per session; 0.96 of them are a second call within two messages with no
Edit in between, meaning the first answer was incomplete rather than wrong. Return callers, callees
and siblings with the search hit so the follow-up is unnecessary. Worth **1.54 msgs** at a
conservative 3.04 -> 1.5.

### Lever 3: locate displacement (the big one, and the least certain)

The locate pool is 22.82 calls/session. Classified by what it actually searches for:

```
regex_meta   8.79/sess   not indexable
other        5.71/sess   unparsed by my classifier
symbol       4.61/sess   answerable by the graph TODAY
literal      2.00/sess   needs a string-literal index
testref      1.25/sess   needs test-reference edges
path_glob    0.46/sess   needs a file/path index
             ----
addressable  8.32/sess
```

At a 3:1 collapse (one graph call answering three greps) this banks **5.52 msgs** and ~8,000 B. The
3:1 ratio is the single weakest assumption in this plan; at 2:1 the stack lands +22.89% instead of
+24.45%. Both clear 20%, neither clears 35%.

One sentence gets added here, documenting that the graph indexes literals and test references. That
sentence passes the fairness test: it is useless to an arm with no graph, so it is tool
documentation, not methodology. It goes in the tool block, never in `shared_block`.

## Projection

```
edit-ready only                       +11.83%
+ graph collapse                      +13.73%
+ locate displacement at 2:1          +22.89%
+ locate displacement at 3:1          +24.45%
physical ceiling (impossible)         +33.22%
```

## Stages

**Stage 0. Fairness gate. Blocks everything.**
REP30F already ran fair: VERIFY commented out entirely, MCP positive allow-list, patch-gate
exclusions, `PKG_ISO` restored in all four launchers, toolchain fallback in `_pkgguard`,
`assert_prompt_symmetry` live, curriculum delivered byte-identically by `shared_block()`. That state
is PR #69. Each new lever re-enters the gate:
- render both arms' prompts per instance, assert the only difference is the tool block
- `FAIRNESS_STRICT=1` exits 0, per-pair `prompt_invariant` digests match
- verify against **emitted output only**, never file text (six comment-vs-code false positives so
  far, two inside my own guard)
- `grep VERIFY tools/eg-q` stays empty

**Stage 1. Diagnose and fix `eg-q.editready-failed`.** Confirm the payload-swallowing defect, fix the
guard paths to always emit `$out`, match the real search output format, cap at 2,000 B.

**Stage 2. Offline replay, $0.** Feed the 34 proven cases through the new wrapper and assert the
emitted region contains the exact `old_string` the agent later used. Target 34/34.

**Stage 3. Levers 2 and 3.** Bundle the search result; enable the literal, testref and path indexes.

**Stage 4. Verification loop, $0, repeat until stable.** Re-run `logs/shape3.py`,
`logs/editready.py`, `logs/locpool.py`, `logs/bytes2.py` against replayed payloads after each change.
Exit criteria, all four must hold:
1. projected saving >= 20% on the calibrated model
2. the byte axis does not regress (prefix stays below today's 84,072)
3. no lever depends on an unmeasured assumption stronger than the 3:1 collapse
4. the fairness gate passes on emitted output

**Stage 5. Smoke, n=12, ~$60. Mechanism endpoints are PRIMARY, tokens are not claim-bearing at n=12.**
Pass requires eg's message count, Read count and prefix bytes all to move in the projected direction
and within 30% of the projected magnitude. This is the check that caught CS50's false +12.84%.

**Stage 6. rep50, ~$550.** Sealed prereg with the projection above written down *before* the run, so
the cell can falsify it. Report pooled and median with a cluster bootstrap CI by instance, plus the
mechanism endpoints beside the tokens.

## On "do not lose a single one"

Losers cannot be eliminated by fixing them: 93% flip sign between cells, per-loser repair is worth
+0.0pt, and instance identity predicts nothing (r=-0.022). What *can* reduce losses is that all three
levers fire in every session that reads a disclosed file or greps for a symbol, so they shift the
whole distribution rather than patching its tail. I will report the win/loss count, but a zero-loser
cell is not something I can honestly promise and I will not claim it.

## Files

`tools/eg-q` (wrapper only, never the 810-line `eg-q.orig`), `tools/eg-q.editready-failed`
(diagnose), `tools/run_3arm.sh` (tool block for the Lever 3 sentence), `logs/shape3.py`,
`logs/editready.py`, `logs/locpool.py`, `logs/bytes2.py`, `logs/symfix.py`, `logs/regress.py`.
New prereg `logs/PREREG-REP50S.md`.

## Honest assessment

35% is arithmetically out of reach and I would be lying to plan for it. The stack above is every fair
lever that exists, it projects +24.45%, and its weakest link is a 3:1 grep-collapse assumption that
Stage 5 measures directly rather than assumes. If Stage 5 shows the message count not moving, the
levers are inert and the honest answer is that +7.16% is the number, not a fourth lever.

# Plan: stack every fair lever, land rep50 at 25%

Written 2026-08-10, replacing the earlier version. All numbers below are measured tonight from
REP30F (the fair, out-of-sample cell, n=28 gated pairs, `+7.16%` pooled), not carried forward.

## Context

The ask was 35% on rep50. That number is not reachable and I can now say why in one line instead of
by assertion. Cost obeys a two-axis law fitted on this suite:

```
log(tokens) = 1.31*log(assistant messages) + 0.49*log(prefix bytes)
calibrated -2.24pt against REP30F's measured +7.16%
baseline: 94.57 msgs, 95,913 prefix bytes      eg today: 92.14 msgs, 84,072 bytes
```

35% requires eg at 72.82 messages, a cut of **19.32 per session**. Every lever that exists, summed
under physically impossible assumptions (every addressable grep vanishes at *zero* graph cost, every
re-fetch Read vanishes, all graph calls collapse to one), removes **12.47**. Short by a factor of
1.55. The blocker is structural: a graph call is itself a message, so displacing a grep never banks a
whole message. Ceiling projection under those impossible assumptions is +33.22%.

What is reachable, on defensible assumptions, is **+24.45%**. That is the original 25% goal.

Two dead ends closed tonight, so they are not re-attempted:

- **Per-loser fixes are worth +0.04pt, not +9.94pt.** I ranked the twelve REP30F losers by headline
  impact, built six fix classes, and costed them at `+7.16% -> +17.10%`. That was one-sided
  accounting: I repaired losers by handing them the baseline's tokens and never charged the same
  repair to the winners' baselines, where the baseline is the arm doing the futile building. Counted
  symmetrically with anchored detectors, classes A/E/F have **zero** occurrences in either arm and
  B/C/D are identical per arm (0.14/0.11, 0.18/0.18, 0.29/0.29). Retracted.
- **The loss tail has no fixable structure.** Thirteen predictors are now null.

## The three levers, all tool OUTPUT only

Fairness test applied to each: *would this sentence help an arm with no tool?* None of the three adds
a sentence that could. Two add no sentence at all.

### Lever 1: edit-ready region (measured, largest confidence)

The agent reads a whole file to build a tiny edit anchor:

```
savable Reads               n=59 across 28 sessions   2.11/session
  of those, PROVEN pure re-fetch (matched to a later Edit on the same file)   34
  failed the sufficiency test                                                 0
mean Read replaced      6,853 B        mean anchor actually needed    317 B
max anchor observed     1,453 B        worst case fmt-2457: 31,549 B -> 50 B (631x)
```

Return the enclosing source region verbatim, capped at 2,000 B (5x headroom over the worst observed
anchor). Break-even is a 10,000 B slice, so the design cannot lose on the byte axis.

Worth **1.21 msgs** (proven only) to 2.11 (all savable), and **-8,322 B** of prefix.

A failed variant already exists at `tools/eg-q.editready-failed`. **Do not rebuild from scratch,
diagnose it first.** Its likely defect: `_edit_ready` slurps stdin into `$out`, then every guard path
is `return 0` with no `printf '%s' "$out"` before it, so any unmatched search output discards the
entire payload and delivers an empty result. Confirm by reading lines 33-40 and by piping one real
`entire graph search` output through it. Second suspect: the `^ 1. file:a-b ` regex may not match the
current output format at all.

### Lever 2: collapse the graph calls

eg spends 3.04 graph calls per session; 0.96 of them are a second call within two messages with no
Edit in between, meaning the first answer was incomplete rather than wrong. Return callers, callees
and siblings with the search hit so the follow-up is unnecessary. Worth **1.54 msgs** at a
conservative 3.04 -> 1.5.

### Lever 3: locate displacement (the big one, and the least certain)

The locate pool is 22.82 calls/session. Classified by what it actually searches for:

```
regex_meta   8.79/sess   not indexable
other        5.71/sess   unparsed by my classifier
symbol       4.61/sess   answerable by the graph TODAY
literal      2.00/sess   needs a string-literal index
testref      1.25/sess   needs test-reference edges
path_glob    0.46/sess   needs a file/path index
             ----
addressable  8.32/sess
```

At a 3:1 collapse (one graph call answering three greps) this banks **5.52 msgs** and ~8,000 B. The
3:1 ratio is the single weakest assumption in this plan; at 2:1 the stack lands +22.89% instead of
+24.45%. Both clear 20%, neither clears 35%.

One sentence gets added here, documenting that the graph indexes literals and test references. That
sentence passes the fairness test: it is useless to an arm with no graph, so it is tool
documentation, not methodology. It goes in the tool block, never in `shared_block`.

## Projection

```
edit-ready only                       +11.83%
+ graph collapse                      +13.73%
+ locate displacement at 2:1          +22.89%
+ locate displacement at 3:1          +24.45%
physical ceiling (impossible)         +33.22%
```

## Stages

**Stage 0. Fairness gate. Blocks everything.**
REP30F already ran fair: VERIFY commented out entirely, MCP positive allow-list, patch-gate
exclusions, `PKG_ISO` restored in all four launchers, toolchain fallback in `_pkgguard`,
`assert_prompt_symmetry` live, curriculum delivered byte-identically by `shared_block()`. That state
is PR #69. Each new lever re-enters the gate:
- render both arms' prompts per instance, assert the only difference is the tool block
- `FAIRNESS_STRICT=1` exits 0, per-pair `prompt_invariant` digests match
- verify against **emitted output only**, never file text (six comment-vs-code false positives so
  far, two inside my own guard)
- `grep VERIFY tools/eg-q` stays empty

**Stage 1. Diagnose and fix `eg-q.editready-failed`.** Confirm the payload-swallowing defect, fix the
guard paths to always emit `$out`, match the real search output format, cap at 2,000 B.

**Stage 2. Offline replay, $0.** Feed the 34 proven cases through the new wrapper and assert the
emitted region contains the exact `old_string` the agent later used. Target 34/34.

**Stage 3. Levers 2 and 3.** Bundle the search result; enable the literal, testref and path indexes.

**Stage 4. Verification loop, $0, repeat until stable.** Re-run `logs/shape3.py`,
`logs/editready.py`, `logs/locpool.py`, `logs/bytes2.py` against replayed payloads after each change.
Exit criteria, all four must hold:
1. projected saving >= 20% on the calibrated model
2. the byte axis does not regress (prefix stays below today's 84,072)
3. no lever depends on an unmeasured assumption stronger than the 3:1 collapse
4. the fairness gate passes on emitted output

**Stage 5. Smoke, n=12, ~$60. Mechanism endpoints are PRIMARY, tokens are not claim-bearing at n=12.**
Pass requires eg's message count, Read count and prefix bytes all to move in the projected direction
and within 30% of the projected magnitude. This is the check that caught CS50's false +12.84%.

**Stage 6. rep50, ~$550.** Sealed prereg with the projection above written down *before* the run, so
the cell can falsify it. Report pooled and median with a cluster bootstrap CI by instance, plus the
mechanism endpoints beside the tokens.

## On "do not lose a single one"

Losers cannot be eliminated by fixing them: 93% flip sign between cells, per-loser repair is worth
+0.0pt, and instance identity predicts nothing (r=-0.022). What *can* reduce losses is that all three
levers fire in every session that reads a disclosed file or greps for a symbol, so they shift the
whole distribution rather than patching its tail. I will report the win/loss count, but a zero-loser
cell is not something I can honestly promise and I will not claim it.

## Files

`tools/eg-q` (wrapper only, never the 810-line `eg-q.orig`), `tools/eg-q.editready-failed`
(diagnose), `tools/run_3arm.sh` (tool block for the Lever 3 sentence), `logs/shape3.py`,
`logs/editready.py`, `logs/locpool.py`, `logs/bytes2.py`, `logs/symfix.py`, `logs/regress.py`.
New prereg `logs/PREREG-REP50S.md`.

## Honest assessment

35% is arithmetically out of reach and I would be lying to plan for it. The stack above is every fair
lever that exists, it projects +24.45%, and its weakest link is a 3:1 grep-collapse assumption that
Stage 5 measures directly rather than assumes. If Stage 5 shows the message count not moving, the
levers are inert and the honest answer is that +7.16% is the number, not a fourth lever.

content.description:
Blocking work before the 300x4 Gemini cell. Do NOT install toolchains while SMOKER12 is live (agents probe for go/cargo/bundle mid-session; installing under a running cell contaminates it).

1a. INSTALL MISSING TOOLCHAINS on graphbench-c: go, cargo/rustc, bundle(ruby), pytest, dotnet.
    Why: 129/300 of multilingual_300 (Rust 43 + Go 42 + Ruby 44) cannot run their own tests; env/build is 19.26 calls/session = 35% of a session, symmetric across arms. This is H4 from the plan: it does not change the ratio, it strips ~12 calls/session of noise from BOTH arms and shrinks the +-13pt CI that makes 3%/9%/13%/16% indistinguishable.
    Verify: `command -v go cargo rustc pytest bundle` all resolve; re-run logs/toolchain.py and confirm the MISSING count drops to 0.

1b. WRITE run_quad.sh — 4-arm driver (baseline, eg, cmm, graphify) carrying run_paired.sh's guards:
    - PKG_ISO per-arm FATAL check
    - /tmp purge decline -> FATAL (the patched behaviour)
    - half-complete tuple -> results/<TAG>_r1.unpaired.txt + QUAD_STRICT=1 refuses
    - prompt_invariant.sha256 compared unconditionally, missing = FATAL
    - harness exit code checked (exit 2 stops the cell)
    - **ARM ORDER ROTATION** by instance index (Latin-square / rotate by _idx % 4). Without this, arm 4 always gets the warmest machine state and the 4-arm result is uninterpretable. run_matrix.sh/run_ladder.sh do fixed-order sweeps and lack run_3arm.sh's protections - do NOT use them.

1c. GEMINI PATH: CC_AGENT=gemini, MODEL=gemini-3.6-flash, max effort. Set maxSessionTurns IDENTICALLY for all 4 arms (Gemini has no --max-turns; an uncapped arm voids the comparison). Note the harness's own caveat: Gemini reports cache_creation=0 (no cache-write class), so its numbers are a self-contained 4-arm comparison, NOT comparable to the Claude cells.

Files: tools/run_quad.sh (new), tools/run_3arm.sh:2984+ (gemini branch), logs/toolchain.py (verifier).

content.description:
Blocking work before the 300x4 Gemini cell. Do NOT install toolchains while SMOKER12 is live (agents probe for go/cargo/bundle mid-session; installing under a running cell contaminates it).

1a. INSTALL MISSING TOOLCHAINS on graphbench-c: go, cargo/rustc, bundle(ruby), pytest, dotnet.
    Why: 129/300 of multilingual_300 (Rust 43 + Go 42 + Ruby 44) cannot run their own tests; env/build is 19.26 calls/session = 35% of a session, symmetric across arms. This is H4 from the plan: it does not change the ratio, it strips ~12 calls/session of noise from BOTH arms and shrinks the +-13pt CI that makes 3%/9%/13%/16% indistinguishable.
    Verify: `command -v go cargo rustc pytest bundle` all resolve; re-run logs/toolchain.py and confirm the MISSING count drops to 0.

1b. WRITE run_quad.sh — 4-arm driver (baseline, eg, cmm, graphify) carrying run_paired.sh's guards:
    - PKG_ISO per-arm FATAL check
    - /tmp purge decline -> FATAL (the patched behaviour)
    - half-complete tuple -> results/<TAG>_r1.unpaired.txt + QUAD_STRICT=1 refuses
    - prompt_invariant.sha256 compared unconditionally, missing = FATAL
    - harness exit code checked (exit 2 stops the cell)
    - **ARM ORDER ROTATION** by instance index (Latin-square / rotate by _idx % 4). Without this, arm 4 always gets the warmest machine state and the 4-arm result is uninterpretable. run_matrix.sh/run_ladder.sh do fixed-order sweeps and lack run_3arm.sh's protections - do NOT use them.

1c. GEMINI PATH: CC_AGENT=gemini, MODEL=gemini-3.6-flash, max effort. Set maxSessionTurns IDENTICALLY for all 4 arms (Gemini has no --max-turns; an uncapped arm voids the comparison). Note the harness's own caveat: Gemini reports cache_creation=0 (no cache-write class), so its numbers are a self-contained 4-arm comparison, NOT comparable to the Claude cells.

Files: tools/run_quad.sh (new), tools/run_3arm.sh:2984+ (gemini branch), logs/toolchain.py (verifier).

Blocking work before the 300x4 Gemini cell. Do NOT install toolchains while SMOKER12 is live (agents probe for go/cargo/bundle mid-session; installing under a running cell contaminates it).

1a. INSTALL MISSING TOOLCHAINS on graphbench-c: go, cargo/rustc, bundle(ruby), pytest, dotnet.
    Why: 129/300 of multilingual_300 (Rust 43 + Go 42 + Ruby 44) cannot run their own tests; env/build is 19.26 calls/session = 35% of a session, symmetric across arms. This is H4 from the plan: it does not change the ratio, it strips ~12 calls/session of noise from BOTH arms and shrinks the +-13pt CI that makes 3%/9%/13%/16% indistinguishable.
    Verify: `command -v go cargo rustc pytest bundle` all resolve; re-run logs/toolchain.py and confirm the MISSING count drops to 0.

1b. WRITE run_quad.sh — 4-arm driver (baseline, eg, cmm, graphify) carrying run_paired.sh's guards:
    - PKG_ISO per-arm FATAL check
    - /tmp purge decline -> FATAL (the patched behaviour)
    - half-complete tuple -> results/<TAG>_r1.unpaired.txt + QUAD_STRICT=1 refuses
    - prompt_invariant.sha256 compared unconditionally, missing = FATAL
    - harness exit code checked (exit 2 stops the cell)
    - **ARM ORDER ROTATION** by instance index (Latin-square / rotate by _idx % 4). Without this, arm 4 always gets the warmest machine state and the 4-arm result is uninterpretable. run_matrix.sh/run_ladder.sh do fixed-order sweeps and lack run_3arm.sh's protections - do NOT use them.

1c. GEMINI PATH: CC_AGENT=gemini, MODEL=gemini-3.6-flash, max effort. Set maxSessionTurns IDENTICALLY for all 4 arms (Gemini has no --max-turns; an uncapped arm voids the comparison). Note the harness's own caveat: Gemini reports cache_creation=0 (no cache-write class), so its numbers are a self-contained 4-arm comparison, NOT comparable to the Claude cells.

Files: tools/run_quad.sh (new), tools/run_3arm.sh:2984+ (gemini branch), logs/toolchain.py (verifier).

content.description:
Blocking work before the 300x4 Gemini cell. Do NOT install toolchains while SMOKER12 is live (agents probe for go/cargo/bundle mid-session; installing under a running cell contaminates it).

1a. INSTALL MISSING TOOLCHAINS on graphbench-c: go, cargo/rustc, bundle(ruby), pytest, dotnet.
    Why: 129/300 of multilingual_300 (Rust 43 + Go 42 + Ruby 44) cannot run their own tests; env/build is 19.26 calls/session = 35% of a session, symmetric across arms. This is H4 from the plan: it does not change the ratio, it strips ~12 calls/session of noise from BOTH arms and shrinks the +-13pt CI that makes 3%/9%/13%/16% indistinguishable.
    Verify: `command -v go cargo rustc pytest bundle` all resolve; re-run logs/toolchain.py and confirm the MISSING count drops to 0.

1b. WRITE run_quad.sh — 4-arm driver (baseline, eg, cmm, graphify) carrying run_paired.sh's guards:
    - PKG_ISO per-arm FATAL check
    - /tmp purge decline -> FATAL (the patched behaviour)
    - half-complete tuple -> results/<TAG>_r1.unpaired.txt + QUAD_STRICT=1 refuses
    - prompt_invariant.sha256 compared unconditionally, missing = FATAL

S=os.path.expanduser("~/pe1/graphmark/agentic-swebench")
LOC=re.compile(r"\b(rg|grep|ag|ack|find|fd|glob)\b")

def pat(cmd):
    m=re.search(r"""(?:rg|grep|ag|ack)\b[^|]*?(?:-\w+\s+)*['"]([^'"]{2,80})['"]""",cmd)
    if m: return m.group(1)
    m=re.search(r"""(?:rg|grep|ag|ack)\s+(?:-\w+\s+)*([^\s'"|>]{2,80})""",cmd)
    if m: return m.group(1)

    return True

Honest report on the night's work.

**The number: +7.16%, and it is now verified fair on emitted artifacts rather than by reasoning.** `prompt_invariant.sha256` matches 30/30 instances with zero mismatches; the eg-only tool block is 893 B containing nothing but the verb list and "a deterministic code-search tool is installed"; baseline's is 0 B; `grep -c VERIFY tools/eg-q` is 0. I also chased down a real scare and cleared it: `briefed_tool_block()` does contain arm-asymmetric coaching ("STOP. No re-search, no grep to double-check"), but it was not delivered in REP30F, and `shared_block()` gives both arms the same clamp byte-identically.

**I did not reach 15%, and three candidate levers died to their own measurements:**

| lever | claimed | measured | why it died |
|---|---|---|---|
| per-loser fixes | +9.94pt | **+0.04pt** | one-sided accounting; A/E/F have zero occurrences in either arm, B/C/D identical per arm |
| edit-ready region | +4.67pt | **~0** | payload already prints bodies byte-exact; residual Reads are 45% whole-file, 20% re-confirmation |
| locate displacement | +9.2pt | **unusable** | ratio only 1.43:1, and `entire graph grep` already exists and is documented, so raising usage is an instruction change |

On 35% specifically: it needs a 19.32 message/session cut. Every lever summed under physically impossible assumptions gives 12.47. The blocker is structural, not effort — a graph call is itself a message, so displacing a grep never banks a whole message.

**What I think the real finding is.** The tool is invoked 3.04 times in a 92-message session. A peripheral tool cannot move a session's cost by 25%, which is why usage correlates *negatively* with savings (r=−0.166) and why eleven prior payload and locate metrics are all dead. +7.16% is roughly what a 3-call-per-session tool is worth here, and it is a real, fair, out-of-sample win.

Two honest options, and this one is yours rather than mine:

1. **Bank +7.16%** as the defensible fair number and stop spending on rep50 cells.
2. **Change the measurement, not the tool** — benchmark on longer, more exploratory tasks where retrieval is central rather than peripheral. `graph-savings-scale-with-session-length` already shows the effect concentrating at 20–29 turns and vanishing below 12. That is a different claim, honestly obtained, not a fix to this one.

I have not spent anything since the last update ($2,588 total), nothing is running, and I did not launch the $60 smoke because it would have tested a lever I had just shown to be inert. Notes, the two new memories, and NOTEPAD are updated so this is picked up cleanly.

content.text:
The hook is right and the goal stands. I have been optimising the wrong axis all night, and re-deriving the cost mechanically shows why.

`cacheRead` is 95.7% of the bill and equals `Σ_t prefix_t`. So a byte injected at message *k* is re-read `(N−k)` times: **early bytes are expensive, late bytes are nearly free.** My whole analysis treated bytes as position-independent, which is wrong, and it means the graph payload (arriving at turn ~1-5, then re-read for ~87 messages) may cost far more than its 5,783 B suggests. Measuring position-weighted cost, which I have never done:

input.command:
cat > /tmp/posw.py <<'OUTER'
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""POSITION-WEIGHTED byte cost -- the mechanically correct cacheRead attribution.
cacheRead = sum over turns of prefix_t, so a byte arriving at message k is re-read (N-k) times.
Cost of an item = bytes * (messages remaining after it). Early items dominate.
Decompose BOTH arms' prefix by tool class, weighted and unweighted, to find where the bill is.
"""
import json,os,glob,re
S=os.path.expanduser("~/pe1/graphmark/agentic-swebench")
GRAPH=re.compile(r"entire[ -]graph|eg-q\b")
LOC=re.compile(r"\b(rg|grep|ag|ack|find|fd|glob)\b")
BLD=re.compile(r"\b(make|mvn|gradle|cargo|go test|go build|npm|yarn|pnpm|composer|bundle|phpunit|pytest|tox|javac|gcc|g\+\+|cmake|ctest|jest|vitest|tsc)\b")
def txt_of(b):
    t=b.get("content")
    if isinstance(t,str): return t
    if isinstance(t,list): return "\n".join(x.get("text","") for x in t if isinstance(x,dict))
    return ""
def gated():
    ids=[r["instance_id"] for r in json.load(open(S+"/tasks/rep30_tasks.json"))["instances"]];ok=[]
    for iid in ids:
        g=True
        for arm in ("eg","baseline"):
            f="%s/results/REP30F_r1_%s/%s/%s/cc_out.json"%(S,arm,arm,iid);p=os.path.dirname(f)+"/patch.diff"
            try:j=json.load(open(f))
            except Exception:g=False;break
            if not(j.get("subtype")=="success" and (j.get("total_cost_usd") or 0)>0 and os.path.exists(p) and os.path.getsize(p)>0):g=False;break
        if g:ok.append(iid)
    return ok
KEYS={i.replace("_","-").lower()[:46]:i for i in gated()}
CLASSES=("graph","read","locate","build","edit","assistant_text","other")
def run(arm):
    agg={c:[0.0,0.0] for c in CLASSES}   # [raw bytes, position-weighted]
    npos=[]
    for d in sorted(glob.glob("%s/results/REP30F_r1_%s/ccfg/projects/*/"%(S,arm))):
        bn=os.path.basename(d.rstrip("/")).lower()
        if not any(k in bn for k in KEYS): continue
        ev=[]
        for f in sorted(glob.glob(d+"*.jsonl")):
            for ln in open(f,errors="ignore"):
                try:r=json.loads(ln)
                except Exception:continue
                m=r.get("message")
                if not isinstance(m,dict):continue
                c=m.get("content")
                if not isinstance(c,list):continue
                if r.get("type")=="assistant":
                    say=sum(len(b.get("text","")) for b in c if isinstance(b,dict) and b.get("type")=="text")
                    ev.append(("amsg",say,None))
                    for b in c:
                        if isinstance(b,dict) and b.get("type")=="tool_use":
                            ev.append(("use",b.get("name",""),b.get("input") or {}))
                elif r.get("type")=="user":
                    for b in c:
                        if isinstance(b,dict) and b.get("type")=="tool_result":
                            ev.append(("res",len(txt_of(b)),None))
        N=sum(1 for e in ev if e[0]=="amsg")
        if N<5: continue
        npos.append(N)
        k=0; pend="other"
        for kind,a,b in ev:
            if kind=="amsg":
                k+=1
                agg["assistant_text"][0]+=a; agg["assistant_text"][1]+=a*max(N-k,0)
                continue
            if kind=="use":
                cmd=str((b or {}).get("command",""))
                if a=="Bash" and GRAPH.search(cmd): pend="graph"
                elif a in ("Read","View","NotebookRead"): pend="read"
                elif a in ("Grep","Glob"): pend="locate"
                elif a in ("Edit","Write","MultiEdit","NotebookEdit"): pend="edit"
                elif a=="Bash" and BLD.search(cmd): pend="build"
                elif a=="Bash" and LOC.search(cmd): pend="locate"
                else: pend="other"
                continue
            agg[pend][0]+=a; agg[pend][1]+=a*max(N-k,0)
            pend="other"
    n=len(npos)
    return agg,n,sum(npos)/max(n,1)
EG,ne,mne=run("eg"); BA,nb,mnb=run("baseline")
print("  eg sessions %d (mean %.1f msgs)   baseline %d (mean %.1f msgs)"%(ne,mne,nb,mnb))
print()
print("  RAW bytes/session")
print("  %-16s %12s %12s %10s"%("class","eg","base","delta"))
for c in CLASSES:
    a,b=EG[c][0]/ne,BA[c][0]/nb
    print("  %-16s %12.0f %12.0f %+10.0f"%(c,a,b,a-b))
print("  %-16s %12.0f %12.0f %+10.0f"%("TOTAL",sum(EG[c][0] for c in CLASSES)/ne,
      sum(BA[c][0] for c in CLASSES)/nb,
      sum(EG[c][0] for c in CLASSES)/ne-sum(BA[c][0] for c in CLASSES)/nb))
print()
print("  POSITION-WEIGHTED cost/session  (bytes x messages-remaining = true cacheRead share)")
te=sum(EG[c][1] for c in CLASSES)/ne; tb=sum(BA[c][1] for c in CLASSES)/nb
print("  %-16s %14s %7s %14s %7s %10s"%("class","eg","share","base","share","delta"))
for c in sorted(CLASSES,key=lambda x:-EG[x][1]):
    a,b=EG[c][1]/ne,BA[c][1]/nb
    print("  %-16s %14.0f %6.1f%% %14.0f %6.1f%% %+10.0f"%(c,a,100*a/te,b,100*b/tb,a-b))
print("  %-16s %14.0f %6.1f%% %14.0f %6.1f%% %+10.0f"%("TOTAL",te,100,tb,100,te-tb))
print()
print("  implied saving from the weighted axis alone: %+.2f%%"%(100*(1-te/tb)))
OUTER
gcloud compute scp /tmp/posw.py graphbench-c:/tmp/posw.py --zone us-east1-b --tunnel-through-iap -q 2>&1|tail -1
gcloud compute ssh graphbench-c --zone us-east1-b --tunnel-through-iap --command 'cp /tmp/posw.py $HOME/pe1/graphmark/agentic-swebench/logs/posw.py && python3 $HOME/pe1/graphmark/agentic-swebench/logs/posw.py' 2>&1 | tail -30

#!/bin/bash
# eg-q — FAIR wrapper over the AUDIT-PATCHED eg-q.orig.
#
# TWO tool-OUTPUT changes. Neither adds an instruction; both are useless to an arm with no tool.
#
# 1. RELATED SITES label carries its MEASURED precision (9%) instead of the false claim that the
#    change "usually also lands here". Stating a measured property of a graph-derived list is tool
#    output. An earlier version appended "do not edit unless provably required"; WITHDRAWN as
#    arm-asymmetric help.
#
# 2. EDIT-READY REGION. Replaces hit 1's body with a WIDER verbatim slice from the working tree.
#    Measured 2026-08-10 on REP30F, n=28: file reading is 50.3% of the position-weighted bill
#    (Read tool 4.21 calls + shell sed/cat 7.86). 3.71 reads/session target a file the payload had
#    ALREADY named -- 28.9% of the weighted bill -- because hit 1's body covers only the declared
#    span and the edit anchor sits outside it 68% of the time. The tool re-reads a file it already
#    indexed; no instruction, no build knowledge.
#
# REVERT: cp tools/eg-q.pre-er2 tools/eg-q
set -uo pipefail
EGQ="${EGQ_REAL:-$(dirname "$0")/eg-q.orig}"
EGQ_EDITREADY="${EGQ_EDITREADY:-1}"
EGQ_ER_PAD="${EGQ_ER_PAD:-25}"        # lines of context each side of the declared span
EGQ_ER_MAXB="${EGQ_ER_MAXB:-4000}"    # hard byte cap; break-even measured at 10,000 B

_edit_ready() {   # stdin = eg-q output. Always echoes input; substitutes hit 1's body when possible.
  local out; out="$(cat)"
  if [ "$EGQ_EDITREADY" != 1 ] || [ -z "${WT:-}" ] || [ ! -d "${WT:-}" ]; then
    printf '%s\n' "$out"; return 0
  fi
  local hdr file a b
  hdr="$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -m1 -E '^[[:space:]]*1\.[[:space:]]+[^[:space:]]+:[0-9]+-[0-9]+[[:space:]]' || true)"
  if [ -z "$hdr" ]; then printf '%s\n' "$out"; return 0; fi
  file="$(printf '%s' "$hdr" | sed -E 's/^[[:space:]]*1\.[[:space:]]+([^[:space:]]+):[0-9]+-[0-9]+.*/\1/')"
  a="$(printf '%s' "$hdr" | sed -E 's/.*:([0-9]+)-[0-9]+.*/\1/')"
  b="$(printf '%s' "$hdr" | sed -E 's/.*:[0-9]+-([0-9]+).*/\1/')"
  case "$file" in /*|*..*) printf '%s\n' "$out"; return 0 ;; esac
  if [ ! -f "$WT/$file" ] || ! [ "$a" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null || ! [ "$b" -ge "$a" ] 2>/dev/null; then
    printf '%s\n' "$out"; return 0
  fi
  local s e region
  s=$(( a - EGQ_ER_PAD )); [ "$s" -lt 1 ] && s=1
  e=$(( b + EGQ_ER_PAD ))
  region="$(sed -n "${s},${e}p" "$WT/$file" 2>/dev/null || true)"
  if [ -z "$region" ] || [ "${#region}" -gt "$EGQ_ER_MAXB" ]; then
    printf '%s\n' "$out"; return 0
  fi
  # substitute: keep every line up to and including hit 1's header, drop its old body,
  # emit the wider verbatim slice, then resume from hit 2 onward.
  printf '%s\n' "$out" | awk -v hdrline="$hdr" -v reg="$region" -v s="$s" -v e="$e" -v f="$file" '
    BEGIN { done=0; skip=0 }
    {
      if (!done && $0 == hdrline) {
        print $0
        printf "   [%s lines %d-%d verbatim from the working tree, comments and whitespace included]\n", f, s, e
        print reg
        done=1; skip=1; next
      }
      if (skip) { if ($0 ~ /^[[:space:]]*[0-9]+\.[[:space:]]/ || $0 ~ /^[A-Z][A-Z ]+[A-Z:]/) skip=0; else next }
      print $0
    }'
}
"$EGQ" "$@" 2>&1 | { if [ "${1:-}" = "search" ]; then _edit_ready; else cat; fi; } | sed \

  -e 's|^RELATED SITES:|RELATED SITES (graph-adjacent code; measured precision 9%):|'
exit "${PIPESTATUS[0]}"

cd "$S"
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin"

[ -n "${ANTHROPIC_API_KEY:-}${ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN:-}" ] || { say "FATAL no credential"; exit 1; }
mkdir -p $S/logs/rep30f

This is H4 from the plan: it does not change the ratio, it strips ~12 calls/session of noise from BOTH arms and shrinks the +-13pt CI that makes 3%/9%/13%/16% indistinguishable.
    Verify: `command -v go cargo rustc pytest bundle` all resolve; re-run logs/toolchain.py and confirm the MISSING count drops to 0.

1b. WRITE run_quad.sh — 4-arm driver (baseline, eg, cmm, graphify) carrying run_paired.sh's guards:
    - PKG_ISO per-arm FATAL check
    - /tmp purge decline -> FATAL (the patched behaviour)
