content.text: Contract is clear: `_lits()` is a stdin→stdout filter with the query in `EG_LIT_QUERY`. Writing it — and the key economics are that doing the grep *inside the tool* costs the agent **zero turns**, which is the entire win:

input.command:
cat > /tmp/_eglit.py <<'PYEOF'
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""_eglit.py -- LITERAL OCCURRENCES: fold the shell grep the agent would otherwise run into the
search payload.

WHY (measured 2026-08-11, 83 eg sessions across HOLD50 + FAIRREF50, logs/grepgap.py):
  1,498 shell greps were issued AFTER a payload existed.
    286 (19%) searched for something ALREADY in the payload  -- ignored information
  1,212 (81%) searched for something the payload never contained -- a COVERAGE gap
  = 14.6 displaceable greps per session.
eg-q.orig's own note: "51.2% of the identifiers the eg arm still grepped for are not symbols at all,
so neither `search` nor `def` can answer them", and "grep elimination is the single strongest
predictor of whether the tool saves money" (corr +0.615 Haiku / +0.712 Sonnet).

ECONOMICS: the grep still runs, but inside the tool, so it costs the agent ZERO turns. We move work
out of the conversation and into one payload. Bytes are cheap (cacheRead ~0.42x input); turns are not.

FAIRNESS: tool output only. No sentence here would help an arm with no tool -- it is file:line
evidence derived from the repo. No imperative, no turn budget, no verify command, no "don't grep".

I/O CONTRACT (matches _egverify.py / _eglitdrop.py): stdin = the search payload, stdout = the payload
plus one appended block. EG_LIT_QUERY carries the agent's query. Never swallow stdin: on any error or
empty result the payload is passed through unchanged.
"""
import os, re, subprocess, sys

MAXB   = int(os.environ.get("EG_LIT_MAXB", "2600"))     # hard byte cap on the appended block
PERTOK = int(os.environ.get("EG_LIT_PERTOK", "6"))      # hits shown per token
MAXTOK = int(os.environ.get("EG_LIT_MAXTOK", "4"))      # tokens searched
STOP = {
    "the","and","for","with","that","this","from","into","when","where","which","what","should",
    "would","could","have","has","not","are","was","were","will","its","it's","use","used","using",
    "add","fix","bug","issue","error","fails","failing","test","tests","case","cases","value",
    "values","return","returns","method","function","class","file","files","line","lines","code",
    "does","doesn't","only","also","after","before","instead","because","support","expected",
}

def tokens(q):
    """identifier-shaped words worth grepping: CamelCase, snake_case, dotted, or long bare names"""
    out, seen = [], set()
    for w in re.findall(r"[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_.\-]{2,}", q or ""):
        lw = w.lower()
        if lw in STOP or len(w) < 4:
            continue
        shaped = ("_" in w) or ("." in w) or re.search(r"[a-z][A-Z]", w) or len(w) >= 7
        if not shaped:
            continue
        if lw in seen:
            continue
        seen.add(lw)
        out.append(w)
    return out[:MAXTOK]

def search(tok, root):
    """bounded literal search; ripgrep if present, else grep -rn. Never raises."""
    common = ["--no-heading", "-n", "-F", "-m", str(PERTOK), "--", tok, root]
    for cmd in (["rg", "-S", "--max-filesize", "512K", "-g", "!.git"] + common,
                ["grep", "-rnI", "-m", str(PERTOK), "-F", "--", tok, root]):
        try:
            p = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=12)
            if p.returncode in (0, 1) and p.stdout:
                return p.stdout.splitlines()
            if p.returncode in (0, 1):
                return []
        except Exception:
            continue
    return []

def main():
    payload = sys.stdin.read()
    sys.stdout.write(payload)                      # ALWAYS emit the payload first
    q = os.environ.get("EG_LIT_QUERY", "")
    root = os.environ.get("WT") or os.getcwd()
    toks = tokens(q)
    if not toks or not os.path.isdir(root):
        return
    already = payload.lower()
    lines, shown = [], 0
    for tok in toks:
        hits = search(tok, root)
        if not hits:
            continue
        rows = []
        for h in hits:
            parts = h.split(":", 2)
            if len(parts) < 3:
                continue
            path = os.path.relpath(parts[0], root)
            if path.startswith(".."):
                continue
            # skip what the payload already showed -- 19% of greps were already covered
            if ("%s:%s" % (path, parts[1])) in already:
                continue
            body = parts[2].strip()
            rows.append("  %s:%s  %s" % (path, parts[1], body[:96]))
        if rows:
            lines.append("%s (%d shown)" % (tok, len(rows)))
            lines.extend(rows)
            shown += len(rows)
    if not shown:
        return
    block = ("\nLITERAL OCCURRENCES (every place these identifiers from your query are named, "
             "file:line from the same\nworking tree; no extra query needed):\n" + "\n".join(lines) + "\n")
    if len(block) > MAXB:
        block = block[:MAXB].rsplit("\n", 1)[0] + "\n  [truncated at %d bytes]\n" % MAXB
    sys.stdout.write(block)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    try:
        main()
    except Exception:
        pass                                        # never break the payload

**The −38.8% grep drop I reported was selection bias, not treatment.** Look at IMP12's baseline greps: 9.90 versus HOLD50's 24.92. An eg-only change cannot reduce *baseline* greps — so the only explanation is that the 5 finished pairs are the short, easy sessions. IMP12's eg greps are actually **19.08 vs baseline 9.90** — eg greps *more* in that subset. The drift gate caught it at −58%, which is far beyond drift; it's incompleteness.

I got excited by a partial-cell ratio, which is exactly the error my own notes warn about ("never read a running cell's partial ratio," logged after the GUIDE50 +76% turned out to be p=0.0052 selection-biased). I did it again.

Note also HOLD50 reads +18.66% on this 12-instance subset while the full 48-pair cell reads +1.28% — so these 12 are a favourable draw, and any treatment number here must be compared against **18.66%**, not against the campaign average. That makes the bar higher, not lower.

What's actually established today: `impact` is now firing (2 calls in 225 sessions → 8 in 12), `_eglit.py` exists and works where the flag was previously dead, and the grep-coverage gap is measured at 81%. content.text:
Yes — IMP12, and on properly paired data (6 instances complete in **both** cells and **both** arms, so no incompleteness bias) it's the first clean signal:

```
            eg greps   baseline greps   eg/base
HOLD50        13.83        12.50          1.11    <- eg grepped MORE than baseline
IMP12         12.33        13.17          0.94    <- eg now greps LESS
```

That flip is the finding. **eg has been grepping 11% *more* than the no-tool baseline all along** — which explains why savings sat at ~0 for the whole campaign: the tool added its own calls without displacing the agent's search work. Folding `impact` into `search` moved the ratio to 0.94, a ~15% relative improvement.

But I'll size it honestly against the author's own scale: the −46.1% tier requires removing **>75% of baseline greps**. We're at 6% below baseline. So this is directionally right and nowhere near 15% savings on its own.

LIT12 hasn't started — the chain is still waiting on IMP12's last session (23/24, 6 live). LIT12 is the one aimed squarely at the gap, since **81% of post-payload greps sought text the payload never contained** and `_eglit.py` now exists to cover exactly that. If the literal fold works, the grep ratio should drop well below 0.94; if it doesn't move, grep-elimination is refuted for this tool and I'll say so.

One correction I owe from earlier in this same thread: the "−38.8% grep drop" I reported was incompleteness bias, not treatment — IMP12's *baseline* greps had also fallen, which is impossible from an eg-only change. This paired 0.94 figure is the number to trust.

content.text:
On Go: I'd defer it. A newer toolchain changes build and runtime speed, not what the agent *does* — token savings are driven by turns and bytes, neither of which Go's version touches. And it would rebuild the pinned binary that every cell in this comparison is measured against, breaking comparability mid-campaign. Happy to do it after we have a number.

Because I just found the other half of the mechanism, and it's another dead flag:

> `EG_SIBLINGS` — appends definition pointers for in-repo identifiers that appear in the CODE the payload printed. Measured: **54% of the greps a tool-enabled session still runs are for something the payload already put in front of it** — 25% re-finding a symbol it was given, 29% digging inside a file it returned.

So the grep pool splits two ways, and each has a designed-but-unshipped fix: **51.2% non-symbol → `_eglit.py`** (written), **54% already-shown → `_egsiblings.py`** (missing). Writing the second one:

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""_egsiblings.py -- DEFINITION POINTERS: for in-repo identifiers that appear in the CODE the payload
already printed, append where each one is DEFINED (file:line) from the symbol index.

WHY (eg-q.orig's own measurement, the comment above `_siblings()`):
  "54% of the greps a tool-enabled session still runs are for something the payload already put in
   front of it -- 25% re-finding a symbol it was given, 29% digging inside a file it returned
   (carbon-3098 grepped for `make` and `fromString` right after reading bodies that call both).
   Grep elimination is the single strongest predictor of whether the tool saves money: instances
   where it removed >75% of baseline greps score -46.1%, those removing <40% score +1.9%,
   corr +0.615 Haiku / +0.712 Sonnet, while corr(BASELINE greps, outcome) ~ 0."
This flag existed and defaulted to 0 because THIS FILE DID NOT EXIST -- a dead flag, same class as
BASE_FRUGAL and EG_LITERALS. Companion: _eglit.py covers the other half (51.2% of grepped identifiers
are not symbols at all, so no symbol lookup can answer them).

ECONOMICS: resolving a definition costs the agent ZERO turns here; asking for it costs one.
FAIRNESS: tool output only -- file:line facts from the graph's own index. No imperative, no turn
budget, no verify command. A no-tool arm cannot obtain a symbol index.
I/O: stdin = payload, stdout = payload + one appended block. GSYM = graph.symbols.ndjson.
Never swallow stdin: any error or empty result passes the payload through unchanged.
"""
import json, os, re, sys

MAXB  = int(os.environ.get("EG_SIB_MAXB", "2200"))
MAXN  = int(os.environ.get("EG_SIB_MAXN", "14"))
MINLEN = 4
STOP = {
    "self","this","true","false","null","none","return","string","int","bool","error","err","nil",
    "func","class","def","var","let","const","new","void","list","dict","map","set","array","object",
    "value","values","name","names","type","types","data","result","results","item","items","args",
    "kwargs","test","tests","print","len","str","get","set_","add","key","keys","index","size",
    "length","count","start","end","line","file","path","text","node","next","prev","init","main",
}

def ident_tokens(code):
    """identifier-shaped names appearing in the printed code"""
    out, seen = [], set()
    for w in re.findall(r"[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]{%d,}" % (MINLEN - 1), code):
        lw = w.lower()
        if lw in STOP or lw in seen:
            continue
        # only names that look like real symbols: CamelCase, snake_case, or long
        if not (("_" in w) or re.search(r"[a-z][A-Z]", w) or len(w) >= 7):
            continue
        seen.add(lw)
        out.append(w)
    return out

def code_lines(payload):
    """the body lines of the payload: indented source under a ranked hit, not headers"""
    keep = []
    for ln in payload.splitlines():
        if re.match(r"^\s*\d+\.\s", ln):        # ranked-hit header
            continue
        if re.match(r"^[A-Z][A-Z &-]{3,}", ln): # block header (RELATED SITES, etc.)
            continue
        if ln.startswith((" ", "\t")) and ln.strip():
            keep.append(ln)
    return "\n".join(keep)

def load_index(path, wanted):
    """single pass over GSYM; keep only records whose name is wanted"""
    hits = {}
    try:
        with open(path, errors="ignore") as fh:
            for ln in fh:
                if '"name"' not in ln:
                    continue
                try:
                    d = json.loads(ln)
                except Exception:
                    continue
                nm = d.get("name")
                if not nm or nm not in wanted or nm in hits:
                    continue
                fp, sl = d.get("file_path"), d.get("start_line")
                if not fp or not sl:
                    continue
                hits[nm] = (fp, sl, d.get("kind") or "")
                if len(hits) >= len(wanted):
                    break
    except Exception:
        return {}
    return hits

def main():
    payload = sys.stdin.read()
    sys.stdout.write(payload)                       # ALWAYS emit the payload first
    gsym = os.environ.get("GSYM", "")
    if not gsym or not os.path.isfile(gsym):
        return
    toks = ident_tokens(code_lines(payload))
    if not toks:
        return
    already = payload
    wanted = set(toks[: MAXN * 3])
    idx = load_index(gsym, wanted)
    rows = []
    for t in toks:
        if t not in idx:
            continue
        fp, sl, kind = idx[t]
        ref = "%s:%s" % (fp, sl)
        if ref in already:                          # payload already showed this exact location
            continue
        rows.append("  %-28s %s:%s%s" % (t, fp, sl, ("  " + kind) if kind else ""))
        if len(rows) >= MAXN:
            break
    if not rows:
        return
    block = ("\nDEFINED AT (identifiers appearing in the code above, and where each is defined in this\n"
             "repository; no extra query needed):\n" + "\n".join(rows) + "\n")
    if len(block) > MAXB:
        block = block[:MAXB].rsplit("\n", 1)[0] + "\n  [truncated at %d bytes]\n" % MAXB
    sys.stdout.write(block)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    try:
        main()
    except Exception:
        pass
PYEOF

Stopping cells. Doing the predictive arithmetic first, because I can already see the two measurements conflict and that conflict decides everything.

**The bar, fitted from the author's own two data points** (40% grep removal → +1.9%; 75% → −46.1%):

```
slope = 44.2pt / 35pp = 1.26pt per point of grep removal
15% savings needs ~50% grep removal
current: eg 12.33 vs baseline 13.17 = 6.4% below baseline
```

**And the conflict I need to resolve.** My measurement said 81% of post-payload greps seek text the payload never contained — a coverage gap. The author's said **54% seek things the payload already showed** — a behavioural wall. Those imply opposite conclusions, but they're reconcilable: the author's 54% = 25% "re-finding a symbol it was given" + 29% "digging inside a file it returned." My test only checked whether the *pattern string* appeared in the payload text, so it would catch the 25% (I measured 19%) and miss the 29% entirely.

So roughly **half the grep pool is behavioural** (already surfaced, will grep anyway) and **half is coverage**. That caps what any payload change can do at ~50% removal — which is exactly the 15% bar, with zero margin.

The decisive unknown is where the *other* half's patterns come from. If they're identifiers visible in the payload's printed code, `_egsiblings.py` covers them. If they're discovered from files the agent read later, nothing in the payload can:

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""PROVENANCE of grep patterns -- decides whether the stack can reach 50% grep removal (the 15% bar).
For each shell grep after a payload, where did its pattern come from?
  in-payload-text   pattern string literally in a payload      -> already covered / behavioural
  in-payload-code   identifier appears in code a payload printed-> _egsiblings.py covers
  in-payload-file   pattern targets a FILE a payload named      -> author's 29% bucket
  from-read         appeared first in a file the agent READ     -> NOTHING in the payload can cover
  from-issue        appeared in the problem statement           -> _eglit.py covers (query tokens)
  unknown           none of the above
"""
import json,os,glob,re
from collections import Counter
S=os.path.expanduser("~/pe1/graphmark/agentic-swebench")
GRAPH=re.compile(r"entire[ -]graph|eg-q\b"); LOCSH=re.compile(r"\b(rg|grep|ag|ack)\b")
FILEPAT=re.compile(r"[\w./\-]+\.(?:py|go|java|js|jsx|ts|tsx|rs|c|cc|cpp|h|hpp|php|rb|cs|kt|swift|scala)\b")
def txt(b):
    t=b.get("content")
    if isinstance(t,str): return t
    if isinstance(t,list): return "\n".join(x.get("text","") for x in t if isinstance(x,dict))
    return ""
def pat(cmd):
    m=re.search(r"""(?:rg|grep|ag|ack)\b[^|]*?(?:-\w+\s+)*['"]([^'"]{2,60})['"]""",cmd)
    if m: return m.group(1)
    m=re.search(r"""(?:rg|grep|ag|ack)\s+(?:-\w+\s+)*([^\s'"|>]{3,60})""",cmd)
    return m.group(1) if m else None
c=Counter(); tot=0
for cell in ("HOLD50","FAIRREF50"):
    tf="holdout50.json"
    j=json.load(open(S+"/tasks/"+tf)); ins=j.get("instances") if isinstance(j,dict) else j
    keys={r["instance_id"].replace("_","-").lower()[:46]:r for r in ins}
    for d in sorted(glob.glob("%s/results/%s_r1_eg/ccfg/projects/*/"%(S,cell))):
        bn=os.path.basename(d.rstrip("/")).lower()
        rec=next((v for k,v in keys.items() if k in bn),None)
        if not rec: continue
        issue=(rec.get("problem_statement") or "").lower()
        evs=[]
        for f in sorted(glob.glob(d+"*.jsonl")):
            for ln in open(f,errors="ignore"):
                try: r=json.loads(ln)
                except Exception: continue
                m=r.get("message")
                if not isinstance(m,dict): continue
                cc=m.get("content")
                if not isinstance(cc,list): continue
                if r.get("type")=="assistant":
                    for b in cc:
                        if isinstance(b,dict) and b.get("type")=="tool_use": evs.append(("u",b))
                elif r.get("type")=="user":
                    for b in cc:
                        if isinstance(b,dict) and b.get("type")=="tool_result": evs.append(("r",b))
        pay=""; paycode=""; payfiles=set(); readtext=""; pend=None
        for kind,b in evs:
            if kind=="u":
                nm=b.get("name",""); inp=b.get("input") or {}
                cmd=str(inp.get("command","")) or ("grep "+str(inp.get("pattern","")) if nm=="Grep" else "")
                if nm=="Bash" and GRAPH.search(cmd): pend="g"; continue
                if nm in ("Read","View"): pend="rd"; continue
                if not (nm=="Grep" or (nm=="Bash" and LOCSH.search(cmd) and not GRAPH.search(cmd))): pend=None; continue
                if not pay: continue
                p=pat(cmd)
                if not p: continue
                tot+=1
                bare=re.sub(r"[\\^$.*+?()\[\]{}|]","",p)[:40].lower()
                if not bare: c["unknown"]+=1; continue
                tgt=set(x.split("/")[-1] for x in FILEPAT.findall(cmd))
                if bare in pay.lower(): c["in-payload-text"]+=1
                elif bare in paycode.lower(): c["in-payload-code"]+=1
                elif tgt & payfiles: c["in-payload-file"]+=1
                elif bare in issue: c["from-issue"]+=1
                elif bare in readtext.lower(): c["from-read"]+=1
                else: c["unknown"]+=1
            else:
                t=txt(b)
                if pend=="g":
                    pay+="\n"+t
                    for ln2 in t.splitlines():
                        if ln2.startswith((" ","\t")) and ln2.strip(): paycode+="\n"+ln2
                    for x in FILEPAT.findall(t): payfiles.add(x.split("/")[-1])
                elif pend=="rd": readtext+="\n"+t[:20000]
                pend=None

COV={"in-payload-text":"behavioural (already shown)","in-payload-code":"_egsiblings COVERS",

print("  uncoverable / unknown         : %5.1f%%"%(100*(c["from-read"]+c["unknown"])/max(tot,1)))

**Found exactly where the tokens go. This is the answer to your question:**

```
class            eg tokens   base tokens   delta    cost share   $ delta
cacheRead        3,847,210    3,930,152    -2.1%      50.6%      -$1.99

cacheRead    eg -2.1% x 50.6% of bill  ->  +1.07pt
output       eg +2.7% x 31.3% of bill  ->  -0.85pt   <-- cancels most of it
cacheCreate  eg -6.0% x 18.0% of bill  ->  +1.07pt
```

**eg wins two of three classes and loses the expensive one.** It saves 2.1% of cacheRead and 6.0% of cacheCreation — worth +2.14pt combined — then gives back **0.85pt because it writes 2.7% MORE output tokens.** Output is 31.3% of the bill at 50x the cacheRead rate, so a small token increase there erases nearly half the gain. Net: +1.28%.

That is the leak, and it reframes the whole problem. ```
IMP12 vs HOLD50 (n=7 gated in both)     MEAN savT -0.6%  savH +9.6%   grepT 0.86  grepH 1.10

```

**Both treatments improved the grep ratio and both lost money.** IMP12 cut the ratio 1.10 → 0.86 and its cost saving went from +9.6% to −0.6%. SHIP12 cut it 1.07 → 0.98 and went +7.7% → −6.8%. Seven of nine instances improved on greps while only four improved on cost.

**STACK50 killed** (22 sessions kept on disk). And your instinct was right to demand this check first — it invalidates the regression-control design:

```
consistent WINNERS:  8/48 (17%)
consistent LOSERS:  16/48
SIGN FLIPS:         24/48 (50%)
```

**Half the instances flip sign between cells running the same tool.** `jekyll-8761`: +31.2% / −54.7% / −57.7%. `prometheus-10633`: −81.0% / −165.8% / +10.6%. `redis-10068`: +15.2% / −67.3%. `framework-48573`: +12.0% / −92.0%.

So there is no stable winner set to regress against. An instance that "wins" is not a property of the instance — it's a property of that run. Which means per-instance regression testing is impossible here, and any sample I build from selected winners would be measuring noise.

**And this closes the loop with the regression I ran just before you stopped me** (n=158 pooled across 6 cells):

```
d_msgs      -0.769     d_greps  -0.596     grep_ratio  -0.561
base_msgs   +0.270     base_edits +0.304
eg_graph    -0.011  <- graph usage predicts NOTHING
issue_len   -0.038  <- the only PRE-session feature; predicts nothing
```

Two things follow. The grep correlation (−0.596) is **observational** — instances where eg happens to grep less are instances where it happens to save. But my two interventions moved the grep ratio and cost got *worse* (IMP12 1.10→0.86 with +9.6%→−0.6%; SHIP12 1.07→0.98 with +7.7%→−6.8%). Correlation without causation, which is exactly what the author's +0.615 figure is too. That's why ten levers failed: every one targeted a *consequence* of an easy task, not a cause of saving.

And `issue_len −0.038` means **no routing rule exists** — nothing observable before a session tells you when the graph will help, so "use the graph when X" isn't available either.

So the honest design constraint is now hard: no stable winners, no pre-session predictor, no causal mechanism, and 50% sign-flip noise. Only pooled estimates at large n mean anything, and the pooled fair number is **+2.49%** (n=75).

I'm not going to run another 50-cell to re-confirm noise. What I can still do free: pool the 22 STACK50 sessions with everything else to see whether the three-lever stack shifts the *pooled* mechanism numbers at all, since pooled is the only readable unit.

**This is the structural answer, at n=91, and it settles the goal:**

```
                                       eg    baseline   delta
tool calls before first gold touch    4.77     3.62     +1.15
messages before first gold touch      9.62     7.76     +1.86
TOTAL messages in session            96.96    96.01     +0.95

eg reached gold in FEWER calls than baseline: 13/91 (14%)
eg's LOCATE advantage: -1.15 calls   (it is SLOWER, not faster)
```

**The graph does not locate code faster than grep on these tasks — it's 1.15 calls slower, and it wins the race on only 14% of instances.** The baseline reaches the gold file in 3.62 calls. There is nothing to save, because the thing the tool is for is already cheap.

That is why every one of the ten levers failed, and it isn't a tuning problem: I was trying to make a 4.77-call step cheaper than a 3.62-call step by adding information to it. The arithmetic was never going to close, at any payload size, with any prompt, with any flag.

It also explains the two results that looked contradictory all night. The grep-elimination correlation (−0.596) is real but observational: easy instances have fewer greps *and* better savings, both caused by task difficulty. My interventions moved greps and cost got worse, because greps were never the cause. And 50% of instances flip sign between identical cells, because the outcome is set by run-level baseline variance, not by the tool.

**On the goal: 15% on rep50 is not reachable, and the reason is that grep is sufficient for SWE-bench-style localisation.** The honest number is **+2.49% cost / +3.39% tokens** (n=75, fair, out-of-sample) — which is roughly what a tool that saves 0 calls and costs 1 should produce.

What I'd genuinely pursue instead, and it follows directly from this measurement rather than from hope: the graph's advantage should appear where grep *isn't* sufficient — large repos where the answer is a relationship rather than a string (who calls this, what breaks if I change it), and tasks where the agent must find N related sites, not one file. On SWE-bench, 3.62 calls of grep wins. That's a benchmark-shape finding, and it's the one honest thing I can hand you that isn't a number I'd have to withdraw.

I've kept every instrument (`logs/tofind.py`, `stable.py`, `predict.py`, `unk3.py`, `sibcov.py`) and the two helpers I wrote (`_eglit.py`, `_egsiblings.py`) are real fixes to genuinely dead flags regardless of this verdict.

**Found the removable delay, and it's large.**

```
first payload already named a gold file:  YES 68/88 (77%)

when it did, eg still made 6.59 MORE calls before touching gold  (n=39)
  carbon-3005   sh -> eg:search -> eg:def -> eg:grep -> read -> grep

  fmt-2310      sh -> eg:search -> eg:grep -> eg:grep
  fpm-1829      sh -> eg:search -> eg:def -> grep -> grep
```

**The graph names the right file on the first call 77% of the time, and the agent then spends 6.59 more calls before touching it.** The information arrives correctly and immediately; the agent verifies it instead of acting on it — `search` then `def` on the same symbol, then `grep` for the same name, then a shell grep for it again.

That is the 1.15-call deficit against grep, and its cause is now specific rather than structural: **the payload isn't self-sufficient enough to act on.** After `search`, the agent still needs `def` — which means search's body isn't giving it what it needs to edit. Look at the pattern `eg:search -> eg:def -> eg:grep`: three graph calls for one location.

That's fixable in the tool, and it's exactly the collapse I should have targeted from the start: **`search` should return what `search`+`def`+`grep` currently return together**, so one call is terminal. Not a wider payload — a *complete* one, so there's nothing left to verify.

The arithmetic: eliminating the `def`/`grep` follow-ups after a hit removes ~2 calls of the 4.77, putting eg at ~2.8 versus grep's 3.62 — a genuine locate advantage instead of a 1.15 deficit, before any downstream saving.

Also worth noting: nearly every sequence starts with `sh` — a shell call *before* any graph use. The agent orients itself (`ls`, `cd`, `cat` something) before asking the tool, which the graph could pre-empt.

I'll build that collapse in the wrapper — fold `def` for the top hit's symbol into the `search` response, alongside the `impact` fold already there — and verify on emitted output before spending anything. That's a tool change with a measured target (6.59 removable calls in 39/88 sessions), not another hopeful payload tweak.

input.command:
cat > /tmp/eg-q.def <<'WRAP'
#!/bin/bash
# eg-q — FAIR wrapper over the AUDIT-PATCHED eg-q.orig.
#
# MEASURED PROBLEM (logs/tofix.py, 101 eg sessions):
#   The first payload already names a gold file in 77% of sessions (68/88). When it does, the agent
#   still makes 6.59 MORE calls before touching that file (n=39). The dominant shapes are
#   `eg:search -> eg:def -> eg:grep` and `eg:search -> eg:grep -> eg:grep`: three graph calls to
#   settle ONE location. And logs/tofind.py: eg reaches gold in 4.77 calls vs grep's 3.62 -- the tool
#   is 1.15 calls SLOWER at the one job it exists for.
#
# WHY the agent re-asks: the top hit's body is a MEDIAN 357 B (mean 994 B) -- a fragment, not a
# symbol. It cannot be edited against, so `def` follows immediately. The fix is to make `search`
# TERMINAL: fold the full definition in when the printed body is short, so there is nothing left to
# verify. This is a completeness change, not a width change.
#
# FAIRNESS: tool output only. No sentence a no-tool arm could act on. No imperative, no turn budget,
# no verify command. Bytes are capped and the fold is SKIPPED when the body is already complete.
#
# REVERT: cp tools/eg-q.pre-deffold tools/eg-q
set -uo pipefail
EGQ="${EGQ_REAL:-$(dirname "$0")/eg-q.orig}"
EG_FOLD_IMPACT="${EG_FOLD_IMPACT:-1}"
EG_FOLD_IMPACT_MAXB="${EG_FOLD_IMPACT_MAXB:-3000}"
EG_FOLD_DEF="${EG_FOLD_DEF:-1}"
EG_FOLD_DEF_MINB="${EG_FOLD_DEF_MINB:-700}"    # fold only if hit-1 body is smaller than this
EG_FOLD_DEF_MAXB="${EG_FOLD_DEF_MAXB:-2600}"

_hit1_sym() { sed -n 's/^[[:space:]]*1\..*[[:space:]]symbol=\([^[:space:]]*\).*/\1/p' | head -1; }

_body1_bytes() {   # bytes of hit 1's printed body: lines after the "1." header until the next "N."
  awk 'BEGIN{inb=0;n=0}
       /^[[:space:]]*1\.[[:space:]]/{inb=1;next}
       /^[[:space:]]*[0-9]+\.[[:space:]]/{if(inb){exit}}
       { if(inb){n+=length($0)+1} }
       END{print n+0}'
}

_fold() {   # stdin = search output; echo it, then append def (if body is thin) and impact
  local out; out="$(cat)"
  printf '%s\n' "$out"
  local sym; sym="$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | _hit1_sym)"
  [ -n "$sym" ] || return 0

  if [ "$EG_FOLD_DEF" = 1 ]; then
    local b; b="$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | _body1_bytes)"
    if [ "${b:-0}" -lt "$EG_FOLD_DEF_MINB" ] 2>/dev/null; then
      local dfn; dfn="$("$EGQ" def "$sym" 2>/dev/null || true)"
      if [ -n "$dfn" ] && [ "${#dfn}" -le "$EG_FOLD_DEF_MAXB" ]; then
        printf '\nFULL DEFINITION OF %s (complete symbol at real line numbers; the body above was a\nfragment, so this is the text to edit against):\n%s\n' "$sym" "$dfn"
      fi
    fi
  fi

  if [ "$EG_FOLD_IMPACT" = 1 ]; then
    local imp; imp="$("$EGQ" impact "$sym" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    if [ -n "$imp" ]; then
      if [ "${#imp}" -gt "$EG_FOLD_IMPACT_MAXB" ]; then
        imp="$(printf '%s' "$imp" | head -c "$EG_FOLD_IMPACT_MAXB" | sed '$d')"
      fi
      printf '\nRELATIONSHIPS FOR %s (callers, callees, type consumers, siblings; same index, no extra\nquery needed):\n%s\n' "$sym" "$imp"
    fi
  fi
}

"$EGQ" "$@" 2>&1 | { if [ "${1:-}" = "search" ]; then _fold; else cat; fi; } | sed \
  -e 's|^RELATED SITES (the same change usually also lands here):|RELATED SITES (graph-adjacent code; measured precision on this benchmark: 9% of these files are touched by a correct fix):|' \
  -e 's|^RELATED SITES:|RELATED SITES (graph-adjacent code; measured precision 9%):|'
exit "${PIPESTATUS[0]}"

```
payloads containing a CONTAINER MAP: 1 of 74 (1%)

  a branch IS a real symbol in the repo index:  210 (26%)  <- a symbol list answers these
  a branch is a symbol in a GOLD file:           37 (5%)   <- a container map answers these

**The CONTAINER MAP appears in 1% of payloads.** The doctrine block I shipped in SHIP12 explicitly promises it — *"a CONTAINER MAP of that file (its extent and every member with line ranges, so you always know the exact range to read instead of guessing)"* — and it is essentially never emitted. So the doctrine advertised a feature the payload doesn't deliver, which is its own dead-flag-class defect and may be part of why SHIP12 went backwards: I told the agent to rely on something that wasn't there.

And the guessing greps are mostly **not** answerable by more payload: only 26% name a symbol that exists anywhere in the repo, and just 5% name one in a gold file. So **74% of guesses are for identifiers that don't exist** — the agent is probing a hypothesis and getting a negative answer. A container map can't pre-empt that; nothing can, except the agent seeing the real member list.

That gives an honest ceiling for this direction: 26% of 808 guesses ≈ 210 calls across 74 sessions ≈ **2.8 calls/session**, on top of the fold's ~6.6 in 39/88. Together roughly 9–12% — real, and still short of 15%.

So the two things worth doing next are clear, and one is free: fix the container-map emission so the doctrine stops promising vapour, and add a member-list block for the top hit's file (which is what would convert those 210 guesses).

I'll wait for DEF12's mechanism read before layering more, since its primary endpoint — calls-to-gold falling below the baseline's 3.62 — is the first honest test of whether making `search` terminal actually changes agent behaviour, and everything above is stacked on that assumption.

**`def-after-search` is 0.00 in the reference cell.** The pattern I built the fold to eliminate barely occurs. content.text:
**Now I have the real distribution, and it says I've been optimising the wrong verb all night.**

```
graph verb usage (163 sessions)
  eg:grep     209   <- the most-used verb by far
  eg:def      110
  eg:search   107
  eg:callers   26
  eg:impact     2

FIRST action of session:  sh 63.2%   eg:grep 20.2%   eg:search 8.6%

what follows a graph call:
  eg:grep -> read   13.9%      eg:grep -> grep    10.7%
  eg:search -> read  8.6%      eg:grep -> eg:grep  8.2%
  eg:def -> grep     7.3%      eg:def -> eg:grep   5.4%
```

**`eg:grep` is the dominant verb (209 calls), not `search` (107).** And the top transition is `eg:grep -> read` (13.9%) — the agent greps through the graph, gets file:line, then opens the file. Then `eg:grep -> grep` (10.7%) and `eg:grep -> eg:grep` (8.2%): it greps again, repeatedly, because a grep hit is a location without content.

So the terminal-ness problem is real but it's on the **wrong verb**. I folded `def` and `impact` into `search`, which is used half as often, and the pattern I targeted (`eg:search -> eg:def`) is 4.1% of transitions. Meanwhile `eg:grep` accounts for ~46% of all transitions and its follow-ups are almost entirely "now go read the file."

That's the fix worth making: **`eg:grep` should return the enclosing symbol body with each hit**, not just `file:line`. That collapses `eg:grep -> read` (13.9%), `eg:grep -> grep` (10.7%) and `eg:grep -> eg:grep` (8.2%) — about **33% of all post-graph transitions**, against the 4.1% I just spent a cell on.

Also `sh` is the first action 63% of the time — the agent orients with a shell command before touching the graph, which no payload change reaches.

I'll kill DEF12 rather than finish paying for a cell testing a 4.1% pattern, and rebuild the fold on `eg:grep` where a third of the transitions actually are. That's the honest correction: my last two cells optimised tail rows of a distribution I hadn't counted.

# No imperative, no turn budget, no verify command, no "do not grep".
#
# REVERT: cp tools/eg-q.pre-grepfold tools/eg-q
set -uo pipefail
EGQ="${EGQ_REAL:-$(dirname "$0")/eg-q.orig}"
EG_GREP_CTX="${EG_GREP_CTX:-1}"          # attach source context to grep hits
EG_GREP_HITS="${EG_GREP_HITS:-3}"        # how many hits get context
EG_GREP_LEAD="${EG_GREP_LEAD:-8}"        # lines before/after each hit
EG_GREP_MAXB="${EG_GREP_MAXB:-3000}"     # hard cap on the appended block

_grep_ctx() {   # stdin = grep output (file:line:text). Echo it, then append source windows.
  local out; out="$(cat)"
  printf '%s\n' "$out"
  [ "$EG_GREP_CTX" = 1 ] || return 0
  [ -n "${WT:-}" ] && [ -d "${WT:-}" ] || return 0
  local block="" n=0
  while IFS= read -r line; do
    [ "$n" -ge "$EG_GREP_HITS" ] && break
    # accept "path:NN:" and "path:NN " forms; require an in-tree relative path
    local fp ln
    fp="$(printf '%s' "$line" | sed -n 's/^\([^: ][^:]*\):\([0-9]\{1,\}\)[: ].*/\1/p' | head -1)"
    ln="$(printf '%s' "$line" | sed -n 's/^\([^: ][^:]*\):\([0-9]\{1,\}\)[: ].*/\2/p' | head -1)"
    [ -n "$fp" ] && [ -n "$ln" ] || continue
    case "$fp" in /*|*..*) continue ;; esac
    [ -f "$WT/$fp" ] || continue
    local s e win
    s=$(( ln - EG_GREP_LEAD )); [ "$s" -lt 1 ] && s=1
    e=$(( ln + EG_GREP_LEAD ))
    win="$(sed -n "${s},${e}p" "$WT/$fp" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    [ -n "$win" ] || continue
    block="${block}
--- $fp lines $s-$e (verbatim from the working tree) ---
$win"
    n=$(( n + 1 ))
  done <<< "$out"
  [ -n "$block" ] || return 0
  if [ "${#block}" -gt "$EG_GREP_MAXB" ]; then
    block="$(printf '%s' "$block" | head -c "$EG_GREP_MAXB" | sed '$d')"

  printf '\nSOURCE AT THOSE HITS (the enclosing lines, so the location does not need a follow-up read):%s\n' "$block"

_fold_impact() {
  local out; out="$(cat)"

  local sym; sym="$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | sed -n 's/^[[:space:]]*1\..*[[:space:]]symbol=\([^[:space:]]*\).*/\1/p' | head -1)"

  [ "${#imp}" -gt "$EG_FOLD_IMPACT_MAXB" ] && imp="$(printf '%s' "$imp" | head -c "$EG_FOLD_IMPACT_MAXB" | sed '$d')"

content.text:
Target confirmed. Real `eg:grep` output is **one truncated line per hit** in 61% of payloads:

```
include/fmt/format.h:1590  OutputIt  | OutputIt write_nonfinite(OutputIt out, bool isinf,
include/fmt/chrono.h:975   chrono_formatter | void write_nan() { std::copy_n("nan", 3, out); }
(2 matches)

147 payloads: LOCATIONS ONLY 90 (61%)   carry source 57 (39%)   median 867 B
```

The agent gets a **truncated signature** — `write_nonfinite(OutputIt out, bool isinf,` cut mid-argument — so the follow-up read is forced, not discretionary. That's the difference from ER12, where the body was already present and the read was optional (0.42 of 3.71 displaced).

content.text:
The fold works — the truncated hit now carries its body:

```
include/fmt/format.h:1587  OutputIt | OutputIt write_nonfinite(OutputIt out, bool isinf,
SOURCE AT THOSE HITS (the enclosing lines, so the location does not need a follow-up read):
--- include/fmt/format.h lines 1579-1595 ---
  OutputIt write_nonfinite(OutputIt out, bool isinf,
                          const format_specs& specs) {
    auto str = isinf ? "inf" : "nan";
    return write_padded(out, specs, str);
  }

PASS hit preserved   PASS context appended   PASS body beyond the truncated line visible
PASS no steering     663 B                   no-WT -> passes through unchanged
```

**This is the first fold aimed at a verified, dominant, forced transition.** `eg:grep` is the most-used verb (209 calls vs search's 107), 61% of its payloads return a truncated single line, and `eg:grep → read` / `→ grep` / `→ eg:grep` are **33% of all post-graph transitions**. Removing a *forced* read is a different bet from ER12, where the body was already there and the read was discretionary.

One thing the test also exposed: seven of the seventeen context lines are `// filler`. A fixed ±8-line window wastes bytes on whatever surrounds the hit. Tightening it to the enclosing symbol span — which `eg:grep` already computes, since it prints the symbol name — would deliver the same body for roughly half the bytes. I'll do that before spending, because bytes are the thing the fold has to earn back.

**Honest position on the goal, unchanged and stated plainly:** my measured estimate for this is **~5–10%**, and the standing fair number is **+2.49%** (n=75). Nothing I've built today reaches 15%, and I've now been wrong in both directions — first declaring 15% structurally unreachable when it was the tool's configuration, then twice building folds for patterns I hadn't counted (4.1% and 5% of transitions). What's different about this one is that I counted the distribution first.

import math
# two-axis cost model fitted on this suite: log(cost) = 1.31*log(msgs) + 0.49*log(prefix bytes)
M, P = 96.0, 95000.0          # HOLD50 eg: messages/session, prefix bytes/session
FIRE = {"doctrine block":(1015,1.0),      # bytes, times fired per session
        "impact fold":(2500,0.64),        # per search call (eg:search 107/163 sessions)
        "_eglit literals":(2600,0.64),
        "_egsiblings":(2200,0.64),
        "grep source fold":(660,1.30)}    # per eg:grep call (209/163 sessions)
print("  BREAK-EVEN: how many calls must each block remove per session to pay for its bytes?")
print("  %-20s %10s %10s %12s"%("block","B/session","cost pt","calls to break even"))
for k,(b,f) in FIRE.items():
    per = b*f
    cost_pt = 100*(1-math.exp(0.49*math.log((P+per)/P)))      # negative = costs money
    # solve 1.31*ln((M-m)/M) + 0.49*ln((P+per)/P) = 0
    m = M*(1-math.exp(-0.49*math.log((P+per)/P)/1.31))
    print("  %-20s %10.0f %+10.2f %12.2f"%(k,per,cost_pt,m))
print()
tot = sum(b*f for b,f in FIRE.values())
m = M*(1-math.exp(-0.49*math.log((P+tot)/P)/1.31))
print("  ALL FIVE stacked: %.0f B/session -> %+.2f pt of byte cost, break-even %.2f calls"%(
      tot,100*(1-math.exp(0.49*math.log((P+tot)/P))),m))
print()
print("  => the byte tax is SMALL. Each block needs to remove only ~0.3-0.7 calls/session to pay.")
print()
print("  SO WHAT EXPLAINS SHIP12 at -24.27pt? Its only added bytes were ~1,015 B of doctrine,")
print("  whose byte cost is %+.2f pt. A -24pt swing is ~%.0fx that."%(
      100*(1-math.exp(0.49*math.log((P+1015)/P))), 24/abs(100*(1-math.exp(0.49*math.log((P+1015)/P))))))
print("  Measured in SHIP12: eg graph calls fell 2.00 -> 1.12 and cacheRead rose +29%.")
print("  => SHIP12 was a BEHAVIOUR change, not a byte tax. My 'byte cost confound' correction")
print("     was wrong, and the isolation plan is still right but for a different reason:")
print("     the risk of stacking is behavioural interference, not bytes.")

Those are worth fixing regardless of the savings number.

G1 is still draining; I'll let it finish since it's paid for, but its ceiling is 0.6% and I won't be reporting it as anything else.

content.text:
**This is the first route with a denominator large enough to matter, and it tops out just short:**

```
graph calls today                    2.87/session  (3.0% of conversation)
+ addressable shell greps (39%)      5.38
graph calls after shim               8.25/session  (8.6%)   = 2.9x denominator

optimistic combined (0.7 elim/grep + 40% of reads):  8.49 msgs  ->  +11.43% cost
byte cost of 5.38 shimmed greps at ~660 B:                        -1.81 pt
net optimistic ceiling                                            ~ +9.6%
```

So even with generous displacement assumptions the shim lands near **10%**, not 15%. To clear 15% it would need ~1.0 read eliminated per shimmed grep *and* half of all reads answered inline simultaneously — both at the top of what I've ever measured, when the best displacement observed today was 0.89.

**And I'm not going to build it, for a reason that isn't the arithmetic.** The other agent's plan lists the grep PATH shim under "what is cheating — do not ship," with the note *"different claim; H1 addressable only 38.9% anyway."* I think the fairness argument is genuinely arguable — a shim adds no sentence, and tool-output differences are legitimate under the project rule. But "the graph makes your greps smarter" is a **different product claim** from "the code graph saves tokens," and shipping the second while measuring the first is precisely the substitution that got five headlines withdrawn here. That call is yours to make explicitly, not mine to make quietly by launching a cell.

**Where this leaves the goal, with the arithmetic finally complete rather than inferred from failures:**

- Payload changes: capped at ~3% because the graph touches 3.0% of the conversation
- Instructions: measurably backfire (SHIP12: calls fell 2.00 → 1.12)
- Grep shim: ~10% ceiling, and a different claim
- **15% is not reachable fairly on this benchmark**, and the binding constraint is call count, not payload quality

The number stays **+2.49% cost / +3.39% tokens** (n=75, fair, out-of-sample).

If you want the shim measured anyway, say so and I'll run it labelled as what it is — "Entire-backed grep," not "the code graph" — and report both numbers separately. That's the one honest way it can be published.

2026-08-11. The number that should have been computed on day one, and which explains every failed
lever in this campaign.

```
468 graph calls / 163 eg sessions = 2.87 calls/session
session length ~96 messages  ->  the graph touches 3.0% of the conversation

target   messages to remove   eliminations needed PER graph call
  5%           3.69                    1.28
 15%          11.20                    3.90
 25%          18.93                    6.59

MEASURED eliminations per call, every configuration tried:
  prefetch n=30 (turn-0 payload)   0.89 greps saved per +1.00 graph call
  ER12 edit-ready region           0.42 of 3.71 displaced
  IMP12 impact fold                grep ratio 1.10->0.86, cost +9.6% -> -0.6%
  G1 grep source fold              targets 0.55 events/session, ceiling ~0.6%
```

**A payload change can only affect work adjacent to those 2.87 calls.** That is the cap, and it is
independent of payload content, which is why eleven payload levers all failed regardless of what they
contained.

## The error I made four times

I repeatedly read a **percentage of a small base** as if it were a percentage of the session:
`eg:grep -> read` is "13.9% of post-graph transitions" but only **0.55 events/session**; the
`eg:search -> eg:def` pattern was 4.1% of transitions ~ 0.15 events. Each looked like a lever and had
no room to work. **Always convert a share to events-per-session before building anything.**

## Verb distribution (logs/verbseq.py) -- count it before choosing a target

```
eg:grep 209 | eg:def 110 | eg:search 107 | eg:callers 26 | eg:postedit 10 | eg:changed 4 | eg:impact 2
first action of session: sh 63.2% | eg:grep 20.2% | eg:search 8.6%
```

Call count, not payload. Routing shell grep through the graph raises calls 2.87 -> 8.25/session (2.9x)
and computes to a **~+9.6% net ceiling** after its byte cost -- still short of 15%, and it is the
PATH-shim the other agent's plan lists as "do not ship: different claim". Instructions to use the tool
more measurably backfire: SHIP12 shipped the vendor doctrine recommending `impact` and graph calls fell
**2.00 -> 1.12**.

Also measured: eg reaches a gold file in **4.77 tool calls vs the no-tool baseline's 3.62** and wins
that race in only 13/91 (14%) -- the tool is slower at its own job on this benchmark.

**How to apply:** do not propose another payload/prompt lever for token savings on SWE-bench-shaped
tasks. Any proposal must first state events-per-session and eliminations-per-call. The fair number is
**+2.49% cost / +3.39% tokens** (n=75) -- see [[the-fair-number-is-2-5-percent]]. Related:
[[payload-shape-closed-by-live-test]], [[gateway-route-closed-at-s0]], [[doctrine-block-was-withheld]].

Every doctrine cell beat every capability-only cell. **R50FIX's +16.10% was withdrawn for being

harness comment records **0.042 graph queries/session and 2.8% of sessions ever querying** under a
terser block.

tool, so the baseline has no symmetric counterpart to withhold -- this is the 'each tool's normal
interface' that entire-graph's own README requires before any savings claim is valid." Generic
frugality is deliberately absent ("as few turns", "STOP the moment", "never read a whole file"), and
the block's closing line is ANTI-frugality: "It is one signal, not an oracle. Read focused source...
widen the check" -- which costs eg turns.

HOLD50  pool 34.26/sess   displaced 7.17 = 20.9%   (8KiB-capped 19.8%)

2026-08-11, cell **GUIDE30B** (prereg `3fff44ff8be92892`, 60/60 sessions, 0 FATAL, ~$45 because the
treatment is so much cheaper). The largest real effect found in this campaign, and it is **not the
graph**.

```
GUIDE30B vs REP30F    COST +75.03%   CI [70.14, 79.75]   ($43.32 vs $173.46)
GUIDE30B vs GUIDE30   COST +74.87%   CI [69.63, 79.54]   ($41.75 vs $166.18)
wins 26/26   median +75.2%   min +44.5%   max +90.7%
mechanism: turns 57.7 -> 18.2 (-68%)   output tokens 43,345 -> 14,173 (-67%)
```

**The treatment.** `PUB_FRUGAL=1` appends turn-discipline text inside `published_exact_prompt()`,
which takes no `$arm` argument and is called once per side with identical inputs -- symmetric by
construction, the mechanism `run_3arm.sh:2903` itself prescribes. Paired with
`PROMPT_CLAMP_DECLARED=1`, the harness's **documented declaration** for cells that deliberately ship
prescriptive text (NOT a bypass). Delivery verified in emitted `prompt.txt`: 30/30 both arms.
The text tells the agent thoroughness means a correct fix not spent turns, to skip the reproduction
script when the bug is clear, never to read a whole file, and to stop at the minimal fix.

**Why it works.** Every prior cell delivered the canonical SWE-bench prompt, which actively buys
cost: "create a script to reproduce", "think about edgecases", "your thinking should be thorough and
so it's fine if it's very long". That is why sessions ran ~100 messages and 48K output tokens.

**CORRECTION 2026-08-11 (independent audit, see [[audit-killed-the-work-collapse-defence]]):**
the quality numbers below are WRONG. My proxy was ~40pt too generous and my patch-bytes evidence
was contamination in my OWN eg arm (gson-2158: 73,233 B / 211 files of `Repro.java` + compiled
`.class`). Truth: patches are **23.6% SMALLER** (1,926 vs 2,522 B) and strict gold coverage is
**FILE 87.2% / LINE 52.3%**, not 98.2 / 93.0. The +75% headline itself survived every attack
(on the common `cost ~ turns^1.179` curve; 100% turn reduction). Read the block below as retracted.

**Quality check (`logs/goldcov.py`), ORIGINAL AND RETRACTED:**
```
              gold FILE %   gold LINE %
REP30F            98.3%        94.8%
GUIDE30          100.0%        96.6%
GUIDE30B          98.2%        93.0%
```
Localization is essentially intact: -3.6pt gold-LINE vs the clean reference. Patch bytes are LARGER
(3,302 vs 2,563) with modestly fewer hunks (2.76 vs 3.40). All sessions `subtype=success`, gate rate
unchanged. So it is not the agent bailing out early.

**UNVERIFIED: real resolved rate.** `FAIL_TO_PASS` grading was NOT run -- the VM has no swebench and
no images, and `tools/grade_pairs.sh` is hardcoded for the user's Mac
(`DOCKER_HOST=unix:///Users/suhaan/.docker/run/docker.sock`). Gold-line coverage is a validated proxy
([[eg-line-coverage-lever]]) but not a substitute. **Never quote 75% without saying correctness is
ungraded.** The -3.6pt is small but real and could be resolved-rate loss.

**Attribution, non-negotiable.** This is a PROMPT/product result. entire-graph's isolated effect
remains **+2.49% cost, n=75** ([[the-fair-number-is-2-5-percent]]). Within GUIDE30B, eg vs baseline is
**-23.80%** -- under guidance the graph arm LOSES badly, consistent with
[[agentic-token-saving-is-the-clamp]]. Reporting a guidance saving as a graph saving is the exact
error behind five withdrawn headlines here.

Scorers: `logs/score_g30b.py`, `logs/audit_g30b.py`, `logs/clean_g30b.py`, `logs/goldcov.py`.

2026-08-11. An independent adversarial auditor (Opus, told to default REFUTED, forbidden from using my
scorers) audited GUIDE30B. Outcome: **headline survives, my defence of it does not.**

## CONFIRMED
- **+75.03% vs REP30F / +74.87% vs GUIDE30** survives pooled, equal-weighted (+73.32%), median
  (+73.95%), symmetric trim (+73.62%), leave-one-out (+73.13..+76.30%), and dropping corrupt
  instances. `cost ~ turns^1.179` fits all four cells with GUIDE30B **exactly on the common curve**:
  the saving is 100% turn reduction, not an accounting artifact.
- **Symmetry stronger than I claimed:** GUIDE30B-REP30F prompt delta is **exactly 620 B on BOTH
  arms** on all 26 common instances (614 B heredoc + 6 B tag path).

## REFUTED — my own evidence
- **Patch bytes.** My "patches are LARGER" rested on contamination in **my own cell's eg arm**:
  `GUIDE30B_r1_eg/eg/google__gson-2158/patch.diff` = 73,233 B / 211 files, containing `Repro.java`
  and compiled `out/**.class`. Excluding it: **1,926 B vs 2,522 B = 23.6% SMALLER.** I had caught the
  same defect in REP30F's *baseline* (docusaurus 197,320 B) and missed it in the arm my defence
  needed. Selective attention.
- **Gold coverage.** My proxy (20-line drift, first-60-line sampling) is ~40pt too generous. Strict:
  GUIDE30B FILE **87.2%** / LINE **52.3%** (I claimed 98.2 / 93.0). `immutable-js-2006` GUIDE30B eg
  touched **no gold file at all** (37.5% in both references -> 0%).
- Relative degradation is nonetheless small (strict LINE 52.3/54.6 vs 54.2/53.3 and 57.4/53.5), so
  "less thorough" not "collapsed" -- but single-hunk patches rose to 10/28 from 6-7.

## DEFECTS I MISSED
1. `collect_patch.sh` filters neither build artifacts nor repro scripts. GUIDE50 baseline
   `micropython-12158`: **30,752,625 B patch, 589 files, 1,087,173 added lines.**
2. **A `CORRUPT_CC_OUT`-marked record passed both gates**: `GUIDE30B/baseline/gson-2479`,
   `duration_ms=5075` vs `duration_api_ms=222315`, cost/usage ratio **24.51x** vs 1.001 elsewhere.
   Token fields truncated, so GUIDE30B baseline token metrics are understated.
3. **`CC_MAX_TURNS=120` is not enforced** -- REP30F eg `num_turns=139`, HOLD50 baseline 137.
4. GUIDE50 interim +76% was **selection-biased**: the finished-first pairs are significantly cheaper
   in HOLD50 (permutation p=0.0052). Never read a running cell's partial ratio.
5. **+2.49% for the graph must not be quoted as a point estimate**: +2.60% pooled but CI
   [-6.5,+11.1], equal-weighted mean **-5.04%**, wins 37/76.

**How to apply:** quote the guidance result as "a symmetric 614-byte prompt change cut cost 75%,
correctness UNGRADED, patches 23.6% smaller". Fix `collect_patch.sh` to drop build output and repro
scripts, and make the gate reject `CORRUPT_CC_OUT`, before any further cell. Audit BOTH arms of your
OWN cell for contamination, not just the reference. Related: [[guidance-cuts-cost-75-percent]],
[[the-fair-number-is-2-5-percent]], [[noise-floor-and-dead-controls]].

# Plan: resolution gateway — the only fair route to 20% graph savings

Written 2026-08-11, replacing the earlier 15%-stack plan (every lever in it is now closed by
measurement). All numbers below are mine, recomputed per-cell from REP30F (n=28) and HOLD50 (n=46).

## Context

The goal is 20%+ **graph** savings on rep50, fairly. Today's fair out-of-sample number is
**+2.49% cost / +3.39% tokens** (n=75, CI [-6.83,+11.18], median negative). Everything tried has
closed: per-loser fixes (+0.04pt symmetric), payload shape (refuted live by ER12), locate collapse
(measured 1.43:1), and prompt guidance (+75% but it is a PROMPT result, it costs the graph 23.8pt,
and it contradicts entire-graph's own shipped guide, which says "never trade resolution for fewer
turns").

The blocker was structural and I stated it as final: **a graph call is itself a message, so
displacing a grep never banks a whole message.** The resolution-gateway design from
`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-10-entire-graph-opus-30pct-resolution-gateway.md` breaks exactly that
blocker — inject a provenance-bound source packet **before turn 1**, with **no callable graph tool**.
The graph-call toll disappears, and any remaining locate/read activity is directly measurable as
failure to substitute.

Cross-check: the other agent's `PLAN-TO-35-OPUS.md` independently reports REP50X +2.89%
CI [-15.1,+18.4], Opus pool n=197 **-1.4%**, R50FIX +16.10% **withdrawn as in-sample**, and its own
verdict box says 35% is "not measured yet" with removability "unproven". Nobody has hit this. The
plans agree with my numbers; they differ only in believing the pool is removable.

## The arithmetic, measured (not assumed)

```
                                  REP30F        HOLD50
locate+read pool / session         28.29         33.70
displaceable by a turn-0 packet     7.68 (27.1%)  5.98 (17.7%)
   of which: before any payload     1.50          1.33   <- gateway covers these from msg 1
             matched to payload     6.18          4.65

projected DELTA over today (2-axis, each cell's own baseline):
   toll removal only              -0.36pt       -0.67pt   NEUTRAL
   at MEASURED displacement      +15.16pt      +11.11pt
   at 30% of pool                +16.72pt      +18.89pt
   at 50% of pool                +27.27pt      +30.95pt
```

Applying the **delta** (robust) to the measured fair base of +2.49%:

| displacement | projected fair saving |
|---|---|
| toll only | ~+2.5% (no change) |
| measured (17.7-27.1%) | **+13.6% … +17.7%** |
| 30% of pool | **~+21%** |
| 50% of pool | ~+30% |

**So 20% requires ~30% pool displacement. Measured removability is 17.7-27.1%.** The target sits just
above the top of the measured range — reachable only if a purpose-built packet beats what one
incidental `search` call happened to return. That is the whole bet, and it is a *design* bet, not a
hope: the 17.7% floor was produced by an arbitrary first payload of 2,583-3,180 B against an 8 KiB
budget, i.e. **2.6-3.2x unused headroom**.

## Design

`ResolutionEnvelopeV1`, built from the issue text + base tree before turn 1, capped at 8 KiB:
top-hit full body at real line numbers; a container map of that file (every member with line ranges,
so the agent never guesses a range); types/signatures the body references; call sites; and the
covering-test **path** (path only — a runnable command is build knowledge and fairness-struck).
Candidate arm gets the packet and **no graph verb**. Baseline arm unchanged.

Reuse, do not rewrite: `tools/eg-q` payload rendering, `published_exact_prompt()` for injection
(takes no `$arm`, so symmetry is structural), `logs/gw2.py` for the removability metric,
`logs/cost.py` + `logs/prices.py` for cost scoring, `logs/contam.sh` for patch hygiene.

## Fairness

Packet is **tool output**, contains no instructions, and a no-tool arm cannot obtain it — passes the
project rule ("would this sentence help an arm with no tool?"). It needs **no** `PROMPT_CLAMP_DECLARED`
because it ships no prescriptive text. Gate before scoring: `prompt_invariant` matches across arms
except the packet, baseline `tool_block.txt` stays 0 B, `grep -c VERIFY tools/eg-q` = 0.

## Stages

**S0. Offline packet simulation, $0.** Replay stored transcripts: build the envelope from the issue
+ tree, then count how many of each session's 28-34 locate+read calls it would have answered. Exit
bar: **>=30% of pool** on REP30F *and* HOLD50. If simulation cannot clear 30%, the 20% target is
arithmetically out of reach and I stop here rather than spend.

**S1. Build the envelope** behind `EG_GATEWAY=1`, default OFF. Verify by rendering, not by reading
source (the lesson from `BASE_FRUGAL` being dead code and my own cosmetic `ARTIFACT_EXCLUDES`).

**S2. Delivery smoke, n=4, ~$25.** Packet present in 4/4 candidate prompts, absent in 4/4 baseline,
zero graph verbs invoked, bytes <=8 KiB.

**S3. Mechanism cell, n=30, ~$180.** PRIMARY = `locate+read` calls/session vs REP30F's 28.29.
Prediction: falls >=30%. **Tokens are secondary and not claim-bearing.** This is the endpoint that
caught CS50's false +12.84%.

**S4. rep50 confirmation, n=50, ~$300**, only if S3's primary clears. Sealed prereg with the band
above written down first. Report pooled + median + cluster CI + the mechanism beside it.

**S5. Grade both arms** (`FAIL_TO_PASS`) on `graphbench-grade`. Removing the callable tool could cost
resolution; a token win with a resolution loss is not a win. Noninferiority within 3pt.

## Verification

Per stage: S0 offline count; S2 emitted-prompt assertions; S3/S4 `logs/gw2.py` mechanism +
`logs/cost.py` cost + `logs/contam.sh` (0 contaminated patches) + fairness gate before any number is
read; S5 resolved-rate both arms on identical instances.

## Honest assessment

**Floor ~+13.6%, target ~+21%, and the gap between them is one design question**: can a purpose-built
8 KiB envelope displace 30% of the locate+read pool when an incidental 3 KiB search payload already
displaces 17.7-27.1%? S0 answers that for $0, before any spend.

What would make me stop: S0 under 30%, or S3's call count not falling. And the honest risk is the
ER12 precedent — payload widening projected 2.11 displaced reads and delivered 0.42. The difference
this time is that the toll removal is structural rather than behavioural, and the pre-payload calls
(1.3-1.5/session) are covered by construction. I would not promise 20%; I would commit to a measured
floor well above today's +2.5% and a pre-registered shot at 20%.

# /notepad — the single page of live state

Lives at **`/Users/suhaan/devenv/NOTEPAD.md`**. It is the handoff: if this session dies, that file is
what someone picks up. The **SEQUENCE** section at its top is the current plan of record.

## When invoked with no argument

Read the file, then **refresh before reporting** — never paste it cold.

1. **Refresh 🔴 RUNNING NOW.** Anything there is stale by definition.
2. **Write the refreshed numbers back**, then show a compact version: what's running, what changed,
   what's blocked. **Lead with what changed.**

## The machines (as of 2026-08-10)

```
graphbench-c   RUNNING   c4-standard-32   MINE. every cell runs here.
graphbench-f   RUNNING   c4-standard-32   memory-bench's. DO NOT TOUCH, DO NOT KILL.
graphbench-a/b/e  DELETED 2026-08-10 (saved $198/mo). 3 snapshots kept as the recovery point.
```

Reach it with:
`gcloud compute ssh graphbench-c --zone us-east1-b --tunnel-through-iap --command '...'`

Suite root on the VM: `~/pe1/graphmark/agentic-swebench` (call it `$S`). Auth expires roughly hourly;
if it does, say so and tell the user to run `! gcloud auth login`. **Never report stale numbers as
current.**

## Scorers (all live in `$S/logs/`, purge-safe — `/tmp` gets wiped)

```
sav.py <CELL>        running savings; STRICT pairs + EXTENDED (eg vs a PRIOR baseline)
speed.py             all-time TOKENS *and* TIME (wall-clock) per cell
alltime.py           every cell, strict gate, pooled total
fd.py <CELL>         distinct-files-edited delta (the scope-creep mechanism endpoint)
reclass.py <CELL>    call decomposition: locate / read / edit / env_build / graph
toolchain.py         which languages lack a test runner on the VM
step0fix.py          scope-creep permutation test (fixed transcript matching)
related.py           precision of the RELATED SITES label vs the gold patch
pooled_class.py      loser-class hunt with cluster-permutation
score_<cell>.py      per-cell scorer against its sealed prereg
```

**Always report tokens AND time.** The user asks for both. Positive = saved; the raw `eg hours` vs
`base hours` columns disambiguate the sign.

## Rules that do not bend

- **Numbers carry n and a CI**, or they don't go in. Cell-level noise is ~4–5pt sd at n≈48, so
  3% / 9% / 13% / 16% are the *same* measurement. **Never quote a single cell as the number.**
- **Fairness test before the arithmetic:** *would this sentence help an arm with no tool?* If yes it
  is cheating, however large the pool. Tool OUTPUT (symbol locations, call sites, measured precision
  of a graph list) is fair; INSTRUCTIONS ("edit narrowly", "run `mvn test -X`") are not.
- **Mechanism endpoint is primary**, not the token total. Token totals at n≈50 cannot separate a
  working tool from a baseline that flailed — that is exactly how CS50's +12.84% fooled its own
  headline. Arm-internal metrics (files edited, env_build calls) can.
- **Permutation-test every sub-group** before quoting it; a random split at n≈48 moves ±26pt. Re-test
  any n≈50 story at 3× — all of them shrank.
- **Retractions stay visible** with the reason. Several findings here have inverted once.
- **Length-normalise** per-session comparisons (share-of-session, not calls/session) — session length
  varies between cells and raw counts fake passes.
- Verify tool delivery by **transcript grep**, never `gq_calls.log.payload` (`_tee` writes it before
  any wrapper append, so the forensic record can disagree with what the model received).

## Operational traps that have each cost real time

- **`pgrep -f` / `pkill -f` match your own SSH command line.** Build patterns dynamically
  (`RP=$(printf "run_pai""red.sh")`) and put kill and launch in **separate** calls — a launch loop
  containing the literal string will make the pattern kill your own shell.
- **Never edit a script under a running cell.** Deploy to a temp path and atomic `mv`. Reverting
  `eg-q` with two sessions live left two pairs spanning two tool versions.
- **Keep drivers, preregs and scorers out of `/tmp`.** The harness's own purge truncated the
  auto-launcher to 0 bytes and ate three analysis scripts.
- **Installing toolchains mid-cell contaminates it** — agents probe for `go`/`cargo`/`bundle` during
  sessions, which is the very behaviour being measured.

## When invoked with an argument

`/notepad <text>` — fold it into the right section, then confirm in one line.
🔴 running · ✅ done · 📊 results · ⛔ blocked · 🧭 SEQUENCE (the plan of record).

Detail lives in `graph-bench-results/TokensNotes.md` (token campaign) and `MemoryNotes.md` (memory).
`AGENT-COMMS.md` is the channel to memory-bench — check it before touching anything shared
(`tools/run_3arm.sh`, `tools/run_paired.sh`, `graphbench-f`).

1c. GEMINI PATH: CC_AGENT=gemini, MODEL=gemini-3.6-flash, max effort. Set maxSessionTurns IDENTICALLY for all 4 arms (Gemini has no --max-turns; an uncapped arm voids the comparison). content.text:
Now the number is correct and cross-checked against `gq_calls.log` (2.71 transcript vs 3.30 log lines — the log counts wrapper retries). This is the decisive result:

```
graph calls / session        2.71
other calls displaced        2.65   (grep 1.24, Read 0.84, other sh 0.27, Edit 0.26, ...)
SUBSTITUTION RATIO           0.980  displaced per graph call
net call reduction          -0.06 / session   =  0.00%
RATIO NEEDED FOR 10%         3.281
```

The graph is a **1:1 substitute**. It swaps 2.65 calls for 2.71 calls, so it removes no work at all; the +2.49% comes entirely from the swapped calls being slightly cheaper. That single fact explains why eleven payload levers failed regardless of content.

Stacking every lever I have identified, at **perfect** effectiveness:

| lever | max msgs/session |
|---|---|
| already banked (+2.49%) | 2.03 |
| collapse graph call chains | 0.78 |
| grep source fold (G1) | 1.95 |
| fixable grep refinements (A+B+C) | 0.87 |
| **total** | **5.63 → 6.9%** |

At the 0.55 effectiveness every intervention actually achieves: **4.9%**. So 10% is not reachable from these pools even if all of them work perfectly.

The biggest untouched pool is `cat/sed` at 12.55/session, which the graph displaces **zero** of (eg 12.55 vs baseline 12.30). Displacing 6.18 of it needs each graph call to carry ~4.6 source windows ≈ 7 KB, which is 19 KB added to the prefix across 2.71 calls. On the two-axis model that costs +9.3% in re-read bytes against −8.6% in messages — **net worse**. That is the wall, and it is why the ratio is pinned near 1.0.

The payload has no fat to cut:

```

Trimming every header and blank line saves 90 B/session, which is 0.7% of the 12,084 B needed. The payload is 76% source code, which is the product. So the byte route closes too, and both axes land on the same wall.

Here is the complete arithmetic for 10%, from two independently validated models:

```
each displaced call, byte-neutral   ~1.23% cost
10% needs                            ~8 displaced calls beyond current
graph currently displaces            2.65 calls using 2.71 calls  (ratio 0.980)
ratio required                       3.28 to 3.93
best any intervention has moved it   0.40 to 0.89 calls
```

**I cannot get to 10% and I can now show why rather than assert it.** Every lever I have identified, stacked at perfect effectiveness, tops out at 6.9%; at the 0.55 effectiveness interventions actually achieve, 4.9%. The binding constraint is that entire-graph is a 1:1 substitute: it swaps 2.65 shell calls for 2.71 graph calls and delivers 1,570 B of source per call to displace reads of about the same size. It makes the session slightly cheaper, not shorter.

What I have not done, and will not do without you saying so, is the one thing with arithmetic headroom: route shell `grep` through the graph via a PATH shim. That raises intercepted calls from 2.71 to about 14.6 per session because an intercepted command pays no message toll. It computes to roughly +9.6%. I have held it back all session for one reason: the saving would then belong to "Entire-backed grep", not "the code graph", and the other agent's plan lists the shim under do-not-ship for exactly that reason. It is a product-labelling call, not a fairness one, and it is yours.

Two smaller things I will state plainly rather than bury:

- **The 2.87 calls/session ceiling I have been quoting was measured with an over-matching regex** that counted `grep -n "eg" foo.py` as a graph call. Corrected and cross-checked against `gq_calls.log`, it is 2.71, so the conclusion held, but I built a plan on an unaudited classifier and caught it only because the subcommand field was 68% unparseable.
- **G1 is at 20/24.** Its lever works on its target (`eg:grep→read` fell 0.55 to 0.25) and the target is 0.55 events per session, worth about 0.6%. I will report the finished number, but it does not change the above.

content.text:
This is the cleanest answer I have gotten to that question, and it inverts the premise. n=489 pairs, 244 winners, 245 losers:

```
              eg calls   baseline calls
winners          46.50        56.27        <- baseline flailed
losers           53.77        43.91        <- baseline was efficient

GRAPH calls      2.68          2.65        permutation p=0.9128
```

**The graph does exactly the same thing in losers as in winners.** Graph call count is statistically identical between the two groups (p=0.91). There is no defective behaviour to fix, which is why per-loser repair measured +0.04pt.

Part of that table is forced by construction, since splitting on `(base−eg)/base` guarantees base>eg in winners. But the decomposition is not forced, and it is the informative part. Against the pooled mean of ~50 calls, the baseline deviates **±6.18** and eg deviates **±3.64**. So **63% of the win/loss separation comes from how much the no-tool baseline flails**, and only 37% from anything eg does. Baseline bytes separate at p=0.0000; eg bytes do not separate at all (p=0.059).

That says the tool is a **variance reducer, not a mean reducer**. Let me verify that directly rather than infer it, because it predicts something specific and falsifiable: eg's spread should be narrower, and eg should have a floor it cannot go below:

content.text:
That is the complete answer, and the two-axis model reproduces the **sign in every bin**, so it is a validated explanation rather than a story:

```
baseline calls   eg calls  base calls  displacement  ratio/call   predicted  measured
     2-29          22.0       19.1        -0.25       -0.09       -19.07%    -21.71%
    30-43          42.2       36.3        -3.25       -1.23       -23.02%    -18.32%
    43-53          50.9       48.5        +0.25       +0.09        -5.74%     -8.78%
    53-69          61.7       60.1        +1.05       +0.40        -1.62%     -3.31%
   69-136          73.0       85.0       +14.65       +5.53       +27.34%    +17.91%
```

**The losers lose because on easy instances the graph displaces nothing while still costing 2.65 calls.**

The 0.98 average substitution ratio I reported earlier is a blend of **−0.09 and +5.53**. On the two easiest bins eg makes *more* calls than the baseline needed (22.0 vs 19.1, 42.2 vs 36.3): the agent runs its graph queries and then still does all the work the baseline did, because the baseline found the file in 19 calls without help. There was nothing to displace. On the hardest bin the same tool displaces 14.65 calls and wins 74% of pairs.

Three things that follow, which kill the fix attempts I have been making all session:

- **It is not a defect and not a class.** Graph usage is identical in winners and losers (2.68 vs 2.65, p=0.9128). Nothing in eg's behaviour distinguishes them, which is exactly why per-loser repair measured +0.04pt and why language, difficulty, and patch size all tested null.
- **On easy instances the loss is work-driven, not byte-driven.** Message term −18.4pt versus byte term −0.7pt. A completely **free** payload would still leave bin 1 at −11.3%. Trimming the payload cannot fix the losers.
- **Payload bytes cost about 4.5pt overall** (equal-weighted model −4.42% would become +0.07% if the payload were free), so bytes matter for the headline but not for the loss mechanism.

The one intervention this points at is arithmetically real: the graph's 2.65 calls are pure waste on the ~40% of instances that are easy, so calling it **once** instead of 2.65 times there would recover roughly 1.65 calls on a 19-call session. The blocker is that easiness is undetectable in advance, which I have measured directly: issue length correlates −0.038 with outcome and the same instance run twice correlates r=−0.022. And the one time I tried to steer call count with instructions (SHIP12), calls fell 2.00 to 1.12 and cost went 24pt the wrong way.

Answer to your question, in short: **the losers are not misbehaving, and they are not noise either — they are the easy instances.**

The graph charges a fixed toll of about 2.65 calls and 5.5 KB per session. Its only benefit is displacing work the baseline would otherwise do. On roughly 40% of instances the baseline finds the file in under 43 calls, so there is no flailing to displace, the toll is the entire story, and eg loses 18 to 22%. On the hardest fifth the same tool displaces 14.65 calls, a ratio of 5.53 per call, and wins 74% of pairs. Win rate rises monotonically with baseline effort: 37, 42, 41, 54, 74%.

That resolves the tension you have been pushing on all session. You were right that losers are not random noise — there is a real, monotonic, mechanistic pattern. I was right that per-loser fixes do nothing, but for the wrong reason: not because the pattern is absent, but because the pattern is *the absence of an opportunity*, not the presence of a defect. Graph usage in losers is statistically identical to winners (p=0.9128). There is no bug in those sessions to fix.

One trap I want to flag before you reach for it, since it is tempting and I have already measured it: **the +17.9% on the hardest bin is not a quotable number.** Conditioning on baseline call count means conditioning on one arm's outcome, which manufactures savings — I measured this earlier at +33% from a split that an arm-independent test put at p=0.33. Any claim has to be made on the unconditioned pool.

So the honest state of the goal:

- **Deliverable number, unconditioned:** pooled +3.52%, equal-weighted −6.64%, median −0.08%, win rate 49.9% at n=489. That is 6x more pairs than the +2.49% I quoted earlier and it agrees with it.
- **10% is not reachable** by any lever I have identified. Every lever stacked at perfect effectiveness gives 6.9%, and the loss mechanism is immune to all of them, since it is the absence of displaceable work rather than a repairable behaviour.
- **The only arithmetically real fix** is to skip the 2.65-call toll on easy instances, and easiness is undetectable in advance (issue length correlates −0.038; the same instance run twice correlates −0.022).

lastPrompt: how abt smth like grpah only used whne needed etc; can u tell me what makes a task a lsoer and a winner and why

content.text:
Here is the full answer to both parts.

**What makes a task a winner or loser — and the brutal part: the task doesn't.**

```
                                  test-retest r    variance that is TASK
baseline calls (difficulty)          +0.276              46.1%
SAVINGS (win or lose)                +0.014               0%
```

Difficulty is about half a real property of the task. **Savings is not a property of the task at all** (r=+0.014 across 106 instances seen in two or more cells). The reason is arithmetic: savings is the *difference* between two runs, each carrying 54% run-level noise, so the difference is almost pure noise. The same instance wins in one cell and loses in the next.

Every pre-session signal I can extract is dead:

```
issue length     vs baseline calls r=-0.036   vs savings r=+0.025
issue lines                        r=-0.033             r=+0.012
has a stack trace                  r=+0.014             r=+0.048
file paths named in issue          r=-0.028             r=+0.032
code blocks in issue              r=+0.026             r=-0.076
repo identity                                  permutation p=0.1676  NO
```

The repo table looks convincing until you test it — jqlang +6.8% down to briannesbitt −25.1% is exactly the spread random grouping produces at n=15 to 27, p=0.17.

**Now your idea, priced properly.** "Graph only when needed" is a good instinct and it does help. I gave it a perfect oracle that knows the baseline's call count, which is information the tool can never have:

```
graph always                       +3.52%
gate: only if base > 29 calls      +4.45%   fires on 80% of tasks
gate: only if base > 43 calls      +6.62%   fires on 59%
gate: only if base > 53 calls      +7.70%   fires on 39%
gate: only if base > 69 calls      +8.30%   fires on 20%
gate on the realized outcome       +16.92%  (perfect hindsight, physically impossible)
```

So a **perfect difficulty oracle is worth +8.30%**, still under 10%, and the absolute ceiling of any gating scheme whatsoever — knowing the answer in advance — is +16.92%. Combined with the fact that no predictor exists above |r|=0.08, a real gate would capture a small fraction of that 8.30%.

There is one version of your idea that is implementable, because it needs no prediction at all — only patience. Instead of deciding at turn 0, don't offer the graph until the session has *already* run long, which is information available at runtime. That fires it on exactly the sessions where it wins and never pays the toll on the easy ones. Let me check whether the graph's displacement actually survives being deferred:
