gcloud compute ssh graphbench-c --zone us-east1-b --tunnel-through-iap --command '
S=$HOME/pe1/graphmark/agentic-swebench
python3 - <<'"'"'PY'"'"'
import os,json,glob,re,collections,statistics as st
S=os.path.expanduser("~/pe1/graphmark/agentic-swebench")
GRAPH=re.compile(r"(?:^|[|;&`(]|&&|\|\|)\s*(?:\S*/)?(?:eg|eg-q)\s+|(?:^|[|;&`(])\s*entire\s+graph\b")
def isg(nm,inp):
    return nm in("Bash","bash") and bool(GRAPH.search((inp.get("command") or "")))
pos=[]; sess=[]
for cd in sorted(glob.glob(S+"/results/*_r1_eg")):
    for f in glob.glob(cd+"/ccfg/projects/*/*.jsonl"):
        seq=[]
        for ln in open(f,errors="ignore"):
            ln=ln.strip()
            if not ln: continue
            try: r=json.loads(ln)
            except Exception: continue
            if not isinstance(r,dict) or r.get("type")!="assistant": continue
            c=(r.get("message") or {}).get("content")
            if not isinstance(c,list): continue
            for b in c:
                if isinstance(b,dict) and b.get("type")=="tool_use":
                    seq.append(1 if isg(b.get("name",""),b.get("input") or {}) else 0)
        if not seq or not any(seq): continue
        n=len(seq); g=[i for i,x in enumerate(seq) if x]
        sess.append((n,g))
        for i in g: pos.append(i/max(n-1,1))
print("=== WHERE IN THE SESSION DOES THE GRAPH GET CALLED?  (%d sessions with >=1 call) ==="%len(sess))
q=sorted(pos)
print("  fraction-through-session of each graph call:")
print("    p10 %.2f  p25 %.2f  median %.2f  p75 %.2f  p90 %.2f"%(q[int(.1*len(q))],q[int(.25*len(q))],q[len(q)//2],q[int(.75*len(q))],q[int(.9*len(q))]))
print("  share of graph calls in the FIRST QUARTER of the session: %.1f%%"%(100*sum(1 for x in pos if x<.25)/len(pos)))
print("  share in the first 10 tool calls (absolute):            %.1f%%"%(100*sum(1 for n,g in sess for i in g if i<10)/sum(len(g) for n,g in sess)))
print("  first graph call: median absolute call index = %.0f"%st.median([g[0] for n,g in sess]))
print()
for K in (10,20,30):
    kept=sum(1 for n,g in sess for i in g if i>=K); tot=sum(len(g) for n,g in sess)
    fires=sum(1 for n,g in sess if any(i>=K for i in g))
    print("  gate: suppress graph until call %2d -> keeps %4.1f%% of graph calls, fires in %4.1f%% of sessions"%(K,100*kept/tot,100*fires/len(sess)))
print()
print("  NOTE: a late gate can only keep displacement that happens late. If most graph")
print("  calls are early, deferring the tool removes the benefit along with the toll.")

content.text:
That closes it, and cleanly:

```
where the graph actually gets called
  median graph call is 5% into the session
  80.4% of calls land in the first quarter
  76.5% land in the first 10 tool calls
  median index of the FIRST graph call = 1   (the very first thing the agent does)

gate: suppress until call 10 -> keeps 23.5% of graph calls
gate: suppress until call 20 -> keeps 14.1%
gate: suppress until call 30 -> keeps  9.4%
```

The agent's first tool call *is* a graph call. So deferring the tool until a session proves itself hard throws away 90% of its usage, and the displacement goes with the toll. The runtime version of your idea does not survive contact with where the calls actually happen.

So, both parts answered:

**What makes a winner or loser:** not the task. Savings has a test-retest correlation of +0.014 — the same instance wins in one cell and loses in the next. What makes a winner is that the baseline *happened* to flail on that run, and 63% of the win/loss separation is baseline-side variance. Mechanically the graph charges a fixed 2.65 calls and its benefit is displacement, which runs from −0.09 per call on easy runs to +5.53 on hard ones.

**"Graph only when needed":** the right instinct, and the highest-value direction anyone has measured here. A perfect difficulty oracle is worth +8.30%, and perfect hindsight is worth +16.92% — compare that with 6.9% from every payload lever stacked. The problem is purely that the signal does not exist at decision time: my pre-session features all came in under |r|=0.08, repo identity tests p=0.17, and a runtime gate arrives too late to matter.

One honest qualification, because it is the only door I found that is not closed: **46.1% of difficulty variance is genuinely task-level.** That is an upper bound on what any difficulty predictor could reach, and my hand-built features (issue length, stack traces, paths named, code blocks, repo) captured essentially none of it. A learned predictor over the issue text plus repo structure is not ruled out by anything I measured — it is just unbuilt. That would be a real project, not a config change, and its ceiling is 8.30%, not 15%.

Recording both results:

content.text:
Recorded in memory and in the notepad handoff.

The summary of where this leaves us:

**Losers are easy tasks, not broken tasks.** The graph opens the session with a query (median first graph call is tool call #1), pays 2.65 calls, and on the 40% of instances where the baseline finds the file in under 43 calls there is simply nothing for it to displace. Same tool, same behaviour, no bug: usage in losers is statistically identical to winners at p=0.9128.

**Your gating instinct is the best direction found in this campaign**, and I can now put a price on it: +8.30% with a perfect difficulty oracle, +16.92% with impossible hindsight, against 6.9% for every payload lever stacked together. It fails not on value but on information — savings has zero task-level signal (r=+0.014), every pre-session feature lands under |r|=0.08, and a runtime gate arrives after 90% of the graph calls have already happened.

The one thing I did not close, and I want to be precise rather than encouraging: 46.1% of *difficulty* variance is genuinely task-level, so a learned predictor over issue text and repo structure is not ruled out by any measurement I made. My hand-built features captured essentially none of it. That is a real modelling project with a hard ceiling of +8.30%, so it reaches your earlier 10% target only if paired with something else, and it does not reach 15% at all.

Two accounting notes so nothing here gets misquoted later: the +8.30% and +16.92% figures are conditioned on one arm's outcome, so they are upper bounds and not reportable results. And the honest unconditioned number at n=489 is pooled +3.52%, equal-weighted −6.64%, median −0.08%, win rate 49.9% — with correctness still ungraded per your rule.

Two computations decide whether a 10% plan can even be written. First: how accurate would a difficulty predictor have to be, given a perfect one is only worth 8.30%?

import os,json,glob,re,collections,statistics as st,math,random
S=os.path.expanduser("~/pe1/graphmark/agentic-swebench")

    if not pe or not pb: continue
    P.append({"d":(b["cost"]-v["cost"])/b["cost"],"cb":sum(pb.values()),
              "xe":v["cost"],"xb":b["cost"]})
XB=sum(p["xb"] for p in P); n=len(P)
cb=[p["cb"] for p in P]; mu,sd=st.mean(cb),st.pstdev(cb)
z=[(c-mu)/sd for c in cb]
def gate_val(pred,frac):
    # fire on the top `frac` by predicted difficulty
    idx=sorted(range(n),key=lambda i:-pred[i])[:int(frac*n)]
    fire=set(idx)
    xe=sum((P[i]["xe"] if i in fire else P[i]["xb"]) for i in range(n))

        vals=[]
        for seed in range(40):
            rnd=random.Random(1000+seed)
            pred=[rho*z[i]+math.sqrt(max(1-rho*rho,0))*rnd.gauss(0,1) for i in range(n)]
            vals.append(gate_val(pred,f))
        row.append(st.mean(vals))
    best[rho]=max(row)
    print("  %-6.1f"%rho, "".join("%+8.2f%%"%(v*100) for v in row))
print()
print("  best achievable by rho:")
for rho,v in best.items():
    print("    rho=%.1f -> %+.2f%%   %s"%(rho,v*100,"REACHES 10%" if v>=0.10 else ""))
need=[r for r,v in best.items() if v>=0.10]
print("  => 10%% from gating ALONE needs rho >= %s"%(("%.1f"%min(need)) if need else "IMPOSSIBLE at any rho (max %.2f%%)"%(max(best.values())*100)))

Decisive: **gating alone cannot reach 10% at any predictor accuracy.** Max is +8.29% at ρ=1.0, and since only 46.1% of difficulty variance is task-level, a perfect task-level predictor is capped at ρ=√0.461=0.68, which the table prices at **+6.4%**. At a realistic ρ=0.5 it is +5.14%.

So a 10% plan needs a second, independent lever worth 4 to 5 points. The one candidate I have never measured: the payload is 76% source body, and if the agent reads that file anyway the bytes are paid twice. Checking:

Everything above is **cost**; the campaign has also reported **tokens**, and they differ (+2.49% cost vs +3.39% tokens) because eg's savings concentrate in cheap cached prefix. I will not shop for the friendlier estimator, so let me measure both and put them side by side:

# Plan: resolution gateway — the only fair route to 20% graph savings

Written 2026-08-11, replacing the earlier 15%-stack plan (every lever in it is now closed by
measurement). All numbers below are mine, recomputed per-cell from REP30F (n=28) and HOLD50 (n=46).

## Context

The goal is 20%+ **graph** savings on rep50, fairly. Today's fair out-of-sample number is
**+2.49% cost / +3.39% tokens** (n=75, CI [-6.83,+11.18], median negative). Everything tried has
closed: per-loser fixes (+0.04pt symmetric), payload shape (refuted live by ER12), locate collapse
(measured 1.43:1), and prompt guidance (+75% but it is a PROMPT result, it costs the graph 23.8pt,
and it contradicts entire-graph's own shipped guide, which says "never trade resolution for fewer
turns").

The blocker was structural and I stated it as final: **a graph call is itself a message, so
displacing a grep never banks a whole message.** The resolution-gateway design from
`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-10-entire-graph-opus-30pct-resolution-gateway.md` breaks exactly that
blocker — inject a provenance-bound source packet **before turn 1**, with **no callable graph tool**.
The graph-call toll disappears, and any remaining locate/read activity is directly measurable as
failure to substitute.

Cross-check: the other agent's `PLAN-TO-35-OPUS.md` independently reports REP50X +2.89%
CI [-15.1,+18.4], Opus pool n=197 **-1.4%**, R50FIX +16.10% **withdrawn as in-sample**, and its own
verdict box says 35% is "not measured yet" with removability "unproven". Nobody has hit this. The
plans agree with my numbers; they differ only in believing the pool is removable.

## The arithmetic, measured (not assumed)

```
                                  REP30F        HOLD50
locate+read pool / session         28.29         33.70
displaceable by a turn-0 packet     7.68 (27.1%)  5.98 (17.7%)
   of which: before any payload     1.50          1.33   <- gateway covers these from msg 1
             matched to payload     6.18          4.65

projected DELTA over today (2-axis, each cell's own baseline):
   toll removal only              -0.36pt       -0.67pt   NEUTRAL
   at MEASURED displacement      +15.16pt      +11.11pt
   at 30% of pool                +16.72pt      +18.89pt
   at 50% of pool                +27.27pt      +30.95pt
```

Applying the **delta** (robust) to the measured fair base of +2.49%:

| displacement | projected fair saving |
|---|---|
| toll only | ~+2.5% (no change) |
| measured (17.7-27.1%) | **+13.6% … +17.7%** |
| 30% of pool | **~+21%** |
| 50% of pool | ~+30% |

**So 20% requires ~30% pool displacement. Measured removability is 17.7-27.1%.** The target sits just
above the top of the measured range — reachable only if a purpose-built packet beats what one
incidental `search` call happened to return. That is the whole bet, and it is a *design* bet, not a
hope: the 17.7% floor was produced by an arbitrary first payload of 2,583-3,180 B against an 8 KiB
budget, i.e. **2.6-3.2x unused headroom**.

## Design

`ResolutionEnvelopeV1`, built from the issue text + base tree before turn 1, capped at 8 KiB:
top-hit full body at real line numbers; a container map of that file (every member with line ranges,
so the agent never guesses a range); types/signatures the body references; call sites; and the
covering-test **path** (path only — a runnable command is build knowledge and fairness-struck).
Candidate arm gets the packet and **no graph verb**. Baseline arm unchanged.

Reuse, do not rewrite: `tools/eg-q` payload rendering, `published_exact_prompt()` for injection
(takes no `$arm`, so symmetry is structural), `logs/gw2.py` for the removability metric,
`logs/cost.py` + `logs/prices.py` for cost scoring, `logs/contam.sh` for patch hygiene.

## Fairness

Packet is **tool output**, contains no instructions, and a no-tool arm cannot obtain it — passes the
project rule ("would this sentence help an arm with no tool?"). It needs **no** `PROMPT_CLAMP_DECLARED`
because it ships no prescriptive text. Gate before scoring: `prompt_invariant` matches across arms
except the packet, baseline `tool_block.txt` stays 0 B, `grep -c VERIFY tools/eg-q` = 0.

## Stages

**S0. Offline packet simulation, $0.** Replay stored transcripts: build the envelope from the issue
+ tree, then count how many of each session's 28-34 locate+read calls it would have answered. Exit
bar: **>=30% of pool** on REP30F *and* HOLD50. If simulation cannot clear 30%, the 20% target is
arithmetically out of reach and I stop here rather than spend.

**S1. Build the envelope** behind `EG_GATEWAY=1`, default OFF. Verify by rendering, not by reading
source (the lesson from `BASE_FRUGAL` being dead code and my own cosmetic `ARTIFACT_EXCLUDES`).

**S2. Delivery smoke, n=4, ~$25.** Packet present in 4/4 candidate prompts, absent in 4/4 baseline,
zero graph verbs invoked, bytes <=8 KiB.

**S3. Mechanism cell, n=30, ~$180.** PRIMARY = `locate+read` calls/session vs REP30F's 28.29.
Prediction: falls >=30%. **Tokens are secondary and not claim-bearing.** This is the endpoint that
caught CS50's false +12.84%.

**S4. rep50 confirmation, n=50, ~$300**, only if S3's primary clears. Sealed prereg with the band
above written down first. Report pooled + median + cluster CI + the mechanism beside it.

**S5. Grade both arms** (`FAIL_TO_PASS`) on `graphbench-grade`. Removing the callable tool could cost
resolution; a token win with a resolution loss is not a win. Noninferiority within 3pt.

## Verification

`logs/cost.py` cost + `logs/contam.sh` (0 contaminated patches) + fairness gate before any number is
read; S5 resolved-rate both arms on identical instances.

## Honest assessment

**Floor ~+13.6%, target ~+21%, and the gap between them is one design question**: can a purpose-built
8 KiB envelope displace 30% of the locate+read pool when an incidental 3 KiB search payload already
displaces 17.7-27.1%? S0 answers that for $0, before any spend.

What would make me stop: S0 under 30%, or S3's call count not falling. And the honest risk is the
ER12 precedent — payload widening projected 2.11 displaced reads and delivered 0.42. The difference
this time is that the toll removal is structural rather than behavioural, and the pre-payload calls

# Plan: hit 10% graph token savings via a zero-toll difficulty gate

Written 2026-08-11. Replaces the 20% resolution-gateway plan, which its own S0 offline gate closed
(21-26% displacement measured against the 30% it required). Target metric is **pooled total tokens**
(user decision). Gate-as-product accepted (user decision).

## Context

The goal is 10% graph savings, fairly. Today, on 556 paired gated instances pooled across every cell
on disk: **tokens +6.22%, cost +4.61%** (median +2.35% / +2.78%, equal-weighted negative).

Why every previous plan failed, now measured rather than guessed:

```
graph calls/session          2.71        (transcript, cross-checked vs gq_calls.log 3.30)
other calls displaced        2.65
SUBSTITUTION RATIO           0.980       <- a 1:1 substitute removes no work by construction
net call reduction          -0.06/session
```

entire-graph swaps 2.65 shell calls for 2.71 graph calls. The +6.22% comes from the swapped calls
being cheaper, not from a shorter session. That single fact explains why eleven payload levers all
failed independent of their content, and why every lever stacked at *perfect* effectiveness tops out
at 6.9% cost.

The loss mechanism is not a defect. Split by how much the no-tool baseline flails:

```
baseline calls  eg calls  base calls  displacement  ratio/call  win rate   cost delta
    2-29          22.0       19.1        -0.25       -0.09       37.1%     -21.71%
   30-43          42.2       36.3        -3.25       -1.23       42.3%     -18.32%
   43-53          50.9       48.5        +0.25       +0.09       41.2%      -8.78%
   53-69          61.7       60.1        +1.05       +0.40       53.6%      -3.31%
  69-136          73.0       85.0       +14.65       +5.53       74.3%     +17.91%
```

Losers are **easy tasks**. The graph pays its 2.65-call toll and displaces nothing, because the
baseline found the file in 19 calls unaided. Graph usage in losers is statistically identical to
winners (2.68 vs 2.65, permutation **p=0.9128**) — there is no behaviour to repair, which is why
per-loser fixes measured +0.04pt. The two-axis model
(`1.31*ln(calls) + 0.49*ln(bytes)`) reproduces the **sign in all five bins**.

So the only lever with real headroom is **not paying the toll on easy tasks**.

## The arithmetic, and why this plan stops where it does

Noisy-oracle simulation (40 seeds per cell, gate fires on the top fraction by predicted difficulty),
where `rho` is the predictor's correlation with true baseline effort:

```
rho    fire20%   fire40%   fire60%   fire80%  fire100%
0.0     +0.92     +1.41     +2.07     +2.80     +3.53     (cost %)
0.5     +4.08     +5.14     +5.12     +4.58     +3.53
0.68    ~+5.2     +6.40     +5.7      +4.8      +3.53
1.0     +8.29     +7.51     +6.68     +4.45     +3.53
```

**Gating alone cannot reach 10% at any rho** (max +8.29% cost even with a perfect oracle). And rho is
itself capped: only **46.1%** of baseline-effort variance is task-level (test-retest r=+0.276 across
106 instances seen in 2+ cells), so a perfect task-level predictor is bounded at
rho = sqrt(0.461) = **0.68**.

Second, independent lever. The payload is 76.1% source body, and that body is sometimes paid twice:

```
files shown with a body in a payload   4.17/session
of those, agent LATER read the file    35.0%
lines shown that were re-read anyway   58.0%   -> 2,466 B/session of pure waste
```

Combining the two (independent mechanisms, tokens = 1.35x cost leverage measured on the same pairs):

| build | cost | tokens |
|---|---|---|
| today | +4.61% | +6.22% |
| gate rho=0.50 + body cap | +6.80% | +9.18% |
| **gate rho=0.60 + body cap** | **+7.50%** | **+10.13%** |
| gate rho=0.68 (max buildable) + body cap | +8.06% | +10.88% |
| perfect oracle + full body trim | +11.19% | +15.10% |

**The plan needs rho >= 0.60**, i.e. the predictor must capture (0.60/0.68)^2 = **78% of all
available task-level signal**. That is the whole bet and S0 tests it for $0.

## Design

**1. Zero-toll difficulty gate.** The gate must not cost an agent turn, or it eats its own margin
(one graph call on 60% of non-fired tasks is a 0.74pt drag). So it runs in the harness **before
turn 1**, consulting the graph index directly — never as a tool call.

Features, all computable pre-session from `problem.txt` plus one direct index query (no agent
message): the retrieval score distribution of the issue-derived query (top-1 score, top1-top5 gap,
score entropy over top-10, number of distinct files in the top-10, whether any symbol named in the
issue resolves in the index), plus repo scale (indexed symbol count, file count). The score
distribution is the load-bearing feature and it is the graph's own machinery: a sharply-peaked
ranking means the task is localizable, hence easy, hence the graph will not pay off.

Hand-built *text* features are already known dead and are not in this list: issue length r=-0.036,
lines -0.033, stack trace +0.014, paths named -0.028, code blocks +0.026, repo identity p=0.1676.

**2. Body cap, no prediction required.** Re-read files have disproportionately large spans (35% of
files but 58% of lines), so capping each shown body at N lines cuts preferentially from the wasted
ones. N is chosen in S0 by simulation, not guessed.

Files to modify:
- `tools/_eggate.py` (new) — feature extraction + fitted gate, mirroring the structure of the
  existing `tools/_eglit.py` / `tools/_egsiblings.py` helpers
- `tools/eg-q` — read `EG_GATE` / `EG_BODY_CAP`; the wrapper already has the `_grep_ctx` / `_fold_impact`
  fold points to hook into
- `tools/run_3arm.sh` — invoke the gate before the eg arm's first turn and, when it says "skip",
  emit the eg arm with an empty `tool_block.txt` (identical config to baseline)
- `logs/gatefit.py`, `logs/score_g10.py` (new scorers), reusing `logs/cost.py`, `logs/prices.py`,
  `logs/loserwhy.py`'s gate+pair loader, `logs/contam.sh` for patch hygiene

## Fairness

The gate reads only the issue text and the graph's own index, ships **no instructions**, and the
baseline arm is untouched. On non-fired tasks the eg arm runs with an empty tool block, i.e. the
identical configuration to baseline. Passes the project rule ("would this sentence help an arm with
no tool?" — there is no sentence). No `PROMPT_CLAMP_DECLARED` needed.

Pre-scoring gate, every cell: `prompt_invariant` matches across arms except the eg tool block;
baseline `tool_block.txt` is 0 B; `grep -c VERIFY tools/eg-q` = 0; `logs/contam.sh` reports 0
contaminated patches; reject any `CORRUPT_CC_OUT` record (a `GUIDE30B/baseline/gson-2479`-class
record passed both gates before).

**Mandatory disclosure in any writeup:** part of this gain is *avoided losses*, not added value, and
the tool declines to engage on ~60% of tasks. The headline must read "entire-graph with automatic
gating: tokens +X%, engaging on Y% of tasks".

## Stages

**S0. Offline feasibility, $0.** Fit the gate on the 556 existing pairs using only pre-session
features; report **cross-validated** rho against baseline effort (grouped CV by instance, so the
same instance never spans train and test). Simulate the body cap over stored payloads to pick N and
measure recovered bytes. Combine both through the two-axis model.
**Exit bar: projected tokens >= 10.0% at the cross-validated rho.** If rho < 0.60, stop and report
the shortfall with the number — do not spend.

**S1. Build**, both behind flags defaulting OFF. Verify by rendering an actual payload and an actual
prompt, never by reading source: `EG_LITERALS` and `EG_SIBLINGS` were silent no-ops in every cell
ever run because their helper files did not exist, and I shipped a cosmetic `ARTIFACT_EXCLUDES` array
that was never wired in.

**S2. Delivery smoke, n=4, ~$25.** Gate fires on 4/4 predicted-hard and 0/4 predicted-easy; the
skipped arm's `tool_block.txt` is 0 B; body cap present in rendered payloads; bytes <= budget.

**S3. Mechanism cell, n=30, ~$180.** PRIMARY endpoints, pre-registered, both arm-internal:
gate precision/recall against realized baseline effort, and eg payload bytes/session falling from
5,590 B. **Tokens are secondary and not claim-bearing at this stage** — this is the discipline that
caught CS50's false +12.84% (it scored positive while `locate_symbol` rose).

**S4. rep50 confirmation, n=50, ~$300**, only if S3's primary clears. Sealed prereg with the band
above written first. Report pooled **and** median **and** equal-weighted **and** cluster-bootstrap
CI, with the mechanism beside them, in both tokens and cost.

**S5. Grade both arms** (`FAIL_TO_PASS`), only after the 10% token bar is met, per the standing rule.
Withholding the tool on 60% of tasks could cost resolution; noninferiority within 3pt or the token
win does not count.

## Verification

Per stage: S0 grouped cross-validated rho printed with n and a permutation p-value; S2 assertions on
emitted `prompt.txt` and `tool_block.txt`; S3/S4 the fairness gate above runs **before** any number
is read, then `logs/score_g10.py` for mechanism and `logs/cost.py` for tokens and cost; S5 resolved
rate on identical instances both arms.

## Honest assessment

**Floor +9.18% tokens (rho=0.50), target +10.13% (rho=0.60), ceiling +10.88% (rho=0.68).** The 10%
bar sits *inside* this band but not at its floor, so this plan can fail honestly and I have written
the failure number down in advance.

Two named risks. First, rho: the predictor must capture 78% of available task-level signal, and
every hand-built feature I have tried captured essentially none — the entire bet rests on the
retrieval-score distribution carrying signal that text features do not. S0 settles it for $0.
Second, the ER12 precedent: payload widening projected 2.11 displaced reads and delivered 0.42, so
the body cap's simulated value should be treated as an upper bound.

What would make me stop and report instead of spending: S0's cross-validated rho below 0.60, or S3's
gate precision no better than chance. I am not promising 10%; I am committing to a pre-registered
shot at it with a $0 gate in front of the money, and to reporting the shortfall in the same terms if
it misses.

0.0     +0.92     +1.41     +2.07     +2.80     +3.53     (cost %)
0.5     +4.08     +5.14     +5.12     +4.58     +3.53
0.68    ~+5.2     +6.40     +5.7      +4.8      +3.53
1.0     +8.29     +7.51     +6.68     +4.45     +3.53
```

itself capped: only **46.1%** of baseline-effort variance is task-level (test-retest r=+0.276 across
106 instances seen in 2+ cells), so a perfect task-level predictor is bounded at
rho = sqrt(0.461) = **0.68**.

Second, independent lever. The payload is 76.1% source body, and that body is sometimes paid twice:

lines shown that were re-read anyway   58.0%   -> 2,466 B/session of pure waste

|---|---|---|

| gate rho=0.68 (max buildable) + body cap | +8.06% | +10.88% |
| perfect oracle + full body trim | +11.19% | +15.10% |

message): the retrieval score distribution of the issue-derived query (top-1 score, top1-top5 gap,

distribution is the load-bearing feature and it is the graph's own machinery: a sharply-peaked
ranking means the task is localizable, hence easy, hence the graph will not pay off.

Hand-built *text* features are already known dead and are not in this list: issue length r=-0.036,
lines -0.033, stack trace +0.014, paths named -0.028, code blocks +0.026, repo identity p=0.1676.

**2. Body cap, no prediction required.** Re-read files have disproportionately large spans (35% of
files but 58% of lines), so capping each shown body at N lines cuts preferentially from the wasted
ones. N is chosen in S0 by simulation, not guessed.

- `tools/_eggate.py` (new) — feature extraction + fitted gate, mirroring the structure of the
  existing `tools/_eglit.py` / `tools/_egsiblings.py` helpers
- `tools/eg-q` — read `EG_GATE` / `EG_BODY_CAP`; the wrapper already has the `_grep_ctx` / `_fold_impact`

- `tools/run_3arm.sh` — invoke the gate before the eg arm's first turn and, when it says "skip",

gating: tokens +X%, engaging on Y% of tasks".

the shortfall with the number — do not spend.

prompt, never by reading source: `EG_LITERALS` and `EG_SIBLINGS` were silent no-ops in every cell
ever run because their helper files did not exist, and I shipped a cosmetic `ARTIFACT_EXCLUDES` array
that was never wired in.

skipped arm's `tool_block.txt` is 0 B; body cap present in rendered payloads; bytes <= budget.

caught CS50's false +12.84% (it scored positive while `locate_symbol` rose).

caught CS50's false +12.84% (it scored positive while `locate_symbol` rose).

**S4. rep50 confirmation, n=50, ~$300**, only if S3's primary clears. Sealed prereg with the band
above written first. Report pooled **and** median **and** equal-weighted **and** cluster-bootstrap
CI, with the mechanism beside them, in both tokens and cost.

**S5. Grade both arms** (`FAIL_TO_PASS`), only after the 10% token bar is met, per the standing rule.
Withholding the tool on 60% of tasks could cost resolution; noninferiority within 3pt or the token
win does not count.

## Verification

Per stage: S0 grouped cross-validated rho printed with n and a permutation p-value; S2 assertions on
emitted `prompt.txt` and `tool_block.txt`; S3/S4 the fairness gate above runs **before** any number
is read, then `logs/score_g10.py` for mechanism and `logs/cost.py` for tokens and cost; S5 resolved
rate on identical instances both arms.

## Honest assessment

**Floor +9.18% tokens (rho=0.50), target +10.13% (rho=0.60), ceiling +10.88% (rho=0.68).** The 10%
bar sits *inside* this band but not at its floor, so this plan can fail honestly and I have written
the failure number down in advance.

Two named risks. First, rho: the predictor must capture 78% of available task-level signal, and
every hand-built feature I have tried captured essentially none — the entire bet rests on the
retrieval-score distribution carrying signal that text features do not. S0 settles it for $0.
Second, the ER12 precedent: payload widening projected 2.11 displaced reads and delivered 0.42, so
the body cap's simulated value should be treated as an upper bound.

What would make me stop and report instead of spending: S0's cross-validated rho below 0.60, or S3's
gate precision no better than chance. I am not promising 10%; I am committing to a pre-registered
shot at it with a $0 gate in front of the money, and to reporting the shortfall in the same terms if
it misses.

content.text:
Here is the plain answer to both questions.

## What makes a task a winner or a loser

Every task is a race between two runs of the same agent. One run has the graph, one does not. The graph costs about 2.65 extra tool calls per session, and it earns that back only by saving the other run's wasted searching. So the whole outcome comes down to one thing: **did the run without the graph waste any time?**

I sorted all 489 tasks by how much work the no-graph run needed:

| work the no-graph run needed | graph run | no-graph run | who wins | result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2 to 29 calls | 22.0 | 19.1 | graph loses | −21.7% |
| 30 to 43 | 42.2 | 36.3 | graph loses | −18.3% |
| 43 to 53 | 50.9 | 48.5 | roughly even | −8.8% |
| 53 to 69 | 61.7 | 60.1 | roughly even | −3.3% |
| 69 to 136 | 73.0 | 85.0 | graph wins | +17.9% |

Read the first row carefully, because it is the whole story. On easy tasks the no-graph run found the file in 19 calls. The graph run used 22. It ran its graph searches **and then still did all the same work anyway**, because there was nothing to skip. The graph got charged and delivered nothing, so it lost 21.7%.

Now the last row. Here the no-graph run flailed for 85 calls. The graph run finished in 73. Same tool, same behaviour, but this time there was 12 calls of wasted searching to prevent, so it won 17.9%.

**Losers are easy tasks. Winners are hard tasks.** Nothing is broken in the losers. I checked whether the graph behaves differently when it loses, and it does not: it makes 2.68 calls in winners and 2.65 in losers, which is a statistical dead heat. There is no bug in those sessions to fix. That is why all my attempts to repair the losers produced almost exactly zero.

The uncomfortable part: **whether a task is easy is mostly luck, not a property of the task.** I found 106 tasks that were run in more than one experiment. How hard a task turned out to be repeated only weakly between runs, and whether the graph won or lost did not repeat at all. Run the same task twice and it wins once, loses once. Slightly less than half of the "difficulty" is a real property of the task; the rest is the agent having a good or bad day.

## Your idea: only use the graph when needed

This is the right instinct, and it is the best idea anyone has had on this problem. I measured what it is worth by giving it a **perfect** crystal ball that already knows how hard each task will be:

| rule | savings | how often the graph fires |
|---|---|---|
| always use the graph | +3.5% | 100% |
| only if the task needs 29+ calls | +4.5% | 80% |
| only if 43+ | +6.6% | 59% |
| only if 53+ | +7.7% | 39% |
| only if 69+ | +8.3% | 20% |
| perfect hindsight, impossible | +16.9% | — |

So even with a perfect crystal ball the idea gives **8.3%**. That is a lot better than anything else I have tried, and it still does not reach 10% on its own.

Then there is the harder problem: building the crystal ball. Everything obvious fails. Issue length, whether the issue has an error trace, how many file names the issue mentions, how much code is in the issue, which repository it is: all of them are essentially uncorrelated with difficulty. The repository looked promising at first, with one repo at +6.8% and another at −25.1%, until I tested it and found that spread is exactly what you get from shuffling tasks into random groups.

I also tried the version that needs no crystal ball at all: just wait, and only turn the graph on once a session has clearly gone long. That fails for a simple reason. **The agent's very first tool call is usually a graph call**, and three quarters of all graph calls happen in the first ten calls. If you make the graph wait until call 30, you throw away 90% of its use, and the benefit leaves along with the cost.

## So how the plan reaches 10%

Gating alone tops out at 8.3%, so the plan pairs it with a second, unrelated saving. The graph's answer includes chunks of source code, and I measured that in 35% of cases the agent goes and reads that same file anyway. Those bytes get paid for twice. Trimming that waste is worth another 1.7%.

Gate plus trim comes to about 8.1% in dollars and **10.9% in tokens**, which is why you chose tokens as the measure. The gap between the two is real and I will keep stating both: the graph's savings sit mostly in cheap cached text, so it saves more raw tokens than dollars.

The one thing that has to be true, and which I am testing right now for zero dollars before spending anything: the crystal ball has to work. Not perfectly, but it has to reach about 60% of perfect. My plan is to build it from the graph's own search scores rather than from the issue text, on the theory that when the graph's top result stands out sharply from the rest, the task is easy to locate and the graph will not pay off. That test is running now. If it comes back too weak, I will tell you the number and stop rather than spend $500 on a run I already know will miss.

content.text:
S0 fails its exit bar, and the reason matters. Out-of-fold rho = **+0.193** against the 0.60 required, and the fitted gate is worth *less than no gate at all* (firing on 60% gives +4.18% tokens versus +4.49% for always firing).

Look at which features carried the signal: `is_search` (+0.302), `nscore` (+0.225), `ent` (+0.198). Those are not task properties — they describe **which verb the agent chose first**, which is leakage from agent behaviour and is not available before turn 1 anyway. The score features the plan was betting on came in at top1 +0.099 and gap +0.012.

But there is a confound I should rule out before declaring failure: scores exist in only 34% of payloads, so `top1`/`gap`/`ent` are zero-filled for two thirds of rows, which would crush their correlation. Testing on the subset where scores actually exist:

input.command:
gcloud compute ssh graphbench-c --zone us-east1-b --tunnel-through-iap --command '
S=$HOME/pe1/graphmark/agentic-swebench
python3 - <<'"'"'PY'"'"'
import os,re,statistics as st,random,math
src=open(os.path.expanduser("~/pe1/graphmark/agentic-swebench/logs/s0fit.py")).read()
exec(src.split("print(f\"=== S0 DATA")[0])
# rows[] is built. Restrict to rows whose FIRST payload actually carried a ranked list.
sub=[r for r in rows if r["F"]["nscore"]>=5]
print("=== S0b: SEARCH-ONLY SUBSET (first payload carried a ranked list) ===")
print("  n = %d of %d rows"%(len(sub),len(rows)))
if len(sub)<60:
    print("  too few rows to cross-validate honestly; stopping"); raise SystemExit
def pear(a,b):
    n=len(a); ma,mb=st.mean(a),st.mean(b); sa,sb=st.pstdev(a),st.pstdev(b)
    if sa==0 or sb==0: return 0.0
    return sum((x-ma)*(y-mb) for x,y in zip(a,b))/(n*sa*sb)
SK=["top1","gap","ent","nscore","nfiles","concentration","nlines","bytes","ilen","itrace","ipaths","icode"]
Y=[r["y"] for r in sub]
print("\n  univariate r vs baseline effort, on rows where scores EXIST:")
for k in SK: print("    %-14s r=%+.3f"%(k,pear([r["F"][k] for r in sub],Y)))
def solve(A,b):
    n=len(A); M=[row[:]+[b[i]] for i,row in enumerate(A)]
    for i in range(n):
        p=max(range(i,n),key=lambda r:abs(M[r][i]))
        if abs(M[p][i])<1e-12: continue
        M[i],M[p]=M[p],M[i]
        for r in range(n):
            if r==i: continue
            f=M[r][i]/M[i][i]
            for c in range(i,n+1): M[r][c]-=f*M[i][c]
    return [M[i][n]/M[i][i] if abs(M[i][i])>1e-12 else 0.0 for i in range(n)]
def cv(keys,lams=(10.,50.,200.,1000.)):
    insts=sorted({r["inst"] for r in sub}); rnd=random.Random(99); rnd.shuffle(insts)
    F={x:i%5 for i,x in enumerate(insts)}
    best=-9
    for lam in lams:
        oof=[None]*len(sub)
        for k in range(5):
            tr=[r for r in sub if F[r["inst"]]!=k]; te=[i for i,r in enumerate(sub) if F[r["inst"]]==k]
            if len(tr)<20 or not te: continue
            mu={q:st.mean([r["F"][q] for r in tr]) for q in keys}
            sd={q:(st.pstdev([r["F"][q] for r in tr]) or 1.) for q in keys}
            X=[[1.]+[(r["F"][q]-mu[q])/sd[q] for q in keys] for r in tr]; y=[r["y"] for r in tr]; p=len(keys)+1
            A=[[sum(X[i][a]*X[i][b] for i in range(len(X)))+(lam if a==b and a>0 else 0.) for b in range(p)] for a in range(p)]
            bb=[sum(X[i][a]*y[i] for i in range(len(X))) for a in range(p)]
            w=solve(A,bb)
            for i in te: oof[i]=w[0]+sum(w[j+1]*((sub[i]["F"][q]-mu[q])/sd[q]) for j,q in enumerate(keys))
        ok=[i for i,v in enumerate(oof) if v is not None]
        if len(ok)<40: continue
        r_=pear([oof[i] for i in ok],[sub[i]["y"] for i in ok])
        if r_>best: best=r_; bo=oof
    return best,bo
r1,o1=cv(SK)
r2,o2=cv(["top1","gap","ent","nscore","concentration"])
print("\n  grouped-CV rho, all features        = %+.3f"%r1)

content.description:
Blocking work before the 300x4 Gemini cell. Do NOT install toolchains while SMOKER12 is live (agents probe for go/cargo/bundle mid-session; installing under a running cell contaminates it).

1a. INSTALL MISSING TOOLCHAINS on graphbench-c: go, cargo/rustc, bundle(ruby), pytest, dotnet.
    Why: 129/300 of multilingual_300 (Rust 43 + Go 42 + Ruby 44) cannot run their own tests; env/build is 19.26 calls/session = 35% of a session, symmetric across arms. This is H4 from the plan: it does not change the ratio, it strips ~12 calls/session of noise from BOTH arms and shrinks the +-13pt CI that makes 3%/9%/13%/16% indistinguishable.
    Verify: `command -v go cargo rustc pytest bundle` all resolve; re-run logs/toolchain.py and confirm the MISSING count drops to 0.

1b. WRITE run_quad.sh — 4-arm driver (baseline, eg, cmm, graphify) carrying run_paired.sh's guards:
    - PKG_ISO per-arm FATAL check
    - /tmp purge decline -> FATAL (the patched behaviour)
    - half-complete tuple -> results/<TAG>_r1.unpaired.txt + QUAD_STRICT=1 refuses
    - prompt_invariant.sha256 compared unconditionally, missing = FATAL
    - harness exit code checked (exit 2 stops the cell)
    - **ARM ORDER ROTATION** by instance index (Latin-square / rotate by _idx % 4). Without this, arm 4 always gets the warmest machine state and the 4-arm result is uninterpretable. run_matrix.sh/run_ladder.sh do fixed-order sweeps and lack run_3arm.sh's protections - do NOT use them.

1c. GEMINI PATH: CC_AGENT=gemini, MODEL=gemini-3.6-flash, max effort. Set maxSessionTurns IDENTICALLY for all 4 arms (Gemini has no --max-turns; an uncapped arm voids the comparison). Note the harness's own caveat: Gemini reports cache_creation=0 (no cache-write class), so its numbers are a self-contained 4-arm comparison, NOT comparable to the Claude cells.

Files: tools/run_quad.sh (new), tools/run_3arm.sh:2984+ (gemini branch), logs/toolchain.py (verifier).

2026-08-11. The pre-registered S0 gate on the 10%-token plan. **FAILED, $0 spent, ~$505 saved.**
Scorer `logs/s0fit.py`.

## Gate: rho +0.193 against a 0.60 bar

```
variant                                          n     grouped-CV rho
first graph payload, all features              474        +0.193
first payload, search-only (has ranked list)      2        unusable
first score-bearing payload anywhere (optimistic) 350     +0.142 (score feats) / +0.011 (all)
```
Folds split by INSTANCE so the same instance never spans train and test. Permutation p=0.0000, so
the +0.193 is real but far too small.

**Value of the ACTUAL fitted gate (not a simulation):**
```
fire on   20%    40%    60%    80%   100%
tokens  +2.17  +2.64  +4.18  +3.66  +4.49
```
Gating is WORSE than always-on at every rate except a +0.10pt sliver on the optimistic subset
(+6.16 vs +6.06). The gate does not work.

## What the features said

The top-1 signal was **leakage, not a task property**: `is_search` r=+0.302, `nscore` +0.225,
`ent` +0.198 all describe WHICH VERB the agent chose first -- unavailable before turn 1. The score
features had the **sign the design predicted** (`top1` r=-0.164, `ratio` -0.144: a sharply-peaked
ranking does mean an easy task) but 0.16 is not 0.60. All issue-text features stayed under |0.10|.

## Body cap: my own plan over-counted it 6x

```
cap each body at N lines:  N=10 -> +1.13% tokens (cuts 22.8% of payload, WOULD force reads)
                           N=40 -> +0.39%    N=80 -> +0.11%
dedupe only (file shown twice; needs no prediction, cannot force a read): +0.38% tokens
```
The plan's "+1.66% cost / +2.24% tokens" came from the 2,466 B/session of bodies that were re-read
anyway -- but identifying those in advance is **another prediction problem**. The genuinely free
subset is 420 B/session = **+0.38% tokens**. I counted a prediction-dependent quantity as free.

## Honest total

```
today (n=556)          tokens +6.22%   cost +4.61%
+ best gate            +0.10pt
+ dedupe               +0.38pt
TOTAL                  ~+6.7% tokens
```

**How to apply:** the 10% token target is not reachable by gating. Before proposing any predictor,
state its cross-validated rho on held-out INSTANCES and check the top features are not
agent-behaviour leakage. Before crediting a payload trim, check the bytes are identifiable without
prediction. Related: [[gating-ceiling-is-8-3-percent]], [[losers-lose-on-easy-instances]],
[[graph-is-a-1to1-substitute]], [[instance-identity-predicts-nothing]].

content.text:
S0 did its job: it cost nothing and stopped a $505 spend. The result, plainly:

**The gate fails.** Cross-validated rho is **+0.193** against the 0.60 the plan required, folds split by instance. The fitted gate is worth **+0.10 percentage points** over just always using the graph. The features that carried signal turned out to be leakage — `is_search` (+0.302) describes which verb the agent picked first, which is not knowable before turn 1. The retrieval-score features had exactly the sign my design predicted (`top1` −0.164: a sharply-peaked ranking does mean an easy task) but at a quarter of the needed strength.

**And S0 caught an error in my own plan.** I credited the body trim at +1.66% cost / +2.24% tokens. That figure came from the 2,466 B/session of source bodies the agent re-read anyway — but knowing *which* bodies those are in advance is another prediction problem, so I had counted a prediction-dependent quantity as free. The genuinely free subset is bodies shown twice for the same file: 420 B/session, worth **+0.38% tokens**. Capping bodies harder does cut more (+1.13% at 10 lines) but removes 22.8% of the payload and would force the reads it was meant to prevent.

```
honest total for the approved plan
  today (n=556)     tokens +6.22%    cost +4.61%
  + best gate               +0.10pt
  + safe dedupe             +0.38pt
  TOTAL                    ~+6.7% tokens      <- against a 10% target
```

**G1 also finished** — 24/24, 10 gated pairs: cost **−9.50%**, tokens **−8.59%**. The isolated grep-source-fold lever lost. At n=10 that sits inside my measured noise floor of ~8.6% between identical cells, so it is not conclusive, but nothing about it supports the lever.

So the approved route does not reach 10%, and I am reporting that rather than running S1 through S4 into a wall I can already see.

That leaves exactly one option with enough headroom, and now that tokens is the agreed metric the arithmetic changed in its favour: **routing shell `grep` through the graph**. Intercepted commands pay no message toll, which lifts graph-touched calls from 2.71 to about 14.6 per session — the only denominator large enough to matter. It computes to roughly +9.6% cost, which at the measured 1.35x token leverage is about **+13% tokens**. That clears 10%.

The single blocker has never been fairness — the shim ships no instructions and the baseline keeps real grep, so it passes the project rule. It is that the saving would belong to "Entire-backed grep" rather than "the code graph," and the other agent's plan lists the shim under do-not-ship for that reason. You accepted gate-as-product on the same kind of reasoning, so I think you may well accept this one, but it changes what the headline claims and I will not relabel the product on my own.

Say the word and I will write the prereg for it with the honest label and run it. Everything else I have measured is closed.

content.text: Proceeding with the shim. But before I spend anything, the same $0 discipline applies — and there is a number in my own +9.6% estimate I never audited. I derived it from the message axis alone, assuming each intercepted grep displaces about one call. My own measurements say the displaceable pool is much smaller than that, and graph output may be **fatter** than raw grep output, which would cost bytes. Auditing both sides first:

egb=B[("eg","eg:grep")]/max(N[("eg","eg:grep")],1)
nsh=N[("eg","sh:grep")]/ne
print()
print("  a shim replaces %.2f shell greps/session at %.0f B with graph-grep at %.0f B"%(nsh,shb,egb))
delta=(egb-shb)*nsh
TOT=74138.0

print()
print("=== MESSAGE-AXIS BENEFIT, bounded by MEASURED pools ===")

print()

content.text:
The shim audit changes the picture in an important way, and it is better than I said. Note that the byte cost is small (graph-grep is 1,286 B/call vs shell grep's 1,146 B, so only −1.33%), but the displaceable pool I used as the bound excludes the biggest piece:

```
shim intercepts        14.56 shell greps/session at 1,146 B
replaced with          graph-grep at 1,286 B  ->  byte axis only -1.33% cost
displaceable pool I bounded it with:
  fixable refinements   0.87
  grep -> follow-up read 1.95
  TOTAL                 2.82   -> even at PERFECT effectiveness only +6.16% cost
```

That 2.82 bound **deliberately excludes the 3.43 wrong-guess greps per session** — the 62% of refinements where the agent tried a completely different string. I excluded them because better output for a *wrong pattern* cannot help. But a graph-backed grep is exactly the thing that can answer a wrong pattern, by falling back to semantically related symbols when the literal match misses. Include that pool and the projection clears 10% tokens even at 20% realisation.

So the whole decision rests on one untested assumption. Testing it for $0 — when the agent's literal guess missed, did the graph already know the file the agent eventually needed?

Design decision from that: the shim will be a **pure passthrough on a match** and only write to **stderr on a literal miss**, so stdout and exit codes stay byte-identical and no build script can break. That also targets the measured mechanism exactly, since a wrong guess is a literal miss.

But that makes the trigger rate critical: if few greps actually return nothing, the shim rarely fires. Measuring it before I write code:

content.text:
S0g kills the shim, and it does so by exposing the flaw in my own projection. The number that matters:

```
shell/Grep calls                       14.81/session
  returned effectively NOTHING          1.34/session  (9.1%)
  machine-parsing mode (-q/-c/-l/-o)    2.26/session  (shim must stay silent)
  SHIM WOULD SAFELY FIRE                1.07/session  (7.2%)

wrong-guess transitions                 6,043
  where the PRIOR grep was EMPTY        520  (8.6%)
```

**Only 8.6% of wrong guesses follow a grep that returned nothing.** The other 91.4% follow a grep that *did* return hits — the agent got results, they were not useful, so it tried a different string. So a safe miss-only trigger reaches **0.18 calls/session** of the 2.09 addressable pool, worth +0.19 to +0.33 points. Against the 643 B/session of hint text, that nets to roughly zero or slightly negative.

And the `literal only` rows in that table are not reachable by this design either. That pool (0.87 fixable refinements plus 1.95 grep-then-read) consists entirely of greps that **succeeded** — you read the file your grep just found. A miss-only shim never fires on them. To capture them the shim would have to rewrite the output of *successful* greps, which is both the build-breaking design and the one thing already measured: G1's source fold did exactly that and came back **−9.50%**.

So the shim fails S0 too. My +9.6% estimate assumed every intercepted grep displaces work; the audit shows the displaceable events almost never coincide with a condition it is safe to trigger on.

I had credited it at +2.24% tokens using the 2,466 B/session of bodies the agent re-read anyway, but identifying those in advance is another prediction problem, so I had counted a prediction-dependent quantity as free. The genuinely free part is **+0.38%**.

Then the trigger audit: **91.4% of wrong guesses follow a grep that returned hits**, not one that missed. A shim can only be made safe by firing on a miss, so it reaches 0.18 of the 2.09 addressable calls per session, which nets to zero or slightly negative after its own 643 B of hint text. # AGENTS.md — operating guide for coding agents

Hand this to any coding agent working in a repo where the `entire graph` plugin
is installed. It moves initial code-location work from broad grep/read
exploration to targeted graph queries; token impact depends on the task and
model, and no end-to-end savings claim is current.

## What this gives you

A precomputed, **deterministic** code graph is available through the `entire graph` command — functions, classes, methods, types, routes, and the calls/inheritance/field/service relations between them, parsed with tree-sitter, 100% locally (no network, no model, no keys). Use it to **LOCATE** and **UNDERSTAND** code *before* broad grep / find / cat / whole-file exploration. Every command is no-egress and safe to run inside a sandboxed session. The same commit yields the same graph, but static relations can be heuristic or incomplete; inspect focused source and verify the resulting change.

Default flags to remember: pass `--repo .` when you're not inside an Entire session; the graph reads your **working tree by default** (your uncommitted edits are visible), and `--head` switches to committed-tree semantics with a cached, reusable index.

---

## The parts of the graph

Reach for the smallest tool that answers your question.

### 🔍 search — *find the code for a task* (your first move)
Ranked source regions for a plain-language description, with the source and `file:line` inline. Hybrid ranking over bodies, identifiers (camelCase/snake_case aware), signatures, paths, and graph neighbors. Output is budgeted (16 KiB by default) to drop straight into context.

```sh
entire graph search --repo . --query "<the task or bug in one plain sentence>" --format text --top-k 8
```

- `--format agent` for compact ranked output with latency telemetry; `json`/`ndjson` for the full schema (completeness, partial failures, diagnostics).
- `--top-k N` result count; `--max-context-bytes N` byte budget (`0` = unbounded).
- Working tree by default; add `--head` for committed-tree + cache reuse.
- `--profile syntax-only|fast|full` (default `fast`); `--index-all-files` or `--max-indexed-files N` to widen/bound cold-search parsing.

**When:** the start of essentially every task. One good query lands you on the fix area.

### 🕸️ neighbors — *who calls this / what does it call* (targeted relations)
Direct incoming/outgoing relations for **one** symbol, with definition locations, plus bounded two-hop paths at `--depth 2`. For the full blast radius of a change, prefer `impact`; use `neighbors` when you want one specific relation/direction. Never `edges` for this (full stream).

```sh
entire graph neighbors --repo . --symbol NAME --relation CALLS --direction in   # who calls NAME
entire graph neighbors --repo . --symbol NAME --relation CALLS --direction out  # what NAME calls
```

- `--file path` — **required** when the symbol name is ambiguous (multiple defs); the graph returns definitions only until you disambiguate.
- `--relation CALLS` (default is the call family) — pick another relation to follow it instead.
- `--direction both|in|out`, `--depth 1|2`, `--limit N`.
- `--internal-only` drops unresolved external endpoints; `--exclude-tests` drops test-only neighbors.
- `--format agent|text|json`; `--head` for cached committed-tree; `--profile fast` for shallow call resolution (default `full` favors correctness).

**When:** "what breaks if I change X", "who uses this", tracing a call chain — after search has given you a concrete symbol name.

### 💥 impact — *one-shot blast radius for a change*
Everything the graph knows about changing **one** symbol, in a single bounded explanation: direct + transitive callers (depth ≤ 2), callees, type consumers (`USES_TYPE`/`PARAM_TYPE`/`RETURNS_TYPE`), data flows, files that historically change together with the symbol's file, and same-container siblings. Text output is sectioned, `file:line` per entry, capped per section and ~4 KB total.

```sh
entire graph impact --repo . --symbol NAME [--file path] [--depth 1|2] [--format text|json]
```

- Ambiguous names return the definition list — rerun with `--file` to pick one.
- `--depth` 1|2 (default: 2); `--limit N` per-section entry cap; `--max-context-bytes N` total text budget; `--exclude-tests`; `--head` / `--profile` as in `neighbors`.

**When:** before changing behavior of a specific function/type — "you're changing ordering: here is every place results are ordered, limited, or consumed downstream" — one command instead of chaining neighbors + edges + git log.

### 📇 symbols — *definitions*
Full stream of symbol records (stable `compound-v1` ID, kind, qualified name, source range, signature, language, container). This is a **bulk NDJSON stream of the whole repo**, filtered to the symbol record type — there is **no positional name argument** and no server-side name filter; grep the stream client-side, or prefer `search`/`neighbors` for a targeted single-symbol lookup.

```sh
entire graph symbols --repo . --format ndjson [--worktree]
```

**When:** you need the complete definition inventory (e.g. ingesting into a store), not a single lookup.

### 🔗 edges — *relations*
Full stream of relation records across all 30 types (`CALLS`, `IMPORTS`, `EXTENDS`, `HANDLES_ROUTE`, …), each tagged with resolution and confidence. The stream is whole-repo by default; `--to`, `--from`, and `--relation` filter it server-side. For one symbol's callers/callees, prefer `neighbors` because it annotates resolved definitions and call sites from source.

```sh
entire graph edges --repo . --format ndjson [--worktree] [--to ID|NAME] [--from ID|NAME] [--relation TYPE[,TYPE...]]
```

**When:** you want every relation (bulk export / ingestion) or a filtered relation stream. For a targeted one-symbol question, use `neighbors`.

### 🗺️ snapshot — *the whole graph*
One header record, then file, external-endpoint, symbol, and relation records, streamed so memory stays bounded. Superset of `symbols` + `edges` + files.

```sh
entire graph snapshot --repo . --format ndjson [--worktree]
```

**When:** ingesting the full graph into agent memory or a store such as Entire Brain.

### 🧬 diff / analyze / commit / checkpoint — *what changed + risk*
Entity-level change list (added / removed / renamed / signature-changed / body-changed) with a heuristic **dependent count**, so a signature change with many dependents stands out.

```sh
entire graph commit HEAD --json                     # a commit vs its first parent
entire graph diff --base main --head HEAD --json    # between two refs (analyze is an alias)
entire graph checkpoint <id> --json                 # the commit behind an Entire-Checkpoint trailer
```

**When:** judging whether a change is safe to keep / revert / continue, or reviewing a branch/PR. High dependent counts on a signature change = run tests first.

### 🏗️ index — *build / warm the cache*
Prebuilds the durable, query-independent committed-tree index and verifies it was written, before latency-sensitive work.

```sh
entire graph index --repo . --head --profile full --cache-dir /path/to/cache --format json
```

**When:** once, up front, on a large repo before a batch of `--head` searches/neighbors queries. Re-running it is also how you "refresh" a committed-tree cache — same tree hits, changed tree rebuilds.

### 🧭 capabilities / doctor / version — *feature-detect*
```sh
entire graph capabilities --json    # semantic vs inventory-only languages, relation types, features
entire graph doctor --json          # environment, repo resolution, no_egress=true
entire graph version [--json]       # provider name + plugin version
```

**When:** before assuming a language is semantically parsed, or to confirm the no-egress environment.

### 📊 stats — *did the graph actually save anything?* (for humans, not for you)
```sh
entire graph stats --repo . [--since 30d|7d|all] [--format text|json] [--sessions-dir path|--transcript path]
```

Local, read-only report over the coding-agent session transcripts already on disk
(`~/.claude/projects/<path-slug>/*.jsonl`; `--sessions-dir` overrides the lookup). Reports graph
calls per verb vs. exploration calls (`Read` whole-file / `Read` line-range / `Grep` / `Glob` /
shell `grep|find|cat|head|tail|sed|awk`), the bytes each path pulled into context, billed session
tokens read from transcript `usage`, a graph-first rate (share of sessions whose first locate-ish
tool call was a graph call), and an **estimated** token saving. The savings model is an explicit
assumption printed next to the number: each `search`/`neighbors`/`impact` call is credited with the
one whole-file read it replaced — on-disk size of the top-hit file it pointed at (repo median
tracked-file size when unresolvable) minus the bytes that call returned, floored at 0, at 4 bytes =
1 token. It is not a measured counterfactual. No network, no writes. `--transcript <path>` narrows
the whole report to one session (that transcript plus its `<session>/subagents/*.jsonl`), which is
what `scripts/entire-graph-statusline.sh` renders as a live Claude Code status line badge.

**When:** a human asks what the graph is buying them. Agents should not run it as part of a coding task.

---

## Resolution-first agent prompt (copy-paste this)

The former “measured-best” early-stop prompt and its 54.9%/57.7% token claims
are withdrawn. It optimized token use without preserving resolution parity and
could reward a cheap wrong patch. Use this correctness-first guidance instead;
substitute your search invocation for `<search-cmd>`:

```text
A precomputed code-search tool is available: <search-cmd> . Use it to LOCATE the fix BEFORE any
grep/find. Your FIRST action must be ONE search:
  <search-cmd> "<the bug in one sentence>"   <-- ranked relevant code (file:line + source)
Then open the top hit's file with your native Read tool (pass a line range around the reported
line), inspect enough surrounding behavior to justify the change, and make the smallest complete
edit. Treat graph output as evidence, not an oracle. Check callers/impact when the change can affect
other sites. If the result prints a `VERIFY:` line, run that exact command after editing before
claiming the task is done; it may be a per-file command or a whole-suite fallback when no narrow
command can be derived. Never report that tests pass without executing the command. If verification
cannot be run, state why and perform a bounded source-level check. Optimize turns only after
correctness.
```

For bug-fix/locate tasks, run search at `--profile full` (call-graph expansion active) with default
text output (tiered: full snippet for the top hits, terse locators after). Prefer
targeted follow-up queries over whole-graph dumps, but use the graph and source
checks needed to make and verify a complete fix.

## Operating doctrine

1. **Search first for location tasks.** Start with one `entire graph search --query "<task>"` before broad grep/find exploration.
2. **Treat results as evidence, not truth.** Read focused source around the result and widen the check when behavior, aliases, generated code, or dynamic dispatch could matter.
3. **Use graph follow-ups when they answer a real question.** `impact`, `callers`, and `neighbors` are appropriate for blast radius and related-site checks; avoid exploratory whole-graph dumps.
4. **Make the smallest complete change.** Check sibling sites and contracts when the task implies them.
5. **Verify before stopping.** Run the `VERIFY:` command when search prints one; it may be a whole-suite fallback when no narrow command exists. Never report that tests pass without having run them. If execution is unavailable, perform a bounded source-level verification and disclose the limitation.
6. **Optimize context after correctness.** Prefer precise queries and line ranges, but never trade resolution for fewer turns.
7. **Feature-detect before you trust.** If a language might be inventory-only, check `capabilities --json` first — inventory-only files have file records but no semantic relations.

Quick mental model:

```text
locate  →  entire graph search --query "..."          (ranked code + file:line)
impact  →  entire graph impact --symbol X              (one-shot blast radius: callers, types, data flow, co-change)
callers →  entire graph neighbors --symbol X ...       (targeted callers/callees of X)
change  →  entire graph diff --base A --head B          (entity-level, with dependents)
ingest  →  entire graph snapshot --format ndjson        (whole graph)
report  →  entire graph stats --repo .                  (human-facing: graph vs grep/read usage + estimated token savings)
```

---

## Working on entire-graph itself

If your task is modifying this repository (not just using it), the build/test surface is in `mise.toml`:

```sh
mise run build   # go build -o entire-graph ./cmd/entire-graph  (needs CGO for tree-sitter)
mise run test    # go test ./...
mise run check   # fmt + vet + race tests + build
```

Contract rules that must not break: schema `1.x` is frozen and additive-only (`docs/adr/0001-ga-schema-contract.md`); the provider is **no-egress** (never add remote fetches, hosted API calls, telemetry, or runtime grammar downloads); `compound-v1` symbol IDs must stay stable across ordinary edits; unsupported/unparseable files must surface as machine-readable partial failures, never silent drops. All logic lives under `internal/` (`sem` = parsing/graph/search, `cli` = hand-rolled dispatch, `gitutil` = git subprocess); `cmd/entire-graph/main.go` is a thin entry point. The plugin manifest (`entire-plugin.yml`) registers the subcommand `graph`, so users type `entire graph ...`. This project was **previously named `entire-sem`** — do not reintroduce the old name. **Entire Brain** (`entire-brain`) is the separate downstream consumer of this provider's NDJSON — not an old name for this project.

This repo has the entire-graph code graph installed. Before exploring code with
grep/find/whole-file reads, read .entire/graph-agent.md — the search-first, verify-once
doctrine for coding agents: search instead of grepping, then check the sibling sites and
compile (or run the nearest existing test) once before you finish.

gh pr create --repo entireio/entire-graph --base main --head fix/worktree-cache-untracked-noise \
 --title "fix(cache): stop unindexable untracked files disabling the search cache" --body "$(cat <<'BODY'
## What

`worktreeSnapshotCacheable` required a **wholly pristine** working tree before it would reuse a tree-keyed index. It asked `WorktreeMatchesHEAD`, which is a plain `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all` compared against empty output. So a single file no parser ever opens — a `.DS_Store`, a compiled binary, a log, an editor swap file — disabled the search cache for the **entire repository**, and every query re-indexed from scratch.

A path that cannot contribute a symbol or a relation cannot make a snapshot stale, so it is not a reason to throw one away.

## Measured, on this repo

```
with a .DS_Store present
  run 1: cache_hit=False  index_ms=3704   total_ms=4480
  run 2: cache_hit=True   index_ms=131    total_ms=908
  run 3: cache_hit=True   index_ms=126    total_ms=887

control, untracked .go present (must NOT cache)
  run 1: cache_hit=False  index_ms=3598
  run 2: cache_hit=False  index_ms=3675
```

28x on index latency, 5x on total, and the control still bypasses correctly. Before the change the first case behaved like the control: never cached. On the working checkout this was `index_cache_hit=false` with `index_latency_ms=9062` on a back-to-back repeat of the same query.

## How

- `gitutil` gains **`WorktreeDirtyPaths`**, the factual list of paths that diverge from HEAD. `WorktreeMatchesHEAD` becomes `len(paths)==0` and keeps its exact contract, so its existing callers and tests are unaffected. Both sides of a rename are reported, since porcelain `-z` spends a second record on the source path and that record has no status prefix of its own.
- `worktreeSnapshotCacheable` forgives a dirty path only when **`extensionUnsupported`** says so — the same predicate the indexer uses to skip a file, so the two cannot disagree about what is read.

## Why this is safe

- **Conservative on extensionless paths.** `extensionUnsupported` treats them as supported, because a shebang can make one a script. A stray binary named `entire-graph` (no extension) therefore still bypasses the cache. That is deliberate, and asserted in a test.
- **Per-path, not a blanket "ignore untracked".** One indexable untracked file still bypasses, even alongside four unindexable ones.
- **`.gitignore` edits are forgiven, and that is sound.** Ignore rules can only change whether *untracked* files are walked, and an untracked file that is indexable already fails the gate on its own. So no combination of ignore-rule change plus untracked file can serve a stale snapshot.
- **Ignored files were already out of scope** — git omits them without `--ignored`, matching the provider's working-tree walk.

## Tests

- `TestWorktreeDirtyPaths` — clean / untracked / modified / **renamed (both paths)** / ignored, and asserts `WorktreeMatchesHEAD == (len(paths)==0)` in every case.
- `TestWorktreeSnapshotStillCachesWithUnindexableUntrackedFiles` — four unindexable untracked files keep the cache warm with an **identical symbol set**; an extensionless file still bypasses; an untracked `.go` still bypasses and is still indexed.
- The pre-existing `TestWorktreeSnapshotBypassesCacheForUntrackedFiles` (untracked `.go`) is unchanged and still passes.

`gofmt` clean, `go vet` clean, `go build ./...` clean, full `./internal/gitutil` and `./internal/sem` suites pass.

## Context

Found while measuring entire-graph's wall-clock cost on a benchmark: across 1,175 paired agent sessions the graph arm ran **7.9% slower** than the no-tool arm (127.0 h vs 117.7 h) while saving tokens. A never-hitting index cache is one contributor — an agent's checkout almost always has some untracked scratch file in it, so in practice the cache was off far more often than intended.
BODY

  run 1: cache_hit=False  index_ms=3704  total_ms=4480
  run 2: cache_hit=True   index_ms=131   total_ms=908     28x index, 5x total
control, untracked .go (must NOT cache)
  run 1/2: cache_hit=False  index_ms=3598 / 3675
```

It forgives only paths `extensionUnsupported` rejects — the indexer's own predicate, so the two cannot disagree about what gets read. Extensionless paths stay conservative because a shebang can make one a script. `gofmt`, `go vet`, `go build ./...` clean; full `gitutil` and `sem` suites pass.

**graphmark — https://github.com/entirehq/graphmark/pull/70**

`collect_patch.sh` had lowercase-only repro filters and no `out/` exclusion, so `Repro.java` and compiled `.class` files graded as the model's answer. Verified on a synthetic tree: a one-line Java fix beside `Repro.java`, `out/classes/*.class` and `explore_thing.py` now yields a 245-byte patch containing only the fix, all four assertions passing. Plus `analysis/savings/` with the 13 scorers, so the decomposition is reproducible instead of re-derived.

**Harness reverted.** `tools/eg-q` is back to the fold-free 1,268-byte wrapper, with zero sessions live and an atomic move, backup kept. Both folds I had added measured negative in isolation — grep-source-fold −9.50%, impact-fold −0.6% — so removing them *is* the best honest state. `grep -c VERIFY tools/eg-q` is 0.

Three things worth flagging about how I scoped this:

**I did not ship what I could not stand behind.** The local graphmark checkout had modifications to `run_3arm.sh` that are someone else's experimental tool-block work; sweeping those into my PR would have attributed them to me and shipped untested changes to a shared file. Same for `_eglit.py` and `_egsiblings.py` — they fix genuinely dead flags, but neither was ever measured to help, so they stay out.

**Two real defects are named in the PR rather than fixed.** The gate accepts `CORRUPT_CC_OUT` records and `CC_MAX_TURNS` is unenforced. Both live in the shared `run_3arm.sh` path and deserve a coordinated change, not a drive-by from me at the end of a long session.

**One correction to my own commit.** My first graphmark commit message claimed to add the scorers, but `agentic-swebench/logs` is gitignored so only `collect_patch.sh` landed. I caught it before pushing, moved them to the tracked `analysis/` tree, and amended — the pushed commit matches its message.

cat > "$SP/score_haiku50.py" <<'PY'
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Scores HAIKU50 against sealed prereg d096913c166b5ebe.
PRIMARY = substitution ratio (arm-internal mechanism). Tokens are SECONDARY."""
import json,os,glob,re,collections,statistics as st,random
S=os.path.expanduser("~/pe1/graphmark/agentic-swebench")
TAG=os.environ.get("TAG","HAIKU50")
GRAPH=re.compile(r"(?:^|[|;&`(]|&&|\|\|)\s*(?:\S*/)?(?:eg|eg-q)\s+|(?:^|[|;&`(]|&&|\|\|)\s*entire\s+graph\b")
def is_graph(nm,inp):
    return nm in("Bash","bash") and bool(GRAPH.search(inp.get("command") or ""))
def usage_total(J):
    u=J.get("usage") or {}
    g=lambda *ks: next((u[k] for k in ks if u.get(k) is not None),0)
    return (g("input_tokens")+g("output_tokens")
            +g("cache_read_input_tokens","cache_read_tokens")
            +g("cache_creation_input_tokens","cache_creation_tokens"))

# ---------- gate
rec={}; drops=collections.Counter()
for arm in ("eg","baseline"):
    for idir in glob.glob(f"{S}/results/{TAG}_r1_{arm}/{arm}/*/"):
        inst=os.path.basename(idir.rstrip("/")); f=idir+"cc_out.json"; p=idir+"patch.diff"
        if not os.path.exists(f): drops[f"{arm}:no_cc_out"]+=1; continue
        raw=open(f,errors="ignore").read()
        if "CORRUPT_CC_OUT" in raw: drops[f"{arm}:CORRUPT_CC_OUT"]+=1; continue
        try: J=json.loads(raw)
        except Exception: drops[f"{arm}:unparseable"]+=1; continue
        if isinstance(J,list): J=J[0] if J else {}
        if J.get("subtype")!="success": drops[f"{arm}:subtype={J.get('subtype')}"]+=1; continue
        if J.get("is_error"): drops[f"{arm}:is_error"]+=1; continue
        if not(os.path.exists(p) and os.path.getsize(p)>0): drops[f"{arm}:empty_patch"]+=1; continue
        rec[(arm,inst)]={"cost":J.get("total_cost_usd") or 0,"tok":usage_total(J),
                         "turns":J.get("num_turns") or 0,"ms":J.get("duration_ms") or 0}
# ---------- transcripts -> calls
calls=collections.defaultdict(lambda:{"tot":0,"graph":0})
for arm in ("eg","baseline"):
    for f in glob.glob(f"{S}/results/{TAG}_r1_{arm}/ccfg/projects/*/*.jsonl"):
        inst=None; tot=0; g=0
        for ln in open(f,errors="ignore"):
            ln=ln.strip()
            if not ln or ln[0]!="{": continue
            try: r=json.loads(ln)
            except Exception: continue
            if inst is None and r.get("cwd"): inst=os.path.basename(r["cwd"])
            if r.get("type")!="assistant": continue
            c=(r.get("message") or {}).get("content")
            if not isinstance(c,list): continue
            for b in c:
                if isinstance(b,dict) and b.get("type")=="tool_use":
                    tot+=1
                    if is_graph(b.get("name",""),b.get("input") or {}): g+=1
        if inst: calls[(arm,inst)]["tot"]+=tot; calls[(arm,inst)]["graph"]+=g
# ---------- pair
pairs=[]
for (arm,inst),v in rec.items():
    if arm!="eg": continue
    b=rec.get(("baseline",inst))
    if not b: continue
    pairs.append({"inst":inst,"e":v,"b":b,
                  "ce":calls.get(("eg",inst),{"tot":0,"graph":0}),
                  "cb":calls.get(("baseline",inst),{"tot":0,"graph":0})})
print(f"=== {TAG} — prereg d096913c166b5ebe ===")
print(f"  gated pairs: {len(pairs)}   (prereg requires >= 35)")
if drops:
    print("  drops:")
    for k,v in sorted(drops.items(),key=lambda kv:-kv[1]): print(f"    {k:34} {v}")
if len(pairs)<5:
    print("  too few pairs to score"); raise SystemExit
# ---------- PRIMARY: substitution ratio
gp=[p for p in pairs if p["ce"]["graph"]>0 and p["ce"]["tot"]>0 and p["cb"]["tot"]>0]
if gp:
    G=sum(p["ce"]["graph"] for p in gp)/len(gp)
    E=sum(p["ce"]["tot"] for p in gp)/len(gp)
    B=sum(p["cb"]["tot"] for p in gp)/len(gp)
    disp=(B-E)+G
    print(f"\n=== PRIMARY: substitution ratio (n={len(gp)} with transcripts) ===")
    print(f"  eg calls/session        {E:6.2f}")
    print(f"  baseline calls/session  {B:6.2f}")
    print(f"  graph calls/session     {G:6.2f}")
    print(f"  calls displaced         {disp:+6.2f}")
    print(f"  RATIO                   {disp/G:6.3f}   (Opus reference 0.980; prereg predicts > 1.10)")
    print(f"  VERDICT: {'PASS - exceeds 1.10' if disp/G>1.10 else 'FAIL - 1:1 substitution holds, model-independent'}")
else:
    print("\n  PRIMARY unavailable: no transcripts parsed")
# ---------- SECONDARY: tokens & cost
def boot(vals,it=5000):
    rnd=random.Random(20260811); out=[]
    for _ in range(it):
        s=[vals[rnd.randrange(len(vals))] for _ in range(len(vals))]
        num=sum(b for _,b in s); den=sum(a for a,_ in s)
        out.append((num-den)/num if num else 0)
    out.sort(); return out[int(.025*it)],out[int(.975*it)]
print(f"\n=== SECONDARY: savings (n={len(pairs)}) ===")
for k,lab,ref in (("tok","tokens","+6.22%"),("cost","cost","+4.61%")):
    ve=[p["e"][k] for p in pairs]; vb=[p["b"][k] for p in pairs]
    pooled=(sum(vb)-sum(ve))/sum(vb) if sum(vb) else 0
    per=[(b-e)/b for e,b in zip(ve,vb) if b]
    lo,hi=boot(list(zip(ve,vb)))
    print(f"  {lab:7} pooled {pooled:+7.2%}  median {st.median(per):+7.2%}  equal-wt {st.mean(per):+7.2%}"
          f"  CI [{lo:+.2%},{hi:+.2%}]  wins {sum(1 for x in per if x>0)}/{len(per)}   Opus ref {ref}")
# ---------- wall clock + turns
print(f"\n=== WALL-CLOCK and TURNS (report beside tokens, per prereg) ===")
for k,lab,unit in (("ms","wall-clock","min"),("turns","turns","")):
    e=sum(p["e"][k] for p in pairs); b=sum(p["b"][k] for p in pairs)
    d=(b-e)/b if b else 0
    f=60000.0 if k=="ms" else 1.0
    print(f"  {lab:11} eg {e/f/len(pairs):8.2f}{unit}  baseline {b/f/len(pairs):8.2f}{unit}  delta {d:+.2%}"
          + ("   (negative = eg SLOWER)" if k=="ms" else ""))
tot=sum(p["e"]["cost"]+p["b"]["cost"] for p in pairs)
print(f"\n  cell spend on gated pairs: ${tot:.2f}")
PY

content.text:
Interim read — **and I need to caveat this hard, because I've been burned by exactly this before.** At 15 of 50 pairs:

```
tokens   pooled  -3.84%   median +0.22%   equal-wt  -8.21%   CI [-20.36,+9.63]   wins  8/15
cost     pooled  +2.30%   median +6.20%   equal-wt  -0.64%   CI [ -9.64,+11.60]  wins 10/15
                                                              Opus ref: tokens +6.22%, cost +4.61%

PRIMARY  eg calls 67.14  baseline 61.29  graph 4.29  ->  displaced -1.57, RATIO -0.367
wall-clock  eg 7.59min vs baseline 7.50min (-1.27%, eg slower)
turns       eg 59.47 vs baseline 56.80
```

**Why you should not trust these numbers yet.** They come from the pairs that finished *first*, and I measured that bias directly in an earlier cell: finished-first pairs are significantly cheaper, permutation p=0.0052. A partial ratio here read +76% on a cell that was nothing like that when complete. Also 18 of 33 records dropped as unparseable (13 baseline, 5 eg) — those are files still being written mid-run, not defects, but the asymmetry alone can swing a 15-pair read.

**What is nonetheless worth noting.** The direction is against my sealed prediction, not for it. I predicted the substitution ratio would exceed 1.10 on a weaker model because Haiku should flail more and leave more displaceable work. Instead eg is making **more** calls than baseline (67.1 vs 61.3), so the ratio is negative — the graph is adding work rather than displacing it. If that holds at n=50, the 1:1-substitute finding is not just model-independent, it's worse on Haiku, and the token number is noise whatever it lands on.

Two other early signals: Haiku is hitting the 120-turn cap (`error_max_turns` on 2 baselines), and eg is again slightly slower in wall-clock, consistent with Opus.

At 90/100 with 34 gated pairs — and the answer is that **the graph loses on Haiku**:

```
                pooled     median   equal-wt   CI                wins     Opus ref
tokens          -5.49%     -3.03%   -10.97%    [-15.62,+3.52]   17/34    +6.22%
