# Plan: land every entire-graph security fix as its own verified PR

Written 2026-08-19. Replaces the token-savings plan (that work is closed; see the artifact and
`graph-is-a-1to1-substitute` in memory).

## Context

A full adversarial security review of entire-graph at `cceb4de` produced **19 findings / 36
verdicts**: 14 confirmed (1 high, 5 medium, 8 low), 4 more from a completeness critic, 3 refuted.
Report: https://claude.ai/code/artifact/6ef583b3-6366-4678-a45b-2aacb48bfcc0

Six PRs are already open (#125–#130). Three passed adversarial audit, **two failed**, one audit is
still running. This plan finishes the job: repair the two failures, then one PR per remaining
finding, each independently verified.

The review's own thesis is what the remaining work must respect: **five guards already exist in this
codebase and each is applied at some call sites and not others** — newline-path fallback 3 of 4,
leading-dash argv 3 of 8, `maxNestedIgnoreFileBytes` nested-only, `os.OpenRoot` reads-only,
`termsafe` text/agent-only. Every fix below pushes its guard into the **sink**, not the call site.

### What is already banked

| PR | Fix | Audit |
|---|---|---|
| #126 | escape control bytes in the fatal error report | **SHIP** — auditor built a stronger exploit than the author |
| #127 | guard cache-key ignore-file reads | **SHIP** — reproduced the block both directions |
| #128 | reject paths the cat-file batch protocol cannot carry | **SHIP** — reproduced at the real CLI |
| #130 | bound the root ignore file's size and rule count | audit pending |

`test (windows-latest)` failures on #127/#128 are already fixed and pushed: both were
platform-assuming fixtures (Windows forbids `\n` in filenames; `os.DevNull` is `NUL` and resolves as
a *regular* file, so the POSIX type guard is unreachable there while the `io.LimitReader` still
bounds the read on every platform).

## Two repairs first — both block merges

**R1 · #125 SECURITY.md.** Code is fine; the prose makes three claims the auditor refuted: that the
org policy "is the umbrella" (it contradicts this doc on routing), that no private channel exists
(`/security/policy` returns 200 today), and that GitHub gates the "Report a vulnerability" button on
SECURITY.md (it gates on private vulnerability reporting, which is **disabled** on this repo). Also
drop the hardcoded version table — `main` is already `v0.4.0-10-g`, so it self-falsifies on the next
tag. Fix the file; do not restate unverified claims.

**R2 · #129 `.env`/`.npmrc`** — user decision: **rework to fix the real cause.** The auditor rebuilt
the patched binary and the credential leak is **byte-for-byte unchanged**, because the search corpus
is built by `preselectSearchFiles` → `source.paths` (`internal/sem/search.go:1698`) independent of
`languageForPath`. The patch also silently raised secret-file scores ~1.5. So: keep the two-line
table removal, add the corpus exclusion that actually stops emission, delete the false claim from the
commit message (`symbols` never emitted the dump as a durable record), and disclose the score change.

## Then one PR per finding

Ordered by regression risk, safest first. Each is its own branch off `origin/main`.

**Tier A — mechanical, contained**
1. `09` Escape U+0080–U+009F in the machine-format encoders. JSON is `search`'s default on a TTY and
   `encoding/json` does not escape C1. Reopens #96, whose test asserts only on `0x1b`.
2. `12` Resolve `--base`/`--head` through `git rev-parse --verify --end-of-options` at the CLI
   boundary (`internal/cli/root.go:748,754`). Three siblings in the same file already do this.
3. `13` Make `.git` unconditional in `skipVendoredDir` (`provider.go:10061`), matched on path
   component before `ReincludesDescendant` is consulted.
4. `C1` Harden `newCmd` (`internal/gitutil/git.go`): `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM` and `-c core.fsmonitor=`.
   Verify no legitimate reliance on user git config first.
5. `C4` `cmd/graph-bench/main.go:246` — a committed manifest ref reaches a `git fetch` positional.

**Tier B — containment, the load-bearing work**
6. `01` **HIGH** `index --report` write containment via `os.OpenRoot` + `O_NOFOLLOW`, plus the
   content-injection half (`report.go:55-57` prints tracked filenames verbatim). Apply to
   `verify.go:238-243` in the same patch. Must keep a legitimate absolute `--report /tmp/x` working.
7. `02` `init-agents` write containment. **Trap:** a naive `os.Stat`→`os.Lstat` swap regresses the
   documented AGENTS.md↔CLAUDE.md alias feature (`agents.go:158-176`, `os.SameFile`). Use
   `os.OpenRoot` and preserve the alias.
8. `03` `gitutil.ShowFileLimited` at the four uncapped readers (`provider.go:9785`,
   `search.go:1433`, `analyze.go:109,115`), routed into the existing `E_FILE_TOO_LARGE` path so the
   file does not silently disappear.
9. `04` `openSource` repoRoot confinement (`provider.go:9836`). Hot indexing path — open one
   `os.Root` for the `openedSource` lifetime, mirroring `callsite.go:211` and `cache_entry.go:71`.

**Tier C — subtle and architectural** (user decision: attempt all three)
10. `05` Depth counter through every recursive walker reachable from `parseWithProfile`, emitting an
    `E_PARSE_DEPTH` partial failure. Go stack overflow is unrecoverable, so this must be a *limit*,
    not a `recover()`.
11. `06` Give the relation and search phases a real wall-clock budget — `root.go:32` hands every
    provider `context.Background()`, so `--max-seconds` can never fire — then fix the three quadratic
    sites.
12. `C2` Agent-payload record forgery. No obviously correct fix; a repo-committed `VERIFY:` line is
    indistinguishable from tool output and the guide tells agents to execute it. Attempt the
    narrowest credible change (provenance marking rather than fencing, which would break parsers) and
    **say plainly in the PR if the result is a mitigation rather than a fix.**
13. `C3` `.graphignore` silently controls the graph's field of view. Surface exclusions in the
    payload so a hidden file is visible as hidden.

## Verification — the gate that has already caught two bad PRs

Per PR, non-negotiable:
- **Failing-first test, proven.** Restore the production file from `origin/main`, keep the new test,
  show it fails. A test that only fails to *build* on main is too weak (#130 hit this and said so).
- `gofmt -l` empty · `go vet ./...` · `go build ./...` · package tests green.
- **Windows-aware fixtures.** Any test using symlinks, device files or exotic filenames gets a
  `runtime.GOOS` guard with a comment saying why the input is unrepresentable there. This bit #127
  and #128; it is now a checklist item, not a discovery.
- **Adversarial audit** by a second agent that rebuilds `origin/main` itself, re-runs the exploit
  against the patched binary, and re-verifies the failing-first claim. This is what caught #129.
- **No unverified claims** in commit messages or PR bodies. Both failed audits were prose, not code.
- No AI attribution footers.

## What I cannot do

`Entire Gates` fails on all six PRs with `Approvals: No reviewers have approved this trail`.
Checks, Findings and Up-to-date all pass. That gate needs a human reviewer and I will not
self-approve. **Enabling private vulnerability reporting** on the repo is also yours — SECURITY.md is
worth little until it is on.

+verdicts**: 14 confirmed (1 high, 5 medium, 8 low), 4 more from a completeness critic, 3 refuted.

+still running. This plan finishes the job: repair the two failures, then one PR per remaining
+finding, each independently verified.
-graph calls/session          2.71        (transcript, cross-checked vs gq_calls.log 3.30)
-other calls displaced        2.65
-SUBSTITUTION RATIO           0.980       <- a 1:1 substitute removes no work by construction
-net call reduction          -0.06/session
+The review's own thesis is what the remaining work must respect: **five guards already exist in this
+codebase and each is applied at some call sites and not others** — newline-path fallback 3 of 4,
+leading-dash argv 3 of 8, `maxNestedIgnoreFileBytes` nested-only, `os.OpenRoot` reads-only,
+`termsafe` text/agent-only. Every fix below pushes its guard into the **sink**, not the call site.
-entire-graph swaps 2.65 shell calls for 2.71 graph calls. The +6.22% comes from the swapped calls
-being cheaper, not from a shorter session. That single fact explains why eleven payload levers all
-failed independent of their content, and why every lever stacked at *perfect* effectiveness tops out
-at 6.9% cost.
+### What is already banked
-The loss mechanism is not a defect. Split by how much the no-tool baseline flails:
-baseline calls  eg calls  base calls  displacement  ratio/call  win rate   cost delta
-Losers are **easy tasks**. The graph pays its 2.65-call toll and displaces nothing, because the
-baseline found the file in 19 calls unaided. Graph usage in losers is statistically identical to
-winners (2.68 vs 2.65, permutation **p=0.9128**) — there is no behaviour to repair, which is why
-per-loser fixes measured +0.04pt. The two-axis model
-(`1.31*ln(calls) + 0.49*ln(bytes)`) reproduces the **sign in all five bins**.
-So the only lever with real headroom is **not paying the toll on easy tasks**.
-## The arithmetic, and why this plan stops where it does
-Noisy-oracle simulation (40 seeds per cell, gate fires on the top fraction by predicted difficulty),
-where `rho` is the predictor's correlation with true baseline effort:
-rho    fire20%   fire40%   fire60%   fire80%  fire100%
-**Gating alone cannot reach 10% at any rho** (max +8.29% cost even with a perfect oracle). And rho is
-itself capped: only **46.1%** of baseline-effort variance is task-level (test-retest r=+0.276 across
-106 instances seen in 2+ cells), so a perfect task-level predictor is bounded at
-Second, independent lever. The payload is 76.1% source body, and that body is sometimes paid twice:
-files shown with a body in a payload   4.17/session
-of those, agent LATER read the file    35.0%
-lines shown that were re-read anyway   58.0%   -> 2,466 B/session of pure waste
-Combining the two (independent mechanisms, tokens = 1.35x cost leverage measured on the same pairs):
-| build | cost | tokens |
+| PR | Fix | Audit |
-| gate rho=0.68 (max buildable) + body cap | +8.06% | +10.88% |

+| #126 | escape control bytes in the fatal error report | **SHIP** — auditor built a stronger exploit than the author |

+table removal, add the corpus exclusion that actually stops emission, delete the false claim from the
+commit message (`symbols` never emitted the dump as a durable record), and disclose the score change.

# Plan: land every entire-graph security fix as its own verified PR

Written 2026-08-19. Replaces the token-savings plan (that work is closed; see the artifact and
`graph-is-a-1to1-substitute` in memory).

## Context

A full adversarial security review of entire-graph at `cceb4de` produced **19 findings / 36
verdicts**: 14 confirmed (1 high, 5 medium, 8 low), 4 more from a completeness critic, 3 refuted.
Report: https://claude.ai/code/artifact/6ef583b3-6366-4678-a45b-2aacb48bfcc0

Six PRs are already open (#125–#130). Three passed adversarial audit, **two failed**, one audit is
still running. This plan finishes the job: repair the two failures, then one PR per remaining
finding, each independently verified.

The review's own thesis is what the remaining work must respect: **five guards already exist in this
codebase and each is applied at some call sites and not others** — newline-path fallback 3 of 4,
leading-dash argv 3 of 8, `maxNestedIgnoreFileBytes` nested-only, `os.OpenRoot` reads-only,
`termsafe` text/agent-only. Every fix below pushes its guard into the **sink**, not the call site.

### What is already banked

| PR | Fix | Audit |
|---|---|---|
| #126 | escape control bytes in the fatal error report | **SHIP** — auditor built a stronger exploit than the author |
| #127 | guard cache-key ignore-file reads | **SHIP** — reproduced the block both directions |
| #128 | reject paths the cat-file batch protocol cannot carry | **SHIP** — reproduced at the real CLI |
| #130 | bound the root ignore file's size and rule count | audit pending |

`test (windows-latest)` failures on #127/#128 are already fixed and pushed: both were
platform-assuming fixtures (Windows forbids `\n` in filenames; `os.DevNull` is `NUL` and resolves as
a *regular* file, so the POSIX type guard is unreachable there while the `io.LimitReader` still
bounds the read on every platform).

## Two repairs first — both block merges

**R1 · #125 SECURITY.md.** Code is fine; the prose makes three claims the auditor refuted: that the
org policy "is the umbrella" (it contradicts this doc on routing), that no private channel exists
(`/security/policy` returns 200 today), and that GitHub gates the "Report a vulnerability" button on
SECURITY.md (it gates on private vulnerability reporting, which is **disabled** on this repo). Also
drop the hardcoded version table — `main` is already `v0.4.0-10-g`, so it self-falsifies on the next
tag. Fix the file; do not restate unverified claims.

**R2 · #129 `.env`/`.npmrc`** — user decision: **rework to fix the real cause.** The auditor rebuilt
the patched binary and the credential leak is **byte-for-byte unchanged**, because the search corpus
is built by `preselectSearchFiles` → `source.paths` (`internal/sem/search.go:1698`) independent of
`languageForPath`. The patch also silently raised secret-file scores ~1.5. So: keep the two-line
table removal, add the corpus exclusion that actually stops emission, delete the false claim from the
commit message (`symbols` never emitted the dump as a durable record), and disclose the score change.

## Then one PR per finding

Ordered by regression risk, safest first. Each is its own branch off `origin/main`.

**Tier A — mechanical, contained**
1. `09` Escape U+0080–U+009F in the machine-format encoders. JSON is `search`'s default on a TTY and
   `encoding/json` does not escape C1. Reopens #96, whose test asserts only on `0x1b`.
2. `12` Resolve `--base`/`--head` through `git rev-parse --verify --end-of-options` at the CLI
   boundary (`internal/cli/root.go:748,754`). Three siblings in the same file already do this.
3. `13` Make `.git` unconditional in `skipVendoredDir` (`provider.go:10061`), matched on path
   component before `ReincludesDescendant` is consulted.
4. `C1` Harden `newCmd` (`internal/gitutil/git.go`): `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM` and `-c core.fsmonitor=`.
   Verify no legitimate reliance on user git config first.
5. `C4` `cmd/graph-bench/main.go:246` — a committed manifest ref reaches a `git fetch` positional.

**Tier B — containment, the load-bearing work**
6. `01` **HIGH** `index --report` write containment via `os.OpenRoot` + `O_NOFOLLOW`, plus the
   content-injection half (`report.go:55-57` prints tracked filenames verbatim). Apply to
   `verify.go:238-243` in the same patch. Must keep a legitimate absolute `--report /tmp/x` working.
7. `02` `init-agents` write containment. **Trap:** a naive `os.Stat`→`os.Lstat` swap regresses the
   documented AGENTS.md↔CLAUDE.md alias feature (`agents.go:158-176`, `os.SameFile`). Use
   `os.OpenRoot` and preserve the alias.
8. `03` `gitutil.ShowFileLimited` at the four uncapped readers (`provider.go:9785`,
   `search.go:1433`, `analyze.go:109,115`), routed into the existing `E_FILE_TOO_LARGE` path so the
   file does not silently disappear.
9. `04` `openSource` repoRoot confinement (`provider.go:9836`). Hot indexing path — open one
   `os.Root` for the `openedSource` lifetime, mirroring `callsite.go:211` and `cache_entry.go:71`.

**Tier C — subtle and architectural** (user decision: attempt all three)
10. `05` Depth counter through every recursive walker reachable from `parseWithProfile`, emitting an
    `E_PARSE_DEPTH` partial failure. Go stack overflow is unrecoverable, so this must be a *limit*,
    not a `recover()`.
11. `06` Give the relation and search phases a real wall-clock budget — `root.go:32` hands every
    provider `context.Background()`, so `--max-seconds` can never fire — then fix the three quadratic
    sites.
12. `C2` Agent-payload record forgery. No obviously correct fix; a repo-committed `VERIFY:` line is
    indistinguishable from tool output and the guide tells agents to execute it. Attempt the
    narrowest credible change (provenance marking rather than fencing, which would break parsers) and
    **say plainly in the PR if the result is a mitigation rather than a fix.**
13. `C3` `.graphignore` silently controls the graph's field of view. Surface exclusions in the
    payload so a hidden file is visible as hidden.

Per PR, non-negotiable:
- **Failing-first test, proven.** Restore the production file from `origin/main`, keep the new test,
  show it fails. A test that only fails to *build* on main is too weak (#130 hit this and said so).
- `gofmt -l` empty · `go vet ./...` · `go build ./...` · package tests green.
- **Windows-aware fixtures.** Any test using symlinks, device files or exotic filenames gets a
  `runtime.GOOS` guard with a comment saying why the input is unrepresentable there. This bit #127
  and #128; it is now a checklist item, not a discovery.
- **Adversarial audit** by a second agent that rebuilds `origin/main` itself, re-runs the exploit
  against the patched binary, and re-verifies the failing-first claim. This is what caught #129.
- **No unverified claims** in commit messages or PR bodies. Both failed audits were prose, not code.
- No AI attribution footers.

## What I cannot do

`Entire Gates` fails on all six PRs with `Approvals: No reviewers have approved this trail`.
Checks, Findings and Up-to-date all pass. That gate needs a human reviewer and I will not
self-approve. **Enabling private vulnerability reporting** on the repo is also yours — SECURITY.md is
worth little until it is on.

returns before clobbering.

agents_test.go:494 TestInitAgentsCreatesDanglingSharedAliasTargetOnce, which asserts the symlink
SURVIVES via os.Lstat + ModeSymlink.
WHY Lstat-swap breaks it: Lstat returns the LINK's inode so SameFile is false for all four shapes ->
both files written -> symlink replaced by a regular file. And root.OpenFile REFUSES all symlinked
components outright, so plain os.Root breaks it a second way.

predicate: root.Lstat(name) -> if symlink, filepath.EvalSymlinks -> filepath.Rel(root, resolved) must
not start with ".." and must not be absolute-outside -> then write via
root.OpenFile(resolvedRelPath, O_WRONLY|O_CREATE|O_TRUNC). A symlink resolving INSIDE the root is

NOT confined because the cache dir is caller-owned. The distinguishing argument is that init-agents
writes into the REPO TREE and docs/trust-and-security.md:38-40 promises "exactly three repository
files".

`--record-baseline /tmp/base.json`; docs/trust-and-security.md:41-44 says both write "to the path you
give it", relative to process CWD, deliberately caller-owned.

breaks the documented example, breaks `--report ../reports/x.md` in CI, and breaks every
`/tmp/...` example on macOS where /tmp is itself a symlink to private/tmp.

  1. abs := filepath.Abs(path)  (matches today's CWD-relative semantics)
  2. rel, err := filepath.Rel(repoRoot, abs). If rel starts with ".." or is absolute -> OUTSIDE the
     repo -> write EXACTLY as today (os.WriteFile / os.MkdirAll). Caller-owned; a symlink there was

  3. If rel is INSIDE the repo -> that is the attack surface (hostile clone ships GRAPH_REPORT.md as
     a symlink) -> os.OpenRoot(repoRoot) + root.OpenFile(rel, O_WRONLY|O_CREATE|O_TRUNC|O_NOFOLLOW).

as outside. index.go already has repo at :74, so threading is trivial.

filepath.Join normalizes ../secret above the root.

on a stored ABSOLUTE path with no symlink check (set at :9840 registry.note).
ONE os.Root for the openedSource lifetime is correct and safe: os.Root methods are goroutine-safe,
which matters because provider_parallel.go calls the closures concurrently. Cost is ONE extra openat
per openedSource; per-file cost unchanged (root.Lstat+root.Open are the same 2 syscalls, *at-relative).
MUST set close: in the worktree return at :9869 (today nil). Consumers already guard for nil at
provider.go:940-941, search_cache.go:566-567, search.go:1715-1716 — chain, do not replace.

search_cache.go:615; provider_parallel.go:76; search_literals.go:220; search_related.go:205;
search_closedset.go:605; search_needle.go:224) and .readPrefix( at provider_parallel.go:83 + :63.

js_scopes.go:392/597/646/686; rust.go:219; kotlin.go:432 — the last already takes depth int, the only

content.text:
The scoping agent came back and it **materially corrects three of the fixes I had planned wrong**. Saved to `SCOPING-CORRECTIONS.md` for batch 2, because two of these would have shipped bugs.

## The three corrections that matter

**`os.OpenRoot` is the wrong tool for `index --report`.** I'd planned it as the fix. But `--record-baseline /tmp/base.json` is *documented, advertised usage* (`help.go:375`), and an `os.Root` rejects absolute paths, `..` escapes, and symlinked components — so it would break the documented example, break `--report ../reports/x.md` in CI, and break every `/tmp/...` example on macOS, where `/tmp` is itself a symlink. The correct rule is conditional: resolve the path, and if it lands **outside** the repo write exactly as today (caller-owned, and a symlink there was planted by the caller), but if it lands **inside** the repo — the attack surface — use `os.OpenRoot` + `O_NOFOLLOW`.

**`os.OpenRoot` alone destroys the init-agents alias feature.** I knew a naive `Stat`→`Lstat` swap was a trap. What I didn't know: `root.OpenFile` refuses *all* symlinked components, so plain containment breaks it a second, independent way. AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md are allowed to be the same inode, and a symlink resolving *inside* the root is the legitimate feature — only one escaping the root is the attack. Two existing tests pin this, including one that asserts the symlink survives.

**`GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM` would cause the leak it's meant to prevent.** This is the one I'm most glad to have caught. `git.go:107-112` documents that delegating exclusion to git is *the point*, because it applies `core.excludesFile` — and `docs/trust-and-security.md` promises users that. Suppressing global config would silently pull globally-ignored trees like `node_modules` and `.env` **into** the corpus. The safe set is just `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` plus `-c core.fsmonitor=` on three listing commands.

## Two findings are bigger than the audit said

**The `.env` fix has to go into `ignore.go`, not the prior machinery.** Proof the language table was never the boundary: `inventoryLanguageForSuffix` only matches suffixes with more than one dot, so **`.env.local` and `.env.production` are already outside the table today and remain fully searchable**. And `classifySearchFile` has no secret class at all — priors are *multiplicative de-ranking* and can never make a secret unquotable.

**The parser fix needs ~13 walkers, not 3** — and two in particular must be done together, since `initializerTypeBodies` is called *from* `walkEntitiesScoped` so they mutually amplify, and `collectParseErrorDetails` runs on every file with a syntax error, which is exactly the adversarial input class.

Also a third unconfined read nobody had flagged: `oversizeRegistry.lookup` digests a stored absolute path with no symlink check.

Batch 1 is running with 7 agents. Its git-hardening task already carried my warning to verify `core.excludesFile` before touching config, so it should land on the narrow fix — I'll check that specifically when it reports, since I now have the evidence to judge it against.

content.text:
**The trap was caught by experiment, not by taking my word for it.** #134's agent:

> DROPPED `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM` ON PURPOSE — task said say so if it breaks excludesFile. **It does, verified**: with `GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM` set to a config whose `core.excludesFile` hides `secret.txt`, `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard`…

It set up the config, ran the command, and watched the previously-hidden secret become visible. That's the exact failure mode the scoping agent predicted — suppressing global config would have *caused* a leak while trying to prevent one — and it shipped the narrow fix instead.

## Progress

```
#125  SECURITY.md              repaired (prose claims corrected)
#126  stderr control bytes     SHIP
#127  cache-key ignore reads   SHIP
#128  cat-file batch newline   SHIP
#129  .env/.npmrc              reworking into ignore.go
#130  root ignore file caps    SHIP
#131  graph-bench git fetch    NEW
#132  .git always excluded     NEW
#133  diff rev validation      NEW
#134  git subprocess hardening NEW
      C1 machine-format escape branch pushed, PR pending
```

10 of 13 PRs exist. Failing-first proofs are landing correctly this time — all three new ones explicitly confirm the test **compiles on main and fails at runtime**, which was the weakness called out on #130.

## One deliberate deviation to flag

**#133 did not implement what I asked.** I specified `git rev-parse --verify --end-of-options` for validating `--base`/`--head`; the agent declined because that needs a new function in `internal/gitutil`, which it didn't own, and disclosed it in the PR body under "Not done here" rather than quietly widening scope or silently doing something weaker. That's the right call on ownership — but it means the fix may be a shape check rather than real resolution, so I'll verify what it actually does before calling it done.

## One thing needs you

**#132 reports `Findings: 1 unresolved agent finding(s)`** on the Entire Gates check — and the agent could not read it. That's your review system flagging something on the `.git`-exclusion PR that I can't see from the API. Everything else across the fleet is the expected `Approvals` failure only.

Audits are running behind each PR. Batch 2 — the four containment fixes and the architectural three — starts once these clear, using the corrections doc so the `index --report` and `init-agents` fixes don't ship the `os.OpenRoot` mistake I'd originally planned.

Trail: fix(sem): never index .git, even when .gitignore re-includes it
    Number:  92
    ID:      01M0DF18MK1Y7ME9Q4PAX10X99
    Branch:  security/git-dir-always-excluded
    Base:    main
    Status:  open
    Author:  suhaanthayyil
    Phase:   building
    URL:     https://entire.io/gh/entireio/entire-graph/trails/92
    Assignees: suhaanthayyil
    Created: 2026-08-19T16:52:53Z
    Updated: 2026-08-19T16:55:20Z
  
  Description:
  Problem: The semantic provider could leak credentials from .git/config in search results when a repository's committed .gitignore used negation syntax like !.git/** to re-include the .git directory. On systems where git ls-files fails (uid-mismatched filesystems, missing git binary, corrupt index), the fallback worktree walk would descend .git and index its contents, surfacing credentials from remote URLs in ranked search snippets.
  Solution: Introduced an unconditional exclusion of the repository's own .git directory (and files within it) in skipVendoredDir and the worktree file walk, bypassing the gitignore negation logic entirely. The isRepoGitDirPath function matches .git and paths starting with .git/ at the first path component only, preserving legitimate repository contents like .github/ directories. Added comprehensive tests verifying the fix prevents both directory traversal and credential leakage in end-to-end search operations, even with malicious gitignore patterns.

fix(sem): never index .git, even when .gitignore re-includes it#92
Threads

Problem: The semantic provider could leak credentials from .git/config in search results when a repository's committed .gitignore used negation syntax like !.git/** to re-include the .git directory. On systems where git ls-files fails (uid-mismatched filesystems, missing git binary, corrupt index), the fallback worktree walk would descend .git and index its contents, surfacing credentials from remote URLs in ranked search snippets.

Solution: Introduced an unconditional exclusion of the repository's own .git directory (and files within it) in skipVendoredDir and the worktree file walk, bypassing the gitignore negation logic entirely. The isRepoGitDirPath function matches .git and paths starting with .git/ at the first path component only, preserving legitimate repository contents like .github/ directories. Added comprehensive tests verifying the fix prevents both directory traversal and credential leakage in end-to-end search operations, even with malicious gitignore patterns.

## THE FINDING (verbatim from the reviewer, rated High, on internal/sem/provider.go)
"This hard-codes the Git directory as the first component .git, but Git supports a .git pointer to an
arbitrary --separate-git-dir inside the worktree (for example .repo-git). If git ls-files fails and
triggers the filesystem fallback, that resolved Git directory is still walked and its config/hooks
can be indexed, so the credential-leak path this change intends to close remains open; resolve or
locally parse the actual gitdir and skip it when it is under the repository root."

## WHY IT IS RIGHT
`git init --separate-git-dir=.repo-git` (or `git clone --separate-git-dir`) makes `.git` a FILE whose
contents are `gitdir: <path>`, and that path can be INSIDE the worktree. The current fix's
`isRepoGitDirPath` only skips the literal first component `.git`, so `.repo-git/config` — holding
remote URLs with credentials — is still walked and indexed by the filesystem fallback. Same
credential-leak path, different shape. VERIFY this yourself before fixing: build the branch binary,
create such a repo, force the fallback, and show `.repo-git/config` reaching search results.

## THE FIX
Resolve the real gitdir and skip it when it is under the repository root. Constraints:
- The filesystem fallback exists precisely BECAUSE git failed or is unavailable, so do NOT depend on
  `git rev-parse --git-dir`. Parse the `.git` file locally: if `<repo>/.git` is a regular FILE, read
  it, accept a leading `gitdir: ` prefix, resolve the value (it may be relative to the repo root or
  absolute), and if the result is inside the repo root, exclude that path too.
- Keep the existing literal `.git` skip (the common case where `.git` is a directory).
- Preserve the existing behaviour that `.github/` and any other `.git`-PREFIXED name is NOT skipped —
  match on whole path component, and there should already be a test for this. Do not regress it.
- Bound the read: a `.git` file is tiny; refuse anything implausible rather than slurping.

## SCOPE
You own internal/sem/provider.go (the skipVendoredDir / isRepoGitDirPath / worktree-walk region only)
and its test file. Another PR touches other regions of provider.go — keep the diff tight.

## GATE, all must pass before you commit
- A regression test that FAILS AT RUNTIME on the current branch tip (not merely fails to compile).
  Prove it: stash your production change, keep the test, run it, capture the failure output.
- `gofmt -l .` empty, `go vet ./...`, `go build ./...`, `go test ./internal/sem` green.
- Windows-aware: if any fixture uses a symlink or an exotic filename, guard with `runtime.GOOS` and a
  comment. Two PRs in this series already broke test (windows-latest).
- Commit message: conventional prefix, explains the gap and the fix with file:line. **NO AI
  attribution footer, no Co-Authored-By, no "Generated with".**
- Push to the same branch (it updates PR #132), then add a PR comment explaining that this addresses

- Do NOT claim anything you have not verified with a command.

input.summary: Two more blockers on PR 132 from adversarial audit
input.message:
Good work on the separate-git-dir fix, and good catch that the primary listing path leaks too. Two more blockers on PR #132 from an independent adversarial audit that ran against your branch. Both need resolving before this can ship.

BLOCKER 1 — a NESTED .git still leaks against the patched binary.
The auditor reproduced, live: a repo containing `vendor/dep/.git` (a vendored dependency carrying its own git directory) plus a root `.gitignore` that re-includes it. Your `isRepoGitDirPath` / `repoGitDirFilter` matches the FIRST path component only, so `vendor/dep/.git/config` is not skipped and its remote-URL credentials reach search snippets. Your own test asserts `vendor/dep/.repo-git` -> false, so this is a deliberate boundary you drew — but the credential-leak path the PR claims to close is still open for the nested shape.

Decide and implement one of these, then say which and why in the PR body:
 (a) Skip ANY path component named `.git` at any depth (not just the first). Check what this costs: does anything legitimately need to index a nested `.git`? A vendored dep's git dir is never program text, so I expect not — but verify against the existing tests, especially anything covering vendored trees.
 (b) If you have a concrete reason (a) is wrong, say so explicitly and scope the PR title/body to "the repository's own git directory" so the PR does not claim more than it delivers. That is the failure mode two other PRs in this series were caught on.
Whichever you pick, add a regression test for the nested shape that fails first on your current tip.

BLOCKER 2 — the failing-first transcript in the PR body does not match the committed test.
The auditor states the transcript cited in the body cannot be produced by the test that is actually committed. You have pushed 707837a since, with a real proof, so this may already be resolved — but verify it directly: re-read the current PR body, and make sure every command and every line of output it shows can be reproduced from the committed tree exactly as written. If it cannot, replace it with a transcript you just produced. Do not leave a fabricated or stale transcript in the body; that is the specific class of defect that has failed three audits in this series.

Same gate as before: failing-first must fail AT RUNTIME, gofmt/vet/build/test green, Windows-aware fixtures, no unverified claims in the body or commit message, no AI attribution footer. Report what you changed and the new proof output.

fix(cli): confine in-repo --report and --record-baseline writes
fix(cli): confine in-repo --report and --record-baseline writes#96
Threads
T

Problem: The entire graph index --report and verify --record-baseline verbs accept caller-specified paths but write unconfined: os.WriteFile follows symlinks at the destination. When the path is inside the scanned repository—as with the in-repo spelling GRAPH_REPORT.md the tool itself suggests—the file location is controlled by untrusted repository content. A clone that commits the path as a mode-120000 symlink causes the report or baseline bytes to truncate and replace whatever the symlink points at. A second vulnerability in report rendering: Git pathnames allow any byte except NUL and /, so a tracked file with an embedded newline is rendered as a whole table row in the markdown output, allowing the repository to inject arbitrary report content.

Solution: New outputpath.go applies a boundary rule: outside-repository paths write exactly as before (caller-owned, symlinks allowed), while inside-repository paths write through os.Root with Lstat refusal of symlinked final components. Classification runs both lexically and on resolved paths (using resolveExistingPrefix for symlinked ancestors), and inside wins, because each alone is wrong in one direction—resolved alone misclassifies a repository reached through a symlink, and lexical alone is escaped by committed symlinked directories. Both verbs (index.go, verify.go) now call writeOutputFile instead of os.WriteFile/os.MkdirAll. Report table rendering in report.go now escapes pathname keys through termsafe.Line, which renders control characters safely without merging files into one row. Comprehensive test suite (outputpath_test.go) covers both symlink refusal and out-of-repo write preservation, including symlinked parent directories, missing ancestor creation, and newline-in-filename escaping.

An explicit --repo may name a subdirectory, while the Git operations still index the entire top-level repository. Using that subdirectory as the confinement root misclassifies sibling paths in the same checkout as caller-owned; for example, from the repository root, index --repo subdir --report GRAPH_REPORT.md follows a committed root-level symlink and can truncate its external target. Resolve the Git top level before classifying output paths, with an appropriate non-Git fallback for verify.

Medium
AI

internal/cli/outputpath.go:95
34m ago

filepath.Rel uses case-sensitive lexical comparison on Unix even when the underlying filesystem is case-insensitive, as is common on macOS, and EvalSymlinks does not canonicalize ordinary component casing. An in-repository path using a differently cased spelling of the repository root therefore falls through as caller-owned and is written with unrestricted os.WriteFile, allowing a committed output symlink to be followed. Determine containment using filesystem identity or canonical component casing rather than lexical paths alone.

fix(sem): never index a git directory, whatever its name or depth#92
Threads

Problem: The semantic provider could leak credentials from .git/config in search results when a repository's committed .gitignore used negation syntax like !.git/** to re-include the .git directory. On systems where git ls-files fails (uid-mismatched filesystems, missing git binary, corrupt index), the fallback worktree walk would descend .git and index its contents, surfacing credentials from remote URLs in ranked search snippets.

Solution: Introduced an unconditional exclusion of the repository's own .git directory (and files within it) in skipVendoredDir and the worktree file walk, bypassing the gitignore negation logic entirely. The isRepoGitDirPath function matches .git and paths starting with .git/ at the first path component only, preserving legitimate repository contents like .github/ directories. Added comprehensive tests verifying the fix prevents both directory traversal and credential leakage in end-to-end search operations, even with malicious gitignore patterns.

input.message:
The trail review posted a NEW finding on PR #132 against your latest head 79167fb. It is a fifth shape and it looks correct to me. Rated High, on internal/sem/provider.go:

"Observe the listed path itself before walking its ancestors. A tracked nested repository is emitted by git ls-files as a gitlink such as vendor/dep without a trailing slash, so this loop starts at vendor and never reads vendor/dep/.git; if that pointer targets an ordinary in-repo path such as state/.dep-git, the target's config, hooks, and objects remain listed and can be indexed."

So: a submodule / gitlink entry. `git ls-files` emits `vendor/dep` as ONE entry with no trailing slash, so your ancestor loop observes `vendor` and stops — it never treats `vendor/dep` itself as a directory that might hold a `.git` pointer file. If that pointer names an in-repo target such as `state/.dep-git`, that target is still listed and indexed, config and hooks included.

Please:
1. REPRODUCE IT FIRST against your current head, exactly as you did for the previous four shapes. Build a repo with a tracked gitlink whose `.git` pointer targets an in-repo directory, and show the credential reaching a search snippet. If it does NOT reproduce, say so with evidence and push back — you were right to correct the auditor last time on the `!vendor/**` trigger, and the same standard applies here.
2. If it reproduces, fix it by observing each LISTED PATH itself before walking its ancestors, so a gitlink entry is examined as a potential pointer holder rather than only as a path component.
3. Add it as shape 5 to the before/after table in the PR body, with real output, and add a failing-first regression test.
4. Re-check the whole family after the change: I want the five (now six) shapes all still covered, not a fix that closes this one and reopens an earlier one.

Same gate: failing-first must fail at runtime, gofmt/vet/build/test green, Windows fixture safety, every transcript in the body reproducible from the committed tree, no AI attribution footer.

Note the review has now found an adjacent shape on each of your three heads. That is the system working, not a criticism of your work — but it does suggest the boundary is worth stating explicitly in the PR body: enumerate what IS and IS NOT treated as a git directory, so the next reviewer can check the rule rather than hunt for the next variant.

The PR adds a boundary rule: paths OUTSIDE the repository write as before (caller-owned, symlinks
allowed, because `--record-baseline /tmp/base.json` is documented usage), while paths INSIDE the
repository write through os.Root with Lstat refusal. Two findings say the "inside" test is escapable.

"An explicit --repo may name a subdirectory, while the Git operations still index the entire
top-level repository. Using that subdirectory as the confinement root misclassifies sibling paths in
the same checkout as caller-owned; for example, from the repository root,
`index --repo subdir --report GRAPH_REPORT.md` follows a committed root-level symlink and can
truncate its external target. Resolve the Git top level before classifying output paths, with an
appropriate non-Git fallback for verify."

## FINDING 2 — MEDIUM — internal/cli/outputpath.go:95
"filepath.Rel uses case-sensitive lexical comparison on Unix even when the underlying filesystem is
case-insensitive, as is common on macOS, and EvalSymlinks does not canonicalize ordinary component
casing. An in-repository path using a differently cased spelling of the repository root therefore
falls through as caller-owned and is written with unrestricted os.WriteFile, allowing a committed
output symlink to be followed. Determine containment using filesystem identity or canonical
component casing rather than lexical paths alone."

## METHOD — non-negotiable
1. REPRODUCE EACH ONE FIRST against the current branch head. Build the binary, construct the repo,
   show the external target being truncated. If either does NOT reproduce, say so with evidence and
   push back rather than "fixing" a non-bug — a sibling agent correctly refuted part of a finding on
   another PR in this series and that was the right call.
2. Then fix. For finding 1, resolve the git top level (git rev-parse --show-toplevel) and classify
   against THAT, with a sensible fallback when git is unavailable or the path is not in a repo —
   note `verify` may legitimately run outside a git repo, so the fallback must not break it.
   For finding 2, use filesystem IDENTITY (os.SameFile on the resolved directories) rather than
   lexical comparison, or canonicalize casing — pick one, justify it, and make sure it still works
   when the target does not exist yet (that is the common case for an output file).
3. Do not break what the PR already gets right: `--report /tmp/x.json` and
   `--record-baseline /tmp/base.json` OUTSIDE the repo must still work, including on macOS where
   /tmp is itself a symlink to /private/tmp. Test that explicitly, both before and after.

- A failing-first regression test per finding that FAILS AT RUNTIME on the current head, not merely
  fails to compile. Print the real failure output.
- gofmt -l . empty, go vet ./..., go build ./..., go test ./internal/cli green.
- Windows-aware: symlink fixtures need a runtime.GOOS guard and a reason. Two PRs in this series
  already broke test (windows-latest). Note Windows is also case-insensitive, which is relevant to
  finding 2 — think about whether your fix behaves correctly there rather than just skipping.

  as written. Three PRs in this series failed audit on fabricated or stale transcripts.
- No AI attribution footer, no Co-Authored-By, no "Generated with".
- Push to the same branch (updates PR #136) and update the PR body with the new shapes covered.

REPORT caveman-ultra compressed: whether each finding reproduced, what you changed with file:line,
the failing-first output, gate results, and anything you could not do.

**15 PRs, all with green CI. 13 of 15 have clean trail reviews.** Two have open findings and both are now being fixed.

I read them in the browser — all three are legitimate:

**#136** (`--report` write confinement, the one HIGH from the review) has two:
- **High** — `--repo` may name a *subdirectory* while git indexes the whole top-level repo, so using that subdir as the confinement root misclassifies sibling paths as caller-owned. `index --repo subdir --report GRAPH_REPORT.md` would still follow a root-level committed symlink.
- **Medium** — `filepath.Rel` compares case-sensitively on Unix even when the filesystem is case-insensitive, as on macOS. A differently-cased spelling of the repo root falls through to unrestricted `os.WriteFile`.

**#132** has a fifth shape: a tracked **gitlink** (submodule) is emitted by `git ls-files` as `vendor/dep` with no trailing slash, so the ancestor walk starts at `vendor` and never reads `vendor/dep/.git` as a pointer.

Every one of these is the same pattern the whole review is about — a containment rule with one shape it doesn't cover. The trail reviewer has now found an adjacent variant on each of #132's three heads, which is the system working rather than failing. I've told that agent to **reproduce before fixing and push back if it doesn't reproduce** — it correctly refuted part of an earlier finding, and I'd rather it do that again than patch a non-bug — and to enumerate the boundary explicitly in the PR body so the next reviewer can check the rule instead of hunting for variant six.

Still outstanding: these three fixes, batch 2's remaining audits, and the #129/#131 repairs. Link list when it's all clean.

**My recommendation**, and I'll do this unless you say otherwise: keep full audit rounds for anything that changes behaviour, but for pure-prose defects — a wrong line number, an imprecise sentence — fix and ship without re-running a whole adversarial pass. Otherwise we spend another hour on typography. The trail review keeps running on every push regardless, so real regressions still get caught.

Also worth noting: the batch-2 auditor independently flagged the **same two residuals** on #136 that the trail reviewer did — case-variant repo root, and `--repo <subdirectory>` escape. ## DEFECT 1 — real bug, fix it
`ensureContainedInRepo` misattributes EVERY non-ENOENT stat error as a repository escape. So a
permission error, an I/O error, a too-many-symlinks error, or an interrupted syscall all get
reported as "path escapes the repository" — a wrong and misleading refusal in production, and it
will send someone hunting a security problem that isn't there.
Fix: distinguish the containment verdict from an operational error. Only an actual escape should be
reported as an escape; other errors should surface as what they are. Check how the surrounding code
reports read failures (there is an existing partial-failure/oversize path) and be consistent with it.

## DEFECT 2 — false claim, and it is baked into SHIPPED SOURCE
A code comment (repeated in the commit message and PR body) asserts "containment is the only behavior
that changes". That is FALSE: os.Root changes more than containment — it refuses paths through
symlinked intermediate directories that previously resolved fine, so a repository whose listing
reaches a file through a symlinked directory now gets a read failure where it previously got content.
Fix the comment to state what actually changes, and correct the commit message and PR body to match.
A false claim in a source comment outlives every PR, which is why this one matters more than the
usual prose nit.
While you are there: the PR body says such a file "is now unreadable rather than ..." — make that
sentence precise about what the user actually observes.

- Verify defect 1 by reproducing it: make a path that fails stat for a NON-escape reason (a directory
  with permissions removed is the easy one; use runtime.GOOS to skip on Windows where the semantics
  differ) and show the current code reporting it as an escape.
- Add a regression test for it that fails at RUNTIME on the current head, not merely fails to compile.
- Keep every behaviour the PR already gets right. Re-run the full package suite.

## GATE
gofmt -l . empty, go vet ./..., go build ./..., go test ./internal/sem green. Windows-aware fixtures
with a runtime.GOOS guard and a reason where the input is not representable. Every transcript in the
commit message and PR body must be reproducible from the committed tree exactly as written. No AI
attribution footer, no Co-Authored-By, no "Generated with".

Title: fix(sem): bound AST walk recursion (CWE-674) · entireio/entire-graph · Entire
URL: https://entire.io/gh/entireio/entire-graph/trails/100/fix-sem-bound-ast-walk-recursion-cwe-674

entireio

entire-graph

fix(sem): bound AST walk recursion (CWE-674)
fix(sem): bound AST walk recursion (CWE-674)#100
Threads
T

Problem:

The parser's recursive AST walkers had no depth bounds. A source file with deeply nested syntax (parentheses, field initializers, or error nodes stacked thousands of levels deep) would cause unbounded recursion into a goroutine stack that cannot be recovered from via recover(). A Go stack overflow is a fatal, unrecoverable process abort, killing all entire graph verbs (search, symbols, index, snapshot, edges, def, impact, neighbors) that rely on parsing. This is CWE-674 (uncontrolled recursion).

Three separate recursive walks in parser.go were vulnerable:

walkEntitiesScoped (main entity extraction)

initializerTypeBodies (field initializer traversal in class fields)

collectParseErrorDetails (syntax error detail collection, run on every file with parse errors)

Real files slip past existing guards: a 900k-level nested structure is only 1.8 MB (well under the 4 MiB parser input cap) and fits on fewer than 1 line per level (under the 5000-column minification check), so nothing rejected it before the walkers were reached.

Solution:

Introduce a hard depth limit maxParseWalkDepth = 5000 applied before recursion in all three walkers. The limit is set based on measurements over 55,900 real files in 21 languages: the deepest named-AST nesting observed was 464 levels, leaving ~10× headroom while capping stack usage at ~3.8 MB (well within Go's 1 GB goroutine limit).

When a walk hits the limit:

Entities above the truncation point are still emitted (shallow symbols survive).

The truncated file is marked with a new status code E_PARSE_DEPTH_EXCEEDED (instead of silently reporting partial results as complete).

The code is registered in intentionalSkipFailureCodes so one pathological file does not degrade the repository's completeness metric.

The fix is accompanied by a comprehensive test suite (parser_depth_test.go) that pins the three vulnerable walkers, verifies unbounded input no longer causes process abort, confirms shallow symbols still extract cleanly, and validates end-to-end behavior in snapshot output.

48m ago

Findings
High
AI
Trail Review
internal/sem/parser.go:3701
43m ago

This check bounds only walkEntitiesScoped's child recursion. Before that recursion, entityFromNode can invoke the independently recursive firstNameDescendant/firstDescendantOfType over an arbitrarily deep subtree (for example, a deeply parenthesized C declarator), so hostile input can still cause uncontrolled stack growth or process termination without reaching this guard.

AI
Trail Review
internal/sem/parser.go:319
49m ago

The depth guard is applied only after language preprocessing. For Rust, maskRustUnsupportedSyntax first calls the still-unbounded recursive unwrapRustItemWrapperMacros, so a file containing a matching cfg_*! { hint plus a sufficiently deep named AST can still fatally overflow the Go stack before this guarded walk or partial failure is reached.

Medium
AI
Trail Review
internal/sem/parser.go:395
43m ago

Marking depth truncation as ParseError makes Analyze treat a valid depth-limited file with zero extracted entities as a total parse failure and suppress its entire file delta. For example, a Python file containing only a module-level assignment with more than 5000 nested parentheses previously produced a module-scope change, but now git diff/analyze emits only a warning and loses that change.

AI
Trail Review
internal/sem/provider.go
49m ago

Classifying depth truncation as an intentional skip makes completenessFailureCount ignore it even though the file is marked parsed and declarations were dropped. A repository where every file has a shallow symbol followed by deeply nested declarations can therefore report completeness_level: ok, misleading consumers into trusting a systematically incomplete graph.

Fix four findings from an automated reviewer on open PR #140. No audit round after — fix, verify,
push, done. Go 1.26:
  export PATH="$HOME/.local/share/mise/installs/go/1.26.5/bin:$PATH"

PR #140: https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph/pull/140  (trail 100)
BRANCH: security/bound-parser-recursion
WORKTREE (already on that branch; NEVER commit in /Users/suhaan/devenv/entire-graph):
  /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-suhaan-devenv/b0108f24-43a4-413e-94c9-bd361b6fafc5/scratchpad/pr-parserdepth
YOU OWN: internal/sem/parser.go, internal/sem/provider.go (completeness/failure-code region only),
internal/sem/provider_parallel.go (partial-failure translation only), internal/sem/analyze.go if
finding 3 requires it, and their tests.

The PR adds `maxParseWalkDepth = 5000` to three walkers. The reviewer says the guard is both
INCOMPLETE (two more unbounded walkers reach the stack first) and MISCLASSIFIED (two ways).

## FINDING 1 — HIGH — parser.go:3701
"This check bounds only walkEntitiesScoped's child recursion. Before that recursion, entityFromNode
can invoke the independently recursive firstNameDescendant/firstDescendantOfType over an arbitrarily
deep subtree (for example, a deeply parenthesized C declarator), so hostile input can still cause
uncontrolled stack growth or process termination without reaching this guard."

## FINDING 2 — parser.go:319
"The depth guard is applied only after language preprocessing. For Rust, maskRustUnsupportedSyntax
first calls the still-unbounded recursive unwrapRustItemWrapperMacros, so a file containing a
matching cfg_*! { hint plus a sufficiently deep named AST can still fatally overflow the Go stack
before this guarded walk or partial failure is reached."

## FINDING 3 — MEDIUM — parser.go:395
"Marking depth truncation as ParseError makes Analyze treat a valid depth-limited file with zero
extracted entities as a total parse failure and suppress its entire file delta. For example, a Python
file containing only a module-level assignment with more than 5000 nested parentheses previously
produced a module-scope change, but now git diff/analyze emits only a warning and loses that change."

## FINDING 4 — provider.go
"Classifying depth truncation as an intentional skip makes completenessFailureCount ignore it even
though the file is marked parsed and declarations were dropped. A repository where every file has a
shallow symbol followed by deeply nested declarations can therefore report completeness_level: ok,
misleading consumers into trusting a systematically incomplete graph."

Findings 3 and 4 pull in opposite directions — one says the truncation is treated as too FATAL, the
other says it is treated as too BENIGN. Resolve them together: depth truncation is neither a total
parse failure nor an intentional skip. It is a PARTIAL result. Decide what that means for
(a) Analyze's file delta, (b) completeness, and (c) the emitted status code, and make the three
consistent. Justify the model in the PR body in a few sentences.

## METHOD
1. REPRODUCE each of 1 and 2 against the current head — a deeply parenthesized C declarator, and a
   Rust file with a matching `cfg_*! {` plus deep nesting. Show the process aborting. If either does
   NOT reproduce, say so with evidence and push back rather than patching a non-bug; a sibling agent
   correctly refuted part of a finding on another PR and that was right.
2. Then bound those walkers too. A prior scoping pass found ~13 recursive walkers in this package
   (parser.go:388, :6660 firstNameDescendant, :7444, :7804 firstDescendantOfType;
   parameters.go:285; js_scopes.go:392/597/646/686; rust.go:219 rustUseImportBindings;
   kotlin.go:432 which ALREADY takes a depth int and is the style to match). Bounding only the two
   named leaves the rest reachable — survey them, bound the ones that are reachable from
   parseWithProfile on hostile input, and say in the PR body which you bounded and which you did not
   and why. Do not claim completeness you have not established.
3. Verify the limit does not truncate legitimate code. The PR cites 464 levels max over 55,900 real
   files; keep that evidence and re-run it if your changes alter which walkers count depth.

## GATE
Failing-first tests that fail AT RUNTIME on the current head — for the stack-overflow cases that
means the test must demonstrate the abort is now prevented; a fatal stack overflow cannot be caught
by recover(), so run those in a subprocess (`exec.Command(os.Args[0], "-test.run=...")` with an env
guard) and assert on the exit status. Print the real output.
gofmt -l . empty, go vet ./..., go build ./..., go test ./internal/sem green, plus -race on the
depth tests. Windows-aware fixtures. Every claim in the commit message and PR body reproducible from
the committed tree. No AI attribution footer, no Co-Authored-By, no "Generated with".
Push to the same branch, update the PR body.

REPORT caveman-ultra compressed: which findings reproduced, what you changed with file:line, the
walker survey result, how you resolved the 3-vs-4 tension, failing-first output, gate, caveats.

content.text:
#140's four findings are the most substantive left, and two vindicate the scoping report's warning that the package has ~13 recursive walkers while the fix budgeted three:

- **High** — `entityFromNode` calls the still-unbounded `firstNameDescendant`/`firstDescendantOfType` *before* the guard, so a deeply parenthesized C declarator overflows without ever reaching it
- Rust preprocessing runs `unwrapRustItemWrapperMacros` unbounded *before* the guarded walk
- Marking truncation as `ParseError` makes `Analyze` drop the whole file delta — a Python file with deep parens loses its module-scope change
- Registering it as an intentional skip makes completeness report `ok` on a systematically incomplete graph

The last two pull in opposite directions — one says it's treated as too fatal, the other too benign — so I've told the agent to resolve them together: truncation is a *partial* result, neither a parse failure nor a skip, and the status code, completeness and file delta must agree on that.

**Status: 16 PRs, zero CI failures. 13 clean.** #132 and #137 cleared. #136's review is re-running, #137 has a stat-error fix in flight, #140 has this. That's the last of it.

**Fixes**
1. https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph/pull/136 — confine in-repo `--report` / `--record-baseline` writes
2. https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph/pull/137 — confine `init-agents` writes to the repository root
3. https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph/pull/138 — confine working-tree source reads to the repository root
4. https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph/pull/139 — cap every git blob read the size ceiling was meant to bound
5. https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph/pull/140 — bound AST walk recursion (CWE-674)
6. https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph/pull/132 — never index a git directory, whatever its name or depth
7. https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph/pull/129 — exclude credential stores from every graph corpus
8. https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph/pull/130 — bound the root ignore file's size and rule count
9. https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph/pull/127 — guard the cache-key ignore-file reads against non-regular files
10. https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph/pull/135 — escape C1 controls in the machine-format encoders
11. https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph/pull/126 — escape terminal control bytes in the fatal error report
12. https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph/pull/128 — reject paths the cat-file batch protocol cannot carry
13. https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph/pull/133 — reject option-shaped revisions before they reach git argv
14. https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph/pull/134 — stop honoring executable git config from the indexed repository
15. https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph/pull/131 — stop a manifest ref reaching `git fetch` as an option

**Policy**
16. https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph/pull/125 — add SECURITY.md with a private reporting path and threat model

**Status: 15 of 16 fully clean** — green CI and clean trail review. #140 has an agent finishing four findings on the parser depth guard, and #137 just pushed so its review is re-running.

Two things I got wrong that the agents caught, worth stating plainly:

**My scoping doc contained a false claim.** I wrote that `root.OpenFile` refuses all symlinked components. That's true on Windows but **not on Unix** — `os.Root` follows a symlink that stays inside the root. The #136 agent proved it with a standalone program (`root.OpenFile(in-root symlink) err = <nil>`, target clobbered) and added an `Lstat` that's genuinely load-bearing. Had it trusted my doc, the fix would have shipped broken.

**I told an agent to use `O_NOFOLLOW`.** It declined, because `syscall.O_NOFOLLOW` is undefined on Windows — exactly the `windows-latest` break two earlier PRs hit.

Two things need you: **enable private vulnerability reporting** on the repo (SECURITY.md's preferred channel is inert until then), and **approve the trails** — `Approvals: No reviewers have approved` is the only remaining gate on all 16, and I won't self-approve.

**Why 16, not 14.** The 14 was my earlier count of *confirmed* findings only. The actual arithmetic:

```
14 confirmed findings   ->  13 PRs   (one has no PR — see below)

```

**And three findings still have no PR — which is my miss, not a rounding difference.** When I asked how to handle the architectural three, you chose "PR them too, best effort." I said I'd do them last and then didn't:

- **Finding 06** — three quadratic blowups, and `root.go:32` hands every provider a `context.Background()` so `--max-seconds` can never fire

**Why one subagent is left.** Only `#140` is genuinely still working — 7 minutes in on its four findings. So: **15 of 16 clean, #140 in flight, and 3 findings with no PR at all.** Want me to open those three now? C2 is the one where I'd expect to ship a mitigation and say so rather than claim a fix — there's no obviously correct answer without changing a payload format that agents already parse.

content.text:
Honestly? It's the weakest PR in the set, and the audit already knocked down the original justification.

The first version claimed there was no private reporting channel. That was **false** — the auditor ran `curl` and found `github.com/entireio/entire-graph/security/policy` returns 200 anonymously today and already surfaces `security@entire.io`, inherited from `entireio/.github`. So a researcher isn't actually stranded.

What survives is narrower but real: **the inherited org policy is actively wrong for this project.** It issues advisories only for a vulnerability "exploited by a remote or non-local actor" and routes local-execution issues to public GitHub Issues as "bug reports rather than security advisories." entire-graph is a local binary with no remote surface — so read literally, that rule sends **100% of the findings in this review** to a public tracker. Including a working `git clone && entire graph init-agents` exploit that overwrites files outside the repo.

So the file's job is a routing override plus a repo-specific threat model, not "we have no policy."

Three honest caveats:

- Its *preferred* channel is inert. GitHub's "Report a vulnerability" button is gated on private vulnerability reporting, which is `{"enabled":false}` on this repo, and merging a file can't flip it. Until you enable it in Settings, only the email fallback works — and that already worked.
- It fixes zero code.
- It's the only PR whose value depends on a repo setting you'd have to change anyway.

**If you want only code, drop #125.** The action that actually matters is enabling private vulnerability reporting — that's worth more than the file, and it takes you about ten seconds. If you do that, the file becomes genuinely useful; if you don't, it's mostly documentation.

# Plan: land every entire-graph security fix as its own verified PR

Written 2026-08-19. Replaces the token-savings plan (that work is closed; see the artifact and
`graph-is-a-1to1-substitute` in memory).

## Context

A full adversarial security review of entire-graph at `cceb4de` produced **19 findings / 36
verdicts**: 14 confirmed (1 high, 5 medium, 8 low), 4 more from a completeness critic, 3 refuted.
Report: https://claude.ai/code/artifact/6ef583b3-6366-4678-a45b-2aacb48bfcc0

Six PRs are already open (#125–#130). All six audits are complete: **4 SHIP, 2 FIX-FIRST**. Every
non-Approvals CI check is green. This plan finishes the job: repair the two failures, then one PR per
remaining finding, each independently verified.

The review's own thesis is what the remaining work must respect: **five guards already exist in this
codebase and each is applied at some call sites and not others** — newline-path fallback 3 of 4,
leading-dash argv 3 of 8, `maxNestedIgnoreFileBytes` nested-only, `os.OpenRoot` reads-only,
`termsafe` text/agent-only. Every fix below pushes its guard into the **sink**, not the call site.

### What is already banked

| PR | Fix | Audit |
|---|---|---|
| #126 | escape control bytes in the fatal error report | **SHIP** — auditor built a stronger exploit than the author |
| #127 | guard cache-key ignore-file reads | **SHIP** — reproduced the block both directions |
| #128 | reject paths the cat-file batch protocol cannot carry | **SHIP** — reproduced at the real CLI |
| #130 | bound the root ignore file's size and rule count | **SHIP** |
| #125 | SECURITY.md | **FIX-FIRST** → R1 |
| #129 | `.env`/`.npmrc` | **FIX-FIRST** → R2 |

Two disclosed regressions to decide on before merge, both real and both currently buried in a PR
table row: #127 makes a plain regular `.graphignore` over 1 MiB hard-error (intended cap, but a large
generated ignore file now fails), and #126's `termsafe.Line` escapes LF so any multi-line error
prints as one line with literal `\x0a`.

`test (windows-latest)` failures on #127/#128 are already fixed and pushed: both were
platform-assuming fixtures (Windows forbids `\n` in filenames; `os.DevNull` is `NUL` and resolves as
a *regular* file, so the POSIX type guard is unreachable there while the `io.LimitReader` still
bounds the read on every platform).

## Two repairs first — both block merges

**R1 · #125 SECURITY.md.** Code is fine; the prose makes three claims the auditor refuted: that the
org policy "is the umbrella" (it contradicts this doc on routing), that no private channel exists
(`/security/policy` returns 200 today), and that GitHub gates the "Report a vulnerability" button on
SECURITY.md (it gates on private vulnerability reporting, which is **disabled** on this repo). Also
drop the hardcoded version table — `main` is already `v0.4.0-10-g`, so it self-falsifies on the next
tag. Fix the file; do not restate unverified claims.

**R2 · #129 `.env`/`.npmrc`** — user decision: **rework to fix the real cause.** The auditor rebuilt
the patched binary and the credential leak is **byte-for-byte unchanged**, because the search corpus
is built by `preselectSearchFiles` → `source.paths` (`internal/sem/search.go:1698`) independent of
`languageForPath`. The patch also silently raised secret-file scores ~1.5. So: keep the two-line
table removal, add the corpus exclusion that actually stops emission, delete the false claim from the
commit message (`symbols` never emitted the dump as a durable record), and disclose the score change.

## Then one PR per finding

Ordered by regression risk, safest first. Each is its own branch off `origin/main`.

**Tier A — mechanical, contained**
1. `09` Escape U+0080–U+009F in the machine-format encoders. JSON is `search`'s default on a TTY and
   `encoding/json` does not escape C1. Reopens #96, whose test asserts only on `0x1b`.
2. `12` Resolve `--base`/`--head` through `git rev-parse --verify --end-of-options` at the CLI
   boundary (`internal/cli/root.go:748,754`). Three siblings in the same file already do this.
3. `13` Make `.git` unconditional in `skipVendoredDir` (`provider.go:10061`), matched on path
   component before `ReincludesDescendant` is consulted.
4. `C1` Harden `newCmd` (`internal/gitutil/git.go`): `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM` and `-c core.fsmonitor=`.
   Verify no legitimate reliance on user git config first.
5. `C4` `cmd/graph-bench/main.go:246` — a committed manifest ref reaches a `git fetch` positional.

**Tier B — containment, the load-bearing work**
6. `01` **HIGH** `index --report` write containment via `os.OpenRoot` + `O_NOFOLLOW`, plus the
   content-injection half (`report.go:55-57` prints tracked filenames verbatim). Apply to
   `verify.go:238-243` in the same patch. Must keep a legitimate absolute `--report /tmp/x` working.
7. `02` `init-agents` write containment. **Trap:** a naive `os.Stat`→`os.Lstat` swap regresses the
   documented AGENTS.md↔CLAUDE.md alias feature (`agents.go:158-176`, `os.SameFile`). Use
   `os.OpenRoot` and preserve the alias.
8. `03` `gitutil.ShowFileLimited` at the four uncapped readers (`provider.go:9785`,
   `search.go:1433`, `analyze.go:109,115`), routed into the existing `E_FILE_TOO_LARGE` path so the
   file does not silently disappear.
9. `04` `openSource` repoRoot confinement (`provider.go:9836`). Hot indexing path — open one
   `os.Root` for the `openedSource` lifetime, mirroring `callsite.go:211` and `cache_entry.go:71`.

**Tier C — subtle and architectural** (user decision: attempt all three)
10. `05` Depth counter through every recursive walker reachable from `parseWithProfile`, emitting an
    `E_PARSE_DEPTH` partial failure. Go stack overflow is unrecoverable, so this must be a *limit*,
    not a `recover()`.
11. `06` Give the relation and search phases a real wall-clock budget — `root.go:32` hands every
    provider `context.Background()`, so `--max-seconds` can never fire — then fix the three quadratic
    sites.
12. `C2` Agent-payload record forgery. No obviously correct fix; a repo-committed `VERIFY:` line is
    indistinguishable from tool output and the guide tells agents to execute it. Attempt the
    narrowest credible change (provenance marking rather than fencing, which would break parsers) and
    **say plainly in the PR if the result is a mitigation rather than a fix.**
13. `C3` `.graphignore` silently controls the graph's field of view. Surface exclusions in the
    payload so a hidden file is visible as hidden.

## Verification — the gate that has already caught two bad PRs

Per PR, non-negotiable:
- **Failing-first test, proven.** Restore the production file from `origin/main`, keep the new test,
  show it fails. A test that only fails to *build* on main is too weak (#130 hit this and said so).
- `gofmt -l` empty · `go vet ./...` · `go build ./...` · package tests green.
- **Windows-aware fixtures.** Any test using symlinks, device files or exotic filenames gets a
  `runtime.GOOS` guard with a comment saying why the input is unrepresentable there. This bit #127
  and #128; it is now a checklist item, not a discovery.
- **Adversarial audit** by a second agent that rebuilds `origin/main` itself, re-runs the exploit
  against the patched binary, and re-verifies the failing-first claim. This is what caught #129.
- **No unverified claims** in commit messages or PR bodies. Both failed audits were prose, not code.
- No AI attribution footers.

## What I cannot do

`Entire Gates` fails on all six PRs with `Approvals: No reviewers have approved this trail`.
Checks, Findings and Up-to-date all pass. That gate needs a human reviewer and I will not
self-approve. **Enabling private vulnerability reporting** on the repo is also yours — SECURITY.md is
worth little until it is on.
